title: Web audio still crackles: both stream caches load lazily, inside gameplay frames
description:
A phone running the Web build still reports choppy audio after plant-tower-defense-t416 raised audio/driver/output_latency.web to 140.

Sfx.stream_for (game/sfx.gd) and Music._stream_for (game/music.gd) both cache on FIRST USE, so every cue pays its load() inside the frame that first fires it -- a run's first kill, first volley, first bite, first denied purchase -- and the RUN bed (a 1.8MB mp3, the largest file shipped) loads during the crossfade that starts a run, with the outgoing bed already decoding.

project.godot's [audio] block is why that is an audio defect and not just a dropped frame: default_playback_type.web=0 routes every voice through the engine's WASM mixer, and variant/thread_support=false means that mixer's ring buffer is refilled from the main loop once per rendered frame. A stalled main thread IS a missed refill, and a missed refill is crackle. The 140ms buffer buys headroom for a frame that runs long; it buys none for a frame that has not finished decoding, because that frame does not render until it has.

Not a polyphony problem: Sfx already pools 8 AudioStreamPlayers plus a dedicated ambience voice under the scene tree root, and Music holds 2 for crossfade.
design:
Sfx.prewarm() and Music.prewarm() load every entry in SOUNDS/TRACKS plus the ambience bed, called from Game._ready where the frame is a loading frame already. Sfx.prewarm also builds the pool and the bed voice, gated on is_headless() so no suite gets a scene-tree side effect; the loading half is ungated so a headless test can assert the whole table resolves.

Rejected: variant/thread_support=true, which costs no latency and is the better fix, but needs COOP/COEP headers from the host and a host that does not send them serves a game that will not boot. Same reason it was refused in plant-tower-defense-t416.
acceptance_criteria: prewarm() returns SOUNDS.size() + 1 and TRACKS.size(); a test makes the caches cold via forget_streams(), builds game.tscn, and reads both caches back full -- and that test fails when the two calls are removed from Game._ready.

title: Web audio crackles and lags on mobile: 50ms buffer starves under main-thread mixing
description:
The only export preset is Web (export_presets.cfg preset.0) with variant/thread_support=false, and project.godot pins audio/general/default_playback_type.web=0 (Stream) — the shipped fix for the runtime-bus WebAudio feedback loop documented at game/sfx.gd:658. Stream playback means every voice is mixed by the engine's own software mixer in WASM, and with no thread support that mixer's ring buffer is refilled from the main loop, once per rendered frame. Desktop at 60fps refills a 50ms buffer every 16.7ms and never notices. A phone running this board at 25-30fps refills every 33-40ms, and any hitch (a wave spawning, a volley landing, the ambience loop plus a music bed plus up to POOL_SIZE=8 sfx voices all mixing at once) pushes a refill past the buffer's own length. An underrun in an audio ring buffer is heard as crackle and as drift, which is exactly the report: distorted and laggy.

audio/driver/output_latency.web is at Godot's default of 50 (confirmed by reading property_get_revert off the 4.7.1 binary; audio/driver/mix_rate.web is already 0, i.e. follow the browser's own rate, so resampling is not the cause).
design:
Raise audio/driver/output_latency.web in project.godot. It is a web-only override, so desktop keeps its 15ms and nothing about the desktop feel changes.

Rejected: variant/thread_support=true. It moves mixing onto a real worklet thread and is the better fix in principle, but it requires SharedArrayBuffer, which requires COOP/COEP cross-origin isolation headers from whoever hosts the build. If the host does not send them the game does not boot at all. That is a deploy-coupled change, not a simple one.

Rejected: reverting default_playback_type.web to Sample and adding a default_bus_layout.tres so the buses exist before driver start. This is very likely the real fix — Sample playback hands the streams to native WebAudio and stops using the WASM mixer entirely, which is precisely what a phone needs, and adding the layout removes the runtime-bus-add that game/sfx.gd:665 names as the root cause of the feedback loop. But the failure mode if the reasoning is wrong is the shipped bug again: a closed unity-gain loop reaching 78x full scale. It cannot be verified from this machine without deploying a build and reading the browser's audio graph, so it is not a change to make blind.
acceptance_criteria: project.godot carries audio/driver/output_latency.web with a comment saying why, and test/unit/test_selftest.gd asserts the value, in the same shape as the existing test_web_playback_type_is_stream — because comments in project.godot do not survive an editor settings save and the test is the only durable record.
close_reason:
audio/driver/output_latency.web is now 140 in project.godot, up from Godot's web default of 50, with the argument written beside it. Web-only override, so desktop keeps 15 and nothing about the desktop feel moves.

test_web_audio_output_latency_has_mobile_headroom in test/unit/test_selftest.gd asserts a FLOOR derived from fps_min in devtools_config.json (four frames at the gated 30fps = 134ms), not the literal 140 — a retune that is still correct should not turn the suite red, and a project that later gates on 60fps should not silently keep a buffer sized for 30. It also asserts a 250ms ceiling, so the buffer cannot grow into a delay line, and that the base output_latency stays below the web value, so desktop never pays a tax it does not owe.

The test earned its place immediately: the first value written here was 120, chosen by eye as "roughly four slow frames", and the derived floor rejected it at 134. Being short of the floor is being wrong in exactly the direction the bug runs in.

Not verified on a phone — no Web export was built or deployed from this machine, and the symptom is unreproducible on desktop, where the .web suffix is inert and mixing happens on its own audio thread. What is verified is the setting's value, the derivation of the floor, and that desktop is untouched. If a mobile player still hears crackle after this ships, the next move is variant/thread_support=true plus COOP/COEP headers from the host, which is written down in the bead's design field along with the reason it was not the first move.

title: A sport should look mutated, not slightly tinted
description:
`PlantMutation.TINT` is Color(1.10, 0.88, 1.16) — a 12% violet shift multiplied into the parent sprite's modulate (game/plant.gd:499) — and `SportMark` paints a violet disc with a four-point star in it (game/sport_mark.gd:61, game/plant_mutation.gd STAR_POINTS=4). Both were chosen to be quiet. The result is that a sport is hard to tell from its parent at a glance, and the badge reads as a generic 'special' marker rather than as a mutation.

Three asks:
1. The badge should read as the toxic-waste/hazard mark, not a star.
2. The sport's colours should be dramatic.
3. A sport should wear its OWN sprite — custom, but recognisably the parent's drawing.

(3) is the part that decides the shape. Nine plants is 17 sprites once the frame-swapping kinds are counted (bramble x3, chomp x4, dandelion x4), and hand-drawing 17 recolours is 17 chances to drift from art_src/STYLE.md. The sprites should be DERIVED from their parents by a deterministic generator, with a --check mode a gate can run, so the mutant art cannot drift from the art it is derived from.
design:
Recolour-only derivation: the sport SVG has byte-identical geometry to its parent, so every geometric gate in test_sprite_style.gd (canvas size, retina doubling, bilateral centring, in-canvas bounds) passes for the sport exactly because it passes for the parent.

Colour mapping: source hue picks one of two mutant ramps (60..200 deg -> toxic acid green, else -> mutagen magenta); achromatic colours are left alone. Within a ramp, a sprite's own distinct colours of that family are spread across the ramp anchors by normalised luminance, monotonically, so the parent's darker-than ordering — which is what the outline check enforces — is preserved by construction.

Every emitted colour is a ramp anchor, i.e. a literal palette entry, so anti-aliased edges land on palette-pair segments exactly as the parent's do. The anchors go in a MUTANT_PALETTE the gate applies ONLY to _sport stems, so the base sprites' palette contract does not weaken.
acceptance_criteria:
- tools/gen_sport_svg.py generates all 17 art_src/*_sport.svg from their parents and --check exits 1 when a committed sport SVG differs from what the generator would emit
- test_sprite_style.gd passes with the 17 new stems in EXPECTED_SIZE, and MUTANT_PALETTE is accepted only for _sport stems
- tools/svg_style_check.py reports no errors over art_src/
- a sport plant loads its own texture, and so do the bramble/chomp/dandelion frame swaps
- SportMark paints a hazard trefoil; badge_trefoil() is pure and assertable headless
- new checks live in test/unit/test_selftest.gd
close_reason:
Done, and the shape it landed in is not the one the bead sketched.

WHAT SHIPPED. tools/gen_sport_svg.py derives all 17 art_src/*_sport.svg from their parents: geometry copied byte for byte, only paint remapped onto one of two constant-hue ramps chosen by the source colour's hue (60-200 deg -> toxic acid green at 78, everything else -> mutagen magenta at 310, achromatic left alone). A bare run is the check and --write is the flag, because check_all.py runs every tools/*.py with a NOT COVERED line bare and in parallel. Plant.frame_texture_path is the single funnel every texture load goes through, so the Bramble's three damage frames, the Dandelion's four fluff frames and the Chomp's four eating frames all resolve to their mutant twin. PlantMutation.TINT is gone and SPORT_MODULATE is white. SportMark paints a hazard trefoil (3 blades, 60 deg each with 60 deg gaps, hazard yellow on near-black) instead of a four-point star.

THE PREMISE HELD but the design note was wrong in one place. It said colours would be spread across the ramp by their normalised position in the sprite's own luminance range. That fans a bunched family out: the Corn's two leaf greens are 14 luminance apart in a drawing spanning 53, so they landed on rungs 5 and 7 of 8 and the plant grew one dark leaf and one nearly white one. Caught on a screenshot, by nothing else -- svg_style_check reported 0 errors and all 11 test_sprite_style tests passed, because both ask whether a colour is legal and neither asks how far it is from the colour beside it. Changed to nearest-rung-by-luminance, so a sport is as bright, in the same places, as its parent and only the hue moved.

FOUND ON THE WAY, all fixed:
- test_the_sport_badge_stays_clear_of_the_health_bar ended `return ""` instead of `return err`. Its clearance assertion had been FAILING on every run since it was written while the test reported a pass, and the badge at (17,-25) r8 overlapped the health bar by 4px on every damaged sport that ever shipped. Now (21,-17) r9, exactly 13px clear, and the test returns what it computed.
- `--check` inside the generated banner is `--` inside an XML comment. Godot's SVG loader accepted all 17; ElementTree refused all 17. That is the argument for having a second reader of the same file.
- Mutagen rung 8 at (255,232) is saturation 0.090, which the outline rule reads as a grey fill, so the Aloe drew a coloured rim around bare paper on five shapes.
- badge_ring() was production code nothing drew with, and its test asserted that every point of a circle is one radius from its centre. Lint's orphan pass named it; both gone.

ACCEPTANCE, each line: gen_sport_svg.py generates all 17 and a bare run reports drift (verified by hand-editing a fill and by desyncing MUTANT_PALETTE -- both reported, both named the fix). test_sprite_style passes 11/11 with sport stems in _declared(), which DERIVES a sport's row from its parent's rather than adding 17 hand-typed rows; MUTANT_PALETTE is handed out by _palette_rgb only for a _sport stem, so the kit contract is exactly as tight for the other 34 sprites as before. svg_style_check reports 0 errors, 0 warnings over 51 sprites. A sport loads its own texture and so do the frame swaps -- confirmed live: a sport Bramble driven to health 25 then 8 read bramble_chewed_sport.png then bramble_ragged_sport.png. badge_trefoil() is pure and asserted headless. Six new checks in test/unit/test_selftest.gd. Full suite 1127/1127, lint exit 0, check_all 31 clean.

title: Placement has no ghost, no armed cue, and no way out
description:
Reported from play on touch. Four symptoms, three causes, all in the placement gesture.

1. NO GHOST. A press-drag on the board shows `_cursor` (a cell-tint ColorRect) and `PlacementPreview` (brackets + range ring, game/placement_preview.gd) and nothing that says WHICH plant. game/game.gd:3335 `_update_preview` sets reach, plant_id, covered_now, placeable, at_risk -- no sprite. The player sees where it goes and not what goes there.

2. THE ARMED PLANT HAS NEVER BEEN SHOWN. game/hud.gd:2474 does `button.button_pressed = unlocked and id == selected`. No `toggle_mode` is set on any Button in game/ or test/ (grep, 0 hits), and Godot 4 BaseButton::set_pressed() returns early when toggle_mode is false. The line is a no-op. The only writer of `modulate` on those buttons is `_apply_plant_hints()` (afford-dim + packet-hover tint), which carries no selection channel. So the plant bar has never had an armed cue at all -- this is a dead assignment, not a weak cue.

3. NO WAY OUT, AND NO STATE TO GO TO. game/game.gd:3126 right-click clears `selected_placed` only, and returns early when nothing placed is selected -- `selected_plant` is untouched by it. `selected_plant` defaults to PlantCatalog.CORN (game/game.gd:260) and is never assigned an empty value anywhere; `would_plant_at` (:1984) and `_update_cursor` (:3326) both assume PlantCatalog.has() holds. "Nothing armed" is an unrepresentable state.

4. LIFTING DOES NOT DISARM, which is symptom 3 from the other end: a plant is always armed, so every stray board tap spends seeds.

DECIDED WITH THE REPORTER (both were the recommended option):
  * Gesture model: arm-then-drag, disarm on lift. Tap a plant button to arm. Press/drag the board shows the ghost. A COMMITTED placement disarms. A refusal keeps the arm (losing your pick because you were 5 seeds short is a second punishment). Sliding off the board aborts and disarms, as it already aborts today.
  * Ghost position: the SNAPPED cell, not the touch point -- `_update_cursor(pos, snap)` already resolves that cell via TOUCH_SNAP_RADIUS, and a finger occludes ~50px so a ghost under it is a ghost nobody sees. Mouse AND touch, so it is reachable from the headless suite and from a desktop bridge session rather than only from real hardware (cf. plant-tower-defense-bfbb).
design:
GHOST: a Sprite2D on PlacementPreview itself, not a fourth sibling under Entities. The preview already owns plant_id, already knows the cell, and is already shown/hidden on exactly the frames a ghost should be shown/hidden -- a separate node would be a second copy of that lifecycle to keep in step. Texture from PlantCatalog.texture_path(plant_id), the same source the bar button icons load.

ARMED CUE: a ring Control parented INSIDE each plant button with PRESET_FULL_RECT and MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE, visible only for the armed id. Parented inside rather than positioned over: GridContainer owns those rects, so a ring that computes its own position is arithmetic that goes stale on every resize and lays a frame behind refresh(). Not toggle_mode -- that would fix the dead line but hand the default theme's pressed stylebox a job the HUD deliberately does not use GardenTheme.build() for, and it changes click semantics (second click un-toggles) that nothing in the suite pins.

EMPTY ARM: `selected_plant == &""` becomes legal. PlantCatalog.has(&"") is already false, so would_plant_at() already refuses it; the work is auditing the callers that assume a name is present -- game.gd:1990, :2318, :3326, :3358, :3571 and hud.gd:2474's loop.

RIGHT-CLICK: clears BOTH the placed selection and the arm in one press, and consumes the event only when it cleared something. One rule beats two, and it is still the escape from an armed uproot that lzw4 added it for.
acceptance_criteria:
* A ghost sprite of the armed plant is drawn at the previewed cell, semi-transparent, for mouse hover and for touch drag, and is absent when nothing is armed.
* The plant bar shows which plant is armed, and shows NONE armed when none is.
* python tools/run_tests.py passes, with new checks in test/unit/test_selftest.gd covering: the empty-arm state refusing a placement, the armed cue tracking selected_plant including the empty case, and the ghost's texture matching PlantCatalog.texture_path.
* godot --headless --path . --script res://tools/lint_project.gd exits 0.
* Driven live on the bridge: arm, drag, lift, and confirm the arm is gone and a second board tap plants nothing.
close_reason:
Shipped on main at 34f2513 (fix commit ec459cb). All four reported symptoms addressed, each verified on the running game as well as headless.

WHAT THE BEAD GOT WRONG, corrected before implementing: the ghost was NOT missing. It shipped in plant-tower-defense-bmis and works -- node-bounds on the live game reported Rect 192,392,64x64, visible, correct texture, following a simulated touch drag. It is drawn as exactly one cell at the cell the finger rests on, so a fingertip covers it entirely. The defect was occlusion, and the fix is a one-cell lift while a finger is down (GHOST_LIFT, flipping downward on row 0, touch only). The preview node, brackets, range ring and committed cell do not move.

The other three were as filed. The bar's armed cue was a dead write (button_pressed with no toggle_mode; live: button_pressed=false toggle_mode=false while corn WAS selected_plant) and is now an ArmedRing Panel per button, LEAF, measured against the button's own pixels (#665f52, luminance 0.375 -> separation 0.267, and 0.147 when dimmed). selected_plant now accepts &"": a successful placement disarms, a refusal does not, right-click clears both halves of the selection, and a finger leaving the board disarms.

FOUND AND FIXED MID-RUN, and it is the reason the runtime pass earned its place: the touch abort PASSED headless and FAILED live. It read _hover_cell; dragging off the right edge crosses onto the side panel, which consumes the remaining InputEventScreenDrags, so the cue keeps the last cell it heard about -- measured _touch_index=-1 _hover_cell=(13,8) with the plant still armed. Both callers now share off_board(), asked of the release position, and the test withholds the drag on purpose so it reproduces that state.

Also repaired two suite defects this surfaced: _declaration_line matched only 'const NAME ' with a trailing space, so every typed 'const NAME: Color = ...' read as not aliasing the palette; and the drag-cue sweep armed once for 294 placements, which the disarm turned into a sweep of nothing -- caught by its own snapped>0 vacuity guard.

7 new tests in test/unit/test_selftest.gd. Gates on main after merge: run_tests 1132/1132, 25097 assertions, exit 0; lint 0 errors 0 warnings; name_check 0 errors. Ledger row banked with the failed-then-fixed check recorded as fail+fixed_in_run rather than rewritten green. Harness log entry plus gaps G-083 (fixed in run) and G-084.

title: The mirror gate passes on standard and fails on gentle, because it pins the profile after instantiating
description:
Measured 2026-08-29 on main at 319fd9f, immediately after plant-tower-defense-i8oh added seed_yield to the difficulty profiles.

test/unit/test_mirror_parity.gd pins DIFFICULTY_STANDARD in both scenarios (lines 239 and 320). Standard's seed_yield is exactly 1.0 and Game.seeds_after_yield(n, 1.0) is the identity, so the gate is green. Point it at gentle -- sed 's/Game.DIFFICULTY_STANDARD/Game.DIFFICULTY_GENTLE/g', two sites -- and it FAILS:

  [defended] seeds_earned DRIFTED: tools/run_sim.gd made it 61 and game/game.gd
  made it 37 on the same wave, the same seed and the same garden.
  Expected 37 but got 61

Exit 1, one axis. 61/37 is about 1.65; gentle's seed_yield is 1.5.

WHAT IS NOT YET ESTABLISHED, and it is the whole bead: WHICH SIDE IS WRONG. Two readings, and they have very different consequences.

1. THE GATE'S SETUP. The gate instantiates game.tscn and THEN pins the profile. If Game.seed_yield is assigned in Game._ready from RunConfig.difficulty, it was already fixed at standard's 1.0 before the pin landed, while RunSim reads gentle. A real run sets RunConfig.difficulty before the scene loads, so the shipped game would be fine and only the gate's ordering is wrong. This is the likelier reading.
2. A REAL DIVERGENCE. The two drivers genuinely disagree about where seed_yield comes from or when it is applied, in which case every gentle and harsh number in docs/playtest-runs.jsonl describes RunSim rather than the game -- and i8oh's whole finding rests on that file.

Reading 1 makes this a test fix. Reading 2 makes docs/playtest-runs.jsonl wrong for two of three profiles. Do not assume the first because it is cheaper.

WHY THIS IS P1 RATHER THAN P2. The gate was built by plant-tower-defense-xca3 precisely so a mirror could not drift unwatched, and it caught a divergence on its first day -- but only when pointed somewhere it is not pointed. A gate that is green on the one profile where the axis under test is the identity is a gate asserting 0 == 0. That is the vacuous pass CLAUDE.md warns about loudest, sitting inside the tool built to prevent it.

CONFIRMED, not inferred: standard passes (exit 0, 'Mirror parity: 8 of 8 axes moved across 2 scenario(s)', 83 assertions) and gentle fails (exit 1, seeds_earned), on the same tree, minutes apart, with only the two DIFFICULTY_ constants changed and reverted after.
acceptance_criteria: The gate runs over all three profiles rather than standard alone -- and passes on all three, or names the driver that is wrong and fixes it. Whichever reading turns out to be true is written down at the gate, because the next person will re-derive it otherwise. If reading 2 holds, docs/playtest-runs.jsonl is re-swept and i8oh's gentle/harsh rows are restated. The recorded run_sim.gd:453 mutation still takes the gate red afterwards, proving it did not go vacuous while being widened.
notes:
RESOLVED BY A LIVE READ, 2026-08-29, before anyone worked this. Reading 1 holds: it is the gate's setup ordering, and the shipped game is correct.

Driven through the bridge against the running game:

  get-state /root/RunConfig --property difficulty        -> standard
  find-nodes --class Game --property seed_yield          -> 1.0
  set-state /root/RunConfig --property difficulty gentle
  run-method /root/Game --method _ready
  find-nodes --class Game --property seed_yield          -> 1.5     <-- follows
  (set back to standard, _ready re-run, seed_yield 1.0 again)

Game.seed_yield IS assigned from the profile on the path a real run takes. The gate instantiates game.tscn while RunConfig still says standard and only THEN pins the profile at lines 239/320, so game.seed_yield stays 1.0 while sim gets gentle's 1.5. The 61-vs-37 gap is the gate disagreeing with itself, not the drivers disagreeing.

TWO CONSEQUENCES, the second being the one that mattered:
* docs/playtest-runs.jsonl is NOT invalidated. RunSim.play() sets seed_yield from the same profile lookup, so the gentle and harsh rows describe the driver correctly. Read i8oh's close reason with this note beside it.
* The fix is in the gate's setup, not in either driver: set RunConfig.difficulty BEFORE instantiating game.tscn (or assign game.seed_yield alongside the existing profile pin), then widen both scenarios over all three profiles.

Stays P1 and stays open. The acceptance is unchanged and is still the real work: a gate green on the single profile where the axis under test is the identity is asserting 0 == 0, and widening it must be followed by re-running the recorded run_sim.gd:453 mutation to prove it did not go vacuous while being widened.
close_reason: Fixed: gate now sets RunConfig.difficulty before instantiating game.tscn, and runs both scenarios across all 3 profiles (6 runs). Confirmed NOTES' reading 1 (gate setup-order bug, shipped game was always correct). Recorded run_sim.gd:453 mutation still takes it red.

title: Record where the five game-specific audio files came from, or the game ships unlicensed
description: assets/audio/License.txt now scopes the Kenney CC0 claim to the Kenney files and credits ElvGames for the bought music, but the five cues added by the owner — shoot.wav, hit-received.wav, bug-steps.wav, plant-place.ogg, clickanddrag.ogg — are listed under 'CUES WRITTEN FOR THIS GAME' with their upstream source and terms unrecorded. If any of them came out of a pack rather than being made for the game, that pack's licence has to be named there. Four of the five are wired into Sfx.SOUNDS and the fifth (bug-steps.wav) is the ambience bed, so they all play on every run.
acceptance_criteria: assets/audio/License.txt names, for each of the five files, either the pack and licence it came from or an explicit statement that it was made for this game — and the placeholder paragraph pointing at a bead is gone.
close_reason:
assets/audio/License.txt now states, for all five cues, that they were made for this game by its owner -- confirmed 2026-08-29 -- and the placeholder paragraph pointing at this bead is gone (commit 3383058). The acceptance asked for pack-or-original per file; the answer is original for all five.

Two of them carried the evidence that made the bead worth filing: plant-place.ogg and clickanddrag.ogg have Vorbis TITLE=place10 / TITLE=place6 with MP3GAIN batch tags and no ARTIST, where every Kenney file here carries ARTIST=Kenney. Those tags are now quoted verbatim in the licence section with the explanation, so the question is answered at the place someone would next ask it rather than only in this close reason.

Beyond the acceptance: tools/audio_license_check.py (2a8e266, 72fe660) reads the credit embedded in every audio file -- Vorbis, ID3v2 and RIFF LIST/INFO -- and reconciles it against License.txt. Four gating rules plus one waivable advisory, a kept --self-test of 12 cases, auto-discovered by check_all.py (28 checkers, 0 unclassified), clean over the shipped tree with 19 of 19 files reachable by both readings. The bead could recur without it; it cannot now.

title: RunSim mirrors ten of Game methods and nothing checks they still agree
description:
`tools/run_sim.gd` re-derives the game's economy rather than calling into it, and says so
in its own header: "the economy below is a re-derivation of `Game`'s, not a call into it.
Every branch that moves seeds cites the `game/game.gd` function it mirrors BY NAME rather
than by line, because nothing checks a citation inside GDScript and a line number here
would rot unread" (run_sim.gd:21-24).

**"Nothing checks" is the bead.** Seven functions carry a `Mirrors Game.X` comment
(verified 2026-08-28 by grepping `^## Mirrors` in run_sim.gd):

| RunSim | mirrors |
|---|---|
| `_new_pest` | `Game._new_pest` |
| `_on_pest_died` | `Game._on_pest_died` |
| `_on_pest_escaped` | `Game._on_pest_escaped` |
| `_spawn_brood` | `Game._spawn_brood` |
| `_on_plant_grew_seeds` | `Game._on_plant_grew_seeds` |
| `_on_plant_destroyed` | `Game._on_plant_destroyed` |
| `_apply_weather` / `_refresh_neighbour_buffs` / `_tick_cross_breeding` / `_install` | the matching `Game` methods |

Every balance number this project now records comes out of those. The moment one drifts,
the sweep reports a balance change the game did not make, or misses one it did — and the
record is committed, diffed, and read by a tuning pass as though it described the game.
That is a worse failure than having no record, because the record is trusted.

## WHY THE MIRROR EXISTS, AND WHY THAT REASON IS WEAKER THAN IT LOOKS

The header's stated reason (run_sim.gd:13-19): hosting a `Game` and awaiting frames would
make the run reproducible "only up to how busy the machine was", so it hand-steps loose
nodes instead.

The premise is not quite right, and it is worth writing down because it is the thing that
would decide a future rewrite. Hosting a `Game` does not require awaiting real frames: a
driver can host `res://game/game.tscn` and then call `game._process(DT)` and
`_physics_process(DT)` by hand over the subtree at a fixed dt, exactly as this file does
over its own nodes, with no `await` anywhere in the run. That was built and measured in
parallel with this file (branch `worktree-playtest-driver`, commit 95f4ccd, not merged):
two runs on one seed produced byte-identical wave records, so the determinism this file
gives up `Game` for is available without giving up `Game`.

Three things that driver needed which are worth knowing before anyone rewrites this one:
a `Tween` is stepped by the `SceneTree` and not by any node, and `Pest._play_death` frees
its corpse through one on BOTH sides of the animations gate, so a hand-stepped tree must
step tweens or wave 1 never ends; `Game._process` starts the next wave itself at prep zero
(game.gd:519-521), so a driver that steps the whole prep gap must not then ask; and
`queue_free()` never lands, so it has to detach the dead itself — the same problem this
file solves with `_collect_garbage`.

**This bead is NOT "rewrite run_sim.gd".** That trade is genuinely arguable: this file has
`road_corners`, an income breakdown split three ways, husk sweeping and upgrades, none of
which that driver had. What is not arguable is that the mirror is unchecked.

## THE ASK

A gate that fails when the mirror and `Game` disagree, rather than a promise that they do
not.

The shape that would actually catch it: play ONE wave twice — once through `RunSim`, once
through a hosted `game.tscn` driven by the same fixed-dt hand-stepping and the same seed
and the same garden — and assert the pair agree on the numbers the mirror is responsible
for: seeds earned, seeds from each of the three sources, lives lost, pests killed, pests
escaped, plants lost. A single wave is enough; the mirrored functions all fire inside one.

Cheaper and weaker alternatives, listed so the choice is deliberate rather than defaulted
into: a static checker that fails when a `## Mirrors Game.X` comment names a function that
no longer exists (catches a rename, misses every behaviour change); or a checker that
compares the two function bodies for token-level divergence (noisy, and a mirror is
*supposed* to differ — it has no HUD, no signals, no tweens).

## WHAT TO WATCH

- `test_the_three_income_sources_are_all_in_the_loop`
  (`test/unit/test_playtest.gd:303`) already asserts all three sources fire in `RunSim`.
  It does not compare any of them to `Game`, which is exactly the gap.
- `Game.new_plant` and `Game.weather_seed_value_for` are statics extracted so the driver
  calls them instead of copying them (`784c0ff`). That is the pattern the fix should
  extend: every mirrored branch that CAN become a shared static should, and the gate then
  covers only what genuinely cannot.
- Whatever is built must not need a second whole-run driver in the repo to exist. One wave,
  one hosted `Game`, inside `test_dir`.
- `docs/playtest-runs.jsonl` is committed and read by `tools/playtest_report.py`. Until
  this gate exists, treat every number in it as "what `RunSim` believes", not "what the
  game does".
acceptance_criteria: A gate in test_dir plays one wave through RunSim and one through a hosted game.tscn hand-stepped at the same fixed dt with the same seed and the same garden, and asserts the two agree on seeds earned, seeds from kills, seeds from growth, seeds from husks, lives lost, pests killed, pests escaped and plants lost. Deliberately breaking one mirrored branch in run_sim.gd makes the gate fail - proving it can fail is the acceptance, not the pair currently agreeing.
close_reason:
test/unit/test_mirror_parity.gd (merge e34b5e9..; lane commit d2c5b5f) hosts res://game/game.tscn, hand-steps it at the same fixed dt as RunSim on the same seed and the same DERIVED garden, and compares all eight axes the acceptance names: seeds earned, seeds from kills, seeds from growth, seeds from husks, lives lost, pests killed, pests escaped, plants lost.

PROVING IT CAN FAIL WAS THE ACCEPTANCE, and it was observed, not predicted. Mutating run_sim.gd:417 to '+ paid + 1' took the gate from exit 0 to exit 1 with:

  [defended] seeds_from_kills DRIFTED: tools/run_sim.gd made it 8 and game/game.gd made it 6 on the same wave, the same seed and the same garden.

Exactly one of the eight arms fired. Reverted; git status clean. Clean run: exit 0, 83 assertions, 'Mirror parity: 8 of 8 axes moved across 2 scenario(s)'.

Two scenarios rather than one wave, deliberately: one wave with one garden leaves escaped, lives_lost and plants_lost reading 0 == 0, which is eight axes agreeing about nothing. 'defended' reaches kills, husks and growth; 'walled' reaches escapes, lives and a plant lost; the gate asserts every axis moved somewhere and prints NEVER MOVED when one did not.

The bead's own table UNDERCOUNTED: ten '## Mirrors' comments naming eleven Game methods, not seven -- the last row collapsed four into an ellipsis. run_sim.gd is NOT in the diff.

Five static extractions were identified and deliberately NOT applied (lane C owned game.gd this cycle); they are written out as copy-pasteable code in the lane report and belong in a follow-up bead. Note for whoever takes it: extracting them does not make this gate redundant, because what it checks and no shared static can is the COMPOSITION -- the order payments happen in, which counter each increments, and whether a branch fires at all.

title: Eleven save tests fail on a scratch file no run in the suite wrote
description:
Found while running the full suite for plant-tower-defense-4n66. Eleven tests
failed on a clean checkout, and the same eleven passed after deleting one file in
`user://`. Nothing in the run named that file.

## THE SYMPTOM

`python tools/run_tests.py` on an unmodified tree, 2026-08-28:

    Total: 1035  |  Passed: 1024  |  Failed: 11  |  Skipped: 0

All eleven are save-shaped, across two files:

    test_a_record_is_kept_per_difficulty_and_not_shared
    test_a_well_formed_save_round_trips_exactly
    test_a_refused_save_is_not_immediately_overwritten
    test_a_run_with_milestones_round_trips_through_the_save
    test_the_colourblind_option_round_trips_through_the_save
    test_the_two_mutes_round_trip_through_the_save
    test_the_two_levels_round_trip_through_the_save
    test_pressing_a_dial_row_turns_the_volume_down_and_writes_it_down
    test_the_keys_screen_rebinds_a_verb_and_writes_it_down
    test_the_options_screen_shows_and_flips_every_persisted_flag
    test_rebound_keys_survive_a_save_and_load

Every one of them fails on the SAME line of the composed save -- the difficulty
line that `RunConfig.compose_difficulty_line` writes (game/run_config.gd:751):

    Expected ... d0 ... but got ... d2 campaign:gentle=3453 campaign:harsh=3453

## WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG

The suite points RunConfig's writes at a scratch path rather than the player's
real save -- `user://headless_scratch.save`, per the setup() block test_combat.gd
documents and `tools/save_persist_check.py` enforces. That redirects the WRITES.
It does not clear the file, and nothing else does either, so the scratch save is
cumulative across suite runs. This machine's copy read:

    v9 / 3453 / 0 / m5:campaign_cleared,... / cb0 sfx0 mus0 spd0 svol0 mvol0
    d2 campaign:gentle=3453 campaign:harsh=3453 / 0

`RunConfig` is an autoload; it loads that file at process start, so
`difficulty_high_scores` (game/run_config.gd:453, filled at :1511) is already
populated before the first test method runs. A test asserting a composed save
equals a literal ending `d0` then compares against a `d2` line it never wrote.

CONFIRMED, not inferred: deleting `user://headless_scratch.save` and re-running
the same selector took the round-trip subset from 3 failed to 0 failed with no
code change, and the subsequent full run was 1035/1035.

## WHY IT IS WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN SWEEPING

Three separate reasons, and the third is the one that matters:

  1. The suite's result depends on which tests a DIFFERENT run happened to
     execute weeks earlier. `test_economy.gd:829/882` stashes and restores
     `difficulty_high_scores` in memory precisely because it knows this is
     shared; the on-disk half has no such guard.
  2. It fails in ISOLATION as well as in the full suite, so the usual
     "run it alone to see if it is pollution" move reports pollution as a real
     defect. That cost most of the diagnosis time here.
  3. It reads as eleven broken save features. A new session running the gates
     for the first time sees a suite eleven failures deep in the save code and
     has no way to tell that from a regression -- which is exactly the wrong
     signal for the file whose own header argues that a bad parse destroying a
     score is unrecoverable.

## THE ASK

Make the scratch save's state at the start of a suite run a property of THAT
run, not of every run before it. Two shapes, and the choice is a real one:

  * delete `user://headless_scratch.save` in the setup that redirects to it, so
    every suite starts from no save. Cheapest, and matches what the manual fix
    did. Loses the ability to test "a save written by a previous process is read
    back", which `test_a_version_one_save_still_migrates_into_the_endless_slot`
    and friends do by writing the file themselves first -- check that none of
    them rely on a file they did not write.
  * give each run its own scratch path (plant-tower-defense-l6zo asks a related
    question about run_tests.py and save paths -- read it before choosing, the
    two may be one fix).

Either way, RESET THE IN-MEMORY FIELDS TOO. Redirecting the path does not undo
the autoload's load, and `difficulty_high_scores` is the field that bit here;
`milestones`, `key_bindings` and the preference flags are the same shape and are
loaded from the same parse.

## WHAT TO CHECK IT WITH

The check that would have caught this is not another assertion inside a save
test -- those all passed on a clean file. It is: write a poisoned
`headless_scratch.save` (a `d2` line, a milestone set, a rebound key), run the
suite, and require the same result as a run with no file at all. That is one
test that pins the whole class, and it fails today.

`tools/save_persist_check.py` already reasons about which test scripts can reach
`RunConfig._save()`; whether it should also require the redirect to CLEAR is a
question for that tool and may be the cheaper gate.

## WHAT THIS IS NOT

Not about `SAVE_VERSION` or the v9 format, which round-trips correctly. Not
about the real `user://highscore.save`, which was untouched and holds `d0`. Not
a flake: it is deterministic given the file, and deterministic the other way
without it.
acceptance_criteria: A suite run starting from a poisoned user://headless_scratch.save (a d2 difficulty line, a milestone set, a rebound key) produces the same result as one starting from no file at all; the redirect that points RunConfig at the scratch path also clears the in-memory fields the autoload loaded from it, difficulty_high_scores included; a test pins that property rather than a new assertion inside an existing save test; and run_tests.py exits 0 twice in a row from a dirty starting state.
close_reason:
Fixed at the autoload, not in the setup blocks, because the bead cited the wrong redirect. Lane A confirmed no setup() anywhere points at headless_scratch.save -- test_combat.gd redirects to its own test_combat_suite.save and deletes it in teardown, and all five suite setups do the same. RunConfig._ready() resolves onto the scratch path itself, so that is where the discard belongs.

game/run_config.gd gains reset_persisted_state(), discard_scratch_save() and adopt_save_path(env, name); _ready() now calls the last of those, which discards ONLY when the resolved path is HEADLESS_SAVE_PATH. Keyed on the resolved path rather than on 'are we headless': a caller that named PLANT_TD_SAVE_PATH has said what it wants and may have staged bytes there, and the player's real save is reached through the same branch. A test pins that half, and it is the half that could destroy data.

ACCEPTANCE OBSERVED IN THE PARENT PASS, not predicted. Poisoned user://headless_scratch.save with a d2 difficulty line, a milestone and a rebound key, then:

  run 1: exit 0, Total 1054 | Passed 1054 | Failed 0
         user:// on entry: 4 pre-existing file(s) -- ..., headless_scratch.save, highscore.save
  run 2: exit 0, Total 1054 | Passed 1054 | Failed 0
         user:// on entry: 3 pre-existing file(s) -- headless_scratch.save GONE

Three named checks each reached and passed: poisoned_scratch, named_save_path_survives, discard_throws_away.

A SECOND DEFECT the bead did not name, and the actual proximate cause of the eleven: test_economy's _with_scratch_save() reset NINE persisted fields with a comment numbering them, and a save carries ELEVEN. difficulty_high_scores and key_bindings were the two missing, and both compose into every byte-exact save assertion. A hand-list that drifted -- exactly what derive-the-list describes.

Deliberately NOT a per-run save path, and plant-tower-defense-l6zo stays open. That bead explicitly forbids changing the default: HEADLESS_SAVE_PATH staying one known file is what keeps a bare 'godot --headless --script res://tools/lint_project.gd' safe, and a per-run path would fix run_tests.py while leaving the linter and the import gate accumulating as before. What this does NOT fix is concurrency -- two headless processes still share the path, and a second one's discard now removes the first's file. user:// cannot be isolated at all (harness gh#28). That trade is l6zo's, and it is written into adopt_save_path's doc comment so the next reader finds it at the code.

title: The campaign swings from lost-on-wave-7 to never-lost on one policy rule, and difficulty changes neither
description:
Filed from the first automated playtests this project has run, and REWRITTEN once, because
the first version of this bead reported half the picture as the whole of it. Both halves
are below and the difference between them is the finding.

## WHAT IS REPRODUCIBLE FROM THIS REPO TODAY

    godot --headless --path . --script res://tools/playtest.gd -- \
        --difficulty gentle --difficulty standard --difficulty harsh --waves 22 \
        --out res://docs/playtest-runs.jsonl
    python tools/playtest_report.py

| run (shipped `RunSim.greedy_cover`, seed 1) | ended | wave | lives | earned |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| gentle | eaten | 7 | 0 of 15 | 477 |
| standard | eaten | 7 | 0 of 10 | 458 |
| harsh | eaten | 7 | 0 of 5 | 472 |

Three profiles, three identical verdicts: **dead on wave 7**, every life spent, within 19
seeds of the same income. `docs/playtest-runs.jsonl` is that record, committed.

## WHAT WAS MEASURED WITH A POLICY THIS REPO NO LONGER CARRIES

A second driver, written in parallel for the same bead and not merged, played the same
board and seed with a policy that keeps buying after the road is covered — when no
placement adds NEW coverage it plants for total coverage instead, thickening the lane.
That policy reached **victory on wave 22 having lost zero lives**, on all three
difficulties, ending on 91 plants and 3,453 seeds earned.

Recorded here as an observation and NOT as a repo fact, because nothing in the repo can
reproduce it today. That is the first thing the ask below fixes.

## THE TWO FINDINGS

**1. The gap between the two policies is the whole game, and neither end is designed for.**
The shipped policy stops planting the moment `covered.size()` reaches the road
(`run_sim.gd:667`), because every remaining placement scores `gain <= 0`. From wave 3 on it
holds at six plants, replaces what dies, banks the rest, and is overrun on wave 7. Thicken
instead and the campaign is not merely winnable, it is unlosable. A game whose outcome
swings from "dead a third of the way in" to "never lost a life" on one policy rule has an
enormous unmarked skill cliff in it, and nothing in the game tells a player which side of
it they are on.

**2. The difficulty selector is inert wherever it matters.** `Game.DIFFICULTIES`
(game.gd:54-76) differs only in `lives`, `prep_seconds` and `starting_seeds`, and the same
waves are sent to all three — gentle's blurb says so out loud, "the same waves"
(game.gd:57). Under the shipped policy all three die on wave 7. Under the thickening policy
all three win having spent no lives at all. Lives cannot separate runs that lose none;
prep time cannot separate a policy that spends the instant the window opens; starting seeds
shift the first plant by part of a wave. Harsh's blurb promises "Half the beds, half the
thinking time, one plant's grace" (game.gd:71) and delivers gentle's run in both
directions.

The one place the profiles DO separate is a player who plants nothing: `--no-sweep` and an
empty garden diverge cleanly, which is what a lives-based axis is good at. So the axis
works at the bottom of the skill range and nowhere else.

## WHAT THIS IS NOT

- **Not a claim about a human.** Both policies are machines; a person misclicks, hesitates,
  and reads the board. The claim is about what the RULES permit, not about difficulty as
  felt.
- **Not measured across seeds or boards.** One seed, the shipped road. The wave table is
  fixed but the mutation and packet rolls are not. Widen `--seeds` before treating any
  single number here as the number.
- **Not a policy bug.** `greedy_cover` is a reasonable reading of "cover the road", and its
  stopping rule is deliberate and commented. The finding is that the game rewards going
  past it by an enormous margin and never says so.

## THE ASK

1. **Give `RunSim` a thickening policy** beside `greedy_cover`, so both ends of the skill
   range are in the repo and this bead's second table becomes reproducible. This is the
   prerequisite for everything else here and is the smallest piece.
2. **Decide what the difficulty selector is for**, then make it bind. Three shapes, and
   this bead does not pick between them: vary what the waves SEND (which contradicts
   gentle's blurb as written); vary the ECONOMY so harsh cannot afford the thick garden;
   or accept it and rewrite the three blurbs, which currently promise a difference no run
   shows.
3. Whichever is chosen, the acceptance is the same: a re-swept `docs/playtest-runs.jsonl`
   shows the three profiles ending DIFFERENTLY under the same policy and seed, and a test
   in `test_dir` pins that separation so a later balance pass cannot erase it silently.

## WHAT TO WATCH

- `test_the_difficulty_profile_is_read_rather_than_restated`
  (`test/unit/test_playtest.gd:267`) already pins that `RunSim` reads the profile rather
  than copying it; a new axis has to be read somewhere or it will not reach the driver.
- `test_a_record_is_kept_per_difficulty_and_not_shared`
  (`test/unit/test_economy.gd:1131`) and `RunConfig.difficulty_high_scores` assume the
  profile set is `Game.DIFFICULTIES`; adding or renaming a profile moves the save format
  (`SAVE_VERSION`, run_config.gd:98).
- `Game.difficulty_profile()` falls back to standard for an unknown name (game.gd:87-90).
  That is deliberate and must stay: a save from a later build must not crash a run.
- The three profiles are read in exactly one place, `Game._ready` (game.gd:364-367). A key
  added to the table that nothing reads is the failure mode this bead is already about.
- `plant-tower-defense-t5yy.2` will assert endless depth. If difficulty is made to bind, it
  binds there too and that bead's numbers move.
acceptance_criteria: RunSim carries a thickening policy beside greedy_cover so both ends of the skill range are reproducible from the repo; and a re-swept docs/playtest-runs.jsonl shows gentle, standard and harsh ending DIFFERENTLY under the same policy and seed - a different wave reached, a different life count, or a different seed total, not merely a different starting life count that is never spent - with a test in test_dir pinning that separation. If the decision is instead to accept the current behaviour, the acceptance is that the three blurbs in Game.DIFFICULTIES no longer promise a difference no run shows, and a test pins the blurbs against the measurement.
close_reason:
Both halves shipped (merge of lane/i8oh: eb8aae5 policy, b343641 economy).

ITEM 1. RunSim carries a thickening policy beside greedy_cover, so both ends of the skill range are reproducible from this repo and the bead's second table stopped being an unreproducible observation. greedy_cover's first clause moved into best_placement(sim, only_new) with no behaviour change, proven by the greedy row returning byte-identical (458, wave 7).

ITEM 2, the decision the bead deliberately left open: THE ECONOMY. seed_yield joins each profile (gentle 1.5, standard 1.0, harsh 0.5), read on the path every run takes and routed through one new static Game.seeds_after_yield across four seed-moving branches -- Game and RunSim _on_pest_died and _on_plant_grew_seeds. The numbers are derived rather than tuned: gentle already ran 1.5 / 1.44 / 1.6 against standard on beds, prep and opening seeds, harsh 0.5 / 0.5 / 0.6, so the yield takes the ratio the profiles' own axes already agreed on, and a test asserts it sits in that band.

Rejected, with reasons: varying what the waves send (gentle's blurb says 'The same waves' out loud, and _raw_threat is asserted strictly rising to wave 300, so a strength multiplier must be re-verified against that property rather than added beside it); and accepting-and-rewriting-the-blurbs, which resolves nothing because the blurb key is read by NOTHING -- filed as plant-tower-defense-h5s3.

ITEM 3, the acceptance. Re-swept docs/playtest-runs.jsonl now carries both ends, 6 runs / 93 rows, playtest_report.py 0 findings. The three profiles end differently under the same policy and seed:

  thicken: gentle ceiling w22, 125 plants, 8837 earned
           standard ceiling w22, 116 plants, 5735 earned
           harsh   ceiling w22,  79 plants, 3328 earned

Before the change all three earned 5735 to the digit. Harsh now genuinely cannot afford the thick garden, which was the stated intent. Standard's rows are UNCHANGED in both policies -- that is the evidence this is a difficulty axis and not a rebalance. Under greedy all three still fall on wave 7, because that policy stops buying once the road is covered; the axis binds exactly where the player's decisions bind, and that is stated rather than hidden.

Four new tests in test/unit/test_playtest.gd pin the separation. First executed in the parent pass: suite 1061/1061, exit 0, 0 engine errors.

ONE THING THIS CLOSE DOES NOT COVER, and it is filed P1 rather than buried here: test_mirror_parity.gd pins DIFFICULTY_STANDARD, whose yield is exactly 1.0 and the identity. Pointed at gentle it FAILS -- seeds_earned, run_sim 61 vs game 37. Whether that is the gate's setup ordering or a real driver divergence is not established, and if it is the latter then the gentle and harsh rows above describe RunSim rather than the game. See the new bead.

title: A run driver that plays waves in sequence, carrying seeds, lives and plants forward
description:
From the report: "come up with a way for you to playtest this game". Everything else the
reporter asked for is a question this driver is the instrument for. Nothing here decides
whether a number is right; it produces the run the other three beads read.

## WHAT EXISTS NOW (verified 2026-08-28 by reading the cited lines)

`_over_promise_run(wave, corn_cells, chomp_cells, corn_level, roll_seed, max_frames,
road_corners := [])` at `test/unit/test_combat.gd:4525` is already a real playtest robot
for ONE wave. It steps the real `Board`, the real `Plant` subclasses, the real `Kernel`
and the real `WaveDirector` schedule by hand at `dt = 1.0 / 60.0`, awaiting nothing after
the host is up, so the engine runs no frame the loop did not drive. Tally built at
`test_combat.gd:4623`; loop exits at `test_combat.gd:4797` when
`spawned >= director.current_wave_pest_count()` and nothing is alive.

What it does not do, and what this bead is:

- **One wave.** `wave` is a parameter and the director is built for it. Nothing carries
  forward.
- **No economy.** Grepped lines 4525-4830 for `SeedBank`, `bank`, `cost`, `pay_for`: zero
  hits. The garden is two arrays of cells, planted free.
- **No damage carried forward.** Plants are constructed fresh at full health each call,
  so a wave that leaves the cobs at 20 percent is indistinguishable from one that does not.
- **No lives.** `Game.lives` (`game/game.gd:3193`) is where a run actually ends; the
  helper counts `escaped` and stops there.

The economy the driver has to reproduce, all three sources, verified in `game/game.gd`:
per-kill `bank.add_seeds(weather_seed_value(pest.seed_value))` at `game.gd:1101`, a
Sunflower payout through `_on_plant_grew_seeds` at `game.gd:2013`, and a swept husk at
`game.gd:2914`. Starting seeds and lives come from the difficulty profile
(`Game.DIFFICULTIES`, `game/game.gd:54`) - gentle/standard/harsh differ ONLY in `lives`,
`prep_seconds` and `starting_seeds`, and send the same waves.

## THE ASK

A deterministic, headless, hand-stepped driver that plays a WHOLE RUN and returns a
per-wave record. Concretely:

- Waves in sequence from 1, carrying seeds, lives, plant identities and plant HEALTH
  forward across the wave boundary.
- A `SeedBank` in the loop: plants are paid for, packets can be bought, income accrues
  from the three sources above.
- A **policy** seam - the thing that decides, between waves, what to buy and where to
  plant. It must be a parameter, not baked in, because bead 3 varies it and bead 2 runs
  it for hundreds of waves. Start with one honest policy (a greedy cover, ideally derived
  the way `test_combat.gd` already computes one, not a hand-listed cell list).
- Difficulty as a parameter, reading `Game.DIFFICULTIES` rather than restating its
  numbers.
- Endless as a parameter (`WaveDirector.endless`, set in the live game at
  `game/game.gd:387`).
- One record per wave: at minimum wave number, seeds at start and end, seeds earned,
  lives at start and end, escaped, killed, plants alive, plants lost, unlocked set,
  frames spent, and the `threat`/`threat_level` pair `Game.state()` already computes
  (`game/game.gd:3209-3210`). Bead 4 formats these; this bead only has to emit them.
- Same seed, same records, run twice.

Where it lives is a real decision the implementer should make explicitly: it is test
support, so `test_dir` is the default per CLAUDE.md, but bead 2 needs to run it for far
longer than a `/verify` should take. A `tools/` script that both a test and a human can
call is the likely shape. Say which and why in the commit.

## WHAT THIS WILL BREAK OR TRIP OVER

- **`tools/settle_read_check.py`** - `_T.instantiate_scene` pumps `UI_SETTLE_FRAMES`
  frames before returning, so any value read straight after the host is up is asserted
  against a frame count no test states. `_over_promise_run` carries the explicit
  `# settle-read-check: ok` marker at its single await (`test_combat.gd`, just above the
  `foreign` read); a second driver needs the same treatment or the checker fires.
- **`tools/group_leak_check.py` and the `godot-test-isolation` skill** - the driver reads
  the tree-global `pests` group, and the runner keeps stepping while a test awaits, so a
  sibling test's pests can be standing in the tree. `_over_promise_run` counts them into
  `foreign_pests` and every caller asserts it is zero. Inherit that, do not re-derive it.
- **`plant-tower-defense-x44s`** - "Find the unbounded test loop before it hangs a run
  instead of failing it". A whole-run loop is exactly that hazard. `max_frames` per wave
  is not enough; a run needs a wave ceiling too, and blowing either must FAIL with the
  wave number, never hang.
- **`tools/run_tests.py` vacuity** - a driver whose loop never entered returns a clean
  record. Assert the wave count the run actually played, and print it.
- **`tools/suite_reach_check.py`** - a new file naming a lot of the public surface moves
  `tools/suite_reach_baseline.json`. Expected; regenerate deliberately, do not fight it.
- **Runtime.** `/verify` re-runs `test_dir` on every change. Budget the campaign sweep;
  if it is too slow, the fast subset and the full run must be two selectors and the fast
  one must print what it skipped (`run_tests.py` takes selectors via `-- ...`).

## ACCEPTANCE

Code only. This bead deliberately asserts nothing about whether the game is balanced -
that is beads 2, 3 and 4, and mixing them makes a bead that closes on neither.
acceptance_criteria: A headless, hand-stepped driver plays a whole run from wave 1 with a SeedBank in the loop, carrying seeds, lives, plant identity and plant health across wave boundaries, taking difficulty, endless and a swappable policy as parameters read from Game.DIFFICULTIES and WaveDirector rather than restated; it returns one record per wave including wave, seeds start/end, seeds earned, lives start/end, killed, escaped, plants alive, plants lost, unlocked set, frames and threat level; the same seed produces identical records twice; the wave count actually played is asserted and printed as a denominator; a run that exceeds its wave or frame ceiling fails naming the wave rather than hanging; foreign pests from sibling tests are counted and asserted zero as _over_promise_run already does; and run_tests.py exits 0 with the assertion count risen.
close_reason:
RunSim (tools/run_sim.gd, class_name RunSim extends RefCounted) plays a whole run hand-stepped at dt=1/60 with a SeedBank in the loop; tools/playtest.gd is the human-callable half and test/unit/test_playtest.gd the suite half, both driving the same class.

WHERE IT LIVES, and why (the bead asked for this explicitly): tools/, not test_dir. /verify re-runs test_dir on every change and has to stay fast; bead t5yy.2 needs hundreds of endless waves. Two budgets, one driver. The tests keep to SHORT_RUN=3 waves; the sweeps run out of playtest.gd.

WHAT IT DOES. Waves in sequence from 1, carrying seeds, lives, plant identity and plant health forward. A prep window of the difficulty's own prep_seconds is STEPPED rather than skipped, so Plant._regrow and Sunflower._act happen between waves as they do in the real game -- and prep_seconds is one of the three things gentle/standard/harsh differ by, so skipping it would have made two of the three difficulties the same run. All three income sources are in the loop with a record column each: per-kill seeds (Game._on_pest_died), a Sunflower payout (_on_plant_grew_seeds) and a swept husk. Brood, cross-breeding sports, weather fire-rate/heal and Mint neighbour buffs are all mirrored. Difficulty reads Game.difficulty_profile; endless is WaveDirector.endless; the policy is a Callable re-asked between waves until it stops issuing orders.

A driver holding its own copy of either is the drift its own header warns about.

RECORD_KEYS is the one place the record schema is written down; test_every_record_carries_exactly_the_declared_keys checks it in BOTH directions, so beads t5yy.2/.3/.4 can iterate it instead of hand-listing.

CEILINGS (plant-tower-defense-x44s): a blown per-wave frame ceiling FAILS naming the wave, the spawned/expected counts and the still-walking count -- test_a_wave_that_cannot_clear_fails_naming_the_wave pins it with a 4-frame ceiling. A policy still issuing orders after policy_round_ceiling rounds fails the same way. foreign_pests and foreign_plants are counted at run start and asserted zero by every test, inheriting _over_promise_run's rule.

DETERMINISM: all three RNG streams are seeded -- WaveDirector, SeedBank, and the sim's own cross-breeding generator, which Game itself leaves randomized. test_the_same_seed_plays_the_same_run_twice compares every record key of every wave.

GATES: name_check 0 errors, import OK, lint 0/0, run_tests.py 1033 of 1033 passed, 19852 assertions, 8 suites (11 new tests here plus one in test_economy.gd closing the new static's suite_reach finding). Live: findings 0 across 4 of 5 checks; find-nodes confirmed place_plant builds CornCobbler/ChompFlower/Sunflower through the renamed static, and weather_seed_value returned 4 clear / 6 drought. Ledger row recorded warranted, worktree reach 1/2 with nothing unreached.

CAUGHT BY RUNNING IT: tools/playtest.gd did not compile under --headless --script -- Godot compiles the script before registering autoloads, so naming RunSim reached RunConfig and failed seven times over, played zero waves and exited 0. Fixed by loading run_sim.gd/game.gd after the first frames, and a run that plays no waves now exits 2. Logged in log-devtools.md.

ASSERTS NOTHING ABOUT BALANCE, by design -- that is beads t5yy.2, .3 and .4.

title: Two plants of a kind side by side can throw a mutant sport
description:
The player asked for it directly: when two plants stand next to each other there should be a rare chance they spawn a mutated version of that plant in an adjacent free square. The mutant looks similar but different, and its effect is slightly different and slightly better.

Nothing in the game reads the board as a GARDEN today. Plants are placed one at a time by the player (Game.place_plant, game/game.gd:1678) and the only plant-to-plant relationship that exists is Mint's neighbour_interval_scale (game/game.gd:3003). A cross-breed is the first thing on this board that produces a plant nobody bought.

Design constraints found by reading, not assumed:
- A mutant cannot be a new PlantCatalog entry. test_placement.gd:851 asserts PlantCatalog.ids().size() == PLANTS.size(), so every entry is in ORDER, and ORDER is the shop bar (Hud.plant_bar_layout) and the title screen's hand-placed slots (game/title_screen.gd:211). Nine more entries would put nine unbuyable plants in the shop.
- So a mutant is the SAME kind carrying a flag, the way a Pest carries a mutation rather than becoming a species.
- The roll must be pure and assertable with no tree: the pest mutation roll already is.
design: A PlantMutation table (kind -> mutant display name, tint, buff), a CrossBreeder that takes the plant dictionary plus the board plus an RNG and returns {kind, cell} or {}, Plant.is_mutant with the tint and a drawn marker, and each subclass reading its own buff.
acceptance_criteria: A pure roll function assertable headless; a mutant plant visibly distinct on the board; every plant kind has a mutant buff and the buff is strictly better; the pair scan only ever picks a buildable free cell adjacent to the pair; /verify green.
close_reason:
Shipped. CrossBreeder (the rule, pure), PlantMutation (the trait table), SportMark (the badge), Plant.is_sport, and a tick in Game._process. Every plant kind has a sport with a strictly-better one-respect buff, read through its own seam (fire_interval, chew_seconds_against, Sunflower.interval, slow_factor, shot_interval, Mint worth-two, sting_interval, Aloe.heal_for, bite_resistance).

Acceptance, item by item: pure roll assertable headless - yes, CrossBreeder is RefCounted and 8 of the 12 new tests need no Game. Visibly distinct - a violet tint on the sprite plus a badge node, confirmed on screen against a plain cob one cell away. Every kind has a buff and it is strictly better - test_every_plant_has_a_sport_and_every_sport_is_strictly_better walks PlantCatalog.ids(), not the table's own keys. The pair scan only picks a buildable free cell - test_a_sport_only_lands_where_that_kind_could_have_been_planted, plus a guard on the ENTRY POINT after live driving planted cobs in the road. Gates: name_check 0, import 0, lint 0/0, tests 1021 pass / 19616 assertions, check_all 23 of 24 clean (the one finding is pre-existing on -3r3n).

Three defects found, all recorded in the ledger row: the ungated sprout cell (found by James from the screen), the selection panel quoting StickySundew.SLOW_FACTOR as a constant, and the Sundew's order-dependent slow.
