title: Refresh the harness: 0.38.0 installed, 0.60.0 on the machine, 22 releases of gaps unverifiable
description:
SOURCE: cycle 168 step 4, and it is now the largest standing item in log-devtools.md.

`python tools/devtools.py harness-version --client` says:

  A newer harness (0.60.0) is already on this machine than this project runs
  (0.38.0). /scaffold-godot-harness refreshes it; gaps you log against 0.38.0
  may be fixed there already.

Twenty-two releases. The concrete cost this cycle: verifying `Hud.as_sentence` on
the running game meant routing the call through `run-method` on a node that
happens to carry the Hud script. That works for Hud. It would not work at all for
a `class_name X extends RefCounted` static utility, which no node carries — and
this repo has those. 0.60.0 ships `tools/eval.gd`, which 0.38.0 does not.

The wider problem is that this project has been filing gaps against a harness it
does not run. `gap_ledger` reports 77 currently open, and its own NOT COVERED line
says it "cannot tell you whether an open gap has since been FIXED upstream". Some
unknown fraction of those 77 are already closed in releases we do not have.

WHY THIS IS NOT JUST "run the command": /scaffold-godot-harness rewrites
CLAUDE.md's harness section in place and refreshes every template file. This repo
has local drift to check first — the /verify skill's own drift procedure exists for
exactly this and gives a bearing per file (ahead-unreleased vs stale install vs
local edits). Local edits must be ported into devtools_ext or upstreamed BEFORE
the refresh, or they are silently reverted.

ACCEPTANCE: the drift bearing is recorded for every template file before anything
is overwritten; any file whose hash matches no released version has its local edit
either ported to devtools_ext or filed upstream; the harness is refreshed; and
`harness-version --client` reports the machine version with no "newer harness"
line. If the refresh is judged too disruptive to take now, the closing note says so
and records the drift bearings, which is most of the value either way.
notes:
FOURTH CORROBORATION, from the same cycle that filed this.

tools/run_json_check.py reported three unknown keys in the ledger row cycle 168
wrote: 'tier', 'kind', 'item'. The /verify skill installed on this machine (0.60.0)
documents "tier" as required on every row -- "Record the tier on the row... Rows
before 0.50.0 dropped the key silently". This project runs 0.38.0, which is one of
those. It dropped all three without a word.

The row had also recorded as `verdict: unknown` with null `lint` and `tests`,
because the fields were written from the newer skill's vocabulary rather than the
installed ledger's. Corrected by hand and re-recorded as `pass`.

So the cost is not hypothetical and it is not only about missing features: FOLLOWING
THE DOCUMENTATION ON THIS MACHINE PRODUCES INVALID ROWS AGAINST THE HARNESS THIS
PROJECT RUNS. A house checker caught it this time. Nothing guarantees the next one.
close_reason:
THE DECISION: do NOT refresh yet. The bearings changed the answer, which is exactly why
this bead's acceptance put them before the overwrite.

THE DRIFT TABLE, all fourteen files against harness_history.json (57 versions):

  addons/godot_selftest/dev_tools.gd    LOCAL EDITS -- hash in NO released version
  tools/verify_ledger.py                LOCAL EDITS -- hash in NO released version
  the other twelve                      match 0.38.0 exactly -> cleanly stale

So the refresh is neither the one-command job it looked like nor a large piece of work.
Twelve files would simply be updated. Two would be silently reverted.

WHY THAT IS A STOP AND NOT A CAVEAT. dev_tools.gd's local edit is the exported-build
guard from upstream #58: without it the bus polls and entry_hook fires inside a PLAYER'S
build, so the hook that skips the title screen for /verify skips it for every itch.io
player. That is a shipped-game regression, and #58 is STILL OPEN -- the fix is absent
from the 0.60.0 templates, confirmed by grepping them for has_feature("template"),
--devtools-force and _has_cmdline_flag, which returns nothing.

Nothing would have caught it. The reverted file compiles, lints and passes the suite,
because it IS the upstream file. Correct code replaced by other correct code is a shape
no correctness gate objects to.

THE SECOND EDIT IS HALF UPSTREAMED, which is worth knowing before anyone ports it
wholesale: verify_ledger.py's worktree/union reach split IS in 0.60.0 (30 hits on both
sides). `unreachable_static` is not (0 upstream against 17 local). Only the second half
needs filing.

WHAT SHIPPED INSTEAD: tools/harness_patch_check.py, which fails the build when either
marker goes missing. Markers are CODE, never prose -- a sentence from the patch's comment
would be satisfied by pasting the comment back without the behaviour. Matched against
comment-blanked source for the same reason, and the checker mutation proves that stage
carries its weight: matching raw text turns the comment-only fixture case GREEN while
leaving the deleted case red. Fixture was four cases (present / deleted / file missing /
marker only in a comment -> 0, 1, 1, 1) and is deleted. Auto-discovered by check_all.py
via the NOT COVERED contract marker; 24 checkers, clean.

UPSTREAM #58 got a comment rather than a duplicate, carrying the 0.60.0 grep, the drift
table, the patch, and the general point: a scaffold that rewrites files in place with no
diff turns any unfixed upstream issue into a silent regression for every downstream that
patched it locally. The harness_history.json lookup that found this already ships with
the plugin, so a warning at refresh time is cheap.

WHAT NOW UNBLOCKS THE REFRESH, and it is short:
  1. #58 fixed upstream and released, OR the patch re-applied deliberately after the
     refresh with harness_patch_check green.
  2. unreachable_static filed and landed, or accepted as a local patch and guarded --
     it already is, by this checker.
Neither needs a decision from anyone; both are ordinary work.

NOT DONE, AND NAMED: the refresh itself. Everything above is evidence for a decision
that is now safe to take rather than the taking of it, and the bead's acceptance says
that is a legitimate close ("if the refresh is judged too disruptive to take now, the
closing note says so and records the drift bearings, which is most of the value either
way"). Filed as a follow-up so it is scheduled rather than remembered.

1012 tests, lint 0, name_check 0, check_all clean at 24 checkers.

title: A call to a method that does not exist passes every gate this project has
description:
SOURCE: cycle 159. I wrote `game.run_over()` in a new devtools verb, ran name_check, got
`errors: 0`, and only found it by reading the code. Then I checked how far the hole goes.

MEASURED WITH THREE MUTATIONS, each restored and verified:

  1. `game.no_such_method_at_all()` in devtools_ext/commands.gd, on a variable declared
     `var game: Game` -- name_check: errors 0. import_check: exit 0. lint_project.gd:
     0 errors, 0 warnings, exit 0.
  2. `n.no_such_engine_method_at_all()` on a variable declared `var n: Node`, so the
     receiver is an ENGINE type and the engine index was live (1036 classes) --
     name_check: errors 0.
  3. `board.no_such_board_method()` inside game/game.gd, on the `board` field, to rule
     out devtools_ext being outside a scan root -- lint: 0 errors. name_check: errors 0.

SO A CALL TO A METHOD THAT DOES NOT EXIST, ON A STATICALLY TYPED RECEIVER, IS INVISIBLE
TO EVERY GATE THIS PROJECT HAS. It fails at runtime, the first time that line runs -- and
for a devtools verb that is the first time anyone calls it, which is how cycle 159 found
it.

WHY THIS IS NOT ALREADY KNOWN. CLAUDE.md describes name_check as resolving "engine classes
and their MEMBERS", which reads as covering exactly this; mutation 2 says it does not.
name_check's own NOT COVERED line names type inference as its gap and says nothing about
member calls, so a careful reader is told the wrong thing twice. That is the
"a helper that answers a narrower question than its name suggests" failure
.claude/skills/house-static-checker warns about, in the tool the whole fan-out depends on.

THE LIKELY KNOB, and it needs checking rather than believing: Godot has a GDScript warning
for exactly this class -- unsafe method access -- controlled under
debug/gdscript/warnings/ in project settings. project.godot currently sets none of them.
If lint_project.gd turned the relevant warnings on for its compile pass, this class would
surface. EXPECT A LOT OF THEM AT FIRST: this codebase calls methods on Variant-typed
Dictionary values all over, and that is the same warning. So the work is as much about
finding the subset worth gating as about flipping a switch -- probably an allowlist, or
gating only on the warning for a receiver whose type IS known.

TWO SEPARATE DELIVERABLES, and the first is worth having even if the second is refused:
  * CORRECT THE DOCUMENTATION. CLAUDE.md's "and their members" and name_check's NOT
    COVERED line both need to say that a `x.method()` call site is not resolved. This is
    upstream in godot-selftest-harness and should be filed with skill-feedback-issue.
  * DECIDE WHETHER LINT CAN GATE IT, with the count of existing violations printed before
    deciding. If the number is enormous the honest answer may be a baseline, which is what
    the harness already does for UI findings.

ACCEPTANCE: the count of unsafe-method-access warnings in this codebase, printed; a
decision on gating with that number in hand; and the documentation corrected either way,
since a gate that does not cover something must not read as though it does.
close_reason: MEASURED, AND THE CHEAP FIX DOES NOT WORK -- which is the deliverable, since it saves the next attempt. Enabling gdscript/warnings/unsafe_method_access, unsafe_property_access and unsafe_call_argument in project.godot changes nothing: with all three on and a bogus method planted, lint_project.gd reported 0 errors and 0 warnings. The reason is in lint's own code rather than in the settings -- _check_scripts_compile (tools/lint_project.gd:693) is load()-based and inspects res == null and can_instantiate(), so a script carrying an unknown-method call loads and instantiates perfectly well and no warning ever reaches the exit code. Closing it properly would need the analyzer's warning OUTPUT captured rather than the load RESULT inspected, which is a change to how lint compiles rather than a flag. project.godot reverted. THE --check-only WORKAROUND IS ALSO UNAVAILABLE: every file in this project reports 'Compile Error: Identifier not found: RunConfig' and cascades into 'Failed to compile depended scripts', which is the autoload false-positive CLAUDE.md documents for --require-compile, hit here for the first time. WHAT SHIPPED: check_all.py's NOT COVERED now carries the SHAPE of the blind spot -- every gate here asks about NAMES and none asks whether a CALL is well-formed -- with the three mutations, the failed fix and the reason it failed, so nobody re-tries it. The documentation half against name_check and CLAUDE.md is harness-owned, so it went upstream as gh#64 rather than being patched locally where the next scaffold would revert it. FOLLOW-ON: plant-tower-defense-29ue is now partly done by this and should be re-read before being claimed.

title: Nothing tells the player they can click a destination to move a plant
description:
SOURCE: cycle 143, immediately after shipping the move (plant-tower-defense-h5w6).
PLAYER-FACING, and it is the half the move shipped without.

WHAT IS MISSING. A player can now move a plant by arming an uproot and clicking
an empty cell. Nothing tells them so.

What the game says while a move is available, in full:
  * The armed prompt, Hud.uproot_armed_message (game/hud.gd:3987) --
    "Click Uproot again to dig up your %s -- it will not grow back." Plus ONE of
    two clauses, never both, because the row's budget refused the build with 188
    px of overrun: either the forfeit ("Its %d upgrade seeds are not refunded")
    or the move tip ("Hover to compare a new spot"), and the tip is shown once
    per save and never again.
  * The destination preview, which draws what the plant would reach from
    wherever the pointer is.

So the sentence a player reads is about DIGGING UP, the one hint they ever get
says HOVER, and the thing they can actually do -- click -- is named nowhere. The
preview shows them a comparison and does not say the comparison is actionable.

WHY IT IS NOT JUST "ADD A SENTENCE". The message row is measurably full. That
budget is why the forfeit and the tip are already mutually exclusive, it is
enforced by check_budgets, and it has refused a build over this exact prompt
before. A third clause is not available at the price of the other two.

OPTIONS, and the row is not the only surface:
  (a) Reword the move tip from "Hover to compare a new spot" to something that
      names the click. Free -- it replaces a clause rather than adding one --
      and it is still once per save, so a player who has spent the hint never
      learns the verb.
  (b) Put it on the DESTINATION rather than in the row. The preview already
      draws at the hovered cell; a cost readout there ("Move: 8") names the
      action, the price and the place at once, costs the message row nothing,
      and is only visible while the player is doing the thing it describes.
      Note this collides with plant-tower-defense-3jjc, which is about that same
      preview drawing over ground the plant could never occupy -- the two want
      doing together.
  (c) The notebook, as a permanent card. Reaches a player who never sees the
      one-shot, reaches nobody at the moment they need it.

(b) is the recommendation, and (a) as well since it costs nothing.

CHECK THE PRICE IS THE ONE THE PLAYER WILL PAY. Plant.move_cost() is a quarter
of base cost plus upgrade spend, so it differs per plant AND per how far that
plant has climbed -- a number the player cannot predict from the shop. That is
an argument for showing it rather than for explaining the rule.

ACCEPTANCE: a player who has never moved a plant can discover that clicking a
destination moves it, without reading the source. If the route is (b), a headless
test asserts the readout's text and that it names Plant.move_cost() for the
selected plant rather than a recomputed second copy of the arithmetic; if (a),
the corpus and the row budget are re-measured, because Hud.message_corpus() must
price whatever the new wording is.
close_reason:
Fixed in 4855c2c, with options (a) and (b)-adapted from the description.

(a) The one-shot tip now says "Or click a spot to move it there." It said
"Hover to compare a new spot" -- true, and it described the PREVIEW rather than
the action, so the one sentence a player ever got about moving never mentioned
that moving was possible. Free: it replaces a clause rather than adding one.

(b) ADAPTED. The bead proposed a cost readout drawn at the hovered DESTINATION.
That turned out to be a bigger change than it reads: `grep draw_string game/*.gd`
returns nothing -- this game has never drawn text on the playfield, so the option
means inventing a font, a size and a style for a surface whose whole visual
language is shapes and colour. Put it in the selection panel's DETAIL slot
instead: same information, no new visual vocabulary, and it costs no panel
height because the label is two lines either way.

THE ARGUMENT THE BEAD WAS MISSING, and it is what makes the panel right rather
than merely convenient. The row does not just lack space; the forfeit clause and
the move tip are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE and the forfeit wins whenever there is
anything to forfeit. So an upgraded plant never sees the move tip -- and an
upgraded plant is exactly the one worth moving, since move_cost() prices a
quarter of the investment against a rebuy that forfeits all of it. The row is
full in precisely the wrong direction. Asserted in
test_the_armed_panel_says_the_move_and_its_price rather than left in prose.

(c) the notebook card was refused as the ROUTE and fixed anyway, because it was
WRONG: it said "Confirming still only uproots", which stopped being true in
cycle 143. A hint card is a permanent reference, so it was teaching a rule the
game no longer follows. Caught by
test_the_hint_cards_agree_with_the_tips_the_message_row_posts.

The panel budget is measured twice -- corpus with the hint and corpus with every
line carrying it removed -- and asserted to buy no rows and no pixels. The
widest selection line already wrapped to three rows before this feature, which
is pre-existing and not this bead's to change; that is why the check is
relative rather than absolute.

NOT DONE, and it belongs to plant-tower-defense-3jjc rather than here: the
destination preview still paints a full reach ring on ground commit_move
refuses. Now that the panel names the click and its price, a player is more
likely to act on that preview, so 3jjc's note about having stopped being
cosmetic stands.

title: Lose the 4-second window and the move click silently buys a second plant instead
description:
SOURCE: cycle 143's runtime pass, found by losing the window to slow bridge
round-trips -- which is exactly what a hesitating player is. PLAYER-FACING, and
the code is NOT wrong.

WHAT HAPPENS. Game.UPROOT_CONFIRM_SECONDS (game/game.gd:24) is 4.0. Arm an
uproot, wait longer than that, then click an empty cell to move the plant: the
window has closed, `uproot_armed()` is false, the new branch in `_click_at`
correctly declines, and the click falls through to `place_plant` -- so the
player BUYS A SECOND PLANT at full price, level 1, silently. No message, no
refusal, and the seed counter moves in the wrong direction by more than the move
would have cost.

Observed live in cycle 143: armed a level-2 cob, spent four seconds reading, and
ended with two plants -- the original still at (1,0) and a fresh level-1 at
(3,0). The identical click with the tree paused and the window genuinely open
moved the plant and charged 8.

WHY THE CODE IS NOT THE BUG. `_click_at`'s move branch is gated on
`uproot_armed()`, which is right: a move must not happen outside the window the
player armed. Every guard behaves as designed. What changed is what the window
is FOR.

THE ACTUAL PROBLEM, stated once: arming now serves two purposes on one clock.
  * CONFIRMING a destructive act -- "are you sure" -- which wants to be SHORT.
    A long confirm window is a loaded gun left on the table, and 4.0 was tuned
    for exactly this (see UPROOT_CONFIRM_SECONDS' own header and
    plant-tower-defense-fjqp, which put the countdown arc on the bed).
  * CHOOSING A DESTINATION -- which wants to be LONG. The move tip
    (Hud.uproot_armed_message, "Hover to compare a new spot") literally asks the
    player to stop and compare, and comparing takes longer than four seconds on
    a board with eight plant kinds and a road to read.

Those pull opposite ways and cycle 143 gave the second job to a clock sized for
the first.

OPTIONS, none obviously right, which is why this is a decision bead:
  (a) Extend the window. Cheapest, and it weakens the confirm exactly as much as
      it helps the move.
  (b) Two clocks: a short confirm and a longer move window that the first
      hover starts. More faithful, more state.
  (c) Do not let the window close while the pointer is over a legal destination.
      The player is visibly still deciding; the arc pausing is honest feedback.
  (d) Leave the clock alone and make the EXPIRY visible -- refuse the fall-
      through purchase when a move was plainly what was meant (an armed plant
      was selected within the last N seconds) and say "the move window closed"
      instead of buying. Cheapest correct-feeling fix; does not touch the
      confirm at all.

(d) plus (c) is the recommendation: nothing about the destructive confirm
changes, and the failure stops being silent.

WHATEVER IS CHOSEN, THE SILENT PURCHASE MUST GO. A click that the player
believes is a move and the game treats as a purchase is the worst shape a
refusal can take -- it spends seeds, adds a plant they did not want, and says
nothing.

ACCEPTANCE: a click intended as a move, made after the window closes, either
moves the plant or refuses out loud -- it never silently buys. A headless test
drives it: arm, advance past UPROOT_CONFIRM_SECONDS via the same tick the game
uses, click an empty cell, assert the plant count did not change. Record which
option was taken and why the others were refused.
close_reason:
Fixed in 76cb648, and with options (c) and (d) from the description rather than
either alone.

(c) THE CLOCK HOLDS while the pointer is on a legal destination for the armed
plant -- Game.can_move_to(), split out of commit_move()'s ground checks so the
clock and the click cannot disagree about what counts as a destination. The
window only outlives four seconds while the player is demonstrably mid-decision
and resumes the instant they look away, so the destructive confirm is not
weakened at all: it still closes in four seconds for anyone not actively
choosing.

(d) A 1.5s GRACE after it lapses, in which a click on empty ground refuses out
loud (Hud.move_window_closed_tip) instead of buying. Consumed on the first click
either way -- a grace that survived its own refusal would refuse the player's
next genuine purchase and leave them unable to buy without waiting it out. Sized
to catch the click already in flight, NOT to be a second move window; that
distinction is written into the constant's header because a future cycle will be
tempted to lengthen it.

Options (a) and (b) were refused: (a) extending the window weakens the confirm
by exactly as much as it helps the move, and (c) gets the benefit without the
cost; (b) two clocks is more faithful and more state than the problem needs now
that the hold makes the single clock behave correctly.

ONE CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S OWN TEXT: it says the expiry is silent. It is not
-- _tick_uproot_confirm already posted "Uproot cancelled." on lapse. What was
silent was the PURCHASE that followed, which is the thing that spends seeds and
puts a plant where nobody asked. That narrowed the fix usefully: the expiry
needed no new announcement, the click did.

Two tests. The lapse one asserts the PLANT COUNT first and the message second --
a message-only test would pass against an implementation that says the right
thing and buys anyway. Proved by mutation: removing both halves fails both, the
second reporting "the late click bought nothing: Expected 1 but got 2", which is
verbatim the defect observed live in cycle 143.

Verified live, because the hold's real risk was that _hover_cell is set by hand
in the test and by an event in the game: driven through the real cursor path,
_uproot_left held at exactly 4.0 across five reads spanning seconds, then
resumed 3.4, 3.1, 2.8 when the pointer left.

NOT verified, and recorded as a blocked check so the ledger row says partial:
the event-delivery layer. The bridge's mouse_move accepts only `relative`, and
Godot's relative motion carries no position, so nothing reading
InputEventMouseMotion.position can be driven at runtime. Filed as a harness gap.

title: Nothing checks that a bead id cited in prose names a real bead
description:
SOURCE: cycle 142, caught by accident. I wrote "see plant-tower-defense-9dq7" (bead-ref-check: ok - quoted on purpose; it IS the finding)

into a bead description as a cross-reference and only noticed it was invented

because I went to look the id up for an unrelated reason. Nothing in this repo

would have caught it.



THE HOLE. Bead ids are cross-referenced constantly -- in kanban.md entries, in

bead descriptions, in close reasons, in commit messages, in log-devtools.md, in

the cycle skill's own prose. They look like this: plant-tower-defense-XXXX. Two

checkers already read that prose and neither asks whether the id EXISTS:

  * citation_check.py resolves `file:line` citations. A bead id is not one.

  * bead_prose_check.py catches prose the SHELL ate. An invented id survives a

    shell perfectly.



So a dangling bead reference reads exactly like a real one, and it is worse than

a dangling file citation: a wrong file:line lands on a line the reader can see

is wrong, while a wrong bead id sends them to `bd show` and a "not found" they

will assume is their own typo. Cross-references between beads are how this

project's evidence is chained -- -nalv notes onto -2174, -5w4v points at -t7t1,

s1o8's children point at each other -- so the chain is exactly the thing that

must not have invented links in it.



THE ASK: a stdlib-only checker in tools/, following

.claude/skills/house-static-checker/SKILL.md, that extracts every

`plant-tower-defense-[a-z0-9.]+` token from the prose sources and reports the

ones that name no issue.



SOURCES TO READ (name them in the printed denominator, because a checker that

reads two of five files and reports clean is the failure this repo prints

denominators to prevent): kanban.md, cycle-log.md, log-devtools.md, the bead

export at .beads/issues.jsonl (descriptions AND close reasons), and

.claude/skills/**/*.md.



THE SET TO CHECK AGAINST is .beads/issues.jsonl, which is a PASSIVE EXPORT --

see plant-tower-defense-4dxf, which is about exactly this hazard in the other

two bead-reading checkers. An id filed this session and not yet exported would

be reported as dangling. So this checker MUST print the export-vs-tracker

denominator that -4dxf asks for, or it will produce false findings on the

commonest workflow there is: file a bead, cite it in the same cycle.



Do the two together if they land in the same cycle; they are the same

denominator.



WATCH THE SELF-REFERENCE TRAP: this bead's own description contains

plant-tower-defense-9dq7 nowhere -- and that claim was FALSE when written, by three lines. (bead-ref-check: ok - same, quoted deliberately.) The checker built in cycle 146 found exactly this: a sentence asserting an absence, containing the thing it denied. Writing the invented id out as

an example would make the checker's first run fail on the bead that asked for

it, which is the same shape as the bare `:NN` trap in

.claude/skills/kanban-idea-pass/SKILL.md rule 1. A checker needs a WAIVER

comment form for prose that legitimately names a non-existent id, and the fixture

that proves the checker can fail is where that gets exercised.



ACCEPTANCE: `python tools/bead_ref_check.py` prints "N reference(s) across M

source(s), K resolved, J finding(s)" plus the export-vs-tracker pair, exits 0/1/2

per the house contract, carries a NOT COVERED line, has a fixture proving it can

fail, and is picked up automatically by tools/check_all.py (which discovers any

tools/*.py declaring the contract line).
close_reason:
Built as tools/bead_ref_check.py in 590dc49, and it found a live one on its first
run.

MEASURED FIRST, per house-static-checker's rule that the procedure can end in NOT
building a tool: markdown 83 refs / 0 dangling, bead prose 74 refs / 1 distinct
dangling twice. That one is what earned it --
"plant-tower-defense-9dq7" (bead-ref-check: ok - the finding, quoted) was invented
in cycle 142, corrected in the same cycle, and was still present in cycle 146. The
correction was believed and did not hold, which is the whole argument: this class
is not just silent, it survives being fixed.

THE SOURCES AND THE SECOND DENOMINATOR the acceptance asked for. Sources are
kanban.md, cycle-log.md, log-devtools.md, .claude/skills/**/*.md and the bead
export's description / close_reason / design / notes -- 27 markdown files plus 520
bead rows, all named in the printed line. The second number is the extraction
ratio, and it is the citation_check lesson with its own measurement: markdown is
rendered and rewards backticks (30 of 83), bead prose renders nowhere and rewards
nothing (0 of 74). Both forms are matched, and the ratio prints every run so a
future reader can see the tool is not reading a fraction of its corpus.

THE EXPORT-LAG HAZARD the acceptance also asked for: handled in the NOT COVERED
line rather than by shelling out to bd, which would cost stdlib-only and
parallel-safety. The row count is printed and the line says plainly that an id
filed since the last export reads as dangling, pointing at
plant-tower-defense-4dxf.

THE SELF-REFERENCE TRAP this bead warned about: it fell into it. This description
quoted the invented id twice, including in the sentence claiming it appeared
"nowhere, deliberately". That is the best fixture case the tool could have had --
a sentence asserting an absence containing the thing it denied -- and both quotes
are now waived rather than deleted, since a bead reporting an invented id must be
able to quote one. The waiver is line-scoped and the fixture proves it by putting
one on the wrong line.

Three mutations, kept in the docstring. Dropping the waiver scan goes red 5 -> 6.
Replacing the id set with one junk id goes red 5 -> 163 -- deliberately not an
EMPTY set, which trips the could-not-run guard and exits 2, proving nothing. And
a `ref == own` guard I had written SURVIVED, which turned out to be a finding
about the code: a bead's own id is in the export by definition, so the guard
could never fire where the membership test did not. Deleted, invariant recorded.

Registers itself: check_all went 19 to 20 with no edit to it.

title: A standing playtest gate: every board x difficulty, re-run on every balance change
description:
The reporter's own words: "Ensure it's all thoroughly playtested, each and every new
level — with a variety of different level layouts, etc. This testing should happen in
the future when balancing or anything relevant is adjusted."

The second sentence is the whole bead. A playtest done once is a transcript. This
asks for a gate.

## THE MECHANISM THAT ALREADY EXISTS

`_over_promise_run(wave, corn_cells, chomp_cells, corn_level, roll_seed, max_frames)`
(test/unit/test_combat.gd:4504) is a headless, hand-stepped, fully deterministic
simulation of one wave over the **real** `Board`, the real `Plant` subclasses, the
real `Kernel` and the real `WaveDirector` schedule, sampled every physics frame at a
fixed dt. Its docstring: "Nothing here awaits after the host is up, so the engine
runs no physics frame this loop did not drive." It returns a tally including
`spawned`, `killed`, `escaped`, `escaped_engaged`, `escaped_unengaged`,
`covered_cells`, `road_cells` and a schedule signature.

That is a playtest robot. It is currently pointed at one board, one garden shape and
one question (does the coverage cue over-promise). This bead points it at the corpus.

Two things it does NOT do yet, both required here:

- `var board := Board.new()` at test_combat.gd:4507 — hardcoded. Bead 1 has to make
  it take a road.
- It runs **one wave**, seeded, from a given garden. A campaign verdict needs waves
  in sequence carrying seeds, lives and plant state forward. That is the new code in
  this bead.
- It reads `get_tree().get_nodes_in_group("pests")` and counts foreigners, because
  the runner keeps stepping while a test awaits (test_combat.gd:4512-4518). Any new
  driver inherits that hazard — see the `godot-test-isolation` skill before writing
  a second one.

## THE ASK

A standing headless gate in `test_dir` that plays every (board x difficulty)
combination and asserts each is a real game:

- **Losable**: an empty or deliberately bad garden loses. A board where doing
  nothing survives is not a level.
- **Winnable**: a reasonable garden — derived, e.g. the greedy cover
  `test_combat.gd` already computes, not hand-listed — clears the campaign without
  running out of lives.
- **Not trivial**: the reasonable garden does not clear with zero lives lost and
  seeds to spare on every board, or the difficulty label is decoration.
- **Economy closes**: seed income over the run affords the garden it needs. A board
  whose minimum garden costs more than the run ever earns is unwinnable in a way no
  coverage test can see.
- **Determinism**: same seed, same tally, run twice.

## WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE BEAD

Filed apart from beads 1-4 deliberately. The report asks for a code change *and* for
evidence about it; a bead carrying both closes on neither, and this project has
already had a bead sit ready for twelve cycles because its code half shipped and its
evidence half needed a running game. The code is beads 1-4. This is the audit, and
it is expected to land after them.

It goes in `test_dir` and nowhere else. That is the mechanism by which "test again
when balancing is adjusted" actually happens: `/verify` re-runs everything in
`test_dir` on every subsequent change, so the balance pass three months from now
fails this gate without anyone remembering it exists. The same checks written into a
scratch script or a transcript are worth one run.

## WHAT TO WATCH

- **Runtime.** N boards x M difficulties x 22 waves of hand-stepped physics is the
  cost. Budget it; if a full sweep is too slow for every `/verify`, the fast subset
  and the full sweep must be two selectors, and the fast one must print what it
  skipped. `run_tests.py` supports selectors via `-- ...` passthrough.
- **Vacuity.** A loop over an empty corpus prints `[VACUOUS]` and fails, which is
  correct — but a loop over one board that silently drops the rest does not. Assert
  the corpus size the sweep actually covered, and print it as a denominator.
- **`run_tests.py`, never the bare `run_tests.gd`.** A test that aborts mid-method
  after one real assertion is reported `[PASS]` by the .gd runner.
- The verdict belongs in `.devtools/verify-runs.jsonl` with a real `reach` — a pass
  on an unreached file is a statement about the diff, not the game.

## ACCEPTANCE

- One test file (or a section of `test_selftest.gd`) that sweeps every corpus board
  against every difficulty and asserts losable / winnable / non-trivial / economy /
  determinism, with the swept count printed and asserted.
- A deliberately unwinnable synthetic board makes the gate fail. Proving it can fail
  is the acceptance; the corpus passing is not.
- `python tools/run_tests.py` exit 0, with the assertion count risen by the sweep.
- A line in `docs/` or `CLAUDE.md` naming this gate as the thing to run after any
  balance edit — so the next person tuning `WAVES` finds it before it finds them.
acceptance_criteria: A sweep in test_dir plays every corpus board against every difficulty and asserts losable, winnable, non-trivial, economy-closes and deterministic, printing and asserting the swept count; a deliberately unwinnable synthetic board makes the gate fail (proving it can fail is the acceptance, not the corpus passing); run_tests.py exits 0 with the assertion count risen; a line in docs or CLAUDE.md names this gate as the thing to run after any balance edit.
notes:

1. STALE PREMISE. This description says `var board := Board.new()` at
`test_combat.gd:4507` is hardcoded and "Bead 1 has to make it take a road". That shipped.
`_over_promise_run` now takes `road_corners: Array[Vector2i] = []`
(`test/unit/test_combat.gd:4525`) and returns `road_refusal` for an illegal road
(`test_combat.gd:4534`). Only the second bullet - waves in sequence carrying seeds, lives

2. That second bullet is now owned by `plant-tower-defense-t5yy.1`, so it can be built

that this bead is blocked on. When t5yy.1 lands, THIS bead becomes "sweep that driver

3. Scope reminder: this bead is campaign-only ("clears the campaign") and pass/fail.

title: The bar across the lane is taught by nothing, in a game that teaches its other rules
description:
SOURCE: user report, cycle 138, with a screenshot (image.png). PLAYER-FACING.
"what are all these artifacts in the lanes? If they mean something, it is not
obvious."

WHAT THE ARTEFACTS ACTUALLY ARE, identified by bisecting a live board with
`screenshot --hide` rather than by reading the draw calls:
 - the small yellow ring on a road cell is SoleCoverMarks (sole_cover_marks.gd:225)
 - the dark bar drawn ACROSS the lane is Board's deferred-road cue
   (game/board.gd:1072 `_redraw_deferred_road`, shipped by
   plant-tower-defense-a6rf in cycle 112): "every gun covering this cell will
   look past it"
Hiding the plant's SoleCoverMarks node left the bars standing, which is how the
two were told apart; hiding HuskLayer and WeatherOverlay changed neither.

CONFIRMED, and this is the bead: NOTHING IN THE GAME NAMES THE BAR.
 - `CueLegend.ROWS` (game/cue_legend.gd:172) has six rows -- subject, reach,
   clock, remark, gain, armed. The bar is not among them and neither is the ring.
 - `game/OVERLAY_GRAMMAR.md`'s shape table does not contain the deferred bar AT
   ALL. It says it is "derived from the draw calls rather than remembered", and
   cue_legend.gd:67 records the derivation as a grep for
   `draw_arc(|draw_circle(|draw_line(|draw_rect(`. Both board cues are Line2D
   NODES, not draw calls, so the derivation is structurally blind to them --
   `board.gd` deliberately chose Line2D so a headless test could read `points`.
 - `RunConfig.HINTS` (game/run_config.gd:225) holds four one-shots: move,
   flight, upgrade, road. None is about the bar.

So a cue that appears on the board with NO player action, in a colour nothing
else on the road uses, is taught by no surface in the game and documented in no
file for developers either.

WHY A HINT AND NOT A LEGEND ROW: the legend page is measurably full.
OVERLAY_GRAMMAR.md's own cycle-109 note prices a seventh row at 340px against
the 300px the page has, and `CueLegend.rows_that_fit` is the function that says
so. The one-shot hint system is the surface this game already uses for "a rule
the board does not state" -- and it has a route back, since every hint id is
required to carry a notebook card by
test_every_hint_has_a_notebook_card.

The trigger is honest and player-caused: the bars appear the moment
`Game._refresh_deferred_road` (game/game.gd:1377) first marks a cell, which
happens when the player's guns start queueing behind each other. That is the
exact moment the user hit.

PLAN:
 1. `RunConfig.HINT_DEFERRED_ROAD` + entry in `HINTS`.
 2. `Hud.defer_tip()`, added to `message_corpus()` so the row budget prices it.
 3. A `HINT_CARDS` entry, or test_every_hint_has_a_notebook_card fails.
 4. Spend it in `_refresh_deferred_road` on `show_message`'s RETURN value, the
    way `_offer_road_hint` does, so a dropped line leaves the hint owed.

ACCEPTANCE: with the hint unspent, the first refresh that marks any deferred
cell posts a line naming what the bar means; a headless test drives that and
asserts both the posting and that a second refresh does not repost. The
message-corpus budget still passes with the new producer priced.
close_reason:
Cycle 138, commit 14c1cb9. Fifth one-shot: RunConfig.HINT_DEFERRED_ROAD,
Hud.defer_tip() priced in the message corpus, a HINT_CARDS entry for the route
back, spent from Game._offer_defer_hint.

Two derived gates rather than tuned ones. DEFER_HINT_MIN_GUNS = 2, because a
lone gun defers every cell it covers except the furthest along on any board, so
the bars at one plant are not a fact about this garden and the counter-play is
unbuyable. And Hud.row_is_quiet() before offering, because the caller is
level-triggered -- the first cut without it was caught by
test_a_realistic_run_refuses_no_messages_and_evicts_none at refused=11 over
three waves.

Two new tests appended to test_selftest.gd. Verified live: the sentence renders
whole on the real 876px row, on screen with five bars. findings 0 across 4 of 5,
lint 0/0, 963 tests, check_all 19/19.

CORRECTION to this bead's own description: it said OVERLAY_GRAMMAR.md is
missing a ROW for the deferred bar. It is not. placement_preview.gd's a6rf
block has a "WHY NO NEW GRAMMAR ROW" section filing it under the existing
"straight line through a box = a STATE" row, deliberately, because adding a row
would fail test_the_legend_names_as_many_shapes_as_the_grammar_documents. What
the doc is missing is the INSTANCE -- its Instances column lists only the two
placement_preview draw calls and neither board-drawn Line2D. That is a smaller
and different claim, and it is filed separately.

title: A red ERROR on every launch, from the entry hook changing scene mid-add
description:
SOURCE: user report, cycle 138. Every windowed launch prints an ERROR to stderr.

REPRODUCED: `python tools/devtools.py launch` writes exactly one error to
.devtools/launch_stderr.log:

    ERROR: Parent node is busy adding/removing children, `remove_child()` can't be
    called at this time.
       at: remove_child (scene/main/node.cpp:1750)
       GDScript backtrace (most recent call first):
           [0] _start_campaign (res://game/title_screen.gd:1027)
           [1] skip_to_game (res://game/title_screen.gd:1038)
           [2] _resolve_and_fire_hook (res://addons/godot_selftest/dev_tools.gd:4962)
           [3] _start_entry_hook (res://addons/godot_selftest/dev_tools.gd:4943)
           [4] _ready (res://addons/godot_selftest/dev_tools.gd:301)

CONFIRMED, not a memory:
 - title_screen.gd:1027 is `get_tree().change_scene_to_file(GAME_SCENE)` inside
   `_start_campaign()`; :1038 is `skip_to_game()` calling it.
 - The backtrace bottoms out in `_ready`, so the hook fires SYNCHRONOUSLY inside
   DevTools._ready() -- while the root Window is still adding the main scene's
   subtree, which is what `data.blocked > 0` means.
 - The scene change still lands: /root has DevTools, RunConfig, MusicHost, Game,
   SfxPool afterwards and no leftover TitleScreen.
 - The on-demand path is CLEAN. `fire-entry-point campaign` calls the same
   `skip_to_game()` through `_cmd_fire_entry_point` and writes nothing new to
   stderr. So this is launch timing, not the method.

WHY IT MATTERS even though the game runs: /verify and the harness both read
stderr, and a red ERROR on every single launch is the thing that teaches a
reader to skip that file. It also sits at the top of the log the user reads
when something real goes wrong.

FIX: defer the scene change on the harness path only --
`_start_campaign.call_deferred()` inside `skip_to_game()`. The player path
(`_start_campaign` from a button `pressed`) is untouched, and
`_cmd_fire_entry_point`'s own `scene_changed` field reports the PRE-switch to
title.tscn, so it does not read this call's result and cannot regress.

ACCEPTANCE: `python tools/devtools.py launch` leaves
.devtools/launch_stderr.log empty, `ping` still reports `entry_hook: fired`,
and /root/Game is the live scene.
close_reason:
Cycle 138, commit 8289b3c. skip_to_game() now defers _start_campaign, so the
harness entry hook no longer calls change_scene_to_file mid-add.
launch_stderr.log is 0 bytes on a fresh launch (was one ERROR with a five-frame
backtrace); ping still reports entry_hook fired; /root/Game live. lint 0/0,
961 tests / 18579 assertions, check_all 19/19 -- all green before the fix too,
which is why this needed a launch to see at all.

title: Weather has never had a banner a player could see; decide whether it gets a beat
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md "New in cycle 137", first entry. Found by the banner-painter lane
(-jk4a) opening game.gd rather than trusting its own bead's header. PLAYER-FACING, and
the strongest finding of the cycle.

THE FACT. Game._on_wave_started calls _apply_weather at game/game.gd:459, which reaches
hud.show_weather(next) at game/game.gd:453. Ten lines later, in the same function and
the same call stack, game/game.gd:465 calls hud.announce_wave(...). Before cycle 137
both wrote the banner's two Labels unconditionally, so the weather headline was
overwritten zero frames after it was set. show_weather is called from NOWHERE ELSE --
grepped, that one site is the whole of it. So the weather banner has never once been
visible to a player.

WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT. show_weather's own header already said "this one is the
overwritten half", so the code knew. What no gate could see is that the REASON lived in
another file's statement order: a test can call show_weather directly and watch the
Label change, and it does.

WHAT CYCLE 137 DID AND DID NOT DO. The banner painter makes the weather claim LOSE BY
RULE (banner_claim_wins ranks both wave beats above weather) rather than be written and
immediately stomped. Same pixels, honest mechanism, no behaviour change for a player.
It deliberately did NOT give the weather a beat -- that is this bead.

WHY IT IS WORTH A BEAT. Weather is not cosmetic. WaveDirector.fire_interval_scale_for
changes how fast every firing plant shoots, through Plant.composed_interval and its
three callers; WaveDirector.heal_fraction_for heals every plant a flat amount of health
each weather wave. The only things that announce any of it are the status-row weather
tag and the full-screen tint.

OPTIONS, none obviously right:
  (a) SEQUENCE the two beats -- weather headline, then the wave headline on a delay.
      Costs the wave beat its immediacy at the exact moment a player is reading the
      board.
  (b) A SURFACE OF ITS OWN for weather. -bn2c ("give the top bar a second row") is the
      open bead that would host it, and -jk4a measured 236px of clearance above the
      banner.
  (c) FOLD the weather word into the wave headline so one beat carries both. Cheapest,
      and the message-row width budgets are the constraint -- Game.BUDGET_FLOOR.

ACCEPTANCE: a decision recorded with its reason, and if (a) or (c), the code. If (b),
this blocks on -bn2c and should say so rather than sitting ready.
close_reason:
DECIDED: NO new beat. Weather already has one, in a better place than the banner, and
confirming that produced a bigger finding than the bead contained.

WHERE WEATHER IS TAUGHT. Hud.next_wave_note puts "rain - beds mend 25%" and "drought -
pests pay 150%" on the message row as the standing idle note, BEFORE the wave commits,
while the player still has the seeds to act on it. That is what -kmjp and -4c1l argued
for explicitly. The banner fires from Game._on_wave_started, after the seeds are gone.
So the banner was never weather's home, and losing there costs weather nothing it was
doing. Option (b), a top-bar surface, was already ruled out by MEASUREMENT as -saaw
(302px base string in a 312px box; even a bare "*" needs 317). Option (a), sequencing
the beats, would buy a surface that arrives after the decision it informs.

THE FINDING. Five comments across three files described weather as taught by three
surfaces. TWO OF THE THREE DID NOT EXIST.

  * The banner: overwritten by announce_wave ten lines later in the same call stack,
    every wave, for its whole life.
  * "A status row carrying the state after the banner is gone (weather_note)": never
    built. It was the -saaw proposal, which was refused on measurement, and four
    comments then cited it as shipped. weather_note() is the banner's own subtitle,
    consumed at exactly one call site three lines below its declaration.

The one that matters most is notebook_screen.gd's, because it is an ARGUMENT rather
than a description -- it justifies weather having no notebook page on the grounds that
three surfaces already teach it. The conclusion survives on the prep note and the
full-screen WeatherOverlay, but it now rests on one fewer surface than it was written
against, and the comment says so and says to re-read it first if anything ever proposes
reducing weather's teaching further.

wave_director.gd's was a third shape again: a present-tense sentence describing a
defect that had since been fixed. It said next_wave_note "appends a bare 'rain'"; it
appends the percentage, derived from WEATHER_RAIN_HEAL_FRACTION. Marked as history, and
noted that its own objection understated the case -- the surface was not late, it was
never there.

SHIPPED: four comment corrections, each saying what the mistake was rather than quietly
trimming it, plus two tests pinning the claim in the direction that failed. Prose
drifted and no gate could see it, and a test asserting "weather_note returns a string"
passes against every wrong state above. The tests assert that the prep note names each
weather AND its percentage (with a clear-wave assertion, so the first two cannot pass
on a note that names both every time), and that weather's banner claim ranks below both
wave beats while still outranking the un-claimed banner -- which is what makes it a
claim that LOSES rather than a no-op.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE: -oo7e, whether weather needs counter-play, is untouched and
still open. This bead was about the ANNOUNCEMENT.

title: [bug] launch --snapshot-userstate stops the game saving, and quit reports success either way
description:
launch --snapshot-userstate PREVENTS THE GAME FROM SAVING, and quit reports success either way.

MEASURED IN CYCLE 133 with a control, harness 0.38.0. The developer's real save was backed up by hand first and verified byte-identical afterwards (sha256 4a0369eb1eb6d1716da1 both times).

  WITH --snapshot-userstate:
      run-method /root/RunConfig toggle_mute_sfx   -> Result: true
      run-method /root/RunConfig _save             -> Result: FALSE
      get-state  /root/RunConfig mute_sfx          -> true      (changed in memory)
      user://highscore.save                        -> "cb0 sfx0 ..."  UNCHANGED

  WITHOUT the flag, same three calls, same build, ~60 seconds later:
      toggle_mute_sfx -> true, _save -> TRUE
      user://highscore.save -> "cb0 sfx1 ..."  CHANGED

RunConfig._save() returns bool (it was given one in an earlier cycle so a failed write could be SEEN rather than inferred), which is the only reason this took two commands rather than a bisect. A project whose save function returns void would experience this purely as "the feature I just verified does not work for James".

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A BROKEN FLAG. The flag exists so a runtime pass can exercise save-related behaviour without writing the developer's real user://. What it actually produces is a game that CANNOT SAVE -- so every such verification taken under it passes identically whether the save path works or not. That is the exact failure the harness's own NOT COVERED discipline exists to prevent, in the tool built to make verification safe.

AND IT REPORTS SUCCESS. quit prints

    userstate: restored 1 file(s) and removed 0 created during the run (quit; patterns *.save)

every time, unconditionally. There was nothing to restore. I read that line twice in cycle 131 as confirmation the flag was working; it is not evidence of anything.

NOT ESTABLISHED, and it decides where the fix goes: WHY the save fails. The plausible cause is the snapshot holding the file open or read-only for the run's duration so FileAccess.open(WRITE) fails, but the harness implementation was not opened. DO THAT FIRST.

AND CHECK THE NEWER HARNESS BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE. This project runs 0.38.0; 0.60.0 is on the machine (-ny3h tracks the refresh, blocked on upstream gh#43). This may already be fixed. `harness-version --client` says outright that gaps logged against 0.38.0 may be fixed in releases it does not have.

ACCEPTANCE: either (a) the newer harness fixes it -- confirm by reproducing the recipe above against 0.60.0 and close, noting that the refresh is the fix; or (b) it does not, in which case this is an upstream issue with the recipe above, and the interim answer for this project is to STOP USING THE FLAG and take a manual backup instead, which is what cycle 133 did and what worked.

EITHER WAY, one thing is worth fixing here regardless: quit's restore line should say what it actually did. "restored 1 file(s)" when the file was never modified is a report about the mechanism, not about the run.
close_reason:
MY DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG. --snapshot-userstate is INNOCENT. The real defect is in this project's own save code, it is worse than what I filed, and it is fixed.

WHAT I FILED (cycle 133): "--snapshot-userstate stops the game saving." Evidence was a paired run -- with the flag, `_save()` returned false and the file never changed; without it, true and the file changed.

WHY THAT WAS WRONG. The pairing was real and the attribution was not. Re-run with the ORDER REVERSED -- plain launch first, flagged launch second -- and `_save()` returns TRUE under the flag, twice. The flag does not touch user:// writability at all: `userstate_snapshot` (tools/devtools.py:1835) COPIES matching files into `.devtools/` with `shutil.copy2` and holds nothing open. I should have read that before filing at P1, and the bead's own acceptance told me to ("read the harness implementation FIRST"). I filed instead.

THE REAL TRIGGER, found by replaying cycle 133's exact call sequence under the flag:

    record_milestones(["SNAPSHOT_PROBE"])  -> ["SNAPSHOT_PROBE"]   (reported as recorded)
    _save()                                -> FALSE
    toggle_mute_sfx()                      -> true
    _save()                                -> FALSE

An UNKNOWN MILESTONE ID BREAKS EVERY SUBSEQUENT SAVE IN THE SESSION. `MILESTONE_ID_CHARS` (game/run_config.gd:146) is lowercase, digits and underscore. `_parse_milestones` rejects any token containing anything else. `_save()` writes the file and then reads it back through the loader's own validator -- deliberately, and its comment says why: "so a future writer that its own reader cannot read fails here, loudly, instead of at some player's next launch." It does fail. But the bad id is still sitting in `earned_milestones`, so it fails again on the next save, and the next. The player's high score, settings and real milestones all quietly stop persisting.

And the reporting is split, which is what made it cost most of a cycle to attribute: `_save()` warns and returns false, while `record_milestones()` has already returned the id as freshly recorded. The caller is told it succeeded.

THE FIX, in game/run_config.gd: `record_milestones` now refuses an id that cannot round-trip, at the door, with a push_warning naming the legal character set -- the same shape as the hint refusal directly above it, which exists for the same reason. The predicate is `is_recordable_milestone(id)`, and it is DERIVED from `MILESTONE_ID_CHARS` rather than restating the rule, because the two halves being written independently is exactly how a writer comes to accept what its own reader rejects.

TESTS, and the second one is the one that matters:
  test_a_milestone_id_that_cannot_round_trip_is_refused_at_the_door -- uppercase, hyphen and
    empty are refused, AND every id in Milestones.TABLE is still recordable. Without that
    second half a predicate returning false for everything passes the first three assertions
    and silently disables milestones.
  test_every_recordable_milestone_survives_the_parser -- builds a real `m7:a,b,c...` line
    from the whole table and asserts the PARSER reads it back. This asserts the round trip
    rather than the rule, because the rule is the thing that drifted.
Red-then-green: making the predicate always-true fails the first test.

REACHABILITY, honestly: no shipping code path calls `record_milestones` with a bad id -- every real id is a lowercase constant. So this is latent rather than live, and it is a P2's worth of severity, not the P1 I filed. It becomes live the moment somebody adds a milestone id with a capital or a hyphen, and the symptom then is "saves stopped working" with nothing pointing at the id.

WHAT I ALSO GOT WRONG AND HAVE CORRECTED ELSEWHERE: cycle 133's entries in kanban.md, log-devtools.md (G-134) and cycle-log.md all state the flag as the cause. All three are corrected in the same commit as this fix, rather than left standing -- a wrong diagnosis published in four places is worse than the bug.

ONE THING FROM THE ORIGINAL BEAD THAT STILL STANDS, and I keep it: `quit` prints "userstate: restored 1 file(s) and removed 0 created during the run" UNCONDITIONALLY. That is a report about the mechanism, not about the run, and reading it as confirmation the flag worked is what let me believe a wrong story for a cycle. The honest form names what it DID -- "restored 1 file(s), 0 of which the run had modified". Not filed as a new bead, per the current instruction to work the queue rather than grow it; recorded here and in log-devtools so it is findable.

VERIFIED: name_check 0 errors, suite green on the milestone filter (16 selected, 286 assertions), red-then-green on the predicate, the developer's real save backed up by hand and confirmed byte-identical (4a0369eb1eb6d171) after four launches.

title: The ninth plant: something that stands in the road and holds a wave
description:
SOURCE: the remaining half of -ibvb (closed 2026-08-18), which named five uncovered plant
roles and got three of them from Mint, Nettle and Aloe. PLAYER-FACING. This is the largest
role a tower-defence roster can be missing: nothing in this game stands in a pest's way.

WHAT IS THERE NOW, read 2026-08-18 rather than remembered:

* Plants cannot go on the road at all, and the rule is a single board-level predicate with
  no per-plant say in it. Board.is_buildable (game/board.gd:377-378) is literally
  `is_inside(cell) and not is_path(cell)`. Game.would_plant_at (game/game.gd:1469) and
  Game.place_plant both call it; place_plant's refusal string at game/game.gd:1491 is
  `"pests walk there" if board.is_path(cell) else "off the garden"`. So the road is
  unbuildable for every one of the eight plants, by construction.

* A pest only ever stops for two things, and neither is a plant standing in front of it.
  Pest._physics_process (game/pest.gd:1240-1268) returns early for `held_by != null` (a
  Chomp's mouth) and, only when `is_hungry`, for `_adjacent_plant()` — which it eats via
  `meal.take_damage(EAT_DPS * delta)`. Every other pest falls through to
  `_advance(delta * speed)`.

* _advance (game/pest.gd:1388-1403) walks `_route` and consults nothing else. There is no
  occupancy query in it at all: no `plant_at`, no board read, no collision. A plant sitting
  on a route waypoint would be walked straight through.

* _adjacent_plant (game/pest.gd:1274-1287) already does the "is there a plant within reach"
  scan, over the `plants` group, bounded by EAT_RADIUS = Board.CELL * 1.15
  (game/pest.gd:465). That is the reusable half — the missing half is a pest that is NOT
  hungry caring about the result.

* Board.is_road_adjacent (game/board.gd:385-389) exists and is orthogonal-only. Useful
  neighbour, not a substitute: it answers "can a road pest reach this grass cell", which is
  the mirror of the question here.

WHAT TO BUILD: a plant that occupies a ROAD cell and holds the wave at it until it is
eaten. The shape that follows from the code above:

1. Per-plant buildability. `is_buildable` cannot stay the only word. Either a catalogue
   flag (e.g. `"on_road": true`) that would_plant_at/place_plant consult, or a
   PlantCatalog predicate beside reach(). Note place_plant's refusal string is asserted
   somewhere — grep before changing the text.
2. A stop rule in _physics_process ahead of `_advance`, so EVERY pest halts at a blocker on
   its own cell, not only a hungry one. Reuse _adjacent_plant's group scan rather than
   writing a second one.
3. Damage while stopped, or the blocker is an infinite wall. EAT_DPS (14.0) and the
   blocker's own health are the two numbers that set how many seconds one purchase buys.
4. The four hand-lists -ibvb enumerated and every plant must be added to:
   PlantCatalog.reach() (game/plant_catalog.gd:120+), Game._new_plant() (game/game.gd —
   its default arm silently returns CornCobbler, so a forgotten entry plants corn),
   NotebookScreen.PAGES (game/notebook_screen.gd:400+ is where mint/nettle/aloe sit), and
   the Hud upgrade path only if it upgrades.
5. Art per art_src/STYLE.md, rendered by tools/render_svg.gd. Needs an engine pass, so this
   is not fan-out work.

OPEN DESIGN QUESTIONS the implementer must answer and record, not guess silently:
* Does a blocker on the road break the dead-ground cue, which is driven by reach()? A
  blocker's "reach" is its own cell.
* Does the placement preview's green-bracket promise still hold over road cells
  (would_plant_at is what draws it, game/game.gd:2120)?
* Can a winged pest fly over it, the way it flies over a Chomp's reach?

ACCEPTANCE (all producible by the closing commit — no screenshot clause, per the loop's
rule that evidence a commit cannot produce is a second bead):
* A ninth entry in PlantCatalog with all four hand-lists fed.
* A test that a non-hungry pest's position stops advancing while a blocker stands on its
  route, and resumes once the blocker is destroyed.
* A test that the blocker can be placed on a road cell and that every OTHER plant still
  cannot.
* The three open questions above answered in comments or in the close, whichever they
  belong in.
close_reason:
SHIPPED as the Barrier Bramble, commit a3a9b58. Answering the acceptance clause by clause,
because a close that does not is how a half-done bead looks finished.

CLAUSE 1 -- "a ninth entry in PlantCatalog with all four hand-lists fed." Done, and the
count was wrong: there were FIVE hand-lists, not four, and the fifth is the one that
mattered most.
  1. PlantCatalog.reach() -- explicit BRAMBLE arm returning 0.0, with the reason written
     out rather than left to the default arm.
  2. Game._new_plant() -- BRAMBLE arm returning Bramble.new(), so the default arm cannot
     silently plant corn.
  3. NotebookScreen.PAGES -- a page, and its note had to be cut from 354 to 280 chars by
     the 300-char budget gate.
  4. Hud upgrade path -- n/a, the Bramble has no ladder.
  5. NOT IN THE BEAD: TitleScreen.PLANT_X, test_sprite_style.EXPECTED_SIZE, the engaging-
     plants count in test_combat, the reachless-plant count in test_placement, and the
     seed-sink maker table in test_selftest. Five more places, all caught by the suite.

CLAUSE 2 -- "a test that a non-hungry pest's position stops advancing while a blocker
stands on its route, and resumes once the blocker is destroyed." Done:
test_a_bramble_stops_an_ordinary_pest_and_it_walks_on_once_the_wall_is_gone asserts both
halves against pest.position, plus the wall actually losing health so the check cannot pass
on a pest that merely stood still. Confirmed live as well: 70.7 -> 173.4 -> 250.1, held
three seconds while health went 40.0 -> 25.8, then walked on once it was destroyed.

CLAUSE 3 -- "a test that the blocker can be placed on a road cell and that every OTHER
plant still cannot." Done, and written over the WHOLE catalogue in both directions rather
than about the one new id, so the tenth plant inherits it:
test_only_the_bramble_stands_on_the_road_and_it_stands_nowhere_else. It also pins the count
at exactly one, which is what PlantCatalog.on_road()'s header promises.

CLAUSE 4 -- "the three open questions answered." All three, and one changed the code:
  * Dead-ground cue: reach() is 0.0, so the cue drops the Bramble entirely. Recorded in
    test_placement as the SECOND of two distinct reasons a plant can be dropped -- the
    Sunflower reaches nothing, the Bramble stands where the cue does not look.
  * Placement preview: it inverts with the selected plant. would_plant_at and the three
    _update_preview call sites all moved to is_buildable_for. Verified live: with a Bramble
    selected, grass reads placeable=false and road placeable=true.
  * Winged pests: YES, they fly over. Bramble.stops(is_winged) is the rule and
    Pest._blocking_plant asks it rather than reading the flag, so the shop line and the
    behaviour cannot drift. Verified live: a winged aphid crossed at 251.4 -> 352.8 -> 416
    with the wall at 40.0 throughout.

ONE THING THE BEAD DID NOT ANTICIPATE, and it is the interesting one. The bead's
"WHAT TO BUILD" step 1 said place_plant's refusal string "is asserted somewhere -- grep
before changing the text". It is (test_placement.gd:64, "pests walk there"), and that
string turned out to be exactly backwards for this plant: pests walking there is the whole
point. So there are three refusals now, not two, and a road plant on grass gets
"no pests walk there".

WHAT IS NOT DONE, named rather than left implied: the move preview
(Game._update_preview's `moving` branch) describes the plant being UPROOTED while
would_plant_at still consults `selected_plant`. That mismatch predates this bead and is now
reachable in a new way -- arming an uproot on a grass plant while a Bramble is selected.
Filed separately rather than folded in here.

title: The game has no touch input at all — mobile plays through mouse emulation
description:
There is no InputEventScreenTouch or InputEventScreenDrag handler anywhere in game/. Game._unhandled_input (game/game.gd:1678) recognises exactly two pointer events: InputEventMouseMotion (hover preview) and InputEventMouseButton LEFT pressed (_click_at). Everything a phone does reaches the game only because Godot's pointing/emulate_mouse_from_touch default is on — and that default is not even written into project.godot, so it is an inherited assumption rather than a decision.

What that costs on a touch device:
- Hover does not exist. _update_cursor() drives the placement preview off mouse motion, so the ring/validity cue a mouse player sees before committing only appears on a phone DURING a drag, if at all. A tap places blind.
- No press-and-hold, no gesture, no drag-to-place. Placement is select-a-packet-then-tap-a-cell; the tap is committed on press, so there is no way to abort a mis-aim once the finger is down.
- No multi-touch and no palm rejection: a second finger anywhere emits another emulated click.
- _click_at() rejects anything above Hud.BAR_HEIGHT or right of board_size().x, so a fat-finger tap a few px into the chrome is silently dropped with no feedback.

NOTE ON SCOPE: the reporter described "click and drag" as the awkward part. No drag interaction exists in the code today, so this bead needs one clarification before implementation — whether the complaint is (a) that dragging is what a player instinctively tries and nothing happens, (b) that the emulated drag mis-fires the tap, or (c) something in the itch.io web build's page-level scroll/pan fighting the canvas. Reproduce on device first.
design:
The likely shape is a real touch layer rather than better mouse emulation:
- Handle InputEventScreenTouch/InputEventScreenDrag explicitly, and commit placement on RELEASE rather than press, so a finger already down can slide to the right cell and the preview updates the whole time. That single change gives touch the hover feedback mouse players get, and makes a mis-aim abortable by dragging off the board.
- Treat drag from a seed packet to a cell as the placement gesture, since that is what the reporter reached for.
- Godot's Input.is_emulating_mouse_from_touch() lets both paths coexist; devtools has touch press/release/drag verbs and set-feature --touchscreen for driving this from the bridge.
Depends on the resolution work only insofar as touch targets are measured in viewport units — the 40px touch minimum the HUD already enforces means nothing if the viewport is a different shape than the layout assumed.
acceptance_criteria:
- Reproduced on an actual touch device or in Chrome device emulation against the itch.io build, with the specific awkwardness named in a comment on this issue.
- InputEventScreenTouch/ScreenDrag handled explicitly in game.gd; placement commits on release.
- The placement preview updates during a touch drag, so a player sees validity before committing.
- A /verify Phase 4 bridge check driving touch press -> drag -> release that asserts the plant lands on the cell under the finger at release, not the one under the initial press.
notes:
CORRECTION: the close above names the split-out device bead as "-0mzu". It is
plant-tower-defense-bfbb. The id was written into the close before the bead was created and
I did not go back and fix it -- recorded here rather than by rewriting the close, per this
project's rule that a close records what was believed at the time.
close_reason:
CODE SHIPPED; the device clause is split out as its own bead rather than left here.

THE PREMISE HELD, re-confirmed rather than trusted: grep for InputEventScreenTouch and
InputEventScreenDrag across game/ returned ZERO. A phone played entirely through Godot's
mouse emulation.

THREE OF THE FOUR ACCEPTANCE CLAUSES ARE MET:

  * "InputEventScreenTouch/ScreenDrag handled explicitly in game.gd; placement commits on
    release." Done. A press shows the cue and plants nothing; the release plants, at the
    RELEASE position -- not the remembered press position, which is the mistake an
    implementation makes and the thing the headless test asserts by planting at a cell three
    to the right of where the finger landed.
  * "The placement preview updates during a touch drag." Done, and verified live: the
    preview moved to x=352 while the finger dragged, with 0 plants on the board.
  * "A /verify Phase 4 bridge check driving touch press -> drag -> release that asserts the
    plant lands on the cell under the finger at release, not the one under the initial
    press." Done: press at (2,3) -> 0 plants, drag to (5,3) -> 0 plants, release -> one
    plant at (5, 3).

THE FOURTH -- "Reproduced on an actual touch device or in Chrome device emulation against
the itch.io build" -- is not done and cannot be produced by a commit. It is now -0mzu, with
the three ways a real device differs from the bridge written out. Splitting rather than
closing quietly, because a criterion no commit can produce makes a finished item look
unstarted in `bd ready` -- which is what -6cqi did for twelve cycles.

THE FINDING WORTH READING, because the obvious implementation is wrong and looks right:

Mouse emulation stays ON deliberately -- every Button in this game is a Control answering
mouse events, so turning it off to get clean touch handling would kill the shop, the pause
card and every Back button on exactly the devices this is for. So the engine sends BOTH
events for one finger, and the whole job is telling them apart.

The obvious way is a flag set by the touch handler. It cannot work, and a probe on the
running game is what showed that:

    PROBE mouse press  device=-1  touch_index=-1
    PROBE screen touch pressed index=0 device=0

The emulated mouse press arrives BEFORE the InputEventScreenTouch that produced it. The
first implementation therefore planted at the PRESS cell -- the exact defect
commit-on-release exists to remove -- and no ordering of the branches in _unhandled_input
fixes it.

The discriminator is the device id: Godot marks the emulated event -1 and a real one 0.
Narrowed by DisplayServer.is_touchscreen_available() on purpose, because -1 means
SYNTHESISED rather than "from touch" -- the devtools bridge's own mouse-move sends one, and
on a desktop with no touchscreen a -1 event is a test driving the game and must be honoured.

WHAT THE HEADLESS TEST CANNOT COVER, stated because it is unusual: the emulated-mouse guard.
is_touchscreen_available() is a property of the machine, not something a test can set. So
the bridge check is genuinely covering a different half rather than re-confirming the suite
-- the one clear case of that this session.

ALSO NOT DONE, from the bead's DESIGN section: "Treat drag from a seed packet to a cell as
the placement gesture, since that is what the reporter reached for." The drag currently
starts on the board. Dragging from the packet button is a different gesture with its own
hit-testing against a Control, and it belongs with -0mzu's answer about what the reporter
actually meant.

title: The HUD is built at a fixed 1152x648 and never re-lays-out on resize
description:
project.godot sets stretch/mode=canvas_items with stretch/aspect="expand", which means the viewport genuinely changes shape at a different window aspect — a widescreen window gets more horizontal viewport units, a 4:3 window gets fewer. But Hud.get_viewport_width()/get_viewport_height() (game/hud.gd:1346-1351) read ProjectSettings display/window/size/viewport_width|height, not the live viewport, and every size derived from them is written once during _build_* and never recomputed.

Concrete consequences, all in game/hud.gd:
- TopBar (:760), StatsRow (:785), PrepBar (:844) are sized to the SETTING width, so on a wider viewport the ink bar stops short of the right edge and on a narrower one it overhangs.
- The side panel is positioned at get_viewport_width() - PANEL_WIDTH (:854), so it detaches from the right edge rather than staying pinned to it.
- MessageLabel is sized viewport_width - 276 (:836) and Banner width viewport_width - PANEL_WIDTH (:1013) — both stale for the same reason.
- The prep countdown fill (:1144) scales against the setting width, so the bar's 100% is not the screen's 100%.
- No node in the HUD connects to get_viewport().size_changed, so nothing re-runs even in principle.

The board has the mirror problem: Board.board_size() is a constant 14*64 x 9*64 = 896x576 (game/board.gd:451), so the playfield neither scales nor centres, and the gap between the board's right edge and the side panel is whatever the aspect happens to leave.

This is the root cause bead; the tile/border artifacts are likely a downstream symptom of the same non-integer scaling and are tracked separately.
design:
Two decisions have to be made before any code moves, and they are separable:
1. Does the HUD REFLOW (anchors/containers that stretch, board centred in the space left over) or does the game LETTERBOX (stretch/aspect=keep, so every aspect gets the same 1152x648 picture with bars)? Letterboxing is a two-line change and would close the visual defect immediately; reflowing is the real fix and is what a phone in portrait actually needs.
2. Whichever is chosen, get_viewport_width()/get_viewport_height() must stop being the seam. Today they name the setting; every caller believes they name the screen. Either make them read get_viewport().get_visible_rect().size and add a size_changed handler that re-runs layout, or rename them to design_width()/design_height() so the fixed-design assumption is legible at every call site.
acceptance_criteria:
- A stated decision (reflow vs letterbox) recorded on this issue before implementation.
- The HUD renders correctly at 16:9, 21:9 and 4:3 with no bar stopping short of an edge, no panel detached from the right edge, and no control overhanging the viewport.
- A check in test/unit/test_selftest.gd that instantiates the HUD at more than one viewport size via _T.instantiate_ui and asserts the top bar spans the full width and the side panel is flush right at each.
- devtools findings reports 0 NEW ui_layout/ui_reachable findings at each tested resolution.
notes:
ABSENCE CLAIM RESOLVED (cycle 104 sweep, -g1o4): STILL TRUE, both halves.
"reads ProjectSettings, not the live viewport" -- confirmed at game/hud.gd:1347 and
:1351, both `ProjectSettings.get_setting("display/window/size/viewport_...")`.
"nothing re-runs even in principle" -- confirmed: `grep -rn "size_changed" game/*.gd`
returns ZERO. No node connects the viewport's resize signal at all.
close_reason:
DONE. The HUD reads the live viewport and re-lays-out when it changes shape.

CLAIMS ALL CONFIRMED before any code was written, including one the bead did not make:
project.godot's [display] section has NO size/viewport_width or height key at all, so the
"setting" the old getters read was Godot's 1152x648 default and the fallback returned the
same number -- which is exactly why this never looked broken at the design size.

WHAT CHANGED: get_viewport_width/height() now read
get_viewport().get_visible_rect().size (canvas units, which is what a canvas_items
content-scale override respects; Window.size would be physical pixels and wrong for a
CanvasLayer). Every viewport-derived rect moved out of the three _build_* methods into one
_apply_viewport_layout(), connected once to size_changed. Re-derived rather than anchored,
because this HUD is built in code against a width budget and a half-anchored,
half-computed layout is worse than either.

VERIFIED LIVE AT THREE SHAPES, which is the half no headless test can reach -- the suite
can prove the HUD obeys whatever viewport it is in, but not that the root window's
content-scale override produces the canvas `expand` documents:

  window 1152x648  -> TopBar 1152 wide, SidePanel at x 896, 896+256 = 1152
  window 1720x720  -> canvas 1548, TopBar 1548, SidePanel at x 1292, 1292+256 = 1548
  window 1024x768  -> canvas 1152x792, TopBar 1152, SidePanel 896+256 = 1152, height 792

The middle row is the bug: before this, the bar stopped at 1152 on a 1548-wide canvas and
the side panel detached from the right edge by 396px. findings ran clean at 1548x648 too --
0 across 5 of 5.

THE WIDTH BUDGET, and the reasoning is better than the fix. Below 1074+40 the failure would
be SILENT: Control.size is clamped UP to get_combined_minimum_size(), and the StatsRow's
minimum is the sum of its children, so asking for less does not squeeze it -- the assignment
appears to succeed and the wave button lands off the right edge with nothing reporting it.
But stretch/aspect="expand" divides window by min(window/base) per axis, so the canvas is
never narrower than the design width and 1114 <= 1152 always holds. That dependency is now
legible rather than assumed: min_viewport_width(), stats_row_shortfall(), a push_warning
per crossing, and a test asserting BOTH that the budget fits the narrowest producible
viewport AND that stretch/aspect is still "expand" -- so changing the setting the floor
rests on goes red instead of the button going quietly off screen.

FOUND AND NOT FIXED, correctly, because the lane did not own those files:
game/title_screen.gd and game/overlay_screen.gd each declare their OWN
get_viewport_width/height() with the identical ProjectSettings body. The same defect lives
there untouched. Filed separately rather than smuggled in.

713/713 tests, 14752 assertions, lint 0/0, check_all 16/16.

title: Give the campaign's back half a real second act
description:
SOURCE: cycle 101's playtest (plant-tower-defense-t52o), derived from all 22 wave rows.

The back half of the campaign does not escalate, and this is a DESIGN QUESTION for James
rather than a defect to go and fix.

DERIVED, not sampled. Running every campaign wave through WaveDirector._raw_threat
(game/wave_director.gd:755) gives the wave-over-wave threat step:

  waves 2-7 : +80.0%, +48.1%, +70.0%, +14.7%, +23.1%, +27.1%
  wave  8   : +43.3%  (after cycle 101's tuning; it was +80.9%)
  waves 9-22: +29.1%, +9.9%, +10.0%, +13.6%, +9.6%, +7.3%, +2.0%, +6.3%, +6.3%,
              +4.7%, +4.8%, +2.2%, +4.5%, +5.3%

So after wave 9 the campaign averages about +6% a wave for thirteen waves, and pest counts
sit between 26 and 37 the whole way.

The cause is structural, not a matter of how the table was typed. health_scale_for
(game/wave_director.gd:850) returns exactly 1.0 for every campaign wave and
mutation_chance_for (:840) returns a flat MUTATION_CHANCE, both via the same `over <= 0`
early return, so every escalation axis the game owns is endless-only BY CONSTRUCTION.
Inside the campaign, difficulty is the table and nothing else.

Confirmed live: the depth-first playthrough won all 22 waves without losing a single life,
finishing with 1129 spare seeds and 41 plants.

THE QUESTION, and it is genuinely a matter of taste rather than of correctness:

  (a) This is fine. The campaign is a 22-wave tutorial whose job is to teach the systems
      and hand the player to endless, where the ramps already exist. A flawless run is a
      satisfying end to a learning curve, not a failure of one.
