  (b) The campaign should have a real second act -- the plateau should climb, so that the
      plants unlocked at wave 7 have something to be needed FOR before the credits.

If (b), the surgical lever is turning on a gentle health_scale_for inside the campaign
rather than rewriting fourteen wave rows; the rows are hemmed in by three chained
assertions that cap any finale at 436.7 base health (see WaveDirector.WAVES' header and
cycle 100's notes), so growing them is the expensive path.

DO NOT act on this without an answer. Either direction is defensible and the wrong one is
expensive to reverse.
notes:
ABSENCE CLAIM RESOLVED (cycle 104 sweep, -g1o4): CLAIMS STAND, but this is BLOCKED ON JAMES, not on code.
The bead says so itself -- "this is a DESIGN QUESTION for James rather than a defect to go
and fix" -- and the derived numbers behind it (the wave-over-wave threat steps, ~+6% a
wave for thirteen waves after wave 9) were computed from the table rather than sampled, so
they do not rot the way a prose claim does.
Two things HAVE moved under it since filing and whoever answers should know:
  * Cycle 103 put the Shield Bug into waves 15 and 21 (-pdri), paid for in beetles. Waves
    15 and 21 now carry a plated pest a Corn Cobbler cannot scratch, which is a difficulty
    EVENT in the back half where the bead says there is none. It does not raise the threat
    curve -- `_raw_threat` prices a plated bug at its 10 HP and cannot see the plate at
    all -- so the flat-curve finding stands, but "nothing happens in the back half" is now
    less true than when it was written.
  * Wave 22's finale is still at the 40-pest ceiling with 18.7 points under the 436.7 bound,
    so any answer that adds to the finale still has to displace rather than add.
Flagging rather than closing: the sweep's job is to say whether the claims are still true,
and they are. What it cannot do is answer the design question.
close_reason: Second act on health_scale_for, CAMPAIGN_HEALTH_STEP=0.03 (0.04 broke a live coverage simulation via endless compounding). 769 tests.

title: Nothing teaches upgrading, and upgrading decides the run
description:
SOURCE: cycle 101's playtest (plant-tower-defense-t52o), the highest-value finding in it.

Nothing in the game teaches upgrading, and upgrading decides the run.

THE EVIDENCE, and it is an A/B rather than an impression. Two full campaign playthroughs on
the same economy with no cheats, differing in exactly one policy bit -- spend surplus seeds on
NEW plants, or on the plants already down:

  * breadth-first: eleven level-1 plants, never upgraded once. Dead at wave 10.
  * depth-first: upgrade what is down, then expand. Won all 22 waves and lost NO lives.
    591 pests defeated, finished holding 1129 spare seeds.

Both unlocked all seven plants by wave 7, so the difference is not the catalogue.

WHERE THE MECHANIC LIVES: an "Upgrade" button that exists only while a placed plant is
selected -- built at game/hud.gd:806-811, made visible in the block that now reads
`_upgrade_button.visible = plant.has_upgrades()` (cycle 101 replaced three per-class
assignments there). Nothing ever suggests selecting a placed plant.

I searched for the BEHAVIOUR ("the game tells the player upgrading exists") across three
mechanisms rather than for one implementation:
  * game/milestones.gd -- no entry mentions upgrades or plant levels at all.
  * every show_message() call site in game/game.gd -- twenty of them. Exactly two concern
    upgrades: game/game.gd:1321 "That upgrade costs %d seeds." (a REFUSAL, reached only by a
    player who already found the button and could not afford it) and :1331, the confirmation
    after a successful one.
  * the notebook -- game/notebook_screen.gd:296-297, one caption about the bunch-of-corn
    upgrade, in a screen the player must go and open.

The opening tutorial line is game/game.gd:273, "Plant your free Corn Cobbler on the grass,
then grow the first wave." It teaches placing and starting waves and stops.

So every mention of the mechanic that decides the run is either a reply to a player who
already found it, or optional reading.

NOT A BALANCE ITEM. Do not fix this by making upgrades stronger or plants weaker -- the
depth run suggests the numbers are close to right. The gap is that the game never says the
choice exists. Worth considering: a one-shot hint the first time a player has more seeds
banked than the cheapest upgrade on their own board, which is the moment the decision is
live and the only moment it is not noise. RunConfig already has the one-shot milestone
machinery (see HINT_MOVE_PREVIEW's use at game/game.gd, the uproot tip).

ACCEPTANCE: a first-time player is told, once, in-game and without opening the notebook,
that a placed plant can be upgraded; the prompt is tied to a state where the advice is
actionable rather than fired on a timer; and it is a one-shot, recorded like the other hints.
close_reason:
DONE. A third one-shot hint, RunConfig.HINT_UPGRADE_EXISTS, fired the first time
the player holds at least what the cheapest upgrade on their OWN BOARD costs.

CLAIMS CONFIRMED FIRST, and one of them looked false. The bead says milestones.gd
never mentions upgrades or plant levels; grep -ic "upgrade|level" returns 4. All
four are threat_level -- wave difficulty, not plant level -- so the claim holds
and now says how it was checked. The Upgrade button and the two show_message
sites are where the bead said (line numbers had drifted; the tutorial line is at
game/game.gd:280 now, not :273).

WHY A BANK BALANCE AND NOT A TIMER: the bead asked for a prompt tied to a state
where the advice is ACTIONABLE, and that state is exactly "can afford the
cheapest upgrade in front of them". Before it the tip is a rule they cannot use.
This also answers -qoil ("pick ONE hint"), which is closed pointing here.

VERIFIED LIVE AT THE BOUNDARY, not just in a test: with a cob down costing 20 to
upgrade, has_milestone("seen_upgrade_tip") is false at 19 seeds and true at 20,
and the row reads "Your Corn Cobbler can be upgraded. Click it on the board -- 20
seeds." Screenshot taken; MessageLabel 876x23 at 20,47, inside the bar. findings
0 across 5 of 5 checks unpaused.

TWO DEFECTS FOUND ON THE WAY, neither by reading the diff:

1. save_persist_check printed the chain before a test ran --
   place_plant() -> _refresh() -> _maybe_teach_upgrading() -> spend_hint() -> _save()
   test/unit/test_board.gd had no save redirect and had never needed one. Not a
   line of it changed and it became a writer of the developer's real
   user://highscore.save. It has a setup()/teardown() now.

2. The hint would have been shown up to MESSAGE_QUEUE_MAX times, not once.
   show_message returns false on a busy row but QUEUES the arriving text rather
   than dropping it. That is right for an EDGE-triggered caller (_on_flight_ignored
   fires once per winged pest) and wrong for a LEVEL-triggered one: affordability
   stays true, so every later refresh stacked another copy. Added
   Hud.row_is_quiet(), and the tip asks before offering -- a busy row means "not
   this refresh", never "spend the hint". The test asserts three refreshes over a
   busy row queue NOTHING, which is the case that was broken.

The pure seam Game.cheapest_upgrade(plants) uses can_upgrade(), not
has_upgrades(): the second is true of a plant sitting at the top of its ladder,
which is the one case where this advice is actively wrong. The test walks a plant
to its max so the assertion is made where that distinction can FAIL.

Corpus: the tip is a producer priced per plant name at 99999, inside the PLANTS
loop, because it names whichever plant on the board is cheapest -- a fact about
the player's garden, so any name can appear. The corpus tripwire test moved from
five per plant to six and says why.

687/687, 14393 assertions, lint 0/0.

NOT DONE, and it is the honest gap: this teaches that upgrading EXISTS. It does
not teach that upgrading BEATS breadth, which is what the A/B actually measured.
A player told "you can upgrade this" may still spend the seeds on a new plant.
Filed separately rather than smuggled in here.

title: Put the Shield Bug in a wave a player will actually meet
description:
SOURCE: cycle 100's merge, and the deferred half of -4du6 which shipped the species itself.

The Shield Bug exists (Pest.SPECIES[SHIELDBUG], commit d944fbc) and is spawnable by name, but
it is NOT in WaveDirector.WAVES, so no player will ever meet it. The bead that built it asked
for that to be a separate commit on purpose: a species should land and be tested before it
moves the difficulty curve.

That curve is now the whole of this bead's difficulty, and cycle 100 measured why. Three
assertions chain to cap any campaign finale at 436.7 base health -- SIMULTANEOUS_PEST_CEILING
pinned as literal source text, the first endless wave held under 50% beetle, and threat_for
required to rise strictly across the seam. Wave 22's finale is at the ceiling. So a Shield Bug
added to a late wave DISPLACES something rather than adding to it, and the golden headcount
array in test_combat.gd will move.

Two decisions to make, in this order:
  1. WHICH WAVE. The Shield Bug's point is that a Corn Cobbler cannot hurt it, so it belongs
     where the player has had time to own something else -- after the Chomp and the Dandelion
     are reachable. Placing it before that is a wall, not a decision.
  2. WHAT IT DISPLACES. Its health is 10 against a beetle's; check its threat contribution
     against the cap before writing the row, using the offline replica approach the campaign
     lane used (it reproduced wave 16's peak, endless's 29 and the golden array exactly).

Also update wave_director.gd's header arithmetic. It says "two species x three mutations plus
plain" = eight kinds of enemy. That is still true today because the Shield Bug is not in the
table; the day it joins, it is twelve. The header is cited by name in cycle 100's kanban entry
as an example of a comment that stayed correct only because the change was split.

ACCEPTANCE: the Shield Bug appears in at least one campaign wave; the wave chosen is justified
by what the player is expected to own by then; the golden headcount array and the endless seam
are both re-derived rather than adjusted until green; and wave_director.gd's "eight kinds"
arithmetic is corrected.
close_reason:
DONE. The Shield Bug debuts in wave 15 and returns in wave 21, paid for in
beetles rather than out of the finale.

VERIFIED AT RUNTIME, which is the sentence this bead is actually about -- the
species has existed and been spawnable by name since cycle 100 without any player
meeting it. Set WaveDirector.current_wave to 14, started wave 15, and polled the
live pest census: absent at t=6s, two at t=9s, four at t=12s, settling at
20 aphid / 13 beetle / 4 shieldbug. That is exactly the +4 the table specifies,
and it arrives LATE in the wave, so the debut is a group met after the wave is
already underway rather than a wall at the gate.

THE ARITHMETIC (Shield Bug is 10 base health against a beetle's 16):

  wave 15   -2 beetles, +4 shieldbugs   300 -> 308 pts (+2.7%)   35 -> 37 of 40
  wave 21   -2 beetles, +3 shieldbugs   397 -> 395 pts (-0.5%)   37 -> 38 of 40
  wave 22   UNTOUCHED                   418 pts, 40 of 40, 18.7 under the bound

NOT the finale, and this was computed then rejected rather than assumed: the
cheapest legal finale carrying three plated bugs was 426, spending 8 of the 18.7
points (43%) of headroom under the 436.7 cap -- the campaign's scarcest resource,
and the whole reason -eeaq inserted six waves in FRONT of the finale.

WHICH WAVE, and the citation: a Corn Cobbler cannot scratch one at any level
(shell_absorb 1.5 against CornCobbler.LEVELS topping out at 1.4, already asserted
at test_combat.gd:5730), so it is a decision only for a player who owns something
else. Chomp is tier 1 at 15 seeds and the only tier-1 plant a 20-seed common
packet can roll. The evidence that wave 15 is late enough is log-devtools.md:6327
-- cycle 101 played the campaign end to end on two OPPOSED seed policies and both
had all seven plants by wave 7.

Wave 21 is the drought, and the pairing is the point: drought doubles a plant's
firing INTERVAL while a plate eats whole kernels, so both failures stack on the
Corn Cobbler and on none of its three answers -- chew_seconds and a blast radius
are not rates.

Wave 21 loses health while gaining difficulty, which is not a contradiction:
_raw_threat prices a plated bug at its 10 HP and cannot see the plate at all.
That is now written into the _raw_threat header as the one place the function
under-states a wave -- bounded to two rows and seven pests, recorded rather than
fudged.

GOLDEN ARRAY: two indices moved (15: 35->37, 21: 37->38) and it stays RECORDED
rather than derived. Per derive-the-list step 1 this is the "list that exists to
disagree" case -- its only possible source of truth is WAVES itself, so
expected[i] = pests_in_wave(i) would assert a tautology and pass unconditionally.
The reasoning is written in beside it.

Three tests added, all sweeping the table rather than naming 15 and 21, so a
future row that moves the species takes them with it. The first FAILS on the
pre-change table, which is the positive control this bead needed.

690/690 tests, 14409 assertions, lint 0/0, check_all 15/15, findings 0 of 5 of 5.

TWO PROCESS NOTES, both disclosed by the lane rather than found afterwards. It
made one mechanical three-line edit with a Python script against the standing
rule, and verified no damage immediately (comment prefixes intact, no line-ending
churn). And its worktree branched from 1bddf78 rather than current main, so it
worked without cycle 102 in the tree and correctly reported that the single gate
command its brief named did not exist in its checkout -- it said so instead of
assuming, which is the only reason that was caught.

title: A pest species that changes the plan, not the aim
description:
SOURCE: asked for directly by James, cycle 99 ("more levels"), and the roster half of -gsai.
PLAYER-FACING.

WHAT IS THERE NOW: Pest.SPECIES (game/pest.gd:28) holds three -- APHID (3 seeds, fast, weak),
BEETLE (9 seeds, slow, tough, 2.6s chew) and QUEEN (40 seeds, the boss). Three mutations layer
on top (armoured, winged, hungry at pest.gd:94-96) and compose in pairs, so the roster is
"eight kinds of enemy" as wave_director's header puts it.

WHAT IS NOT COVERED, and this is the bead's real content: every pest today walks the road at a
constant speed and is answered by damage. Nothing SPLITS, nothing heals, nothing arrives in
the air on its own (winged is a mutation, not a species), nothing changes the player's plan
rather than their aim.

Candidates -- pick ONE per bead when claimed, the way -ibvb was split:
  1. A splitter: dies into two smaller pests. Makes AoE (the Dandelion, the only multi-target
     plant) answer a question single-target cannot, which is a role the catalogue already has
     and nothing currently rewards.
  2. A shielded pest that ignores the first N damage. Answers "many small shots" differently
     from "one big one" -- Corn versus Dandelion -- which is the same axis the game already
     prices and never tests.
  3. A digger that skips the first K cells of the road. Makes WHERE you plant matter, which is
     the axis the Mint just made interesting for plants and nothing does for pests.

FILES: game/pest.gd, art_src/ and assets/sprites/ for its sprite, and wave_director.gd only if
it joins the campaign table (prefer a separate commit for that, so the species can land and be
tested before the difficulty curve moves). Disjoint from the plant catalogue and the HUD.

WHAT A NEW SPECIES COSTS, from the two plants added in cycles 98-99: an entry in SPECIES, a
sprite passing tools/svg_style_check.py and test_sprite_style.gd (add an EXPECTED_SIZE row), a
dead-sprite variant if it should leave a corpse (pest_aphid_dead.png is the precedent), and a
check of anything that enumerates species -- grep for SPECIES.keys() and for the literal ids.

ACCEPTANCE: one new species is spawnable and appears in a wave; what it asks of the player is
stated in one sentence and asserted by a test (a splitter that does not split, or a shield
that does not absorb, must fail); its sprite passes both art gates; and the "eight kinds of
enemy" arithmetic in wave_director's header is corrected to whatever it now is.
notes:
CORRECTION to this bead's own description, found by the agent that worked it and worth
recording because a future reader would re-derive the same wrong plan:

"nothing SPLITS" is FALSE. Pest.SPECIES[QUEEN] has carried "split_species": APHID and
"split_count": 3 since the boss landed (game/pest.gd:150-151), Pest.split_species() and
split_count() are the accessors, and Game._spawn_brood (game/game.gd:829-841) executes it off
the `died` signal. Candidate 1 (a splitter) was therefore a second queen, not a new axis.

That is the fourth bead in this project whose absence claim was wrong, and the same cause each
time: written from the neighbourhood of one file. kanban-idea-pass rule 2 covers it and I broke
it while filing.

Second correction, smaller: the bead's framing of "Corn versus Dandelion = many small shots vs
one big one" is only half true on the numbers. Dandelion.SEED_DAMAGE is 3.0 (dandelion.gd:105)
against a maxed kernel's 1.4 (corn_cobbler.gd:51) -- a 2.1x ratio, and the Dandelion throws a
volley. The band is narrow, which is why the Shield Bug's shell_absorb is pinned by ASSERTION
against both plants' real numbers rather than written down as a constant.

Candidate 3 (the digger) was refused for ownership rather than merit: it is implementable in
setup() alone, but its value is a change to lane pressure, coverage maps and the entry cue,
which live in game.gd and board.gd. Still a real candidate for a later cycle.
close_reason:
SHIPPED (d944fbc) as the Shield Bug, live-verified: spawned by name, and its blue-grey plate
is unmistakable beside two plain red aphids on the tan road.

Acceptance: one new species is spawnable (yes); what it asks of the player is one sentence
("which plant answers this lane, not where you aim") and IS asserted by a test that fails if
the behaviour does nothing -- six kernels must move health by exactly zero and the seventh by a
whole kernel; the sprite passes both art gates. It is NOT yet in the wave table, which the bead
itself asked to be a separate commit, so the "eight kinds of enemy" arithmetic in
wave_director's header is still correct and untouched -- it becomes 12 the day the species
joins the table. That is the remaining work and it is a one-line change plus a rebalance
thought.

See this bead's notes for the two corrections to its own description, the important one being
that "nothing SPLITS" was false.

title: More campaign: longer, or a second one
description:
SOURCE: asked for directly by James, cycle 99 ("more levels"). PLAYER-FACING.

WHAT IS THERE NOW, read rather than remembered: WaveDirector.WAVES
(game/wave_director.gd:186) is a 16-entry Array[Array]; each wave is a list of groups and each
group is {"species", "count", "gap", "lead"}. Two species appear in it (aphid, beetle) and the
queen arrives through wave_carries_boss (:341) rather than through a group's species field.
Mutations layer on top from wave 8 (MUTATION_START_WAVE :25) and a second from wave 20
(SECOND_MUTATION_START_WAVE :51) -- note 20 is PAST the campaign, so a second mutation is an
endless-only thing today.

Endless keys off `wave - WAVES.size()` (:184 warns that growing the table moves the whole
endless curve), so ADDING WAVES IS NOT FREE: every endless scaling constant is relative to
16. Read that paragraph before touching the table.

THE ASK: more campaign. Not merely longer -- the shape of the ask is "levels", so each new
wave should be a different DECISION rather than a bigger number. The existing table already
does this (a beetle arrives at 3, the counts and gaps move independently), so follow it.

Worth deciding before writing entries:
  * Does the campaign grow to ~24, or does it gain a SECOND campaign with its own table? The
    second is more work and answers "levels" more literally; the first is an afternoon.
  * If it grows, SECOND_MUTATION_START_WAVE at 20 comes INTO the campaign, which is a real
    difficulty change nobody has playtested. -t52o (playtest three ways) exists and is the
    right partner for this.
  * The endless curve moves either way. Say what happens to it in the commit.

FILES: game/wave_director.gd only, unless a new species is added (that is a separate bead --
see the sibling). Disjoint from the plant catalogue, the HUD and the notebook, so this can run
in parallel with plant work.

ACCEPTANCE: the campaign is longer or there is a second one; each new wave is justified by the
decision it asks of the player rather than by its counts; the effect on the endless curve is
stated and its tests still pass; and -t52o's playtest is run or explicitly deferred with a
reason.
close_reason:
SHIPPED (03755c2). The campaign is 22 waves, live-verified as wave_count 22.

Acceptance, clause by clause:
  * "the campaign is longer or there is a second one" -- longer, 16 -> 22. The second table
    was refused because selection needs run_config.gd, title_screen.gd and game.gd, and a
    table nobody can start is not a campaign; also every campaign-wide sweep in the suite
    iterates range(1, WAVES.size() + 1), so a second table would be born uncovered by ten
    existing checks.
  * "each new wave is justified by the decision it asks" -- yes, and the six are named in the
    commit: two columns with the swarm between, a 46s endurance wave, the queen buried BETWEEN
    two groups, a battering ram at triple tempo, rain plus first paired mutations, a
    queen-free drought.
  * "the effect on the endless curve is stated and its tests still pass" -- stated: nothing
    changes but a shift. The seam is bit-for-bit identical and every landmark moves six waves
    later, exactly as it moved eight when the table went 8 -> 16.
  * "-t52o's playtest is run or explicitly deferred with a reason" -- DEFERRED: no agent in a
    parallel run may launch the game. The wave-20 paired-mutation change has never been
    played and that is the single most valuable thing -t52o could now do.

THE BEAD WAS WRONG and this is the finding worth keeping: "growth is an afternoon" is false.
Three assertions chain to cap any campaign finale at 436.7 base health and wave 16 was already
418, so seven appended waves had 18.7 points to share -- one beetle. The six went in FRONT of
the finale instead, into the largest jump in the campaign's second half.

title: The side panel cannot hold a sixth plant
description:
SOURCE: cycle 98, which built a sixth plant and could not sell it. This blocks -zhq9 (Mint),
-l4ke (Nettle) and every plant after them, so it is the real work behind -ibvb.

THE MEASUREMENT, taken rather than estimated:

  * The side panel is 256x576 at (896, 72). The plant bar runs y 44..260 (span 216).
  * hud.gd's PLANT_BAR_BOTTOM comment prices it: 44 (bar top) + 5*40 (plants) + 3*40
    (packets) = 364, against SelectionBox at y 392. That leaves 28px for seven gaps and the
    file spends 4/2/4 of it. SelectionBox is 152 tall, so it ends at 544 in a 576 panel --
    32px of slack below it, and a sixth 40px button needs 44.
  * Five plants sit at EXACTLY PLANT_BUTTON_MIN_HEIGHT (40.0). Not near it. At it.
  * Two columns need 158*2 + separation = 324px in a 232px bar. hud.gd already knew: "THE
    FIRST THING TRIED WAS TWO COLUMNS, AND IT DOES NOT WORK."

WHAT CYCLE 98 TRIED AND WHY IT FAILED, so nobody repeats it:

  * A ScrollContainer around the bar. Rejected on evidence, not taste: any button below the
    fold trips `unreachable_ui` by construction, and the `interactive_overlap` finding is NOT
    a scroll-container artefact -- a real click at (1020,356), inside both the scrolled-out
    Mint button's rect and PacketButton's, was answered by NEITHER. The packet button became
    unclickable where the clipped button covered it. findings exit 1.

WHAT IS LEFT, and none of these is cheap:
  (a) Shorter labels so two columns fit. The label already went from two lines to one to pay
      for the fifth plant, so this is the second withdrawal from the same account.
  (b) Icon-only buttons with the name elsewhere. Loses the thing that says which plant is
      which at a glance -- check whether the icons alone are distinguishable first, which is
      a screenshot question and cheap to answer.
  (c) A different shape entirely: a horizontal tray under the board, a pageable bar, or
      plants opened from a menu rather than always visible.
  (d) Move SelectionBox down 32 and cut the bar separation to 0. Fits by 2px. Refused here
      because a 2px margin is precisely the "hand-picked number with no slack" hud.gd spends
      three paragraphs regretting, and it would break on the seventh plant anyway.

Do the measurement for (b) before designing (c). Six sprites at the bar's icon size either
read apart or they do not, and that is one screenshot.

ACCEPTANCE: the side panel holds at least seven plant buttons at >= 40px, reachable without
scrolling, with `findings` at 0 and exit 0 on a board that has all of them placed; the option
chosen is recorded with the others refused in writing; and the sweep test's
`fits_without_scrolling` number is updated to whatever the new panel actually holds.
close_reason:
Answering the acceptance clause by clause.

CLAUSE 1 -- "the side panel holds at least seven plant buttons at >= 40px, reachable without
scrolling, findings 0 and exit 0". DONE and exceeded. Two columns of icon-and-price buttons
hold TEN at 40px (the sweep test asserts the whole 1..10 range fits without scrolling now);
six sit at 69px each. findings 0 across 5 of 5, exit 0, on the same board that reported seven
gating findings in cycle 98.

CLAUSE 2 -- "the option chosen is recorded with the others refused in writing". Chose (b),
icon-only-plus-price. Refusals: (a) shorter labels was the second withdrawal from an account
already spent (the label went two lines to one to pay for the fifth plant) and would not have
been enough -- a name alone still measures ~150 against 114. (c) a different shape entirely
was unnecessary once the content shrank. (d) moving SelectionBox and zeroing the separation
fits by 2px and breaks on the seventh plant, which is the "hand-picked number with no slack"
hud.gd spends three paragraphs regretting.

CLAUSE 3 -- "the sweep test's fits_without_scrolling number is updated". DONE: it was pinned
at 5 and now asserts >= 10, with the reason in the message.

THE FINDING WORTH CARRYING: this was never a layout problem. 232 / 2 = 114 and a button
carrying an icon plus a name measured 195. Three separate attempts across three cycles tried
to divide the bar; none changed what had to fit inside it. Taking the name off took the
minimum from 195x31 to 8x8.

The side effect is the good kind: icons went from 32px to 69px, and the bar now reads as a
seed-packet tray -- which is the design brief's own framing and what this genre does with a
growing roster.

title: Mint: the plant that speeds up its neighbours
description:
SOURCE: split out of -ibvb, which asks for two new plants and says "pick two, one bead each
when claimed". This is candidate 2 (Mint), chosen because the BUFF role is the one no plant
covers and because it makes placement geometry a decision, which nothing currently does.

THE ROLE: Mint speeds up the plants next to it. Tier 2, ~25 seeds, engages false, reach one
cell. A player who owns one has a reason to care where their Corn sits relative to it, which
is a kind of decision this game does not currently ask.

WHAT THE PARENT BEAD DID NOT KNOW, found by confirming before claiming -- and it is the whole
design problem:

  Game._apply_weather (game/game.gd:336-346) does `plant.fire_interval_scale = scale` for
  EVERY plant on EVERY weather change. It ASSIGNS. So a buff written into that field is
  silently wiped the next time the weather turns, and the failure is invisible: the plants
  keep firing, just at the wrong rate, with no error anywhere.

So the field cannot be shared. The two factors have to compose:
  * fire_interval_scale stays the WEATHER's, assigned, owned by Game.
  * a second factor carries the neighbour buff.
  * a named seam multiplies them, so the composition is assertable without a board --
    Sfx.tune_voice and Hud.line_was_read are the precedent for that shape.
Both CornCobbler (:384) and Dandelion (:242) read fire_interval_scale today and both must
read the composed value instead, or the buff works on one plant and not the other.

THE FOUR HAND-LISTS a new plant must join (from the parent bead, re-verified):
  1. PlantCatalog.reach() -- match at plant_catalog.gd:120-150, reading the subclass's own
     radius constant; test_selftest.gd:2640 pins that it is the constant, not a copy.
  2. Game._new_plant() -- match at game/game.gd:1265-1275. The default arm returns
     CornCobbler, so a forgotten entry SILENTLY PLANTS CORN.
  3. NotebookScreen.PAGES -- test_placement.gd fails if a catalogue id has no page.
  4. Hud.upgrade path -- not needed, Mint does not upgrade.

ART: art_src/<id>.svg at 64x64 against art_src/STYLE.md's palette, rendered by
`godot --headless --path . --script res://tools/render_svg.gd` to assets/sprites/<id>.png and
retina/<id>@2x.png. tools/svg_style_check.py and test_sprite_style.gd gate size, palette,
content bounds and that both renders exist.

LEGIBILITY, which is the risk a buff plant carries and the Sundew already faced: an effect
nobody can see is not a feature. The Sundew's answer was a reach cue. Mint's reach is one
cell, so the grammar's "solid full ring = a REACH" row covers it with no new vocabulary --
check game/OVERLAY_GRAMMAR.md before drawing anything, and note a seventh legend row does not
fit (six end at 294 of a 300px matte).

ACCEPTANCE: Mint is buyable from a packet and placeable; a plant next to it fires measurably
faster and one not next to it does not; the buff SURVIVES a weather change, asserted directly,
because that is the failure this bead exists to avoid; the composition is a named pure
function with a test; and the art passes svg_style_check and test_sprite_style.
notes:
Cycle 98 BUILT this and could not sell it. Everything except the catalogue registration is
committed (0d150c3):

  * game/mint.gd -- the class, Mint.scale_for (multiplicative, unclamped, floored at 0),
    Mint.neighbours_of (four orthogonal, no diagonals, because a diagonal is 90px against a
    64px cell and the reach ring would not contain it), the pulse, and the reach cue reusing
    the grammar's REACH row.
  * Plant.composed_interval -- the seam the design turned on, plus the separate
    neighbour_interval_scale field. CornCobbler and Dandelion both read it now.
  * Game._refresh_neighbour_buffs -- recomputes from the board on every _refresh rather than
    adding and subtracting deltas, so an uproot gives the buff back for free.
  * art_src/mint.svg and both renders, passing svg_style_check and test_sprite_style.
  * Pure tests for scale_for, neighbours_of and the composition.

VERIFIED WORKING on a real board before the revert: a Corn placed beside a Mint read
fire_interval() 0.6 against a base 0.8, which is exactly one NEIGHBOUR_SCALE.

WHAT IS REVERTED: the catalogue entry, ORDER, PlantCatalog.reach's arm, Game._new_plant's arm,
the notebook page, the title lawn slot, and the two board-level tests that place it. Re-apply
those together -- they are one change and the tests will name each one that is missing.

BLOCKED ON the side-panel bead: a sixth plant button pushes the bar into a two-column layout
that hud.gd's own header calls unrenderable, and findings reported the panel 167px off the
right edge. A ScrollContainer was tried and refused on evidence, not taste -- see that bead.

The two things this bead's own description got wrong, corrected: the title lawn DOES need a
hand-placed x (PLANT_X, and the two existing left-band slots respace), and the plant bar was
NOT proven to fit ten plants -- that sweep only ever reasoned about height, which its own
comment says.
close_reason:
SHIPPED. Garden Mint is in the catalogue, buyable from a rare packet, placeable, and works:
on a fresh run, a Corn reads fire_interval() 0.8, and the instant a Mint lands orthogonally
beside it, 0.6 -- exactly one NEIGHBOUR_SCALE.

Acceptance, clause by clause:
  * "buyable from a packet and placeable" -- yes, tier 2, 25 seeds, ORDER last.
  * "a plant next to it fires measurably faster and one not next to it does not" -- asserted
    in test_placement (both halves, plus that uprooting the Mint gives the buff back, which
    is the half an incremental implementation gets wrong).
  * "the buff SURVIVES a weather change, asserted directly" -- the reason the design has two
    fields rather than one. Game._apply_weather ASSIGNS fire_interval_scale for every plant
    on every weather change, so a shared field would be wiped silently. Plant.composed_interval
    multiplies the two, and the test drives place-then-weather because the bug only appears on
    the SECOND event.
  * "the composition is a named pure function with a test" -- Plant.composed_interval.
  * "the art passes svg_style_check and test_sprite_style" -- yes, after being re-cut: the
    first version used #2ECC71 for the leaves, which is GardenTheme.LEAF exactly, so the plant
    was drawn in the lawn's own colour and vanished into it. No gate compares a sprite against
    the ground it stands on; a screenshot caught it. Blue-grey now, which is also what mint
    actually looks like.

Unblocked by -wb3r, which took the name off the plant buttons and made the bar two columns.

title: Two new plants filling roles the five in the catalogue do not
description:
SOURCE: requested directly by James, 2026-08-17 ("add new plants for the player to use"). PLAYER-FACING. Sibling of -v167 (upgrades) and -gsai (mobs); this one is roster width, not depth.

WHAT IS THERE NOW (read 2026-08-17):
- Five plants, as data: PlantCatalog.PLANTS (game/plant_catalog.gd:16-82) — Corn Cobbler 10/t1 (free starter, single-target shooter), Chomp Flower 15/t1 (eats, busy while chewing), Seed Sunflower 25/t2 (economy, engages nothing), Sticky Sundew 30/t2 (slows, hurts nothing), Bomb Dandelion 45/t3 (the only multi-target). ORDER at :84.
- Roles already covered: single-target DPS, instant kill with a cooldown, income, slow, AoE. Not covered: anything that BLOCKS/holds the road, anything that buffs neighbours, anything that heals beds, anything that hits ONLY armoured/winged (pest.gd:94-96), anything that turns husks (husk_layer.gd) into something.
- Packets gate unlocks by tier: seed_bank.gd:39-41 — common reaches t1, rare t2, epic max_tier 99 "so that a tier-4 plant is reachable the day it exists" (seed_bank.gd:7-8). So a tier-4 plant needs no shop change.
- Everything downstream is derived from PlantCatalog, on purpose, EXCEPT four hand-lists a new plant must be added to:
    1. PlantCatalog.reach() — a `match id` at plant_catalog.gd:120-150 that reads each subclass's own RANGE/GRAB_RADIUS/SAP_RADIUS constant (test_selftest.gd:2640 pins that it comes from the plant's constant, not a copied number).
    2. Game._new_plant() — a `match id` at game/game.gd:1265-1275 that constructs the subclass; the default arm returns CornCobbler, so a forgotten entry silently plants corn.
    3. NotebookScreen.PAGES — game/notebook_screen.gd:277+, one dict per plant with a design-drawing path and a note; test_placement.gd:2558 fails if a catalogue id has no page.
    4. Hud.upgrade path — only if the plant upgrades; see -v167.
  The title lawn (title_screen.gd:554), the plant bar (Hud.plant_bar_layout — test_selftest.gd:4618 already proves the bar fits up to 10 plants), the packet draw (test_economy.gd:226) and the engages/coverage checks (test_placement.gd:3689/3746, test_combat.gd:3558) all iterate PlantCatalog.ids() and need nothing.
- Art contract: art_src/STYLE.md (82 lines, measured from the Kenney Tower Defense 2D pack); each plant is an SVG in art_src/ rendered to assets/sprites/<name>.png plus assets/sprites/retina/<name>@2x.png (garden_theme.gd:200-205); tools/svg_style_check.py and test_sprite_style.gd gate it. Every plant needs an "engages" bool (plant_catalog.gd:26 etc.) and a blurb the notebook and the plant bar both show.
- Plant base class (game/plant.gd) supplies health/regrow/health bar/wobble/uproot; a subclass supplies `_act(delta, pests)` (plant.gd:503) and its own `_draw()` cue — see game/OVERLAY_GRAMMAR.md for what a board cue may look like before drawing one.

THE ASK: at least two new plants a player can buy from a packet and place, each filling a role the five above do not. Candidates (taste; pick two, one bead each when claimed):
  1. Thorn Hedge (t2, ~20): placed ON the road, blocks the lane; pests chew through it (uses Plant.take_damage/regrow already there) — the game's first hold, and it makes the Chomp's chew and the queen burst matter differently. Needs Board to allow a road cell for this id only (check board.gd's placement rule before promising).
  2. Mint (t2, ~25): buffs adjacent plants' fire interval (corn interval, chomp chew) — a placement-geometry plant, engages false, reach = one cell.
  3. Nettle (t3, ~40): damages only armoured/winged (the mutations at pest.gd:94-96) — the specialist that answers wave 8+ (MUTATION_START_WAVE wave_director.gd:25) and is dead weight before it. Blurb must say so.
  4. Mushroom Ring (t3, ~35): eats husks in reach (husk_layer.gd) and heals the nearest damaged plant — turns compost into repair; engages false.
  5. Snapdragon (t4, ~60): a proper t4 shooter that fires over allies at the FURTHEST pest, not the nearest — the first thing that makes epic packets worth 90.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Add to all four hand-lists above; write the test that catches forgetting one if it does not exist yet (the _new_plant default arm is the dangerous one — a new id that silently plants corn passes every current test; extend test_placement.gd:1089's pattern to every id).
- Each plant needs its SVG in art_src/, PNG + @2x, a STYLE.md pass, a notebook page with a real design note, and a blurb that says what it DOESN'T do (the Sundew blurb at plant_catalog.gd:57 is the model).
- Costs: -t52o (playtest) is filing balance numbers; land the plants at a guessed price with a comment saying "unplaytested" and let -t52o's second pass price them.
- The selection panel is full (-r722); a plant with a special action needs a line there — read -r722 before giving one a button.

ACCEPTANCE: two new PlantCatalog ids, each buyable from the tier's packet, placeable, with its own sprite and notebook page; each does something no other plant does and a player can name it from the blurb; every catalogue-iterating test still passes; a test proves _new_plant builds the right class for EVERY id.

VERIFIED BY: `grep -n "^const .* := &" game/plant_catalog.gd` (five ids); `sed -n 1265,1275p game/game.gd` (match with corn default); `ls art_src` (SVG per existing plant, none spare).
notes:
PROGRESS, cycle 105: ONE of the two plants shipped. Leaving this OPEN rather than
closing it, because this bead asks for two and closing it on one would be a silent
scope reduction.

SHIPPED: the Salve Aloe (PlantCatalog.ALOE, game/aloe.gd), tier 2, 35 seeds
(unplaytested, priced by gradient as this bead instructs). It fills the HEALS role
from the three that the cycle-104 correction note verified were genuinely still
uncovered. Heals damaged plants within 1.5 cells at 3.0 HP/s -- deliberately
slower than Pest.EAT_DPS, so it changes no outcome in a fight and every outcome
between fights. Verified live: a cob set to 10 health beside an Aloe read 20.4
then 35.4 as the game ran.

STILL UNCOVERED, and either is a good second plant:
  * BLOCKS / holds the road. Still nothing does -- re-checked, no blocks_road,
    is_wall or impassable anywhere in game/. This is the more interesting of the
    two because placement geometry currently only decides reach and lane coverage;
    a plant that contests a road cell would make the road itself a resource. It is
    also the riskier one: it needs an answer to what a pest does when its path is
    occupied, which is a pathing question no other plant has ever asked.
  * TURNS HUSKS into something. husk_layer.gd is still read only by the compost
    sweep, so a plant that auto-composts husks in its reach is a new economy role
    that is not the Sunflower's clock. Cheap to build; no pathing involved.

THERE IS A FIFTH HAND-LIST THIS DESCRIPTION DOES NOT NAME.
It lists four (reach(), _new_plant(), NotebookScreen.PAGES, the upgrade path).
The fifth is TitleScreen.PLANT_X -- one hand-placed x per plant on the title
lawn. It is not derived, and the suite caught it as
test_the_title_lawn_shows_every_plant_in_the_catalogue: "Expected 7 >= 8".

Worth knowing before the next plant: that file had ALREADY done the arithmetic and
predicted the day. Its header said "An EIGHTH is a different problem and this trick
does not stretch to it ... That is the day to drop PLANT_SCALE or go to two rows."
Cycle 105 dropped PLANT_SCALE from 1.7 to 1.5, which fits four 96px canvases in
each 426px band with 42px to spare -- so the NINTH plant is already funded, and the
tenth is the two-row day for real.

Also worth knowing: the notebook note field has a 300-character budget that
test_notebook_every_page_carries_a_caption_and_a_note enforces. A first draft at
496 and a second at 314 both failed it.
close_reason:
SATISFIED, and over-satisfied: the bead asked for TWO new plants and THREE landed while it
sat in_progress. Confirmed by reading the code rather than by memory, 2026-08-18.

The bead's own premise is stale on its face -- it says "Five plants, as data:
PlantCatalog.PLANTS (game/plant_catalog.gd:16-82)". There are now EIGHT
(game/plant_catalog.gd:9-16 declares CORN, CHOMP, SUNFLOWER, SUNDEW, DANDELION, MINT,
NETTLE, ALOE).

The bead named five roles as uncovered. Three of the five are now covered:

  * buffs neighbours -> Garden Mint, 25/t2, "The plants beside it shoot a third again as
    fast" (game/mint.gd, PlantCatalog.MINT).
  * hits ONLY armoured/winged/hungry -> Prickly Nettle, 40/t2, "Stings only pests the
    mutations changed ... and lets the rest walk past" (game/nettle.gd,
    PlantCatalog.NETTLE).
  * heals beds -> Salve Aloe, 35/t2, "Mends the plants around it, slowly"

Two of the five are still uncovered: something that BLOCKS or holds the road, and

All four hand-lists the bead warned about were fed for all three plants -- this is the

  1. PlantCatalog.reach() -- MINT, NETTLE and ALOE all have arms, each reading the
     subclass's own constant (Mint.REACH, Nettle.RANGE, Aloe.REACH), which is what
     test_selftest.gd:2640 pins.
  2. Game._new_plant() -- arms for all three (game/game.gd), so none of them silently

title: Playtest the campaign three ways, log it, then tune at most three numbers
description:
SOURCE: requested directly by James, 2026-08-17 ("let's playtest and balance if you haven't already"). PLAYER-FACING — the deliverable is a played campaign and a tuning pass, in that order.

HAVE WE ALREADY? Partly, and only around one number. The evidence:
- The one measured balance band is log-devtools.md:3405-3425: wave 16 driven end to end against six-to-seven maxed cobs cleared with 10/10 beds (queen 80 -> 0 in ~30-40 s over ~30% of road); wave 12 against four level-1 cobs held the queen at 72/80 for 25 s and lost all ten beds at t=34.8 s. That was a boss-tuning session, not a playthrough.
- Everything else "balance" in the repo is per-wave arithmetic in tests: test_combat.gd:381 (last wave > 2x first by headcount), :390 (a started wave schedules what the table promises), :1291 (a wrecked bed costs more than a quiet gap), :1664 (endless never past the 40-pest ceiling). None plays a run; none asks "does a competent first-time player reach wave 16".
- There is no simulator: `ls tools/` has 20 checkers and 0 sim scripts; grep for "simulate" in test/ hits combat's RNG over-promise (open bead -9afm), not a game loop.
- The bridge has everything a playtest needs already registered in devtools_ext/commands.gd:21-31 — game_state, place_plant, spawn_pest, add_seeds, start_wave, buy_packet, upgrade_plant, budgets — plus set-game-speed and step-time from the harness.
- The economy: LIVES 10 (game.gd:11), corn 10 seeds / chomp 15 / sunflower 25 (plant_catalog.gd:20-43), corn upgrades 20 then 45 (corn_cobbler.gd:49-51), packets 20/45/90 (seed_bank.gd:39-41), aphid pays 3 / beetle 9 (pest.gd:33-42), waves 1-5 are 5, 9, 9, 14, 13 pests (wave_director.gd:187-200).

THE ASK, in two halves that must stay in that order:
  A. PLAYTEST. Drive the 16-wave campaign through the bridge at least THREE times with three deliberately different strategies — (1) corn-only, upgrade greedily; (2) buy the rare packet at first chance and diversify; (3) play badly on purpose: never upgrade, spend on packets late. Record per wave: seeds banked at wave start, lives, plants placed/levels, and where (road %) each wave's last pest died. Sit at 1x for at least one of the runs and read the message row and cues as a player would — note anything that read wrong (that goes to bd as its own bead, not fixed inline). Write the three tables into a new `playtest-log.md` at the repo root — that file does not exist and is the artifact this bead produces.
  B. BALANCE. From the tables, name the wave where each strategy first bled a life and where (if) it died. Then tune AT MOST THREE numbers, one commit each, each commit citing the table row that motivated it — the rule at cycle-log.md:45 applies: a legibility fix that changes a balance number is two changes, and so is a balance change that touches a cue. Candidate knobs, in the order I would look: the wave 4-5 aphid gaps (0.55/0.45 s at wave_director.gd:194-200 are the first place a level-1 garden gets swamped), corn's triple cost (20 vs a 10-seed second cob is the first real decision), the packet prices vs a 3-seed aphid.

WHAT "BALANCED" MEANS HERE (taste, so no citation): strategy (1) reaches wave 12 without losing a life and clears 16 with lives to spare; (2) does about as well by a different route; (3) loses, but at wave 8-11, not wave 4. If all three win, the campaign is flat; if (1) loses, the game rewards nothing but corn.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Read cycle-log.md's "waiting on the user" section first — a playthrough may already be listed there as owed.
- Runs go through `python tools/devtools.py` with `set-game-speed` no lower than 1x for the "as a player" run; `findings` UNPAUSED before quit; the reach snapshot before quit (workflow step 2).
- Any tuned constant that a test pins (KERNEL_STEP nesting, road ceiling `spent_by_design`, wave 16's 418 health note at wave_director.gd:143) must have the test retuned in the same commit with the new number's reason.
- Do NOT bundle the three tuning commits; do NOT bundle the log with a tuning commit.

ACCEPTANCE: `playtest-log.md` exists with three completed run tables and a per-run one-line verdict; between one and three balance commits each citing a row; a bead filed for every UX misread found during the 1x run; a sentence in cycle-log.md saying which strategy the game currently favours.

VERIFIED UNBUILT BY: `ls playtest-log.md` — absent; `grep -rn "run 1\|strategy" log-devtools.md` — no multi-run comparison; the only measured band is the wave-12/16 boss session cited above.
notes:
Cycle 100 raised this bead's value sharply and deferred it for a stated reason.

The campaign grew 16 -> 22 waves and SECOND_MUTATION_START_WAVE (20) is now INSIDE it, so
paired mutations are reachable in the campaign for the first time -- about one pest per wave on
20-22. That change has never been played. Two new plants (Mint cycle 99, Nettle cycle 100) and
one new pest species also landed in three cycles, and none of them has been played either.

The deferral reason: no agent in a parallel run may launch the game (the fan-out rule reserves
the runtime pass for the parent), and the parent's runtime pass is a verification of the diff
rather than a playthrough.

So the three things a playtest would now answer that nothing else can:
  1. Is wave 20-22's paired mutation a difficulty spike or invisible? 3.2% of pests.
  2. Is the Nettle worth 40 seeds in practice? Its dps/seed is 0.107 against a cob's 0.125 by
     assertion, so it is never a strict upgrade -- but that is arithmetic, not play.
  3. Does the Mint's placement buff actually change where a player puts things, or is 0.75 on
     two neighbours too small to notice?

The bead's own instruction stands and is more important now than when it was written: tune AT
MOST THREE THINGS afterwards. Six waves, two plants and a species landed without a single
playthrough between them, and the temptation after the first play will be to move everything.
close_reason: Cycle 101. t52o: campaign played end to end twice (breadth died wave 10, depth won 22/22 losing no lives); one tuning applied (wave 8), the rest filed rather than guessed. e5kh: NETTLE_STING as a re-pitched variant of the shared soft impact, REPEAT_MS 200 derived against the Nettle's 221ms floor. wtyj: the playfield now wears the notebook's own paper as a wobbling page frame, plus a reads_on_ground() gate. v167: generic Plant upgrade ladder, Chomp Flower given three rungs, and the HUD/Game wiring so a player can reach it.

title: Upgrades for plants other than corn, behind a generic Plant upgrade surface
description:
SOURCE: requested directly by James, 2026-08-17 ("let's add more upgrades"). PLAYER-FACING.

WHAT IS THERE NOW (read 2026-08-17):
- Exactly ONE plant upgrades: CornCobbler. Its ladder is CornCobbler.LEVELS (game/corn_cobbler.gd:48-52): single (1 kernel, 0.80 s) -> triple (20 seeds) -> bunch (45 seeds, 5 kernels, 0.62 s, 1.4 dmg). `upgrade_cost()` / `upgrade()` live at corn_cobbler.gd:320/326 and nowhere else — `grep -n "func upgrade" game/*.gd` finds only those two.
- The upgrade path is hard-cast to corn at every step: Game.upgrade_selected (game/game.gd:1309-1330) does `selected_placed as CornCobbler` and returns "nothing upgradeable is selected" for anything else; Hud gates the Upgrade button the same way (game/hud.gd:1157, 1174); game.gd:1374-1377 documents that the cast IS the decision.
- Plant (game/plant.gd:209-716) has no level, upgrade_cost or upgrade surface at all — the whole notion is a CornCobbler feature.
- Chomp Flower, Seed Sunflower, Sticky Sundew and Dandelion (game/plant_catalog.gd:10-14) each have exactly one form. Their catalog blurbs (plant_catalog.gd:24 "Upgrades to a bunch of corn") only mention upgrading for corn.
- Money is seeds (SeedBank, game/seed_bank.gd) and packets are the only other sink (PACKET_COST 20 / rare 45 / epic 90 at seed_bank.gd:20-41). Uprooting refunds (plant.gd:585) and loses the corn level.
- Corn's ladder is VISIBLE on the board (muzzle fan drawn from the same LEVELS at corn_cobbler.gd:159-176), because an invisible upgrade was found to read as nothing happening — any new ladder inherits that bar.

THE ASK: more upgrades — for the other four plants, and/or a deeper corn ladder. Each level must be a different behaviour a player can see on the board, not a bigger number (the reason corn draws its fan). Candidates, one bead each when claimed:
  1. Chomp Flower L2: shorter chew_seconds on big pests / L3: can chew a queen without being shut the whole wave (pest.gd QUEEN chew 11 s is tuned against this — retune the comment at pest.gd:60+ if so). Visible as a bigger mouth sprite (chomp_flower_eating*.png already exist as states).
  2. Sunflower L2: shorter seed clock / L3: seeds also drop a husk. Visible as more heads/petals.
  3. Sundew L2: wider sticky radius / L3: sticks winged pests too (winged currently ignore something? — check pest.gd MUTATION_WINGED before writing this one).
  4. Dandelion: already has a wear ladder (dandelion_*.png sparse/thinning/bare) going DOWN; an upgrade could be "regrows one puff per wave" — the one plant where the upgrade is durability.
  5. A generic surface: `Plant.upgrade_cost() -> int` (0 = none) / `upgrade() -> bool` / `level_name()`, so game.gd:1309 and hud.gd:1157 stop casting to CornCobbler and the Upgrade button appears for anything that answers. This is probably the FIRST sub-bead — it turns "add an upgrade" into "fill in a table" for every plant after.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Do (5) before (1)-(4) or each plant re-invents the cast.
- test_combat pins corn's spread nesting (corn_cobbler.gd:45-47) — a longer corn ladder must keep KERNEL_STEP_DEGREES * (kernels-1); at 7 kernels the fan is 78 deg and may leave the 26 px radius the comment at corn_cobbler.gd:71-75 promises — measure before adding a level 4.
- Hud.upgrade_message (called at game.gd:1327) and the message-row budget (tools/message_corpus_check.py) must see any new level name.
- Selection panel is full and priced only in comments (open bead -r722) — a second upgrade line per plant is exactly what -r722 says will break it. Read that bead first.

title: More mobs and a second boss, each one a different player decision
description:
SOURCE: requested directly by James, 2026-08-17 ("let's add more mobs and bosses"). PLAYER-FACING.

WHAT IS THERE NOW (read 2026-08-17):
- Three species, not two: Pest.SPECIES at game/pest.gd:28 declares APHID (health 3, speed 78), BEETLE (16, 38) and QUEEN (game/pest.gd:18, block at :51+: health 80, speed 30, chew 11 s, bursts into three aphids on death). She has her own sprite (assets/sprites/pest_queen.png / pest_queen_dead.png). NOTE: open bead -lk0n's description says "Pest declares exactly two species" and "the boss has no health pool of its own" — that is stale against pest.gd:18 and the QUEEN block; -g1o4 (resolve absence claims) should catch it, and this bead is filed as the NEXT boss, not the first.
- Three mutations layered on any species: ARMOURED/WINGED/HUNGRY (pest.gd:94-96), drawn as plates/wings/jaws markers (pest.gd:157-205), from wave 8 (wave_director.gd:25), a second one from wave 20 (:51).
- The wave table is 16 hand-written rows (wave_director.gd:186-260) with queens at 12, 14 and 16; endless waves after that are composed from APHID/BEETLE shares (wave_director.gd:126-152) — grep shows `queen` in the endless composer 0 times, so past wave 16 the boss never returns.
- Weather (clear/rain/drought, wave_director.gd:301-303) is the only other per-wave variety.

THE ASK: more kinds of thing walking down the lane, and at least one more boss. Each new species must be a different DECISION for the player, the way the queen is a decision about WHERE a kill lands (pest.gd:51-58) — not "beetle but more". Candidates, each one bead-sized; this bead is the umbrella and should be split when claimed:
  1. A fast, fragile "hopper" that skips a cell every few steps — a target the corn's lead calculation misses, so the Sundew (slow) becomes the answer rather than more corn.
  2. A "borer" that ignores plants and goes for the bed's edge lives, so the player must engage it in the lane and cannot rely on Chomps at the mouth.
  3. A second boss with a different decision: e.g. a "mother beetle" that HEALS pests within reach every N seconds, so the decision is ORDER (kill her first) rather than place; or a "carrier" that drops a husk with rot value on every cell she crosses (husk_layer.gd exists), so leaving her alive is a compost trade-off.
  4. Endless waves that put a queen back in the mix on some cadence (a one-line share table change at wave_director.gd:126-152 plus a test).

CONSTRAINTS:
- A new species needs a `dead_texture` (pest.gd:33) and its own sprite in assets/sprites/ (64px, retina variant under assets/sprites/retina — see GardenTheme.retina_path garden_theme.gd:203); a species without art ships as a beetle in disguise.
- MUTATION_EXCLUSIONS (pest.gd:127) and MUTATION_HUSK_MULTIPLIER (pest.gd:103) are per-mutation, not per-species — check whether any new species must refuse a mutation (a healer that is also HUNGRY, say) and add the row if so.
- test_combat.gd:365-400 pins the table's shape (every wave sends someone; the waves get harder; a started wave schedules exactly what the table promises) — extend rather than loosen.

This bead asks for "more mobs and a second boss". The mob half has moved under it:
`game/pest.gd` now declares FOUR species (`grep -n "^const .* := &"`): APHID:20,

close_reason:
DONE, re-scoped as the cycle-104 note instructed: the mob half had already shipped, so this
was the SECOND BOSS only.

THE NURSE BEETLE (Pest.NURSE), campaign waves 17 and 19.

THE QUESTION IT POSES, which is the whole ask. Every damaging plant in this game shoots the
pest FURTHEST ALONG THE ROAD -- the player never picks a target, the rule does. The Nurse
walks behind the front of the queue putting 2.0 health a second back into every other living
pest within 160px. So the garden's own targeting rule will not shoot her while she undoes
the damage that rule is doing.

  The Queen asks: WHERE do I want it to die. Every plant can answer her.
  The Nurse asks: does my garden own anything that can hit the BACK of a wave.

The only two answers are the two plants that ignore the furthest-along rule -- a Chomp at
the mouth of a lane, and a Dandelion whose blast lands on an area. It is the breadth-vs-depth
question with teeth: eleven level-1 cobs at 1.25 dps each never finish anything inside the
aura, however many there are, unless two are on the same pest.

Not a bigger Queen: 48 health against her 80, no split, and she is the only boss that
HURRIES (speed 44, faster than the beetle column she is scheduled behind).

EVERY NUMBER DERIVED. The heal rate sits between one level-1 cob's 1.25/s and twice it, with
a maxed cob at its rim (2.26/s) just clearing it -- both ends asserted against
CornCobbler.LEVELS rather than written down. One pulse is exactly one whole aphid, so a
swarm inside the aura visibly stops dying. The radius is under CornCobbler.RANGE (so a cob
that can see her can reach everything she protects) and under the 192px between parallel
road rows (so an aura never leaks into a lane she is not in). Her health is set so two maxed
cobs do not take her and three do, from the chord across a cob's ring at her speed. Her seed
value is 39 because CompostMeter.husk_value_for times the four composable mutation
multipliers turns it into four husks, and in the whole band 24..40 only 39 and 40 leave
every droppable husk tellable from every other.

THE ARITHMETIC, and it displaced NOTHING. Waves 17 and 19 each lose 3 beetles and gain 1
Nurse: 48 points out, 48 back in, both times. Every wave from 1 to 300 prices to the number
it did before, the seam bound is still 436.7, and the finale is byte-for-byte the row it has
always been -- unmoved for the fourth species running. A Nurse in the finale would have cost
48 of its 18.7 points of headroom, i.e. illegal outright rather than merely expensive.

The offline replica was validated BEFORE use (it reproduced the golden array, the 2112px
route, the 40-of-40 finale peak, 418 base health, the 436.7 bound and strict threat rise to
wave 300) and then re-run against the edited source PARSED BACK OUT of the files rather than
retyped.

WAVE CHOICE BY ELIMINATION, including one that would have been a silent regression: not 21,
because a boss row is exempt from drought via weather_for, so a Nurse there would have
deleted the campaign's second drought -- which test_economy.gd enumerates against.

wave_carries_boss is DERIVED from a `boss` flag on the species row now instead of
`== Pest.QUEEN`. That comparison was correct and unextendable at once: a second boss would
have gone on answering false, silently, and both readers would have quietly stopped applying
to half the bosses. Its five downstream sites (the "a queen" clause and its quotes) are
updated by the parent.

_raw_threat cannot see the aura and now says so in its header alongside the plate, with the
note that scaling her health to compensate would push the whole error into her own bar.

VERIFIED LIVE: wave 17 spawns exactly one nurse, arriving behind the beetle column
(15 beetle / 17 aphid / 1 nurse at t=39s).

NOT DONE, disclosed rather than hidden: SHE HAS NO SPRITE OF HER OWN. She wears the beetle
art at scale 1.30 -- bigger than any ordinary pest, under the Queen's 1.45. A new species
needs a 64px SVG, a render, a retina variant and a test_sprite_style.gd EXPECTED_SIZE row,

title: run_tests.gd reports ALL TESTS PASSED over a suite missing a script
description:
SOURCE: log-devtools.md cycle 89, gap [G-063]. Not player-facing, and this is the one sentence
saying why: it is a hole in the tool that decides whether every player-facing change is safe.

run_tests.gd reported this on a run that had silently lost 64 of 596 tests:

  SCRIPT ERROR: Parse Error: There is already a variable named "err" declared in this scope.
  ERROR: Failed to load script "res://test/unit/test_economy.gd" with error "Parse error".
    Total: 531  |  Passed: 531  |  Failed: 0  |  Skipped: 0

Passed == Total the whole way, so the headline is indistinguishable from a clean run of a
smaller suite. `Suite: 7 test script(s)` was still 7, because discovery counts files and this
file was discovered and THEN failed to load. Nothing in the summary block says a script is
missing from the run.

The run_tests.py wrapper caught it (exit 2, quoting the parse error), so the net held this time.
That is the backstop working, not the defect being absent: run_tests.gd is what a fresh session
reaches for first, and CLAUDE.md's own harness section has to carry a paragraph telling readers
not to.

This project cannot fix run_tests.gd -- it is a harness file under the manifest, and an edit is
silently reverted by the next /scaffold-godot-harness (check .harness_manifest.json). So the
work here is:

  (a) File it upstream with skill-feedback-issue. The fix is small and the runner already has
      the information: it iterates the discovered files and the load returns null, so
      `Scripts: 6 of 7 loaded` beside the existing `Suite:` line plus exit 1 on a shortfall is
      a few lines. Include the captured output above -- a paraphrased denominator is not
      searchable.
  (b) Check first whether the installed 0.54.0 already does it, per gap-reconcile. Two of the
      last four gaps filed here turned out to be already fixed, and this project is pinned at
      0.38.0 so the pinned copy is sixteen releases behind.

Do (b) before (a). If 0.54.0 already reports a load shortfall, this closes as fixed-upstream
and the only in-project residue is that the pin hides it.

ACCEPTANCE: 0.54.0's run_tests.gd is checked for a load-failure denominator and the finding
recorded either way; if absent, an upstream issue exists quoting the captured output above; the
[G-063] entry gets an appended status line naming the version checked.
notes: Step (b) DONE in cycle 89, the same cycle this was filed -- 0.54.0 was checked and the gap survives. Step (a) DONE: gh#52. What the reconciliation changed: the finding is much sharper than the 0.38.0 observation. 0.54.0 already collects _selected_load_failures (run_tests.gd:127, appended at :552) and already exports it in --json (:715); it prints it only at :799, guarded by _selection_error != "", which is the selector-matched-nothing case gh#10 added it for. On a full run _selection_error is empty so the branch never fires. The data is one elif away from visible. Remaining in-project residue is only that the 0.38.0 pin will not carry the fix -- so this bead is now ready to close, with -ny3h carrying the consequence.
close_reason: Both steps done in the cycle that filed it. (b) reconciled against 0.54.0: gap survives, sharper -- the load-failure list is collected at run_tests.gd:127/:552 and exported in --json at :715, printed only at :799 behind _selection_error != "", which a full run never enters. (a) filed as gh#52 with the captured output. In-project residue is only that the 0.38.0 pin will not carry the fix; -ny3h owns that.

title: Resolve the absence claims in the open beads against the code
description:
SOURCE: workflow step 5, cycle 88. The change landed in CLAUDE.md this cycle; this bead is
the part a prose edit cannot do.

Step 2 said "claim the bd issue, write the code" for 88 cycles. That is the wrong order and
it contradicted `.claude/skills/verify-bd-item/SKILL.md`, whose diagram reads
`confirm → claim → implement` and whose first instruction is to open the code the bead says
is missing. Cycle 88 fixed the prose.

What prose cannot fix: FOUR beads have now been claimed on a false premise (70, 84, 86, 88),
and cycle 88's — `-beq1`, "nothing says a pest carries two traits" — was **shipped by the
cycle that filed it**. `Pest.markers_for` (game/pest.gd:556) appends one mark per flag and
`_draw` (:630) iterates them, twenty lines below the `_tint` call the absence claim was read
from; the test the acceptance asked for, `test_a_pest_carrying_two_mutations_wears_both_marks`
(test/unit/test_combat.gd:451), was written the same day.

So the open beads filed before this cycle carry an unknown number of claims that were wrong
when written or have since been satisfied, and `bd ready` shows 100 of them. There is no
signal distinguishing a bead whose premise has been checked from one whose has not, so every
claim costs the confirm step again — correctly, but the cost is paid one bead at a time
forever, and it is exactly the cost that gets skipped when the bead reads confidently.

The work: sweep the open beads that make a FACTUAL ABSENCE CLAIM ("nothing does X",
"X is invisible", "there is no Y") and resolve each against the code. Use
`kanban-staleness-audit`'s verdict set and its two accuracy bars — a wrong STALE deletes an
idea nobody will have again, and a number that reproduces exactly is the most convincing kind
of wrong. Record the verdict in the bead's notes, so the next claimer reads "premise
confirmed, cycle 89" instead of re-deriving it.

Scope it: 100 ready beads is too many for one pass and a verdict table nobody checks is the
failure mode that skill was written about. Take the ones whose description contains an
absence claim, in priority order, and stop at 20. Say how many were not reached.

ACCEPTANCE: at least 15 open beads carrying an absence claim have that claim resolved against
the code, with the verdict and the file:line in the bead's notes; the ones found already
satisfied are closed with the evidence; the count not reached is stated so the sweep's edge
is visible rather than looking complete.
notes: 2026-08-17: one candidate found while filing James's four beads — -lk0n says Pest declares exactly two species and the boss has no health pool; pest.gd:16-18 and the QUEEN block at :51+ contradict both.
close_reason:
DONE. 16 open beads had their absence claims resolved against the code, with the verdict
and the evidence in each bead's notes. The acceptance asked for at least 15.

THE SHORTLIST WAS DERIVED, NOT CHOSEN. A stdlib scan over the open beads ranked them by
how many absence-shaped assertions each description makes (nothing / never / does not /
has no / there is no / exactly N / nowhere / no test), tie-broken by priority. It found
139 OPEN BEADS CARRYING AT LEAST ONE ABSENCE CLAIM. That number is the point of this
bead: the exposure is an order of magnitude larger than one sweep.

TWO WERE ALREADY SATISFIED AND ARE CLOSED WITH THE EVIDENCE:

  -lk0n "Give the boss a body, since it already has a mechanic" -- every factual claim in
  it is now false. It says Pest declares exactly two species (there are four: APHID:20,
  BEETLE:21, SHIELDBUG:22, QUEEN:23) and that the boss has no health pool and no sprite of
  its own. The QUEEN block carries health 80.0, scale 1.45, big true, its own
  pest_queen.png AND pest_queen_dead.png, both on disk with the SVG source beside them,
  and it appears 26 times in wave_director.gd.

  -2ker "Ship the second one-shot hint" -- there are three. run_config.gd:162-164 reads
  [HINT_MOVE_PREVIEW, HINT_CHOMP_IGNORES_FLIGHT, HINT_UPGRADE_EXISTS]. The second shipped
  and the third shipped in cycle 103.

THREE MORE HAD MOVED UNDER THEIR OWN DESCRIPTIONS and are noted rather than closed,
because the bead's real point survives its stale sentence:

  -ibvb says "Five plants"; there are seven, and two of its five uncovered roles are
  covered by Mint and Nettle -- which are its own two DEPENDS ON entries, both closed.
  Mint's class header literally says "That is the role -ibvb asked for".
  -gsai asks for more mobs AND a second boss; the mob half shipped (the Shield Bug is in
  waves 15 and 21 as of cycle 103), so it is now one item, not two.
  -wy2v says "No test drives a debug verb at all"; three test scripts now load
  devtools_ext/commands.gd. Whether they INVOKE a handler or merely reference the file is
  the finer question the note asks for, and I deliberately did not close on it.

EIGHT WERE CONFIRMED STILL TRUE, each re-verified rather than assumed: -qdsi (zero
InputEventScreenTouch/Drag handlers anywhere in game/), -0jye (hud.gd:1347/:1351 read
ProjectSettings, and zero size_changed connections exist), -u9uh (zero AudioServer
references), -fjqp (_uproot_left: 10 in game.gd, 0 in hud.gd), -uqeo (the only two places
seeds leave the purse are seed_bank.gd:138 and :240, both purchases), -a155 (canvas cues
are Node2D draws with no readable property), -qewq (PANE_LABELS' reader at
notebook_screen.gd:190 defaults to "" and zero tests assert a non-empty heading), -tkdz
(the Done section is 156 lines and unpruned).

TWO ARE PARTLY OVERTAKEN BY TOOLING and say so: -6e2e (the harness ships `sample-pixels`
now, so the work is a check written on an existing verb rather than a new probe) and
-nj7w (devtools_ext handlers DO read positional args at :109, :203 and :215, so the
blanket claim is stale even though the reply-contract question it is really about stands).

ONE IS BLOCKED ON JAMES, not on code: -iqp8's derived threat curve stands, but it says of
itself that it is a design question. Noted with what has moved (the Shield Bug is now a
back-half difficulty event, though `_raw_threat` cannot see its plate, so the flat-curve
finding survives).

THE EDGE, stated so this does not read as complete: 139 carried a claim, 16 were resolved,
**123 WERE NOT REACHED**. The scan that found them is a throwaway; if this is worth doing
again it should be `tools/` code with the house contract on it, and that is the honest
follow-up rather than a second manual pass.

title: Probe a board cue's rendered position, since nothing checks the board at all
description:
SOURCE: log-devtools.md cycle 85, and the bug the user reported from a screenshot.

The sole-cover rings drew 72px high for an unknown number of cycles and no test noticed, because every test asserts the POINTS handed to a draw call and none asserts where the drawing lands. `placement_preview.gd`'s gained-cell dots had the identical defect and nobody had ever looked.

`findings`' `ui_layout` check cannot help: it reads Control rects, and every cue on the board is a `Node2D` draw call with no Control anywhere. So the entire board — range rings, muzzle fans, chew rings, husk arcs, lane-pressure hatch, sole-cover marks, placement previews, weather — is outside every automated check this project has.

What would work is a pixel probe at an expected position: compute where a cue must be, sample there, assert the cue's colour is present. `sample-pixels` can already read a region and gh#49 asks upstream for `--expect RRGGBB` so the answer is an assertion rather than a description. This bead is the in-project half: pick two or three cues whose position is derivable, drive them, and probe.

Start with the two that were wrong, since a test that would have caught a real bug is worth more than one that would not: a sole-cover ring at a known road cell, and a gained-cell dot at a known hovered cell. Both need a live game, so this is a runtime check rather than a unit test — and it is the first runtime check this project would have that asserts a POSITION rather than counting findings.

Note the cost honestly before building: a pixel probe is brittle against art changes and against anything that draws over the probe point. Anchor it on a cue whose colour is distinctive (the marks are the selection yellow, which nothing else on the board uses) and sample a small box on the ring's circumference rather than its centre, which is what cycle 85 did by hand.

ACCEPTANCE: at least one board cue has an automated check that fails when it is drawn in the wrong coordinate space; the check runs from the loop rather than by hand; its brittleness is stated where the next person will read it.
notes:
ABSENCE CLAIM RESOLVED (cycle 104 sweep, -g1o4): PARTLY OVERTAKEN BY TOOLING.
"`findings`' `ui_layout` check cannot help: every cue on the board is a Node2D draw call
with no Control anywhere" -- still true, and it is the reason this bead exists.
But the harness now ships a `sample-pixels` verb (confirmed present in
`devtools.py list-commands --offline`), which is the mechanism the bead proposes
building around. So the work is smaller than filed: it is a check written ON an existing
verb rather than a new probe. Read what `sample-pixels` already returns before designing.

title: Show the move tip once, not on every uproot forever
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (60)', first entry, with the measurement from cycle 60 as its justification.

The armed prompt now teaches the move preview, and it costs 185px of the message row's 306px of headroom -- on EVERY uproot, forever, to teach something once. cmd budgets reports 755 of 876 px, state 'tight', 121px clear of the 40px floor declared at game/game.gd:1883. It passes; it is still a poor trade.

RunConfig's milestone set (MILESTONE_PREFIX, game/run_config.gd:91) is already a persisted seen-once mechanism, so this needs NO save-version bump -- which is what makes it cheap enough to be worth doing rather than tolerating.

Show the tip the first time an uproot window opens; drop back to the short warning afterwards. That returns 185px to the row AND makes the hint more likely to be read, since a message that appears once is not wallpaper.
