NOTE: the acceptance criterion I wrote was wrong -- cmd budgets stays at 755/tight, correctly, because the corpus prices both forms and the budget measures the ceiling the format allows, not frequency. 0eb443c

title: Tell the player the move tool exists
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (59)', first entry. PLAYER-FACING, and the highest-value item in the queue right now because the feature is already built.

Arming an uproot and hovering a destination shows cost and gain together (cycle 59). Nothing hints that this is possible. The only signal is a button reading 'Really uproot? (+N)' (game/hud.gd:1206), which asks the player to confirm a DELETION -- it does not invite them to go looking at other cells.

So a complete tool is sitting behind a prompt that says the opposite of what it does. Either a few words in that button, or a one-shot message the first time a window opens.

BLOCKED-ISH on width, like -eupm: 'Really uproot? (+99)' is already the longest state that button takes, and the selection panel has no slack (-r722). Measure first. The one-shot message route avoids the width problem entirely and goes through Hud.message_corpus(), which is budgeted.

ACCEPTANCE: a first-time player discovers the move preview without being told; the new string is measured against its box or added to the message corpus.
close_reason: The armed prompt now points at the move preview: 'Hover to compare a new spot.' Deliberately a comparison and not a promise to move, since -h5w6 is undecided. Costs 185px of the message row's headroom, leaving 121 against a 40px floor -- state 'tight', which is the argument for the one-shot follow-up.

title: Write the run.json schema down where /verify can see it
description:
SOURCE: this cycle's step 4, gap [G-058], filed upstream as gh#46.

I passed Phase 4 evidence to verify_ledger record under a key named `phase4`. It was accepted without comment, dropped, and then reported as missing ('warranted with no Phase 4 checks recorded'). The real key is `checks`, with name/result entries. `tier`, `phases` and `notes` were dropped the same way.

The upstream fix is gh#46 (warn on unknown keys). The IN-PROJECT half is cheaper and does not wait on a release: write the schema into .claude/skills/verify-bd-item/, which already carries the ledger-before-commit rule, with a filled-in example. Recovering the shape by reading verify_ledger.py is what this cycle did, and it is not repeatable knowledge until it is written down.

ACCEPTANCE: verify-bd-item carries a correct run.json example; a row recorded from it reports no 'no Phase 4 checks' warning.
notes: SECOND SIGHTING, cycle 69 (not a duplicate filing -- this bead already covers it). This time it cost a wrong row rather than a warning: lint_exit / tests_exit / tests_total / tests_failed / assertions were all accepted silently and the row came out 'verdict': 'unknown', 'lint': None, 'tests': None. The real shape is nested (lint: {new:...}, tests: {failed:...}) plus a top-level verdict, and none of it is in --help. Note also that upstream gh#46 is CLOSED and fixed at 0.47.0 (difflib suggestion on unknown keys, templates/tools/verify_ledger.py:1101-1107) -- this project pins 0.38.0 on purpose (gh#43, bead -ny3h), so writing the schema down locally is the fix available here. Raised to P1: it has now silently corrupted the evidence file twice.
close_reason: Shipped as tools/run_json_check.py rather than a document: the key set is derived from every run.get() in the installed verify_ledger, so a harness upgrade updates it for free. Found 'tier' on its first run -- a key I had written into every run.json this session and which is read nowhere. 769e045

title: Build scope-vs-claim: does a check's stated scope match its actual scope
description:
SOURCE: step 0's second pre-flight item. SECOND INDEPENDENT IDENTIFICATION, which is this project's build-it bar -- filed at P1 so it does not get named a third time.

First (cycle 49, log.md): 'budget-corpus-audit' -- _budget_hud_message_row's evidence string said 'over every plant name and corn level' and was true when written, false for seven cycles after, while the budget reported green over a subset of its row.

Second (cycle 50): three of four cardinal-facing cases were covered by tests BY ACCIDENT (+X in the gait test, -X via the corpse test, +Y used without its value asserted) and the fourth by nothing. Nothing in the suite's own descriptions gave any way to see the gap.

Third, same shape, already fixed: mirror_check compared a block it had silently truncated, and suite_reach_check's autoload map returned empty without saying so.

The general question is bigger than budgets and bigger than checkers: **a check states a scope in prose and covers a scope in code, and nothing compares the two.** That is why the failure is always silent -- the description is what a reader trusts and it is the half that cannot fail.

The skill should carry the recognition patterns (a free-text evidence/corpus string; a region delimited by a marker; a set of cases enumerated by hand; a denominator that can be zero for two different reasons) and the cheap test for each: name the scope out loud, then ask what else falls inside it. Cross-reference derive-the-list, which handles the case where the set IS derivable, and house-static-checker's denominator rules.

ACCEPTANCE: .claude/skills/scope-vs-claim/SKILL.md exists and cites all three incidents above as its evidence, with the file:line for each.
close_reason: Built .claude/skills/scope-vs-claim/SKILL.md citing all four incidents with file:line.

title: Build the verify-bd-item skill, identified twice and never built
description:
SOURCE: step 0's second pre-flight item (skill ideas in log.md vs .claude/skills/).

log.md:3115 names it, log.md:3201 opens with 'Same as last cycle: a verify-bd-item loop skill. Ran the identical fifteen-step sequence five more times.' Two explicit identifications, absent from .claude/skills/. CLAUDE.md step 0: 'Two independent identifications of the same missing skill means build it -- do not identify it a third time.'

It is not hypothetical any more. Cycle 48 ran that sequence by hand and dropped a step: the verify ledger row was recorded AFTER the commit, so reach came back 0/0 and the row carries no evidence for its own 'warranted' verdict. That is the exact failure the original identification predicted ('every one is a place to silently drop a step').

The skill should carry the ORDER and the traps, not just the list: ledger row before the commit (reach is computed from the diff); take a suite count on both sides of a rename or dependency change; read the denominators not the exit code; gap-id scan before appending to log-devtools.md; never rewrite a ledger row to look better.

ACCEPTANCE: the skill exists, names the ordering constraint that broke cycle 48, and is written so following it produces a ledger row with non-zero reach.
close_reason: Built .claude/skills/verify-bd-item/SKILL.md, leading with the ordering constraints rather than the step list. 2e8993d

title: Pests have no idle animation, only plants do
description: The second half of James's 'animate all the plants and enemies' ask. Plant._wobble_time now drives an idle sway for every placed plant (plant-tower-defense-04x), but Pest has no equivalent - a walking aphid or beetle is a static sprite sliding along the road, and the new facing rotation (129) made that more visible, not less. Give pests idle/locomotion motion (a walk bob, antenna twitch, wing flutter for winged mutations), gated behind GardenTheme.animations_enabled() and cheap enough for SIMULTANEOUS_PEST_CEILING pests at once.
close_reason: Closed

title: An animated dandelion that blows its seeds as bombs, in an epic packet tier
description: James's direct ask, still unshipped. A fifth plant: seed-puff attack animation where the dandelion visibly loses fluff as it fires, and seeds that ARC and DETONATE rather than travelling straight like a Corn Cobbler kernel or landing instantly like a Chomp bite. Ships in a new 'epic' seed packet tier above the current common/rare split (see SeedBank.PACKET_COST / packet_pool and PlantCatalog). Needs art in art_src/ per STYLE.md (64x64, top-down, up-screen facing, outline = darker shade of fill) rasterised to assets/sprites/ + retina, and must pass test_sprite_style.gd's contract.
close_reason: Closed

title: More waves, and a boss pest
description: James's direct ask, still unshipped. WaveDirector.WAVES ends at 8 fixed waves before endless takes over with escalating mutation chance on the same two pests (aphid, beetle). Add real additional waves to the table, and at least one boss pest: bigger health pool, a distinct sprite, and a mechanic that is NOT just 'armoured but more'. Note the endless scaling (health_scale_for/speed_scale_for/mutation_chance_for) and SIMULTANEOUS_PEST_CEILING budget already exist and are tested - extending the table must keep those honest.

title: Four tests write the developer's real user://highscore.save
description: test_selftest.gd:679 (test_run_config_high_score_only_ever_goes_up), :1014, :4326 and :4921 (test_a_record_set_by_quitting_is_announced_on_the_title_screen) all set RunConfig.campaign_high_score/endless_high_score in memory and then call RunConfig.record_score(), while RunConfig.save_path is still the REAL user://highscore.save. record_score() calls _save(), so each headless suite run rewrites the developer's own save with whatever number the test just staged. Observed over two runs of the full suite on 2026-08-16: the file went v5/308/5008 -> v6/310/5010 -> v6/2/2. Both high scores were destroyed; only a scratchpad copy taken before the work brought them back. These tests stash and restore the in-memory scores, which is what makes it invisible -- the FILE keeps the last number written. Fix: give each of them the scratch-save redirect test_economy._with_scratch_save already implements (RunConfig.save_path = a user://test_*.save, restore and delete afterwards), or add the same wrapper to test_selftest.gd. Related: harness issue #33 (--isolated isolates the bus, not user://), which makes this worse under two concurrent agents.
close_reason: Fixed: four tests redirected to scratch paths (three named in the bead plus a fourth in test_economy.gd found by the new guard), scores restored as well as save_path, and test_no_test_persists_through_the_players_own_save added as a comment-stripping source guard. Real save verified byte-identical across two full suite runs.

title: Sweep test/ for other group reads taken by index
description: test_kernels_launch read kernels[0] from a tree-global group and measured a leaked object every run - green for months, red the moment four unrelated tests were appended. Nothing enumerates the other group reads (pests, husks, kernels, plants); any taken by index has the same defect. A sweep for get_nodes_in_group(...)[0] in test/ finds the rest in one pass.
close_reason: Closed

title: A damaged plant's health bar eats clicks on the playfield
description: Plant._health_back and _health_bar are ColorRects with the default MOUSE_FILTER_STOP, parked over the playfield. A damaged plant therefore has a 32x5 strip that swallows clicks meant for the board. Pre-existing; found while adding the health bar notches.
close_reason: Closed

title: Post-mortem calls your best chokepoint your weakest ground
description: Game._note_lane_loss is called from _on_pest_died (every kill, at the pest's position) as well as _on_pest_escaped. So _run_losses counts kills, not damage. That is correct for LanePressureOverlay, whose doc says 'how far did pests get' - a kill at cell 30 of 40 IS pressure. But run_summary.gd:201 _worst_cell_text() labels the highest-count cell 'Weakest ground - N lost there', so a well-defended chokepoint is reported to the player as their weakest ground, every run. The advice is not just useless, it is inverted. Found by the agent building the prep depth readout, which declined to reuse worst_run_cell() for exactly this reason.
close_reason: Closed

title: A truncated save silently zeroes a high score that can never be restored
description: RunConfig._save stamps a SAVE_VERSION line on every write and _load tests only begins_with('v') -- the version is written and never actually read, so a future format change has no migration hook despite the field existing to provide one. Worse, int('') is 0 in GDScript, so a truncated or partially-written save loads as a zero high score, and record_score only ever raises a record: once it reads 0 the real number is gone forever with no way back. A save file is the one thing in this project the player cannot regenerate by playing.
acceptance_criteria: A malformed, truncated or short save leaves the existing in-memory scores untouched rather than zeroing them, and the version field is actually consulted. Unit tests cover a truncated file, a garbage file, and a future version number.
close_reason: Closed

title: Quitting an endless run through pause files no score
description: RunConfig.record_score has exactly one caller, Game._end_run, reached only from the victory branch or from lives hitting 0. has_more_waves() is unconditionally true in endless, so victory is unreachable there -- meaning the ONLY way to bank an endless score is to lose. Cycle 8's pause screen then added two exits that bypass _end_run entirely: RestartButton calls reload_current_scene and GateButton calls change_scene_to_file. So a player who quits a long endless run voluntarily files nothing, and the run they were most likely to be proud of is the one guaranteed not to count.
acceptance_criteria: Leaving a run through any exit files the score exactly once, and a re-entry cannot file it twice. Unit test covers quitting via both pause exits.
close_reason: Closed

title: Uproot-as-score: refunds credit seeds_earned_total, so plant-uproot cycling inflates the high score
description: SeedBank.refund routes through add_seeds, which increments seeds_earned_total -- the number both per-mode high scores are kept on. So planting a Corn for 10 and uprooting it for 6 costs 4 seeds of wallet and CREDITS 6 to the recorded score, repeatably. A 100-seed float converts to roughly +150 score with no gameplay at all. Scaling the refund by health in cycle 7 killed uproot-as-repair and left this untouched; the seed_bank comment 'Refunds count too' documents the behaviour as deliberate, but it predates high scores being a scoreboard players compete on.
acceptance_criteria: Uprooting cannot raise seeds_earned_total. A unit test plants and uproots in a loop and asserts the recorded score does not move, while ordinary income still counts.
close_reason: Closed

title: Common seed packets silently become rare ones once Chomp unlocks
description: SeedBank._roll_packet filters the locked pool to ids at or below the packet's max_tier, then falls back to the WHOLE locked pool when that filtered pool is empty. Chomp is tier 1 and Sunflower is tier 2, so the moment Chomp unlocks the filtered pool for a common packet is always empty and a 20-seed common packet can hand out the tier-2 Sunflower. That makes the two packet tiers indistinguishable in the only way they were supposed to differ, and both tooltips become false: the common button says 'tier 1 only' and the rare one says 'the only reliable way to a Seed Sunflower'.
acceptance_criteria: A common packet can never yield a plant above its max_tier. When nothing at or below that tier remains locked, the purchase is refused with a reason rather than silently upgraded, and the tooltips match the behaviour. Unit test covers the exhausted-pool case.
close_reason: Common packets refuse rather than falling back to the whole locked pool; no charge on refusal, no soft-lock possible. Fixed a pre-existing test that was green only because of the bug.

title: Style contract + first sprite set (Corn Cobbler, Chomp Flower, pests, seed packet)
description: Measured the Kenney Tower Defense kit's conventions into art_src/STYLE.md, authored 6 SVG sources, rasterised them to assets/sprites (64) + retina (128), and gated the contract with test/unit/test_sprite_style.gd.
close_reason: Closed

title: A hungry pest eats a bed with no visible bite at all
description: Pest._physics_process drains a plant at EAT_DPS * delta every physics frame (game/pest.gd:1681 for a Bramble, :1686 for a meal). Nothing about that is an EVENT: there is no wind-up, no strike, no moment the player can point at. The only tells are Plant's flinch -- re-armed every single frame, so it reads as a continuous shudder rather than as a hit (game/plant.gd:287) -- and Sfx.REPEAT_MS[PLANT_BITTEN]'s 420ms gate, which is currently the ONLY thing turning ~60 damage applications per second into an audible rate (game/sfx.gd:472). The pest also keeps facing the way it walked while it eats (game/pest.gd:1932), so a bug destroying a plant one cell off the road is drawn walking past it. Make the bite a discrete, telegraphed chop: the pest turns to face what it is eating, winds up, strikes, and the damage lands in a lump on the strike.
design: Cadence derived, not chosen. CHOPS_TO_FELL=3 lumps of Plant.MAX_HEALTH/3 each, and chop_period() set so the THIRD strike lands at exactly Plant.MAX_HEALTH / Pest.EAT_DPS -- the moment the old continuous drain finished the plant. So EAT_DPS keeps meaning what every derived reader already assumes it means (Plant.wilt_threshold, Bramble.seconds_to_fall, WEATHER_RAIN_HEAL_FRACTION) and this is a legibility change with no balance change. Pose is a pure static (chop_pose/chop_reach/chop_stretch) per assert-an-animation; strike counting is a pure static over the clock so a long frame owes its chops.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A hungry pest adjacent to a plant applies damage in discrete lumps, not per frame. 2. Three chops fell a full-health plant, and the third lands within a frame of Plant.MAX_HEALTH/Pest.EAT_DPS. 3. The pest's facing turns to the plant it is eating. 4. chop_reach peaks (max forward lunge) at the strike, and is rearward through the wind-up. 5. Same for a Bramble. 6. Full suite + check_all + lint green.

title: Make the pressable next-wave button pulse read at a glance
description: The pressable cue on NextWaveButton is a 1.0->0.8 modulate alpha breath at 0.5s half-cycle (Hud.NEXT_WAVE_PULSE_DIM/SECONDS). A 20% alpha dip on a paper-styled button against the HUD's paper backdrop is close to invisible in the running game, so the cue that was supposed to say 'clicking is the thing to do now' still leaves the button looking the same as any other button in the row. Widen the cue so it reads at a glance without becoming a flashing alarm.

title: Slow the free starter cob's level-1 fire rate
description: The Corn Cobbler is the free starter and its level-1 interval (0.80s) sits only 10% off level 2's 0.72s, so the first upgrade barely reads as a rate change. Slow level 1 so the pre-upgrade cob is visibly slower and the first 20 seeds buy something felt.

title: A sport should be rarer news and worth more when it lands
description: CrossBreeder.CHANCE_PER_TICK (0.04, mean 150 s) and the PlantMutation.TABLE buffs (rate 0.70..0.85, power 1.25..2.0) were tuned as a pair: a frequent, small event. The ask is the other trade — a sport arrives less often and is worth more when it does, so it reads as news rather than as background income. Move the chance down and every buff up one notch, keeping the table's own invariants (exactly one of rate/power moves; rate <= 1.0; power >= 1.0) and the seconds band test_a_sport_is_rare_enough_to_stay_an_event pins.
acceptance_criteria: CrossBreeder.mean_seconds_between() stays inside (90, 600). Every PlantMutation row still moves exactly one of rate/power. StickySundew.slow_factor for a sport stays above MIN_SLOW_FACTOR with headroom. Full unit suite green, including test_playtest_sweep. Every comment quoting an old number is updated.

title: Upstream the draw-call budget gate to godot-selftest-harness (G-159)
description:
Local patch shipped this session, guarded by tools/harness_patch_check.py under marker 'draw_calls_over_budget'. A /scaffold-godot-harness refresh will drop it until it lands upstream.

WHAT IT IS. 'findings' gated fps and orphan growth and nothing else. Meanwhile _cmd_performance (addons/godot_selftest/dev_tools.gd) has read Performance.RENDER_TOTAL_DRAW_CALLS_IN_FRAME since it was written, and tools/devtools.py:1404 has printed it as 'Draw calls:'. Nothing ever compared it against anything.

WHY IT IS WORTH A GATE NEXT TO fps_min, which looks like it covers the same ground: fps is a fact about the MACHINE. The Cutworm's 2000-draw-call frame read 165 fps on this desktop with the body still emerging and 8.5 with it fully out, on a board that idles at 171 -- so an fps_min tuned anywhere useful is noise on a fast machine and silence on a slow one. The draw-call count is the same number on both. It is the one render metric a project can hold a budget against, and it is already being collected.

THE SHAPE OF THE PATCH: read draw_calls_max from devtools_config.json (default 0 = off, so no existing project starts failing), compare in the same performance block of _run_findings, and record a SKIP -- not a silent pass -- both when it is off and when the run is headless, since a headless frame renders nothing and its 0 is not a scene fact. Config key sits beside fps_min; documented in CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md.

WHAT IT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT: the defect that produced it, on the first frame, instead of on the third relaunch via wait-frames' own wall-clock print.
acceptance_criteria: Filed upstream at SeveralHerr/godot-selftest-harness with the fps-is-machine-dependent argument. Once released, drop the local patch and its harness_patch_check.py row in the same commit, and confirm findings still reports the skip line when draw_calls_max is 0.
close_reason: Obsolete: the godot-selftest harness was removed from this project on 2026-08-29 (the addon, the devtools bridge, devtools_ext/, the verify ledger and log-devtools.md all deleted at the user's request). There is no `findings` run, no `_cmd_performance`, and no `tools/harness_patch_check.py` left to guard the local patch, so there is nothing here to upstream from. The underlying observation is still true and worth keeping: RENDER_TOTAL_DRAW_CALLS_IN_FRAME is a machine-independent render budget while fps is not. If a draw-call budget is wanted again it would be built fresh against whatever runtime tooling this project grows next, not against the deleted bridge.

title: Re-measure the Cutworm's frame rate live, now that the draw cost is budgeted
description:
The fix for the >2000-draw-call frame (OUTLINE_STEP 4 -> 12, the dorsal facet from a filled strip to one draw_polyline) is gated headless by Cutworm.body_polygon_cost against MAX_BODY_POLYGONS, and that gate passes -- but the FRAME RATE it exists to protect was never re-read on a running game. The session was asked to stop using devtools before the confirming run.

What was measured, before the fix: the same 'wait-frames 200' call took 1213 ms with the body still emerging and 23454 ms once it was fully out (165 fps against 8.5), on a board 'performance' reports at 'FPS: mean 171.2 min 132.4'.

What is claimed, unmeasured: ~330 polygon draws per frame instead of ~2000, i.e. roughly a 6x reduction, which should put the full-length body back near the idle rate.

This is the outstanding half of an otherwise-verified change, and it is filed rather than assumed because a draw-call count is a proxy: it cannot see per-call cost, overdraw, or the shadow strip's fill rate.
acceptance_criteria: Spawn a Cutworm via 'cmd spawn_pest', let the whole body emerge, and read 'performance' with it on the board. The mean FPS with a full-length body is within 20% of the idle board's, and 'wait-frames 200' returns in about the same wall time whether the body is emerging or fully out -- which is the specific reading that exposed the problem.

title: The Chomp bites for damage instead of deleting what it holds
description:
Owner, 2026-08-29: 'Chomper shouldn't instant kill' and then 'the chomper should take a few ticks to kill the small bugs, too.' Chosen shape: scale the damage so only small pests die in the mouth and big ones are spat out damaged.

Before: game/chomp_flower.gd held a pest for chew_seconds and then called Pest.kill(DEATH_BITTEN) outright. It dealt NO damage - grep health game/chomp_flower.gd returned one hit, in a comment - so health, Shield Bug plates and Nurse healing were all irrelevant to it. plant_catalog.gd:442's hurts(CHOMP) arm said so in as many words: 'the one arm with no constant to read'. The catalogue blurb sold it as 'Eats small pests instantly.'

After: BITES_PER_MEAL 3 -> 6 and a new BITE_DAMAGE of 1.0, so a meal is worth six health and each bite is a real take_damage(BITE_DAMAGE, DEATH_BITTEN). The clock decides how long the lane is blocked; the bites decide who dies.
design:
BITE_DAMAGE is capped at 1.0 by the aphid's 3 health - the owner asked for a few ticks, so the smallest bug must need at least three bites, and at 1.5 it dies on the second. That cap is what forces BITES_PER_MEAL up to 6 rather than 3: who dies is B*D against health and how many ticks the smallest takes is health/D, and one number cannot serve both, so the count is the free variable.

meal_damage() of 6 lands in a GAP in the health table (3, 4, 5, then 10, 16, 48, 80): it clears the biggest casualty by a point and falls four short of the smallest survivor, rather than sitting on a species and deciding it by float rounding.

_spat_out exists because release() leaves the bug where it was caught - inside the reach and already past GRAB_LEAD - so without a guard the next frame picks it straight back up and grinds a beetle down six at a time on the spot. Cleared by DISTANCE rather than by a timer: what makes it fair game again is that it has left.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every bite goes through Pest.take_damage so plates, healing and the fought mark all apply.
- A pest the mouth cannot finish is released alive and is not re-grabbed while it stands in the reach.
- The bite loop pays every bite a long frame owed, not one per call.
- The catalogue blurb and PlantCatalog.hurts(CHOMP) both stop describing the old delete; hurts derives from BITE_DAMAGE.
- Sizing asserted off Pest.SPECIES at both ends, not hard-coded.
- Suite, lint, name_check green; driven live.
close_reason: Shipped. BITES_PER_MEAL 3 -> 6, new BITE_DAMAGE 1.0, so a meal is worth six health and every bite is take_damage(BITE_DAMAGE, DEATH_BITTEN). Who dies: aphid 3hp on bite 3, locust 4hp on bite 4, hopper 5hp on bite 5; shieldbug/beetle/nurse/queen all spat out alive. The Shield Bug leaves at FULL health and zero plates - a plate absorbs 1.5 against a bite of 1.0 and is spent per hit either way - so a Chomp strips it for the cobs behind. _spat_out stops the flower re-eating what it just released, cleared by distance not by a timer. PlantCatalog blurb rewritten and hurts(CHOMP) now derives from BITE_DAMAGE instead of being written out. 6 new tests plus 3 restated; sizing derived from Pest.SPECIES at both ends. Two defects found in-run: damage was paid per FRAME not per bite owed (fixed with a while, which also matters because plates are spent per hit), and the new tests grabbed off settle frames feeding _act the tree-global pests group. Third consequence pinned rather than hidden: an aphid dies at 0.5 progress so it never reaches LATE_BITE_THRESHOLD 0.6 and shows no late-bite frame. title: The playtest sweep cannot see a timing change to any plant's engagement
description:
CLAUDE.md says 'After any balance edit (wave tables, Game.DIFFICULTIES, plant prices/reach), run the playtest sweep', and docs/playtest-sweep.md repeats it. plant-tower-defense-q9h4 was exactly such an edit - a Chomp now refuses a pest until it is GRAB_LEAD past the stem, which changes how long every bug in a Chomp lane survives - and the sweep ran green while being structurally incapable of noticing.

RunSim scores gardens by COVERAGE, not by combat: tools/run_sim.gd:718 best_placement ranks a placement by Game.engagement_reach(id) cells covered per seed, and tools/run_sim.gd:686 buys income once the road is covered. Nothing in it ever grabs, chews, or fires. So any edit that changes WHEN a plant engages - rather than how far it reaches or what it costs - is invisible to the whole sweep, on every board and every difficulty.

Not a defect in the sweep so much as an unstated boundary on the instruction above: the rule reads as though the sweep covers balance, and it covers the coverage-and-economy half of balance.
acceptance_criteria:
- docs/playtest-sweep.md gains a NOT COVERED paragraph in the same register the house checkers use, naming coverage-vs-combat as the boundary and saying which kinds of edit fall outside it.
- The pointer in CLAUDE.md (and its AGENTS.md mirror, python tools/mirror_check.py --fix) stops implying the sweep answers a timing change.
- Decide, and record, whether RunSim should model engagement at all or whether the boundary is the right answer - a per-plant combat model is a large build and may be the wrong one.

title: A Chomp waits until a pest is a little way past it before the mouth closes
description:
Requested by the owner 2026-08-29: 'make it so the chomper only grabs them once they're a little ways past the chomper.'

Today _nearest_free_pest (game/chomp_flower.gd) takes the nearest non-winged, unheld pest inside grab_radius() with no regard for which way it is walking, so the mouth closes on the leading edge of the circle - the bug is caught before it is even level with the flower. Wanted: the flower lets them walk on a bit, then snaps from behind.

Geometry available: Pest._facing (game/pest.gd:1032) is already snapped to one of four cardinals by _update_facing and is set at spawn (game/pest.gd:1120), so the travel direction is exact and needs no route inspection. Projecting (pest - plant) onto that heading gives a signed 'how far past me is it'.

Window arithmetic, level 1: GRAB_RADIUS is 73.6px and the road sits one CELL (64px) off the grass, so the half-width of the reach along the road is sqrt(73.6^2 - 64^2) = 36.3px. A lead of 16px (CELL * 0.25) leaves a 20.3px window. The fastest pest is the aphid at 78px/s, doubled by GameSpeed's 2x step, which is ~2.6px per physics frame - about 8 frames of window. That margin is the thing a test has to hold, because a lead that closes the window is a flower that silently never eats, which is the exact failure GRAB_RADIUS's own header records from 62px.
acceptance_criteria:
- A pure static on ChompFlower answers 'how far past me has this pest walked', and a second one answers 'is it far enough yet'; both asserted with no board and no frame.
- Pest exposes its travel direction as a unit vector derived from _facing, not from _route.
- The rule is asserted for all four cardinal headings (a pest walking each way past a flower), not just the one the default road happens to use.
- A gate holds the WINDOW open: for every species, at its top effective speed and 2x game speed, the pass-window at level 1 is at least 4 physics frames wide. A lead that closes it must go red.
- A degenerate heading grabs as before rather than never grabbing - 'found no prey' and 'there is no prey' look identical, and the silent-never-eats failure is worse than an early catch.
- Balance: this is a wave-timing change, so test/unit/test_playtest_sweep.gd runs and docs/playtest-sweep.md's matrix is consulted.
- name_check, lint, run_tests.py all exit 0, and the change is driven live through the bridge.
close_reason: game/chomp_flower.gd: GRAB_LEAD = Board.CELL * 0.25 (16px). _nearest_free_pest now refuses any pest that has not walked that far past the stem, measured by pass_distance() projecting onto the pest's own heading - a projection and not a coordinate test, because PATH_CORNERS runs +X,+Y,-X,+Y,+X,-Y,+X and pest.x > plant.x would be backwards on one leg and meaningless on three. Pest.travel_direction() derives the heading from _facing (already cardinal, set at spawn) rather than from the current route leg, which is zero-length the moment a pest stands on its waypoint. A degenerate heading grabs as before: a flower that silently never eats is the worse failure. Live: flower at x=224, mouth closes at x=240.33 (GRAB_LEAD + one frame), and the beetle walked through 187.7 - the old leading edge - untouched. 3 new tests: all four headings by cross product, the selector taking the bug that has gone by over the nearer one arriving, and a window gate written in FRAMES (>= 4 for every species at its top speed x the fastest GameSpeed step) - mutation-verified, 0.60 cells closes the window and 0.47 leaves it open at 2.4 frames, both red. 17 existing tests staged prey level with the flower; restaged through a new _prey() helper in both suites, and two of them had been passing vacuously. Suite 1148/1148, 25587 assertions, lint/name_check/import 0, check_all 33/34. NOTE: the playtest sweep ran green and is structurally blind to this - RunSim scores coverage, never combat; filed separately.

description:

title: Species row, the solo wave, and the two plants that must refuse it
description:
SPECIES row in pest.gd:64 with boss: true, so wave_carries_boss() (wave_director.gd:1009) and the rule that drought never lands on a boss wave (wave_director.gd:1001) pick it up for free -- that flag exists precisely so a second boss did not have to edit a comparison in another file.

Numbers, as approved:
  * health 1800. Band-only DPS is what has to kill it: two to four plants cover the band at a time, ~18 DPS raw, 45 after the 2.5x. At 20 px/s the fight lasts 153 s, so a well-built box gets ~2100 through and a badly-built one ~900. 1800 puts the pass mark where the box is.
  * speed 20 px/s. Below the Locust's 24 (pest.gd:273), so it is the slowest thing that has walked this road. 2112 px / 20 = 105.6 s head-to-exit; the tail clears 953 px later at 153.3 s.
  * seeds 120 -- three Aphid Queens (40 each, pest.gd:426). It funds the rebuild of everything the head ate.

WAVE. One row, one entry, nothing else spawns: {species: cutworm, count: 1, gap: 1.0, lead: 0.5}. SIMULTANEOUS_PEST_CEILING (wave_director.gd:286) is untouched -- one pest node, whatever its length. The WAVES header's coda arithmetic has to be re-stated the way every wave change in that file re-states it.

REFUSALS. A Chomp Flower refuses the grab outright, the same way it already refuses is_winged (chomp_flower.gd:544) -- chew_seconds is meaningless against a body that never ends, and one boss trivialised by one 50-seed plant is not a boss. A Barrier Bramble does not stop it: the head eats through at roughly three times an ordinary pest's EAT_DPS (pest.gd:606) and keeps its speed. Sticky Sundew still bites, at half effect -- the answer to a boss you cannot block is a boss you can stretch.

It escapes tail-last: damage keeps landing for 48 s after the head leaves the board, and the lives are only spent when the tail clears.

title: Damage zones: a hit's position decides what it is worth
description:
Fifteen cells of body means every plant on the board is in range of SOMETHING at once. Left alone that is the whole board's DPS on one target -- and a level-3 Corn Cobbler that lands one kernel of five on an aphid lands all five on a wall (corn_cobbler.gd:100, 5 kernels x 1.4 dmg / 0.62 s). Worse, _furthest_along_in_range picks the pest furthest along the road, and with one pest on the board that is trivially the worm, so every cob on the field fires at it. The hide multiplier is the only thing between this and a two-second boss.

Three zones, by arc distance from the head:
  * maw, the head -- 100%. What every player tries first, and it is the part eating the garden, so it is the honest option and never the efficient one.
  * hide, the trunk -- 15%. NOT zero: a player raking the body should see chip damage, because blanks read as a bug.
  * weak band, stations 5-7 (~2 cells) -- 250%. The clitellum. It rides five stations behind the head, which is 220 px of road the head has already walked and already chewed.

That last row is the fight. The plants that can hit the band are the plants the worm has just eaten past: you are not defending a line in front of it, you are building a kill box BEHIND it and paying for the ground with plants you already know you will lose. It is the first pest in the game answered from anywhere but the front of the queue.

Pest.take_damage (pest.gd:2046) grows an optional hit-position argument; every existing caller keeps working without it and an ordinary pest ignores it. Zone lookup is a pure static func of (hit position, head_s) so it is assertable with no tree.
acceptance_criteria: Pure zone lookup tested at every station over the whole walk: exactly the stations in [5,7] return 2.5, the head returns 1.0, everything else 0.15. take_damage with no position argument behaves identically for all seven existing species -- assert that over the derived species list rather than a hand-picked pair (.claude/skills/derive-the-list).

title: Peristalsis: one sine read twice, bounded by what the lane has left
description:
A 64 px lane leaves no room to slither sideways and a snake wiggle would put the body on the grass. Real earthworms do not wiggle anyway -- they move by a thickness wave running head to tail. Modulate radius by +/-10% at a 150 px wavelength, and surge the head's speed off THE SAME term at +/-25%, so the body's pulse and the worm's lurch can never look out of step with each other.

The amplitude is derived, not chosen: 29 x 1.10 = 31.9 against a 32 px lane half-width. Swept in the design page, +/-12% puts 5,568 body-edge samples on the grass and +/-10% puts none over 382,068 samples. Girth and amplitude come out of one budget -- change either and re-run the sweep.

Speed 20 px/s surging between 15 and 25.

Per CLAUDE.md the wave has to be a pure static func of (arc position, time) so the suite can hold a claim about it without pumping frames; see .claude/skills/assert-an-animation for which single claim is left for the running game.
acceptance_criteria: assert_margin-style gate on the amplitude against the girth: the fat phase of the wave stays inside 32 px, and a 12% amplitude fails the same check. Animations-off leaves a standing radius equal to the unmodulated profile, the way Plant._wobble already behaves.

title: Cutworm: one scalar of state, and a body swept along the spine from it
description:
game/cutworm.gd, class Cutworm extends Pest. It keeps the health pool, the damage pipeline, died/escaped, the 'pests' group and progress() -- everything targeting already reads (corn_cobbler.gd:232's _furthest_along_in_range, dandelion.gd:273) -- and replaces exactly two things: how it moves and how it draws.

STATE. One scalar, head_s, the head's distance along the road. Station i sits at head_s - i*44. No position-history buffer and no per-segment lerp, so there is nothing to desynchronise and the whole worm is one number. Before head_s reaches i*44 station i has not emerged and the body is simply cut off at s=0 -- which is off the west edge of the board, so that is the burrow for free. Same at the far end: the body keeps drawing after the head has left.

DRAWING. Every 4 px along the live span take the normal and offset +/- radius(u); left edge forward, right edge back, close, fill, stroke the rim. Segmentation is drawn ON TOP as ticks across the body at each station -- annelid rings, not sprite seams. radius(u) is a blunt head, a long even trunk, and a tail tapering to a point over the last quarter.

Per CLAUDE.md's convention the geometry goes in a pure static func, not inside _draw: headless executes no _draw, so a shape assembled there is a shape no test can reach. See .claude/skills/assert-an-animation.

MEASURED CONSTANTS (design page, against the real road):
  * 22 stations x 44 px = 924 px, + 29 px head cap = 953 px = 14.9 of 32 cells
  * girth 29 px half-width; the hard ceiling is 32 (half a cell) and it is set by the STRAIGHTS, not the corners -- swept at 33 the body clips grass, at 32 it does not
  * 0 of 104,136 body-edge samples leave a road cell at fillet 26 / girth 29
acceptance_criteria: Static geometry funcs produce the outline for a given head_s with no tree. Tests assert the 953 px span, that no sampled edge point leaves a road cell over the whole walk, and that a head_s below one spacing draws a body clipped at s=0 rather than a body hanging off the entry bracket.

Two defects found live and fixed: self-intersecting/degenerate polygons reaching the triangulator, and a >2000-draw-call frame that took the board to 8.5 fps. Suite 1177, lint 0.

title: A filleted spine beside Board.route(), so a long body has a tangent to follow
description:
Board.route() (board.gd:672) is one waypoint per path cell bracketed by an off-board entry and exit, so every leg is axis-aligned and every corner is an exact right angle. That is what makes Pest._update_facing's four-way snap correct (pest.gd:1907) and it is exactly what a 953 px body cannot walk: the tangent flips instantly at a vertex.

Add a second reader beside route() that returns the same road with each interior corner cut back by a fillet radius and replaced by a quadratic Bezier through the vertex. Pure and static where it can be, so it is assertable with no scene tree -- the same shape road_cell_count/road_length_px already have (board.gd:138, board.gd:154).

MEASURED, in the design page's JS against these exact PATH_CORNERS:
  * raw route length 2112 px, 32 cells -- agrees with the constants board.gd:24-35 says were measured against this road
  * fillet 26 shortens the spine to 2053.1 px, -2.8%

That shortening is the trap. If the walk clock and progress() are keyed to the filleted length the boss arrives early and every wave-timing number in wave_director.gd moves under it. Keep progress() and the walk on the unfilleted arc length; the fillet is for DRAWING and for the body's tangent only.
acceptance_criteria: A static func returns the filleted spine for any corner list. Tests assert: raw length is 2112 px over 32 cells; fillet 26 gives 2053.1 px; a fillet of 0 returns the route unchanged; the diagonal-segment refusal set_road() already makes (board.gd:118) still holds.

title: The Cutworm: a boss whose body fills fifteen road cells at once
description:
Design approved 2026-08-29; the full spec, with the measured geometry, is docs/cutworm-design.html on branch worktree-worm-boss.

A single pest whose drawn body spans 953 px (14.9 of the road's 32 cells). It is the only pest in its wave. Every other pest is a 64 px Sprite2D that snaps to one of four cardinal rotations at a corner (Pest._update_facing, pest.gd:1907) and nobody notices; a 960 px body is inside three of the road's five corners at once and cannot do that.

The body is NOT a chain of follower sprites. It is one continuous outline swept along a filleted copy of Board.route(), parameterised by a single scalar head_s. Measured in the design page against the real PATH_CORNERS: 32 cells, 2112 px, and 0 of 104,136 body-edge samples leave a road cell across the whole walk at 26 px fillet / 29 px girth.

Stats as approved: health 1800, speed 20 px/s (below the Locust's 24 -- the slowest thing that has walked this road), seeds 120, 22 stations x 44 px spacing.

The fight: fifteen cells of body means every plant on the board is in range of something at once, so the hide has to matter. Maw 100%, hide 15%, weak band 250%; the band rides five stations BEHIND the head, over road the head has already chewed. That is the boss -- the first pest in the game answered from behind rather than at the front of the queue.

title: Plant button tint conflates 'locked' with 'too poor to buy'; seeds readout has no spend-vs-gain cue
description:

A player low on seeds sees the same grey as a plant they have not unlocked yet and cannot tell 'save up' from 'buy the packet'.

Separately, game/hud.gd:2830 _punch_readout() and :2886 _arm_seeds_roll() give the Seeds counter the same scale-punch and roll-count animation whether the total just rose (compost payout) or fell (a purchase) -- hud.gd:2863-2866 says the roll direction was already added because 'the purchase is the case the bead was filed about', but the readout itself carries no colour distinguishing a spend from a gain, so a purchase and a payout look identical at the one place seeds are displayed. Purchase-time refusal (game.gd:3566, SeedBank.pay_for_plant) already shows a message + shake + sound (game.gd:583) -- this bead is about the passive/ambient cues (button tint before you click, readout colour on change), not the refusal path, which is already covered.

title: The Chomp catches with vines and eats the bug on top of itself
description:
A Chomp's catch is currently invisible as a CATCH: `_grab` sets `_held`, plays a 0.05s lunge and swaps to `chomp_flower_eating.png`, and the pest simply stops where it stood on the road (game/chomp_flower.gd:569, game/pest.gd:1586). Nothing shows the flower reaching, nothing shows the bug being taken. A player sees a bug halt mid-road beside a flower that twitched once.

Wanted: vines lash out from the flower to the pest, then retract and haul the pest up ONTO the flower, where the existing chew (bites, chew ring, champ, eating/late sprites) plays out with the meal visibly in the mouth. One bug at a time is already true (`_held`) and must stay true.

Constraints:
- The haul must be COSMETIC. `Pest.position` is what Kernel targeting, `_adjacent_plant`, `_blocking_plant` and the escape route all read; moving the node off the road would silently stop cobs from shooting a held pest. Carry on a sprite-space offset instead, the channel `_sprite.position` already reserves for death knockback.
- No Tween may OWN the carry position. Per .claude/skills/assert-an-animation rung 1, derive it from a clock the flower already advances so headless leaves a correct state on every frame.
- No balance change: the meal clock keeps running through lash+haul, and the capture window is capped as a fraction of `chew_total` so a 0.45s aphid is not all haul.
acceptance_criteria:
- `ChompFlower` exposes pure statics for the capture phase, the lash/haul progress, the carried offset and the vine curve; every one asserted in test/unit/test_combat.gd with pinned endpoints (not expressed only as multiples of the amplitude).
- A held pest's `position` is unchanged by the haul: test asserts `pest.position` after a full capture equals the grab position, and that `carry_offset` is non-zero at the same instant.
- Release restores `carry_offset` to zero for a pest let go alive; a pest killed mid-carry keeps the offset so the corpse does not snap to the road.
- `chew_seconds` totals are untouched — `test_the_chomps_shop_line_is_true_of_the_chew_table` and the playtest sweep stay green.
- python tools/name_check.py, lint_project.gd, run_tests.py all exit 0; the change is driven live once through the bridge.
close_reason: Shipped in cc56c42. Three vines lash out, haul the bug onto the flower via a cosmetic Pest._carry_offset (node stays on the road, so Kernel targeting is untouched), and the existing chew plays with the meal in the mouth. Every beat is a pure function of _capture_elapsed, no Tween. 9 new tests in test/unit/test_combat.gd; full suite 1126/1126, lint 0, name_check 0. Driven live via the bridge: pause + step-time frame by frame confirmed the lash, the arc, the landing on CARRY_ANCHOR (carry_offset 24,44 against an unmoved position 200,96) and the corpse staying up on the flower. Vine constants widened after that run - see log-devtools.md 2026-08-29.

description:

title: Thirty files are over 500 lines, and the test half of that contradicts CLAUDE.md
description:
Measured 2026-08-29 on main at 91dc3b8, with 'wc -l game/*.gd test/unit/*.gd tools/*.gd | awk $1>500'. Thirty files. The top of the list:

  23083  test/unit/test_selftest.gd
  11299  test/unit/test_combat.gd
   9288  test/unit/test_placement.gd
   5092  test/unit/test_economy.gd
   4405  game/hud.gd
   4361  game/game.gd
   2026  game/pest.gd
   1711  game/run_config.gd
   1649  test/unit/test_board.gd
   1446  game/plant.gd
   1420  game/wave_director.gd

then a tail of nineteen more between 505 and 1402, ending game/cue_legend.gd at 505.

THE FINDING IS NOT THE COUNT. It is that the four biggest are TEST files, and splitting them is the opposite of what this repo's own instructions say. CLAUDE.md's harness section is explicit: 'res://test/unit/test_selftest.gd -- add to it, don't start a new file beside it', and the reason given is that /verify re-runs everything in test_dir on every subsequent change, so a check written there is inherited by the next session. The four test files are 48762 of the 76000-odd lines in this survey, i.e. the majority of the problem is in the half where the house rule says do not split.

So this needs a DECISION before it needs work, and the decision is the deliverable:

* If the size rule wins, CLAUDE.md's harness block has to change with it -- and note that block is regenerated by /scaffold-godot-harness, so an edit there is overwritten on the next refresh. That makes it a change to the harness upstream, not to this repo.
* If CLAUDE.md wins, the rule applies to game/ and tools/ only, and the survey is nineteen production files, of which game/hud.gd (4405) and game/game.gd (4361) are the two that actually matter.

WHY THIS WAS NOT JUST DONE. game/game.gd was owned by a parallel lane the day this was filed, and test/unit/test_mirror_parity.gd now hand-steps a hosted game.tscn and compares eight economy axes against tools/run_sim.gd -- so a game.gd split moves the ground under a gate that was built precisely to notice movement. Split it AFTER that gate is trusted, not before, and re-run the recorded run_sim.gd:417 mutation afterwards to prove the gate still fails when it should.
acceptance_criteria: A written decision on which of the two rules governs test/unit/, recorded where the next session reads it rather than in this bead. If the answer is that game/ and tools/ are in scope and test/ is not, the survey narrows to nineteen files and the two that matter are named with a proposed split each. No file is split before test/unit/test_mirror_parity.gd has been shown to still fail under the recorded mutation.
close_reason: Decision recorded in cycle-log.md (## Cycle 181): CLAUDE.md's append-only rule wins for test/unit/ (that block is regenerated by /scaffold-godot-harness from the upstream project, not this repo's call). The 500-line convention applies to game/ and tools/ only -- narrows to 23 files (re-measured post-4-lane-fan-out). game/game.gd (4544) and game/hud.gd (4405) are the two that matter; filed as their own beads (plant-tower-defense-2dlh, plant-tower-defense-tar5) with their sequencing constraints rather than attempted here -- each is a bigger undertaking than fits alongside a fan-out, and game.gd sits next to the parity gate this cycle just finished trusting.

title: Extract the five RunSim/Game mirror branches that CAN become shared statics
description:
Lane B of cycle xca3 identified five mirrored branches whose bodies are already identical bar a variable name, and wrote each out as copy-pasteable GDScript rather than applying it, because game/game.gd and tools/run_sim.gd were owned by another lane that cycle. The full text is in that lane's report; the shapes are:

(a) Game.kill_payout(pest, under) -> {seeds, husk} -- the two arithmetic lines in _on_pest_died that actually drift. Highest value: collapses the seed price and the husk price into one place.
(b) Game.refresh_neighbour_buffs_over(plants) -- the WHOLE body of _refresh_neighbour_buffs. It differs from RunSim's only in _plants vs plants, and both are the same cell -> Plant dictionary. Game._refresh_neighbour_buffs() becomes one line.
(c) Game.apply_weather_over(plants, next) -- the garden half of _apply_weather. The overlay and banner stay with the caller; those are the only part a driver with no HUD cannot do.
(d) Game.brood_entries(parent) -> Array[Dictionary] -- the geometry of _spawn_brood, which is the whole body bar the guard.
(e) Game.setup_pest(pest, species, on_board, wave) -- the setup pair in _new_pest. Parenting, the two signals and the ambience stay with the caller, because those are what actually differ.

This continues the pattern 784c0ff started with Game.new_plant and Game.weather_seed_value_for: every mirrored branch that CAN become a shared static should, so the parity gate covers only what genuinely cannot.

THREE THINGS DELIBERATELY NOT EXTRACTABLE, recorded so they are not re-proposed:
* _install_plant / RunSim._install. The obvious build_plant() static would have to call plant.setup() before the caller's add_child(), and Plant.setup() joins the tree-global plants group -- so the extraction reorders the one thing _install_plant's own header calls the thing a caller could get wrong.
* _on_pest_escaped, _on_plant_grew_seeds, _on_plant_destroyed. One or two lines each, and the shared part is already a signal payload.
* _tick_cross_breeding's clock could become cross_tick(clock, delta), but it is three lines and the two copies already differ in what they do after the tick. Marginal.

DOES NOT MAKE test_mirror_parity.gd REDUNDANT, and this is the trap. Each extraction makes the gate compare a shared static against itself for that branch. What the gate checks and no static can is the COMPOSITION: the order the payments happen in, which counter each one increments, and whether a branch fires at all.
acceptance_criteria: Each of (a)-(e) is either extracted as a static on Game and called from both sides, or has a written reason beside it for why not. test/unit/test_mirror_parity.gd still passes, and still FAILS when a mirrored branch is mutated -- re-run the recorded run_sim.gd:417 mutation to prove the gate did not become vacuous as the bodies converged.
close_reason: Extracted all five (a)-(e) mirror branches into shared Game statics (kill_payout, refresh_neighbour_buffs_over, apply_weather_over, brood_entries, setup_pest), called from both Game and RunSim; the three already-decided non-extractable branches left untouched. Re-ran the recorded run_sim.gd mutation (+paid+1 on seeds_from_kills) post-extraction: test_mirror_parity.gd still fails on exactly that axis, proving the gate still checks composition, not vacuously comparing a static to itself. title: [bug] Diagonal bars on the corner grass are a cue the player has no route to the sentence for
description:
Reported out of band, verbatim: "there seems to be some weird diagonal lines on the corner
of the map, in the grass area."

Those lines are not a rendering artifact. They are the board-wide dead-ground cue, working
exactly as built — and the report is the finding: a player looking straight at the cue read
it as a glitch, because on the screen they were looking at, nothing had ever named it.

## WHAT THE GAME DOES NOW (verified 2026-08-28, by reading the call chain end to end)

- `PlacementPreview.DEAD_BAR_ANGLE = -PI * 0.25` (`game/placement_preview.gd:159`) — the
  bars are diagonal by construction, one stroke per cell through the cell centre
  (`dead_bar_arm()`, `game/placement_preview.gd:785`).
- `Board.mark_dead_ground()` (`game/board.gd:952`) paints one `Line2D` per marked cell into
  a `DeadGroundMarks` layer added last, so the marks sit over the tiles and the page frame
  (`game/board.gd:1004`). Buildable cells only — the road is filtered out — so every bar a
  player sees is **on grass**.
- The marked set is `PlacementPreview.board_dead_cells(board, _hovered_shop_plant,
  bank.unlocked)`, called from `Game._refresh_dead_ground()` (`game/game.gd:1509-1519`),
  which `Game._refresh()` calls on every seed payout. With **nothing** hovered in the shop
  it answers about the garden's unlocks: every buildable cell further from the road than the
  longest reach the player owns. On the default 14x9 road (`Board.PATH_CORNERS`,
  `game/board.gd:50`) those are the cells farthest from the snake — i.e. the corners.
  `test_dead_ground_is_exactly_the_cells_no_road_cell_reaches`
  (`test/unit/test_board.gd:1348`) is the definition of that set.
- Colour is `board_dead_color()` = slate `DEAD_COLOR` at `BOARD_DEAD_ALPHA = 0.40`
  (`game/placement_preview.gd:774`), width `DEAD_BAR_WIDTH = 3.0`.

**So: the cue exists, it renders where reported, and it is on screen from the opening
screen.** `Game._offer_dead_ground_hint`'s own header says so in as many words: "these bars
are on the board from the opening screen" (`game/game.gd:1527`).

## THE ACTUAL DEFECT: the bars are ambient, the sentence that names them is not

`_offer_dead_ground_hint()` (`game/game.gd:1556`) returns early unless
`_hovered_shop_plant != &""`. The one line that ever names the cue —
`Hud.dead_ground_tip()`, "Slanted bars mark grass this plant would never fire from — plant
it closer to the road" (`game/hud.gd:3884`) — is therefore reachable **only** by hovering a
shop packet. A player who selects plants by clicking, or who looks at the board before
touching the bar at all, sees unexplained diagonal slate strokes on the far grass and has no
route to the sentence.

That gate was a deliberate decision and its reasoning is written out at
`game/game.gd:1523-1549`: ungated, the hint would fire at a board the player has done nothing
to and would teach "some grass is far from the road" — true and unactionable. The reasoning
is about the HINT ROW. It is not an argument that the ambient bars should be visible before
the sentence is reachable, and this report is the evidence that the two halves came apart.

`CueLegend` records the same tension from the other side: row 6 lists the board dead-ground
bars as TAUGHT "by HINT_DEAD_GROUND, cycle 151" (`game/cue_legend.gd:90-92`), and the "still
no [grammar row]" note at `game/cue_legend.gd:120` calls it "the strongest case". The
coverage claim in row 6 is only true for a player who hovers.

## THE CHOICE THIS BEAD IS ASKING FOR (pick one, in the bead, before implementing)

1. **Do not paint what nothing explains.** Suppress the ambient (no-hover) set entirely; keep
   the marks only while a shop packet is hovered, where the sentence is already reachable.
   Smallest change, and it makes row 6's claim honest. Costs the ambient cue, which was added
   on purpose (plant-tower-defense-g8kc).
2. **Make the sentence reachable without a hover.** Widen the gate — e.g. offer once after the
   first placement, or on plant SELECT as well as hover — keeping the ambient bars.
3. **Give it a grammar row** in the notebook (`CueLegend`), which is the route
   `game/cue_legend.gd:120` explicitly considered and declined for width reasons.

Not a fix: changing the angle or the colour. Diagonal-on-grass is the cue's whole shape and
is shared with the hover bar by construction.

## TESTS AND BUDGETS A FIX WILL MEET

- `test/unit/test_selftest.gd:20948` `test_the_dead_ground_hint_waits_for_a_hovered_packet` —
  **pins the current gate**. Option 2 changes this test; changing it is the deliverable, not
  a casualty, and the replacement must still pin whatever the new gate is.
- `test/unit/test_selftest.gd:21000` `test_the_dead_ground_hint_is_spent_only_once`
  (`RunConfig.HINT_DEAD_GROUND`).
- `test/unit/test_placement.gd:6618` `test_the_shop_hover_is_wired_to_the_boards_dead_ground`
  — option 1 must keep the hover path intact.
- `test/unit/test_placement.gd:6246` `..._matches_the_hover_cue_plant_by_plant` and `:6294`
  `test_the_dead_sets_are_nested_so_the_two_cues_can_never_be_two_marks` — the ambient set and
  the hover set are asserted NESTED; do not break the nesting.
- `test/unit/test_placement.gd:6544` `test_remarking_dead_ground_reuses_its_marks_instead_of_
  growing_the_board` — the pool is reused, never re-created; a fix that clears by freeing
  marks fails this and shows as node churn on `performance --by-type`.
- `test_the_board_mark_and_the_hover_bar_are_one_stroke_not_two` — the board mark and hover
  bar must stay one stroke from one `dead_bar_arm()`.
- Contrast budget: `GardenTheme.GROUND_SEPARATION_MIN = 0.12` (`game/garden_theme.gd:163`),
  swept at `test/unit/test_placement.gd:7003-7032`. `BOARD_DEAD_ALPHA = 0.40` composites to
  0.149 separation on grass and clears it by a quarter; its header
  (`game/placement_preview.gd:766-773`) records that 0.34 cleared by six thousandths. Any
  alpha nudge is re-priced by that sweep.
- `game/cue_legend.gd` row 6 is a written coverage claim. If option 1 or 2 lands, row 6's
  parenthetical must be updated to match, and `CueLegend`'s own consistency gate will read it.

## ACCEPTANCE

Code-only, closeable by the commit that lands it:

1. One headless test in `test/unit/` that pins the chosen behaviour by name — for option 1,
   that `Game`'s no-hover refresh marks zero cells and a hovered refresh marks a non-empty
   set; for option 2, that the hint is offered on the new trigger with no shop hover and
   still only once. Vacuity guard required: assert the non-empty side is non-empty.
2. `game/cue_legend.gd` row 6's coverage note edited to state the new truth, and the
   `game/game.gd:1523-1549` header amended — it currently argues for a gate that the fix may
   have moved, and a stale argument there is worse than none.
3. `python tools/run_tests.py` and `godot --headless --path . --script res://tools/lint_project.gd`
   both exit 0.

Explicitly NOT acceptance: a screenshot. Whether the corners now read as intentional is a
live-game audit and belongs in a separate bead if wanted — see this project's history of a
bead sitting ready for twelve cycles because its code half had shipped and its evidence half
needed a running game.

---

DECIDED 2026-08-29 by the reporter, from a crop of the live board (image.png): none of the
three options in the description. **Change the glyph.** The bars stop being a shape that
needs a sentence and become a padlock, which carries its own meaning.

Scope this pulls in, all of it forced by invariants already asserted:

* The board's ambient mark and the hover dead bar are ONE stroke by construction
  (`PlacementPreview.dead_bar_arm`, asserted by
  `test_the_board_mark_and_the_hover_bar_are_one_stroke_not_two`). Both become the lock,
  from one shared geometry function, or that invariant is what the change breaks.
* The redundant-patch cue (two parallel bars at `DEAD_BAR_ANGLE`) is NOT changed. Its
  header derives it from the dead bar ("dead ground is one straight bar; redundant ground
  is two parallel bars on that same angle") and that sentence stops being true, so the
  header is rewritten even though the drawing is not.
* A padlock is a shape `OVERLAY_GRAMMAR.md` does not have. It is appended as a new
  numbered row rather than slotted in, per that table's own renumbering warning. Row 6
  ("straight line through a box") keeps only the redundant pair and therefore goes
  `untaught` in `CueLegend`'s ledger, because `seen_dead_ground_tip` moves to the new row.
* `Hud.dead_ground_tip()` and the `seen_dead_ground_tip` card both say "Slanted bars" in
  their text. Both are rewritten; `tools/teaching_ledger_check.py` reads the
  `grammar_row` key and will fail if the ledger and the card disagree.

The hint is KEPT, not deleted. A lock reads as "you cannot do this here" on sight; it does
not on its own say "because this plant's reach does not touch the road, so move one bed
closer". The icon fixes the reported problem — a mark that looked like a rendering
artifact — and the sentence still carries the counter-play.
design:
Fixed by changing the glyph, which was the reporter's own call and none of the three options
this bead was filed with. The dead-ground mark is a padlock.

WHAT LANDED
* `PlacementPreview.dead_lock_points()` — one static returning the 16-point outline, centred
  on the cell. `LOCK_BODY_HALF_W` / `LOCK_SHACKLE_RADIUS` / `LOCK_HALF_HEIGHT` are fractions

* `_draw_dead_bar()` -> `_draw_dead_lock()`, drawing those points with `draw_polyline`.
* `Board.mark_dead_ground()` takes a `PackedVector2Array` glyph where it took a
  `bar_arm: Vector2`. A Vector2 could only describe a two-point stroke, so the parameter had
  to widen with the shape. Still one `Line2D` per cell, still pushed in by Game, still the
  same pool.
* The hover mark and the board's ambient marks read the SAME function, so
  `test_the_board_mark_and_the_hover_bar_are_one_stroke_not_two` still holds — rewritten to
  compare every point rather than two endpoints.
* A padlock is a shape the grammar did not have: appended as row 13 of `OVERLAY_GRAMMAR.md`,
  with `NotebookScreen.OVERLAY_GRAMMAR_SHAPES` 12 -> 13. Row 6 keeps only the redundant pair
  and goes `untaught` in `CueLegend`'s ledger; `seen_dead_ground_tip` moves to `grammar_row`
  13. `tools/teaching_ledger_check.py` exits 0 on that pairing.
* The hint was KEPT and reworded — "A padlock marks grass this plant would never fire from —
  plant it closer to the road." A lock says "closed" on sight and does not say "because its
  reach does not touch the road"; the icon fixed the report, the sentence carries the
  counter-play.
* The redundant-patch pair is unchanged and its argument is not: it was legible by being
  COUNTABLE against a single dead bar, and that contrast is gone. Written down at
  `_draw_redundant_bars`, and pinned by a new test rather than left in a header.

WHAT THE RUNNING GAME CAUGHT THAT THE SUITE DID NOT
The first proportions (body 1.85x the shackle) drew a HANDBAG. Every one of the 1043 tests
passed on it — the shape test reads the `LOCK_*` constants, so it moved with them, which is
correct and is exactly why it cannot hold this bead's claim. Found in a screenshot of the
corner the report came from; retuned to 1.4 and re-read the live `Line2D` points to confirm
the running game took it. Recorded in `.devtools/verify-runs.jsonl` and in `log-devtools.md`.
