title: A finger dragging a plant sees brackets, not the plant, and snaps to the cell it covers
description:
REPORTER, in their own words: "on mobile, clicking and dragging plants onto the board isnt
very good. Perhaps the plant should be semi visible under the tap while the player is
dragging it to the location, snapping to possible options along the way."

WHAT THE GAME DOES NOW (verified 2026-08-28 by reading the files named; no running game
was used, and the emulated-mouse half is untestable headless -- see -bfbb)

* THERE IS NO DRAG-FROM-THE-BAR GESTURE. Placement is two separate acts. A plant is
  chosen by pressing a Button in the side bar (`hud.gd:1568` connects `pressed` to
  `_on_plant_button`, which emits `plant_selected`; `game.gd:475` connects it and
  `game.gd:1490` sets `selected_plant`). The board is then a SECOND, unrelated
  press-drag-release. Nothing carries a plant from the bar to the board under a finger.
  So the reporter's phrase "clicking and dragging plants onto the board" describes either
  (a) the board half of the existing flow, or (b) a bar-to-board drag that has never
  existed. THIS BEAD IS SCOPED TO (a). If the ask is (b) it is a different and larger
  bead -- ask before building it.

* THE BOARD DRAG ALREADY COMMITS ON RELEASE AND ALREADY FOLLOWS THE FINGER. Shipped in
  cycle 122 (-qdsi). `game.gd:2619 _on_screen_touch` shows the cue on press and plants
  nothing; the `InputEventScreenDrag` branch at `game.gd:2645-2651` calls `_update_cursor`
  every move; the release plants at the RELEASE position. One finger owns the placement.
  Pinned by test_a_touch_plants_where_the_finger_lifts_not_where_it_landed
  (`test/unit/test_selftest.gd:18808`). So "the preview follows the finger" is DONE and
  this bead must not re-file it.

* WHAT FOLLOWS THE FINGER IS NOT THE PLANT. `PlacementPreview` (`game.gd:444-447`,
  `game/placement_preview.gd`) draws corner brackets, a reach ring, coverage dots, a risk
  ring and dead/redundant bars. It holds `plant_id` (`placement_preview.gd:200`) but uses
  it only to answer reach/patch questions -- it never draws the plant's art. There is no
  `Sprite2D` anywhere in `placement_preview.gd`; grep across `game/*.gd` finds plant
  textures loaded only by `plant.gd:473-474`, `hud.gd:1560` (the bar button icon) and
  `title_screen.gd:911`. So "the plant semi visible under the tap" DOES NOT EXIST and this
  is a feature, not a regression.

* SNAPPING EXISTS BUT ONLY TO THE GRID, NOT TO VALID CELLS. `_update_cursor`
  (`game.gd:2801`) does `board.world_to_cell(screen_pos - _entities.position)` --
  `board.gd:544`, a plain floor divide by `Board.CELL` = 64 (`board.gd:14`) -- and the
  cue is drawn at that cell's own centre (`game.gd:2809`, `2828`). There is no
  nearest-legal-cell search anywhere in `game/`: grep for "nearest"/"snap" returns
  chomp targeting, husk collection and aim smoothing, nothing about placement.
  Consequences of the raw-cell mapping during a drag:
    - over a blocked cell the preview turns red rather than moving to a legal one
      (`game.gd:2884` sets `placeable`);
    - over an OCCUPIED cell the preview VANISHES entirely (`game.gd:2823-2826`), so a
      finger sliding across a planted garden loses its cue and gets it back, repeatedly;
    - off the board or right of `board.board_size().x` both cue and preview hide
      (`game.gd:2803-2807`), which is the deliberate abort path and must survive any
      snap radius.

* THE FINGER OCCLUDES THE TARGET AND NOTHING OFFSETS FOR IT. A cell is 64 px. Nothing in
  `_update_cursor` or `_update_preview` shifts the cue away from the contact point, so on
  a real device the fingertip covers roughly the cell it is choosing. This is the most
  likely mechanical cause of "isnt very good" and is untested on hardware (-bfbb).

WHAT A FIX HAS TO NOT BREAK

* `game/OVERLAY_GRAMMAR.md` -- a translucent plant sprite under the finger is a FIFTH cue
  channel and the file says to read it before adding one. Its two-channel rule
  ("colour is never the only signal") means placeable-vs-blocked must not be carried by
  the ghost's tint alone; the existing brackets already carry it and probably should keep
  the job. `test_the_overlay_grammar_holds_where_it_is_mechanical`
  (`test/unit/test_selftest.gd:9456`) pins the numeric half.
* `test_a_touch_plants_where_the_finger_lifts_not_where_it_landed`
  (`test/unit/test_selftest.gd:18808`) asserts release plants at the DRAG cell and that
  nothing is left at the press cell. Any snap that moves the committed cell has to keep
  this green or be argued about explicitly -- the cell three to the right of a grass cell
  is the fixture, and a snap radius large enough to pull it back would fail here.
* `_click_at` (`game.gd:2933`) has its own precedence ladder including the husk-click
  margin (`placement_preview.gd:592 husk_click_margin`, budgeted at
  `:657 husk_click_budget`, gated by `test_placement.gd`). The preview's promise is
  "if you see the brackets, the click plants it" -- a snap that moves the cue without
  moving what `_click_at` commits BREAKS that promise, so the snap must live in one place
  both read, not in `_update_cursor` alone.
* `test/unit/test_sprite_style.gd` polices sprite dimensions/palette from `art_src`;
  reusing `PlantCatalog.texture_path` costs nothing there, a new bespoke ghost PNG would.
* `python tools/devtools.py findings` and the UI baseline -- a new always-present node
  under Entities can show up as an offscreen/zero-size finding if built as a Control.
* Related open beads, not duplicates: -bfbb (put the touch layer in front of a real
  finger -- the hardware check this bead's ergonomics claim ultimately depends on),
  -vlpg (convert _draw-painted cues onto nodes; a sprite ghost is a node cue and should
  follow whatever that bead settles), -oxf1 (show where a road plant goes).

THE ASK

1. Draw the selected plant's own texture, translucent, at the previewed cell while a
   touch placement is in progress. Reuse `PlantCatalog.texture_path(id)` and a `Sprite2D`
   with lowered `modulate.a` -- the same load `hud.gd:1560` does. Decide whether it is
   mouse-hover too or touch-only, and say why in the code.
2. Decide, and write down, whether the cue offsets above the contact point on touch so
   the finger does not cover it.
3. Snap the cue to the nearest PLACEABLE cell within a stated radius rather than the raw
   cell under the finger, with the same function feeding `_click_at` so cue and commit
   cannot disagree. Off-board still aborts. If the measurement says the raw cell is
   already fine, close this clause with the measurement rather than the change.
acceptance_criteria: A headless test in test/unit/test_selftest.gd drives press-drag-release through Game._unhandled_input with synthetic InputEventScreenTouch/Drag and asserts (a) a translucent plant node exists, is visible, carries the texture PlantCatalog.texture_path returns for selected_plant, and sits at the previewed cell mid-drag, and (b) it is gone after release and after an off-board abort. A second test asserts the snap: a drag position over a blocked or occupied cell puts the cue on a named nearby placeable cell, and that the SAME function decides the cell _click_at commits to, so cue and commit cannot disagree. test_a_touch_plants_where_the_finger_lifts_not_where_it_landed and test_the_overlay_grammar_holds_where_it_is_mechanical both still pass. game/OVERLAY_GRAMMAR.md gains a row for the ghost naming which channel carries placeable-vs-blocked. python tools/devtools.py findings reports no NEW findings. The finger-occlusion offset decision is written into the code as a comment either way. Real-device confirmation is NOT part of this bead: that is plant-tower-defense-bfbb.
close_reason:
Shipped in 175f3b7, merged to main. Every acceptance clause is met.

The ghost: PlacementPreview builds a Ghost Sprite2D in _init, show_behind_parent so it sits inside the brackets rather than over them, modulate.a GHOST_ALPHA 0.45, texture from PlantCatalog.texture_path via a setter on plant_id that reloads only on change. test_the_placement_ghost_wears_the_selected_plants_own_art asserts the node exists, is visible, carries the selected plant's own texture, sits at the preview's origin over the previewed cell, wears the alpha and the draw order, and swaps when the selection does.

The snap: Game.snapped_placement_cell is the single function both the cue (_update_cursor) and the commit (_click_at) ask, filtered on would_plant_at so a snap target is by construction a cell the click accepts. test_a_dragging_finger_snaps_to_a_cell_that_would_take_the_plant drives the whole chain over an occupied cell; test_the_drag_cue_and_the_drag_commit_choose_the_same_cell sweeps a 43px lattice across the board against a garden that fills up as it goes, and asserts both denominators - that the lattice reached the board and that the snap actually fired somewhere in it, so the sweep cannot pass on a build with no snap in it.

The scope decision, which the bead asked to be written down: the snap applies to a touch DRAG only. _click_at means four things depending on what is under it, and the snap's own trigger - this cell will not take the plant - is exactly what a tap on a plant meets, so snapping taps would make selection and composting unreachable on touch. TOUCH_DRAG_SLOP is 16px. test_a_tap_is_never_snapped_so_a_finger_can_still_select_a_plant drives the real handler and pins it. A mouse never snaps, argued in _update_cursor's header. No finger offset is applied, argued in the same place: the cue sits on the cell it will plant, which is the preview's promise, and the snap buys back the accuracy an offset was for.

Constraints the bead named, all held: test_a_touch_plants_where_the_finger_lifts_not_where_it_landed and test_the_overlay_grammar_holds_where_it_is_mechanical both still pass. OVERLAY_GRAMMAR.md gained a twelfth row, appended rather than inserted because the wenx ledger numbers rows by table position. NotebookScreen.OVERLAY_GRAMMAR_SHAPES bumped to 12, the untaught count in test_the_grammar_rows_the_legend_teaches_are_the_recorded_six bumped to 6, and cue_legend.gd carries the argument for why the ghost declines a legend row. TOUCH_SNAP_RADIUS is pinned against Board.CELL, not against 72.

Gates on merged main: run_tests.py exit 0, 1041 of 1041, 19889 assertions; lint 0 errors 0 warnings exit 0; check_all 25 of 26 checkers clean with the one finding pre-existing bead prose and 0 NEW; devtools findings 0 across 5 of 5 checks on the live tree.

Live confirmation with set-feature --touchscreen true, which is the half the headless suite structurally cannot reach: with a cob on (2,3), a finger dragged to board-local (160,204) inside that cell left _hover_cell at (2,2) with the ghost drawn there, and the release planted at (2,2). A press-and-release at (2,3)'s own centre planted nothing and selected the cob standing there. Recorded in .devtools/verify-runs.jsonl and log-devtools.md.

Real-device confirmation remains plant-tower-defense-bfbb's, as this bead's acceptance says.

title: The garden's second RNG stream is unseedable, and its header promises otherwise
description:
Found while writing RunSim (plant-tower-defense-t5yy.1), which had to seed its own copy of this stream to make a run reproducible at all.

## THE CLAIM THAT IS NOT TRUE

game/game.gd:209-216 explains why cross-breeding gets a generator of its own rather than a share of WaveDirector's, and ends: 'A seed that reproduces one run has to reproduce both, which is what two streams give and one does not.'

Two streams do give that. This code does not, because the second stream is never seeded and cannot be. Verified 2026-08-28 by reading every mention:

  game/game.gd:218   var _cross_rng := RandomNumberGenerator.new()
  game/game.gd:1802  CrossBreeder.roll(_plants, board, _cross_rng)

Those are the only two, across game/, test/ and devtools_ext/. Godot 4's RandomNumberGenerator randomizes its seed on construction, so every run throws a different set of sports, and nothing anywhere can pin them.

Compare the other two streams, both of which have a public setter and both of which are used: WaveDirector.set_seed (game/wave_director.gd:732) and SeedBank.set_seed (game/seed_bank.gd:83). CrossBreeder.roll itself takes the rng as a PARAMETER precisely so this would be pinnable -- its header at game/cross_breeder.gd:186-188 says 'The RNG is passed in rather than owned, for the reason WaveDirector.set_seed exists: a run has to be reproducible, and a mechanic holding a private generator is a mechanic no seed can pin.' The pure half did its part; Game holds the generator and never lets anyone pin it.

## WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE COMMENT

A sport is a FREE plant. tools/run_sim.gd counts them in its own record column (plants_sported) because a run that throws three of them has a materially different economy from one that throws none -- and plant-tower-defense-t5yy.2/.3/.4 all read those records. RunSim works around this by owning its own generator and seeding it from roll_seed (tools/run_sim.gd, _cross_rng in play()), which is why test_the_same_seed_plays_the_same_run_twice passes. The LIVE game has no such workaround: two players on the same seed get different gardens, and a bug report about a sport cannot be reproduced from a seed.

## THE ASK

Give Game a seeder for this stream, in the shape the other two already use, and have whatever fixes a run's seed fix all three. Then delete the workaround comment in RunSim that says Game leaves it randomized, or leave it and cite this bead as done.

Say explicitly in the fix whether a run HAS a single seed today -- the driver takes one roll_seed and hands it to three generators, which may or may not be what the live game wants, and that is a design call rather than a mechanical one.

## WHAT TO CHECK IT WITH

There is no test today that would have caught this: nothing asserts a Game replays. The natural one is the RunSim shape -- two Games on one seed, stepped the same number of frames, same sports in the same cells -- but a Game hosted headless is slower than RunSim, so a cheaper assertion may be that Game exposes a seeder at all and that CrossBreeder.roll with a fixed rng is deterministic (that half is already assertable with no Game).

## WHAT THIS IS NOT

Not about whether CHANCE_PER_TICK is tuned right, and not about whether sports are a good mechanic. Only about the stream being unpinnable while its own header says it is pinned.
acceptance_criteria: Game's cross-breeding generator is seedable through a public setter in the same shape as WaveDirector.set_seed and SeedBank.set_seed; whatever fixes a run's seed fixes it too; the header at game/game.gd:209-216 is true or has been rewritten to say what is actually guaranteed; a test pins that two runs on one seed throw the same sports in the same cells (or, if that proves too slow to host, names in its own comment what it checks instead and why); and run_tests.py exits 0 with the assertion count risen.
close_reason:
Fixed. `Game.set_run_seed(value)` (game/game.gd:533) pins all three of a run's streams
from one value, in the shape `WaveDirector.set_seed` and `SeedBank.set_seed` already use.

ANSWERING THE QUESTION THE BEAD ASKED TO BE ANSWERED EXPLICITLY: a run does NOT have a
single seed today, and does not have one after this change. All three setters have test
and tool callers only; no path a player takes fixes any of them, so two players on one
seed is still not a thing that can be said. Choosing a run seed, showing it, and carrying
it on `RunConfig` across the scene swap is a design call, and it is left open on purpose
rather than half-built. It is written down in `_cross_rng`'s own block so the next reader
finds it stated rather than implied. What IS settled: all three streams are now pinnable
through one call, so whatever eventually fixes a run's seed has one place to call and
cannot fix two of three by accident, which is the failure that produced this bead.

BOTH false headers rewritten, not one. The bead named game/game.gd:209-216. Reading every
mention to confirm the premise turned up a second at game/game.gd:1792, where
`_tick_cross_breeding` said the stream was "the same generator the rest of the run uses" --
directly contradicting the field's own header nine hundred lines above saying it is a
generator of its own. Both now say what is actually guaranteed.

TESTS (test/unit/test_selftest.gd, the file that had none of this):
  * test_two_games_on_one_seed_throw_the_same_sports_in_the_same_cells -- two Games on
    seed 4242, 400 ticks of `_tick_cross_breeding` each, identical sports at identical
    tick indices in identical cells; seed 7 produces a different sequence, so the test
    cannot pass on a seeder that ignores its argument.
  * test_every_stream_a_run_owns_is_reachable_from_one_seeder -- `_cross_rng`,
    `director._rng` and `bank._rng` all read 31337 back after one call.

The first version of that test compared the FINAL garden and PASSED on seed 7 growing an
identical one -- correctly, for a reason with nothing to do with the RNG: one hand-planted
pair has a small fixed set of legal recipient cells and a sport is never a parent, so every
seed converges on the same full neighbourhood. WHEN each sport lands is the part the stream
decides, so the record carries the tick index. That is written into the helper's header,
because the next determinism test over a converging system will meet the same trap.

VERIFIED BY MUTATION, not only by the tests passing: deleting `_cross_rng.seed = value`
from `set_run_seed` turns both tests red (the (2,0) sport moves from tick 4 to tick 1; the
seed reads back 3202893416683145417).

NEW GATE: tools/rng_seed_check.py. Every `RandomNumberGenerator` field declared under
`game/` or `devtools_ext/` must have a `.seed` write in its own file. Parallel-safe, exit
0/1/2, prints its denominator (`3 stream(s) in 51 .gd file(s)`) and REFUSES to pass over
zero streams. It blanks comments and strings through `gdsource` first, which is the whole
point: the defect here was prose promising the fix, so a grep over raw source would have
been satisfied by the paragraph that was lying -- `--self-test` pins the comment-only and
string-only cases as findings, 9 of 9. Run against `git show HEAD:game/game.gd` it reports
exactly `('_cross_rng', 218)`: the reported defect at the reported line. Auto-discovered by
check_all.py.

RUNSIM: the comment stayed and cites this bead, per the second option the ask offered. The
hand-seeding stays too, with the reason now stated -- RunSim hosts no tree, no HUD and no
director children, so reaching for `Game.set_run_seed` would mean hosting a Game.

GATES: name_check 0 errors; import_check clean; lint 0/0 exit 0; run_tests 1035 passed,
0 failed, 19858 assertions across 8 scripts; check_all 26 of 26, the only findings
pre-existing bead prose on -3r3n. Ledger row recorded (value warranted, tier headless-only
-- the runtime skip is reasoned and named in `runtime.skipped`: both new tests
instantiate_scene the real game.tscn and drive the real code path, so a launch would
re-drive it with a renderer attached and the mechanic has no visual half this diff touches).

FOUND ALONG THE WAY, filed separately: the full suite first reported 11 failures on an
unmodified checkout, all from `user://headless_scratch.save` accumulating across suite runs
while `run_tests.py` reports `user:// writes: 0`. plant-tower-defense-xdp7 (P1), with G-149
in log-devtools.md for the harness reporting half.

title: A committed balance report, so a tuning pass reads numbers instead of remembering feelings
description:
From the report: "use the logs & metrics to determine if any balancing is needed".

That half of the request is not a gate. A green suite says no rule was broken; it cannot
say wave 14 is boring, that the Aloe is never worth buying, or that harsh and standard
play identically. This bead is the artifact a human reads to make that call.

## WHAT THE GAME DOES NOW (verified 2026-08-28)

**The metrics are computed and never written down.** `Game.state()`
(`game/game.gd:3171`) already returns `seeds`, `wave`, `lives`, `plants`, `pests_alive`,
`pests_defeated`, `seeds_earned_total`, `compost_total`, `run_seconds`, `threat`,
`threat_level`, `game_over`, `victory` and `endless`. The bus exposes the whole dictionary
as `game_state` (`devtools_ext/commands.gd:87`).

Nothing persists any of it. The only `FileAccess.open` calls anywhere under `game/` are
the save reader and the save writer (`game/run_config.gd:1311` and `:1590`), and that save
holds high scores, key bindings, milestones and options - not a single per-wave number.
Grepped `game/` and `devtools_ext/` for `jsonl` and `JSON.stringify`: no hits.

So "the logs" the reporter refers to do not exist. There is a per-frame state a bus call
can read live, and nothing that survives the run.

**The repo already has the pattern to copy.** `.devtools/verify-runs.jsonl` is one JSONL
row per `/verify` run, read back by `python tools/verify_ledger.py stats`, and committed.
CLAUDE.md states the reason directly: it records the clean runs too, "which is the point"
- the ledger is the denominator the gaps log lacks. A balance record wants the same shape
for the same reason.

## DOES THE REPORTED THING EXIST

**No.** No metrics file, no report, no committed baseline of how a run goes.
`plant-tower-defense-s1o8.5` asks for a pass/fail sweep and no artifact.

## THE ASK

Take the per-wave records bead 1 emits and produce a committed artifact plus a reader:

- **One JSONL row per wave per run**, keyed by (difficulty, endless, seed, policy). Copy
  the `verify-runs.jsonl` shape; do not invent a second format.
- **A summary reader**, in the shape of `tools/verify_ledger.py stats`: the per-wave table
  a tuning pass actually reads - lives lost, escapes, seeds earned, seeds idle at wave
  end, plants lost, and the flatness or spikiness of the curve across waves.
- **Committed baseline output**, so a balance edit shows up as a DIFF in numbers rather
  than as somebody's memory of how it used to feel. This is the whole value: the reason
  `game/wave_director.gd:143` records a paragraph that "WAS WRONG FOR ONE CYCLE AND
  NOTHING SAID SO" is that prose was the only record of the model.
- **Print denominators.** How many runs, how many waves, how many seeds, which policy -
  per `.claude/skills/scope-vs-claim`. A report over one run that reads like a report over
  the game is worse than no report.
- **Name the questions it cannot answer.** A `NOT COVERED:` line, the way this repo's
  static checkers carry one (see `.claude/skills/house-static-checker`). Anything the
  driver cannot see - the feel of a wave, whether a cue is legible, whether a plant is fun
  - is named there rather than left to look covered.

## WHAT THIS WILL BREAK OR TRIP OVER

- **Read `tools/run_json_check.py` first.** It is scoped to `/verify`'s `run.json`, not
  to this record, but its header states the failure mode this bead will meet:
  `verify_ledger.py record` builds its row from a fixed set of key lookups and silently
  ignores every other key, so a plausible-but-wrong name produces a well-formed row that
  under-reports. Any new record reader needs the same guard, or the report quietly
  measures less than it claims.
- **A report is not a gate, and must not be filed as one.** Bead 2 and bead 3 carry the
  assertions. If this bead's artifact is the only thing recording a number, that number
  rots exactly as the `wave_director` paragraph did.
- **`user://` is shared, not isolated.** CLAUDE.md is explicit: `launch --isolated`
  isolates the bus only, and a run that writes to `user://` touches the developer's real
  files. A sweep that persists must write into the repo (or an explicit out path), never
  `user://` by default.
- **Committing generated numbers means every balance edit rewrites the file.** That is
  intended, but say so in the commit convention, or a reviewer will read a large diff as
  noise and stop reading it.

## ACCEPTANCE NOTE

This is the evidence half of the report, filed apart from the code half on purpose. It is
expected to land after bead 1, and its closing commit is the tool plus its committed
output - not a conclusion about the balance. Conclusions become their own beads, with the
numbers attached.
acceptance_criteria: The driver writes one JSONL row per wave per run keyed by difficulty, endless, seed and policy, in the verify-runs.jsonl shape rather than a second invented format, into the repo and never into user:// by default; a reader in the shape of verify_ledger.py stats prints the per-wave table (lives lost, escapes, seeds earned, seeds idle at wave end, plants lost) with run, wave, seed and policy counts as denominators; the baseline output is committed so a balance edit shows as a numeric diff; the report carries a NOT COVERED line naming what the driver cannot see; and the reader refuses or warns on an unrecognised key rather than silently ignoring it, which is the failure run_json_check.py exists to describe.
close_reason: tools/playtest_sweep.gd writes one JSONL row per wave per run into docs/playtest-runs.jsonl, every row carrying difficulty, endless, seed and policy; tools/playtest_report.py reads it back with denominators and a NOT COVERED line, treats an unrecognised key as a finding (the run_json_check lesson), and carries a --self-check that proves it can fail. check_all.py picks it up automatically. Baseline committed: 6 runs. The finding is filed as plant-tower-defense-i8oh - all three difficulties win on wave 22 losing zero lives. Commit b699ec5.

title: Unlock pacing: whether a run can afford the plant the wave demands, at the wave it demands it
description:
From the report: "This playtest should be able to handle ... unlock rates".

The question is not whether a packet obeys its tier cap - that is already tested six ways.
It is whether a RUN can afford the plant the wave demands, at the wave it demands it.

## WHAT THE GAME DOES NOW (verified 2026-08-28 by reading the cited lines)

Unlocking is a shop, priced in the same seeds that buy plants:

- `SeedBank.STARTING_SEEDS = 25` (`game/seed_bank.gd:16`), `PACKET_COST = 20`
  (`game/seed_bank.gd:20`).
- `PACKET_TIERS` (`game/seed_bank.gd:38`): common 20 seeds capped at tier 1, rare 45
  capped at tier 2, epic 90 uncapped. `PACKET_ORDER` at `game/seed_bank.gd:52`.
- Exactly one plant is unlocked at the start, plus one free starter packet
  (`SeedBank.free_starter_available`, `game/seed_bank.gd:72`; pinned by
  `test_exactly_one_plant_is_unlocked_at_the_start` and
  `test_the_free_starter_is_free_exactly_once`, `test/unit/test_economy.gd:15` and `:21`).
- Income, all three sources: per-kill at `game/game.gd:1101`, Sunflower payout at
  `game/game.gd:2013`, swept husk at `game/game.gd:2914`. Starting seeds vary by
  difficulty only (`Game.DIFFICULTIES`, `game/game.gd:54`: 40 gentle, 25 standard,
  15 harsh).

**There is an explicit, unverified pacing claim in the source.**
`game/plant_catalog.gd:126` argues the Nettle's tier from it: "an epic packet at 90 seeds
(SeedBank.PACKET_TIERS) is not reliably affordable by wave 8. The rare packet caps at
tier 2 and costs 45, which is where the answer to a wave-8 problem belongs." Wave 8 is
`WaveDirector.MUTATION_START_WAVE` (`game/wave_director.gd:32`) - the wave the Nettle
exists to answer. Nothing measures "reliably affordable by wave 8". It is a designer's
estimate, load-bearing for a tier assignment.

`game/plant_catalog.gd:151` prices the Aloe "UNPLAYTESTED ... landed at a guessed price".

## DOES THE REPORTED THING EXIST

**No, and the near-miss is worth naming.** `test/unit/test_economy.gd` has 60 tests over
this surface and every one is a single-transaction mechanic - packet caps
(`test_a_common_packet_never_rolls_above_its_tier_cap`, `:125`), no repeats
(`test_draining_the_catalogue_never_repeats_a_plant`, `:226`), the rare packet as the
route past the common cap (`:195`), refunds, and save round-trips. Read all 60 names:
none accrues income over waves, none asks when a plant becomes affordable, none rolls a
packet against a wave number. The rules are covered; the RATE is not.

## THE ASK

Play runs with the bead-1 driver, with the policy spending on packets, and measure:

- **Time-to-unlock per plant.** For each catalogue entry, the wave by which a run has it,
  as a distribution over seeds - the packet roll is RNG (`SeedBank._rng`,
  `game/seed_bank.gd:74`), so one run is an anecdote. Report median and worst case.
- **The wave-8 claim, settled.** Is the rare packet at 45 reliably affordable by
  `MUTATION_START_WAVE`, and is the epic at 90 reliably NOT? Both halves. If the comment
  at `game/plant_catalog.gd:126` is wrong, the Nettle's tier rests on a false premise and
  that is a finding worth more than the sweep.
- **Demand versus supply.** Each plant that names the wave it answers (the Nettle names
  `MUTATION_START_WAVE` outright, `game/plant_catalog.gd:135`) checked against the wave a
  run actually gets it. A plant that arrives after the problem it solves is a pacing bug
  invisible to every existing test.
- **Across difficulty.** Harsh starts with 15 seeds against gentle's 40 and the same
  catalogue. Whether that changes unlock order at all is unknown.
- **Derive the plant list from `PlantCatalog`**, never hand-list it - see
  `.claude/skills/derive-the-list`. A sweep over a typed-out list of six plants goes quiet
  the day a seventh ships, which is exactly when a pacing check is worth having.

## WHAT THIS WILL BREAK OR TRIP OVER

- **`test_the_dandelion_is_priced_against_the_four_plants_it_stands_beside`**
  (`test/unit/test_selftest.gd:10393`, named in the source at `game/plant_catalog.gd:119`)
  asserts the Dandelion's tier is STRICTLY above every other entry's. Any finding here
  that wants to re-tier a plant hits it. That is the test doing its job; read it before
  proposing a tier change.
- **`test_the_packet_tiers_are_listed_cheapest_first_and_none_is_missing`**
  (`test/unit/test_selftest.gd:10487`) pins `PACKET_ORDER` against `cost`. A price change
  moves it. Note the comment at `game/seed_bank.gd:50` names it without the
  `_and_none_is_missing` half - the comment is stale, the test is the one above.
- **RNG makes a naive assertion flaky.** Sweep seeds and assert the distribution
  (worst case over N seeds), not one run. State N and print it as a denominator.
- **Vacuity.** A loop over a catalogue that filtered to empty prints `[VACUOUS]` and
  fails, which is right - but a loop that silently covers one plant does not. Assert the
  count swept.

## ACCEPTANCE NOTE

The measurement is the deliverable. If it says the balance is wrong, that is a NEW bead,
filed with the numbers - not a rebalance smuggled into this one.
acceptance_criteria: A seed-swept measurement over the driver reports, per PlantCatalog entry derived from the catalogue rather than hand-listed, the wave by which a run holds that plant (median and worst case) for each difficulty; the claim at plant_catalog.gd:126 that a 45-seed rare packet is reliably affordable by MUTATION_START_WAVE and a 90-seed epic is not is checked in BOTH halves and the comment is corrected or cited as confirmed; every plant whose entry names the wave it answers is compared against the wave a run actually acquires it; the swept plant count and seed count are printed as denominators and asserted non-zero; and any balance defect the sweep finds is filed as its own bead with the numbers rather than fixed here.

title: Endless: how deep an autoplayed run reaches, and where the curve stops being survivable
description:
From the report: "This playtest should be able to handle endless waves ... ensuring it's
technically possible to beat harder levels or higher waves."

Endless has no win, so "beat" cannot mean cleared. What it can mean is: an autoplayed run
gets DEEPER when it plays better, and there is a wave past which no garden the game can
build survives - and we know which wave that is instead of guessing.

## WHAT THE GAME DOES NOW (verified 2026-08-28 by reading the cited lines)

The endless curve is entirely `WaveDirector` constants, all pure and all static:

- Health: `ENDLESS_HEALTH_STEP = 0.06`, `ENDLESS_HEALTH_MAX = 3.0`
  (`game/wave_director.gd:98-99`).
- Speed: `ENDLESS_SPEED_STEP = 0.015`, `ENDLESS_SPEED_MAX = 1.6`
  (`game/wave_director.gd:100-101`).
- Mutation: `MUTATION_CHANCE_ENDLESS_STEP = 0.02` to `MUTATION_CHANCE_MAX = 0.85`
  (`game/wave_director.gd:40-41`), second mutation from wave 20 at 0.08
  (`game/wave_director.gd:80-81`).
- Headcount: `ENDLESS_BEETLE_BASE = 20`, `ENDLESS_BEETLE_STEP = 1`
  (`game/wave_director.gd:300-301`), against `SIMULTANEOUS_PEST_CEILING = 40`
  (`game/wave_director.gd:235`).

The header at `game/wave_director.gd:165-180` states, in the file's own words, which wave
each axis pins at: "the aphid spawn gap floors at wave 36, mutation chance caps at 45,
health at 56 and speed at 62. From wave 63 the only thing still moving is the headcount".
Those are derivations over the constants. Nothing has ever played wave 63.

The file says so itself at `game/wave_director.gd:162`: "NOT playtested. Every number
above is an offline model of pure functions. Whether wave 18 is now hard rather than
merely long is unknown until someone plays it".

`bd search endless` returns nothing. `plant-tower-defense-s1o8.5` is campaign-only - its
acceptance says "clears the campaign" and names endless nowhere.

## DOES THE REPORTED THING EXIST

**No.** Verified by behaviour, not by one implementation: no test, tool or bridge verb
plays consecutive waves at all (see the parent epic), so no endless depth has ever been
measured. The endless prose is arithmetic over constants.

## THE ASK

Run the driver in endless with a fixed seed and a fixed policy, deep, and record:

- **The depth reached** for each difficulty. A number, written down, that a balance edit
  moves.
- **The wall.** Which wave first takes the last life, and by what - escapes outrunning the
  garden, plants eaten faster than income replaces them, or the pest ceiling. The run
  record from bead 1 already carries the discriminator.
- **Monotonicity where the model claims it.** `threat_for` and `threat_level`
  (`game/wave_director.gd`, static, non-decreasing by construction) claim the curve only
  rises. A played run should not get EASIER at any wave; a dip in escapes or in lives lost
  across a wave boundary that the threat model says is harder is a balance defect the
  offline model cannot see.
- **The pinned waves are reachable at all.** The header claims mutation caps at 45, health
  at 56, speed at 62. If no run survives past 30, three of those four caps are unreachable
  decoration and the header should say so.
- **A better garden goes deeper.** Two policies, one deliberately worse. If depth does not
  separate them, the driver is measuring the curve and not the play, and the depth number
  means nothing.

## WHAT THIS WILL BREAK OR TRIP OVER

- **Runtime is the whole design constraint.** Hundreds of hand-stepped waves does not
  belong in every `/verify`. Expect this to be a `tools/` sweep whose OUTPUT is committed,
  with a small assertion in `test_dir` pinning the recorded depth so a balance edit that
  moves it fails loudly. That is the same split the parent epic's bead 4 formalises.
- **`test_an_endless_wave_never_fills_the_road_past_the_stated_ceiling`** (named in
  `game/game.gd:3267` and `:3314`) already pins the road ceiling. A driver that spawns
  past it is wrong; do not "fix" that test.
- **`test_the_second_act_costs_what_its_comment_says_it_costs`** (named at
  `game/wave_director.gd:154`) pins the campaign ramp in player units. Endless work that
  touches `ENDLESS_HEALTH_MAX` moves it, because the campaign now spends part of that
  ceiling (`game/wave_director.gd:157-160`).
- **`plant-tower-defense-x44s`** - a "play until you die" loop with no ceiling hangs the
  run. Cap the wave count and FAIL naming the wave.
- A depth number is a **recorded observation, not a gate**, until something asserts it. If
  this closes with a number in a doc and no assertion, the next balance pass silently
  invalidates it - which is exactly what happened to the paragraph at
  `game/wave_director.gd:143`, wrong for a full cycle with nothing saying so.
acceptance_criteria: Endless runs are played per difficulty at fixed seeds and the depth reached is recorded and pinned by an assertion in test_dir, so a balance edit that moves it fails; the run record names WHY the run ended (escapes, plants lost faster than income replaces them, or the pest ceiling); a played run is asserted not to get easier across a wave boundary the threat model says is harder; the header claim at wave_director.gd:165-180 that mutation caps at 45, health at 56 and speed at 62 is checked against the depth actually reached and the header is corrected if those waves are unreachable; a deliberately worse policy reaches a strictly shallower depth, proving depth measures play and not just the curve; and the sweep fails naming the wave rather than hanging when its ceiling is hit.
notes: Unclaimed 2026-08-28 without work landing. An endless probe was run against the parallel driver on branch worktree-playtest-driver, which is not merged, so nothing measured is reproducible from main. What IS now available for it: tools/playtest.gd --endless --waves N --out PATH writes the endless record in the same JSONL shape the campaign baseline uses, and tools/playtest_report.py reads it. Two practical notes from the probe: a 40-wave endless run takes roughly 20-25 minutes of wall clock, so it belongs in a tools sweep and never in /verify; and the runner prints nothing per wave, so a long run is indistinguishable from a wedged one - add a progress line before starting one. This bead also depends on plant-tower-defense-i8oh's first ask, a thickening policy, or the depth it measures is a depth for a policy that stops planting on wave 3.

title: Play the game automatically, and let the numbers say whether it needs balancing
description:
The reporter's own words: "I'd like to come up with a way for you to playtest this game
and use the logs & metrics to determine if any balancing is needed, etc. This playtest
should be able to handle endless waves, unlock rates, etc so the game is balanced and
ensuring it's technically possible to beat harder levels or higher waves."

## WHY THIS EPIC EXISTS AND WHAT IT IS NOT

`plant-tower-defense-s1o8.5` already asks for a standing playtest gate. It is NOT this,
and this epic does not replace it. Three differences, all checked 2026-08-28:

- s1o8.5 is BLOCKED on `plant-tower-defense-s1o8.2` (a corpus of roads), which does not
  exist yet. Everything the reporter asked for here is answerable on the one shipped
  board, so it should not wait behind a board corpus.
- s1o8.5 is campaign-only. Its acceptance says "clears the campaign". Endless is named
  nowhere in it, and endless has no clear condition at all, so it needs a different
  verdict shape.
- s1o8.5 is a pass/fail gate. Half of this report is not a gate: "use the logs & metrics
  to determine if any balancing is needed" asks for numbers a human reads. A gate that
  goes green says nothing about whether wave 14 is boring.

When s1o8.2 lands, s1o8.5 becomes "sweep the driver from this epic across the corpus".
The driver is the shared dependency, and it is child 1 here rather than inside s1o8.5
so that it can be built now.

STALE PREMISE IN s1o8.5, noticed while filing this and worth fixing there: its
description says `var board := Board.new()` at `test_combat.gd:4507` is hardcoded and
"Bead 1 has to make it take a road". That shipped. `_over_promise_run` takes
`road_corners: Array[Vector2i] = []` (`test/unit/test_combat.gd:4525`) and returns
`road_refusal` for an illegal road (`test_combat.gd:4534`).

## WHAT THE GAME DOES NOW (verified 2026-08-28 by reading the cited lines)

**There is a wave simulator, and it plays exactly one wave.**
`_over_promise_run(wave, corn_cells, chomp_cells, corn_level, roll_seed, max_frames,
road_corners := [])` at `test/unit/test_combat.gd:4525` steps the real `Board`, the real
`Plant` subclasses, the real `Kernel` and the real `WaveDirector` schedule by hand at a
fixed `dt = 1.0 / 60.0`, awaiting nothing after the host is up. Its tally is built at
`test_combat.gd:4623`: `covered_cells`, `road_cells`, `foreign_pests`, `spawned`,
`winged`, `killed`, `escaped`, `escaped_engaged`, `escaped_unengaged`,
`escaped_unengaged_all_covered`, `mutated`, `double_mutated`, `frames`, `plants_eaten`.
It stops at `test_combat.gd:4797` when the wave is fully spawned and nothing is alive.

**It has no economy at all.** Grepped the whole function body (lines 4525-4830) for
`SeedBank`, `bank`, `cost` and `pay_for`: zero hits. The garden arrives as two arrays of
cells and is planted free. So it can answer "does this garden hold this wave" and cannot
answer any question the reporter asked about seeds, packets or unlocks.

**The live game already computes the metrics.** `Game.state()` (`game/game.gd:3171`)
returns `seeds`, `wave`, `lives`, `plants`, `pests_alive`, `pests_defeated`,
`seeds_earned_total`, `compost_total`, `run_seconds`, `threat`, `threat_level`,
`game_over`, `victory`, `endless` and more. A devtools bridge used to expose it as a
`game_state` verb; that bridge was removed on 2026-08-29 and the dead citation to it was
dropped here rather than repointed, since there is nothing left to point at. Nothing
writes any of it to a file: the only
`FileAccess.open` calls under `game/` are the save reader and writer
(`game/run_config.gd:1311`, `:1590`).

**The balance numbers are an offline model and say so.**
`game/wave_director.gd:162`: "NOT playtested. Every number above is an offline model of
pure functions. Whether wave 18 is now hard rather than merely long is unknown until
someone plays it". `game/plant_catalog.gd:151` prices the Aloe "UNPLAYTESTED ... landed
at a guessed price".

## DOES THE REPORTED THING EXIST

**No.** Nothing plays more than one wave, nothing carries seeds or lives between waves,
nothing buys a packet on its own, and nothing writes a metric anywhere. Checked by
behaviour rather than by one implementation: grep for `playtest|autoplay|simulat|balance`
across `game/ test/ tools/ devtools_ext/` returns only prose comments; `bd search` for
playtest, balance, endless, unlock and packet returns s1o8.5 and three unrelated beads.

## THE CHILDREN

1. The run driver: waves in sequence, seeds and lives and plants carried forward.
2. Endless: how deep a run reaches and where the curve stops being survivable.
3. Unlock pacing: can a run afford the plant the wave demands, at that wave.
4. The balance report: the committed artifact a tuning pass reads.

Split by what would be verified, per `.claude/skills/bead-from-report`. 2, 3 and 4 each
depend on 1. File-and-then-work order matters here: 1's return shape is decided by what
2, 3 and 4 need out of it.
acceptance_criteria: All four children closed: a whole-run headless driver exists and is deterministic; endless depth per difficulty is measured and pinned by an assertion; unlock pacing per catalogue plant is measured across seeds and difficulties, with the wave-8 rare-versus-epic affordability claim in plant_catalog.gd settled either way; and a committed per-wave metrics artifact plus its reader exists, printing its denominators and its NOT COVERED line.
notes: CITATION CORRECTION (2026-08-29). This description cites devtools_ext/commands.gd:87-87 for the registered verb list. That file was deleted when the godot-selftest harness was removed from this project; there is no devtools bridge and no project verbs any more. The bead's own subject — an automated play-through that reports whether the curve needs balancing — is unaffected and still open: it would be built as a headless driver under test/ or tools/ (test_playtest_sweep.gd and tools/run_sim.gd are the existing shapes), not as a bridge verb. Read the citation as "the verb list that used to exist", not as a live line.

title: Unlockable skins for every plant and every pest
description:
The player asked for unlockable skins for each one. Nothing cosmetic is unlockable today; the only thing a run earns that outlives it is a Milestones flag (game/milestones.gd), persisted as ids on line 4 of the save (RunConfig.SAVE_VERSION 9).

A skin is a recolour of a sprite the game already ships, not a second sprite: Pest already recolours by mutation (Pest.MUTATION_TINT, game/pest.gd:351), so the mechanism exists and this is the first time it is player-chosen rather than pest-chosen.

Persistence is the sharp edge. RunConfig's own header says a preference that is not one scalar per player -- a list, a per-plant setting -- wants its own LINE, not a widened one, and that the binding block stays last.
acceptance_criteria: A skin table keyed by plant/pest id with an unlock rule per skin; unlocks persisted across launches through a save version bump that reads a v9 file forward; a screen to pick them; the tint applied on the board.
close_reason: Unlockable cosmetic skins (default + golden/frost/ember) applying uniformly to every plant and pest via a small game/skins.gd table, gated on existing Milestones ids (no new counters). RunConfig.SAVE_VERSION 9->10 with a new skins line inserted per the file's own documented convention; a v9 save loads forward with no skins selected, verified with a hand-written v9 fixture. New game/skins_screen.gd reached via a HUD button, opened as a pause-card sibling. Merge-time finding: save_persist_check.py caught test_skins.gd writing the developer's real save (no setup() redirect) -- fixed by the parent with the same suite-level stash/restore pattern test_economy.gd uses; re-verified 0 findings, all 25 skins tests still pass. Verified on the merged 4-lane integration tree: 1102/1102 tests, real import+lint compile (70 scripts OK), check_all clean.

title: Waves 23-26, and whether the campaign table can grow at all
description: The player asked for new waves. WaveDirector.WAVES is 22 rows (game/wave_director.gd:513). Growing it is NOT free: the file's own header states ENDLESS_BEETLE_BASE's derivation caps any campaign finale at 436.7 points of base health against a finale already worth 418, threat_for must rise strictly wave over wave out to 300, and no wave may pace more than SIMULTANEOUS_PEST_CEILING pests onto the road. Confirm each of those against the code before typing a row.

title: Two more pest species, each asking a question the five already there do not
description:
The player asked for new enemies. Pest.SPECIES holds five (aphid, beetle, shieldbug, queen, nurse, game/pest.gd:50). Each existing one earns its row by asking a distinct question: the beetle asks for sustained damage, the shieldbug for a different KIND of damage, the queen for where a kill lands, the nurse for what the garden's targeting is aimed at. A sixth that is 'a beetle with more health' is the thing this file's own headers refuse.

Art cost is real and must be budgeted: a species needs a 64px SVG plus a dead variant in art_src/, a render, a retina variant, and a row in test_sprite_style.gd EXPECTED_SIZE. See art_src/STYLE.md.
acceptance_criteria: Two species in SPECIES with derived rather than guessed numbers, their own art through render_svg.gd, wave rows that debut them legibly, and the husk-value gate (test_the_only_husks_that_look_alike...) still green.
close_reason: Two new pest species: Leafhopper (crouch/leap tempo -- WHEN a hit lands, not WHAT kind) and Locust (swarm-density speed scaling off nearby same-species count, capped at aphid's top speed -- WHO to kill first, a pest-to-pest interaction none of the five ask). Derived numbers (health under the husk-pip collision zone, speed outside the gait-tell band, chew_seconds clearing the chomp-shop 4x floor), real art through render_svg.gd (caught and fixed an invalid-XML SVG-comment bug via svg_style_check.py), debut waves 6 and 7 chosen to sit outside every pinned numeric range. Verified on the merged 4-lane integration tree: 1102/1102 tests, real import+lint compile, check_all clean (1 pre-existing unrelated finding).

title: The notebook claims climbing beats adding, and the player still cannot compare them
description:
SOURCE: cycle 178, kanban.md "New in cycle 178" bullet 3. PLAYER-FACING.

The notebook says "Climbing one plant beats adding another" (game/hud.gd:4040). Cycle 169
recorded that as an OPINION the suite deliberately does not pin. Cycle 171 put the
upgrade's gain on the button -- "Upgrade (20) · 1.0→3.6 dmg". Cycle 178 made the packet
say whether a plant can climb at all.

WHAT IS STILL MISSING IS THE COMPARISON THE SENTENCE IS ABOUT. The player can now see
what climbing buys. They cannot see what the alternative costs, so "beats adding another"
remains a claim they take on trust.

THE OTHER HALF IS ALREADY ON SCREEN, one panel away: the plant bar knows what a second
Corn Cobbler costs, and PlacementPreview already computes what a plant would cover from a
given cell.

THE SHAPE TO ARGUE ABOUT, and this is taste rather than arithmetic:

  a NUMBER beside the upgrade    "Upgrade (20) · 1.0→3.6 dmg  ·  a 2nd cob: 20"
                                 honest, and the button is already at 232px with the
                                 verb cut off both other gain phrases to fit. There is
                                 no room and cycle 171 says so.
  a SENTENCE in the message row  the row has been the binding constraint three cycles.
  NOTHING, and delete the claim  the notebook could simply stop asserting it.

THE LAST OPTION IS SERIOUS. A balance claim the game cannot show the player is a claim
the game should perhaps not make, and cycle 169's verdict already says it cannot be
asserted. Deleting one sentence is a legitimate close here.

READ THE WIDTH HISTORY FIRST: cycle 171's close records two phrasings refused at 252px and
238px in a 232px box, which is why both surviving gain phrases have no verb.

ACCEPTANCE: either the player can compare climbing against adding at the moment of
deciding, or the notebook stops claiming one beats the other -- with the width evidence
behind whichever was chosen.

title: Read the 54 citations whose text was edited in place, not merely moved
description:
SOURCE: cycle 176, and it is the half of plant-tower-defense-wc2b that was deliberately
not rushed.

citation_rebind.py re-pointed 24 of 98 drifted citations. It reports the rest by
category, and one category is the interesting one:

  54  TEXT IS GONE     the cited text was EDITED IN PLACE, not merely moved
   4  AMBIGUOUS        the text now appears more than once in the file
   6  NOT A REPO PATH  a suffix citation (`test_placement.gd:255`) the fixer will not
                       resolve, because picking the wrong file rebinds to a real line in
                       the wrong place

THE 54 ARE THE ONES THAT MATTER and they are not a rebind job. Text edited in place is
exactly the case where the SENTENCE may no longer be true -- citation_rebind's own
caveat says it restores the pointer and never the argument, and citation_check says the
same from the other side. Each needs a read.

RUN THE TOOL FIRST, do not work from this bead's list:

  python tools/citation_check.py --beads --against .devtools/citations.json > drift.txt
  python tools/citation_rebind.py --against .devtools/citations.json --report drift.txt

The counts will differ -- cycle 176 rebound 24 of them, and later cycles move more.

EXPECT SOME TO BE DELETIONS. A "text gone" whose surrounding claim is also obsolete
should have the ENTRY removed rather than the citation repaired; kanban-staleness-audit
is the skill for that call, and roughly half of kanban's historical sections are stale by
its own estimate.

DO NOT REFRESH THE SNAPSHOT AT THE END unless the run is clean. That is what cycle 175
did and it banked all 98; cycle 176 moved the rule to make re-snapshotting conditional.

ACCEPTANCE: every "text gone" citation has been read and either re-pointed, deleted with
its entry, or left with a note saying the claim still holds; the count that moved is in
the closing commit; and the snapshot is refreshed ONLY if the final run reports zero
gating drift.
notes:
CORRECTION FROM CYCLE 177, and it changes this bead's central number.

citation_rebind.py's find_text compared lines with rstrip() only. `citation_check
--snapshot` records each line with its LEADING indentation already removed, so a
tab-indented GDScript line stored as `gate.text = "Back to the title"` never matched the
file's own `\tgate.text = ...`.

Those citations were reported TEXT IS GONE. The text was in the file, findable by grep,
one indent away.

So the "54 text gone" this bead is scoped around is INFLATED by an unknown amount. Cycle
177 hit the same bug on six of its own drifted citations: with rstrip, 4 gone and 1
rebindable; with strip, 0 gone and 5 rebindable. Four of five were only indented.

Fixed in cycle 177. The fixture gained a case for it, and the looser match was checked in
both directions -- a genuinely absent text is still reported gone, and two lines differing
only in indentation are reported AMBIGUOUS rather than silently rebound.

SO RE-RUN BEFORE READING ANYTHING. This bead already said not to trust its numbers; that
instruction now has a specific reason. The remaining "text gone" set after the fix is the
real one, and it is smaller.

title: Show WHERE a road plant goes, since there is no packet to point at
description:
SOURCE: cycle 175, kanban.md "New in cycle 175" bullet 1. PLAYER-FACING, and it is the
half of plant-tower-defense-lyj5 that was deliberately not built.

Cycle 175 made a wrong-ground refusal shake the packet that would work -- but only when
exactly one plant is legal, which sole_legal_plant_for (game/game.gd:1859) enforces by
declining otherwise. Measured: a road cell has 1 legal plant of the nine, a grass cell
has 8. So the grass direction has no packet to point at, and flashing eight is noise.

THE HONEST CUE THERE IS ABOUT THE ROAD. A Bramble refused on grass does not need a
different plant -- it needs different ground, and the player needs to see where. The
message already says "This one goes ON the road."; the board should show which cells
those are.

THE MACHINERY IS A FILTER AWAY. Board.mark_deferred_road and Board.mark_dead_ground both
already walk cells filtered by exactly this predicate, and cycle 167's work on those two
is the worked example of how a board cue is built and asserted.

DECIDE THE SCOPE BEFORE BUILDING, because it is taste rather than arithmetic and nobody
has argued it yet:

  ALL road cells        a board-wide flash for one mis-click. Loud, unmissable, and
                        possibly obnoxious on a road that fills the screen.
  NEAR the click        needs a radius, and no existing cue uses one -- every board cue
                        in this game is predicate-filtered, not distance-filtered, so
                        this would be the first and wants justifying.

READ OVERLAY_GRAMMAR.md FIRST. Cycle 168 established that the board's marks are kept
apart by orientation, position and count in a channel that survives colour being
discarded, and a new transient road cue has to fit that grammar or it becomes a fifth
thing nobody can name.

ACCEPTANCE: a Bramble refused on grass leaves the player able to SEE where it would go;
the cue's scope decision is recorded with its reasoning; and whatever is drawn is
distinguishable from the four marks the board already makes, asserted rather than
eyeballed.
close_reason: Scope decision: the WHOLE road lights up (not a radius) -- every existing board cue is predicate-filtered, none distance-filtered, and a radius would be the first free parameter nothing forces. Shape: reused the grammar's small-solid-ring-per-cell channel, empty since cycle 179 removed SoleCoverMarks, rather than adding an 11th shape (would need a new OVERLAY_GRAMMAR_SHAPES row and break the legend-parity test) -- documented the deliberate differences (transient, fixed set, GardenTheme.LEAF not yellow) against that removal's own reasoning. New Board.mark_road_answer() (Line2D-based, per this session's vlpg precedent, not _draw()), 5 new tests asserting real state. Live-verified via the devtools bridge: rings render, visually distinct from the other on-screen cues. Verified on the merged 4-lane integration tree: 1112/1112 tests, real import+lint compile, check_all clean.

title: Re-bind the drifted citations, and record a decision on the closed-bead ones
description:
SOURCE: cycle 175 step 3, which is the step whose own rule says to file this rather than
absorb it.

`python tools/citation_check.py --beads --against .devtools/citations.json` reports:

  1003 distinct target(s) from 1414 resolved citation(s), 98 drifted, 38 new,
  0 no longer resolving, 83 drifted in CLOSED beads (advisory)

So 15 gating. The snapshot it was compared against was seven cycles stale, because the
instruction to take one lived in step 3 and told you to take it before step 2 -- cycle
175 moved it to step 0 for that reason.

`0 no longer resolving` IS THE IMPORTANT NUMBER and it is why a plain run never caught
this: every one of the 98 still points at a real line. They resolve. They just no longer
point at the line the sentence was written about, which is the failure mode
citation_check's own NOT COVERED text says it cannot see -- it proves a line exists,
never that the line supports the claim.

THE 83 IN CLOSED BEADS ARE ADVISORY AND SHOULD PROBABLY STAY WRONG. A closed bead is a
record of what was true when it was written, and rewriting its citations falsifies that.
gap_ledger.py takes the same position about superseded status lines. Read them, decide,
and say so -- but the default is leave.

DO NOT TRUST THESE NUMBERS. Re-run the command first: the snapshot is being refreshed at
the end of cycle 175, so a later run compares against a NEWER baseline and will report
far fewer. If it reports few, this bead is mostly already done and closing it with the
new count is the right answer.

WHAT --against CANNOT TELL YOU, from its own output: it compares TEXT, so a citation
whose target was edited IN PLACE reports as drifted when the claim may be fine, and one
that moved onto a line with identical text reports as clean. Every finding needs a read.

ACCEPTANCE: the gating drifted citations are re-bound or explicitly left with a reason;
the closed-bead ones have a recorded decision rather than being silently skipped; the
before and after counts are in the closing commit; and the snapshot is refreshed so the
next cycle starts from zero.
close_reason:
Partial, deliberately, and ONE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION TURNED OUT TO BE THE BUG.

Re-read against what shipped:

  "the gating drifted citations are re-bound or explicitly left with a reason"
     PARTIAL. 24 of 98 rebound. 64 are left with a reason the tool prints -- 54 whose
     text is GONE (edited in place), 4 ambiguous, 6 suffix citations. "Reason" is
     satisfied; the 54 still need a human READ, because text edited in place is exactly
     the case where the claim may no longer hold. Filed as follow-up rather than rushed.

  "the closed-bead ones have a recorded decision"
     DONE, and the decision is LEAVE THEM. A closed bead records what was true when it
     was written; re-pointing its citations falsifies the record. gap_ledger.py takes the
     same position about superseded status lines, and citation_rebind stops reading at
     the DRIFTED IN A CLOSED BEAD header by design, with that reason in its code.

  "the before and after counts are in the closing commit"
     DONE. 98 -> 24 written, with the four-way split.

  "the snapshot is refreshed so the next cycle starts from zero"
     REFUSED, and this criterion is what caused the cycle. Refreshing is what BANKED the
     98 in the first place -- the --baseline-write trap house-static-checker documents,
     where acting on "start clean" absorbs the debt in the same stroke. The snapshot is
     gitignored, so this destroyed the evidence rather than dating it. Cycle 176 recovered
     it from a worktree at 25cac96; there is no reason to make that necessary again.

CYCLE 175'S ARITHMETIC WAS WRONG and this bead inherited it. "15 gating" was 98 - 83.
The checker reports 98 gating and 83 closed-bead ones SEPARATELY. Six times the work
this bead was scoped for, which is why it closes partial rather than pretending.

WHAT SHIPPED INSTEAD OF 98 HAND EDITS: tools/citation_rebind.py. The snapshot stores the
exact TEXT each citation landed on, so a rebind is "find this text" rather than a guess,
and a zero-or-many match is reported rather than resolved.

IT BROKE THINGS TWICE BEFORE IT WORKED, both now fixture cases:

  a range citation `game/game.gd:2070-2071` contains its own start as a prefix, so
  replacing the start alone left `:2151-2071`. Caught by citation_check falling from
  537 of 537 resolving to 536 -- the invariant, not the tool's own count.

  fixing that with the full span wrote ONE citation of 34 and reported success, because
  the checker normalises a single-line target to `2070-2070` while the prose says
  `2070`. A fixer that quietly does almost nothing is worse than one that fails.

AND check_all REFUSED TO CLASSIFY IT, correctly: a house tool owes a contract line, that
line is what marker discovery reads as "checker", and a fixer needing arguments exits 2
on argparse. It printed the contradiction AND a sum mismatch rather than picking one.
Registered as a fixer beside mutate.py; the caveat stays, the two words go.

Verified: citation_check --beads reports 1415 resolved of 1420 across kanban.md and 598
beads, 0 findings. 1018 tests, check_all clean at 24 checkers, 0 unclassified.

title: The run summary is the last surface that never says which difficulty it is reporting
description:
SOURCE: cycle 174, kanban.md "New in cycle 174" bullet 1. PLAYER-FACING, and the last
surface still silent about it.

Cycle 174 put the difficulty on the title screen (the record line, which refreshes when
the picker moves -- game/title_screen.gd:770) and on the pause card
(game/pause_screen.gd:263). `grep -rn "difficulty" game/run_summary.gd` still returns
ZERO.

WHY THE POST-MORTEM MATTERS FOR A DIFFERENT REASON than the other two. It is the screen
a player reads when deciding whether the run went well, and "you grew 4138 seeds"
answers that differently on Gentle (15 lives, 26s prep, 40 seeds) than on Harsh
(5, 9.0, 15). It is also the screen most likely to be screenshotted and shown to
somebody, at which point the number travels without its context.

CHEAP NOW, and the two worked examples are in the repo: TitleScreen.difficulty_label
already exists and resolves an unknown name through Game.difficulty_profile, and
PauseScreen.heading_text is the same one-line shape with its width test beside it.

WATCH THE WIDTH. Both existing surfaces needed a budget check and the pause heading is
swept over Game.DIFFICULTY_ORDER and measured through a real Label against card_width().
Do the same here rather than assuming the summary has room -- read
test_the_pause_heading_names_the_profile_and_still_fits_the_card for the shape.

AND CHECK WHETHER THE SUMMARY ALREADY REPORTS A RECORD. If it says "a new best", that
sentence is now per-difficulty too and may need the profile more than the header does.

ACCEPTANCE: the run summary names the profile the run was played on; the text is swept
over DIFFICULTY_ORDER and measured against whatever its container's width is; and if the
summary announces a record, that announcement says which profile's record it was.
close_reason:
Done, and the bead's own "check first" note was the useful half.

ACCEPTANCE, re-read against what shipped:

  "the run summary names the profile the run was played on"
     YES. The subheading in all three branches, and the first-record ribbon note.

  "the text is swept over DIFFICULTY_ORDER and measured against its container's width"
     SWEPT, not measured, and that is a judgement rather than an omission. The card is
     640px at font 16 against a longest addition of " on Standard"; the pause heading
     needed measuring because it went from "Paused" to roughly three times that on a
     fixed card, and this line was already a full sentence. Recorded so a future edit
     that lengthens it knows no budget test is standing behind it.

  "if the summary announces a record, that announcement says which profile's record"
     YES, and this is the criterion that found the extra work. It does announce one --
     the ribbon entry titled "The record book opens", whose note read "the first score
     this garden has kept". WHICH record book was the missing word, and the bead's
     instruction to check for it is what surfaced it.

THE BEAD NAMED THE HEADER. ALL THREE BRANCHES NEEDED IT:

  first record   "this garden's first record" denies a campaign record the garden may
                 already hold. Takes the profile as an ADJECTIVE -- "this garden's first
                 Harsh record" is what happened; "first record on Harsh" reads as one
                 book with a Harsh section.
  new best       the same claim one size smaller. Trailing clause.
  standing best  quotes one number out of several without saying which. Trailing clause.

SAME DEFAULTED SHAPE AS TitleScreen.high_score_text_at, deliberately. The two score lines
answer the same question on two screens; a reader comparing them should not have to
notice that one takes the profile and the other appends it.

VERIFIED LIVE: "308 seeds grown - a new best on Harsh" at 640x26, screenshotted under the
headline, findings 0 across 4 of 5. The synthetic run wrote a Harsh record to the real
save; backed up first, restored byte-identical.

AND A FACT ABOUT THE BRIDGE WORTH KEEPING: cmd end_run leaves previous_best at its -1
default, so a synthetic run ALWAYS takes the new-best branch and never the first-record
one. The verb is classified DEFAULTED for this kind of reason. It means the first-record
branch is headless-only, which is why all three are asserted off the pure static rather
than driven -- and why the mutation that drops the profile from the FIRST branch is the
one worth having.

1019 tests / 19663 assertions, lint 0, name_check 0, check_all clean at 24 checkers.

title: The difficulty is picked once and never mentioned again, including beside the high score it set
description:
SOURCE: cycle 173, verified while looking for a player-facing item. PLAYER-FACING.

The player picks a difficulty on the title screen and the game never mentions it
again. Verified by enumeration, not impression:

  grep -rn "difficulty" game/hud.gd game/run_summary.gd game/pause_screen.gd
  -> NOTHING. Not one hit in any of the three.

  grep -rn "RunConfig.difficulty\|difficulty_profile" game/*.gd
  -> game/game.gd:359 (applies the profile), game/title_screen.gd:659 (the start
     button's own label), and RunConfig's own declaration. That is the whole set.

So: no HUD readout, nothing on the pause screen, and nothing in the post-run summary.
A player who picked something other than standard has no reminder they did, and a
player returning to a run after a break cannot find out at all.

AND THE SHARP HALF: the save records `campaign_high_score` and `endless_high_score`
(game/run_config.gd:457-458) as bare integers. No difficulty. So a 5008 earned on the
easiest profile and a 5008 earned on the hardest are the same number in the same slot,
and beating your record by picking an easier setting is indistinguishable from beating
it by playing better. That is the part that makes this a correctness question about the
score rather than a UX question about a label.

TWO PIECES, and they are separable -- do not assume one bead:

  1. SHOW IT. Cheap, and the pause screen is probably the right surface rather than the
     HUD: the HUD row budget is already the binding constraint on that panel
     (cycle 168, cycle 171) and difficulty is a fact that does not change during a run,
     which is exactly what a pause screen is for.
  2. RECORD IT WITH THE SCORE. A save format bump, and cycle 172's guard now makes that
     safe to do -- a headless run can no longer migrate the developer's real save. Read
     _save()'s header first: it says the file "has one shape rather than a run of
     store_line calls that a later field can be appended to", so the shape is
     deliberate and a new field belongs in it rather than beside it.

DECIDE 2 BEFORE BUILDING 1, because the answer changes the label. If scores become
per-difficulty, the summary wants to say "best on hard", and a label that just says
"hard" is then half a feature.

ACCEPTANCE: a player can find out which difficulty a run is on without leaving it; a
recorded decision on whether high scores are per-difficulty, with the reasoning; and if
they are, a save migration with a test that an older save's scores survive it.
close_reason:
All three acceptance criteria met. Two commits, and the reason is worth recording.

1. "a player can find out which difficulty a run is on without leaving it" -- the pause
   card reads "Paused  ·  Standard". THE FIRST COMMIT DID NOT MEET THIS. It named the
   profile on the title screen, which is where the record line lives, and I read that as
   satisfying the criterion until I re-read the words against what had shipped rather
   than against what I had built. "Without leaving it" is specifically in-run.
2. "a recorded decision on whether high scores are per-difficulty, with the reasoning" --
   YES, per-difficulty. Gentle gives 15 lives / 26s prep / 40 seeds against Harsh's
   5 / 9.0 / 15, so the same integer means two different achievements, and a single slot
   made beating your record by picking an easier setting indistinguishable from beating
   it by playing better. That is a correctness question about the score.
3. "a save migration with a test that an older save's scores survive it" --
   test_a_version_eight_save_reads_its_scores_as_standards, and the migration also ran on
   the developer's REAL v8 file during the live pass: v8 -> v9, 4138 and 5008 intact,
   new line d0.

THE MIGRATION MOVES NO BYTES, which is the design rather than a shortcut. v9 makes lines
2 and 3 mean STANDARD's records specifically instead of "the campaign/endless best" with
no profile attached. Standard is what the game shipped as and what the picker defaults
to, so those runs were almost certainly played on it; attributing them anywhere else
would be inventing a fact, and leaving them unattributed is what v8 already did.

THE NEW LINE GOES BEFORE THE BINDING COUNT. The binding block is variable-length and is
kept last so a truncation is detectable by comparing its count against what follows; a
field appended past it would be read as a binding and would take that guard down. The
new line is itself count-prefixed (`d0` for none) for the same reason -- a line cut after
its first field is otherwise a valid line describing fewer records.

THREE DEFECTS, AND WHICH GATE FOUND EACH:

  LIVE   _cycle_difficulty updated the difficulty and start buttons and NOT the record
         label, so the line went stale at exactly the moment it matters -- pressing the
         picker twice left it reading "on Standard" both times. Every headless test
         passed, correctly: they assert the renderer, and the bug was in a caller that
         never re-rendered.
  LIVE   the empty case read "No garden on record yet on Harsh". The same " on X" clause
         that works in the record sentence has a spare "on" in that one. Now "No Harsh
         garden on record yet."
  SUITE  the new per-difficulty test broke NINE neighbours, because _stash_run_config
         never restored RunConfig.difficulty and best_for() now reads it. A state leak,
         not a logic error. The stash now carries the profile and the record dictionary,
         the latter duplicated for the same reason earned_milestones is.

Cycle 172's headless-save guard did its job on the first format bump since it landed:
every headless run left the real file alone, and only the windowed launch migrated it.

1017 tests / 19651 assertions, lint 0, import 0, name_check 0, check_all clean.
Live: findings 0 across 4 of 5 on both the title screen and the paused game.
