title: A refused or recovered save is invisible to the player who lost the scores
description:
SOURCE: cycle 172, kanban.md "New in cycle 172" bullet 1. PLAYER-FACING.

RunConfig.load_status takes five values and is read by NOTHING outside its own file.
Verified: `grep -rn "load_status" --include=*.gd .` returns only game/run_config.gd and
test/ hits.

  absent     no save yet. Nothing to say.
  loaded     normal. Nothing to say.
  migrated   an old format was upgraded. Arguably nothing to say.
  refused    THE FILE WAS THERE AND WAS NOT READABLE -- truncated, or from a newer
             build, which test_a_save_from_a_newer_build_is_refused_not_reinterpreted
             (test/unit/test_economy.gd:1071) pins as deliberate rather than a bug.
  recovered  an interrupted _save left a complete temp file with no save beside it and
             the game adopted it.

In the last two the player sees a title screen showing zeros, or an older pair of
scores, and is left to conclude their records vanished. The game knows exactly what
happened and says nothing.

THE MACHINERY IS ALREADY THERE AND ALREADY CORRECT. This is not a request to change
how loading works -- the refusal is deliberate and the recovery is the safety net
working. What is missing is one line on the title screen.

NOT Hud.message_corpus(): that is the in-run message row and this is a title-screen
event. Look at how the title screen already reports things before inventing a surface.

WORDING: cycle 168's refusal rules apply -- say what happened and what the player can
do about it, not just the fact. "recovered" has a genuinely reassuring answer ("your
last save was interrupted; the scores are the ones from before it"). "refused" has a
harder one and may be honestly "your save is from a newer version of the game".

ACCEPTANCE: a refused or recovered load is visible to the player on the title screen;
the text is asserted in test_dir against both statuses; and the run reaches the branch
in a test rather than only being constructed.
notes:
CORRECTION: nothing was eaten. The double space bead_prose_check flags is deliberate
COLUMN ALIGNMENT in the load_status table in this bead's description -- the status
names are padded so the descriptions line up, and "refused" is shorter than
"recovered" by two characters.

The prose is exactly as written and needs no repair. This note is the waiver the
checker asks for, and it stands as the record rather than the field being rewritten,
which is that tool's own instruction.

Worth noting as a limit of the checker rather than a defect in it: its NOT COVERED
line already says it "cannot distinguish an author's deliberate double space from an
eaten word -- every finding needs a human read". That is exactly what happened here,
and the read took one look at the table. A checker that flagged nothing would have
been worse.
close_reason: Added TitleScreen.save_status_text(); refused/recovered load states now override the title screen's subtitle line. Pinned in test_selftest.gd (pure wording + a real title.tscn instantiation reading SubtitleLabel.text for both statuses).

title: Nothing tells the player which plants can be upgraded before they buy one
description:
SOURCE: cycle 171, kanban.md "New in cycle 171" bullet 1. PLAYER-FACING.

The notebook tells the player "Climbing one plant beats adding another"
(game/hud.gd:4029). Six of the nine plants cannot climb.

ENUMERATED, not guessed -- `grep -rn "^const LEVELS" game/*.gd` finds three in
game/: game/bramble.gd:112, game/chomp_flower.gd:64, game/corn_cobbler.gd:100. The
fourth hit is game/sfx.gd:508, a volume table. Sunflower, Sticky Sundew, Dandelion,
Mint, Aloe and Nettle have no ladder, so Plant.has_upgrades() is false and
_refresh_selection hides the Upgrade button entirely (game/hud.gd:2487).

THE DESIGN IS PROBABLY RIGHT. Not every plant should be a growth curve, and this
bead is NOT a request to give six plants ladders. The defect is that the advice does
not say who it applies to, and a player has no way to find out which three before
spending seeds on one -- they buy a Sundew, select it, and there is simply no button.

WHERE IT GOES: Hud.plant_button_tooltip (game/hud.gd:2021-2028) already composes name,
blurb and a conditional packet line, and a fourth clause is the pattern it is built
for. Derived from plant.has_upgrades() or from the catalogue, never from a list of
three -- cycle 171 found three ladders where its own bead named one, and a recorded
list is exactly how the fourth gets missed.

CONSIDER ALSO, and decide rather than doing both: the notebook card itself could name
the constraint. That is a rewording of player-facing prose and cycle 168's rules about
refusals apply -- keep the sentence one line, and check the message row's budget.

ACCEPTANCE: a player can tell, before buying, whether a plant can be upgraded; the
source of that answer is derived from the plant rather than listed; and a test asserts
it stays true for a plant added later.
close_reason:
Shipped, and ONE CRITERION IS MET IN SPIRIT AND NOT IN LETTER. Saying which.

  "a player can tell, before buying, whether a plant can be upgraded"
     YES. The packet tooltip says it in both directions, verified live on the running
     game: the Sundew reads blurb / "Does not grow - this is the plant it stays." /
     "Still in a packet: a Rare Packet (45) can hand it over.", in that order.

  "the source of that answer is derived from the plant rather than listed"
     NO, NOT LITERALLY. PlantCatalog.can_grow is a `match` with three ids in it. I looked
     for a true derivation and there is none available without new infrastructure:
     Plant.upgrade_ladder() is an INSTANCE method and the question is asked before any
     plant exists, and the catalogue has no id -> script or id -> scene map to load a
     constant from. Game._new_plant is itself a hard-coded match on id -> class, as is
     PlantCatalog.reach, so a list is this project's existing convention for exactly this
     lookup -- in two places already.

     WHAT THE LISTING IS GUARDED BY, which is why this is a defensible answer rather than
     an excuse: test_the_catalogue_and_the_plants_agree_about_which_can_grow instantiates
     EVERY id and compares the static answer against that instance's own has_upgrades().
     The list cannot disagree with the plants for longer than one test run, and the
     failure names the plant and says the match is what needs the new id. Proven by
     mutation: dropping BRAMBLE from the match fails it by name.

     Filed as a follow-up: an id -> class map would let can_grow, reach and _new_plant all
     derive, and it is a bigger change than this bead.

  "a test asserts it stays true for a plant added later"
     YES, and that is the same test.

INSTANTIATED RATHER THAN SOURCE-SCANNED, and this is worth recording because the obvious
alternative has a trap: `grep -rln "^const LEVELS" game/*.gd` returns FOUR files and only
three are plants -- Sfx.LEVELS is a volume table. A source scan would have to know that.
Asking the object removes it.

BOTH DIRECTIONS IS THE DESIGN, not symmetry for its own sake. Marking only the three that
grow leaves six silent, and silence on a packet reads as "not mentioned" rather than as
"no" -- the original complaint in a new place, applying to two thirds of the catalogue.
The test asserts both branches are taken by at least one plant, so neither can become
unreachable.

Verified: 1021 tests / 19687 assertions, lint 0, check_all clean at 24 checkers, findings
0 across 4 of 5 with 0 NEW ui_layout.

title: A road can make a plant unplayable and nothing in the game would notice
description:
SOURCE: cycle 170, kanban.md "New in cycle 170" bullet 2. PLAYER-FACING.

Cycle 170 asserted, for the Sundew, that every road in the corpus has somewhere
worth laying a patch: if the best buildable cell covers no road at
StickySundew.SAP_RADIUS (game/sticky_sundew.gd:34), a Sundew buys nothing anywhere
on that board and a 30-seed purchase is dead weight.

THE TEST CATCHES IT. THE GAME DOES NOT. Board.set_road (game/board.gd:100-118)
validates STRUCTURE only -- bounds, corner count, zero-length segments, and the
diagonal segment that would hang the walker in _ready() with nothing on screen. It
says nothing about whether the resulting board is worth playing.

THE ASK: a playability predicate beside the structural one. For every plant with a
reach, is there a buildable cell where it does something? Derive the plant set from
PlantCatalog.reach (game/plant_catalog.gd:289) rather than listing it -- a plant
added later must be asked automatically, and Bramble and Sunflower return 0.0 there
deliberately and must not be asked at all.

WATCH THE TWO REACHES THAT ARE NOT ABOUT ROAD. Mint and Aloe reach over PLANTS, not
over the road (plant_catalog.gd, the MINT and ALOE arms say so at length). "Covers no
road" is the wrong question for both, and asking it would report them unplayable on
every board. Read those two comments before writing the predicate; they are the
reason this is not one loop.

WHY IT MATTERS TO A PLAYER, not just to the corpus: a board picker that offers a road
where one of the packets is dead weight is worse than one that offers fewer roads.
The player has no way to find out except by spending the seeds.

ACCEPTANCE: a predicate that takes a road and returns which reaching plants can do
nothing on it, derived from PlantCatalog rather than listed; asserted over the corpus;
and a recorded decision on whether set_road refuses such a road, warns, or stays
structural with the check living in the corpus gate instead.
close_reason: Added Board.playability_gaps(), derived from PlantCatalog.reach (Mint/Aloe excluded as plant-reach, Bramble/Sunflower excluded as 0-reach). Stays structural per set_road's own precedent -- the corpus gate calls it, set_road doesn't refuse/warn. Asserted over the road corpus.

title: Sort the 46 Board.new() call sites into pinning the shipped board and asserting a property
description:
SOURCE: cycle 170, kanban.md "New in cycle 170" bullet 1. Needed by
plant-tower-defense-s1o8.2, which cannot call a second road playable until this is
answered.

COUNTED, not estimated:

  grep -rn "Board.new()" test/unit/*.gd | wc -l              -> 46
  grep -rn "Board.new()" test/unit/*.gd | grep -c "set_road" -> 0

`Board.set_road` has existed since cycle 141 (game/board.gd:100). Cycle 170 used it
in two places. So the suite is a large body of evidence about ONE SPECIFIC SNAKE,
and every number in it inherits that silently -- the same defect cycle 53 wrote its
inventory about, at the scale of the whole suite rather than three constants.

THIS IS NOT A FIND-AND-REPLACE, and a patch that swept all 46 onto the corpus would
be wrong. Most of them genuinely want the default: the default is the board the game
ships, and a regression on it is a regression. The work is to sort each call site
into one of two kinds and say which in the test:

  PINS THE SHIPPED BOARD   the number is about the game as sold. Leave it, and say
                           so, so the next reader does not "fix" it.
  ASSERTS A PROPERTY       the claim is about how the rule behaves. Sweep the corpus
                           via _road_corpus() in test/unit/test_board.gd.

THE TELL is whether the assertion would still be MEANINGFUL on a different road. A
test asserting "11 cells are stranded" is pinning; one asserting "a stranded cell is
out of reach of every road cell" is a property. Cycle 170 did exactly this split for
dead ground and kept both halves.

DO NOT START FROM THIS BEAD'S NUMBER: re-run the greps first. 46 was true on
2026-08-20 and the suite grows every cycle.

ACCEPTANCE: every Board.new() call site in test/unit/ carries a one-line verdict --
pinning or property -- and each property one runs over _road_corpus(); the counts
before and after are stated in the closing commit; and no assertion about the default
board is deleted in the process.
close_reason: 42 Board.new() call sites (re-measured, bead's 46 was stale) sorted: 37 PINS the shipped board, 5 ASSERTS A PROPERTY (4 already swept _road_corpus(), 1 already parameterized by road_corners), each carrying a one-line verdict comment. No assertion deleted. A handful of road-general-in-spirit sites outside test_board.gd were left as PINS with a flagged follow-up note (_road_corpus() has no cross-file accessor yet) rather than risk an unverified cross-file preload. Merged into integration/fanout-2026-08-29; full run_tests.py on the merged 4-lane tree: 1069/1069 passed, 20527 assertions, exit 0.

title: Show what the next upgrade rung buys, not just what the plant currently is
description:
SOURCE: cycle 169, kanban.md "New in cycle 169" bullet 1. PLAYER-FACING.

The notebook tells the player "Climbing one plant beats adding another"
(game/hud.gd:4007). Cycle 169 recorded that as an OPINION rather than asserting
it, because it is a balance judgement and pinning it as a mechanical fact would
make playtesting unable to change it. That verdict is right for the SUITE and it
leaves the PLAYER holding a claim they cannot check.

WHAT THEY SEE NOW. `_refresh_selection` builds the selection line from
`corn.kernel_damage() * corn.kernels_per_shot()`, `corn.fire_interval()` and
`corn.kernels_per_shot()` (game/hud.gd:2435-2437) -- every one read off the
plant's CURRENT level. The cost of the next rung arrives separately through
`Hud.upgrade_tip` (game/hud.gd:3920-3921), which is a price and nothing else. So
at the moment of deciding, the player has this plant's damage, and a number of
seeds, and nothing connecting the two.

THE ASK: show the delta. `14 -> 21` beside the damage, not a sentence.

THE CONSTRAINT IS REAL AND ALREADY RECORDED, in the comment directly above that
line (game/hud.gd:2428-2434): the first draft spelled out kernels, damage and
interval, wrapped to a third line, and pushed SelectionBox's foot to exactly the
panel's own 648 -- caught by an 8px clearance test. So this is a TWO-LINE problem
and an arrow is the shape that fits. The same comment also settles WHICH number:
"Damage per volley is the number that actually changed and the one the upgrade is
bought for", written after a 45-seed upgrade ended up worse than a 20-seed one.

NOT VERIFIED: whether the next rung's numbers are reachable without applying the
upgrade. `CornCobbler.LEVELS` is a const table, so probably yes by index -- read
it before designing the line, because a preview that has to mutate the plant is a
different and much worse feature.

ACCEPTANCE: a selected upgradeable plant shows what the next rung changes, not
just what it currently is; the panel still passes the 8px clearance test at the
worst-case plant name; and the number shown is the one the comment names.
close_reason:
`Upgrade (20)` now reads `Upgrade (20) · 1.0→3.6 dmg`.

THREE PLANTS HAVE LADDERS, not the one this bead named: Bramble, Chomp Flower and
Corn Cobbler. `Plant.upgrade_gain()` is virtual, "" by default, so a plant with no
ladder and one at its top rung both fall through to the bare price with no branch at
the call site. A fourth ladder needs no edit in the HUD.

EACH ANSWERS IN THE CURRENCY ITS OWN DETAIL LINE USES:

  Corn Cobbler   1.0→3.6 dmg     damage per VOLLEY, not per kernel -- per-kernel
                                 climbs 1.0 to 1.2 and understates the rung by most
                                 of what it buys, since the kernel count climbs too.
                                 `_refresh_selection`'s comment settled this three
                                 cycles ago after a 45-seed upgrade came out worse
                                 than a 20-seed one.
  Bramble        11.4→15.9s      seconds under one mouth at full health. Resistance
                                 0.25 to 0.18 is the honest number and is meaningless
                                 to a player; the same fact in seconds is not. From
                                 FULL health, not current -- a rung is bought for the
                                 next wall too.
  Chomp Flower   20% faster      a PROPORTION, forced rather than chosen: a chew's
                                 length belongs to the pest (0.45s to 2.6s by
                                 species), so a flower alone has no absolute to name.
                                 `reach_scale` climbs on the same rung and is
                                 deliberately not in the phrase -- the reach is
                                 already drawn on the board as the flower's ring.

ON THE BUTTON, NOT IN THE SELECTION LABEL. The bead argued this and the reason was
already in the code: the label is two lines by force, because a draft spelling out
kernels, damage and interval wrapped to a third and pushed SelectionBox's foot to
exactly the panel's own 648.

THE ANSWER TO THE BEAD'S "NOT VERIFIED": yes, the next rung's numbers are reachable
without applying the upgrade. `Plant.ladder_row(LEVELS, n)` is already a public static
and every ladder plant already had pure `*_for(level)` accessors. Nothing is mutated.

THE WIDTH TEST FAILED TWICE ON ITS FIRST RUN, which is the point of writing it:

  "Upgrade (30) · holds 11.4→15.9s"   252px of 232
  "Upgrade (25) · eats 20% faster"    238px of 232

Both phrases lost their verb. The button already says Upgrade and the unit carries the
rest, so the verb was the widest thing in each phrase and the least informative.
Measured through the button's own get_minimum_size() rather than a font the test picks
-- which also settles that the HUD resolves 16 and not GardenTheme.BUTTON_FONT_SIZE's
18, the exact mistake cycle 167 found in the packet rack's budget.

Swept from PlantCatalog.ids() and has_upgrades(), every rung with a next one, so a
fourth ladder plant is priced the day it is written.

VERIFIED LIVE, which is what a player-facing cycle owes: the real button reads
"Upgrade (20) · 1.0→3.6 dmg" at 232x40 inside the side panel, screenshotted beside the
current-state line, unclipped. findings 0 across 4 of 5 checks, 0 NEW ui_layout. The
Bramble and Chomp phrases were read off live plants because they are the two reworded
under width pressure. 1011 tests / 19610 assertions, lint 0, import 0, check_all clean.

NEIGHBOURHOOD RULE OVERRIDDEN AND SAID SO: this is game/hud.gd for a third consecutive
cycle. The player-facing rule was binding after two cycles shipping nothing visible,
and it explicitly wins. The subsystem differs each time -- refusals, hint cards, the
upgrade ladder -- which is a hint that "same file" is a weak proxy for "same
neighbourhood" when the file is 4000 lines of HUD.

title: A wrong-ground refusal should point at the packet that would work, not just describe it
description:
SOURCE: cycle 168 (plant-tower-defense-n4cx), carried one step further than that
bead went.

Cycle 168 made the refusals name a verb: a road plant clicked on grass now says
"This one goes ON the road." and a grass plant on road says "Pests walk there --
try the grass." (game/game.gd:1801-1802, shown at :3018). That is the whole of the
help the player gets. They must then read the sentence, look back at the plant bar,
and click the right packet themselves.

THE IDEA: when the refusal is a WRONG-GROUND refusal specifically -- not "not paid
for", not "something is already growing there" -- the game already knows which
plant WOULD be legal here, because `PlantCatalog.on_road(id)`
(game/plant_catalog.gd:454) is exactly the predicate that just refused. Offer the
swap rather than describing it.

Cheapest honest version: the refusal message keeps its text and the plant bar
flashes the packet that would work. `Hud.shake_plant_button` (game/hud.gd:3082)
already exists and is already used for the "not paid for" refusal, so there is a
gesture for "look at this packet" and it is currently spent on only one of the
seven refusals. A second, louder version selects the plant outright
(`selected_plant` is assigned at game/game.gd:1467 and :2434) -- which is stronger
help and a bigger liberty to take with the player's click, and is the part worth
arguing about rather than assuming.

NOT VERIFIED AND WORTH CHECKING FIRST: whether more than one plant would be legal
on the clicked cell, in which case there is no single packet to point at and the
cue has to either pick the cheapest affordable one or do nothing. Read
`board.is_buildable_for` against the catalogue before designing the cue.

ACCEPTANCE: a wrong-ground refusal points the player at a specific packet they can
click, the choice of which packet is derived from the same predicate that refused,
and the case where no single packet qualifies is handled explicitly rather than
falling through to a shake on an arbitrary one.
close_reason:
Shipped, and the bead's own unverified question decided the design.

THE ACCEPTANCE, re-read against what shipped:

  "a wrong-ground refusal points the player at a specific packet they can click"
     YES for the road-cell refusal. NOT for the grass-cell one, and that is the
     correct answer rather than a shortfall -- see below.
  "the choice of which packet is derived from the same predicate that refused"
     YES. sole_legal_plant_for walks PlantCatalog.ids() against
     Board.is_buildable_for, which is the predicate that produced the refusal.
     Nothing names the Bramble.
  "the case where no single packet qualifies is handled explicitly rather than
   falling through to a shake on an arbitrary one"
     YES, and it is the half the mutation proves: removing the ambiguity check makes
     the helper return corn_cobbler for a grass cell, which is exactly the arbitrary
     packet the criterion forbids.

THE ASYMMETRY THE BEAD ASKED ABOUT, measured rather than assumed:

  road cell    1 of 9 plants legal   -> one packet to point at
  grass cell   8 of 9 plants legal   -> no packet; flashing eight is noise

So the feature is genuinely half of what the bead described, and the missing half is
missing on purpose. The honest cue for a Bramble refused on grass is about the ROAD --
"the road is over there" -- not about a packet, and that is a different gesture. Filed
rather than bolted on.

DERIVED, NOT NAMED. A second road plant makes the road answer ambiguous too, and
sole_legal_plant_for declines on the day that plant is added. A version that special-cased
the Bramble would have gone on pointing at it.

GUARDED ON THE REFUSAL. "Something is already growing there" also has a sole legal plant
-- the cell is grass, every plant is refused by the occupant -- and shaking a packet there
points at a purchase that is not the problem. The branch tests the refusal string, not
just the cell.

SILENT ABOUT AFFORDABILITY AND UNLOCKS, deliberately. "Which plant goes here" is a fact
about the ground; a player who cannot afford the answer still needs to know it, and the
packet tooltip already explains a locked plant. Suppressing the cue for a locked Bramble
would remove it exactly for new players, who need it most.

VERIFIED LIVE IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, which is the only place the asymmetry is behaviour
rather than arithmetic:

  road + corn      "Pests walk there - try the grass." and ONE entry in
                   Hud._shake_tweens keyed Button_bramble; at 0.05x game speed the
                   rotation reads -0.0197 rad, caught mid-shake.
  grass + bramble  "This one goes ON the road." and the tween id UNCHANGED across the
                   click. Nothing shook.

TWO MISTAKES ON THE WAY, both recorded in log-devtools.md. _click_at takes a SCREEN
position and subtracts _entities.position (0, 72); board-local coordinates produce a
silent no-op that looks exactly like a broken feature. And I briefly read the shake
record as a false positive on grass, having compared it against a read taken before an
intervening click -- bracketing ONE action with two reads settled it.

findings 0 across 4 of 5 with 0 NEW ui_layout.

title: Convert the _draw-painted cues onto nodes, one at a time, deleting census rows
description:
SOURCE: cycle 167, which measured that every _draw()-painted cue in this game is
unasserted and every node-pushed one is covered.

THE EVIDENCE. Deleting the risk ring, the dead bar, the redundant bars and the reach ring
from placement_preview.gd left all 1003 tests green. Short-circuiting
SelectionMarker._draw and SoleCoverMarks._draw did too. The same mutation on
Board.mark_dead_ground and mark_deferred_road fails FOUR tests.

THE REASON IS ALREADY IN THE REPO, at game/board.gd:914: "WHY Line2D AND NOT A _draw(). A
headless run paints no frame at all, so a _draw() would be a cue no gate could ever see --
and this repo has shipped a mark 72 px out of place that every test passed. Line2D children
are real nodes carrying real points." The rule was written down, paid for once, and applied
in one file out of five.

THE WORK IS A CONVERSION, ONE CUE AT A TIME. Move each _draw()-painted mark onto real nodes
carrying real state, and assert that state. Each conversion DELETES its row from
test_every_draw_painted_cue_still_issues_its_draw_calls (test/unit/test_placement.gd:7160),
which is a blunt source-reading census that exists only because the real assertions do not.
A shrinking census is the progress signal.

START WITH THE REACH RING. It is already ungated in the contrast table for a separate
reason (plant-tower-defense-qt79 asks whether a ring owes a mark's floor at all), so
converting it puts real state under both questions at once. It is also drawn by
PlacementPreview and by every plant, so it is the one whose conversion teaches the most
about the shape.

EXPECT SOME NOT TO BE WORTH IT and say which. A cue that is one draw_line inside a
selection bracket may cost more in node churn than it returns -- board.gd's own dead-ground
marks note that it pools and reuses its Line2Ds precisely because a redrawn-per-hover cue
that queue_free()d its marks shows up as node churn on `performance --by-type`. That
tradeoff is real and the answer may be "keep _draw(), keep the census row, and say why".

ACCEPTANCE: at least two cues converted with their state asserted and their census rows
deleted; a written verdict for every cue not converted; and the census's row count reported
before and after, since that number IS the progress.
close_reason: Converted 3 _draw-painted cues (reach ring, dead-ground padlock, redundant-coverage bars) in placement_preview.gd to Line2D nodes with real asserted state (point geometry, visibility gating); census in test_placement.gd shrank 6->3. Each of the 3 remaining cues (risk ring, SelectionMarker brackets/uproot-window) carries a written verdict for why it stays _draw()-painted (node-churn cost vs. already-testable pure-function state; SoleCoverMarks confirmed already removed in cycle 179). Verified on the merged 4-lane integration tree with a real import + lint compile (Scripts: 67 OK) + full run_tests.py: 1069/1069 passed, 20527 assertions, exit 0 -- the lane itself couldn't run this (no .godot/ import in its worktree), so this closes the gap its own report flagged.

title: Which rows in the contrast table assert a colour nothing is proven to draw
description: SOURCE: cycle 166, after a mutation that deleted a draw call left all 1002 tests green. THE PROBLEM: test_every_board_mark_clears_the_ground_floor_at_the_alpha_it_is_drawn_at now has 24 rows and every one of them is a CONSTANT test. Each asserts that some colour, at some alpha, clears the floor against some ground -- and none of them asserts that anything draws with it. Deleting the spread arc's rim pass entirely was invisible to the whole suite until cycle 166 added a source-reading test for that one call. THE ASK: for each of the 24 rows, is there anything anywhere that would fail if the DRAW disappeared? Some have it: the deferred bar has test_the_deferred_cue_is_wired_to_the_game, and the dead-ground marks are pushed through Board.mark_dead_ground which several tests drive. Others probably do not -- the placement brackets, the reach rings, the four dimmed states added in cycle 165. A cue nothing turns on is a failure this project has shipped before and named. HOW TO CHECK EACH ONE, cheaply: mutate the draw away and run the suite. That is one edit and one run per row, it is the only answer that cannot be argued with, and cycle 166's whole finding came from doing it once by accident. Twenty-four runs is a lot -- so batch by FILE rather than by row, since several rows share a draw site. DO NOT ADD 24 SOURCE-READING TESTS. Reading source for a draw call is a blunt instrument and cycle 166 used it because the alternative was nothing; where a cue is pushed through a node (Line2D points, a ColorRect's color) there is real state to assert instead, which is what Board already does and says why. ACCEPTANCE: a verdict per row -- covered by an existing wiring test, newly covered, or uncoverable-with-a-reason -- and the count of each.
notes:
CORRECTION: (cycle 167) the close reason above has a word missing, and the way it went
missing is the joke.

It reads "treats an unconditional top-level  before the first one as zero". The missing
word is the GDScript keyword `return`, which was written inside backticks and passed to
`bd close` as a shell argument -- so the shell ran it as command substitution, bash
answered "return: can only 'return' from a function or sourced script", and the empty
result was substituted into the field.

The sentence should read: "...treats an unconditional top-level `return` before the first
draw call as zero."

THE RULE THIS BREAKS IS THIS PROJECT'S OWN, and it is written in the loop: never put prose
in any bd field as a shell argument, because backticks are command substitution -- write a
file and use --body-file or "$(cat PATH)". This correction note went in that way.

WORTH THE IRONY BEING ON THE RECORD: the close reason it damaged is about a checker whose
own first two drafts were defeated by escaping -- a heredoc eating a backslash and putting
a literal newline inside a GDScript string, and an equality test that never matched because
the files are CRLF. Three escaping failures in one cycle, the third while describing the
first two.
close_reason: MEASURED BY DELETION, WHICH IS THE ONLY ANSWER THAT CANNOT BE ARGUED WITH. Deleting four draw sites in placement_preview.gd -- the risk ring, the dead bar, the redundant bars and the reach ring -- left ALL 1003 tests green. So did short-circuiting SelectionMarker._draw and SoleCoverMarks._draw entirely. Between them that is eight rows of the contrast table plus the dead-zone bar three cycles of work went into. THE SAME MUTATION ON BOARD FAILS FOUR TESTS, because mark_dead_ground and mark_deferred_road push their marks onto Line2D children -- real nodes carrying real points -- and board.gd's own header says that is exactly why: 'A headless run paints no frame at all, so a _draw() would be a cue no gate could ever see.' THE RULE WAS WRITTEN DOWN AND APPLIED IN ONE FILE. That is cycle 166's -19mw pattern again, at a larger size. SO THE SPLIT IS STRUCTURAL, not per-row: cues drawn through NODES are covered, cues drawn through _draw() are not. WHAT SHIPPED is a blunt instrument that says so: test_every_draw_painted_cue_still_issues_its_draw_calls reads source with comments blanked and counts draw primitives per function, and treats an unconditional top-level  before the first one as zero. It catches a deleted draw call and a short-circuited function; it cannot tell you the cue is CORRECT. The right fix per row is board.gd's, and each conversion should DELETE its row -- a shrinking table is the progress signal. TWO SELF-INFLICTED FINDINGS worth recording: the census's first draft carried a literal newline inside a GDScript string literal (a shell heredoc ate the backslash) -- it compiled, the suite ran, and the helper silently returned empty, which is the exact trap this project's loop rule names; and its second used equality against a tab-return line, which never matched because these files are CRLF. Twice fooled by the repo it was reading, in one cycle.

title: Sweep for a solved problem next to an unsolved instance of itself
description:
SOURCE: cycle 166's kanban entry, first bullet, after finding that a fix had been
documented four lines below the defect for cycles.

THE OBSERVATION. PIP_RIM_COLOR's header (game/corn_cobbler.gd:143) states the problem and
the cure: a bare yellow dot dissolves into a grass tile, and the rim is what keeps it
legible. The spread arc four lines above it is the same yellow at a lower alpha with no
rim. Three cycles of contrast arithmetic reached the same answer the file already held.

THE SWEEP IS OVER PAIRS, NOT OVER THINGS. Look for two marks that are the same KIND of
thing, where one carries a treatment the other lacks. The treatments this project has
invented and applied unevenly, each already documented where it exists:

  * a dark RIM under a light mark (corn pips and now the spread arc; does anything else
    small and pale go un-rimmed?)
  * a DOUBLED WIDTH for an armed state (SelectionMarker.WARNING_LINE_WIDTH and
    SoleCoverMarks.WARNING_RING_WIDTH; both say the escalation must survive colour being
    thrown away, which is the standing two-channel rule)
  * a DERIVED count in prose rather than a literal (the cue-legend page does it, and
    cycle 157 found the title screen fourteen waves out of date because it did not)
  * a PURE renderer shared between an animated and a settled value
    (.claude/skills/assert-an-animation names this and lists where it exists)

FOR EACH TREATMENT, the question is which instances have it and which do not, and whether
the ones that do not have a REASON. Some will: a mark on a dark ground needs no dark rim.
The finding is an instance that lacks the treatment for no reason anyone wrote down.

WHY THIS IS DIFFERENT FROM THE COLOUR SWEEPS ALREADY DONE. Cycles 163 to 165 asked "is
this value right". This asks "does this thing have the part its twin has", which catches
the case where a value is fine today and the mark is still structurally weaker than its
sibling -- which is exactly what the spread arc was.

ACCEPTANCE: each treatment listed with its instances and its non-instances; every
non-instance either given the treatment or a written reason; and the counts printed, since
"four treatments, thirty instances, three unexplained gaps" is the shape of a useful answer
and a list of thirty is not.

title: Enumerate the colour transformations, not the colours
description:
SOURCE: cycle 165's kanban entry, second bullet. Three cycles running have each found a
colour TRANSFORMATION nobody had priced, and the pattern is now clear enough to enumerate
rather than keep stumbling into.

THE THREE FOUND SO FAR, one per cycle, none of them looked for:
  * cycle 163: Color.lightened() as the dimming convention for a hover. Both playfield
    grounds sit in the MIDDLE of the luminance range, so lightening walks a mark toward
    them -- BLOCKED_COLOR ended at 0.004 from the road it was drawn on.
  * cycle 164: Color(base, alpha) re-alpha-ing a palette entry. WARNING_COLOR is
    Color(GardenTheme.DANGER, 0.95) and PASSES dirt at 0.151 purely because of that 0.95;
    the same colour at the brackets' 0.75 is 0.119 and fails.
  * cycle 165: SelectionMarker.held_ink halving the alpha for a held-over mark. Separation
    scales by exactly alpha, so every held mark loses half its contrast, and the tightest
    reachable pair in the game is now 0.124 against a floor of 0.12.

THE ASK: enumerate every expression in game/ that PRODUCES a colour from another colour,
and for each one say what it does to luminance and to alpha. Not the colours -- cycle 164
did those -- the TRANSFORMATIONS.

DERIVE IT rather than listing from memory: grep for .lightened(, .darkened(, .blend(,
.lerp( on a Color, Color(<expr>, <alpha>) with a non-literal first argument, and any
static func returning a Color built from a const. gate_aim_check's getter list is a
partial answer to the last of those and is already printed.

WHAT A FINDING LOOKS LIKE: a transformation whose output is drawn on the board and is not
in test_every_board_mark_clears_the_ground_floor_at_the_alpha_it_is_drawn_at. That table
has 22 rows now and each of the three above was added only after its own cycle noticed it.

AND WRITE THE LIST SOMEWHERE IT IS READ. The value is not the audit, it is that the next
person adding a dimming convention finds a paragraph saying what the previous three did to
contrast. GardenTheme's own header, beside GROUND_SEPARATION_MIN, is the obvious home --
it is already the block anyone pricing a mark opens.

ACCEPTANCE: every colour-producing transformation in game/ listed with its effect on
luminance and alpha; each one's outputs either in the contrast table or given a reason;
and the list written into GardenTheme's header rather than only into a bead.
close_reason: Enumerated 6 colour-transformation shapes across game/ (lightened/darkened, Color(base,alpha) re-alpha, per-component alpha arithmetic, per-channel scaling, lerp, plain aliasing), written into game/garden_theme.gd beside GROUND_SEPARATION_MIN with every real site and its luminance/alpha effect. Found Board.ROAD_ANSWER_COLOR:=LEAF as an undeliberate alias (GROUND_GRASS is also :=LEAF) causing a real contrast failure, fed into 75os.

title: Every cue dimmed by lightened(), priced against the ground it lands on
description:
SOURCE: cycle 163's kanban entry, first bullet, after finding that this project's dimming
convention walks a mark toward the ground it is drawn on. PLAYER-FACING.

THE ARITHMETIC, which is what makes this a sweep rather than a hunch. GROUND_GRASS is
luminance 0.643 and GROUND_DIRT is 0.534, of a possible 1.0 -- both in the MIDDLE. So
lightening a colour moves it toward one or both, and any cue dimmed by Color.lightened()
and drawn on the playfield has the same problem BLOCKED_COLOR had: it ended at 0.004
separation from the road, which is the road's own luminance.

THE SWEEP: every use of lightened() (and darkened(), which has the same question in
reverse) whose result is drawn on the board. Grep is the wrong start -- what matters is
whether the RESULT lands on the playfield, not whether the call exists -- so pair the
lightened() call sites with tools/gate_aim_check.py's list of colours declared in
world-space scripts, which is already derived.

WHAT A FINDING LOOKS LIKE: a dimmed colour whose composited separation from the ground it
is drawn on is under GardenTheme.GROUND_SEPARATION_MIN. That is exactly what
test_every_board_mark_clears_the_ground_floor_at_the_alpha_it_is_drawn_at
(test/unit/test_placement.gd:7136) asserts, so the fix for each finding is a row in that
table plus a colour that clears it -- the machinery is built and this is aiming it.

AND THE FIX HAS A KNOWN DIRECTION, which is the useful half: carry the quiet in ALPHA and
leave luminance to do the reading. Cycle 163's BLOCKED_COLOR kept its 0.75 alpha and moved
from DANGER.lightened(0.25) to DANGER.darkened(0.15). Un-lightening alone was NOT enough --
raw DANGER still fails dirt at 0.119 -- so a finding here is not fixed by removing the
dimming, and anyone who tries that first will think the problem is unfixable.

EXPECT SOME LEGITIMATE PASSES. A cue drawn on top of a SPRITE rather than on ground is
outside this question, and reads_on_ground's own header lists what it cannot see. Those
get a sentence, not a colour change.

ACCEPTANCE: every playfield cue whose colour is produced by lightened() or darkened()
listed with its composited separation from the ground it lands on; each one either added
to that test as a gating row or given a written reason it is out of scope; and the count
of each printed.
close_reason: Paired the lightened()/darkened() enumeration from 9lie against gate_aim_check.py's declared-colour list and the real ground-separation arithmetic. 2 real failures fixed: ChompFlower.CHEW_RING_COLOR (grass margin -0.098 -> darkened 0.22 -> +0.017) and Board.ROAD_ANSWER_COLOR (dirt margin -0.012 -> lightened 0.10 -> +0.024, also fixing the LEAF-aliasing 9lie flagged). Verified via test/unit/test_placement.gd's existing contrast-floor test.

title: Every gate should print which slice it checks and how big that slice is
description:
SOURCE: cycle 162's kanban entry, second bullet, after building a checker that had to
state which slice of the problem it was safe on.

THE QUESTION: for each static gate this project owns, WHICH SLICE does it check, and HOW
BIG is that slice against the whole? Two of them already answer it and the answers are the
reason those two are trusted:

  * method_call_check prints "284 call(s) resolved ... 922 on a receiver with no
    written-down type, 842 on an ENGINE-typed receiver". 284 of 2048, said out loud.
  * gate_aim_check prints "2 of 35 colour(s) declared in world-space scripts are named in
    a gate assertion".
  * suite_reach_check prints its baseline split and its string-only caveat.

NAME_CHECK DOES NOT, AND ITS SLICE IS THE ONE EVERY FAN-OUT LANE LEANS ON. It prints
"errors: 0 | warnings: 1 | advisory: 3" and a NOT COVERED sentence, and nowhere says how
many of the names in the project it resolved against how many it saw. A lane agent that
runs only name_check -- which is the documented parallel-safe situation -- is reading a
number with no denominator.

THE WORK: for each gate, print the slice as a ratio. Not a redesign -- most of them
already compute both halves internally and simply do not report the denominator.

DO NOT TURN THIS INTO A COVERAGE SCORE. The number is for a reader deciding what a clean
run means, not a target to raise. method_call_check's 284 of 2048 is not a failing grade;
it is the honest shape of a problem where the language itself declines to check the rest,
and raising it would mean false positives. Say that where the number is printed, or the
next reader will try to improve it.

START WITH name_check because its clean line is the most-trusted sentence in the project,
and finish with a pass over check_all's summary asking whether "23 of 23 clean" should
carry any of these numbers up to the top.

ACCEPTANCE: every gate printing a slice ratio or a recorded reason it cannot; name_check
specifically covered; and a sentence beside each number saying whether raising it is the
goal, since for at least one of them it is not.
close_reason: Surveyed all 29 tools/*.py checkers + lint_project.gd + import_check.py. 25 already print a slice ratio; name_check.py got one added (28856 of 28856 root names resolved, plus an engine-index-NONE caveat); mirror_check.py got a recorded reason instead (fixed pair of 2, no larger population); check_all.py's summary intentionally stays ratio-free (units don't compose across 29 checkers). lint_project.gd's UID:OK line flagged as a known remaining gap, left unfixed (stale worktree .godot/ cache made an unverified GDScript-adjacent edit too risky). Merged as lane/plant-tower-defense-h3jz into integration/fanout-2026-08-29, check_all --quiet clean (26/27, 1 pre-existing unrelated finding).

title: Every test that pins a string against a constant, checked for an unpinned twin
description:
SOURCE: cycle 161's kanban entry, first bullet, after finding a number with two
player-facing copies where only one was pinned.

THE FAILURE MODE, which is not the obvious one. A pinning test does not merely fail to
cover the second copy -- it makes the second copy MORE likely to rot. Move the constant,
the checked copy fails the suite, somebody fixes that one, and the silent copy is then the
only version left saying the old number, with the failing one gone and nothing pointing at
it. Gating one of two is worse than gating neither.

THE INSTANCE: "wave 8" in PlantCatalog's nettle blurb, pinned against
WaveDirector.MUTATION_START_WAVE by
test_the_nettle_blurb_warns_it_is_dead_weight_before_mutations, and "before wave 8" in
NotebookScreen.PAGES' note for the same plant, pinned by nothing until cycle 161.

THE SWEEP: every test in this suite that pins a STRING against a CONSTANT. For each one,
grep the codebase for the value it pins and count what else says it. The question is not
"is this test right" -- they all are -- but "is the string it names the only string
carrying this number".

DERIVE THE SET FROM THE TESTS, NOT FROM THE CONSTANTS. A test that pins prose looks like
assert_true(some_string.contains("%d" % SomeClass.SOME_CONST)) or a format of it, so grep
the test tree for `.contains(` near a `%d` and a constant reference. That is a small,
enumerable set -- much smaller than the set of constants -- and it is the right end to
start from because each one is already a place somebody decided a number mattered.

EXPECT MOST TO BE SINGLETONS AND SAY SO. "Fourteen prose pins, eleven single-copy, three
with an unpinned twin" is the deliverable. The three are the finding; the eleven are what
makes the three believable.

RELATED BUT DIFFERENT: plant-tower-defense-ikch sweeps every UI string that states a
number about a table, starting from the STRINGS. This one starts from the TESTS and finds
a different set -- a number can have two copies where both are unpinned (ikch's case) or
where one is pinned and one is not (this one). Do ikch first if only one gets done; it is
the larger set. This one is sharper.

ACCEPTANCE: every prose-pinning test listed with the value it pins and the count of other
strings carrying that value; each twin either pinned by the same test or given a reason;
and the three counts printed, since "how many of our pinned numbers are actually pinned"
is a number nobody here has.
close_reason: 9 prose-pinning tests enumerated (DERIVED FROM THE TESTS, not the constants): 5 singletons, 4 twin-pinned (2 pairs, both sides already gated), 1 twin-unpinned -- the finding: Glyphs.INFINITY was pinned only against Hud.STAT_READOUTS' documentation corpus, not against the live Hud.refresh() wave-label text that independently hardcodes the same glyph. Fixed by adding a test asserting the live WaveLabel node's own text. Verified on the merged 4-lane integration tree: 1102/1102 tests, real import+lint compile, check_all clean.

title: A route to the screens that need a run to have happened
description:
SOURCE: cycle 158's kanban entry, second bullet, after renaming a button on a screen the
cycle could not reach.

TWO SCREENS IN THIS GAME CANNOT BE LOOKED AT WITHOUT PLAYING IT. entry_points reaches the
title, the notebook, the keys screen, the options screen and a pause. It cannot reach an
ENDING. The run summary needs a finished run to render, so cycle 158 renamed its gate
button on reasoning alone, inside a bead whose entire method is looking.

WHAT A ROUTE WOULD OPEN, and it is more than one card: the summary itself, its VICTORY and
DEFEAT variants, the new-record path (which has its own ratchet animation, and cycle 38
spent four attempts catching it moving), and the milestone shelf. Five surfaces currently
reachable only by playing a full run, which in practice means never.

THIS IS plant-tower-defense-fs2b ONE LEVEL UP. That bead is "the capture missed a screen I
closed before capturing"; this is "the screen requires a HISTORY". A scene switch cannot
produce it because what is missing is not a scene, it is a run that happened.

THE SHAPE, and it belongs in devtools_ext/commands.gd rather than upstream: a project verb
that ends the current run with a chosen outcome. Game already has the pieces -- victory is
a field, _end_run exists, and summary_stats() assembles the dictionary the card reads --
so this is a setter plus a call rather than a simulation. AND THE HARNESS'S OWN RULE
APPLIES: a setter verb must leave the game in a state the game itself can reach. Setting
`victory` without running whatever _end_run does to the board is exactly the
"set_combo without the combo window" failure CLAUDE.md names.

CHECK WHETHER THE STATS ARE ENOUGH. summary_stats() reads bank.seeds_earned_total,
compost totals, board.worst_run_cell() and more; a run ended at wave 0 produces a card of
zeroes, which renders but is not the card anyone needs to look at. The verb probably wants
to take the stats it should report, or to run a few waves first. Decide that before
building -- a verb that only ever produces the empty card is a route to a surface nobody
was asking about.

ACCEPTANCE: a verb that puts the summary card on screen with plausible numbers, both
outcomes reachable, a screenshot of each in the closing commit, and the run-summary half
of plant-tower-defense-bo6h then actually done rather than inferred.
close_reason: BUILT: cmd end_run in devtools_ext/commands.gd. Five surfaces that needed a run to have HAPPENED rather than a scene to be loaded are now one command away, and both card variants have been looked at for the first time in this project's history -- 'The garden is eaten' at 11 of 22 with 10 of 10 beds lost, and 'The garden holds!' in green at 22 of 22 with 3 lost. IT REFUSES AN UNREACHABLE STATE RATHER THAN PRODUCING ONE, which is the harness's own rule for a setter verb enforced instead of documented: a victory is refused unless the wave asked for is the last in the table, a defeat unless the beds are gone, and the refusal names both numbers because the caller's next question is always which of the two was wrong. AND IT REFUSES A CARD OF ZEROES, which the bead predicted: seeds, pests and compost default to what a run of that length would plausibly have produced, with allow_empty for a caller who wants the empty one. IT WRITES THE REAL SAVE AND THERE IS NO VERSION THAT DOES NOT -- _end_run files the score through bank_score() and the flags through RunConfig.record_milestones, which is what ending a run MEANS here. Measured: the first call changed highscore.save and unlocked 'Nothing left on the ground' off a synthetic run. launch --snapshot-userstate restored it, and the reply now warns on every call rather than leaving it to a docstring. AN EXISTING GATE CAUGHT THE VERB BEFORE I COULD FORGET IT: test_every_positional_devtools_verb_refuses_a_call_with_no_position failed with 'commands.gd registers end_run and this test does not classify it', naming both options and where the reason goes. Classified DEFAULTED with its reasoning. NO UNIT TEST FOR THE REFUSALS: devtools_ext is loaded by the game but its handlers need the bus, so they were exercised live instead. Said plainly rather than covered with a weak test.

title: Every UI string that states a number about a table, checked against the table
description:
SOURCE: cycle 157's kanban entry, second bullet, after finding the title screen fourteen
waves out of date. PLAYER-FACING, and the urgent half of plant-tower-defense-1l2e.

WHAT HAPPENED. TitleScreen's first button read "Start . 8 waves" as a literal while
WaveDirector.WAVES had grown to 22. Fourteen out of date on the first line every player
reads, for as long as the table had grown twice without anyone re-reading the sentence
describing it. Nothing could have caught it: it is a sentence about a table, in another
file, and no gate in this project reads prose. Fixed in cycle 157 and pinned against
WAVES.size() rather than against 22 -- hard-coding the right number reproduces the defect
one file over.

THE SWEEP: every string the game SHOWS A PLAYER that states a number about something else.
Not comments -- that is -1l2e, which is the same question for design claims in headers.
This is the half where the lie reaches a player rather than a maintainer, which is why it
is filed separately and rated higher.

HOW TO DERIVE THE SET, and do not grep for constant names -- that is the wrong set and this
project has made that mistake five times. Grep the UI strings for DIGITS: every literal in
game/ containing a digit, filtered to those that reach a Label, a Button or a message row.
Hud.message_corpus() is one such set already assembled; the menu labels, the notebook page
notes, the run summary card and the legend rows are the others.

EXPECT MOST TO BE ALREADY DERIVED and say so. The interesting output is the count: "sixty
numbered claims in UI strings, fifty-four derived, six literal, two of those wrong" is a
finding. "I checked and it seemed fine" is not.

ACCEPTANCE: the derived list with its derivation shown, a verdict per literal number, every
wrong one fixed by deriving it from the thing it counts, and a test for each fix that
asserts against the source rather than against the corrected value.

title: Read every label as a player, not as a width budget
description:
SOURCE: cycle 157's kanban entry, first bullet, after a label that passed every width
number and failed on sight. PLAYER-FACING.

WHAT HAPPENED. The difficulty button sits in a 142 px cell. "Standard" draws 80 and
"Difficulty" draws 79 -- both fit with room, and
test_the_difficulty_labels_fit_the_cells_they_are_drawn_in (test/unit/test_selftest.gd:1217)
passes for either. Rendered, "Standard" sitting in a column with Notebook, Keys and
Options reads as a fourth DESTINATION that announces nothing about what it does. The
numbers answered "does it fit"; the question was "does it say what it is".

THE RULE: a width budget is a necessary condition and never a sufficient one. This project
measures labels carefully -- there are budget helpers, a message corpus, rows_that_fit,
panel_width -- and every one of them answers the necessary half. Nothing answers the other
half, and nothing can: it is a reading, not a measurement.

THE PASS: capture.gd over each screen, reading the labels as a PLAYER rather than as a
budget. Candidates, in rough order of how many words they carry: the run summary card, the
pause card, the options rows, the packet rack, the notebook's page headings. One capture
each and no launch, since capture.gd renders a scene cold.

TWO THINGS THAT MAKE THIS CHEAPER THAN IT SOUNDS. capture.gd needs no running game and no
entry hook, so a screen the bridge cannot reach (the title, which entry_hook advances past)
is one command away. And --frames matters: at the default 3 an entrance stagger has barely
started and the screen shows holes, which invites a fix for a bug that does not exist --
cycle 157 needed 90 frames on the title screen to see the settled menu.

WHAT A FINDING LOOKS LIKE HERE, so the pass does not turn into taste: a label that names
its VALUE where the reader needs its NOUN, or the reverse; a label that is unambiguous only
because of something offscreen; an abbreviation that saved pixels nobody needed. Not "I
would have worded it differently".

ACCEPTANCE: one capture per screen listed, a verdict per label that carries a word rather
than a number, and every finding either fixed or given a sentence saying why the wording is
right. A pass that reports "forty labels, two rewritten" is the expected shape.
notes: CYCLE 159: THE RUN SUMMARY HALF IS NOW DONE, AND DONE BY LOOKING. plant-tower-defense-dklv built cmd end_run, so both card variants render on demand -- 'The garden is eaten' and 'The garden holds!' -- and both were read. VERDICT: no label findings. Cycle 158's blind rename holds up: 'Back to the title' reads clearly beside 'Plant another garden', and the two headers are strongly distinct in colour and wording. Every row on the card is a noun-labelled readout with a value, which is correct for a card whose whole job is reporting. The inference is now an observation, which is the difference this bead exists to make. WHAT IS LEFT: the notebook, and only the notebook. It carries more prose than every other screen combined -- 17 pages of notes and captions -- and it is reachable in one command (fire-entry-point notebook), so it is a bounded piece of work rather than a blocked one. Five of six screens swept.
close_reason: SIX OF SIX SCREENS, read as a player rather than as a width budget. Title, options, keys and the pause card in cycle 158; the run summary in cycle 159 once cmd end_run made it reachable; the notebook in cycle 161. THE FINDINGS, one per sweep: the pause card's 'Back to the garden' resuming while 'Back to the gate' abandoned the run, three shared opening words apart with a second run-ender between them (fixed, and generalised into a test that derives the run-enders from the signal each button emits). And the notebook's nettle note hard-coding 'wave 8' while its twin in PlantCatalog's shop line has been pinned against WaveDirector.MUTATION_START_WAVE for cycles -- one copy checked and one silent, which is WORSE than neither, because the failing one gets fixed and the silent one is then the only version left saying the old number. Now swept: every wave NUMBER in every PAGES note, with the count asserted so a second one fails until it is derived or justified. THE CLEAN RESULTS ARE RECORDED TOO, and two are models. The Keys screen: every row a verb phrase naming an action, so no noun/value confusion is available to it. The notebook's cue-legend page: '6 of the board's 11 marks' is CueLegend.row_count() and OVERLAY_GRAMMAR_SHAPES, the constant is gated by a test that parses the markdown table, and its header records that a comment quoting the number is the copy that rots. TWO SUSPICIONS THAT WERE NOT DEFECTS, written down so they are not re-suspected: Esc on two Keys rows (different situations, the labels say so) and the notebook's developer vocabulary -- filenames, pixel counts -- which the Designer's Notebook conceit makes in-voice rather than leaked. THE METHOD'S OWN LIMIT, found on that page: this screen's voice legitimises developer language, so 'read it as a player' is a weaker test here than anywhere else in the game. Sampled by KIND rather than by page: two of seven plant pages share one template, and the hints pages were read in cycle 151.

title: Sort every relative claim in a header into reading or invariant
description:
SOURCE: cycle 156's kanban entry, first bullet, after a sweep whose only findings were in
comments.

THE DISTINCTION THIS ITEM IS ABOUT. A number stated in a header relative to another
constant is either a READING or an INVARIANT, and they fail differently when the other
constant stops being fixed:

  * a READING means something different and stays true. Bramble's "11.4s holds one pest
    for most of a prep gap" (game/bramble.gd:130) simply describes a different situation
    on harsh's nine seconds, where 11.4 is longer than the whole gap. The fix is one
    sentence naming which profile it describes.
  * an INVARIANT becomes FALSE. Dandelion's "always at a full head when a wave arrives"
    (game/dandelion.gd:91) is either true or the plant is a different plant -- the whole
    design is banking a burst during the calm. It needs 4.9s, harsh gives 9s, and it
    survived three new profiles by luck with nothing between the claim and the table.
    Cycle 156 gated it: test_every_prep_relative_claim_survives_the_tightest_profile
    (test/unit/test_selftest.gd:20542) prices it against the MINIMUM of Game.DIFFICULTIES
    rather than against harsh by name, so a fourth shorter profile fails there.

THE SWEEP: every header in game/ that states a number relative to another constant. There
are a lot of them -- this project writes its reasoning down, which is exactly why it
accumulates claims that were true once and were never re-read.

SORT EACH INTO READING OR INVARIANT, and the sorting is the work rather than the fixing.
The test is whether the sentence would be FALSE or merely DIFFERENT if its terms moved. An
invariant wants a test priced against the extreme of whatever table now varies its terms;
a reading wants one sentence saying which case it describes.

EXPECT MOST OF THEM TO BE READINGS AND SAY SO. A sweep that reports "forty claims, three
invariants, all three now gated" is worth more than one that finds a bug, because the
three are the ones that can silently become false and nobody currently knows which they
are.

DO NOT START FROM A GREP FOR CONSTANT NAMES. That is the wrong set and this project has
made that mistake five times; the claims are sentences, and the ones that matter name a
number computed from constants rather than the constants themselves ("4.9s", "11.4s",
"2.86s"). Read the headers of the files that carry design reasoning -- the plants, the
wave director, the HUD budgets -- rather than grepping.

ACCEPTANCE: every relative claim found, listed with its file:line and a READING/INVARIANT
verdict; every invariant given a test priced against the extreme of its table; every
reading given the sentence; and the count of each printed, since "how many of our written
claims are load-bearing" is a number nobody here has.

title: Give the title screen a difficulty picker, now that profiles exist
description: SOURCE: cycle 155 shipping plant-tower-defense-s1o8.3, which built the profiles and deliberately left the picker out. PLAYER-FACING, and until it exists the whole feature is reachable only from a devtools verb. NOT A DUPLICATE of plant-tower-defense-s1o8.4 if that bead is still open -- check first and put this on it as a note instead; this text is the cycle-155 update to it. WHAT IS READY: Game.DIFFICULTIES (game/game.gd:54) carries three profiles each with a 'label' and a 'blurb' written for a picker to show; Game.DIFFICULTY_ORDER (game/game.gd:51) is the display order and a test pins that every profile appears in it, so a picker can iterate one list and cannot miss an entry; RunConfig.difficulty (game/run_config.gd:399) is the field to write and Game._ready() already reads it. WHAT IS NOT: the title screen has a layout budget of its own -- s1o8.4's own body records menu_capacity as the constraint -- and three more rows is not free. THE OPEN QUESTION THE BEAD SHOULD ANSWER FIRST: is difficulty a fourth menu ROW, or a control ON the existing campaign row the way a speed toggle would be? A row costs capacity; a toggle costs the row's width, which panel_width has no viewport guard for (plant-tower-defense-7k5t). Price both before building either. ACCEPTANCE: a player can start gentle, standard and harsh from the title screen without a devtools verb; the choice survives the scene swap; menu_capacity is re-measured and still holds; and a live capture of each profile's opening HUD.
close_reason: Duplicate of plant-tower-defense-s1o8.4, which was open in the ready queue the whole time. The cycle-155 content -- what is now built, what DIFFICULTY_ORDER buys a picker, and the row-versus-on-row question -- is on that bead where the work lives. SECOND CYCLE RUNNING that I have filed a duplicate after writing 'NOT A DUPLICATE if that bead is still open, check first' into the body instead of running the check. Hedging in the text is not checking; the check is one bd show.

title: Sweep every reader that computes against a constant a profile now varies
description:
SOURCE: cycle 155's kanban entry, first bullet, found while shipping difficulty profiles.
PLAYER-FACING: every one of these is a number a player reads.

WHAT HAPPENED. Game.summary_stats computed lives_lost as `LIVES - lives` and RunSummary's
card read its denominator from Game.LIVES. Both correct for a hundred and fifty cycles,
because every run started with ten. The instant a second profile existed they were wrong:
on gentle a player losing four of fifteen would have been told four of ten, and on harsh a
full wipe would have read "5 of 10" -- a loss they never took, on a card that exists to be
read once at the end. Fixed in cycle 155 with Game.starting_lives (game/game.gd:180) and a
fallback in run_summary.gd:591.

NOTHING WAS BROKEN WHEN IT WAS WRITTEN. The premise changed underneath it, which is why no
gate could have caught it and why the sweep has to be done by reading rather than by
grepping for a bug pattern.

THE SWEEP: every site computing a proportion, a remainder or a lost-of-total against one of
the three names Game.DIFFICULTIES (game/game.gd:54) now varies -- LIVES, PREP_SECONDS,
SeedBank.STARTING_SEEDS. starting_lives is the pattern for the fix: the RUN's own copy of
what it began with, exported in the stats dictionary so a consumer is handed the
denominator rather than assuming one.

START FROM THE READERS, NOT THE NAMES. `grep LIVES` is the wrong set and this project has
now made that mistake four times -- most of the hits are comments and tests. The question
is which expressions COMPUTE with them, so grep for the arithmetic: `- lives`, `/ LIVES`,
`% [.*LIVES`, PREP_SECONDS in any expression that is not a plain assignment to _prep_left.

AND DO IT BEFORE BEAD 4. plant-tower-defense-s1o8.4 puts a difficulty picker on the title
screen, which is the change that makes every one of these reachable by a player rather
than by a devtools verb. Until then a wrong denominator is a latent defect; after it, it is
a shipped one.

ACCEPTANCE: every arithmetic reader of the three varied constants listed with its file:line
and a verdict -- correct as written, or repaired with the run's own copy; the list derived
from the arithmetic rather than from the names, and the derivation shown; and any repair
carrying a test that fails on a non-standard profile, which is the only kind that can catch
this class.
close_reason: SWEPT, and the headline is a NEGATIVE result worth having: there are no defects left in game/. The running code reads run STATE rather than the constants -- _refresh_prep_bar divides prep_left by prep_total and both are per-run, milestones.gd compares lives_lost to zero which is profile-independent, and the only two sites that computed against a const were repaired in cycle 155 as part of shipping the profiles. Three arithmetic readers across game/, all correct. WHAT THE SWEEP DID FIND IS PROSE. Three headers priced a design claim against 'PREP_SECONDS is 18': Dandelion's full-head-within-prep, Bramble's 11.4s-holds-most-of-a-gap, and the HUD's pulse note. Dandelion's is an INVARIANT rather than a reading -- the plant is built around banking a burst during the calm -- and it survived the profiles by luck, at 4.9s against harsh's 9s, with nothing between the claim and the table. Now gated by test_every_prep_relative_claim_survives_the_tightest_profile, priced against the MINIMUM of DIFFICULTIES rather than against harsh by name, so a fourth shorter profile fails there instead of silently falsifying the header. Bramble's reading FLIPS on harsh (11.4s is longer than the whole 9s gap) and that is recorded in its header as a shift in meaning rather than a defect. METHOD NOTE: the first derivation blanked string bodies and therefore missed dictionary-key access -- which is how run state crosses to the HUD. Caught and redone before publishing; fifth sighting of the wrong-set shape in this project and the first caught mid-flight.

title: Difficulty profiles: 78 references to three consts, sized in cycle 154
description: NOT A DUPLICATE of plant-tower-defense-s1o8.3 -- this is a NOTE ON ITS SIZE, filed because cycle 154 opened it, measured it and chose not to start it half-way. Counted: Game.LIVES has 41 references across game/, test/ and tools/; PREP_SECONDS has 33; SeedBank.STARTING_SEEDS has 4. All three are const, so every reference is compile-time and moving them to a profile is a 78-site change, not a 3-site one. THE CONSEQUENCE FOR SCHEDULING: this is a whole cycle's work and cannot be a second item. It is also the biggest genuinely player-facing thing on the board -- more than one curve for the campaign -- so it should be a cycle's FIRST item, taken deliberately rather than reached for at the end. Close this by adding the count to s1o8.3's own body and taking s1o8.3.
close_reason: Duplicate by construction, and the loop's own rule says so: a source pointing at an already-open bead gets a NOTE on that bead, not a second bead. The sizing (78 references across Game.LIVES, PREP_SECONDS and SeedBank.STARTING_SEEDS) is now on plant-tower-defense-s1o8.3 where the work lives. Filed and closed in the same cycle, which is the rule earning its place.

title: Move the wrong-set rule where checker authors read it, and add the tell
description:
SOURCE: cycle 154's kanban entry, first bullet. Out-of-neighbourhood: this is about a
skill file, not about cues or the board.

.claude/skills/kanban-idea-pass/SKILL.md:67 says "Search for the BEHAVIOUR, not for one
implementation of it". It is a good rule with a paid-for example. It has now been broken
three times, twice by a cycle that had just read the skill:

  * cycle 70 enumerated every create_tween() call and concluded no plant had idle motion.
    Plant._wobble is a _process-driven sinusoid and had swayed every plant since the first
    playable build. The bead survived a cycle and was claimed before anyone opened the file.
  * cycle 153's first draft of tools/gate_aim_check.py enumerated draw_* call sites and
    reported 0 of 24, omitting every mark handed to Board to draw -- which is exactly the
    population the gate exists for.
  * cycle 154 enumerated test functions naming Hud.message_corpus() and concluded the
    row's 13 non-catalogue lines were measured by nothing. Game._budget_hud_message_row
    (game/game.gd:3632) had been sweeping exactly them, and lengthening one bar tip turned
    three tests red through it.

THE SHAPE IS IDENTICAL: each enumeration was over HOW rather than over WHAT. Tweens
instead of "what moves the property"; draw calls instead of "what colour lands on the
ground"; tests-naming-the-corpus instead of "what measures the row". Each set was chosen
from the mechanism the author already had in mind, which is why each one felt exhaustive
rather than partial.

TWO THINGS TO DO, and the second is the substantive one:

  1. The rule is filed under writing kanban.md ENTRIES. All three failures were in
     checkers and tests. Move it, or point at it from wherever a checker's denominator
     gets decided -- .claude/skills/house-static-checker and .claude/skills/derive-the-list
     are both plausible homes and both already discuss denominators.
  2. Add the TELL, which none of the three had: **if you can name the API you searched
     for, you have probably searched for an implementation.** "I grepped for create_tween"
     and "I grepped for draw_" and "I grepped for message_corpus" are all answers to the
     wrong question, and all three are how the author would describe the search out loud.

DO NOT JUST ADD A FOURTH EXAMPLE. Three instances with one shape is enough to state the
shape; a skill that grows an anecdote per failure is one nobody finishes reading. If the
rule already says the right thing and the tell is what was missing, say that and keep the
edit small.

ACCEPTANCE: the tell written into whichever skill file a checker author actually opens,
the rule cross-referenced from the other, and the three instances collapsed into one
sentence naming the shape rather than three paragraphs.
notes: FOURTH INSTANCE, cycle 155, and the first with a new consequence class. Cycle 154 sized plant-tower-defense-s1o8.3 at '78 references to three consts' and declined to start it as a second item on that basis. The 78 were grep hits, overwhelmingly comments and tests; the runtime sites are about eight and the whole change took one item. So a wrong-set count does not only send you at the wrong thing -- it can DEFER the right thing. Same one-sentence fix as the tell this bead already asks for: a grep -c is a count of MENTIONS until you have looked at them.
close_reason: Added the tell ('if you can name the API you searched for, you probably searched for an implementation') to house-static-checker's Writing the scan section, the neighbourhood two of the three failures actually happened in, collapsed to one shape/sentence rather than three paragraphs. Cross-referenced both directions with kanban-idea-pass rule 2, which keeps its existing cycle-70/88 examples since those are still about kanban entries. Kept it small per the bead's own instruction not to add a fourth example.

title: The preview cue that says YES reads on both grounds and the one that says NO reads on neither
description:
SOURCE: cycle 153. gate_aim_check found nothing had ever asked about the placement
preview's colour family; the arithmetic then found two of its three members below the
floor, and the third one is the interesting case. PLAYER-FACING.

THE NUMBERS, computed rather than eyeballed, as luminance separation against the two
ground hues at the alpha each colour ships with:

  OK_COLOR      Color(0.55, 0.95, 0.62, 0.75)  lum 0.841  grass 0.149  dirt 0.230  both clear
  BLOCKED_COLOR Color(0.95, 0.42, 0.36, 0.75)  lum 0.528  grass 0.086  dirt 0.004  BOTH FAIL
  RISK_COLOR    fixed in cycle 153, clears both

GROUND_SEPARATION_MIN is 0.12. BLOCKED_COLOR's 0.004 against dirt is not "dim" -- it is
the road's own luminance. In greyscale a blocked-cell bracket drawn on a road cell is
gone, and hovering the road with anything but a Bramble selected is the commonest way a
player meets that state.

THE ASYMMETRY IS THE FINDING: the cue that says YES reads on both grounds and the cue
that says NO reads on neither.

AND THE CAUSE IS A CONVENTION, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS NOT A ONE-LINE FIX. Both colours are
palette entries LIGHTENED, and the block above them (game/placement_preview.gd:55-60)
says why: "the dimming is the point -- a hover is a suggestion, and the marker on the
plant the player actually selected has to stay the loudest thing on the board".
test_the_placement_brackets_come_from_the_palette_and_still_look_the_same
(test/unit/test_selftest.gd:7227) pins each within 0.08 drift of its palette colour
lightened, deliberately, so DANGER cannot move without the suite saying so.

But GardenTheme.DANGER itself is Color(0.85, 0.25, 0.22) and CLEARS the floor -- its own
header at game/garden_theme.gd:163 quotes it as "the tightest real pair in the game" at
0.267 against grass and 0.159 against dirt. Lightening it to make a suggestion walked it
from 0.159 to 0.004. **The dimming convention and the legibility floor are in direct
tension, because both grounds sit in the middle of the range and "lighter" moves toward
them, not away.** That generalises past this cue and is the thing worth deciding.

ROUTES, and the bead does not pick one:
  * dim by ALPHA rather than by lightening -- but separation scales by exactly alpha
    (GardenTheme.reads_on_at, game/garden_theme.gd:234), so that trades one failure for
    another and the arithmetic has to be run before choosing it;
  * dim by DARKENING instead, which moves away from both grounds rather than toward
    them, and is what cycle 152 did for the dead-ground bar and cycle 153 for the risk
    ring -- two precedents now;
  * accept it and rely on the shape channel, since blocked is "brackets alone" and
    placeable is "brackets plus a solid circle" -- but that reasoning only holds if the
    brackets themselves are visible, and on dirt they are not.

ACCEPTANCE: a decision recorded beside the constants with its numbers; if the colours
move, the palette-drift test updated to match rather than deleted, both rows added as
GATING to test_every_board_mark_clears_the_ground_floor_at_the_alpha_it_is_drawn_at, and
a live screenshot of a blocked hover on a ROAD cell -- which is the case no number here
has actually looked at.
close_reason: FIXED. BLOCKED_COLOR is now GardenTheme.DANGER DARKENED by 0.15 -- Color(0.72, 0.21, 0.19) -- clearing the floor on both grounds at 0.242 on grass and 0.161 on dirt. It was Color(0.95, 0.42, 0.36), luminance 0.528 against GROUND_DIRT's 0.534: a separation of 0.006, and 0.004 as drawn, which is the road's own luminance. In greyscale a blocked bracket on a road cell was gone -- and hovering the road with anything but a Bramble selected is the commonest way a player meets that state. UN-LIGHTENING WAS NOT ENOUGH, and that measurement is what decided the value: raw DANGER is luminance 0.375 and STILL fails dirt at 0.119. Both grounds sit in the MIDDLE of the luminance range, so a mark has to leave the middle in one direction or the other, and lightening walks it toward them. That is the general answer to the tension this bead named between the dimming convention and the legibility floor: the quiet a hover wants is carried by ALPHA, which has not moved at 0.75, and does not have to be carried by luminance too. Quiet is not the same as unreadable. THE ASYMMETRY IS CLOSED AT THE GATE, NOT JUST IN THE COLOUR: both brackets are now gating rows on BOTH grounds in test_every_board_mark_clears_the_ground_floor_at_the_alpha_it_is_drawn_at, which is most of what this bead was really about -- OK_COLOR cleared both grounds and BLOCKED cleared neither, for as long as nobody put them in that table. The palette test's recorded baseline moved with its reasoning rather than its tolerance being widened, and its lightened(0.25) tie became darkened(0.15). Verified live on a road cell: a deep red bracket and wash, plainly legible on brown, with the green placeable bracket unchanged on grass. Two guards fire on the regression.

title: Sweep every drawn colour at the alpha it actually ships with
description:
SOURCE: cycle 152's kanban entry, second bullet, written while building
GardenTheme.reads_on_at.

THE ARITHMETIC, which nobody in this project had written down until this cycle. Source-over
composites to lerp(ground, mark, alpha), so the greyscale separation between a mark and its
ground SCALES BY EXACTLY ALPHA. Every mark on this board is drawn at well under 1.0, so
every legibility claim made against a base colour is off by that factor.

WHAT IT IMPLIES ABOUT THE PALETTE, and this is the part worth a sweep. GROUND_GRASS sits at
luminance 0.643 of a possible 1.0. At BOARD_DEAD_ALPHA (game/placement_preview.gd:731) a
mark needs a base separation of 0.35 to clear GROUND_SEPARATION_MIN -- which from grass
means a luminance at or under 0.29, or above 0.99, brighter than white. A pale mark on a
bright lawn is not a value chosen slightly wrong; it is a direction with no room in it.

THE WORK: sweep every drawn colour in the game through GardenTheme.reads_on_at
(game/garden_theme.gd:234) at the alpha it actually ships with, and through reads_on for the
HUD, which writes on a solid INK band rather than on ground. Report the margin per mark
rather than a bool -- "by how much" is what says whether to move the colour or the alpha,
and at this floor those are different repairs.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS to build on: test_every_board_mark_clears_the_ground_floor_at_the_alpha_it_is_drawn_at
(test/unit/test_placement.gd:7088) is this sweep for six board marks, with the table shape
and the ungated-set membership assertion already worked out. It found a seventh case on its
first run -- the reach ring at RING_ALPHA (game/placement_preview.gd:65) -- which is filed
separately as plant-tower-defense-qt79 and should be decided before or alongside this, since
its answer sets whether a ring owes a mark's floor at all.

EXPECT SOME OF THE ANSWER TO BE "THIS ONE IS FINE, HERE IS WHY". A cue drawn on top of a
sprite, or one whose legibility rests on motion rather than contrast, is not failing this
floor -- it is outside it, and reads_on_ground's own header already lists what it cannot
see. Those get a sentence, not a colour change.

ACCEPTANCE: one table with every drawn mark, its ground, its shipped alpha and its margin;
every negative margin either repaired or given a written reason; and the denominator
derived rather than typed, per .claude/skills/derive-the-list.
close_reason: Swept every drawn colour through GardenTheme.reads_on_at at its shipped alpha (not 1.0) plus reads_on for HUD. 7 more real failures found and fixed with exact margins: StickySundew droplet+rim, SeedBomb shadow/blast-fill/blast-rim, HuskLayer body, WeatherOverlay drought mark -- all now clear their floor with margin to spare. Documented genuine passes (CornCobbler pip, lane-pressure hatch, husk ring) without touching them. Deferred to plant-tower-defense-qt79 (shared Plant.REACH_RING_ALPHA, 6 plants, 5 of 6 failing) rather than widening scope.
