Flagged for the parent, not fixed (outside file ownership): Game._update_cursor draws Color(LEAF,0.30) on grass -- 0.0 separation at ANY alpha since LEAF IS GROUND_GRASS, the worst number in the whole sweep. Test table grew 21->39 checked marks. Combined with 9lie/75os, verified on the merged 4-lane integration tree: 1115/1115 tests, real import+lint compile, check_all clean.

title: Count what each gate is actually pointed at, not just which classes are covered
description:
SOURCE: cycle 152's kanban entry, first bullet, written after fixing a cue that failed a
gate this project has owned for many cycles.

THE CASE THAT PROMPTED IT. GardenTheme.reads_on_ground (game/garden_theme.gd:188) exists
because a mark once vanished into the lawn. Two board cues are the same grammar row. The
deferred bar has had test_the_deferred_bar_reads_on_the_road_it_is_drawn_on
(test/unit/test_placement.gd:7048) since the day it shipped. The dead-ground bar had
nothing, and sat at 0.086 separation against a floor of 0.12 (game/garden_theme.gd:163) at
FULL opacity, on the only ground it is ever drawn on. The gate was right, installed, and
aimed at one of the two things it was for.

THE GENERAL SHAPE: a checker's coverage is the set of call sites somebody remembered to
write, and NOTHING IN THIS PROJECT COUNTS THAT SET. coverage_check.py answers a different
question -- which defect CLASSES the project asks about at all -- and would have reported
this class covered, correctly, while the specific cue went unasked.

THE ASK, per gate rather than per class: enumerate what the gate COULD speak about, then
what actually asks it, and print the ratio. For the reads_on family the answer is now known
to have been 3 of 5 before this cycle, which is the kind of number that changes what you do
next.

START WITH THE reads_on FAMILY because it is small and the answer is already half known,
then contained-in, then the budget helpers. Every one of them is a static function with a
countable set of things it could be pointed at: every drawn Color for reads_on, every
Control inside a panel for contained-in.

THE HARD HALF, and it is what makes this a real item rather than a grep: DERIVING THE
DENOMINATOR. "Every drawn colour" is not a list anyone maintains -- it is every const Color
plus every Color(...) built at a draw site, and a sweep that misses half of them prints a
flattering ratio, which is worse than no ratio. Read .claude/skills/derive-the-list before
starting; a hand-maintained list of what a gate should cover is the exact thing that let
this cue go unchecked.

ACCEPTANCE: a ratio per gate over a DERIVED denominator, the derivation printed so a reader
can see what it swept, and each uncovered site either given its assertion or given a
one-line reason it does not need one. Advisory exit 0 -- this is a coverage report, not a
gate, and the house-static-checker skill's rule about permanently-red gates applies.
close_reason: Built tools/gate_aim_check.py; check_all 20 -> 21. THE ANSWER IS 2 OF 35 colours declared in world-space scripts are named in any reads_on assertion -- DEAD_COLOR (added last cycle) and deferred_road_color (tested since it shipped), and nothing else. Advisory exit 0, because most of the 33 are probably outside reads_on_ground's stated scope and a gate red for those would be permanently red. The first draft said 0 of 24 and was measuring its own regex: the numerator was call-scoped (tests bind to a local before passing) and the denominator was draw-call-scoped (which omits every mark handed to Board to draw, i.e. exactly the marks the gate exists for). Both corrections are recorded in the file. Fixture written, run and deleted; three mutations kept in the docstring, one of which took three attempts to kill and whose two survivors are a finding about decl_re's caret anchor. Deliberately supports ONE gate family: contained-in and the budget helpers have no denominator derivable from source, and are absent rather than half-covered.

title: The game now names a mark that may be too faint to find
description:
SOURCE: cycle 151, from the live screenshot taken to verify the tip that names this cue.
PLAYER-FACING.

Cycle 151 gave the dead-ground bar a sentence -- "Slanted bars mark grass this plant would
never fire from" (Hud.dead_ground_tip, game/hud.gd:3867). The screenshot taken to verify it
shows the bars, and they are FAINT: pale diagonal strokes on the green, at 1152x648, easy to
read as texture rather than as a mark. The tip is now the game telling a player to look for
something that may be below the threshold of being findable.

THAT IS A NEW PROBLEM, not an old one. Before the tip, an unnoticed cue cost nothing. Now
there is a sentence promising a mark, and a player who reads it and finds nothing learns
that the game's messages are unreliable -- which is worse than an unnamed cue.

CONFIRM BEFORE CHANGING ANYTHING, because "faint" is one reading of one screenshot:

  * PlacementPreview owns the stroke -- DEAD_COLOR, DEAD_BAR_WIDTH, DEAD_BAR_ANGLE, and
    dead_bar_arm(). Read the alpha and the width, and read them against the deferred bar's
    (DEFERRED_BAR_WIDTH, deferred_road_color) which is the SAME grammar row and reads
    strongly in the same shot.
  * The board's mark and the hover bar are ONE stroke by design -- see
    test_the_board_mark_and_the_hover_bar_are_one_stroke_not_two and the block above
    Board.DEAD_GROUND_LAYER, which says the geometry is pushed in from PlacementPreview
    precisely so the two cannot diverge. Changing this changes both, and the hover bar may
    be at the right strength already for its job.
  * The bars sit on GRASS and the deferred bars on ROAD. Contrast against the ground is the
    variable, not absolute alpha. Compare each against its own background.

AND THE ANSWER MAY BE THE TIP, NOT THE CUE. If the mark is deliberately quiet because it is
ambient with nothing hovered, the fix could be that hovering makes it brighter -- the cue
raising its voice at the moment it acquires a subject, which is the same reasoning the
hint's own gate uses (game/game.gd:1427).

ACCEPTANCE: the alpha and width read and compared against the deferred bar's, a decision
recorded beside whichever constant it is about, and if the cue changes, a screenshot of both
bars on one board showing they still read as the same grammar and not as two.
close_reason:
FIXED, and the suspicion was an understatement. "Too faint to find" turned out to be
"fails the project's own legibility floor at FULL opacity, on the only ground it is
ever drawn on".

MEASURED. PlacementPreview.DEAD_COLOR was Color(0.70, 0.73, 0.80), luminance 0.729
against GROUND_GRASS's 0.643 -- separation 0.086 against GardenTheme's
GROUND_SEPARATION_MIN of 0.12. Composited at BOARD_DEAD_ALPHA it was 0.029, a quarter
of the floor. Board.mark_dead_ground drops non-buildable cells, so grass is the only
ground this mark lands on.

TWO FAILURES THAT COMPOUND, and neither is a taste call:

  * NOBODY POINTED THE GATE AT IT. GardenTheme.reads_on_ground exists because a mark
    vanished into this lawn once, and the deferred bar -- the OTHER half of grammar
    row 6 -- has had test_the_deferred_bar_reads_on_the_road_it_is_drawn_on since the
    day it shipped. This cue had no such test. Meanwhile DEAD_COLOR's own header
    claimed "in greyscale the bar is still the only thing on screen crossing the
    cell", which is a claim about SHAPE sitting directly above a colour that fails the
    greyscale test.
  * THE GATE WAS ALPHA-BLIND AND SAID SO. Its header lists opacity among what it does
    not check. That is the dominant term for every board mark: source-over composites
    to lerp(ground, mark, alpha), so separation scales by EXACTLY alpha.

THE FIX IS DARK, AND THAT IS ARITHMETIC RATHER THAN PREFERENCE. Grass sits at
luminance 0.643 of a possible 1.0. To clear the floor at a third of an alpha from the
PALE side needs a luminance above 1.0. Pale on this lawn is not a value chosen
slightly wrong; it is a direction with no room in it. DEAD_COLOR is now
Color(0.24, 0.27, 0.36) and BOARD_DEAD_ALPHA 0.40 -- the alpha bump is margin, since
0.34 clears by six thousandths and 0.40 by a quarter.

BUILT: GardenTheme.reads_on_at(mark, alpha, ground) and composite_over(), plus
test_every_board_mark_clears_the_ground_floor_at_the_alpha_it_is_drawn_at, a six-row
sweep naming each mark's ground rather than asking about both -- each mark's placement
rule already fixes which ground it can land on.

THE GATE FOUND A SECOND MARK ON ITS FIRST RUN: the dead/redundant reach ring at
RING_ALPHA is 0.112 on grass. Left UNGATED with its number printed, and filed as
plant-tower-defense-qt79 rather than waived, because a ring may not owe a floor
calibrated against hairlines and RING_ALPHA is shared with every non-dead reach ring
in the game. The test pins the ungated set by MEMBERSHIP so a future failing mark
cannot quietly join it.

VERIFIED LIVE, which is the half no number answers -- whether a dark slate reads as a
mark or as a shadow. It reads as a mark, and the cropped hover preview shows the
hovered cell's bar visibly darker than the ambient ones around it, so the two-tier
relationship DEAD_COLOR's header argues for is now actually visible instead of merely
intended. The ring is faint in the same shot, which is why -qt79 is a question.

Gates: 992 tests / 0 failed / 19071 assertions, lint 0/0, check_all 20 of 20. Two
mutations killed on the right assertions.

title: The message row's non-catalogue lines are counted by one test and measured by neither
description:
SOURCE: cycle 151, step 4 -- the question "what would have told me this headlessly?"
after verifying a new message-row line live.

TWO SWEEPS, ONE CORPUS, DIFFERENT SETS.
test_the_message_corpus_covers_every_catalogue_producer (test/unit/test_selftest.gd:11276)
keeps Hud.message_corpus() (game/hud.gd:3676) whole and its header calls the corpus "the
budget's denominator". The budget test is
test_no_message_clips_for_any_plant_in_the_catalogue (test/unit/test_selftest.gd:11365) and
IT NEVER READS THE CORPUS -- it builds its own sweep from PlantCatalog.PLANTS crossed with
the level tables, measures through GardenTheme.measure (game/garden_theme.gd:377), and
compares the worst against label.size.x (:11371, asserted at :11407).

ENUMERATED, not sampled: eight test functions across the suite call message_corpus(), and a
function-scoped scan finds not one of them measuring a width. So the corpus's 13
non-catalogue entries -- both bar tips among them, the two longest plant-name-free lines in
the game -- are counted by one test and measured by neither.

MEASURE THIS FIRST, BECAUSE IT MAY BE THE BIGGER FINDING: what label.size.x actually is
under _T.instantiate_scene. Cycle 144's commit 14c1cb9 says the headless budget "measures
label.size.x under a 64x64 window". If that is so, the EXISTING budget test is passing
against a number unrelated to the shipped 876px row, and adding entries to a sweep with a
wrong budget is worse than not adding them. Print it before writing an assertion.

WHY THIS CANNOT BE ANSWERED BY READING: the row is clip_text with text_overrun_behavior 3,
which CLAUDE.md names as the pair that makes get_minimum_size() report the clip stub rather
than the text. GardenTheme.measure is the route the existing test takes and is the right one.

ACCEPTANCE: one number printed for the headless row width with a sentence saying whether it
is the real one; then either the corpus folded into the existing sweep as its denominator
(so a new tip is priced the day it is written) or a recorded reason not to. Either way the
two tests stop being able to disagree about what "the budget" covers.
close_reason: FALSIFIED, by me, two cycles after I filed it. The 13 non-catalogue entries ARE measured: Game._budget_hud_message_row (game/game.gd:3632) sweeps Hud.message_corpus() through GardenTheme.measure and adds both mute lines at their current keybinds, which no static corpus can do. Lengthening one bar tip past the row turned three tests red through it. My enumeration -- 'eight test functions call message_corpus() and not one measures a width' -- was literally true and over the wrong set: the measurer is in game/, not test/. AND THE ROW IS 876 px HEADLESS, probed rather than argued, exactly what node-bounds reports live; the get_window().size caveat does not touch a Control laid out under a properly-sized root, so cycle 151 launched the game to measure a tip this test could have priced. Kept the tidy-up: the width test now sweeps the corpus instead of rebuilding the catalogue cross, which is a strict superset and removes a second denominator. That cost Hud.upgrade_message its only direct mention and suite_reach_check said so within the minute; bought back with a better assertion, that the corpus still carries the CORN's top rung -- the property the sweep now depends on.

title: The dead-ground bar is named by nothing, and it is the half of row 6 cycle 144 missed
description:
SOURCE: closing plant-tower-defense-xfbo in cycle 151. PLAYER-FACING, and it is the
half of grammar row 6 that cycle 144 did not get to.

THE CUE. Board._dead_ground_marks (game/board.gd:935) draws a diagonal bar at
PlacementPreview.DEAD_BAR_ANGLE on every buildable cell a plant could never fire
from. It is pushed by Game._refresh_dead_ground (game/game.gd:1381) out of
PlacementPreview.board_dead_cells (game/placement_preview.gd:826), which falls back
to the LONGEST REACH AMONG UNLOCKED PLANTS when no shop entry is hovered
(game/placement_preview.gd:795) -- so the bars stand on the board with nothing
selected and nothing hovered, from _refresh() (game/game.gd:1523).

IT IS NAMED BY NOTHING. RunConfig.HINTS (game/run_config.gd:259) holds six ids and
none is about it; grep finds no dead_ground in run_config.gd or hud.gd. CueLegend.ROWS
has six rows and it is not among them, and it must not become a seventh -- cycle 148
decided that at game/cue_legend.gd:194 and the row-6 verdict at :112 says why a single
legend line teaches this WORST.

THE ROUTE IS ALREADY BUILT ONE BAR OVER. plant-tower-defense-0xhf (cycle 144, commit
14c1cb9) taught the DEFERRED-ROAD bar the same way: a hint id
(RunConfig.HINT_DEFERRED_ROAD, game/run_config.gd:243), a card in HINT_CARDS so
test_every_hint_has_a_notebook_card passes, and two derived gates -- a minimum plant
count so the cue says something about THIS garden rather than about having one gun,
and Hud.row_is_quiet() before offering, because the caller is level-triggered and a
refused post is re-offered by the next _refresh(). Read that commit before starting;
its message records both traps.

DECIDE, and this is the real work: WHEN. The deferred bar waited for
Game.DEFER_HINT_MIN_GUNS = 2 for a reason its commit spells out. Dead ground needs its
own answer, and the fallback above is why it is not the same one: with nothing hovered
the bars describe the unlocked catalogue, not a choice the player made, so firing at
first sight teaches "some grass is far from the road" rather than anything actionable.
A stronger trigger is likely the first time the player HOVERS a shop entry and the set
changes under them -- that is the moment the bar is about a decision they are making.

AND SAY WHAT IT MEANS, NOT WHAT IT IS. "This ground is out of reach" is the shape; the
sentence has to survive a 876px row without ellipsis, which the headless budget cannot
measure (it runs a 64x64 window) -- 0xhf verified that live and so must this.

ACCEPTANCE: a seventh hint id with a notebook card, a trigger with its gate reasoned in
the commit rather than tuned, a headless test that drives the trigger and asserts it
fires once and only under the gate, and one live screenshot showing the sentence whole
with dead-ground bars on the board.
close_reason: Shipped. The hover is the gate -- these bars are ambient from the opening frame because board_dead_cells falls back to the garden's unlocks, so no count threshold can make them informative; a hovered packet is what makes them about a decision. Seventh hint id, third hints page (the alarm cue_legend.gd:206 promised fired on three tests at once), corpus non-catalogue count 12 to 13, two tests killed by two mutations. Verified live because clip_text plus text_overrun_behavior 3 make the width unanswerable headless: 876px row, sentence ends near 640px, no ellipsis, bars on the board in the shot.

title: Find the unbounded test loop before it hangs a run instead of failing it
description:
SOURCE: cycle 150's reader-mutation sweep, which hit four of these before it
could report anything (plant-tower-defense-4uts). All four are fixed in 1a3ac67;
this is about stopping the fifth.

THE DEFECT CLASS: a `while` in test/ whose termination depends on the CODE UNDER
TEST making progress.

    while corn.upgrade():                         test_combat.gd
    while not cob.is_max_level():                 test_selftest.gd
    while err == "" and not corn.is_max_level():  test_placement.gd
    while err == "" and chomp.can_upgrade():      test_combat.gd

Mutating `level += 1` out of Plant.upgrade() -- a one-line defect a refactor could
plausibly introduce -- made all four spin forever. The runner is SIGTERMed and
reports NOTHING: no exit code worth reading, no failing test named, an empty log
if stdout was buffered. That is strictly worse than a failing test, and during a
mutation sweep it is indistinguishable from a mutation that never applied.

THE CONVENTION ALREADY EXISTS and is well-followed elsewhere -- `guard < 4000`,
`waited < 30`, `pumped < 20`, `again < 120` appear throughout the suite. Two of
the four offenders even KEPT a counter (`upgrades`, `climbed`) and simply left it
out of the loop condition. That is the tell: a loop that is already counting has
admitted it can run long.

THE ASK: a stdlib-only checker per .claude/skills/house-static-checker/SKILL.md
that finds an unbounded `while` in test_dir. The shape is findable without
parsing GDScript properly:
  * find `while ...:` lines in test/unit/*.gd;
  * a condition is BOUNDED if it contains a comparison against a local counter
    (`< N`, `<= N`) -- that is the convention, and matching it is a regex;
  * anything else is a candidate, and the finding names the loop.

MEASURE FIRST, which that skill's first rule requires and which cycle 89
correctly used to NOT build a tool. Count: how many `while` loops exist in
test_dir (roughly 51 by `grep -c` across the files), how many are already bounded
by the convention, and how many are left. If the answer after this cycle's four
fixes is ZERO, the honest deliverable is a kanban entry recording the class and
its four instances, not a checker -- and that is a success.

EXPECT FALSE POSITIVES and decide the waiver form before building: `while true:`
with an inner `break` is legitimate and common, and a loop over a container
(`while i + 1 < segments.size()`) is bounded by data rather than by a counter.
The house waiver idiom is `# <tool>: ok - <reason>` on the loop's own line.

DO NOT try to prove termination. The check is "is there a bound", not "does it
terminate" -- the second is undecidable and the first is the whole value.

ACCEPTANCE: either a checker with the usual exit contract, a printed denominator
naming how many loops it classified of how many it found, a NOT COVERED line and
a fixture -- or a written measurement saying the count does not justify one.
close_reason: Measured 55 while loops in test/unit/*.gd: 33 already bounded, 22 candidates, 4 of them real recurring bugs (one already carrying a comment noting it had spun forever twice before) -- fixed with the suite's existing guard-counter idiom. Built tools/loop_bound_check.py (house-static-checker contract, waiver form, --fixture proving 7 synthetic cases classify correctly, 4-mutation sweep on the classifier itself all caught). Denominator: 55 found, 37 bounded, 18 legitimately waived, 0 findings. Verified on the merged 4-lane integration tree: 1112/1112 tests, real import+lint compile, check_all clean.

title: Everything _gait composes past the animations gate is unobservable to the suite
description:
SOURCE: cycle 150's reader-mutation sweep (plant-tower-defense-4uts). It is the
one finding that survived the audit, and it is the same hole cycle 149 hit from
the other direction.

THE HOLE, stated once. Pest._gait early-returns on
GardenTheme.animations_enabled(), which is FALSE in every headless test by
construction. So everything _gait composes past that gate is unobservable to the
suite:

    gait_swing / gait_rate / gait_stretch / gait_yaw / flinch_amount
    _flinch_force / chewed_scale

Every one of those is a pure function with good tests. NOTHING can assert that
_gait actually calls any of them. Measured, not assumed: replacing
gait_swing(is_armoured, is_winged) with 0.0 at the call site, and gait_stretch(..)
with 0.0, each SURVIVED the full suite with zero failures. Cycle 149 found the
same thing when pinning _flinch_force = 1.0 survived two freshly-written tests.

Plant._wobble has it identically -- sway, breathe, flinch, wilt and
idle_scale_multiplier all compose past the same gate.

WHY THE OBVIOUS FIX IS NOT ENOUGH. "Add a test that calls _gait" does not work:
the gate returns before anything is written. Flipping the gate in a test is worse
-- GardenTheme.animations_enabled() reads DisplayServer.get_name(), so faking it
means faking the display server for the whole suite.

THE SHAPE THAT WORKS is the one cycle 139 already used for flash_hit and cycle
141 for the champ: MOVE THE COMPOSITION ABOVE THE GATE, or extract it whole.
Concretely, _gait becomes

    compute -> (a pure function returning yaw and stretch)
    if gated: return
    apply

so the composer is callable headlessly and the ungated remainder is two
assignments. The mutation surface shrinks from "the whole body" to "does _gait
assign what the composer returned", which is still ungated but is a far thinner
thing to be blind to -- and cycle 149's flash_hit is the proof this works: its
recoil is assertable ONLY because the arming sits above the gate, a decision made
three cycles before the test that needed it.

DO NOT DO THIS FOR BOTH IN ONE GO. _gait and _wobble are the two busiest
per-frame functions in the game and both have headers arguing their current
structure at length. Take _gait first, confirm the two surviving mutations go
RED, and only then decide whether _wobble is worth the same.

CONFIRM BEFORE STARTING that the survivors are still survivors -- the sweep
harness is at
C:/Users/gotmi/AppData/Local/Temp/.../scratchpad/mut1.py in this session and will
not persist; rewriting it is ten lines and the method is in this bead's parent.
One mutation per foreground run: batched sweeps were killed twice in this
environment, mid-mutation, leaving a game file modified.

ACCEPTANCE: the two mutations that survived in cycle 150 go RED, and the test
that kills them names what it read. A written "the composition still cannot be
reached and here is why the extraction does not work either" is also a complete
answer -- but it has to be argued against an attempt, not predicted.
close_reason: Confirmed both cycle-150 survivors by hand before touching code: gait_swing()->0.0 and gait_stretch()->0.0 each still survived the full 1112-test suite. Extracted _gait's composition into a new pure static Pest.gait_compute(gait_time, phase, for_speed, armoured, winged, hungry, flinch_left, flinch_force) -> {yaw, stretch}, called unconditionally before the animations_enabled() gate; the gated remainder shrank to two assignments. New test calls gait_compute() directly (no scene, no gate) across 3 seeds x 8 armoured/winged/hungry combinations against a hand-built reference composition. Both original mutations re-applied to the new composer: both now go RED (full suite: 1112 passed / 1 failed, exit 1, same test both times). Plant._wobble deliberately untouched per the bead's explicit scope. Verified on the merged 4-lane integration tree: 1114/1114 tests, real import+lint compile, check_all clean.

title: Audit the checks written against constants for whether anything tests the reader
description:
SOURCE: cycle 149's kanban entry, third bullet, written straight after a
mutation exposed it in tests I had just written.

WHAT HAPPENED. Cycle 149 fixed a defect, wrote two tests, and mutated the fix
away to check them. Both passed. The tests were:
  * a CONSTANT test -- is GLANCE_FLINCH_SCALE between 0 and 1, and does it still
    out-read GAIT_SWING;
  * a CALL-SITE test -- which files pass the glancing flag.
Neither mentions `flash_hit`, the function that reads the constant and dispatches
on the flag. So pinning `_flinch_force = 1.0` -- restoring the exact defect --
was invisible to both.

THE TELL, and it is worth stating as a rule: IF NO ASSERTION IN THE TEST NAMES
THE FUNCTION UNDER TEST, THE TEST IS ABOUT ITS INPUTS. That is often fine, but it
is never sufficient on its own.

THE ASK: audit the checks in this repo that are written against constants or
tables for the same gap. Candidates, from memory and NOT confirmed -- confirming
is the work:
  * the gait tables. test_combat asserts gait_rate / gait_swing / gait_stretch as
    pure functions over the trait matrix. Does anything assert that Pest._gait
    actually calls them? Cycle 139 added gait_yaw partly for this reason, so this
    one may already be covered -- check before assuming.
  * the upgrade ladders. Cycle-147 tests sweep every LEVELS table for shape. Does
    anything assert that upgrade() reads the row it is standing on?
  * Hud.message_corpus. message_corpus_check asserts every producer is priced;
    does anything assert the ROW actually renders what the producer returns? The
    sole-cover and lapsed-move tests do for two of them, which suggests the
    others do not.
  * Board.road_cell_count / road_length_px -- cycle 142 deliberately paired the
    arithmetic against the walker, so this is the WORKED EXAMPLE of doing it
    right and is the control for the audit.

METHOD: for each, mutate the reader (not the table) and see whether anything
dies. .claude/skills/house-static-checker's mutation section is the procedure,
including the two traps -- an exit 2 proves nothing, and an equivalent mutant is
a finding about the code rather than the test.

EXPECT SOME TO BE FINE. Several of these were written with the seam in mind and
the audit's value is knowing WHICH, not finding failures everywhere. A written
"all four are covered, here is the assertion that covers each" is a complete
result.

ACCEPTANCE: each candidate has a recorded verdict -- covered by a named
assertion, or not covered and a test added. The closing commit produces the
mutations run and the verdicts.
close_reason:
AUDIT DONE. Six mutations of READERS, one per foreground run, full suite each
time. Verdicts:

  RED       road CONTROL (walker skips a cell)      37 failing
  SURVIVED  _gait ignores gait_swing                 0
  SURVIVED  _gait ignores gait_stretch               0
  RED       upgrade_cost ignores the level           2 failing
  RED       upgrade() does not advance the level    10 failing
  RED       message row renders the idle line always 18 failing

THE CONTROL FIRED FIRST AND CORRECTLY, which is what makes the rest readable:
cycle 142 deliberately paired Board.road_cell_count's arithmetic against the
walker, and the first kill is exactly that test -- "the walker and the arithmetic
disagree, which means one of them is wrong". Method sound.

FOUR OF FIVE REAL CANDIDATES ARE COVERED. The ladders are covered twice over
(the cost accessor and the level advance are separately killed), and the message
row is covered by 18 tests. Those three were the bead's main suspicions and all
three were wrong -- the coverage is there.

THE TWO SURVIVORS ARE THE SAME SURVIVOR, and it is a finding about REACHABILITY
rather than about the tests. Pest._gait early-returns on
GardenTheme.animations_enabled(), which is false in every headless test by
construction, so EVERYTHING _gait composes past that gate is unobservable to the
suite -- gait_swing, gait_stretch, gait_yaw, _flinch_force, chewed_scale. The
pure functions are all asserted; nothing can assert that _gait calls them. That
is the same hole cycle 149 hit from the other side when a _flinch_force mutation
survived, and Plant._wobble has it identically. Filed separately.

WHAT THE SWEEP FOUND THAT IT WAS NOT LOOKING FOR, and it is worth more than the
audit: FOUR TEST LOOPS THAT CAN HANG THE SUITE, each keyed on a condition the
code under test owns. Mutating `level += 1` away made all four spin forever and
the runner was SIGTERMed with no output -- twice, before I stopped assuming it
was slow. A hang is worse than a failure: it names nothing and, during a
mutation sweep, is indistinguishable from a mutation that never applied. Fixed
in 1a3ac67; the suite already had the `guard < N` convention and two of the four
even kept a counter without putting it in the condition.

METHOD NOTE for whoever runs the next sweep: batch runs of six mutations were
killed twice in this environment, both times mid-mutation with a game file left
modified -- a state that reads exactly like a finding. One mutation per
foreground call, restore verified before the next, is the shape that survives.

title: Sweep every two-channel cue for halves that describe the same event differently
description:
SOURCE: cycle 149's kanban entry, first bullet, found by fixing one instance of
it. PLAYER-FACING in its consequence.

THE CLASS. A cue built from two channels can CONTRADICT itself, and nothing in
this project looks for that. Cycle 149's instance: a plate-blocked hit flashed at
Pest.SHELL_FLASH_DIM 0.45 against HIT_FLASH_BOOST 1.9 -- a 4.2x split
deliberately meaning "that did nothing" -- while the recoil said "that hit hard"
in the same frame, because the recoil had no branch at all. Both halves were
written on purpose, two cycles apart, and each was correct alone.

THE RULE THAT WAS MISSING. This project's standing rule is that COLOUR IS NEVER
THE ONLY SIGNAL, and it is cited in half a dozen headers. The corollary nobody
wrote down: a second signal must AGREE with the first. Adding a channel to
satisfy the first rule is exactly how you get an instance of this one, because
the new channel is written by someone reading the rule and not the other
channel's branches.

THE SWEEP: every cue that speaks on more than one channel, asking whether both
halves read the same event the same way. Leads, unconfirmed -- confirm each
against the code rather than trusting this list:
  * the husk: a rot ARC plus PIPS for value above CompostMeter.FULL_VALUE. Do
    the pips and the arc ever describe different husks, or the same husk
    differently?
  * the selection brackets: SelectionMarker's colour plus its DOUBLED WIDTH when
    armed. The doubling is the "armed" grammar row; is there any state where the
    colour says armed and the width does not, or the reverse?
  * the weather: drawn marks on the board plus a HUD banner. The banner is
    announced once; the marks persist. A wave whose weather changes mid-flight
    would have them disagree if anything can do that.
  * the plant health bar plus the new wilt (cycle 147): both read
    health/MAX_HEALTH, so these should agree by construction -- which makes it
    the useful CONTROL for the sweep. If the method finds a disagreement here,
    the method is wrong.

WHAT A FINDING LOOKS LIKE: two channels whose branch conditions are not the same
expression. That is mechanically checkable in the small -- the two Pest flash
peaks branch on `blocked` and the recoil branched on nothing -- but it is not
worth a checker until the sweep says how many instances there are. Read first.

ACCEPTANCE: each multi-channel cue listed with the condition each channel
branches on, and a verdict per cue: agree by construction / agree by care /
disagree. A "disagree" is a bug and gets its own bead; "agree by care" is the
interesting middle and is worth a test. The closing commit can produce all of it
-- this is reading, not running.

title: Compute how long each banded cue is actually visible, under attack and in recovery
description:
SOURCE: cycle 147's kanban entry, first bullet, found by computing the wilt cue's
own visibility rather than by playing. PLAYER-FACING, and it is a measurement
before it is a change.

THE OBSERVATION. A cue tied to a health band has TWO durations and they can
differ by an order of magnitude:
  * how long the band is CROSSED while under attack, and
  * how long it is OCCUPIED during recovery.

The wilt shipped in cycle 147 is the worked example. Its band is
Pest.EAT_DPS / Plant.MAX_HEALTH wide -- exactly one second of chewing -- so an
uninterrupted meal shows the lean for ONE SECOND and then the plant is gone. But
a plant whose attacker is killed mid-meal sits in the band while regrowth climbs
out: REGROWTH_DELAY 6.0 then REGROWTH_RATE 1.5/s is roughly TWELVE seconds. The
cue is twelve times more present in the case nobody designed it for.

Nothing in this repo computes either number for any banded cue, and there are
several:
  * the health bar's own colour, Hud.health_color_on -- a continuous lerp, so
    every fraction is a "band" of zero width and the question is instead how long
    any DISTINGUISHABLE hue lasts.
  * the Chomp's chew ring (chomp_flower.gd's _draw_chew_ring), whose duration is
    chew_seconds per species -- so the ring's visibility is a SPECIES fact and
    the beetle's and the aphid's differ by the ratio their chew times differ by.
  * the Dandelion's regrow window (Dandelion.REGROW_DELAY plus
    FLUFF_REGROW_SECONDS per fluff).

THE ASK: compute both durations for each banded cue and write them down. That is
all -- this is a measurement bead, not a change bead. The deliverable is a table
in kanban.md giving, per cue, the attack-crossing time and the recovery-occupancy
time, derived from the constants rather than timed by hand.

WHAT IT IS FOR. A cue whose crossing time is under a second is not a warning, it
is a receipt -- the player reads it after the outcome is decided. That may be
fine (the wilt's recovery window is where it earns its place) or it may mean the
cue is aimed at the wrong moment. You cannot tell which without the number, and
the number is arithmetic over constants this repo already has.

DO NOT retune anything as part of this. A measurement bead that also changes
balance cannot say which of the two produced the result, and every one of these
constants has an argued header that would have to be re-argued.

ACCEPTANCE: a kanban table with both durations per banded cue, each derived and
citing the constants it comes from, plus one sentence per cue saying whether the
cue is aimed at a moment the player can act in. The closing commit produces all
of it -- arithmetic, no running game.

title: Nothing checks a notebook hint card against the game it describes
description:
SOURCE: cycle 145, found when a stale card surfaced by accident. PLAYER-FACING in
its consequence: these are the sentences a confused player deliberately goes to
read.

WHAT HAPPENED. Hud.HINT_CARDS' seen_move_tip card said "With Uproot armed, hover
another bed to see what the plant would reach there. Confirming still only
uproots." The second sentence stopped being true in cycle 143, when clicking a
destination started moving the plant. It sat wrong for two cycles and was found
only because cycle 145 reworded the matching one-shot tip and
test_the_hint_cards_agree_with_the_tips_the_message_row_posts noticed the two had
diverged FROM EACH OTHER.

THE HOLE. That test checks a card against its TIP. Nothing checks a card against
the GAME. And the cards are not copy -- every one of them makes a factual claim
about a mechanic:

  seen_move_tip     "Confirming still only uproots"  (was FALSE for two cycles)
  seen_flight_tip   "A winged pest passes a Chomp Flower untouched. Corn
                     Cobblers can still hit it."
  seen_upgrade_tip  "Click a plant on the board to select it, then Upgrade.
                     Climbing one plant beats adding another."
  seen_road_tip     "Every other plant is refused on the road ... The Barrier
                     Bramble is the exception: it only goes on road cells, and
                     everything walking one stops to chew through it."
  seen_defer_tip    "Every plant that reaches that cell shoots at the pest
                     furthest along its range first ... It clears when one more
                     plant covers that stretch -- depth, not reach."
  seen_sole_cover_tip "rings mark the road cells no other plant of yours reaches"

Each is exactly the kind of absence-or-behaviour claim
.claude/skills/kanban-idea-pass/SKILL.md exists for, and nobody applies that
standard to them because they read as prose rather than as assertions. A wrong
one is worse than a wrong kanban entry: kanban is read by whoever works the item,
a card is read by a PLAYER who is already confused and went looking for help.

THE WORK, in order:
  1. Read all six against the code that implements each claim. "Corn Cobblers
     can still hit it" is a question about whether CornCobbler targets winged
     pests; "Climbing one plant beats adding another" is a balance claim and may
     simply be an opinion, in which case say so rather than rewording it.
  2. For each claim that is MECHANICALLY checkable, write the assertion. The
     upgrade-vs-breadth one probably is not, and "cannot be asserted" is a fine
     answer recorded per card rather than a silent omission.
  3. Where a card's claim is already asserted somewhere in the suite, NAME that
     test in the card's own comment -- so the next person changing the mechanic
     finds the card through the test.

DO NOT try to derive the card text from the game. It is prose written for a
player and the whole value is that it is written rather than generated; the ask
is a CHECK on the claims, not a generator.

WATCH THE SELF-REFERENCE TRAP: this bead quotes six card strings. If a checker
ever greps prose for card text it will find them here. Quoting is deliberate
(the point is what they claim) and the checker should read Hud.HINT_CARDS, not
prose.

ACCEPTANCE: every card in Hud.HINT_CARDS has either an assertion somewhere in
test_dir that its factual claim still holds, or a one-line note in the table
saying why the claim is not mechanically checkable. The closing commit produces
both -- no running game needed, since these are claims about code.
close_reason:
Every card in Hud.HINT_CARDS now has a recorded verdict, in
test_every_hint_card_claim_still_holds rather than in this field, so a reworded
card has to come back and change a row.

THE BEAD LISTED SIX CARDS. THERE ARE SEVEN. `seen_dead_ground_tip` arrived between
filing and working this, which is precisely why the verdict table is swept against
HINT_CARDS rather than typed beside it -- the sweep caught the bead's own
enumeration on its first run.

PER CARD:

  seen_move_tip        3 claims. "A quarter of what you have put into it" asserted
                       here (Plant.MOVE_RATE == 0.25, plus MIN_MOVE_COST > 0 so a
                       cheap plant's quarter never rounds to free and makes the
                       sentence a lie). "Keeps its level" already asserted by
                       test_a_move_always_costs_something_and_always_beats_uprooting,
                       which checks the SAME instance lands. Hover preview by
                       test_an_armed_uproot_turns_the_hover_into_a_move_preview.

  seen_flight_tip      2 claims. The Chomp exemption asserted here by reading the
                       guard -- there is no predicate to call, and going through a
                       live grab would assert the grab rather than the exemption.
                       "Corn Cobblers can still hit it" already asserted by
                       test_a_winged_pest_only_outruns_the_map_in_a_garden_with_no_corn_in_it.

  seen_upgrade_tip     1 claim, recorded as OPINION with its reason. "Climbing one
                       plant beats adding another" is a balance judgement. Pinning
                       it as a mechanical fact would make playtesting unable to
                       change it. The test asserts the opinion COUNT is one, so a
                       second appearing without a cycle noticing is caught.

  seen_road_tip        2 claims, both asserted here. "The exception" is a claim
                       about ALL the other plants, so it is swept over
                       PlantCatalog.ids() rather than spot-checked -- exactly one
                       plant returns on_road, and it is the Bramble.

  seen_defer_tip       1 claim asserted here: _furthest_along_in_range is still how
                       a cob picks a target.

  seen_sole_cover_tip  1 claim, by test_two_plants_sole_cover_sets_never_share_a_cell.

  seen_dead_ground_tip 3 claims. "Slanted" asserted as a TRUE 45-degree diagonal,
                       not as "not zero" -- 0.1 rad is non-zero and is not slanted,
                       and this is the channel the card itself uses to distinguish
                       these bars from the one square to the lane. The reach
                       comparison asserted here; per-plant dead ground already by
                       test_a_cell_can_be_dead_ground_for_a_chomp_and_good_ground_for_a_corn.

TWO WORDS ARE LOAD-BEARING AND READ AS ORDINARY PROSE. seen_road_tip says everything
WALKING a Bramble stops to chew through it: Bramble.stops(true) is false, so a winged
pest does not stop and the sentence is true only because of that word. Asserted in both
directions -- one direction alone passes on a Bramble that stops nothing at all. And
seen_dead_ground_tip's SLANTED, above.

A VERDICT NAMING ANOTHER TEST IS ITSELF CHECKED: the name must still exist in the
suite source, so renaming that test fails this rather than silently orphaning the
card. The bead asked for the pointer; a pointer nobody can follow is how the card
ends up unwatched again.

NOTED, NOT ACTED ON: Dandelion reaches 192px against the Corn Cobbler's 176. The
dead-ground card uses the cob as its long-reach exemplar and is still correct,
because it only claims the cob out-reaches the SHORT plant it is compared to -- but
the cob is not the longest reach in the game and a future rewording should not
assume it is.

Verified headless, which the bead correctly predicted was enough: 1007 tests /
19203 assertions, lint 0, import 0, check_all clean. Three mutations, three distinct
failures.

title: The bridge cannot drive an absolute mouse position, so hover behaviour is unverifiable
description:
SOURCE: cycle 144, log-devtools.md [G-141]. OUT OF NEIGHBOURHOOD: this is the
verify harness, not the game.

THE GAP, measured rather than inferred. The bridge cannot drive an absolute mouse
position, so nothing that reads InputEventMouseMotion.position can be exercised at
runtime.

    $ python tools/devtools.py cmd mouse_move --args '{"position":[224.0,104.0]}'
    "message": "mouse_move needs relative as [dx, dy]"

The relative form is accepted and does not help: Godot's relative motion carries
no position, so a handler doing `_update_cursor(motion.position)` sees (0, 0).
Measured twice -- _hover_cell stayed (-1, -1) both times, including after warping
-4000,-4000 and then +224,+104, which is the obvious workaround and does nothing
because the OS cursor is not what the event carries.

WHY IT MATTERS HERE RATHER THAN BEING NICHE. This game has at least four
position-readers: Game._update_cursor (game/game.gd:2450, which sets _hover_cell
and therefore the placement preview, the dead-ground cue and now the move
window's hold), the husk sweep's collect_at, PlacementPreview, and every tooltip
surface. Cycle 144 shipped a feature whose whole risk was "does anything actually
set _hover_cell in the real game" and could not answer it through the event
layer -- only by calling _update_cursor directly, one level below the thing in
question. That check is recorded as `blocked` and the ledger row says `partial`
because of it.

THE FIX, small: accept a `position` arg on mouse_move and set it on the
InputEventMouseMotion, with `relative` defaulting to the delta from the previous
position so existing callers are unaffected. Both fields are settable on the
event; nothing about this needs new plumbing.

FIRST STEP, and do not skip it: this project runs harness 0.38.0 and
`harness-version --client` reports 0.60.0 on this machine.
.claude/skills/gap-reconcile/SKILL.md is the procedure for checking the INSTALLED
version rather than the pinned one. If 0.60.0 already takes a position, this
closes as fixed-in and [G-141] gets a new status line APPENDED -- never a rewrite
of the existing one.

IF STILL OPEN AT 0.60.0: it ships from a repo I own, so it goes upstream via
.claude/skills/skill-feedback-issue/SKILL.md with the exact command and refusal
message above in the body. Do NOT patch tools/devtools.py here -- it is
harness-managed, .harness_manifest.json lists it, and a local edit is silently
reverted by the next /scaffold-godot-harness.

ACCEPTANCE: either a new status line on [G-141] recording fixed-in with the
evidence read out of the installed templates, or an upstream issue with the
reproduction. Both are things the closing commit can produce.
close_reason: Reconciled via gap-reconcile: fixed-in harness 0.66.0 (installed on this machine), [G-141] status line appended. No repo code change needed.

title: Decide whether a husk should stop rotting while the player is reaching for it
description:
SOURCE: cycle 144's kanban entry, first bullet, written straight after building the
first instance of the pattern. PLAYER-FACING, and it is a fairness question rather
than a feature.

THE PATTERN, now that the game has exactly one of it. Game._tick_uproot_confirm
(game/game.gd:2050) skips its decrement while can_move_to(_uproot_armed,
_hover_cell) (game/game.gd:2166) is true, so the uproot window holds while the
pointer sits on a legal destination and resumes when it leaves. Measured live in
cycle 144: held at exactly 4.0 across five reads spanning seconds, then 3.4, 3.1,
2.8 once the pointer moved away. The drawn arc stops unwinding with it, which is
the honest half -- the deadline really has stopped, so the countdown is not lying
to the player about how long they have.

THE CANDIDATE THIS BEAD IS ACTUALLY ABOUT: the husk rot timer. A husk decays on a
clock and is collected by clicking it. A player who has SEEN the husk and is
reaching for it is in exactly the state the uproot fix was written for -- visibly
mid-action, losing to a deadline that cannot see them. Unlike the uproot window
there is no confirm being protected, so there is no competing pull at all.

CONFIRM BEFORE BUILDING, because this bead is written from the uproot's side and
not from the husk's:
  * Find the rot clock and its constant. HuskLayer draws a partial arc for it --
    OVERLAY_GRAMMAR.md's "Partial arc at a fixed radius" row cites
    husk_layer.gd:113-122 as a husk's rot timer -- so the countdown is already
    drawn and would already stop with the clock, same as the uproot arc.
  * Find what "reaching for it" means mechanically. The uproot version had
    _hover_cell, set by _update_cursor from real mouse motion. A husk is
    collected by compost.collect_at(local) on a click, and the hover equivalent
    may not exist yet -- if it does not, THAT is the work, and it is more than a
    one-line hold.
  * Decide whether pausing is even right here. An uproot window is a decision the
    player opened; a rot timer is pressure the game applies. Removing pressure a
    player can neutralise by hovering may be a strictly worse game, and "the
    husk decays while you dither" might be the point. This is a taste call and
    should be made as one.

TWO OTHER DEADLINES, listed so the sweep is on the record and neither is
recommended: Game.PACKET_OPEN_STEP_SECONDS is a presentation beat with nothing to
lose to, and Hud.MESSAGE_DEADLINE already has its own arbitration
(uproot_armed_message's header records the budget fight that produced it).

ACCEPTANCE: a decision recorded with its reasoning -- the same shape
plant-tower-defense-h5w6 closed with -- and, if the answer is yes, the hold plus a
headless test that drives the clock with a chosen delta and asserts it holds,
resumes, and still expires. Do NOT wait real seconds in the test; cycle 144's
test_the_move_window_holds_while_a_destination_is_hovered is the model.
notes:
DECIDED: NO. The husk rot decrement gets no hold, and that is now recorded above
CompostMeter._process (game/compost_meter.gd:212-251) in the same shape ix76 used.

CONFIRMED the bead's premise before deciding it. The rot clock is real and is
CompostMeter._process; the arc that draws it is husk_layer.gd:113-122, sweeping
TAU * (life / max_life) against the husk's OWN max_life. So a hold would stop a
visible countdown exactly the way the uproot arc does. That half of the bead held up.

The half that did not: "reaching for it" is not a state this game has. Game._hover_cell
is a CELL, set by _update_cursor (game/game.gd:2592); a husk is swept within
COLLECT_RADIUS of a POINT by collect_at (game/compost_meter.gd:192). Different queries,
and the block above COLLECT_RADIUS records that exactly 4 px separate "this click
sweeps a husk" from "this click places a plant". The bead predicted this ("the hover
equivalent may not exist yet -- if it does not, THAT is the work") and it was right.

FOUR REASONS, in the order they matter:

  * The uproot hold covers a gap between TWO steps -- arm, then confirm at a
    destination -- and the window exists only to bound that gap. Collecting a husk is
    ONE click. There is no in-between state to protect, so the hold would not be
    pausing a decision, it would be pausing the pressure itself.
  * A proximity hold puts the pointer's distance to a husk inside that 4 px margin as
    a second meaning.
  * It would fire without being asked. Husks drop where pests die, on and beside the
    road, which is the ground the pointer crosses while walling a lane. 28 px is a
    distance you pass through incidentally, so the clock would stop for reasons the
    player never chose and cannot see. The uproot hold is legible because the player
    armed it and an arc is unwinding at them.
  * MOUSE PLAYERS COULD REACH IT AND TOUCH PLAYERS COULD NOT. game/game.gd:2438 says
    it in its own words: the drag branch is "the hover a mouse player has had all
    along and a touch player never did". A finger only hovers while it is down, and a
    finger down over a husk collects it on release.

And the cost is not symmetric. MIN_HUSK_LIFETIME gives the size/glow cue its second
job -- a big bright husk is urgent as well as valuable -- so a clock stoppable by
resting the mouse takes one of two readings back off a cue cycle 88 built precisely
because one channel had run out of range.

The two other deadlines the bead listed for the record are unchanged and neither is
recommended: PACKET_OPEN_STEP_SECONDS has nothing to lose to, and MESSAGE_DEADLINE
already has its own arbitration.

No test, because there is no behaviour change to pin. Gates: name_check 0,
import_check 0, lint 0 errors 0 warnings.

title: Relocate the thirteen citations cycle 142's board work left drifted
description:
SOURCE: cycle 142, and it is the first time the loop's own step-3 threshold
fired. Filed BY that rule rather than despite it.

THE RULE, added cycle 140 to .claude/skills/cycle/SKILL.md step 3: "If --against
reports more than ten drifted, the relocation is a WORK ITEM, not part of this
step. Fix what your own entries cite, file the rest, and say in the close how
many you left."

WHAT HAPPENED. Cycle 142 added ~110 lines near the top of game/board.gd (the
road parameterisation) and `citation_check --beads --against` reported SIXTEEN
drifted targets. Four belonged to the bead the cycle was working
(plant-tower-defense-s1o8.1) and were fixed there. THIRTEEN REMAIN and are this
bead, listed so nobody has to re-derive the set:

  game/board.gd:150-162   at kanban.md:4469
  game/board.gd:162       at kanban.md:2370
  game/board.gd:254       at kanban.md:1373
  game/board.gd:811       at kanban.md:397
  game/board.gd:669       at bead plant-tower-defense-s1o8:34
  game/board.gd:76        at bead plant-tower-defense-sp8g:28
  game/board.gd:92        at bead plant-tower-defense-s1o8.2:33
  game/board.gd:72        at bead plant-tower-defense-s1o8.2:25
  test/unit/test_selftest.gd:7612   at kanban.md:5308
  test/unit/test_selftest.gd:8378   at kanban.md:2398

  test_selftest.gd:7760            at kanban.md:2914
  (plus 10 more in CLOSED beads, advisory -- a citation inside a closed bead is
  part of a record and the file moved for its own reasons. Leave those.)

HOW TO DO IT, and the two traps this repo has already paid for twice:
  1. RELOCATING BY OFFSET SATISFIES --against WITHOUT MAKING THE CITATION
     CORRECT. The check compares TEXT, so a citation landing on a blank line, a
     bare `##` or a closing brace matches anywhere. Cycles 139 and 140 found
     TWENTY citations that were already wrong before the cycle that moved them,
     two of them on blank lines. Read what each relocated citation LANDS ON
     against the sentence citing it. If the code it described is gone rather
     than moved, say so in the entry instead of repointing at the nearest
     survivor.
  2. citation_check reports ONE citing location per TARGET, so fixing one
     reveals the next and the pass looks finished before it is -- cycle 141 took
     three rounds. Re-run until it reports 0, and see
     plant-tower-defense-t7t1 for the count that would make this legible.

Also: a bare :NN in kanban.md binds to the last full path before it, and writing
a wrong line number in prose to REPORT it makes it a live citation again. Both
are in .claude/skills/kanban-idea-pass/SKILL.md rule 1.

ACCEPTANCE: `python tools/citation_check.py --beads --against <a snapshot taken
before the work>` reports 0 drifted outside closed beads, and the commit message
names how many of the thirteen were pure offset versus how many were ALREADY
