title: A plant's state reads as a drawn cue while its body does nothing: pick one and give it motion
description:
SOURCE: cycle 141's kanban entry "New in cycle 141", first bullet, plus the
Chomp champ that shipped this cycle (plant-tower-defense-ts34). PLAYER-FACING.

THE PATTERN, stated once rather than per plant: a plant's STATE mostly reads as
a drawn cue while its body does nothing. Cycle 141 fixed the loudest instance --
a chewing Chomp had only its chew ring, a timer readout standing in for a body --
and the argument that justified it ("one channel is not enough") applies
unchanged to at least three more.

THE CANDIDATES, read rather than recalled:
  * A plant NEARLY DEAD. This is the strongest one and the only one that is
    about danger rather than about progress. Plant.FLINCH_RADIANS
    (game/plant.gd:231) fires on the BITE and decays over FLINCH_SECONDS 0.32,
    so it says "just hit" and never "nearly gone" -- a plant at 8% health and one
    at 95% are the same silhouette between bites, and the difference lives
    entirely in a health bar the player has to be looking at.
  * Sunflower FILLING. yield_gauge_rect() (game/sunflower.gd:138) draws the
    progress; the body does not change as it fills.
  * StickySundew HOLDING. It shows a wash on the pest rather than anything on
    the plant, which is the same asymmetry the Chomp had -- the thing being
    acted on shows it, the actor does not.

WHY NOW: the mechanism exists and is free to the plants that do not want it.
Plant.idle_scale_multiplier (game/plant.gd:548) is multiplied into the shared
breathe and returns Vector2.ONE by default, and
test_only_the_chomp_overrides_the_idle_scale_hook already sweeps
PlantCatalog.ids() through Game._new_plant asserting every plant is inert unless
it opts in. Adding a second override is a function and a constant.

THIS IS A DESIGN BEAD, NOT A LIST TO IMPLEMENT. Three states is three channels
on one pivot whose scale now has two writers, and "every plant twitches about
everything" is worse than none. Pick ONE -- the near-death case is the
recommendation, because it is the only one where the information is urgent and
the player is not already looking at a gauge -- and say why the others were
refused.

WATCH THE COMPOSITION: the champ is a scale on _sway_pivot and so is the
breathe. A second scale-based state on the SAME plant would multiply with both,
and three multiplied sinusoids do not read as three states; they read as noise.
A near-death tell probably wants a different channel (the flinch's rotation,
held rather than decaying) for exactly that reason.

ACCEPTANCE: one state gets a motion, with a pure static seam and a headless test
in the shape of test_a_chewing_chomp_champs_further_than_it_breathes, plus a
LIVE measurement of the quiet case it claims to exceed -- see the third bullet
of cycle 141's kanban section for why the quiet side is the one that needs
measuring. The close records which state was chosen and why the other two were
refused.
close_reason:
Shipped in 45f1494. PICKED THE NEAR-DEATH CASE, which was this bead's own
recommendation, and the reasons the other two were refused are below as it asked.

THE MECHANISM, and it is not the one the bead expected. The bead said a
near-death tell "probably wants a different channel (the flinch's rotation, held
rather than decaying)". Right instinct, but rotation already carries TWO
sinusoids on deliberately separate clocks, so a third oscillation of any kind
phase-locks eventually. What works is a HELD LEAN -- a DC offset, no frequency to
lock with, and it composes by construction: the sway keeps its full range,
displaced, so a wilting plant still breathes and still flinches. Scale was
refused for the reason the bead gave: two writers already, and three multiplied
sinusoids read as noise.

THE THRESHOLD IS DERIVED rather than chosen: Pest.EAT_DPS / MAX_HEALTH = 0.35,
one second of chewing. plant.gd's header already reasons in that number. Proved
load-bearing by a mutation PAIR, because the single obvious mutation is
equivalent -- the literal 0.35 survives, since 14/40 is 0.35 today. Retuning
EAT_DPS to 20 passes with the derivation and fails with the literal.

WHY SUNFLOWER FILLING WAS REFUSED: it is progress, not danger, and the player is
already looking at a gauge that says it (yield_gauge_rect). The Chomp's champ
earned its place because a chew ring is a TIMER standing in for a body under
threat; a yield gauge is a readout of something pleasant with no decision
attached. Adding motion there spends a channel on information nobody needs
faster.

WHY STICKYSUNDEW HOLDING WAS REFUSED: it is the same asymmetry the Chomp had --
the thing acted on shows it, the actor does not -- and that argument is real, but
the Sundew is a FIELD effect with no per-pest state on the plant, so the honest
version is a change to the wash rather than to the body. Filed nothing; it is
weaker than both of the above and the bead's own warning ("every plant twitches
about everything is worse than none") applies to it most.

THE RUN REFRAMED THE FEATURE, which is worth carrying: the wilt band is EXACTLY
EAT_DPS worth of health, so during an uninterrupted chew it shows for ONE SECOND
before death. But a plant whose attacker dies mid-meal sits in the band while
regrowth climbs out -- about twelve seconds. So this is mostly not a death
warning; it is a "this bed is still hurt" readout during the intermission, when
the player can act on it. Measured live: rotation 0.240 at 2hp against a healthy
band of +-0.055, 0.034 at full health, and three neighbours at 2hp leaning
+0.240 / -0.204 / -0.237.

title: A Chomp mid-meal sways exactly like an idle one, while the pest in its mouth shows the meal
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md, "Requested directly by James", the "Animate all the plants and
enemies" bullet -- the third word of the original ask, TWITCH. PLAYER-FACING.

THAT BULLET IS NOW PARTLY STALE AND THIS BEAD IS THE PART THAT SURVIVES.
It says "every idle motion in the game is a continuous sinusoid, so nothing is
ever startled, surprised, or briefly out of rhythm." That has been false since
cycle 86 for plants (Plant.FLINCH_RADIANS, game/plant.gd:231, re-armed by
take_damage) and since cycle 139 for pests (Pest.FLINCH_RADIANS,
game/pest.gd:602, armed in flash_hit). Both are damage twitches. The bullet
should be corrected as part of this work rather than left to be read again.

WHAT IS GENUINELY LEFT, and the bullet named it without following it up: "A
Chomp with a full mouth and a plant being eaten both know something a sway does
not." The plant-being-eaten half shipped -- that IS the cycle-86 flinch. The
Chomp half did not.

THE ASYMMETRY, confirmed by reading both sides rather than one:
  * The pest being eaten SHOWS it. ChompFlower._chew calls
    _held.set_chewed(float(taken) / float(BITES_PER_MEAL))
    (game/chomp_flower.gd:548), and Pest._gait multiplies that into its sprite
    scale every frame (game/pest.gd:1547, `var eaten: float = chewed_scale()`).
  * The flower doing the eating does NOT. ChompFlower declares no animation of
    its own: its overrides are upgrade_ladder, grab_radius, _on_setup, the chew
    LAYER (a drawn arc), _act, _grab, _chew, release, is_busy, held_pest,
    chew_progress, reach_ring_*, _draw, _draw_fang_crown, _bite, _on_upgraded --
    not one of them touches the sway. So it inherits Plant._wobble
    (game/plant.gd:506) unchanged and a Chomp mid-meal sways exactly like an
    idle one.

The only tell a chewing Chomp has today is the drawn chew RING
(_draw_chew_ring, game/chomp_flower.gd:432), which is a timer readout rather
than a motion, and this project's standing rule is that one channel is not
enough.

THE SHAPE, and it should copy what already works rather than invent:
Plant._wobble ends at game/plant.gd:526,
`_sway_pivot.transform = sway_transform(angle, breathe_scale(clock))`.
Rotation on that pivot is already spoken for -- sway plus flinch -- so the free
channel is SCALE. Add a subclass hook multiplied into the breathe (default
Vector2.ONE, so no other plant changes at all), and have ChompFlower return a
champ while is_busy(). Pure static for the champ itself, because everything in
_wobble past the animations_enabled() gate is unreachable headless -- the same
seam Plant.breathe_scale (game/plant.gd:544) and Pest.gait_yaw
(game/pest.gd:1603) exist for.

Amplitude must clearly exceed the idle breathe or it reads as nothing:
BREATHE_AMOUNT is 0.022 (game/plant.gd:245) and BREATHE_RATE is 2.0
(game/plant.gd:246). Follow the flinches' ratio rule and pin at least one
endpoint to an absolute number, not to a multiple of the champ's own constant --
the mutation that survived cycle 71 was BREATHE_AMOUNT = 0.0, and every
assertion written in terms of it stayed true.

WRITE THE TEST WITH .claude/skills/assert-an-animation/SKILL.md. This is its
rung 1: the value is a function of a clock the object already owns
(_chew_left/_chew_total, already exposed as chew_progress()), so no Tween is
wanted and the whole thing is assertable through the pure function.

ACCEPTANCE: a Chomp with a pest in its mouth deforms visibly differently from an
idle one, the deformation clearly exceeds the idle breathe, every other plant is
byte-for-byte unchanged (the hook defaults to Vector2.ONE and a test asserts
that for a non-Chomp), and the kanban bullet's "nothing is ever startled" clause
is corrected in the same commit.
close_reason:
Shipped in 65ec56b. A Chomp with a pest in its mouth now champs -- a fast
vertical squash multiplied into the shared breathe -- through a new
Plant.idle_scale_multiplier hook that returns Vector2.ONE for every other plant.

ACCEPTANCE, item by item:
  * "deforms visibly differently from an idle one" -- measured live rather than
    eyeballed, with is_busy and the pivot scale read in the SAME poll:
    idle (is_busy false, 14 samples) x 0.978..1.022; chewing (is_busy TRUE,
    10 samples) x 0.9446..1.0478. Both chewing extremes are outside the idle band.
  * "clearly exceeds the idle breathe" -- and the live run added something the
    constants could not: the idle band IS the breathe's analytic maximum,
    BREATHE_AMOUNT 0.022 reached in play. So the separation is one a player gets,
    not an upper bound the breathe never approaches.
  * "every other plant byte-for-byte unchanged" -- Vector2.ONE is the identity for
    a component-wise multiply, and test_only_the_chomp_overrides_the_idle_scale_hook
    sweeps PlantCatalog.ids() through Game._new_plant asserting every freshly built
    plant, Chomp included, is inert. Keyed to having a pest, not to being a Chomp.
  * "the kanban bullet corrected in the same commit" -- done, and it needed more
    correcting than the bead said: its "nothing is ever startled" clause had been
    false since cycle 86 for plants and cycle 139 for pests, so the bullet is now
    closed with all three twitches named rather than amended again.

WHAT THE RUN CAUGHT THAT THE DIFF DID NOT, both recorded in the verify ledger row:
  * The first pivot samples read +-7% while is_busy had just reported false, which
    reads exactly like "the idle breathe is three times its own constant". A pest
    had been grabbed between the two reads. Nearly filed as a defect in
    breathe_scale.
  * _T.assert_lt does not exist, and the test reported [PASS] while aborting
    mid-method. run_tests.py caught it on the error count; run_tests.gd alone would
    have reported a clean suite.

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY LEFT: the general point under the original ask -- a state a
plant is IN still mostly reads as a drawn cue rather than as motion. The Chomp was
the case where a readout stood in for a body; a Sunflower filling its gauge and a
plant one bite from dying are the same shape. Left in kanban as an idea, not filed,
because each is a judgement about whether the state earns a channel.

title: All three teaching budgets are full at once: decide which to raise before the next cue
description:
SOURCE: cycle 140, and it is a wall the cycle walked into rather than an idea.
PLAYER-FACING in its consequence, though the work itself is a decision.

ALL THREE TEACHING BUDGETS ARE AT THEIR LIMIT AT ONCE, for the first time:

  * RunConfig.HINTS (game/run_config.gd:259) now holds SIX ids. The sixth was
    spent this cycle on the sole-cover rings (plant-tower-defense-bkss).
  * The cue legend page holds six rows and is measurably full --
    game/cue_legend.gd:102, 294px of 300, a seventh prices at 340.
  * The notebook hints page holds three rows per page (hints_capacity(),
    game/notebook_screen.gd:384) and needed a second page the moment the sixth
    hint landed.

So the NEXT cue this game draws cannot be taught by adding a row, a hint or a
card. One of the three has to be raised first.

THIS IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL. game/OVERLAY_GRAMMAR.md already lists marks with no
teaching at all, and the lane-pressure hatch is the worked example of what
happens when the discovery arrives late: game/cue_legend.gd records that by the
time cycle 110 gave the hatch a grammar row "there was no width to teach it with
-- the decision had already been made by the layout, before anyone asked."

THE DECISION TO MAKE, before the next cue rather than during it. Three routes,
and they are not equivalent:

  (a) A second legend page. Already filed as plant-tower-defense-xfbo, and the
      largest of the three: page_for_kind returns the FIRST page of a kind
      (game/notebook_screen.gd:299) and legend_note_text() reads that one entry,
      so both need a per-page answer before a second page can say anything
      different from the first.
  (b) Raise the hint ceiling. Cheapest mechanically -- HINTS is a list -- but
      the ceiling that binds is not the list, it is how many teaching lines a
      player will read in an opening run before they stop reading. That is a
      judgement and it should be made as one, not discovered by adding a
      seventh.
  (c) Teach somewhere that is not a row at all. The hatch's own note argues it
      is the single cue in the game that TEACHES ITSELF, because its coverage
      half is derived from the plants standing right now. If a cue can be made
      self-teaching, it costs no budget -- and that property is a design
      constraint on the CUE, available only while the cue is being designed.

ACCEPTANCE: this is a decision bead. It closes with a recorded choice among the
three and one paragraph on why the other two were refused -- the same shape
plant-tower-defense-bkss closed with. It does NOT require any of the three to be
built; deciding is the deliverable, and the build becomes its own item.
close_reason:
DECIDED: raise nothing. Recorded in game/cue_legend.gd's audit block, which is
where anyone pricing a teaching surface already reads, rather than only here.
Commit f2b6a18.

THE PREMISE IS ARITHMETICALLY TRUE AND PRACTICALLY WRONG. The three are not one
budget and two of them are not budgets:

  * THE LEGEND PAGE IS COMPLETE, NOT FULL. The audit block directly above the
    numbers this bead quotes already dispositions every untaught grammar row by
    name. Row 6 -- which this bead would have been about -- is refused because a
    legend row teaches it WORST: four instances meaning four different things, on
    a row the grammar defines by CHANNEL rather than by meaning. The block says
    "teaching it honestly is four rows, which is more than a page" and names the
    right home as "the hints page or a mark-side tooltip, both of which carry a
    sentence per instance". So 294 of 300px is not stopping anything anyone wants
    to do.
  * THE NOTEBOOK HINTS PAGE IS NOT A CEILING. This bead's third bullet is simply
    wrong: hint_pages_needed() computes pages from the list, hints_on_page()
    slices it, and the book grew to two pages on its own when the sixth hint
    landed. A seventh costs one row in PAGES, with an assertion at
    test/unit/test_placement.gd:2789 that fails until it is there.
  * THE HINT LIST IS THE ONLY REAL CEILING, AND IT IS NOT THE LIST. Six ids is
    not the limit; attention is. Cycle 145 found the binding constraint is
    DELIVERY -- the row's clauses are mutually exclusive with a fixed winner, so
    the forfeit beats the move tip and an upgraded plant never sees it. A seventh
    id would not have helped the player who never saw the fifth.

ROUTE (a) SECOND LEGEND PAGE: refused, and not on cost -- nothing outstanding
wants a legend row at all. -xfbo stays open on its own merits (the notebook's
pager and legend_note_text needing a per-page answer) but it is not on the
critical path for teaching anything.
ROUTE (b) RAISE THE HINT CEILING: refused as stated. The list is not what binds,
and this bead said so itself without following it through.
ROUTE (c) SELF-TEACHING: ADOPTED, and generalised into a rule. Cycles 141, 143
and 147 shipped three cues -- the pest recoil, the Chomp's champ, the wilt -- and
none spent a word, because motion is ICONIC where a mark is ARBITRARY.

A FOURTH SURFACE THIS BEAD DOES NOT LIST, proven in cycle 145 after it was
filed: the selection panel's detail slot. Free of all three budgets, contextual,
and it carries a sentence per instance -- exactly what row 6's verdict asks for.

The recorded order, cheapest first: make it self-evident, then the panel slot if
it is tied to a selection, then a hint budgeted for delivery, then a legend row.

ALSO FIXED WHILE HERE: the ledger listed row 4 as untaught two cycles after the
sixth hint taught it -- a hand-maintained TAUGHT/untaught table with nothing
checking it against RunConfig.HINTS. Same class as cycle 145's stale notebook
card, and plant-tower-defense-snhb is the open bead for that class.

title: Reconcile the 72 open gaps against the 0.60.0 harness on this machine, not the 0.38.0 this project runs
description:
SOURCE: cycle 139 step 4's gap reconcile, plus harness-version --client.
Out-of-neighbourhood item: nothing to do with pests, the gait, or citations.

THE NUMBERS, read this cycle rather than remembered:
python tools/gap_ledger.py --open reports
"151 status line(s), 94 distinct id(s), 72 currently open, 18 superseded".
python tools/devtools.py harness-version --client reports
"A newer harness (0.60.0) is already on this machine than this project runs
(0.38.0)" with "Machine: plugin cache 0.60.0, marketplace clone 0.60.0".

WHY THE 72 IS NOT A BACKLOG OF 72 REAL GAPS. gap_ledger derives each status
from its LAST mention and says so, but its own NOT COVERED line names the
limit precisely: "this reads statuses, not the harness. It cannot tell you
whether an open gap has since been FIXED upstream -- that needs the installed
version opened and the claim re-checked, which is the actual reconciliation
work and is a human job."

This project is 22 minor releases behind the harness on this machine. A gap
filed against 0.38.0 and never revisited is an open question about 0.38.0,
not a claim about 0.60.0 -- and .claude/skills/gap-reconcile/SKILL.md exists
for exactly this and says to open the version INSTALLED ON THIS MACHINE rather
than the one the project pins. Two traps this repo has already paid for and
that must not be repeated here: grep -c "status: open" counts LINES and once
said 61 when the answer was 44, and an id CITED in the installed harness is
not thereby fixed -- 43 of this project's ids appear in 0.38.0 but 29 of those
are only in the harness's own copy of this log.

G-130 is the live example of the cost. It is the 0.38.0-vs-0.60.0 spread
itself: /verify Phase 0.5 (plugin 0.60.0) instructs a "tier" key on the ledger
row, and this project's verify_ledger reads no such key, so the row silently
loses it. It was seen twice in two days (cycles 138 and 139) and only this
repo's own tools/run_json_check.py has ever said so.

THE WORK, in order:
  1. Run gap-reconcile over the open set against the 0.60.0 templates on this
     machine, in batches, appending a new status line per id -- never
     rewriting an old entry, because the format records status per entry and
     gap_ledger resolves from the last one.
  2. Report the split: fixed-in-0.60.0 / still open at 0.60.0 / wontfix /
     could-not-tell.
  3. For anything still open at 0.60.0 and concrete, file upstream with
     .claude/skills/skill-feedback-issue.

DELIBERATELY NOT IN SCOPE: actually running /scaffold-godot-harness to refresh
this project to 0.60.0. That is a separate decision with its own blast radius
(it regenerates CLAUDE.md's managed block and everything under tools/ and
addons/), it is already tracked as -ny3h, and doing it as a side effect of a
bookkeeping pass is how a cycle loses a day.

ACCEPTANCE: a commit that appends one new status line per reconciled id to
log-devtools.md and prints the four-way split in its message. The closing
commit CAN produce that -- no running game, no screenshot, no evidence half
that a commit cannot make. Partial is fine and expected: say how many of the
72 were reconciled and leave the rest open rather than guessing at them.
close_reason: Partially reconciled, as the bead allowed: 12 of 75 open ids, 63 left alone. Split: 10 fixed upstream and NOT installed (status stays open -- a 0.44.0 fix does nothing for a project on 0.38.0, and G-058 proved it by biting cycle 151), 1 still open at 0.60.0 (G-044, where what is installed is a retry loop AROUND a Godot importer segfault rather than a fix of it), 1 wontfix (G-069, wrong at both ends and already refuted in devtools_ext/commands.gd:196-201), 0 could-not-tell. The pass found a defect in the reconciler itself: harness-version --client's second number resolves status PER LINE rather than per id from the last one, so it reported 12 already-fixed-here and was wrong all 12 times. Filed as G-142. Follow-on: the remaining 63 are older and filed against earlier versions, so the same pass over them should be at least as productive.

title: A sundew-stuck pest now recoils exactly as hard as a shot one: decide, do not assume
description:
SOURCE: cycle 139's step-3 pass, filed as taste rather than as a defect.
PLAYER-FACING.

CONFIRMED BY ENUMERATION, not by example. Pest._flinch_left is armed in
exactly one place -- game/pest.gd:1698, inside flash_hit(). Grepped for the
FIELD rather than for the verb, because the field is what the gait reads
(game/pest.gd:1538) and any second writer would have to appear there. So the
set of things that make a bug recoil is exactly the set that calls
flash_hit(), and that set is six call sites across five files:

  game/kernel.gd:85          a kernel that landed and did not kill
  game/seed_bomb.gd:229      blast damage a pest survived
  game/nettle.gd:296         a sting
  game/chomp_flower.gd:551   a mouth holding one
  game/chomp_flower.gd:719   the same, second path
  game/sticky_sundew.gd:285  A PEST IT NEVER DAMAGED

That last one is not an accident and flash_hit's own header says so at
game/pest.gd:1682-1684: StickySundew is named there as the third caller,
"which flashes a pest it never damaged", and it is the reason _last_hit_blocked
is CONSUMED there rather than merely read.

THE QUESTION, which is a design call and not a bug: that was the right shape
for a colour flash standing in for "no". In motion it is a stronger claim -- a
pest stuck in a sundew now recoils exactly as hard as one shot by a kernel, so
"stuck" and "shot" became the same word in the game's vocabulary of movement.

TWO HONEST ANSWERS, and this bead is to pick one rather than to assume:

  (a) Scale the recoil down for the blocked/undamaged case, the way
      SHELL_FLASH_DIM (game/pest.gd:1669) already dims the colour peak for a
      hit a Shield Bug's plate ate. The mechanism is already there: flash_hit
      computes `blocked` on its first line and chooses a peak from it; the
      recoil could take a multiplier from the same bool. This is the answer
      that matches a cue this game already ships.
  (b) Accept it. "Something happened to this bug" is one word, and a player
      does not need the recoil to distinguish causes when the colour already
      does.

DECIDE BY LOOKING, not by reasoning: the amplitude was measured this cycle at
peak 0.366 rad against GAIT_SWING 0.13 (game/pest.gd:550) on a WALKING pest.
A sundew-stuck pest and a Chomp-held pest are not walking, and nothing in
Pest._gait (game/pest.gd:1527) consults the hold -- _play_death
(game/pest.gd:1735-1736) is the only thing that stops the physics process. So
the same yaw plays against a stationary silhouette, where it may read as
struggling (a gift) or as a glitch. That is a screenshot-and-eyes call.

ACCEPTANCE: this is a decision bead. Either a commit lands (a) with a headless
test asserting the blocked recoil is smaller than the unblocked one and larger
than GAIT_SWING, or the bead closes with (b) recorded and one sentence saying
what was seen on screen that settled it. Do not close it silently either way.
close_reason:
Decided and shipped in 30afc59, and the enumeration found a defect sitting beside
the judgement call this bead asked about.

OPTION (a) TAKEN, but not as written. The bead proposed scaling the recoil "for
the blocked/undamaged case, the way SHELL_FLASH_DIM already dims the colour" --
and that conflates two different things, because the sundew is NOT the blocked
case: _last_hit_blocked is false for it, so it was getting the BRIGHT flash and
the FULL recoil. Both had to be handled, by different routes.

THE ENUMERATION, which is what made this bigger. Six things call flash_hit and
only three ever damaged the pest. Kernel, SeedBomb and Nettle do. The Chomp calls
take_damage NOWHERE AT ALL -- `grep take_damage game/chomp_flower.gd` is empty --
and the Sundew never damaged anything. Half the callers were saying "a hit
landed" in motion about a pest that had taken nothing.

AND THE DEFECT THE BEAD DID NOT SEE: a plate-blocked hit already flashes at
SHELL_FLASH_DIM 0.45 against HIT_FLASH_BOOST 1.9, a 4.2x split meaning "that did
nothing", while the recoil said "that hit hard" in the same frame. Two channels,
one event, opposite claims. That is a contradiction rather than a judgement, and
fixing it is not optional in the way the sundew question was.

THE SPLIT IS VIOLENCE VERSUS RESTRAINT, not damage versus no damage:
  * THE CHOMP KEEPS THE FULL RECOIL, and this is the answer this bead's own
    "watch the composition" note was circling. Being eaten alive is the most
    violent thing in the game; routing it through _chew_left rather than
    take_damage is an implementation detail the bug does not care about. A
    gentler shake there would be the cue lying to be consistent with a function
    call. Asserted by name so a future tidy-up has to come past it.
  * THE SUNDEW GETS GLANCE_FLINCH_SCALE 0.35 -- option (a) for the case the bead
    actually raised.
  * A PLATE-BLOCKED HIT GETS IT TOO, from the CONSUMED _last_hit_blocked rather
    than from the caller.

OPTION (b) REFUSED: "something happened to this bug is one word" is true right up
until the colour is already saying two different things, which it was. Accepting
it would have meant keeping a cue that contradicts itself.

DECIDED BY LOOKING, as asked. Frozen between reads on a real pest: full recoil
peaks 0.382, glancing peaks 0.194 -- half the amplitude, still 1.5x the walk's
0.13, so it reads as a recoil rather than as nothing.

THE MOST USEFUL MINUTE was a surviving mutation. My first two tests asserted the
CONSTANT and the CALL SITES, and pinning `_flinch_force = 1.0` -- restoring the
exact defect -- passed both. A table and a list of callers are not the thing that
reads them. test_the_hit_cue_applies_the_verdict_it_computes closes it.

title: Give citation_check a --symbol mode, since --against can only see what THIS cycle moved
description:
SOURCE: cycle 139's step-3 citation pass, and the new kanban.md section
"New in cycle 139". Not player-facing; it is the checker this repo's whole
evidence discipline rests on.

THE FINDING, confirmed by reading every landing rather than by any tool:
eleven kanban.md citations into game/pest.gd were wrong by roughly eight
hundred lines, and every checker had been green over all eleven for an
unknown number of cycles. Three claimed Pest._gait, which is at
game/pest.gd:1527; three claimed _update_facing (game/pest.gd:1502); one each
claimed _apply_facing (game/pest.gd:1519), meal.take_damage(EAT_DPS * delta)
(game/pest.gd:1315), _play_death (game/pest.gd:1735), husk_multiplier()
(game/pest.gd:1957), gait_stretch's hungry branch (game/pest.gd:1582-1584),
and the escaped emit (game/pest.gd:1968-1969). TWO OF THE ELEVEN LANDED ON
BLANK LINES, which match anything.

WHY NOTHING SAW IT, which is the part that matters and is structural rather
than anyone's carelessness:

  * citation_check.py plain mode proves a line EXISTS. Its own NOT COVERED
    output says exactly this and names two cycles that were bitten by it.
  * --snapshot/--against compares the TEXT at each citation before and after
    THIS cycle's edits. A citation that was already pointing at the wrong line
    when the snapshot was taken has its wrong text recorded as the baseline,
    so it compares clean forever. The mode can only ever see citations the
    current cycle moved.

So an already-stale citation in a file nobody touches this cycle is invisible
to both modes, permanently. Cycle 139 found these eleven only because it added
30 lines to game/pest.gd for an unrelated feature.

THE ASK: a --symbol mode. Let a citation optionally name the symbol it means,
in the form this file already writes naturally --

  `Pest._gait` (`game/pest.gd:1527`)

-- and have citation_check verify that the named symbol's func/const/var/signal
declaration falls inside the cited range. Parse the symbol out of the sentence
immediately before the citation (backticked identifier, optionally
Class.method), resolve the declaration in the cited file, compare.

Unlike --against this needs no snapshot and fires on a citation that went stale
three cycles ago in a file nobody has touched since. Unlike plain mode it says
something about whether the line SUPPORTS the claim, for the one class of claim
where support is mechanical: "this citation is for symbol X".

SCOPE HONESTY, to be written into the tool's own NOT COVERED line: this can only
check citations that name a symbol, and most do not -- citation_check already
reports that 339 of 491 entries carry no citation at all. A symbol-checked
citation is a citation whose TARGET is verified, never its argument.

FOLLOW tools/house-static-checker conventions (.claude/skills/house-static-checker):
exit 0 clean / 1 findings / 2 could not run, a printed denominator naming how
many citations carried a checkable symbol out of how many exist, and a synthetic
fixture proving the check can actually fail.

ACCEPTANCE: python tools/citation_check.py --symbol runs over kanban.md and the
bead export, prints "N of M citation(s) name a symbol; K verified, J finding(s)",
exits 1 on a citation whose named symbol is declared outside the cited range, and
a fixture in the repo demonstrates a real failure. Re-pointing the eleven above is
already done and must stay clean under it.
close_reason: tools/citation_check.py --symbol mode: verifies a citation naming a symbol (Class.method, backtick-permissive in files, stricter in bead prose to reject bare English words) against the symbol's real func/const/var/signal declaration span in the cited file. Real run: 99 of 541 kanban.md citations name a symbol, 16 verified, 83 findings; with --beads, 274 of 1576, 34 verified, 101 findings. Self-test: 13 cases including a wrong-range fixture, a nonexistent-symbol case, multi-line-declaration spans, builtin-type exclusion -- 4 hand-run mutations on the classifier all correctly went red. HEADLINE FINDING: the eleven pest.gd citations this bead's own history says were re-pointed at cycle 139 do NOT stay clean -- 69 commits and ~354 lines of pest.gd growth since have drifted them all again (e.g. _gait claimed at 1527, now declared at 1881-1902). Exactly the class of drift --against cannot see; kanban.md itself needs a follow-up repoint pass, outside this lane's file ownership. Verified: check_all clean, default citation_check mode unchanged (541 citations, 0 findings, matching pre-change baseline).

title: Difficulty profiles: the constants that would be one are all const
description:
## WHAT THE GAME DOES NOW (verified 2026-08-19)

kanban.md:2921-2927 filed this and it still holds, with one correction: the campaign
is 22 waves, not eight.

- `Game.LIVES` = 10 (game/game.gd:11), `const`
- `Game.PREP_SECONDS` = 18.0 (game/game.gd:14), `const`
- `SeedBank.STARTING_SEEDS` = 25 (game/seed_bank.gd:16), `const` — kanban.md placed
  this in game.gd; it is in seed_bank.gd
- `WaveDirector.WAVES` (game/wave_director.gd:513) is a literal 22-row table
- `RunConfig` (game/run_config.gd:366) carries one run-shaping field across the
  scene swap: `endless: bool`

The machinery to *describe* difficulty already exists and is unreachable:
`WaveDirector.threat_level()` (game/wave_director.gd:1219) prices any wave as a
multiple of wave 1, and `WaveDirector.set_seed()` (game/wave_director.gd:732) and
`SeedBank.set_seed()` (game/seed_bank.gd:83) have **only test callers** — verified
by grep over game/, test/ and tools/. The campaign is one curve for everyone.

## THE ASK

A difficulty profile: a named bundle of the constants above plus a wave-scaling
factor, carried on `RunConfig` the way `endless` is, applied once at
`Game._ready()` where `director.endless = RunConfig.endless` already happens
(game/game.gd:263).

Not in scope here: the title-screen control that picks one. That is bead 4, because
it has a layout budget of its own.

## WHAT A FIX BREAKS

- Everything reading `Game.LIVES` / `PREP_SECONDS` / `STARTING_SEEDS` as a constant
  in a test. Grep before editing; these are compile-time references, so a `const`
  becoming a member breaks callers loudly rather than silently — that is fine, but
  it will be a wide diff.
- **The save file, and this one is not loud.** `RunConfig` persists to
  `user://highscore.save` with a version header at version 5 (game/run_config.gd:32
  and the SAVE_PATH block). run_config.gd's stated rule is that a save we cannot
  understand leaves the in-memory scores alone, because "silence is recoverable; a
  zero is not". A per-difficulty score slot is a version bump and has to honour that
  rule.
- **The high-score model.** run_config.gd:14-19 argues that a campaign total and an
  endless total are not comparable in either direction, and that sharing one number
  let a single endless run permanently retire the campaign record. The same argument
  applies verbatim to difficulty: a hard-mode score and an easy-mode score in one
  slot repeats the bug the file was rewritten to fix. `best_for(for_endless: bool)`
  (game/run_config.gd:572) is the function that has to grow a second dimension.
- `Milestones` (game/milestones.gd:76) awards `endless_deep` at a wave threshold
  read off run stats. Decide explicitly whether an easy-mode wave 40 earns it.

## ACCEPTANCE

- A difficulty profile is selectable in a headless test and demonstrably changes
  lives, prep time, starting seeds and wave pressure in a real `Game`.
- The default profile reproduces today's numbers exactly (10 / 18.0 / 25, unscaled
  waves), asserted.
- Save round-trips at the new version; a v5 save loads without zeroing any score,
  asserted with a fixture; an unparseable save still leaves memory alone.
- `WaveDirector.threat_level()` reports the profile's curve, so the difficulty is a
  number the game can state rather than a word on a button.
- `python tools/run_tests.py` exit 0.
acceptance_criteria: A difficulty profile is selectable headlessly and demonstrably changes lives, prep time, starting seeds and wave pressure in a real Game; the default profile reproduces 10 / 18.0 / 25 unscaled, asserted; the save round-trips at the new version, a v5 fixture loads without zeroing a score, and an unparseable save still leaves memory alone; threat_level() reports the profile curve; run_tests.py exits 0.
notes: SIZED IN CYCLE 154, which opened it, measured it and deliberately did not start it as a second item. Game.LIVES has 41 references across game/, test/ and tools/; PREP_SECONDS has 33; SeedBank.STARTING_SEEDS has 4. All three are const, so every reference is compile-time and this is a 78-site change rather than a 3-site one. CONSEQUENCE FOR SCHEDULING: it is a whole cycle's work, cannot be a second item, and is also the biggest genuinely player-facing thing on the board -- so it wants to be a cycle's FIRST item, taken deliberately. Cycle 155 takes it.
close_reason: SHIPPED. Game.DIFFICULTIES carries three named profiles -- gentle / standard / harsh -- varying lives, prep_seconds and starting_seeds; RunConfig.difficulty carries the NAME across the scene swap exactly as endless does; Game._ready() applies it ahead of every node it builds, so the HUD is right on the first frame rather than correcting itself. Verified live through the real title->game path: lives 5, starting_lives 5, prep_seconds 9.0, seeds 15, and the top bar reads 'Seeds 15 / Garden 5' with no visible correction. STANDARD IS DERIVED, NOT RESTATED -- its three values read LIVES, PREP_SECONDS and SeedBank.STARTING_SEEDS, so the forty-odd references to those across the repo keep meaning what they meant and there is no second copy to drift. A test pins that. FOUND A LATENT DEFECT: lives_lost was LIVES - lives and the post-mortem's denominator was Game.LIVES, both the standard ten, so on gentle a player losing four of fifteen would have been told four of ten and on harsh a full wipe would have read '5 of 10'. Invisible for as long as there was one profile. Now starting_lives, exported in summary_stats, with RunSummary falling back to Game.LIVES for an older stats dictionary. AND THE SIZING WAS WRONG: cycle 154 measured this at 78 references and chose not to start it as a second item. The 78 are mostly comments and tests; the runtime sites are about eight. That count was itself an enumeration over the wrong set -- mentions, not uses -- which is the fourth instance of that shape in this project and the first where it cost scheduling rather than correctness. OUT OF SCOPE, filed separately: a wave-strength multiplier. _raw_threat's own block records that the curve is asserted to rise strictly wave over wave out to 300, so a scale factor has to be re-verified against that property rather than added beside it.

title: A corpus of roads with genuinely different layouts, plus a validity checker
description:
## THE ASK

Ship a corpus of roads with genuinely different layouts, and a checker that says a
road is playable before anyone plays it.

Depends on the road becoming data. Do not start this first.

## WHY A CHECKER AND NOT JUST EYES

The current road is not arbitrary. Three properties of game/board.gd constrain any
new one, and all three fail invisibly:

- **Tile mask coverage.** `Board.GRASS_EDGE_TILE` (game/board.gd:72) maps a
  four-bit neighbour mask to a Kenney tile. Its own comment: "The kit ships no tile
  for opposite-side or three-side dirt, so those fall back to plain grass; the path
  shape below never needs them." A road that doubles back beside itself renders a
  grass tile in the middle of the dirt and nothing errors. board.gd:92 already marks
  where an intentional exception would go.
- **Reachability.** Plants may not go on road (board.gd header). A road that eats
  too much of a 14x9 / 94-cell field leaves too few plantable cells; today a Chomp
  Flower already strands 36 of 94.
- **Direction coverage.** The current road CLIMBS once, deliberately, because
  `Pest._update_facing()` has a `_facing = 0.0` branch for up-screen travel that had
  never run in a real frame before cycle 53 (game/board.gd:36-43). A corpus where no
  road travels -Y re-orphans that branch.

## VARIETY, STATED AS PROPERTIES RATHER THAN AS A NUMBER

"A variety of different layouts" is the report's words and it is the right ask, but
it cannot be accepted as prose. Make the corpus vary along axes that change how the
game plays, and assert the spread:

- road length in cells (short and dense vs long and thin) — this is what
  `SIMULTANEOUS_PEST_CEILING` is reasoned against
- corner count (a straight run vs a switchback)
- dead ground per plant kind — the number that teaches a player "the top-right is
  useless", and which kanban.md:2111-2116 flags as a thing a player will learn
  falsely from one board and carry to the next
- minimum garden size (the greedy cover derived in test_combat.gd finds five cobs on
  the current road; a road where that number is eight plays differently)
- whether the road travels each of the four directions

## ACCEPTANCE

- A checker — `tools/board_check.py` if it can be static, otherwise a test in
  `test_dir` — that validates every road in the corpus for: single connected path,
  entry and exit on a board edge, every neighbour mask present in
  `GRASS_EDGE_TILE`, a floor on plantable cells, and no isolated plantable pocket.
  It follows the `house-static-checker` contract if written as a tool: exit code 0/1/2,
  a printed denominator, and a NOT COVERED line.
- The checker is proved able to fail, by a synthetic bad road in a fixture — not by
  the corpus passing.
- Assertions in `test_dir` that the corpus actually spans the axes above (a spread
  test, not a per-road literal): road lengths differ by at least X cells, corner
  counts differ, all four travel directions appear somewhere in the corpus.
- Every corpus road passes bead 1's five re-derived shape tests.
- `python tools/run_tests.py` and `godot --headless --path . --script res://tools/lint_project.gd`
  both exit 0.
acceptance_criteria: A checker validates every corpus road for connectivity, edge entry/exit, neighbour-mask coverage in GRASS_EDGE_TILE, a plantable-cell floor and no isolated pocket; it is proved able to fail via a synthetic bad road; spread assertions show the corpus varies in length, corner count and travel direction; every corpus road passes the re-derived shape tests; run_tests.py and lint_project.gd both exit 0.
close_reason: 6-road corpus (up from s1o8.1's 3), spanning cells 14-46, corners 0-8, dead ground 0-84 depending on plant kind, min garden 3-8, all four travel directions incl. -Y on 4/6 roads. New tools/board_check.py (stdlib-only, house-static-checker contract) validates connectivity, edge entry/exit, GRASS_EDGE_TILE mask coverage, plantable floor, no isolated pocket; --self-test proves it can fail via 5 synthetic bad roads. Caught and fixed a real pre-existing bug: s1o8.1's own serpentine road had a 1-cell grass band rendering as fallback grass (mask 0b0101 not in GRASS_EDGE_TILE). Spread assertions added to test_board.gd. Verified on the merged 4-lane integration tree: 1102/1102 tests, real import+lint compile (70 scripts OK), check_all clean.

title: Make the road data, not a const, and derive the five shape-dependent tests
description:
## WHAT THE GAME DOES NOW (verified 2026-08-19)

`Board.PATH_CORNERS` (game/board.gd:50-59) is a `const Array[Vector2i]` of eight
corners. `Board._ready()` (game/board.gd:288-301) walks consecutive pairs and calls
`_add_path_cell` per cell, producing 32 road cells and a 2112 px route. `route()`
(game/board.gd:578) returns one point per road cell bracketed by an off-board entry
and exit; `road_cells()` (game/board.gd:570) returns the cells.

Every consumer resolves the road through a live `Board`, which is the good news —
`Game.covered_road_cells`, `PlacementPreview.covered_road_cell_list`, the coverage
cue and the husk margin all take a board. The blocker is only that a `Board` has no
way to be given a different road.

## THE ASK

Make the road a parameter rather than a constant: `Board` accepts a route
definition, `PATH_CORNERS` becomes the value of the default board, and the tests
below stop recording numbers measured against one specific snake.

## WHAT A FIX BREAKS — name these before starting, do not discover them

`test/unit/test_selftest.gd:7040-7065` is a written-down inventory of exactly this,
put there by cycle 53. It lists five shape-dependent assertions, and warns that the
length/count test **passes in silence** through a reshape that moves all of them:

- `test_the_road_still_has_the_length_and_cell_count_the_constants_were_measured_against`
  (test/unit/test_selftest.gd:7078) — pins 32 cells and 2112.0 px. Guards
  `WaveDirector.SIMULTANEOUS_PEST_CEILING` 40 (game/wave_director.gd:235), which is
  reasoned as "3.5 pests per cell of road". A second road of a different length
  makes 40 mean something else. This test must become per-road, and the ceiling
  must become a function of the loaded road or be re-argued as a hard cap.
- `test_the_real_route_strands_exactly_the_cells_it_was_measured_to_strand`
  (test/unit/test_placement.gd:624-626) — pins dead ground at 11 cells for a Corn
  Cobbler and 36 for a Chomp Flower, of 94. Cycle 53 moved these in **opposite**
  directions over an identical length and count, so they cannot be predicted from
  the invariant; they have to be derived per road.
- `test_a_cell_can_be_dead_ground_for_a_chomp_and_good_ground_for_a_corn`
  (test/unit/test_placement.gd:644) — pins the splitting cell, which moved (2,3) to
  (1,3) at the last reshape.
- `test_the_recorded_gardens_still_have_the_property_they_claim`
  (test/unit/test_combat.gd) — the recorded cob gardens are literal cell lists; a
  reshape can turn a garden cell into road and every downstream ratio keeps
  reporting a number.
- `test_the_preview_warns_about_ground_an_existing_patch_already_covers`
  (test/unit/test_placement.gd) — pins (2,0) covering every road cell (2,2) reaches,
  a fact about this route's geometry alone.
- Guarded by negation and expected NOT to move:
  `test_the_husk_margin_reads_the_road_but_does_not_depend_on_it` — the walk yields
  CELL/2 for any road. Keep that negation; it already caught this block being wrong
  once.

Also: `_over_promise_run` (test/unit/test_combat.gd:4504) — the headless
driven-wave simulator every over-promise test runs on — does `var board :=
Board.new()` at line 4507. It has to take a board or a road, or child bead 5 cannot
be written at all.

`python tools/devtools.py cmd board_info` (devtools_ext/commands.gd:96) prints the
husk click budget and should keep working per board.

## ACCEPTANCE

- `Board` can be built with a road other than the default, in a headless test, with
  no scene edit.
- Each of the five tests above runs over **at least two** distinct roads and derives
  its numbers from the road under test. Deriving means: the assertion recomputes the
  expected value from the route, and a test proves it by failing when handed a road
  that violates the property — not by recording a second literal beside the first.
- The default road produces byte-identical results to today: 32 cells, 2112.0 px,
  11/36 dead ground, splitting cell (1,3).
- `SIMULTANEOUS_PEST_CEILING` either becomes road-derived or gains a comment
  arguing why a fixed 40 is right across the corpus, and a test that fails if a road
  in the corpus makes it wrong.
- `python tools/run_tests.py` exit 0 with the assertion count not lower than before.
acceptance_criteria: Board builds with a non-default road headlessly; the five shape-dependent tests named in test_selftest.gd:7040-7065 each run over at least two roads and recompute their expected values from the route under test; the default road still yields 32 cells, 2112.0 px, 11/36 dead ground, splitting cell (1,3); SIMULTANEOUS_PEST_CEILING is road-derived or argued with a test; run_tests.py exits 0 with no drop in assertion count.
notes:
CYCLE 141 SHIPPED THE FIRST HALF (commit 56b1514) AND THIS BEAD STAYS OPEN.

DONE:
  * Board.set_road(corners) -> refusal string, with validation. The load-bearing
    refusal is DIAGONAL: _build_path walks `while at != to` stepping signi per
    axis, so a non-axis-aligned segment never arrives -- an infinite loop inside
    _ready(), no error, nothing on screen. Also refused: fewer than two corners,
    off-board corners, zero-length segments, and any call once the board is in
    the tree (the tiles are built from the old road and there is no container to
    re-tile through).
  * Board.road_corners(), and _build_path reads it instead of PATH_CORNERS.
  * Board.road_cell_count / road_length_px -- pure, computed from the corners.
  * A three-road corpus in test/unit/test_board.gd: default, short straight,
    long serpentine.
  * test_every_road_in_the_corpus_walks_the_length_its_corners_imply, which
    DERIVES rather than records: expectations come from the arithmetic, actuals
    from the walker. Proven falsifiable by mutation (steps+1 -> steps fails it).
  * The pest-ceiling acceptance bullet, answered the second way. 40 is NOT
    road-derived -- wave_director.gd derives the PROBLEM from the road and sets
    40 by construction from the wave table -- so the new test checks DENSITY
    across the corpus against the 3.5 per cell the header itself names as the
    quantity problem, and pins the default at 1.25.

STILL OPEN -- four of the five shape-dependent tests in cycle 53's inventory
(test/unit/test_selftest.gd, above
test_the_road_still_has_the_length_and_cell_count_the_constants_were_measured_against,
which is kept precisely because that inventory is the only written list of what a
reshape moves):
  * test_the_real_route_strands_exactly_the_cells_it_was_measured_to_strand --
    11 stranded cells for a Corn Cobbler and 36 for a Chomp, of 94. Cycle 53
    moved these in OPPOSITE directions over an identical length and count, so
    they cannot be predicted from the invariant.
  * test_a_cell_can_be_dead_ground_for_a_chomp_and_good_ground_for_a_corn --
    pins the splitting cell, which moved (2,3) -> (1,3) at the last reshape.
  * test_the_recorded_gardens_still_have_the_property_they_claim -- literal cell
    lists that a reshape can turn into road.
  * test_the_preview_warns_about_ground_an_existing_patch_already_covers --
    pins (2,0) covering every road cell (2,2) reaches.

THE HARD PART OF WHAT REMAINS, stated so the next cycle does not rediscover it:
each of those four is a fact about GEOMETRY, and the honest derivation of "which
cells are dead ground for reach R on road X" is the same computation the game
already does. A test that recomputes it the same way asserts nothing. So each
needs either an INDEPENDENT derivation (a different algorithm reaching the same
answer, which is what the length/count pair now does) or a PROPERTY that a bad
road violates -- e.g. "every stranded cell is further than R from every road
cell", which is checkable without reproducing the game's search.

ALSO NOT DONE: _over_promise_run (test/unit/test_combat.gd:4504) still does
`var board := Board.new()` and takes no road. Child bead 5 cannot be written
until it does, and it is a small change now that set_road exists.
close_reason:
Second half, after cycle 141's first. All three entries under cycle 53's "PROPERTY
OF *THIS* ROAD" heading are now derived from the road under test.

  SIMULTANEOUS_PEST_CEILING   cycle 141 -- answered the second way: 40 is not
                              road-derived, wave_director derives the PROBLEM from
                              the road, so the test checks DENSITY across the corpus
                              against the 3.5 per cell the header names.
  the dead-ground counts      THIS CYCLE. The rule, not the numbers: a buildable
                              cell is dead ground for reach R exactly when no road
                              cell's centre is within R of it. Swept over three roads
                              at two reaches, both directions, 382 assertions. 11 and
                              36 stay pinned for the default underneath.
  the Sundew's arithmetic     THIS CYCLE. Two claims -- every road has somewhere
                              worth laying a patch, and the best cell's coverage is
                              NOT constant across the corpus.

ALSO NOT DONE, now done: `_over_promise_run` takes `road_corners`. The one place in
the suite that drives a whole wave over real plants, kernels and schedule could only
run it over the shipped snake. Child bead 5 is no longer blocked on this.

WHY THE DEAD-GROUND DERIVATION DOES NOT CALL covered_road_cells: that is the
function under test, and a derivation that calls it asserts only that it is
deterministic. Two nested sweeps and a distance -- the definition rather than the
implementation.

FALSIFIABILITY, five mutations, five distinct failures:

  cue reports one-covered cells as dead   -> "(8, 0) is called dead ground, but a
                                             road cell lies within 176.0 px of it"
  cue reports nothing dead                -> "no road cell is within 176.0 px of
                                             (9, 0), and the cue does not call it
                                             dead ground"
  helper validates the road then drops it -> "32 vs 32 -- equal counts here would
                                             mean the road was validated and then
                                             thrown away"
  SAP_RADIUS -> 1.0                       -> "the best buildable cell covers 0 road
                                             cells, so a Sundew is unplayable here"
  corpus collapsed to three identical     -> "(5..5 over {default: 5, short
  roads                                      straight: 5, long serpentine: 5})"

NOT DONE, AND NAMED RATHER THAN LEFT SILENT: the live Sundew test in test_combat.gd
still runs on a Game, which builds the default board and cannot be given a road.
Giving `Game` a road is child bead 4's plumbing (the title-screen board picker), not
this bead's. The property test added here covers the CLAIM over the corpus; the live
test stays as the default board's regression, which is what it always was.

A FINDING ABOUT THE QUEUE, not the code: -s1o8.2 has been blocked on this bead since
it was filed, and this bead's prerequisite work shipped in cycle 141. Three beads
were waiting on a half-finished item whose remaining half was written down in its own
notes.

Verified headless, which is the only way the corpus is reachable -- set_road refuses
once the board is in the tree, by design. 1010 tests / 19605 assertions, lint 0,
import 0, name_check 0, check_all clean.

title: Replayability: more than one board, one curve and one difficulty
description:
Reported out of band: "enhance replayability via new boards, levels, difficulties.
Ensure it's all thoroughly playtested, each and every new level — with a variety of
different level layouts, etc. This testing should happen in the future when balancing
or anything relevant is adjusted."

## WHAT THE GAME DOES NOW (verified 2026-08-19 by reading the files named)

There is exactly one board, one campaign curve, and no difficulty selection.

- **One road, and it is a `const`.** `Board.PATH_CORNERS` (game/board.gd:50-59) is
  eight corners expanded to one waypoint per cell in `Board._ready()`
  (game/board.gd:191-199). Nothing reads a road from anywhere else. board.gd:669
  states it outright: "This board has ONE road."
- **One playfield size.** `Board.COLS` 14, `Board.ROWS` 9, `Board.CELL` 64
  (game/board.gd:14-16), also `const`.
- **One campaign curve.** `WaveDirector.WAVES` (game/wave_director.gd:513) is a
  literal table of **22 rows**, not the eight its own doc comments still claim —
  game/run_config.gd:14 says "eight-wave table" and is stale. Endless is the same
  table plus ramp multipliers keyed off `wave - WAVES.size()`.
- **No difficulty setting.** `Game.LIVES` 10 (game/game.gd:11),
  `Game.PREP_SECONDS` 18.0 (game/game.gd:14), `SeedBank.STARTING_SEEDS` 25
  (game/seed_bank.gd:16) are all `const`. `RunConfig` (game/run_config.gd:366)
  carries exactly one run-shaping field across the title→game scene swap:
  `endless: bool`.
- **The title screen has five destinations.** `TitleScreen.MENU_BUTTON_NAMES`
  (game/title_screen.gd:96-98): Start, Endless, Notebook, Keys, Options. The only
  choice a player makes about a run is whether it ever ends.

## DOES THE REPORTED THING EXIST?

**It does not exist.** This is a feature request, not a regression — nobody should
go hunting for a board loader, a level table or a difficulty enum, because there
is not one. Checked by behaviour rather than by one implementation: no `.tres`
level resources, no scene per level (`game/` holds `game.tscn` and `title.tscn`
only), no per-run parameter on `RunConfig` beyond `endless`, and `Board` is
constructed in code with no arguments.

**But the groundwork is real and was deliberate.** Cycle 53 reshaped
`PATH_CORNERS` and re-derived — not re-fitted — the five tests that depend on the
road's shape, and wrote down what a road change costs
(test/unit/test_selftest.gd:7040-7065). kanban.md:2119-2127 records the
conclusion: "A `PATH_CORNERS` that varied per level, with the dead-ground and
garden figures derived at test time instead of recorded, would turn 'another road'
into a data change." That is the unlock this epic spends.

## THE SPLIT

Five children, split by what would be verified rather than by sentence:

1. Road as data (the unlock; everything else waits on it)
2. A corpus of varied roads, with a validity checker
3. Difficulty profiles
4. Choosing a board and a difficulty on the title screen
5. The standing playtest gate — the half of the report that says
   "re-run when balancing is adjusted"

Item 5 is filed separately and on purpose. The report asks for both a code change
and evidence about it; a bead that asks for both closes on neither. Item 5 is a
gate that lives in `test_dir`, so `/verify` re-runs it on every subsequent change
— which is the only mechanism in this project that makes "test again when balance
moves" happen without anyone remembering to.

## ACCEPTANCE (epic)

Closes when all five children close. No code lands against this id directly.
acceptance_criteria: Closes when all five children close. No code lands against this id directly.

title: Only the plant flinches, and a pest's only damage channel is a colour flash
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md "New this cycle (86)", first entry — the out-of-neighbourhood
item for cycle 138. PLAYER-FACING.

CONFIRMED STILL TRUE, and re-cited because every line number in the original
entry has drifted since cycle 86 (they now land on `_health_bar.size`, a doc
comment about live pests, and a `heal_radius` table entry respectively):

 - The plant DOES flinch: `game/plant.gd:177-178` hold `_flinch_left`,
   `game/plant.gd:211-225` argue the design, and `_wobble` is now
   `game/plant.gd:506`. Sway, breathe and flinch ride one pivot.
 - The pest does NOT. `grep -n "flinch\|FLINCH" game/pest.gd` returns nothing.
 - The shape is available: `_gait` is `game/pest.gd:1497` and already reads
   `gait_stretch(sin(clock * GAIT_STRETCH_RATE), is_hungry)` at
   `game/pest.gd:1507` — a continuous sinusoid with per-pest state already
   feeding it, which is exactly `Plant._wobble`'s structure.
 - Its only damage channel today is colour: `HIT_FLASH_DURATION` is
   `game/pest.gd:529`, 0.10s. So a pest taking a kernel to the face and a pest
   that took nothing differ in hue and in nothing else — and this project's
   standing rule is that colour is never the only signal.

WHY THIS ONE RATHER THAN A NEW MOTION: the plant's implementation is the
reference and its argument transfers whole. `game/plant.gd:220-225` records that
the flinch is RE-ARMED every physics frame by `take_damage` rather than
accumulated, so a sustained shudder and a single twitch cost the same three
lines, and that `FLINCH_RADIANS` is three times `WOBBLE_RADIANS` because a
flinch that does not clearly exceed the idle sway reads as nothing. A pest's
equivalent trigger is whatever `HIT_FLASH_DURATION` is already armed from.

WRITE THE TEST WITH `.claude/skills/assert-an-animation/SKILL.md`, and note the
suite's own precedent: cycle 86's surviving mutation was closed by pausing,
stepping and reading `_sway_pivot.rotation` — three commands, no screenshot.
A pest flinch is a node property, so it is on the cheap side of that split.

ACCEPTANCE: a damaged pest visibly deviates from its gait for a bounded time,
the deviation clearly exceeds the idle gait amplitude the way the plant's does,
and a headless test steps the pest and asserts the transform moved on damage and
returned after — never by reading a pixel.
close_reason: Closed

title: The ring on the road is still unnamed, and it is the first cue a player ever sees
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md, "New in cycle 138" third entry. PLAYER-FACING, and the half
of the user's report that did not get answered.

The report named two marks. Cycle 138 answered one -- the bar across the lane,
now taught by the fifth one-shot hint. The other is still unnamed by anything.

`SoleCoverMarks` (`game/sole_cover_marks.gd:227`) draws a small yellow ring on
every road cell the selected plant alone covers. It has a grammar row ("Small
solid ring, cell-sized, centred on a ROAD CELL", `game/OVERLAY_GRAMMAR.md:26`),
no legend row, and no hint.

IT IS THE CUE A PLAYER MEETS FIRST. It appears on the first click of the first
plant -- before the deferred bar (which now waits for a second gun,
`Game.DEFER_HINT_MIN_GUNS`), before the hatch, before anything.

THE DECISION THIS BEAD IS MOSTLY ABOUT: a sixth hint is the cheap answer and may
be the wrong one. The defer tip already fires on the second gun; a sole-cover tip
firing on the first would put two teaching lines on consecutive clicks, which is
the wallpaper `RunConfig.HINTS`' own header warns about -- and the message row
has one line. The alternative is the second legend page
(plant-tower-defense-xfbo), which teaches without spending the row at all but
only reaches a player who opens the notebook.

Note the asymmetry that makes the ring harder than the bar: the ring is drawn in
`SelectionMarker.MARKER_COLOR` and appears with the brackets, so a player has SOME
thread to pull -- it is visibly part of "the plant I clicked". The bar had none.
That is an argument for the legend and against a sixth hint, and it should be
made explicitly rather than assumed.

ACCEPTANCE: the ring is named by a surface a player can reach, and the close
records which route was taken and why the other was refused.
close_reason:
Shipped as a SIXTH ONE-SHOT HINT (RunConfig.HINT_SOLE_COVER, Hud.sole_cover_tip),
fired from _refresh through Game._offer_sole_cover_hint. Commit 6b2c14d.

WHY THE LEGEND ROW WAS REFUSED, which the acceptance asked for: on WIDTH, not on
the reasoning that was already on the record. The legend page is measurably full
at 294px of 300 and a seventh row prices at 340, so a row there costs the second
notebook page -- which is plant-tower-defense-xfbo, a separate item. The hint
also reaches a player who never opens the notebook and STILL leaves a permanent
card in the notebook via Hud.HINT_CARDS, so it buys both surfaces for the width
of neither.

THE BEAD'S FRAMING WAS OVERTAKEN, and this is the part worth carrying forward.
It said the decision was open. It was not: game/cue_legend.gd:134-139 had
already refused this cue a row, with a good argument -- the page teaches the
dashed ring ("on a plant nothing depends on") and the road rings are the same
node's positive case, so the concept was held to be on the page. That argument
lost to a person looking at the board. The note is amended in place rather than
deleted because HOW it failed generalises: the revisit condition it set itself
was "if row 4 gains an instance that is not SoleCoverMarks" -- a fact about the
drawing code -- and the condition that actually fired was a fact about a player.
A teaching decision cannot set its own trigger in the code it is about.

The bead's objection to a sixth hint (two teaching lines on consecutive clicks)
does not arise: the hint is level-triggered behind Hud.row_is_quiet(), so a busy
row leaves it owed rather than stacking a copy. game/game.gd:1463 anticipated
this bead by name -- "it is worth reading before adding a sixth hint."

Three tests in test_selftest.gd: the tip fires on the first selection onto a
quiet row with the real sentence in the real Label; a selection drawing no rings
leaves the one-shot unspent; and the sentence names a SHAPE and never a colour,
because the ring shares SelectionMarker.MARKER_COLOR with the brackets it
arrives with and colour is the one channel that cannot separate them.

Two budgets caught the change on the way through and are recorded in the verify
ledger row: the notebook hints page has its own 300px matte and the sixth card
overflowed it by 35px, and message_corpus_check named the new producer unpriced.

title: A hint fired from _refresh needs row_is_quiet, and only a symptom three files away says so
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md, "New in cycle 138" fourth entry, and this cycle paid for it.

`game/hud.gd:3220` (`row_is_quiet`) documents the rule and the failure exactly:
a LEVEL-triggered caller that posts into a busy row gets a false return, the next
`_refresh()` offers the same line again, and copies stack until
MESSAGE_QUEUE_MAX starts refusing them -- "a one-shot hint shown four times,
which is the wallpaper the whole one-shot mechanism exists to prevent".

Cycle 138 wrote the fifth hint without the guard anyway. It shipped 11 refused
messages into a realistic run before
`test_a_realistic_run_refuses_no_messages_and_evicts_none` caught it.

THAT TEST IS A GOOD GATE AND IT IS THE WRONG DISTANCE. It fires on the symptom,
three files from the cause, and its message is "A non-zero refusal here is a
caller stacking copies into a full queue" -- true, and it does not name the
caller. Finding which of the five hint sites was responsible took a read of all
of them.

THE POPULATION IS REAL, not a single instance. Two of the five spend_hint call
sites are level-triggered and both carry the guard: `game/game.gd:1774`
(`_maybe_teach_upgrading`) and `game/game.gd:1445` (`_offer_defer_hint`). The
other three are edge-triggered and correctly do not.

DESIGN QUESTION THE CHECKER HAS TO ANSWER, and it is why this is not trivial:
distinguishing level- from edge-triggered statically. Reachability from
`_refresh` is the honest proxy -- `_offer_road_hint` is called on SELECTION and
`_on_flight_ignored` on a signal, neither from `_refresh`. A call-graph walk from
`func _refresh` over same-file calls is enough for this file and should say so
rather than claiming more.

ACCEPTANCE: a `tools/` checker following
`.claude/skills/house-static-checker/SKILL.md` reports every `spend_hint(` call
site reachable from `_refresh` with no `row_is_quiet()` guard in the same
function, prints how many sites it classified either way, and has a fixture where
removing the guard makes it fail. It names the file and line the existing test
cannot.
close_reason: tools/hint_guard_check.py: parses game/game.gd, call-graph walks from func _refresh over same-file calls, finds every spend_hint( site, classifies level- vs edge-triggered by reachability, flags a level-triggered site with no row_is_quiet() guard in the same function. Real run: 5 spend_hint sites, 2 level-triggered (both guarded, one via a multi-hop call the bead's cited name for had since been renamed to _offer_dead_ground_hint), 3 edge-triggered, 0 findings -- confirms the known-safe shape, nothing new. --fixture proves it can fail (a guard-removed mutation flags exactly the mutated function; a guard-placed-after-the-call case also correctly fires). Verified: check_all clean (32 checkers discovered).

title: The grammar's derivation cannot see a Line2D cue, and that was reported once already
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md, "New in cycle 138" second entry. A SECOND identification of
something already written down in the repo and never acted on.

`game/cue_legend.gd:61-74` records it in full and ends "reported to whoever owns
OVERLAY_GRAMMAR.md rather than fixed here". That report has sat unread; cycle
138 rediscovered it from the player's side while answering "what are all these
artifacts in the lanes?".

THE CLAIM, confirmed by reading both files:
 - OVERLAY_GRAMMAR.md says its table is "derived from the draw calls rather than
   remembered" and records the recipe as
   `grep -n "draw_arc(\|draw_circle(\|draw_line(\|draw_rect(" game/*.gd`.
 - `Board.mark_dead_ground` and `Board.mark_deferred_road` paint Line2D CHILDREN
   and call none of those four. `game/board.gd:811` says why they had to: "a
   headless run paints no frame, so a `_draw()` here would be a cue no gate could
   ever see".
 - So the census misses exactly the two cues that were built to be gateable.
 - It is an INSTANCE gap, not a row gap. `placement_preview.gd`'s a6rf block has
   a "WHY NO NEW GRAMMAR ROW" section filing the deferred bar under the existing
   "straight line through a box = a STATE" row on purpose, because adding a row
   fails test_the_legend_names_as_many_shapes_as_the_grammar_documents. The
   table's Instances column lists only the two placement_preview draw calls.

WHY A CHECKER AND NOT AN EDIT: editing the Instances column fixes today and
leaves the recipe wrong, and the recipe is what the next cycle will run.
`.claude/skills/derive-the-list/SKILL.md` is the case exactly -- a hand-run grep
IS a list, and one keyed on an API rather than on an effect goes stale the moment
a cue changes renderer. `.claude/skills/house-static-checker/SKILL.md` is the
recipe for the tool, including the exit-code contract, the printed denominator,
the mandatory NOT COVERED line and the synthetic fixture that proves it can fail.

ACCEPTANCE: a `tools/` checker walks `game/*.gd` for BOTH shapes -- the four draw
calls and `Line2D.new()` assigned into a pool -- prints its own denominator, and
fails when a painter has no entry in the grammar table's Instances column. Its
fixture demonstrates a Line2D cue being caught, since that is the whole class the
grep cannot see. It joins check_all's derived set by declaring NOT COVERED.

Built tools/overlay_grammar_check.py walking both shapes (draw_* calls, Line2D.new() pooled into a member/array/dict) matched against the grammar table by function name OR file basename -- the file-name fallback is load-bearing, proven by mutation (dropping it false-positives both real board.gd instances, since the literal pool sites live in private _redraw_* helpers). Legend-parity test (test_the_legend_names_as_many_shapes_as_the_grammar_documents) confirmed still passing live since no doc edit was made. title: Buy legend width from the notebook's pager, since the page itself is measurably full
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md, "New in cycle 138" first entry. PLAYER-FACING.

The game draws 13 cues and teaches 6. `game/OVERLAY_GRAMMAR.md:67` says "Six of
the eleven"; the two board-drawn Line2D cues are not in that count and neither
is in the legend. `CueLegend.ROWS` (`game/cue_legend.gd:172`) is the six.

CONFIRMED that the page cannot take a seventh: OVERLAY_GRAMMAR.md's cycle-109
note prices row seven at 340px against 300px available, and
`CueLegend.rows_that_fit` (`game/cue_legend.gd:264`) is the function that says
so -- a row's whole ink is SWATCH_RADIUS above the centre plus
row_ink_below_center() under it, which is why cutting ROW_PITCH cannot buy one.

CONFIRMED the notebook is already a pager: `NotebookScreen.PAGES` is a list and
`game/notebook_page.gd:137` draws the page-position dot. So the 300px ceiling is
per PAGE. A second KIND_LEGEND page is width that already exists.

WHAT IT COSTS, read rather than guessed:
 - `page_for_kind` (`game/notebook_screen.gd:299`) returns the FIRST page of a
   kind by design, and its header says a second copy for KIND_LEGEND was "the
   obvious move and the wrong one". A second legend page needs a per-page
   answer, not a second lookup.
 - `legend_note_text()` reads `PAGES[page_for_kind(KIND_LEGEND)]["note"]`, so
   both pages would print the same note until that is split.
 - `CueLegend._build_labels` and `_draw` both iterate `ROWS` whole. They need a
   page window. `rows_that_fit(box_height)` already computes the window size and
   takes box_height as an ARGUMENT precisely to avoid naming NotebookScreen back
   -- so the page index has to be pushed in the same way.
 - `test_the_legend_names_as_many_shapes_as_the_grammar_documents` parses the
   grammar table and compares against `NotebookScreen.OVERLAY_GRAMMAR_SHAPES`
   (currently 11). Growing the taught set moves this.

DECIDE FIRST, and this is most of the item: which of the seven untaught cues go
on page two. The hatch has a written exemption (it teaches itself on placement).
The sole-cover ring does not and is the cue a player meets first.

ACCEPTANCE: a second legend page exists, shows rows the first does not, carries
its own note, and the pager reaches it; a test asserts no row appears on both
pages and that every ROWS entry appears on exactly one.
notes:
NOT BUILDING IT. The premise is falsified on its central claim, the decision it
would reverse was already taken with reasons, and the route those reasons named was
already shipped -- by a cycle that ran between this bead being filed and now.

FALSIFIED. The bead says "the two board-drawn Line2D cues are not in that count and
neither is in the legend". They ARE in the count. Grammar row 6 is exactly them:
game/cue_legend.gd:112 reads "BOARD DEAD-GROUND BARS and BOARD DEFERRED-ROAD BARS
(row 6)", and both are the Line2D cues -- game/board.gd:935 holds _dead_ground_marks
and game/board.gd:1079 names DEFERRED_ROAD_LAYER. Eleven grammar rows against
thirteen drawn cues is not two cues missing from the grammar; it is row 6 collapsing
several instances into one CHANNEL, which is what the grammar is organised by. So
"13 drawn, 6 taught, therefore buy width" was arithmetic over the wrong set.

SUPERSEDED. plant-tower-defense-4tt4 offered a second legend page as one of three
routes and cycle 148 declined all three -- game/cue_legend.gd:187, :194, "RAISE
NOTHING ... THIS PAGE IS COMPLETE, NOT FULL". It priced every untaught cue including
row 6, and row 6 is not declined for want of room. It is declined because a single
legend line teaches it WORST: four instances meaning four different things, and the
grammar defines the row by its channel rather than by a meaning, so a row honest to
all four is four rows. This bead asks to spend a page on the one cue the audit
already established a page cannot help.

AND THE NAMED ROUTE IS BUILT. That verdict ends "The right home for it is the hints
page or a mark-side tooltip, both of which carry a sentence per instance. Filed as
that, not as a legend row." Cycle 144 shipped precisely that for the deferred bar
under plant-tower-defense-0xhf, off a player asking what the artifacts in their
lanes were: RunConfig.HINT_DEFERRED_ROAD (game/run_config.gd:243), gated on
Game.DEFER_HINT_MIN_GUNS and Hud.row_is_quiet.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY LEFT, and it is not a legend page. Row 6 is two bars and cycle 144
named one. The DEAD-GROUND bar is still named by nothing: RunConfig.HINTS
(game/run_config.gd:259) holds six ids and grep finds no dead_ground in run_config.gd
or hud.gd at all. It is persistent and hover-free with nothing selected --
_refresh_dead_ground (game/game.gd:1381) falls back to the longest reach among
unlocked plants -- so a player meets diagonal bars on grass and the game never says
why. Filed as its own item, by the route the row-6 verdict named.

The layout facts the bead reports are all true and none of them is the constraint:
rows_that_fit (game/cue_legend.gd:328) does say a seventh row does not fit, PAGES is
a pager, and page_for_kind returning the first page of a kind is a real obstacle. A
correct cost estimate for work that should not happen.
