title: citation_check.py exits clean over bead citations it never read
description:
SOURCE: hit while filing plant-tower-defense-h4v1 and -n2wd on 2026-08-17. Logged as
[G-123] in log-devtools.md.

WHAT THE TOOL DOES NOW (verified 2026-08-17 by running it)

    $ python tools/citation_check.py
    citation_check: 298 citation(s) across 1 file(s), 298 resolved, 0 finding(s)

"1 file(s)" is kanban.md. The tool does not read beads at all. It was run immediately after
roughly twenty fresh file:line citations were written into three bead descriptions, and it
exited clean over every one of them, three of which were wrong: nettle.gd:309 (actual 308),
nettle.gd:319 (actual 326), chomp_flower.gd:436 (actual 438). Each was cited off a grep hit
on a doc comment rather than off the declaration it described. They were caught by hand with
sed -n 'Np' and fixed before the beads were finalised — but nothing in the toolchain was
going to catch them.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN A NORMAL COVERAGE HOLE. A clean exit from a checker named
citation_check is read as "the citations are checked". The tool's own NOT COVERED: line is
honest about what its resolver cannot prove — that a cited line SUPPORTS a claim — but says
nothing about WHICH FILES it read, which is the gap that actually bit. The
.claude/skills/bead-from-report skill requires file:line citations in every bead and this is
the only tool in the repo that looks like it would gate them.

Bead citations decay faster than kanban's, not slower: a bead is read cycles after it is
written, by someone who did not write it, and the whole premise of the skill is that a bead
is trusted BECAUSE it looks like a finding. A stale line number is exactly the decay the
skill's closing paragraph warns about ("would this sentence still be trusted if the reader
could not check it? Because they will not check it").

WHAT WOULD HAVE TO CHANGE

Two separable pieces, and the first is worth doing even if the second is refused:

1. Print the scanned source list. "citation_check: 298 citation(s) across 1 file(s)" should
   name the file. A reader cannot currently tell a clean run from an empty one without
   reading the script.

2. Add a mode that reads bead prose. The citations live in the description, design and notes
   fields of .beads/issues.jsonl — the same export tools/bead_prose_check.py already walks,
   so the file-walking half exists in the repo twice over and the resolver exists once. This
   is a source-list change plus a field extractor, not new machinery.

CONSTRAINTS
  * .beads/issues.jsonl is a passive export, not the source of truth (CLAUDE.md's beads
    block, and bead_prose_check.py's own NOT COVERED: line says the same). A bead updated
    but not exported is invisible to any checker reading it. Say so in the output rather
    than implying live coverage.
  * Closed issues should be advisory, not gating — bead_prose_check.py already draws this
    distinction ("0 finding(s) gating, 10 in closed issues (advisory)") and the same split
    is right here. A closed bead citing a line that has since moved is history, not debt.
  * Beads legitimately cite paths that no longer exist, and beads about DELETING something
    cite it precisely because it is going away. Whatever the failure mode, it must be
    waivable per-issue, the way bead_prose_check.py accepts a correction note as a waiver.
  * tools/g1j9 (Give tools/ a shared source blanker instead of five copies) is open and
    touches this neighbourhood; check it before adding a sixth copy of anything.
acceptance_criteria:
- citation_check.py names the files it scanned in its summary line, so a clean exit cannot be mistaken for coverage it does not have.
- A mode that resolves file:line citations in the description, design and notes fields of .beads/issues.jsonl, with open issues gating and closed ones advisory, matching bead_prose_check.py's split.
- A per-issue waiver path for a bead that deliberately cites something gone or going.
- The output states that it reads the JSONL export, not the Dolt DB, so an unexported update is invisible to it.
- Proof it works: point it at plant-tower-defense-h4v1 with one citation reverted to the wrong line number (nettle.gd:309 for 308) and confirm it goes red, then restore.
notes: POST-CLOSE, and the close itself is the evidence. Re-running the shipped --beads mode over this bead's own close reason dropped the bead count 468 -> 467 and three citations out of the denominator: the close contains the sentence "marker `citation-check: ok` anywhere in the bead's prose drops the whole bead", which was true and thereby made itself false. The waiver now requires the marker to OPEN ITS OWN LINE (BEAD_WAIVER_LINE), and --self-check case 5 is a bead that mentions the marker mid-sentence and must not be waived. Fixed in 629a566. The close reason above is left exactly as written -- it is the artefact that found the defect, and rewriting it would erase that.
close_reason:
SHIPPED, both pieces, commit 27c0cde.

ACCEPTANCE, clause by clause.

"Print the scanned source list by name" -- done. The line now reads

    citation_check: 880 citation(s) across 1 file(s) [kanban.md] + 468 bead(s),
    874 resolved, 0 finding(s)

and, when --beads is OFF but an export exists, it says so in the negative:

    NOT read: bead prose (.beads/issues.jsonl). Citations written into bead
    descriptions and close reasons are unchecked unless --beads is passed.

That second line is the half the bead did not ask for and is the one that would have
caught the original incident: the tool was not wrong, it was silent, and a reader
cannot tell "read one file and it was clean" from "read everything and it was clean"
without opening the script.

"Add a mode reading bead prose from .beads/issues.jsonl description/design/notes" --
done for the fields THAT EXIST. The export carries description and close_reason and
neither design nor notes; the keys are

    ['_type','assignee','close_reason','closed_at','comment_count','created_at',
     'created_by','dependency_count','dependent_count','description','id',
     'issue_type','owner','priority','started_at','status','title','updated_at']

so BEAD_PROSE_FIELDS is ("description", "close_reason"). close_reason was not in the
bead's list and is arguably the more important of the two: a close is where this
project puts its evidence, and a close citing a moved line is read as a record of what
was verified.

"the same export tools/bead_prose_check.py already walks, so the file-walking half
exists in the repo twice over and the resolver exists once" -- and it still exists
once. bead_sources() hands every bead ROOT/kanban.md as its citing path and calls the
SAME _resolve(); there is no second resolver and no sixth copy of anything. Checked
tools/g1j9 as the bead asked: it is about a shared source BLANKER (comment/string
masking), which this does not need -- bead prose is not source.

"say so in output rather than implying live coverage" -- done, printed on every --beads
run: "which is a PASSIVE EXPORT: a bead edited since the last export is not in it, so
this says the exported prose is clean, not that the tracker is."

"closed issues advisory not gating" -- done, and the fixture tests the routing rather
than the detection. A closed bead's findings print under their own heading and are
excluded from the exit code. Reason recorded in bead_sources(): closing a bead would
otherwise convert its citations into future gate failures nobody can clear without
rewriting the record.

"must be waivable per-issue like bead_prose_check.py's correction-note waiver" -- done,
marker `citation-check: ok` anywhere in the bead's prose drops the whole bead.

WHAT THE BEAD DID NOT ANTICIPATE, AND IT IS THE WHOLE RESULT.

The first working version reported

    citation_check: 362 citation(s) across 1 file(s) [kanban.md] + 468 bead(s),
    362 resolved, 0 finding(s)

Ten extra citations from 468 beads. bd stores description and close_reason as PLAIN
TEXT -- nothing renders them, so nothing rewards backticks -- and CITATION requires
them. Measured: 95 backticked against 495 unbackticked. The mode was reading one
citation in six and printing a clean sweep over an input set that was 84% invisible.

That is precisely the failure this repo's NOT COVERED contract exists to prevent,
arriving through the front door of a feature written to close a coverage gap. The only
thing that caught it was the denominator being implausible, and a denominator is
something a reader has to notice. So --self-check now notices instead: four cases, of
which three are about routing, and all three mutants were caught --

    gating always True   -> "SELFCHECK-closed gating=True, expected False"
    waiver disabled      -> "expected 2 sources (waived one dropped), got 3"
    PLAIN needs backtick -> "no citation extracted from unbackticked prose -- this is
                            the 95-of-590 bug returning"

It is cycle 77's lesson a third time, and citation_check.py's own comment above BARE
already stated it: a convention a document grows is invisible to a tool written from
the outside. PLAIN applies to bead sources only; loosening the markdown path would
start matching prose.

ONE THING BEYOND THE BEAD, without which it would have shipped inert. check_all.py's
run_one(name, []) passes no arguments, so an opt-in mode on a pooled checker never runs
in the pool. Added CHECKER_ARGS = {"citation_check.py": ["--beads"]}, plus a guard: a
key naming a checker the pool does not run is exit 2, because a coverage flag that
silently does nothing is the same class of defect the flags exist to fix.

RESULT ON THE REAL CORPUS: 880 citations, 874 resolved, 0 gating findings, 5
advisories -- and all five are correct behaviour, not noise. Three cite log.md, which
lives outside this repo; two cite .fixture_h613.gd, cycle 124's deliberately-deleted
fixture. Nothing was rewritten to make them go away.

NOT DONE, and it is the thing that motivated the bead. The three citations that were
actually WRONG (nettle.gd:309 for 308, nettle.gd:319 for 326, chomp_flower.gd:436 for
438) all RESOLVE -- the files have those lines, they just say something else. Resolve
mode cannot see that by construction; --snapshot/--against is what sees it, and bead
targets had never been snapshotted. They are now: .devtools/citations.json holds 619
distinct targets from 874 resolved citations, so from cycle 127 a bead citation that
drifts is caught the same way a kanban one is. Those three specific ones live only in
this bead, quoted as the evidence FOR it, which is exactly what the waiver marker is
for -- left alone.

VERIFIED: tier (f) tooling-only, no res:// file changed. --self-check plus three
mutants, check_all 19 of 19 clean, --beads --against clean (0 drifted, 308 new).
Ledger row 27c0cde^ recorded before the commit.

title: A checker for unresolved absence claims, since 123 of 139 were not reached
description:
SOURCE: plant-tower-defense-g1o4's close reason, cycle 104. It says this in as many
words: "The scan that found them is a throwaway; if this is worth doing again it should
be tools/ code with the house contract on it."

WHAT HAPPENED: -g1o4 asked for at least 15 open beads to have their absence claims
resolved against the code. Sixteen were. The shortlist came from a scratchpad Python
scan that ranked open beads by how many absence-shaped assertions each description makes
(nothing / never / does not / has no / there is no / exactly N / nowhere / no test),
tie-broken by priority.

THE NUMBER IS THE REASON THIS BEAD EXISTS: **139 open beads carry at least one absence
claim.** Sixteen were resolved. 123 were not reached -- 6 per cent of the exposure -- and
the tool that could find them again was deleted with the scratchpad.

Two of the sixteen were beads whose ENTIRE premise had become false and which were
therefore closed without any code being written (-lk0n, -2ker). That is the payoff: a
bead read at face value costs an implementer their first hour, and one of the two would
have had somebody building a boss that already has 80 health, two sprites and 26 wave
appearances.

ASK: `tools/bead_claim_check.py`, written to `.claude/skills/house-static-checker/SKILL.md`
-- stdlib only, parallel-safe, exit 0/1/2, a printed denominator, a mandatory NOT COVERED
line, a fixture it has been watched fail against, and its mutations in the docstring.

DESIGN NOTES, learned from the throwaway rather than guessed:
  * It is ADVISORY, not gating. The correct response to most of the 139 is "yes, still
    true" -- see house-static-checker's own section on why a permanently-red gate is worse
    than no gate. Report and exit 0; `--strict` may gate.
  * Rank, do not filter. The value is working the densest first and being able to say how
    many were not reached, which is exactly what the acceptance below asks it to print.
  * The waiver is the resolution note, the same mechanism `bead_prose_check.py` already
    uses: a bead whose notes record a verdict against the code stops being listed. That
    keeps the record of the check where the next reader will find it.
  * A citation count per bead is worth printing beside the claim count -- a claim with a
    `file:line` is checkable in seconds and one without is not, and the two should not
    look alike in the output.

NOT COVERED, and it must say so: this can only find the SHAPE of an absence claim in
prose. It cannot tell whether the claim is true -- that is a human reading the code -- and
it cannot see a claim phrased without any of its needles.

ACCEPTANCE: one command lists open beads carrying unresolved absence claims, ranked, with
both the claim count and the citation count per bead; a bead carrying a resolution note is
excluded; the run prints how many carry claims and how many were excluded, so the
denominator is visible; and a fixture demonstrates it firing and not firing.
close_reason:
DONE. tools/bead_claim_check.py, and it joined check_all automatically via the contract
marker -- 15 of 15 checkers before, 16 of 16 after, no registration edit anywhere.

THE NUMBERS IT NOW PRINTS, which is the whole point of the bead:

  436 issue(s) parsed -- 164 open, 272 closed and NOT scanned
  143 of 164 open bead(s) carry at least one absence claim; 13 waived by a resolution note
  130 UNRESOLVED bead(s) carry 360 claim(s) and 194 citation(s); 76 of them cite nothing

76 of 130 cite nothing at all. That is the number an implementer pays for, and it was
invisible before.

The waiver is the resolution note, the same mechanism bead_prose_check already uses, so the
16 beads cycle 104 resolved by hand drop off without a second convention.

THE FINDING OF THE LANE IS A DEFECT IN ITS OWN POSITIVE CONTROL. It ships a control line
asserting the waived beads still match a needle outside their note -- and mutation B
(deleting the `nothing` class entirely) left it GREEN at 13 of 13, against the prediction.
The control could not fail. So it now prints its own STRENGTH beside itself ("the weakest
waived bead relies on 2 distinct needle classes, so this line cannot go red until that many
are lost at once"), and gained `--self-test`: 14 hand-written known-in/known-out cases that
ship in the file and go red on 7 of the 9 mutations. That is house-static-checker's actual
prescription -- a direct unit test of the transform -- rather than the statistic over the
real corpus I reached for first.

Nine mutations, each measured on three corpora, with the numbers recorded rather than the
verdicts. Two are worth carrying: mutation G (removing the citation lookbehind) left the
REAL corpus unchanged at 194 and only the fixture and self-test caught it -- a regression
the production data cannot see; and mutation D (`FIELDS = ("description",)`) moved claims
and citations UP, because it silently disables the waiver too, which is the kind of result
that reads as an improvement if you only look at one number.

The fixture found three bugs reading did not: the bare `:NN` citation pattern matched
`9:00`, overlapping needles counted "there is no test" three times (inflating exactly the
beads the ranking puts on top), and two must-NOT-fire cases fired on their own titles.

That last one is unfixable and is in the NOT COVERED line: this cannot tell a claim from a
QUOTATION of one, which is why -htnt, -thoj and -9vq6 -- beads about absence claims -- rank
high. Also excluded deliberately, with the counts that decided it: `is not` (71 hits),
`cannot` (56), `without` (35), `the only` (30), each of which roughly doubles the set into
noise on this corpus.

Advisory, exit 0 always; --strict exits 1; a missing file exits 2; a corpus of only-closed
issues exits 2 rather than reporting a clean zero.

title: The Nettle's sting is a 0.15s squash and reads as a jiggle, not as a sting
description:
SOURCE: user report, 2026-08-17, verbatim: "The red plant also needs a better animation,
at the moment it just jiggles."

WHICH PLANT. Read as the Nettle, and the identification is worth showing rather than
asserting, because two plants read as red. Sampling the authored sources:
  * art_src/nettle.svg is fill #FF6600 and #FF9C3C over stroke #C25000 — orange-red, and
    the only plant in the catalogue with no green anywhere in its body except one #1F8A4C
    stem stroke.
  * art_src/chomp_flower.svg is #AF392D and #7A2820 — a darker, deeper red.
The report says "also", after a sentence about the Chomp, so it means the other one. If a
playtest shows the Chomp was meant, this bead is wrong about its subject and should be
re-pointed before any work starts — but the described behaviour matches the Nettle and does
not match the Chomp, which lunges rather than jiggling.

WHAT THE GAME DOES NOW (verified 2026-08-17 by reading game/nettle.gd; static read, no live
session)

"Just jiggles" is close but not exact, and the difference is the useful part. Nettle's sting
has three visual components, not one:
  1. _sting_twitch() (nettle.gd:308) tweens _sprite.scale to STING_SQUASH = (1.16, 0.86)
     and _sprite.skew to _sting_lean, both over 0.05s, then both back over 0.10s. Total
     0.15s. The skew is signed and aimed — sting_lean_skew() is a pure static and
     nettle.gd:73 argues for it explicitly: "A shear has a sign, and the sign is the target."
  2. _spawn_prickle_spark() (:326) builds a Node2D of SPARK_SPOKES Line2D spokes fanned
     across SPARK_FAN_RADIANS at the victim's position, scales it 0.55 -> 1.15 while fading
     alpha to 0, and frees itself off the end of its own tween.
  3. Sfx.NETTLE_STING, a pitched variant of the shared soft impact (:229).

So there IS aim and there IS a burst. What there is not is DURATION or FORCE: the plant's
entire contribution is a 0.15s symmetric-ish squash with a small shear, which is the same
grammar as Mint's idle breathing pulse (mint.gd:86) and only slightly sharper. Two of this
file's own comments concede the underlying problem in advance — nettle.gd:63 and :229 both
say that without extra evidence "the only sign a Nettle acted is a hit flash
indistinguishable from a kernel landing from three cells away". The squash and the spark
were the answer to that, and the report is saying they did not go far enough.

Worth knowing: the Nettle is a conditional plant. plant_catalog.gd:123 — it "stings only
pests the mutations changed — armoured, winged, hungry — and lets the rest walk past. Dead
weight until wave 8". So the animation is not just decoration; it is the readout for WHY
this plant fired at that bug and not the one beside it. That is a design lever this bead
should probably use rather than only making the existing twitch bigger.

WHAT WOULD HAVE TO CHANGE, AND WHAT IT WILL BREAK

test/unit/test_combat.gd:6331 sets the pattern, naming Nettle twice:

    "All of it lives past GardenTheme.animations_enabled(), which is false for every test
     in this suite by construction, so the composition was pulled out into pure statics
     (ChompFlower.lunge_offset, Nettle.sting_lean_skew, Nettle.spark_spoke_ends) and
     recorded into fields written ABOVE the gate (_bite_lunge, _sting_lean, _spark_ends).
     ... deleting the composition from the attack goes red instead of silently aiming at
     the origin."

Constraints an implementer will otherwise discover by failing:
  * Both cosmetic paths sit behind GardenTheme.animations_enabled(), false headless. Any new
    animation content must be a pure static recorded into a field written above the gate, or
    test_dir cannot reach it at all.
  * The suite drives the real _sting() path and asserts the recorded _sting_lean and
    _spark_ends. Changing how the lean or the fan is composed must keep those fields written
    above the gate or those tests go red — which is the tripwire working, not a nuisance.
  * Channel ownership, stated at nettle.gd:75-80: rotation belongs to Plant's idle sway on
    _sway_pivot, scale belongs to event tweens, position now belongs to Chomp's lunge, and
    skew was taken as "a fourth free channel". A dramatically bigger sting needs a channel,
    and all four named ones are spoken for. This is the real design constraint and it should
    be settled before code is written.
  * _spawn_prickle_spark parents the spark to the Nettle and frees it off its own tween
    specifically so an uprooted plant takes it with it — nettle.gd:322 ties this to the
    in-tree node growth that devtools performance watches. More or longer-lived particles
    must keep that property; check with performance --by-type.
  * Any new SVG frame needs art_src/STYLE.md compliance, a render through
    tools/render_svg.gd to 1x and retina, a test_sprite_style.gd EXPECTED_SIZE row (:38,
    which already carries "nettle": 64), a clean svg_style_check.py, and a headless import
    pass before the next lint or test run.
design:
The channel question has to be answered first, because it constrains everything else.
nettle.gd:75-80 documents that sway owns rotation on _sway_pivot, event tweens own
_sprite.scale, Chomp's lunge owns _sprite.position, and this class already took skew as
"a fourth free channel". A dramatically larger sting either shares one of those with an
explicit hand-off, or it lives outside the sprite entirely — in a child node, a shader, or
drawn in _draw(). The child-node route is what _spawn_prickle_spark already does and is the
cheapest way to add a lot of motion without renegotiating ownership of anything.

Directions, roughly by payoff per unit of risk:

1. GIVE THE STING A WIND-UP. Right now it is 0.05s out and 0.10s back with no anticipation.
   A brief lean AWAY before the shear toward the target is the oldest trick there is and
   costs one more tween step on a channel this class already owns. Cheap, no art, and it is
   usually most of what "it just jiggles" means.

2. MAKE THE SPINES THE ANIMATION. The plant is a nettle; the spines are the mechanic. The
   spark fan is currently drawn at the VICTIM. Firing visible spines FROM the plant TO the
   victim would give the sting travel and duration, and would read at a glance as this plant
   rather than as a generic squash. spark_spoke_ends() is already a pure static returning
   the geometry, so the testable content mostly exists; it would be re-aimed rather than
   invented.

3. SAY WHY IT FIRED. The Nettle only stings mutated pests (plant_catalog.gd:123) and lets
   everything else walk past. A player watching it ignore a stream of bugs and then twitch
   at one has no cue explaining the difference. An animation that reacts to the mutation —
   or a visible bristle/alert state while a valid target is in range — turns the animation
   into a readout for the plant's actual rule. This is the highest-value option and the
   largest; it may deserve its own bead once the cheap ones land.

4. LONGER AND SHARPER. Extending the 0.15s and deepening STING_SQUASH is the obvious move
   and is listed last on purpose. It makes the existing gesture more emphatic without making
   it more legible, and the constant carries a header arguing for its current value.

Whichever is chosen, keep the aim. nettle.gd:73's "a shear has a sign, and the sign is the
target" is the property the tests pin and the one thing about the current animation that is
already right.
acceptance_criteria:
DECISION (record on this issue before writing code):
- Which channel the bigger sting uses, given sway owns rotation, event tweens own scale, Chomp owns position, and this class already took skew (nettle.gd:75-80).
- Confirmation from a playtest that the Nettle, not the Chomp, is the plant the report meant.

CODE (this bead closes on these):
- The sting reads as a sting rather than a jiggle, and the aim survives: sting_lean_skew and spark_spoke_ends stay pure statics recorded into fields written above the animations_enabled() gate, per test_combat.gd:6331.
- The existing Nettle seam tests stay green unchanged, or are updated with a stated reason.
- python tools/run_tests.py clean; if any SVG is touched, svg_style_check.py clean, a test_sprite_style.gd EXPECTED_SIZE row present, and a headless import pass run first.
- devtools performance --by-type shows no in-tree node growth from added particles across a wave (the self-freeing property nettle.gd:326 relies on).

AUDIT (needs a live game; expected to land after the code — this bead is not unbuilt while only this is outstanding):
- Screenshots or a bridge check of a sting against targets on the left and on the right, confirming the gesture still points at the victim.
notes: Reporter's own words: 'The red plant also needs a better animation, at the moment it just jiggles.' Identification of the Nettle is by SVG palette (#FF6600/#C25000) plus the 'also' following a Chomp sentence — shown in the description rather than assumed, because chomp_flower.svg is also red. Filed alongside plant-tower-defense-h4v1 (Chomp) from the same report; different plants, different tests, deliberately not one bead.
close_reason: Sting redesigned as thrust+hold+slow withdrawal; verified frozen on the running game; own STING_* pair on Nettle

title: A pest in a Chomp's mouth is untouched and still walking until the instant it dies
description:
SOURCE: user report, 2026-08-17, verbatim: "the attack animation for the chomp flower
doesn't really look like it's taking bites out of the bugs, improve the animation
dramatically."

Read plant-tower-defense-81g9 FIRST. It already covers one piece of this (an open-jaw SVG
at the moment of the bite) and is deliberately scoped to the FLOWER. This bead is the other
half and is the one that matches the report: nothing is ever taken out of the BUG.

WHAT THE GAME DOES NOW (verified 2026-08-17 by reading game/chomp_flower.gd and
game/pest.gd; no live session, so every claim below is a static one)

The flower's side of the bite is already substantial, which is worth saying plainly so
nobody rebuilds it:
  * ChompFlower._bite() (chomp_flower.gd:438) plays Sfx.CHOMP_BITE, calls _held.flash_hit()
    once, records _bite_lunge from the pure static lunge_offset(), then tweens
    _sprite.position by 7px toward the meal and _sprite.scale to (1.18, 0.82) over 0.06s,
    recovering over ~0.13s.
  * _grab() (:335) immediately calls _show_eating_sprite(), and _chew() (:350) swaps to
    chomp_flower_eating_late.svg once chew_progress() passes LATE_BITE_THRESHOLD. So the
    flower already has THREE textures and uses all three.
  * _draw() (:401) sweeps an orange chew ring around the flower for the whole meal.

The PEST's side is where the report lands, and it is empty:
  * Pest._physics_process (pest.gd:845-854) calls _gait(delta) BEFORE the held guard, then
    returns. The comment there says this is deliberate — "a pest in a Chomp's mouth is still
    a live creature". The consequence is that a bug being eaten keeps running its walk
    cycle on the spot inside the jaws for the entire chew.
  * The pest receives exactly ONE piece of bite feedback in its whole life inside the mouth:
    the single flash_hit() at :448, at the instant of the grab. Nothing after.
  * Its scale, texture, modulate and rotation are untouched for the duration. It is fully
    intact right up to the frame _chew() calls meal.kill(Pest.DEATH_BITTEN) (:358), at which
    point it swaps to a squashed corpse sprite.

So the picture on screen is: a bug walks in place, unblemished, while a flower squashes at
it once and a ring drains; then the whole bug vanishes into a corpse. There is no repeated
bite, no damage accruing on the victim, no part of the bug going away. The report is
accurate and specific: nothing is being taken out of the bug, because nothing in the code
takes anything out of the bug.

WHAT WOULD HAVE TO CHANGE, AND WHAT IT WILL BREAK

test/unit/test_combat.gd:6331 states the pattern any new animation here must follow, and it
is not optional:

    "All of it lives past GardenTheme.animations_enabled(), which is false for every test
     in this suite by construction, so the composition was pulled out into pure statics
     (ChompFlower.lunge_offset, Nettle.sting_lean_skew, Nettle.spark_spoke_ends) and
     recorded into fields written ABOVE the gate (_bite_lunge, _sting_lean, _spark_ends).
     ... deleting the composition from the attack goes red instead of silently aiming at
     the origin."

Concretely, the constraints an implementer will otherwise discover by failing:
  * Every cosmetic tween in this class sits behind GardenTheme.animations_enabled(), which
    is FALSE headless. Any new animation whose content is only expressible as a tween is
    untestable in test_dir by construction. Extract the content (which direction, how many
    bites, where on the victim) into a pure static and record it into a field set above the
    gate, exactly as _bite_lunge is.
  * test_a_headless_chomp_bite_queues_no_lunge_tween (test_combat.gd:6425) asserts a headless
    bite queues NO tween and leaves the sprite home. A new animation that queues outside the
    gate turns this red, correctly.
  * test_a_chomps_bite_records_a_lunge_toward_the_meal (:6383) and
    test_a_chomps_lunge_points_at_the_meal_from_every_side (:6342) pin the existing lunge
    vector and its LUNGE_DISTANCE length. Retiming or re-aiming the lunge must update both.
  * chew_arc_end / the chew ring is asserted monotonic at test_combat.gd:5260-5290. If bite
    beats are derived from chew_progress(), they share that clock.
  * Channel ownership is documented in Plant._sway_pivot and restated at chomp_flower.gd:464:
    idle sway and flinch own _sway_pivot, event tweens own _sprite.scale, the lunge owns
    _sprite.position. A fourth channel needs a fourth home or it will fight one of these.
  * Any new SVG needs an art_src/ source following art_src/STYLE.md (64x64, top-down,
    outline a darker shade of the fill, sampled palette), a render through
    tools/render_svg.gd to 1x and retina, a row in test_sprite_style.gd EXPECTED_SIZE
    (:38), a clean tools/svg_style_check.py, and a "godot --headless --path . --import"
    pass before the next lint or test run.
  * Pest-side changes must survive release(): Pest.kill() calls held_by.release()
    (pest.gd:1089) and a Chomp destroyed mid-chew releases its meal UNHARMED by design
    (pest.gd:851 comment, _ever_engaged). Any visual damage applied to the victim has to be
    undone on that path, or a released pest walks away visibly half-eaten and at full health.
design:
The report's phrase is the design brief: "taking bites OUT OF the bugs". Three candidate
mechanisms, cheapest first. They compose; they are not alternatives.

1. REPEAT THE BITE. Today one meal is one bite. chew_seconds_for() runs 0.65x to 1.0x of
   the pest's own chew_seconds, so a meal lasts long enough for several. Drive N discrete
   bite beats off chew_progress() rather than one at _grab, each with its own lunge, squash,
   sprite swap and Sfx.CHOMP_BITE. A pure static bite_beats(progress, level) -> int is the
   testable content and fits the pattern test_combat.gd:6331 demands. This alone probably
   closes most of the report, and needs no new art.

2. MAKE THE VICTIM SHOW IT. The bug is currently untouched until it dies. Candidates in
   rising cost: flash_hit() on every beat instead of once; shrink the pest's scale toward
   the flower as the chew progresses; tug the pest's position a few px toward the flower's
   mouth on each beat so it is visibly being pulled in; a torn/partial pest texture past a
   threshold, the same trick chomp_flower_eating_late.svg already uses on the flower. Note
   the release() constraint in the description — whatever this does must be undone when a
   Chomp is destroyed mid-chew.

3. STOP THE WALK CYCLE. pest.gd:845 deliberately runs _gait() while held, and the comment
   defends it. That decision was made for a pest chewing a bed, where it is right. For a
   pest clamped in a jaw it is what makes the bug look unbothered. Consider gating _gait on
   held_by specifically rather than reverting the comment's intent — a struggle animation
   would be better than either, and is the same channel.

Order matters. Do 1 first and look at it; the report may be satisfied before 2 and 3 are
worth their cost, and 2's art is the expensive part. Coordinate with
plant-tower-defense-81g9, which owns the open-jaw frame on the flower — if that lands
first, mechanism 1 gets a much better bite for free, and the two beads should not both be
editing _bite() at once.
acceptance_criteria:
CODE (this bead closes on these):
- A meal produces more than one visible bite. The count is derived by a pure static that test_dir can assert with no running game and no renderer, following the pattern test_combat.gd:6331 sets out.
- The held pest changes visibly over the chew — at minimum a hit flash per bite beat rather than one at the grab.
- A headless test asserting a Chomp destroyed mid-chew releases its meal with every victim-side visual change undone (the unharmed-release invariant at pest.gd:851).
- The existing pins stay green unchanged or are updated with a stated reason: test_a_headless_chomp_bite_queues_no_lunge_tween, test_a_chomps_bite_records_a_lunge_toward_the_meal, test_a_chomps_lunge_points_at_the_meal_from_every_side, and the chew_arc_end monotonicity checks.
- python tools/run_tests.py clean; if any SVG is touched, svg_style_check.py clean, a test_sprite_style.gd EXPECTED_SIZE row added, and a headless import pass run first.

AUDIT (expected to need a live game, and expected to land AFTER the code — do not treat this bead as unbuilt while only this is outstanding):
- A /verify Phase 4 bridge check or screenshot pair over one full chew, confirming the bug visibly loses ground rather than standing intact.
notes: Reporter's own words, kept because they name the defect better than the analysis does: 'doesn't really look like it's taking bites out of the bugs'. Related: plant-tower-defense-81g9 owns the flower-side open-jaw frame; these two beads both touch ChompFlower._bite() and should not be worked concurrently.
close_reason: Pest side implemented: three discrete bites, flash + shrink per bite, corpse keeps it. Verified live on a real beetle. 81g9 (open-jaw SVG) remains separate.

title: The top bar's readouts are four plain Labels on a flat slab and read as one undifferentiated line
description:
Seeds / Wave+threat / Lives / Compost are built by _add_stat() (game/hud.gd:1057) as bare Labels: a font size, a colour, clip_text, and a hairline rule underneath (_readout_rule). Nothing else. On screen that is four strings of near-identical weight sitting on one flat INK ColorRect, so the row has no visual hierarchy — the number a player is scanning for reads the same as the word labelling it, and the four readouts read the same as each other despite being four different kinds of thing (a currency you spend, a clock you cannot stop, a life total, a bankable surplus).

What already exists and should be preserved rather than rediscovered:
- Every readout carries a hard clipped width budget (SEEDS_LABEL_WIDTH, WAVE_LABEL_WIDTH, LIVES_LABEL_WIDTH, COMPOST_LABEL_WIDTH), summed against the bar in test_the_stats_row_budget_fits_the_bar, with roughly 19px of total slack. WORST_CASE_TEXT (:95) pins the longest string each can hold. Styling that adds a StyleBox with content margins spends that slack and will fail those tests — which is the point of them.
- The wave readout already carries a live threat tint eased through _ease_threat_tint, and a colourblind-safe ramp. Any restyle has to keep both legible.
- The compost readout is deliberately 20px against the others' 26 (STAT_FONT_SIZE), baseline-aligned by vertical_alignment. That size difference is the only hierarchy the row currently has.
- The rule under each readout is a ColorRect child of the Label so it costs zero width; the same trick is available to anything else added here.

Related, and worth reading before starting: plant-tower-defense-i5ny (collapse the top bar's three hand-lists of readouts into one table) is the structural version of this work. Doing that first would make this a change in one place instead of four.
design:
The cheap wins that do not touch the width budget, roughly in order of payoff per px:
- Split label from value typographically — smaller/dimmer caps for 'Seeds', full weight for the number — so the eye lands on what changed.
- Give each readout an icon glyph rather than a word where one exists (a seed, a heart); SeedGlyph already exists in game/seed_glyph.gd.
- Vary the rule under each readout by what it measures instead of drawing four identical hairlines.
- Consider whether the flat INK slab wants the same paper treatment the rest of the game uses — GardenTheme.paper_panel() is what the notebook, pause card, run summary and now the board frame are all printed on, and the top bar is the one surface still refusing it.
Prefer per-node theme overrides, as the rest of the HUD does: the HUD deliberately refuses the shared Theme because it would repaint the plant and packet buttons it sizes in code.
acceptance_criteria:
- The stats row has a stated visual hierarchy: a player can name which element they scan first.
- test_the_stats_row_budget_fits_the_bar and test_no_readout_clips_its_own_worst_case still pass unchanged — no readout may buy width from the row's ~19px of slack.
- The threat tint and the colourblind-safe ramp remain legible on the restyled wave readout.
- Before/after screenshots at the same window size on this issue.
- devtools findings reports 0 NEW ui_layout findings.
close_reason: Cycle 109; merged and verified live at runtime (weight hierarchy on the bar, mark+outline on an armed uproot read frozen)

title: Artifacts around the board's page frame — corner kinks and tile seams
description:
Visible styling artifacts around the edge of the playfield. Two independent suspects, both in game/board.gd, and they should be confirmed by screenshot before either is 'fixed':

1. CORNER DISCONTINUITY IN THE WOBBLE. page_edge_points() (game/board.gd:311) offsets every sampled point along the inward normal of the side it belongs to: inward = [DOWN, LEFT, UP, RIGHT]. Each corner is emitted exactly once, carrying only its own side's normal, while the adjacent side's nearest sample carries a normal rotated 90 degrees. At a corner the wobble therefore jumps direction discontinuously instead of easing round, and PAGE_WOBBLE_PX = 2.0 on a 7px line with LINE_JOINT_ROUND makes that jump a visible notch or spur at all four corners. The seam where the loop closes (out.append(out[0]) at :337) is a second candidate at the top-left specifically: begin_cap_mode and end_cap_mode are both LINE_CAP_ROUND, so two round caps stack on the same point over an antialiased line and can read as a blob.

2. TILE SEAMS. _build_tiles() (:225) places 64px Kenney sprites on exact 64px centres, but stretch/mode=canvas_items with aspect=expand means the whole canvas is scaled by a non-integer factor at most window sizes. With default texture filtering that samples across the atlas/texture boundary and produces hairline seams between tiles — most visible at the board perimeter where grass meets the cream page. This suspect shares a root cause with plant-tower-defense-0jye.

The frame is drawn between the tiles and the pressure overlay (_ready(), :175) and covers PAGE_EDGE_WIDTH + GardenTheme.BORDER = 9px of playable ground per side by design, so any fix must not widen it — the outer cells are buildable.
design:
Confirm first, with devtools screenshot --region cropped to one corner at a known window size, and compare against the same corner at an integer scale. That distinguishes suspect 1 (present at every scale) from suspect 2 (present only at non-integer scales).

For the corner kink: sample the wobble against a normal interpolated across the corner, or drop the wobble amplitude to zero in a short window either side of each corner, or round the corners of the box so there is no 90-degree normal flip to bridge. page_wobble() is already a pure static function with tests asserting bounded amplitude and loop closure, so a corner-continuity assertion belongs beside them.
For the seams: texture_filter = TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST on the tile sprites, or a CanvasGroup, or resolve the scaling question in plant-tower-defense-0jye first.
acceptance_criteria:
- A before screenshot on this issue naming which of the two suspects is actually producing the artifact (or both).
- No visible notch, spur, or blob at any of the four board corners or at the loop's closing seam.
- No hairline seam between tiles at the window sizes the game actually ships at.
- The frame still covers no more than 9px of ground per side — assert board_size() and the frame's bounding box are unchanged.
- A test beside the existing page_wobble tests asserting the edge path has no direction discontinuity at the corners.
close_reason: Both suspects refuted/corrected by measurement; refutation pinned as a test. Remaining seam needs a device-pixel screenshot the bridge cannot take - see commit 87a4642.

title: The template-build guard in dev_tools.gd is harness-managed and one refresh from vanishing
description:
SOURCE: cycle 103, found while merging. Filed because the patch is CORRECT and the
risk is that it silently disappears.

WHAT EXISTS: `addons/godot_selftest/dev_tools.gd` carries a local patch gating the
bus and the entry_hook on `OS.has_feature("template")`:

  _passive = _is_script_run() or (OS.has_feature("template")
      and not _has_cmdline_flag("--devtools-force"))

plus the `_has_cmdline_flag` helper it needs. It fixes a real shipped-build defect
-- the entry_hook that skips the title screen for /verify was skipping it for
every itch.io player, so the web build opened straight onto the board. That is
recorded in log-devtools.md as [G-120], reported upstream as
godot-selftest-harness#58.

THE RISK, verified rather than assumed: `dev_tools.gd` IS in
`addons/godot_selftest/.harness_manifest.json` -- checked by loading the manifest
and searching it, not by guessing from the path. CLAUDE.md's own harness section
says everything under `addons/` is regenerated by `/scaffold-godot-harness` and an
edit there is silently lost on the next refresh. The plugin listing already
reports a newer harness on this machine (0.60.0) than this project runs (0.38.0),
so a refresh is a normal thing to do and would revert this without a word.

The failure mode is the bad one: the game would go on building and deploying, the
patch would be gone, and the only symptom is that players land on the board
instead of the title screen -- which is exactly the defect that took a real
itch.io deploy to notice in the first place. No gate can see it. `lint`, the
suite and `findings` all pass either way, because in the EDITOR build the patched
and unpatched code do the same thing.

ASK, cheapest sufficient thing first:
1. A test or a checker that fails if the guard is absent from `dev_tools.gd`.
   `tools/` has the precedent for reading a source file and asserting a token is
   present -- test_selftest.gd already does exactly this for
   `SIMULTANEOUS_PEST_CEILING` via FileAccess.get_file_as_string. A four-line
   check that the file contains `OS.has_feature("template")` would turn a silent
   revert into a red gate.
2. Then decide the real disposition: keep re-applying after every refresh, or
   wait for #58 to land upstream and pin the harness version that carries it.
   Note which in the bead when it is known.

ACCEPTANCE: something fails when the template guard is removed from
`dev_tools.gd`; demonstrated by removing it, watching the gate go red, and putting
it back.
close_reason:
DONE. A silent revert of the template guard now goes red.

WHAT WAS AT RISK: `addons/godot_selftest/dev_tools.gd` gates the bus and the
entry_hook on `OS.has_feature("template")`, fixing a defect that took a real
itch.io deploy to notice -- the hook that skips the title screen for /verify was
skipping it for every player, so the web build opened straight onto the board.

The file IS harness-managed. Verified by loading
`addons/godot_selftest/.harness_manifest.json` and searching it, not by guessing
from the path. `/scaffold-godot-harness` regenerates it, a newer harness (0.60.0)
is already on this machine than the project runs (0.38.0), so a refresh is an
ordinary thing to do -- and the lane working tools/ this cycle independently
noticed the file's recorded sha has ALREADY drifted from its manifest.

THE TEST READS SOURCE, WHICH IS NORMALLY THE WRONG SHAPE, and the justification is
written into it: there is no behaviour to read. `OS.has_feature("template")` is
false in an editor build whatever the code says, so a run with the guard and a run
without it agree on every observable. Lint, the suite and `findings` all pass
either way. The text is the only witness there is.

WATCHED IT GO RED FIRST, per house-static-checker's rule that green on a first run
means nothing: replacing the feature test with `false` fails with the message that
names this bead and says what an exported build would do. Restored; `addons/` is
unchanged in the diff.

It also asserts `--devtools-force` survives, so the patch stays a GATE rather than
becoming a wall that makes driving a real export impossible.

The bead offered two options and asked for the cheapest sufficient one first. This
is it -- a test, not a checker, because the question is about one known string in
one known file and `tools/` gains nothing from carrying it.

STILL OPEN, and deliberately not answered here: the bead's second half, whether to
keep re-applying after every refresh or to pin the harness version that carries
the fix upstream (godot-selftest-harness#58). That is a decision about this
project's harness policy, not a defect, and it now has a tripwire holding the line
while it waits.

705/705, 14585 assertions.

title: launch --snapshot-userstate did not restore, and quit did not say so
description:
SOURCE: [G-122] in log-devtools.md, cycle 103. OUTSIDE this cycle's neighbourhood
-- this is about the harness's own launch flag, not about the game.

WHAT HAPPENED: cycle 103 shipped a one-shot hint, which by construction calls
`RunConfig._save()`. Knowing the runtime pass would write the developer's real
`user://`, I launched with the flag that exists for exactly that:

  python tools/devtools.py launch --snapshot-userstate

Drove the hint, quit cleanly (`pid 7632 exited`), and the real
`user://highscore.save` still read `m1:seen_upgrade_tip` where it had read `m0`.
Nothing was restored, and `quit` printed no restore line either way.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A STALE FLAG: the state it failed to restore was a
ONE-SHOT. A milestone recorded in the developer's save means James never sees the
hint that cycle exists to add -- the feature would have looked shipped and been
invisible to the one person who would notice. And the failure is silent: on the
previous cycle's run `quit` printed `user://: no file changed during this run`,
so a reader has been taught that quit reports on this.

I restored it by hand: the milestone line is length-prefixed and `m0` is the
documented empty form (`game/run_config.gd:84-90`), and the scores either side of
it (3454, 5008) are James's real ones -- so a careless restore here is silent
data loss rather than a broken save. `highscore.save.bak` was no use: it is a v3
file with a score of 140.

ASK, two halves:
1. Establish WHY it did not restore. It may be that the snapshot is taken per
   named glob and the default set does not include `highscore.save`; the flag's
   help reads `--snapshot-userstate [GLOB ...]`. If so the fix is documentation
   plus a sane default, not a bug fix -- but that is a finding, not an assumption,
   so check it before writing anything.
2. Make the outcome legible either way. `quit` already prints
   `user://: no file changed during this run` when nothing moved; that line is the
   natural place for the other outcomes. It should say, per file, unchanged /
   restored / FAILED TO RESTORE, and exit non-zero on the third.

The general form: this flag's failure mode is currently indistinguishable from
its success, and the only reason to reach for it is that you already know the run
will write.

ACCEPTANCE: a stated cause for the non-restore; `quit` reporting per-file restore
outcomes; and a demonstration -- launch with the flag, deliberately change a
user:// file from the bridge, quit, and show the file back at its original bytes
with quit having said so.
notes: CORRECTION to the close reason above: the follow-up bead is plant-tower-defense-ooih, not -q4rj. I wrote the id into the close before creating the bead, which is the second time this session that a close has named an id that did not exist yet. The close is left as written; this note is the correction. The rule that would prevent it: create the follow-up FIRST, then write the close around its real id.
close_reason:
CONFIRMED AS A REAL BUG, but NOT the one this bead describes, and the difference matters enough that the bead is closed and a new one filed rather than the description being edited.

THIS BEAD SAYS: --snapshot-userstate did not restore, so the run's write survived into the developer's real save, and quit printed no restore line either way.

WHAT THE CURRENT HARNESS (0.38.0) ACTUALLY DOES: it does not restore because THE GAME CANNOT SAVE AT ALL WHILE THE FLAG IS ON. Nothing survives because nothing is ever written.

MEASURED, with a control, and with the developer's real save backed up by hand first (this bead is itself the warning that a careless experiment here is silent data loss):

  WITH --snapshot-userstate:
      run-method /root/RunConfig toggle_mute_sfx   -> Result: true
      run-method /root/RunConfig _save             -> Result: FALSE
      get-state  /root/RunConfig mute_sfx          -> true    (in memory)
      the file on disk                             -> "cb0 sfx0 ..."  UNCHANGED
      sha256 before and during the run: identical (4a0369eb1eb6d1716da1)

  WITHOUT the flag, same three calls, same build, one minute later:
      toggle_mute_sfx -> true, _save -> TRUE
      the file on disk -> "cb0 sfx1 ..."  CHANGED

So `_save()` returns false under the flag and true without it. RunConfig._save() was given a bool return in an earlier cycle precisely so a failed write could be seen; that is what made this diagnosable in two commands instead of a bisect.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN THE REPORTED BUG, not better. A flag that fails to restore loses one cycle's state and is loud once you check. A flag that silently prevents saving means:

  - every runtime verification of save-related behaviour taken under it was run against a
    game that CANNOT SAVE, and would pass identically whether the save code worked or not
  - quit still prints "userstate: restored 1 file(s) and removed 0 created during the run",
    which reads as the flag working. It restores unconditionally; there was nothing to
    restore.

I hit that second line twice in cycle 131 and read it as confirmation the flag was doing its job. It was not evidence of anything.

WHAT I DID NOT ESTABLISH, and it decides where the fix goes: WHY the save fails. The plausible cause is that the snapshot holds the file open or read-only for the run's duration, so Godot's FileAccess.open(WRITE) fails -- but I did not open the harness's implementation to check, and 0.38.0 is 22 releases behind 0.60.0 (see -ny3h, blocked on upstream gh#43). It may already be fixed there. Anyone taking this up should read the 0.60.0 template FIRST.

FILED AS: -q4rj, with the reproduce recipe above. This bead is closed because its own claim -- "nothing was restored, and the write survived" -- is not what the current build does, and leaving it open would send the next reader looking for a restore bug that is not there.

ONE CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S OWN TEXT, for the record: it says "quit printed no restore line either way". Current quit prints one, every time, and that line is part of the problem rather than evidence against it.

THE REAL SAVE IS INTACT. Backed up by hand before the experiment, restored after, and verified byte-identical: sha256 4a0369eb1eb6d1716da1 before and after. The full suite passes (920/920 on the save-filtered subset: 34 selected, 322 assertions).

title: Which other show_message call sites are level-triggered and stacking copies?
description:
SOURCE: cycle 103's -gz53, which found this defect in its own new code and fixed
it there. This bead is the sweep for the same shape elsewhere.

WHAT WAS WRONG, and it is subtle enough to be worth stating exactly:
`Hud.show_message` returns false when the row is still readable -- but it QUEUES
the arriving text rather than dropping it (`game/hud.gd`, the `_queue_message`
branch inside `show_message`). For an EDGE-triggered caller that is correct and
intended: `Game._on_flight_ignored` fires once per winged pest crossing a Chomp's
reach, and a queued copy is the line it meant to post.

For a LEVEL-triggered caller it is not. -gz53's upgrade hint is offered from
`Game._refresh`, which runs on every purchase, uproot, plant death and wave
change, and its condition (the player can afford an upgrade) STAYS TRUE once it
becomes true. So a refused post was followed by another refresh offering it
again, stacking a second copy into the queue, then a third, until
`MESSAGE_QUEUE_MAX` refused the rest -- a one-shot hint shown four times, which
is the wallpaper the whole one-shot mechanism exists to prevent.

Fixed for that caller by `Hud.row_is_quiet()` (game/hud.gd:1881), which the tip
asks BEFORE offering itself.

WHAT IS NOT DONE: `row_is_quiet` has exactly one caller. Nobody has asked which
OTHER lines are posted from a funnel rather than from an event, and the question
is not answerable by reading `show_message` -- it is a property of each CALL SITE.

ASK: enumerate every `show_message` call site (there are 17 by
`message_corpus_check`'s count) and classify each as edge-triggered or
level-triggered. For each level-triggered one, say whether its condition can
persist across refreshes; if it can, it is queueing duplicates today.

MEASURE IT RATHER THAN REASONING ABOUT IT: `Hud.messages_refused` and
`Hud.messages_evicted` already exist and are readable with `get-state`. A live
run that plays several waves and reads both counters answers "is this happening"
before anyone reads seventeen call sites.

ACCEPTANCE: a written classification of all 17 call sites, edge vs level; the two
counters read off a real multi-wave run and reported; and either a fix for each
level-triggered site that can persist, or a stated finding that there are none
besides the one already fixed.
close_reason:
DONE, and the answer is a good one: SIXTEEN EDGE, ONE LEVEL, and the one is
already guarded. Full classification in docs/message_trigger_audit.md.

THE DENOMINATOR WAS TESTED, NOT INHERITED. message_corpus_check reports 17 call
sites; that checker's scope is "sites whose text must be priced", scanned as the
token show_message( under game/ -- a different question from "sites that can be
refused". Checked the ways the two could differ: no show_message anywhere outside
game/ (.gd and .tscn, whole repo), no call("show_message")/callv/stored-Callable
indirection, and _queue_message has exactly two callers, both inside show_message,
so it is the only door into the queue. Independently re-counted here: 17 code
sites, plus 2 comment mentions that a bare `grep -c` counts and should not.

What the search would still step over, stated rather than assumed: a file loaded
by path at runtime, or a name built by concatenation. Neither exists.

THE NEAR-MISS WORTH THE AUDIT ON ITS OWN: Hud._idle_message IS level-triggered off
_refresh, but it is a plain assignment that never touches the queue -- idempotent,
cannot stack. That is why the defect is "level-triggered THROUGH THE QUEUE" rather
than "level-triggered", which is a sharper rule than the one this bead was filed with.

The one level-triggered site is _maybe_teach_upgrading, already fixed by
row_is_quiet() in cycle 103. So the audit's conclusion is POSITIVE and worth
recording: row_is_quiet should KEEP exactly one caller. For the other sixteen a
queued copy is the line the caller meant to post, and adding the guard there would
silently drop messages the player is owed.

THE FRAGILE FOUR, which is the finding a pass/fail answer would have hidden:
game.gd:453, :1332, :1582 and the packet-reveal loop are edge-triggered ONLY
because of an explicit latch (_wave_live, _flight_noted, _uproot_left, a bounded
loop). Each is one refactor away from being level-triggered, and nothing marks them.

TWO STALE PROSE NUMBERS found in hud.gd and reported rather than edited, since the
lane did not own that file. Both written by the parent after independent
verification: the return value is read by TWO call sites now (the flight tip and,
since cycle 103, the upgrade tip), not one of 22; and 14 of 17 sites pass no
priority, not 19 of 22. The three that do: MESSAGE_DEADLINE on the armed uproot,
MESSAGE_IMPORTANT on both halves of the packet reveal.

MEASUREMENT: two tests in test_placement.gd, including a CONTROL that drives
messages_refused to a known non-zero by hand before trusting a zero -- because that
counter counts only queue-full refusals, so a zero could mean "nothing stacked" or
"this gauge never moves headlessly". The lane also pins and restores
RunConfig.earned_milestones[HINT_UPGRADE_EXISTS], which is autoload state loaded
from the real save before setup() runs and would otherwise make the test depend on
the developer's own progress and on suite order.

title: Say on the run summary where the run's seeds went - upgrades or new plants
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md's "Added cycle 103" section, and the honest gap named in -gz53's
close reason. PLAYER-FACING.

WHAT THE GAME DOES NOW (verified 2026-08-17): -gz53 shipped a one-shot hint that
tells the player a placed plant CAN be upgraded, fired the first time they can
afford the cheapest upgrade on their own board. That teaches the mechanic EXISTS.

It does not teach that upgrading BEATS breadth, which is what cycle 101's A/B
actually measured: two campaigns, same economy, no cheats, differing only in
where surplus seeds went. Breadth-first reached eleven level-1 plants and died at
wave 10; depth-first won all 22 waves without losing a life. The losing run was
not ignorant of the button -- it spent the seeds elsewhere. One sentence on the
message row cannot carry a strategy, and a second hint that tried to would be the
tutorial -qoil explicitly refused.

WHERE IT BELONGS: the run summary. `game/run_summary.gd` mentions plant upgrades
NOWHERE -- its only two matches for "level" are `threat_level` (:258) and a
layout comment (:84). Verified by reading both, not by grepping for "upgrade"
alone, since the mechanic could have been named as "level".

That card is the right surface for three reasons the message row is not: it is
already the moment a player asks "why did that go wrong", it has room a live HUD
does not (the row is at 86% of capacity, -r722), and the run's own numbers are
sitting in `_stats` when it draws.

ASK: a row on the run summary comparing upgrades bought against plants placed, so
a breadth-first player sees their own policy stated back to them. Decide whether
it is a bare pair of numbers or a sentence; a sentence that scolds is worse than
nothing, so prefer the numbers and let the player draw it.

CHECK BEFORE BUILDING: whether `_stats` already carries an upgrade count. If it
does not, the counter has to be threaded from wherever upgrades are charged
(`game/game.gd`, the path around the "That upgrade costs %d seeds." refusal) and
that is the larger half of this bead.

ACCEPTANCE: the end-of-run card shows how much of the run's spend went into
upgrading versus into new plants; a headless test pins the row against a run with
a known number of each; and the numbers are read off the run rather than
recomputed from a table.
close_reason:
DONE. The run-summary card now carries a "Seeds spent" row reading
"275 on plants, 0 on upgrades".

CLAIMS CONFIRMED, and one the bead did not make changed the shape of the work.
run_summary.gd mentioned upgrading NOWHERE under any spelling (level / upgrade /
spend / spent / seed) -- its only hits were a layout comment, threat_level, and
seeds_earned_total, which is income only and documented as excluding refunds. And
_stats did NOT already carry an upgrade count, which the bead correctly flagged as
the larger half.

THE CARD HAD NO ROOM. rows_capacity() computes 7 and there were exactly 7 rows;
three tests pin the count and the last row's foot against BUTTON_CLEARANCE, and
ROW_GAP had already been cut 8->4 to fit the seventh. So this is a SWAP, per the
file's own documented idiom: "Threat reached" gave up its row and folded onto
"Waves survived" as "10 of 22 -- threat level 3". Loss-free in the strict sense --
summary_stats derives threat_level from the wave number that row already prints,
so the two rows were one measurement stated twice.

SEEDS, NOT COUNTS, and the argument is the bead's own evidence: "11 plants, 6
upgrades" reads as a near-balance where the same run's "275 on plants, 90 on
upgrades" reads as a policy. Seeds are also the variable cycle 101 held everything
else constant around. Numbers and no sentence, placed mid-card among the run's
shape rather than down among the damage, so it reads as a fact rather than as a
cause of death -- a card that scolds is worse than one that says nothing.

READ OFF THE RUN, never recomputed. The two counters increment at the lines that
actually move money: placement reads the price BEFORE pay_for_plant (which
consumes free_starter_available, so a post-charge read would bill the free cob at
full price), and the upgrade counter sits BELOW bank.add_seeds(-price), past every
refusal -- the "That upgrade costs %d seeds." denial is exactly the breadth-first
player this row describes and must not be credited to them.

Totals are gross and packets are a third sink in neither, which spend_text
documents rather than hides: the row names two destinations and never claims to
partition a total.

Three tests. The first drives a real Game and asserts a REFUSED upgrade banks
nothing -- the mutation an increment-above-the-refusal would survive. The third
measures both lengthened rows through _T.text_width (not get_minimum_size, which
returns the ~1px clip stub on these labels) against the 335px column at endless
magnitudes.

suite_reach_check caught spend_text as public-and-unreached: the tests read the
rendered Label and never called the builder. Fixed by asserting the builder directly.

704/704, 14582 assertions, lint 0/0, check_all 15/15.

title: Give the Chomp an open jaw at the moment of the bite
description:
SOURCE: cycle 102, deferred out of the -v104 lane deliberately. Also kanban.md's
"Added cycle 102" section.

WHAT THE GAME DOES NOW (verified 2026-08-17): `ChompFlower._bite()` lunges the
whole sprite `LUNGE_DISTANCE` (7px) toward the held pest and squashes it, then
snaps back. Verified live -- `_bite_lunge` read (-3.449, -6.092) for one meal and
(0.153, -6.998) for the next, both at length 7. It reads as an attack.

But the SPRITE is one picture throughout the bite. `_show_eating_sprite` already
swaps textures during the CHEW, and `art_src/` already holds
`chomp_flower_eating.svg` and `chomp_flower_eating_late.svg` beside
`chomp_flower.svg` -- so the frame-swap machinery is built and used. What is
missing is an open-jaw frame at the MOMENT of the bite rather than during the
chew that follows it.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE IN THE LANE, so nobody re-derives this: a new SVG needs
`godot --headless --path . --import` and a `test_sprite_style.gd` EXPECTED_SIZE
row, and a fan-out lane in a fresh worktree can run neither -- it has no
`.godot/` and is forbidden the engine gates. This is parent work or a solo cycle,
not a lane's.

ASK: one open-jaw SVG in `art_src/`, rendered by `tools/render_svg.gd` to 1x and
retina like the rest, swapped in for the ~0.06s of the bite and back. Follow
`art_src/STYLE.md` -- 64x64, top-down, outline a darker shade of the fill, and
the sampled palette; `svg_style_check.py` gates all of that.

ACCEPTANCE: the bite shows an open jaw; `test_sprite_style.gd` carries its
EXPECTED_SIZE row; `svg_style_check.py` and the import pass are clean; and a
headless test asserts the texture actually changes on the bite path rather than
only during the chew.
notes: 2026-08-17, user report: 'the attack animation for the chomp flower doesn't really look like it's taking bites out of the bugs, improve the animation dramatically.' This bead already covers the flower-side half (an open-jaw frame at the moment of the bite) and stays scoped to that. The other half — the PEST is intact, unmarked and still running its walk cycle for the whole chew, receiving exactly one flash_hit() at the grab — is plant-tower-defense-h4v1. Both edit ChompFlower._bite(); do not work them concurrently. If 81g9 lands first, h4v1's repeated-bite mechanism gets a much better frame to swap to.
close_reason: Gape SVG rendered 1x+retina, EXPECTED_SIZE row, swapped in for BITE_SQUASH_OUT_SECONDS. Verified live; fixed an ordering bug that made it invisible and malformed XML the renderer accepted.

title: Find every checker that walks the repo tree into .claude/worktrees/
description:
SOURCE: cycle 102's fan-out, and [G-078] in log-devtools.md.

WHAT HAPPENED: agent worktrees live at `.claude/worktrees/`, INSIDE the repo.
They are gitignored, but `Path.rglob` does not read `.gitignore`.
`tools/citation_check.py` resolved a bare filename by unique basename anywhere
under the root, so with five lanes running it reported every bare citation in
`kanban.md` as ambiguous:

  FINDING: kanban.md:3713 cites plant.gd:187-190 -- that bare name matches
  .claude\worktrees\agent-a287093c5954505ba\game\plant.gd and ... and game\plant.gd.

Fixed there by excluding `worktrees` from the walk (296 of 296 citations resolve,
0 findings, verified again after the worktrees were removed so the fix is not
just masking).

WHY THIS IS STILL OPEN: citation_check was the one that happened to fire. The
question nobody has asked is which OTHER checkers walk the repo root and would
inherit the same thing. `tools/` has fifteen parallel-safe checkers; most scope
themselves to `game/` and `test/` by name, which is immune, but that is a belief
rather than a measurement.

The failure is nastier than a false positive: a lane running any of these INSIDE
its own worktree sees no nested copies and reports clean, so the finding count
depends on which process is asking. Only the parent ever sees it.

ASK: enumerate every `tools/*.py` that walks a directory tree, and for each say
whether its root can contain `.claude/worktrees/`. Give the ones that can a
shared exclusion -- one helper, not five copies of a tuple, which is
plant-tower-defense-g1j9's shared-source-blanker argument applied to path
walking. Then plant it: create a fake nested worktree, run the set, and confirm
the count does not move.

ACCEPTANCE: a named list of which checkers walk the tree and which were exposed;
the exposed ones share one exclusion; and a planted nested checkout changes no
finding count.
close_reason:
DONE. One exclusion rule, one place: tools/repo_walk.py, imported by the rooted checkers.

THE ENUMERATION, which is the deliverable. Exposed and fixed: world_control_check
(os.walk with --root defaulting to "."), suite_reach_check (os.walk at the
product-reference sweep -- and note its SIBLING text-corpus walk already excluded
.claude/, so the file carried the rule in one half and not the other),
verify_ledger (rglob building a last-writer-wins class index, so `extends Foo`
could resolve to a stale lane copy), citation_check. Exposed but benign and left
alone with a reason: devtools.py's new-uid rglob, which only widens a
collision-avoidance set, and is harness-managed.

Immune, verified by READING each rather than assuming: group_leak_check,
save_persist_check, settle_read_check, message_corpus_check (scoped to game//test/
by name); name_check and meta_key_check (already skip dot-directories);
coverage_check; run_tests; svg_style_check; import_check; check_all. No walk at
all: bead_prose_check, gap_ledger, mirror_check, run_json_check,
check_devtools_log, upstream_gaps.

THE BUG IN THE ALREADY-FIXED TOOL, and this is the finding worth more than the
sweep. Cycle 102's citation_check fix tested `"worktrees" not in m.parts` --
ABSOLUTE parts. Run from inside a lane, whose own path IS .claude/worktrees/...,
that discards every file in the repo. The parent read 298 citations resolved; a
lane read 260 and 38 bogus "matches no file" advisories. The same asymmetry as the
original defect, pointing the other way, and invisible from whichever side you
happened to be standing on. It surfaced only because the checker was run once in
the verbose mode nobody uses, which house-static-checker requires and which had
already paid for itself once on a UnicodeEncodeError.

TWO INDEPENDENT RULES in repo_walk, and the mutation block shows each failing
alone: a DERIVED one (a directory holding a `.git` ENTRY is another checkout --
`git worktree` writes .git as a FILE, so exists() and not is_dir()) and a
hardcoded backstop from .gitignore for a copy with no .git.

PLANTED, not asserted: two fake lanes under .claude/worktrees/ plus a third
checkout at the repo root detectable only by .git -- 98 planted .gd files. Before
the fix world_control_check went 19 -> 38 scripts and 3 -> 6 Controls. After, the
full check_all output is BYTE-IDENTICAL with and without them (diff: 0 lines).
Mutations: emptying NESTED_CHECKOUT_DIRS -> RED; exists() -> isdir() -> RED,
isolating the derived rule. Fixtures deleted.

repo_walk deliberately does NOT contain the contract marker string -- check_all
would otherwise run a library as a checker -- and is listed in NOT_A_CHECKER
instead. That rule is now written into house-static-checker, since it had to be
derived from check_all's classifier.

title: Split reach three ways: unreachable-by-construction is not the same as not reached
description:
SOURCE: cycle 102's fan-out merge, and [G-077] in log-devtools.md.

WHAT HAPPENS NOW (verified 2026-08-17): the verify ledger's `reach` splits a
changed file two ways -- reached, or NOT reached. `game/game_speed.gd` is
`class_name GameSpeed extends RefCounted` and no node carries it, so
`scripts-seen` cannot see it however much of it ran.

MEASURED, not reasoned: the runtime pass for -03t6 pressed the speed button and
watched the label go 1x -> 2x -> half -> 1x with `Engine.time_scale` following
each time, and the ledger row still recorded
`NOT reached: game/game_speed.gd, game/garden_theme.gd, game/key_bindings.gd`.
Three of those four are static utilities. One (`key_binding_screen.gd`) is a real
miss -- a screen the session never navigated to. They printed identically.

CLAUDE.md documents the workaround (`DevTools.mark_script_reached`) and it is now
applied in `GameSpeed._apply`. That is a per-file manual opt-in, so the ledger's
honesty scales with how many static utilities somebody remembered to annotate --
which is the hand-maintained-list smell `derive-the-list` exists to remove.

ASK: give reach the same three-way split the rest of this harness uses. A changed
`.gd` that declares `class_name` and extends `RefCounted`/`Object` is statically
detectable with no engine at all, so it can be reported as
`unreachable-by-construction` rather than folded into NOT reached.

A file that CANNOT be seen and a file that WAS NOT loaded are opposite results,
and only one of them is a reason to go and drive the game.

ACCEPTANCE: a ledger row for a diff touching a static utility and an unvisited
screen names them in different categories; the count of genuinely-not-reached
files goes down without any `mark_script_reached` call being added.
close_reason:
DONE. reach splits three ways, and the split proved itself on this cycle's own row.

Cycle 102's row before and after:
  NOT reached: game_speed.gd, garden_theme.gd, key_bindings.gd, key_binding_screen.gd
  ->
  1 UNREACHABLE BY CONSTRUCTION (no node can carry these...): game/game_speed.gd
  (extends RefCounted); NOT reached (loadable, and this run did not load them):
  game/key_binding_screen.gd

Genuinely-not-reached went 4 -> 1 WITH NO mark_script_reached ADDED. That is the
point: a file that CANNOT be seen and a file that WAS NOT loaded are opposite
results, and only one of them is a reason to go and drive the game. Before this,
game_speed.gd -- which I had personally watched cycle Engine.time_scale three
times under my own hand -- sat in the same list as a screen the session never
navigated to.

Detected statically, no engine: a changed .gd whose top-level `extends` names a
nodeless engine base. Widened past the bead's ask by dropping the class_name
requirement (it contributes nothing to the argument). `Resource` deliberately
EXCLUDED -- over-excusing tells someone not to look, which is the failure this
change exists to prevent, one category over.

APPLIED LAST, so an observation always beats the inference: a file the snapshot
actually reports as loaded is reached, whatever its base class says.

115 historic rows read back unchanged; nothing rewritten; `stats` counts the new
bucket only from rows written since the split existed.

Mutations: emptying NODELESS_ENGINE_BASES -> RED (reproduces the exact defective
row); classifying before observing -> RED (an observed game_speed.gd falls into no
bucket at all); loosening the extends regex -> SURVIVED at 0 of 58 files, recorded
as survived rather than quietly strengthened, with the docstring saying the guard
is not yet load-bearing here.

FOUND MID-RUN: exercising cmd_reach rather than only the line-formatter caught a
well-formed zero just introduced -- a static-only diff printed `reached 0/0 ... git
reports nothing changed here`, flatly false about a diff that changed two files.

verify_ledger.py IS harness-managed: it is listed in
addons/godot_selftest/.harness_manifest.json at 0.38.0 and its sha256 matched the
manifest exactly before the edit, so /scaffold-godot-harness will silently revert
this. The change was written self-contained (stdlib only, no repo_walk import) so
the diff is portable as an upstream patch. Related: plant-tower-defense-kdnl, the
same hazard on dev_tools.gd -- whose sha has ALREADY drifted from its manifest.
