Add a distinct Sfx entry per plant's own attack verb, played from the plant itself at the moment it acts.
close_reason: Added CORN_FIRED, CHOMP_BITE, SUNDEW_CLAIM to Sfx, each reusing an existing vendored stream; wired into CornCobbler._fire_at, ChompFlower._bite, StickySundew._claim. Commit a2f91d9.

title: Plant idle sway is a dead field
description: Plant._wobble_time (plant.gd:104) is declared and never read or written anywhere else in the file - a sweep of every var declared in game/ found exactly one field with no second reference. Wire it up: a small sin(_wobble_time * k) sway on _sprite.rotation (or similar idle motion), gated behind GardenTheme.animations_enabled(), incremented in _physics_process. Ties to James's direct ask ('animate all the plants and enemies') - this is the hook already sitting there for exactly that, unwired. Scope to Plant only for this issue; pests can follow separately.
close_reason: Wired _wobble_time into _physics_process; small sin() sway on the sprite, gated behind GardenTheme.animations_enabled(), phased per-cell. Commit 5792e57.

title: Clearing a wave gets a single status-row sentence, starting one gets a banner and a sound
description:
Game._check_wave_cleared() (game.gd:322-338) sets _wave_live = false, commits the
lane pressure map, and calls hud.show_message(Hud.wave_cleared_line(...), 6.0) -- no
Sfx.play(), no flash, nothing on the board itself. _on_wave_started plays
Sfx.WAVE_STARTED (game.gd:272) into a 48px banner the instant a wave begins
(Hud.announce_wave, hud.gd:1044-1053). The wave a player survives currently
announces itself more quietly than the wave about to attack them. Give clearing a
wave its own cue -- a Sfx entry and/or a brief board-level flourish -- proportionate
to what it is.
close_reason: Added Sfx.WAVE_CLEARED and Hud.announce_wave_cleared, sharing the banner mechanism via _show_banner; wired into _check_wave_cleared alongside the existing status line. Commit 075fce9.

title: RunSummary's entrance does not know whether the run was won or lost
description:
_build_heading() (run_summary.gd:144-153) picks a different heading text and colour
for victory ("The garden holds!" vs "The garden is eaten"), but _play_entrance()
(run_summary.gd:462-470) rises every Control by the identical RISE_OFFSET over the
identical RISE_SECONDS with no branch on `won` anywhere in it. Give a win and a loss
distinct entrance motion (or a distinct one-shot flourish, e.g. a brief flash/shake
on loss) so the card's motion agrees with what its heading already says.
close_reason: Entrance branches on won: faster/overshoot rise for a win, slower plain rise for a loss. Commit 9e06db2.

title: A pest corpse pops out of existence instead of fading
description:
_play_death() (pest.gd:484-505) swaps to the dead-eyes texture, holds it for
DEATH_LINGER (0.35s, pest.gd:136), then tween.tween_callback(queue_free) -- nothing
tweens modulate.a first, so the corpse is at full opacity on its last frame and
simply gone the next. Every other exit in this game fades: Plant.play_exit_and_free()
shrinks a sprite to zero before freeing, and a pest's own arrival fades it in. Add a
short fade-out (gated behind GardenTheme.animations_enabled()) into the existing
tween chain before queue_free.
close_reason: modulate:a now tweens to 0 over the tail of DEATH_LINGER, gated behind GardenTheme.animations_enabled(); commit ab3d8f3

title: Pests never turn to face the direction they're walking
description:
Requested directly by James (kanban.md, 'Requested directly by James' block). Pest
sprites are drawn up-screen per the art style convention, but pest.gd has no
rotation/flip_h/flip_v logic anywhere -- a pest walking down, left, or right the road
still renders facing up-screen the whole way. Give Pest a facing update (rotation or
flip, whichever the kit's sprites tolerate) driven off its walk direction each leg of
PATH_CORNERS.
close_reason: Sprite rotates to face the leg it is walking, snapped to 4 cardinal directions off Board's axis-aligned route; commit 3815587

title: A plant leaving the board always vanishes silently
description: Both Game._on_plant_destroyed (game.gd:987-995) and Game.uproot_selected (game.gd:1084-1093) end in plant.queue_free() with no exit animation; uproot additionally has zero Sfx.play() call anywhere in the function. Neither tweens the sprite out the way Plant._build_visuals tweens one in (plant.gd:187-190, 0.4x to 1.12x to 1.0 over 0.22s). A create_tween() shrinking _sprite.scale toward zero before either queue_free() call, gated behind GardenTheme.animations_enabled(), plus an Sfx entry for uproot specifically, would give leaving the board the same care arriving on it gets.
close_reason: Shipped: Plant.play_exit_and_free() tween-out + Sfx.PLANT_UPROOTED, commit 6117da4

title: Corn Cobbler upgrades have no moment of their own
description: CornCobbler.upgrade() (corn_cobbler.gd:290-297) bumps level and calls queue_redraw() -- a static fact the muzzle fan picks up next paint, not a cue at the instant the player spends the seeds. Contrast ChompFlower._bite() (chomp_flower.gd:139-144), which squashes its sprite on every single meal. A short scale-pop on the cob's sprite plus a new Sfx entry, gated behind GardenTheme.animations_enabled(), would mark the transaction rather than only its aftermath.
close_reason: Shipped: _upgrade_flourish() squash tween + Sfx.PLANT_UPGRADED, commit 388db1a

title: A refused purchase has a sentence and no other feedback
description: SeedBank.pay_for_plant() and buy_packet() both emit purchase_failed with only a reason string on every refusal (seed_bank.gd:111-121, 179-190), and Game._ready wires it straight to hud.show_message(reason) - a caption in the shared status line, nothing more. Sfx.SOUNDS has entries for planting, a plant dying, a pest dying, a wave starting, but none for a purchase bouncing. Add a denial cue: a short red shake on the button actually clicked (or the plant bar slot) plus a new Sfx.SOUNDS entry, so the 'no' lands where the click happened instead of only in text a player mid-wave may not be reading.
close_reason: Shipped: Sfx.PURCHASE_DENIED (reuses error_002.ogg) plays on every bank.purchase_failed; Hud.shake_plant_button/shake_packet_button shake the specific control at the two call sites that know which one was reached for. Commit 2a162f3.

title: Selecting a plant has no motion
description: Plant.set_selected() (plant.gd:462-468) toggles _selection_marker.visible directly and SelectionMarker._draw_brackets() (selection_marker.gd:41-46) draws the four corner brackets at fixed size the instant the flag flips - no tween, nothing between invisible and full-size. Contrast _build_visuals(), which pops a placed plant's sprite in from 0.4x scale over 0.22s (plant.gd:187-190). Give the selection brackets (and by inheritance PlacementPreview's hover cue) a short grow-in/fade tween instead of an instant show, gated behind GardenTheme.animations_enabled().
close_reason: Shipped: SelectionMarker.play_entrance() grows brackets in from 0.55x/transparent. PlacementPreview stays instant (hover cue, redraws every mouse move) -- documented in the commit. Commit 506a0f9.

title: HUD readouts snap instead of punching on change
description: Hud.refresh() overwrites _seeds_label.text, _lives_label.text and _compost_label.text outright every call (hud.gd:731,753,755), while the same file already eases the wave label's colour with a killed-and-restarted Tween in _ease_threat_tint (hud.gd:898-911) instead of snapping it. Give the seeds/lives/compost labels a short scale-punch when their value changes, gated the same way _ease_threat_tint already is (GardenTheme.animations_enabled()), so the game's three most frequent feedback moments (a kill payout, a life lost, a husk composted) get the one motion vocabulary this file has already proven out.
close_reason: Shipped: seeds/lives/compost labels get a scale punch on change, reusing _ease_threat_tint's kill-and-restart Tween pattern. Commit 7296b78.

title: PauseScreen has no entrance or exit motion
description: PauseScreen's own header calls it shaped after RunSummary, being the same kind of object: a card over a live board (pause_screen.gd:12-14). RunSummary and TitleScreen both rise their content in against GardenTheme.animations_enabled(); PauseScreen has no create_tween or modulate write anywhere in the file. The card appears via add_child and disappears via _pause_layer.queue_free() (game.gd:821) on the same frame Escape is pressed. Add a rise-in / fade-out matching the other two card screens' pattern, gated the same way.
close_reason: Shipped: rise-in entrance borrowing RunSummary's constants, and a play_exit() fade Game.resume_run() awaits before freeing the layer. Commit 54152de.

title: Corn Cobbler needs a readiness readout
description: Sunflower's payout clock has an always-on fill gauge (sunflower.gd ~150-156) and Chomp Flower's mouth shows a shrinking chew ring (chomp_flower.gd _draw ~130-136), but CornCobbler._cooldown (corn_cobbler.gd:88, ticked at ~95-97) is read by nothing outside _act(). The muzzle fan (_draw_muzzle_fan, ~141-152) reflects the last shot's spread, not the next shot's timing, so a cob mid-reload and one ready to fire look identical. Add a readiness cue (fill ring, dimming muzzle, or similar) driven off _cooldown / LEVELS interval, matching the visual idiom the other two plants already use.
close_reason: Readiness fade shipped: readiness_at()/readiness() drive a 0.35-1.0 alpha fade on the muzzle fan, off the same _cooldown _act already ticks. Unit-tested exactly (pure math + wired through real _act()); live-confirmed via forced fires (0.02-0.10 readiness right after firing, 1.0 once recovered), zero runtime errors across 7 placed cobblers. Baseline regenerated (fire_interval() is now genuinely test-named). Commit follows.

title: Find tests that read state straight after instantiate_scene
description: test_hosting_a_loaded_cob asserted a volley had fired by the time instantiate_scene returned. That frame count is unspecified, so it was order-dependent - green two cycles, red when unrelated tests shifted timing. Any test reading a group or a live property straight after instantiate_scene without awaiting a condition has the same exposure. A checker for that shape would name them.
close_reason: Closed

title: Tell the player unaimed ground still gets kills
description: Coverage is now measured both directions and neither number is in the game. Under-promise: 7 kills on unaimed ground at up to 202px, because a kernel flies until it leaves the board. Over-promise at the pest: zero of 116. The board says 'unaimed', which is right, but a player never learns unaimed ground still gets kills - which is what would stop them over-buying cover.
close_reason: Closed

title: Assert what Pest.died and escaped carry
description: 15 signals still have nothing asserting what they carry, down from 17. Pest.died is the highest value remaining: it is the income path with the most wiring under it (Game._on_pest_died drops the husk, banks seeds, notes the lane loss). escaped is its pair. Assert the payload and which paths fire, not merely that the signal exists - naming it satisfies the reach gate while proving nothing.
close_reason: Closed

title: No gate says how much of the game the suite never touches
description: run_tests prints Suite: 7 scripts and Assertions: N; the checkers print N of M; lint prints Shaders: N of M. Nothing prints which .gd files are never loaded by any test. The bridge already has scripts-seen and nothing compares it against the file list. That is the one denominator the project lacks, and it is the one that says where the suite is blind.
close_reason: Closed

title: Tell the player which red means fought and which means unreachable
description: coverage_frontier() says how far the garden can reach; LanePressureOverlay says how far pests got. The prep line compares them once to pick a sentence. The board never does - a player sees red tint and cannot tell 'they got here and we fought' from 'they got here and nothing could touch them', which is the whole distinction the coverage work established.
close_reason: Closed

title: Warn at startup when a budget crosses its own tight threshold
description: cmd budgets reports tight/spent from outside, but nothing inside the game reacts. A startup push_warning when any budget crosses its tight threshold means the next person to spend one hears about it on the next run rather than on the next audit. Reuses the budget entries the verb already computes.
close_reason: Closed

title: Tests leak nodes into groups and nothing notices
description: Root cause under the kernels flake: a test that builds a Kernel and does not free it leaves it in the group for every later test. _T.free_ui is called on hosts, but a kernel spawned by _act is parented to the host's PARENT, not the host. A per-test assertion that group counts return to where they started would catch the whole class.
close_reason: Closed

title: Two HUD budgets sit within 8px of their ceilings
description: cmd budgets reports hud_readouts at 161 of 168px (SeedsLabel, 7px left) and hud_stats_row at 1104 of 1112px (8px left). Both are 'tight' by the verb's own <15% threshold. The row sum is the one that matters: widening any single readout is paid out of it, so the two are coupled and both are nearly gone. Worth deciding now whether the stats row needs re-proportioning before the next readout is added rather than after.
close_reason: Shipped: trimmed STATS_SEPARATION 14->10, flat +10px readout margins, ratcheted BUDGET_FLOOR, commit e93241c

title: SIMULTANEOUS_PEST_CEILING is fully spent and nothing said so
description: cmd budgets reports pest_road_ceiling at 40 of 40 pests, 0 left, state 'spent'. That is by construction - the ceiling is enforced by the group shares summing to it exactly - but it means the road budget has no slack at all, so any future wave shape that wants more simultaneous pests has nowhere to take them from. Decide whether 'spent by design' deserves its own state distinct from 'spent because you ran out'.
close_reason: Shipped: Game.BUDGET_SPENT_BY_DESIGN state, pest_road_ceiling passes by_design=true, commit 34a77ae

title: The post-mortem names a cell the road under it may not be reddest at
description: stop_cell is losses-minus-escapes; the tint under the translucent summary card is still painted from raw losses. On a bleeding run the named cell and the reddest cell genuinely differ. Correct and documented, but a player looking from the number to the picture is told nothing. Either the card points at its own cell, or the tint switches to stops.
close_reason: Closed

title: A budgets verb that prints every declared coupling with its headroom
description: Four constants now carry 'moving me costs you X' comments: PATH_CORNERS, COLLECT_RADIUS, SUBHEAD_MAX_WIDTH and the HUD WORST_CASE_TEXT budgets. Each warns about a coupling living in another file, and a person only finds the warning by editing that exact line. A devtools verb printing every declared budget with its current headroom makes the set visible before someone goes looking.
close_reason: Closed

title: Name the husk budget where the road is actually edited
description: board_info now reports the husk click budget, but reaching it needs a running game, a launched bridge and knowing the verb exists. A designer dragging Board.PATH_CORNERS is in board.gd in an editor and nothing there mentions the budget. Add a ## line above PATH_CORNERS and above CompostMeter.COLLECT_RADIUS naming it. Suggested by the agent that built the devtools half, which correctly judged its own work a half-solution.
close_reason: Closed

title: Give the board a second warning channel so red is not carrying three meanings
description: GardenTheme.DANGER now paints lane pressure (pests got this far), the plant health bar (this plant is dying) and an armed Uproot (you are about to destroy this). Three different sentences in one hue at three alphas. Unifying the value was right; colour alone should not carry three meanings - add a shape or hatch channel.
close_reason: Closed

title: Put husk_click_margin in board_info so the budget is visible before a test fails
description: husk_click_margin() exists because the husk-vs-placement conflict is 4px from being real, and a test asserts the clearance stays positive. Nothing tells a designer moving PATH_CORNERS or COLLECT_RADIUS that they are spending it - they find out when a test fails, with no indication 4px was the budget.
close_reason: Closed

title: Show lane pressure during prep, not after the run
description: LanePressureOverlay paints how far pests got, decayed once per wave, and is a readout of the wave that just ended. Board.run_pressure_alpha exists and is shown exactly once by show_run_pressure(), at the moment the run is over. The number that would inform a purchase is held back until purchasing has stopped. Surface it during the prep strip.
close_reason: Closed

title: The notebook is unreachable the moment a run starts
description: NotebookScreen is constructed in exactly one place, title_screen.gd's _open_notebook(), and nothing in game.gd, hud.gd or pause_screen.gd can reach it. So the game's only explanation of anything is closed to the player who actually needs it -- mid-run, holding a plant they do not understand. The pause card is now a full-screen surface that already lists the keyboard verbs and is already the only way to leave a run; a fourth button on it is the whole fix. NotebookScreen already emits back_requested and is built to be added as a child of any Control.
acceptance_criteria: The notebook opens from within a run and returns to the paused game, with the run still paused behind it. A test asserts the pause state survives opening and closing it.
close_reason: Closed

title: The endless spawn gap floors at wave 22 and only the count keeps climbing
description: WaveDirector's aphid spawn gap reaches its floor around wave 22, and the health and speed scales cap around waves 41 and 48. Past 48 the only thing that still moves is count, which is uncapped -- 166 pests at wave 48, 376 at wave 108. Spawn floor times crossing time puts on the order of 100 aphids alive at once on an 896px board. That is precisely the quantity problem the ENDLESS_HEALTH_STEP header says the scales exist to avoid, arrived at from the other direction.
acceptance_criteria: Endless difficulty past the scale caps escalates by something other than raw count, or count is bounded and the difficulty comes from elsewhere. A test asserts simultaneous pest count stays under a stated ceiling at wave 100.
close_reason: Closed

title: A husk eats the click that would have planted, and the preview cannot warn about it
description: CompostMeter.COLLECT_RADIUS is 28, so a husk claims a 56px-wide target on a 64px cell -- 88% of it. Game._click_at sweeps a husk before it reaches the placement branch and returns, so a click on a cell the preview has just drawn as legal composts instead of planting. PlacementPreview now computes four states (illegal, at_risk, dead ground, redundant coverage) and mentions husks exactly zero times, so the one thing that can silently take the click is the one thing the ring cannot warn about. Husks last up to 10s, so the cell is effectively unplantable for that long with no indication.
acceptance_criteria: Either the preview shows that a click on this cell will compost rather than plant, or placement wins on a cell the player has explicitly targeted. Unit test covers a husk overlapping a buildable cell.
close_reason: Precedence fixed: a click that would plant, plants. Measurement showed the conflict cannot occur on the shipping board (32px vs a 28px sweep, 4px margin) -- husk_click_margin() now gates that

title: Every Sundew redraw walks every pest on the board
description: StickySundew._draw_wash calls shared_ground_offsets, which calls _sibling_patches, which walks all of _entities' children -- and pests live there too. So the cost of drawing one patch scales with the number of pests, not the number of patches. _refresh_droplets queues a redraw whenever droplet_radius changes, which it does as pests enter and leave the patch, so the redraws are most frequent exactly when the pest count is highest. Sundew membership changes at only two sites, so the sibling list could be cached and invalidated there instead.
acceptance_criteria: Drawing a patch does not iterate pests. A test asserts the sibling lookup is not called per-pest, or that redraw cost is independent of pest count.
close_reason: Closed

title: The 45-seed Corn upgrade is worse than the 20-seed one against a single pest
description: CornCobbler.LEVELS with evenly-spaced offsets puts level 3's kernels at +/-26, +/-13 and 0 degrees. Against Kernel.HIT_RADIUS 18.0 an outer kernel clears the aimed pest past 18/tan(26) = 37px -- under one cell, against a RANGE of 176. Level 2's +/-7 degrees connects out to 147px. Single-target that is level 2 at 2.78 dps versus level 3 at 1.61, and damage is 1.0 at all three levels. So the most expensive upgrade in the game makes a cob worse against the thing it is aimed at, while the selection panel advertises '5 kernel(s) per shot' and the muzzle fan draws the spread as the benefit.
acceptance_criteria: Each upgrade level is at least as good as the one below it against a single target, or the spread's cost is stated where the player buys it. A test asserts single-target dps is non-decreasing across levels.
close_reason: Closed

title: The pause note is drawn underneath the first button
description: PauseScreen.FIRST_BUTTON_Y is an absolute 232.0 -- the one offset in that file not written as CARD.position.y + N. With CARD at y=152 the Note's box is 228-252 and ResumeButton's is 232-276, so 20 of the note's 24 pixels sit under an opaque stylebox. There is 64px of unused card below the last button. This is a sibling-pair overlap, the class validate-ui and findings structurally cannot see because each Control fits its own box; the repo ships .claude/skills/godot-hud-occlusion-audit for exactly this. The note text is also a constant, 'The wave is waiting.', which is false whenever pause fires between waves.
acceptance_criteria: No pause-screen Control overlaps another, asserted by a pairwise test, and the note says something true about the current state.
close_reason: Closed

title: Two Sundews on the same ground cost 60 seeds and slow nothing extra
description: StickySundew refcounts its slow so overlapping patches hold a pest at 0.55 rather than 0.30 -- correct, and deliberate. But the patch wash composites darker where two patches overlap, so the only thing on screen says the opposite of the rule: it reads as 'more slow here'. A player can spend 60 seeds on two patches covering the same road and get exactly what one would have given. The placement preview has no notion of ground already covered, and crossing_time_multiplier() has no caller outside a test.
acceptance_criteria: Overlapping Sundew ground is visually distinguishable from stacked-and-working, or the preview warns before the second one is placed. A test covers the overlap case.
close_reason: Closed

title: There is no pause, and no way to leave a run you are done with
description: get_tree().paused appears nowhere in game/. Game._unhandled_input handles motion, left click, KEY_R gated on game over, and KEY_M for mute -- there is no pause key. PREP_SECONDS keeps counting down while the player is away from the keyboard, so stepping away mid-run loses beds. TITLE_SCENE is reachable only from RunSummary's GateButton, which means the only way out of a run in progress is to lose it or kill the process. The devtools bridge answers while the tree is paused, so a pause menu is verifiable.
acceptance_criteria: A pause key freezes the run including the prep timer, and offers a way back to the title screen. Unit test asserts the prep timer does not advance while paused.
close_reason: Closed

title: Nothing in the catalogue answers a hungry pest
description: Sticky Sundew deliberately does not answer is_hungry: a hungry pest stops to eat a plant at EAT_DPS 14.0 against Plant.MAX_HEALTH 40.0, under three seconds per bed, and eating is not movement-gated so a slow does nothing about it. Every plant in the catalogue either damages a pest or funds the ones that do; nothing protects or repairs a bed under attack. A real answer needs a regen or armour hook on Plant, which is why it was filed rather than faked.
acceptance_criteria: A plant, upgrade or mechanic exists that meaningfully changes the outcome when a hungry pest reaches a bed. Unit test drives a hungry pest against a defended and an undefended bed and asserts the difference.
close_reason: Closed

title: A plant's health only goes down, and the cheapest repair is to destroy it
description: Plant.take_damage is the only writer of health and there is no heal path anywhere. uproot_refund reads PlantCatalog.cost * 0.6 and never reads health, so uprooting a nearly-dead plant refunds exactly as much as uprooting a pristine one -- making uproot-and-replant the cheapest repair in the game at a net 4 seeds for a Corn. That is a strictly dominant strategy that also makes the new health readout advisory rather than a decision.
acceptance_criteria: Either damaged plants can be healed at a cost, or the uproot refund scales with remaining health so a wrecked plant refunds less. Unit test covers the refund at full and near-zero health.
close_reason: Closed

title: The placement ring is drawn with equal confidence over cells that cover no road at all
description: PlacementPreview computes reach and legality per cell but legality only means buildable-and-empty. Measured against the real PATH_CORNERS route: of 94 buildable cells, 15 cover zero road at a Corn Cobbler's RANGE of 176px, and 34 cover zero road at a Chomp Flower's GRAB_RADIUS of 73.6px. The ring looks identical on all of them, so a player can spend 10 seeds on a plant that can never fire, and nothing says so before or after the click.
acceptance_criteria: A cell that covers no road for the currently selected plant is visually distinct in the preview before the click. Unit test asserts the covered-road count per cell against the real route for both plants.
close_reason: Closed

title: One high score serves both game modes, and the title screen names it wrong
description: Game._end_run calls RunConfig.record_score with the run's seed total and no mode check, and RunConfig persists a single number to user://highscore.save. TitleScreen renders that one number as 'Best endless run' / 'No endless run on record yet'. So a campaign run can take the endless record, and RunSummary._score_line then compares a campaign total against a number that may have come from an endless run. Two different games are sharing one scoreboard and the label claims otherwise.
acceptance_criteria: Campaign and endless keep separate high scores, each labelled for the mode it came from, and an existing single-value save migrates without being lost. Unit test covers a campaign run not overwriting an endless record.
close_reason: Closed

title: The game makes no sound at all
description: A repo-wide grep for AudioStreamPlayer, AudioStream, .ogg and .wav finds no hit anywhere in game code -- assets/ holds only kenney/ and sprites/. Four new cues shipped in cycle 3-4 (uproot arming, plant damage, threat escalation, mutation markers) and not one of them makes a noise. The silent-death case is the worst: compost_meter erases an expired husk with no cue at all, so the player never learns they were too slow. Kenney ships CC0 audio packs in the same collection the sprites came from.
acceptance_criteria: At least placement, pest death, husk collection, husk rot and run end have distinct sounds, with a master mute honoured (devtools_config.json already sets mute:true for automation). A test asserts every declared sound file exists and loads.
close_reason: 11 CC0 Kenney samples, 8-voice root-parented pool, silent-husk-rot fixed; verified live catching a voice mid-playback and surviving a scene reload

title: A mutated pest is a tint, and the two that change the rules are unnamed
description: Pest mutations are signalled only by a _tint colour. Winged makes a Chomp Flower unable to grab it at all (chomp_flower.gd skips pests with is_winged) and hungry makes it eat a plant at EAT_DPS 14.0 against Plant.MAX_HEALTH 40.0 -- under three seconds to destroy a bed. Both change what the player should do and neither is named or shaped differently. The placement preview already computes at_risk, so the vocabulary for warning about this exists.
acceptance_criteria: A winged and a hungry pest are each distinguishable from a plain one by something other than hue -- a shape, an icon, or a label -- and the distinction survives a screenshot in greyscale.
close_reason: Closed

title: Nothing counts down the 18 seconds to the next wave
description: Game.PREP_SECONDS is 18.0 and _process silently decrements _prep_left until a wave starts on its own. The only mention is a 6-second message when the previous wave clears, so for the other 12 seconds the player has no idea how long they have to spend seeds and place plants. The threat tint now tells them how bad the next wave is and still nothing tells them when it lands.
acceptance_criteria: The HUD shows the remaining prep time and it visibly counts down; the readout disappears once a wave is live. Covered by a unit test that pumps _process and asserts the text changes.
close_reason: Closed

title: The message line has one slot, so cues stomp each other
description: Hud.show_message assigns _message_label.text outright and resets a single _message_left timer, so any new message destroys the one before it mid-read. The uproot gate made this concrete: the 4s 'click again to uproot' instruction is wiped by the 2s husk message the moment a pest dies, and the player is left with an armed button and no explanation. A short queue, or a second line, or at minimum refusing to overwrite a higher-priority message before it has been readable.
acceptance_criteria: A message cannot be replaced before a minimum readable time unless the new one is higher priority; the uproot instruction survives an incidental husk pickup. Unit test drives two overlapping show_message calls and asserts what the label reads.
close_reason: Closed

title: A real end-of-run summary panel
description: _end_run paints the run's whole damage map on the board and names the worst cell in a 30s message that expires while the player is still reading the banner. Every number a post-mortem needs is already computed -- waves survived, threat level reached, seeds earned, high score, worst lane cell, husks collected vs dropped. Give them a panel that stays until dismissed, instead of a banner plus a timed message.
acceptance_criteria: An end-of-run panel showing at least waves survived, threat level reached, seeds earned and the worst lane cell, which persists until the player restarts; covered by a headless UI test.
close_reason: RunSummary card with waves/threat/beds/compost/worst-cell, persists until dismissed, replay and back-to-title both wired and verified live

title: Show a selected plant's health in the side panel
description: Hungry pests chew plants down over several seconds and Plant.health drives a bar on the plant itself, but the selection panel shows only the name and blurb. Selecting a half-eaten Corn Cobbler tells the player nothing about whether to uproot and replant it, which is exactly the decision the panel exists to support. Add a health readout to the selection box.
acceptance_criteria: The selection panel shows current/max health for a damaged plant and updates as it takes damage; a unit test drives take_damage and asserts the panel text changed.
close_reason: Health bar + numbers in the selection panel, hidden until damaged, green->red ramp; runtime caught a zero-margin panel foot which is now fixed and gated at 8px

title: Uproot needs a confirm or an undo
description: The Uproot button refunds 60% and destroys the plant instantly with no confirmation. One stray click on a selected Sunflower late in a run silently destroys the economy the whole run was built on -- it is the only irreversible misclick in the game. Add a confirm step (the button re-labels to 'Uproot? Confirm' for a few seconds) or a short undo window that restores the plant and reverses the refund.
acceptance_criteria: A single click on Uproot does not remove the plant; a second within the window does. Unit tests cover both the confirm path and the timeout-cancels path.
close_reason: request_uproot() arms on first click, commits on a second within 4s; verified live (232x40 relabel, exact UPROOT_ARMED red, timeout revert) and covered by 4 tests

title: Designer's Notebook reads as two floating images, not a notebook
description: Six pages, each a bare 320x320 drawing beside a bare 320x320 sprite on a flat dark field, with one six-word green caption and three default buttons below. Nothing says which pane is which, the sprite renders blurry (64px source filtered up to 320), there is no keyboard paging or Escape, no transition between pages, and the page/sprite mapping is wrong in places (image6 is the named Corn Cobbler portrait, not the kernel volley; image3 is where the kernels are).
acceptance_criteria: A paper spread with a binding so it reads as a notebook; per-pane headings; crisp sprite rendering; a real designer note per page, not just a caption; correct drawing-to-sprite mapping; page dots; Left/Right arrows page and Escape closes; a cross-fade between pages; Drawing/Sprite/PageLabel/Backdrop stay direct children of the root so existing tests and bridge paths hold.

title: Title screen is a flat rectangle with default-theme buttons
description: The title screen draws INK over the whole viewport, three stock grey Buttons and three Labels. No art, no motion, no keyboard, and the bottom third is empty — in a game that already ships plant and pest sprites. It is the first thing a player sees and it looks unfinished.
acceptance_criteria: A themed button set (paper/ink/leaf, hover + focus states); a drawn backdrop instead of one flat colour; the game's own sprites on screen; an entrance animation that is skipped headlessly; keyboard focus and Enter to start; existing node paths (Backdrop/StartButton/EndlessButton/NotebookButton) unchanged so tests and the bridge still resolve.

title: HUD compost counter collides with the Grow-the-next-wave button
description: With several husks on the ground the HUD reads 'Compost 0 (11 ready)' and the '(11 ready)' suffix runs underneath the 'Grow the next wave' button. Caught in a screenshot during /verify on 2026-08-15; validate-ui reported 0 findings over that exact frame because the label's own rect is fine -- it is the button that overlaps it, and nothing compares two sibling Controls for occlusion. Give the HUD bar a real layout (HBoxContainer with the button in its own slot) so the counter cannot be run over regardless of how long its text gets.
acceptance_criteria: A HUD with a 2-digit husk count and the wave button both visible has no overlapping screen rects, asserted by node-bounds in a test.

title: Mutated pests should drop a better husk
description: Armoured/winged/hungry mutations all cost the player more to deal with than a plain pest, but _on_pest_died pays the same husk value regardless of mutation. Scale husk value by mutation (e.g. armoured/winged/hungry each worth more) to tie the mutation system into the compost system instead of leaving them side by side.
close_reason: Pest.husk_multiplier() scales husk value by mutation (armoured/winged 1.5x, hungry 2x); verified headless (4 unit tests) and live (compost_state: plain=2, hungry=3)

title: Lane pressure readout on the road
description: The board is a single road, so which end pests got furthest on last wave is always answerable but never shown. Tint the road segment red where pests advanced furthest last wave, fading each wave, to give the player a passive read on lane pressure without opening any menu.
close_reason: LanePressureOverlay tints the road cell where pests got furthest last wave; verified headless (4 unit tests, one of which caught a real game-over-mid-wave commit bug) and live (board_info + run-method + screenshot)

title: Selection needs a second cue beyond the range ring
description: Right now the only sign a plant is selected is the translucent range ring — Corn Cobbler shows it, but Chomp Flower draws no ring at all, so selecting a Chomp shows nothing. Add a thin outline or corner brackets drawn on the sprite itself in the base Plant class (not per-subclass), so selection is legible for every current and future plant.
close_reason: SelectionMarker child node ships in Plant, verified headless (2 unit tests) and at runtime (get-state + screenshot)

title: Corn range indicator on selected plant
description: Placement is blind: corn reaches 176px and nothing shows it. Draw a range ring around the plant when selected/placing so the player can judge coverage.
close_reason: Wired Plant.set_selected() into Game._select() (closes G-007) and added ChompFlower's shrinking chew ring; both verified at runtime via /verify.

title: Chomp Flower occupied readout
description: chew_progress() exists on ChompFlower and nothing draws it. The Chomp/beetle trade-off (mouth busy ~2.6s, lane open) is invisible to the player. Draw a shrinking ring/bar around the flower while chewing.

title: Ambient bees: periodic cosmetic bouts across the garden
description: Purely aesthetic ambient layer, approved from a design page (https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9f73f1c0-ed8b-49df-9483-7387a6033416). Every 22-40s a bout opens: 1-3 bees enter from a hashed edge point, cross the board on a two-sine meander in 9-14s, and exit. set_process(false) between bouts, so idle cost is zero. Nothing in the run reads them and they read nothing but board size and current weather.
design: BeeSwarm is a Node2D sibling of Entities (child order is draw order and plants are added to Entities all run, so parenting there would sink bees under every plant built). Flight is a pure static func of (bout, index, t) so headless can assert it: baseline lerp entry->exit, perpendicular wander of two detuned sines (0.21/0.58 Hz, incommensurate so the path never locks into a tidy S), amplitude eased by sin(PI*t) so entry and exit are exact and straight. Bout parameters come from a hash of the bout number, not an RNG, matching WeatherOverlay.mark_position - reproducible screenshots, no second stream outside the wave director seed. Drawn in _draw (11 primitives), kit palette unwidened: body #FFCC00, rim/stripes #8A6D00. BODY_LENGTH 18px per approval. The offset drop shadow is load-bearing twice: it is a channel no OVERLAY_GRAMMAR cue owns (says airborne, not a mark about this cell), and at 18px it is one of four separations from an aphid (shadow, off-road flight, wandering speed, no health bar or husk). Approved decisions: no plant attraction (a bee curving toward a plant reads as a cue about that plant), drawn not sprited, bouts skipped during rain, 2 bees / 34px wander / 11s cross / 22-40s gap.
acceptance_criteria: BeeSwarm exists as a named sibling of Entities and tracks its position through _apply_board_layout. Pure statics assert: path containment within margin for t in (0,1), no tear between consecutive samples, t=0/t=1 land on the edge points, bout determinism, schedule advance, rain skip. Body and shadow have rows in test_every_board_mark_clears_the_ground_floor_at_the_alpha_it_is_drawn_at on grass and dirt. OVERLAY_GRAMMAR.md names bees as the first drawn board thing that is deliberately not a cue. Gates green: name_check, import, lint_project, run_tests.py.
close_reason: Landed: BeeSwarm layer, 11 tests, 8 contrast rows, 2 devtools verbs, grammar note. Gates green (lint 0, tests 1156/1156, 25893 assertions); live pass confirmed set_process(false) between bouts with a 28.06s timer armed, and the rain skip.

title: A boss health bar, because 32 px of bar over a 953 px body is a joke
description:
Pest's health bar is HEALTH_BAR_SIZE (32, 5) at HEALTH_BAR_TOP -30 (pest.gd:616), screen-locked over the sprite. Over a body 953 px long that is unreadable and, worse, ambiguous: the player cannot tell which end it belongs to.

Filed separately from the boss itself because the boss ships without it and is still playable -- but it is the first thing a playtest will complain about. Likely home is the HUD's own CanvasLayer (hud_layer_name in devtools_config.json) rather than the world, which makes it a Control and brings .claude/skills/godot-hud-occlusion-audit into scope: a full-width boss bar is exactly the kind of node that silently covers an existing readout.

Blocked on the Cutworm existing to have a bar for.
acceptance_criteria: findings reports no NEW ui_layout or occlusion finding on the HUD with the bar shown. The bar reads the same health pool the pest does -- one source, asserted, not a mirrored float.

title: Decide whether tools/gen_bool_classifier.py's --check-* belongs in check_all.py's derived checker list
description: tools/gen_bool_classifier.py (added plant-tower-defense-q7z6) can --check-func/--check-test a spec's generated block against its target file and exit 1 on drift, but it is spec-scoped (needs a SPEC.json + two --check-* paths per call) not project-scoped-with-no-args like every checker tools/check_all.py auto-discovers via the NOT COVERED: contract (tools/check_all.py's own header, house-static-checker skill). Only 2 specs exist today (tools/specs/plant_button_tint.json, seeds_flash_tint.json). Worth reshaping into a no-args, self-discovering checker (glob tools/specs/*.json, --check-* both targets named in each spec, print one NOT COVERED: line) once there are enough specs that a human forgetting to run --check-* by hand is a real, recurring cost -- not before.
acceptance_criteria: Either (a) gen_bool_classifier.py grows a no-args self-discovering check mode and check_all.py picks it up automatically via its existing NOT COVERED: contract, with a test proving a deliberately-staled generated block fails the run; or (b) this is closed wontfix with a one-line reason once reviewed (e.g. still only 2 specs, not worth it yet).

title: hud.gd is still 4168 lines after the tar5 split
description: Project convention (CLAUDE.md, and this cycle's own instructions) is to refactor files over 500 lines into smaller ones using OO design. game/hud.gd is 4168 lines -- hud_selection.gd (plant-tower-defense-tar5) already pulled the selection-panel detail corpus out once, but the bar-building code (_build_top_bar, _build_side_panel and everything they wire: plant buttons, packet buttons, the health row, the banner) is still one file. This cycle added a further preload-only helper (hud_long_press.gd) rather than growing hud.gd more, following the same pattern -- but the base file itself was never revisited. Candidate next split: the plant-bar/packet-bar construction block (roughly hud.gd:1600-1700 plus their tooltip/layout helper functions) into a hud_shop_bar.gd, mirroring hud_selection.gd's shape (preload-only, no class_name, Hud keeps every forwarded symbol).

title: citation_check --symbol misses a wrapped citation on the next line
description: SOURCE: plant-tower-defense-grls's own verification. citation_check.py --symbol's FILE_SYMBOL_PREFIX match requires the backticked symbol and its (file:line) citation on the SAME physical line. kanban.md wraps prose at a column width, so a citation like backtick _apply_facing backtick newline (game/pest.gd:1519) -- symbol and citation split across two lines by markdown wrapping -- is invisible to --symbol even though it names a real, checkable symbol. Measured directly: grls found 11 additional stale pest.gd citations this way that --symbol's own 84-finding run never flagged, only caught by cross-referencing citation_relocate.py's independent line-tracking.
acceptance_criteria: citation_check.py --symbol matches a symbol/citation pair across a line break (e.g. join adjacent lines before matching, or search a small trailing window rather than requiring one physical line), re-run against kanban.md, and confirm the newly-caught wrapped citations are the ones grls's manual cross-reference found.

title: Re-point the eleven pest.gd citations in kanban.md, drifted again since cycle 139
description: SOURCE: plant-tower-defense-nalv's own build/verification. Its new tools/citation_check.py --symbol mode, run for real against kanban.md, found that the eleven Pest citations cycle 139 specifically re-pointed (Pest._gait, _update_facing, _apply_facing, meal.take_damage, _play_death, husk_multiplier, gait_stretch's hungry branch, the escaped emit, GAIT_SWING, FLINCH_RADIANS, SHELL_FLASH_DIM) have drifted again -- 69 commits and roughly 354 lines of game/pest.gd growth since (this session's 4zyb lane alone added ~316 lines to the file) moved every one. Example: _gait was cited at game/pest.gd:1527, is now declared at 1881-1902. This is exactly the class of drift citation_check.py's --against mode structurally cannot see (it only sees what THIS cycle's own diff moved), which is nalv's whole reason for existing.
acceptance_criteria: Run python tools/citation_check.py --symbol against kanban.md (and --beads for the bead export), read each of the newly-reported findings, and re-point every citation whose target genuinely moved (most should be simple line-number updates once the current declaration is located) or mark it with a written reason if the citation's claim no longer holds and needs prose changed, not just a line number. Re-run --symbol clean afterward. Consider whether tools/citation_relocate.py (plant-tower-defense-2174, landed this session) can do the bulk of this mechanically rather than by hand.
close_reason: Re-derived findings fresh rather than trusting the bead's stale eleven: 84 --symbol findings, 14 against the named pest.gd symbols. citation_relocate.py, run --base <cycle-139 fix commit> --head HEAD, correctly relocated all 14 across the full 69-commit span (only 1 unrelated pest.gd citation refused, for cause) -- used as the precision source, cross-checked against manual declarations. Also found 11 MORE stale citations to these same symbols that --symbol's own same-line-only regex misses entirely (wrapped across markdown lines) -- filed as plant-tower-defense-o7fd. Fixed 25 kanban.md lines total. 2 citations' surrounding CLAIMS (not just line numbers) no longer fully hold -- flagged with written notes rather than silently re-pointed (Plant.take_damage's 'exactly one caller' claim, and _play_death's tween-duration description). --symbol: 84->70 findings (exactly the 14 fixed); default mode 0 findings before and after. Verified on the merged tree: 1116/1116 tests, real import+lint compile, check_all clean.

title: Harsh is no harder than gentle for the strongest tested defense
description: SOURCE: plant-tower-defense-s1o8.5's own build, docs/playtest-sweep.md. Surveyed across the whole road-corpus x difficulty matrix on one seed: RunSim.POLICY_THICKEN (the strongest built-in garden policy) clears every single corpus board on every difficulty profile with full lives remaining and hundreds to thousands of seeds still unspent. The difficulty label currently changes nothing measurable for the strongest tested defense. This is why test_playtest_sweep.gd's NOT-TRIVIAL check is gated against the FLOOR (greedy) garden rather than the winning (thickened) one -- a standing gate that is permanently red proves nothing about the next regression, so the real gap was routed around rather than gated on.
acceptance_criteria: Either difficulty profiles are re-tuned so a thickened garden feels the difference (harsh should cost the player something a thickened garden pays for that gentle does not), or a written decision records that this gap is acceptable and why (e.g. difficulty is meant to matter for a floor/average garden, not an optimal one) -- and either way, test/unit/test_playtest_sweep.gd's docs/playtest-sweep.md note is updated to reflect the resolution rather than staying an open finding.
close_reason: Investigated re-tuning Game.DIFFICULTIES; decided against it (Path 2, written decision). RunSim.thicken_cover stops on board capacity, not the wallet, so squeezing the economy further can't bind for the strongest garden -- seed_yield already separates income by difficulty (125/116/79 plants built under THICKEN, pinned by an existing test) but the minimum defensible garden on every corpus road is cheap enough that even harsh clears it with surplus. The lever that WOULD bind -- the wave curve -- was already deliberately scoped out of DIFFICULTIES since s1o8.3 and has its own open bead, plant-tower-defense-jyaq. docs/playtest-sweep.md carries the full reasoning. Bonus: found and fixed a real bug in 3 places (docs/playtest-sweep.md, test_playtest_sweep.gd's header and its own printed skip message) -- the documented '--filter playtest_sweep_full' command matches nothing and exits 2; corrected to '--filter test_full' everywhere. Verified on the merged 5-lane integration tree: 1115/1115 tests, real import+lint compile.

title: s1o8.4's difficulty half shipped across four cycles and its notes never said so
description:
SOURCE: cycle 178 step 0, and it is a note on an in-progress bead rather than new work.

plant-tower-defense-s1o8.4 has been IN_PROGRESS for many cycles and its DIFFICULTY half
is now complete without anyone updating it:

  cycle 161  the title-screen difficulty picker
  cycle 171  the upgrade delta (unrelated, but the picker's neighbour)
  cycle 174  per-difficulty high scores, and the title record line names the profile
  cycle 177  the post-mortem names the profile

So "pick a board AND a difficulty on the title screen" is half shipped. The BOARD half is
what remains, and it is blocked on plant-tower-defense-s1o8.2 (the road corpus), which is
itself unblocked since cycle 170.

THE ASK IS SMALL: update s1o8.4's own NOTES to say which half is done and which is not,
the way s1o8.1's notes did. That is what made s1o8.1 recoverable when cycle 170 finally
picked it up -- its DONE/STILL OPEN list was accurate and the cycle could act on it in
one read.

WHY IT IS WORTH A BEAD AT ALL: cycle 176's pre-flight rule exists because an in-progress
bead is invisible to both `bd ready` and `bd blocked`. The rule surfaces it; nothing makes
its notes true. An in-progress bead with stale notes is worse than one with none, because
the next cycle trusts them.

CONSIDER WHETHER IT SHOULD BE SPLIT instead. "Pick a board and a difficulty" is two
features sharing a screen, and the difficulty one is done. Splitting would let the
difficulty half close and leave a clean board-picker bead blocked on the corpus -- which
is probably the honest shape, but it is a queue-hygiene call worth making deliberately.

ACCEPTANCE: s1o8.4 either carries accurate DONE / STILL OPEN notes naming the cycles that
shipped each part, or has been split with the finished half closed; and its blocked-on
relationship to s1o8.2 is still correct after whichever.

title: Three hard-coded matches answer the same question about a plant id
description:
SOURCE: cycle 178, kanban.md "New in cycle 178" bullet 1.

The same lookup is written as a hard-coded `match id:` in three places:

  Game._new_plant           game/game.gd:2046      id -> constructor
  PlantCatalog.reach        game/plant_catalog.gd:289  id -> the subclass's constant
  PlantCatalog.can_grow     added in cycle 178, same shape, same reason

Each is individually defensible and each is documented. Together they are one lookup
written three times, and EVERY ONE ANSWERS WRONG FOR A PLANT ADDED WITHOUT TOUCHING IT.
A new subclass gets its ladder for free from Plant.has_upgrades(); the catalogue goes on
saying "Does not grow" until somebody edits the match.

THE ASK: an id -> class map, held where the constructors already live (_new_plant), that
the other two can derive from.

WHAT MAKES THIS SAFE TO ATTEMPT and is the reason it is filed rather than done in 178:
cycle 178 added test_the_catalogue_and_the_plants_agree_about_which_can_grow, which
instantiates every id and compares can_grow against has_upgrades. That test is the
regression net for this refactor -- it fails by name if the derivation gets any plant
wrong. Read it before starting.

DO NOT ASSUME A MAP IS BETTER. GDScript classes are not first-class values in the way
this needs; `match id: CORN: return CornCobbler.new()` may genuinely be the clearest
expression available, and a Dictionary of Callables can be worse to read for no gain in
safety once the cross-check exists. The deliverable is a DECISION with the attempt behind
it, not necessarily a map.

AND CHECK HOW MANY MATCHES THERE REALLY ARE. `grep -c "match id:"` gives 3 in
plant_catalog.gd and 1 in game.gd on 2026-08-20; some of those three are not this lookup.
Enumerate before designing.

ACCEPTANCE: every id-keyed match over the plant catalogue is enumerated with what it maps
to; either they derive from one map with the cross-check still green, or a recorded
decision that three explicit matches are clearer than one map, with the attempt described.

title: Write down the rule the difficulty labels arrived at, before the next screen re-derives it
description:
SOURCE: cycle 177, kanban.md "New in cycle 177" bullet 1. PLAYER-FACING.

Cycles 161, 171, 174 and 177 put the difficulty on every screen that reports a number.
The rule they arrived at without ever stating it:

  a surface that reports a NUMBER  says which profile produced it
                                   (title record line, post-mortem score line, ribbon)
  a surface that reports a STATE   says it once, where the player can go look
                                   (pause card)
  the HUD                          says nothing, deliberately -- it reports state
                                   continuously and its message row has been the binding
                                   width constraint in three separate cycles

That is a coherent answer and it is written nowhere a designer would find it. `grep -c
difficulty`: title_screen 30, run_summary 7, pause_screen 5, hud 0.

THE ASK is small and is NOT more difficulty labels: write the rule down where the next
screen's author will read it. OVERLAY_GRAMMAR.md is the closest existing home -- it
already records how the board's marks stay distinguishable, which is the same kind of
cross-surface convention.

WHY IT IS WORTH DOING AT ALL: the next surface to report a number will be built by
someone who has to re-derive this, and the failure mode is not a missing label. It is a
label added to the HUD, which is the one surface where it costs a row the game has spent
three cycles protecting.

CHECK THE CLAIM BEFORE WRITING IT. The four-cycle history above is reconstructed from
close reasons; read them rather than trusting this summary, and if the rule was actually
inconsistent somewhere, say so instead of tidying it into a pattern.

ACCEPTANCE: the number/state/HUD rule is recorded in a file a screen author reads, with
the four surfaces named as its evidence; and if reading the history shows the rule was
not actually followed consistently, that is recorded instead.

title: Every absence-shaped finding should name the cheap check that would disconfirm it
description:
SOURCE: cycle 177 step 4, from a bug found by distrusting a tool's verdict.

citation_rebind.py reported TEXT IS GONE for four citations whose text was sitting in the
file, findable by grep, one indent away -- it compared with rstrip() while
`citation_check --snapshot` stores each line with its LEADING indentation removed. Fixed
in cycle 177.

THE GENERAL SHAPE, and it is why this is a bead rather than a note: an ABSENCE is the
verdict a comparison bug produces most readily, and it is the verdict that reads as most
final. "Not found" looks like a fact about the world. It is a fact about the comparison.

THE ASK: sweep this repo's checkers for verdicts of the form "X is not present" and ask,
for each, what a BUG in the comparison would produce. Candidates from their own output:

  name_check          "not declared" for a name it cannot resolve
  suite_reach_check   "no test names it"
  message_corpus_check "missing from the corpus"
  citation_check      "no longer resolving"
  harness_patch_check  "the local patch is gone"

FOR EACH, THE QUESTION IS WHETHER A CHEAP INDEPENDENT CHECK EXISTS. For citation_rebind
it was one grep. Where such a check exists, say so in the tool's own finding text so the
reader reaches for it -- "if you did not expect this, grep for the string" is worth more
than another paragraph of NOT COVERED.

DO NOT ADD A CHECKER FOR THIS. It is a documentation and phrasing pass over tools that
already exist, and .claude/skills/house-static-checker is explicit that a procedure ending
in not building one is a success.

ACCEPTANCE: every absence-shaped finding in tools/*.py either names the cheap independent
check that would disconfirm it, or records that none exists; and the sweep's denominator
is stated with the grep that produced it.

title: Record what each DEFAULTED verb leaves unset, and which branches that makes unreachable
description:
SOURCE: cycle 177, kanban.md "New in cycle 177" bullet 2. PLAYER-FACING in what it
protects: these verbs are how a screen gets driven for verification, and a branch no verb
can reach is a branch no live check ever sees.

Cycle 177 wanted to photograph the run summary's FIRST-RECORD sentence and could not.
`cmd end_run` leaves `previous_best` at its -1 default, so RunSummary.first_record()
(game/run_summary.gd:290) is false for every synthetic run and the card always takes the
new-best branch instead.

NOTHING IS WRONG WITH THE VERB. devtools_ext/commands.gd is classified DEFAULTED in
test_selftest.gd precisely to record that its setters leave a partial state. What is
missing is the consequence: WHICH branches each DEFAULTED verb cannot reach.

THE ASK: one line per verb in that classification saying what it leaves unset and what
that makes unreachable. The denominator is already there -- the DEFAULTED_VERBS list
names them -- so this is a read, not a survey.

DERIVE IT BY READING THE HANDLER, not by driving each one. Each handler in
devtools_ext/commands.gd builds a stats dictionary; the fields it omits are the fields
whose defaults decide the branch. end_run's is previous_best. Reading is cheaper than
launching and it is also more complete: a branch you fail to reach by driving might be
unreachable for a different reason.

WATCH FOR THE ONE THAT IS ACTUALLY A BUG. A verb that omits a field NOTHING branches on
is fine. A verb that omits a field the screen's headline depends on is a verb that cannot
verify the thing it exists to verify, and that one deserves fixing rather than
documenting. Say which is which.

ACCEPTANCE: every DEFAULTED verb carries a note naming the fields it leaves unset and the
branches that makes unreachable; any verb found unable to reach the branch it exists to
drive is either fixed or filed separately with that stated.

title: A refusal about an occupied cell should point at the plant already there
description:
SOURCE: cycle 175, kanban.md "New in cycle 175" bullet 2, promoted. PLAYER-FACING.

Cycle 175 made the wrong-ground refusals point at the packet that would work. Five of
the ten refusals in Game.refusal_corpus() still have no gesture at all, and for most of
them that is right -- two are unreachable, and "the run is over" has nothing to point at.

ONE OF THEM IS DIFFERENT: "something is already growing there".

The player clicked a cell that is perfectly good ground and got refused. The thing that
refused them is SITTING RIGHT THERE and the game knows exactly which node it is --
Game._plants[cell]. Every other refusal points at a packet in the bar, or at nothing.
This one wants to point at the BOARD.

WHY THAT IS A DIFFERENT KIND OF WORK, and the reason it was left as a first sighting
rather than bundled into lyj5: every existing denial gesture is Hud._shake_control on a
Control in the side panel. A plant is a Node2D on the board. There is no shake for it,
and inventing one means deciding whether the board is allowed to animate in response to
a refused click at all.

READ assert-an-animation BEFORE WRITING A TWEEN. Plant already has a planting pop whose
tween owns its own destination, and that file records what it cost twice -- a paused
plant photographed at 0.4 scale reading as a broken sprite, and a headless test that can
only compare the sprite against itself. A denial shake on a plant must not make the same
trade: set the final state first, animate away from it and back.

AND CHECK WHETHER THE CELL CUE ALREADY SAYS THIS. PlacementPreview draws a blocked
bracket for an occupied cell (cycle 163 darkened its colour), so the player may already
be getting a static answer and the refusal is merely repeating it in words. If so, the
honest close is "no gesture needed, the cue already says it" -- which is a legitimate
result, not a failure.

ACCEPTANCE: a recorded decision on whether the board should answer a refused click, with
the existing blocked-cell cue read first; and if it should, a gesture that leaves the
plant in a correct state when animations are off, asserted in test_dir rather than only
looked at.

title: Decide, per baseline, whether it belongs in git
description:
SOURCE: cycle 176, kanban.md "New in cycle 176" bullet 1. OUTSIDE the citation
neighbourhood -- this is about how this repo stores baselines generally.

Three baselines work by the same mechanism and only one is recoverable:

  tools/suite_reach_baseline.json      TRACKED in git. Diffable, revertable,
                                       comparable across machines.
  .devtools/citations.json             GITIGNORED (.gitignore:8, `.devtools/*`).
  user://ui_findings_baseline.json     Outside the repo entirely, in the player's
                                       user:// directory.

Cycle 176 spent real effort recovering the second one after cycle 175 overwrote it, and
succeeded only because the file's mtime happened to match a commit an hour earlier. The
next one may not be datable at all.

THE QUESTION IS WHETHER THAT ASYMMETRY IS A DECISION OR AN ACCIDENT. Each was created by
a different cycle and none of them argued the placement. There are real reasons on both
sides:

  TRACKING IT     recoverable, diffable, and a refresh becomes a reviewable commit
                  rather than a silent overwrite.
  NOT TRACKING IT the citations snapshot is 232KB of derived data that changes every
                  cycle, which is repository noise; and the UI baseline is genuinely
                  per-machine, since it records what a particular renderer produced.

SO THE ANSWER IS PROBABLY NOT "TRACK THEM ALL". It may well be "track the citations one,
leave the UI one, and say why in each file's header" -- but that is the deliverable, not
the assumption.

CHECK WHETHER user:// IS EVEN A CHOICE. CLAUDE.md records that Godot has no
--user-data-dir flag and honours no GODOT_USERDATA env var (harness gh#28), so the UI
baseline may have nowhere else to live. Read that before proposing to move it.

ACCEPTANCE: a recorded decision per baseline with its reasoning, written into the file or
tool that owns it rather than only into a bead; and if any moves into git, one refresh
performed as a commit to prove the workflow works.

title: Write down how to verify a transient effect, and how to drive a function that fails silently
description:
SOURCE: cycle 175 step 4, from two techniques that turned a confused reading into a
settled one. OUTSIDE the refusal neighbourhood -- this is about driving the bridge.

Cycle 175 spent two rounds on a silent no-op and one on a misread, and both had a
technique that would have avoided them. Neither is written down anywhere.

1. A TRANSIENT EFFECT USUALLY LEAVES BOOKKEEPING. Hud._shake_control stores its tween in
   `_shake_tweens[control]`, so "did the RIGHT button shake" is answerable after the
   shake is over -- a fact rather than a race. Reading that beat every attempt to
   photograph the animation. The general move: before trying to catch an effect
   mid-flight, look for the record it leaves.

2. BRACKET ONE ACTION WITH TWO READS. I had the shake record before and after, but the
   "before" was three commands stale and a changed tween id read as a false positive.
   Re-reading immediately either side of a single run-method settled it in one command.

3. AND THE ONE THAT COST THE MOST: a silent early return is the worst shape to drive
   blind. `_click_at` takes a SCREEN position and subtracts `_entities.position`; fed
   board-local coordinates it returns with no message, no cue and no error, which is
   indistinguishable from the feature under test being broken. The workaround that worked
   was to call the pure predicate directly and compare it against the observed behaviour
   -- verify the parts separately when the whole is silent.

WHERE THIS GOES IS THE FIRST QUESTION, NOT THE LAST. `.claude/skills/read-a-moving-value`
owns the neighbouring question ("what was moving when I read it") and 2 and 3 may simply
be paragraphs there rather than a new skill. Cycle 168 logged a skill as missing that
already existed under another name, and the rule from that is that "absent" is matched on
what a skill DOES, not on its title. READ read-a-moving-value BEFORE WRITING ANYTHING.

AND USE IT IN THE SAME CYCLE, on a real case not drawn from this bead -- the cycle skill
is explicit that the first application is what tells you whether it is a recipe or an
essay.

ACCEPTANCE: the three techniques are written where a session driving the bridge will find
them, in whichever existing skill is the right home; and the closing commit names a case
the new text was applied to that this bead did not supply.

title: Find out whether close reasons actually engage with their acceptance criteria
description:
SOURCE: cycle 174 step 5, which added the rule this bead makes checkable.

Step 2 of the cycle now ends "close against the ACCEPTANCE" -- re-read the criteria
against WHAT SHIPPED rather than against what you built. Cycle 174 needed a second
commit because those two readings felt identical: the bead asked that a player "can
find out which difficulty a run is on without leaving it", the work named the profile on
the title screen, and that read as satisfying it until the words were read again.

A RULE THAT DEPENDS ON REMEMBERING TO RE-READ IS THE WEAKEST KIND. This project's own
answer to that is usually a gate, and there may be a cheap one here.

THE OBSERVATION THAT MAKES IT POSSIBLE: bd close --reason= is prose, and this project
writes long ones that already quote the acceptance -- cycle 174's close begins by
listing all three criteria and marking each. bead_prose_check.py already reads every
close_reason in the JSONL export, so the machinery for reading them exists.

CANDIDATE, and it is advisory at best: for a closed bead whose acceptance_criteria field
is non-empty, does the close_reason mention it at all? That is a very weak check --
it cannot tell whether the criterion was MET, only whether the closer looked at it --
and .claude/skills/house-static-checker is explicit that a check nobody can action is a
NOTE and exits 0.

SO THE FIRST DELIVERABLE IS THE DENOMINATOR, NOT THE TOOL. How many closed beads have a
non-empty acceptance_criteria? Of those, how many close_reasons visibly engage with it?
If most already do, the rule is being followed and a checker would be a permanently-green
gate, which this project treats as worse than none.

DO NOT BUILD IT IF THE NUMBER IS GOOD. Record the number and close saying so -- that is
the same shape as cycle 89, and the acceptance below permits it deliberately.

ACCEPTANCE: the two counts recorded with the query that produced them, and either an
advisory checker or a written decision that the practice is healthy enough not to need
one.

title: Sweep for defaulted parameters whose default is a global read
description:
SOURCE: cycle 174, kanban.md "New in cycle 174" bullet 2. OUTSIDE the difficulty
neighbourhood -- this is about a shape, not about scores.

RunConfig.best_for(for_endless, difficulty_name := &"") (game/run_config.gd:717) falls
back to the live RunConfig.difficulty when the caller names none. That is right for the
call sites and it means EVERY EXISTING CALLER'S BEHAVIOUR NOW DEPENDS ON A GLOBAL THE
CALLER NEVER MENTIONS.

The cost was immediate and nine tests wide: cycle 174's new test left difficulty on
Gentle, and nine unrelated tests failed because _stash_run_config restored save_path and
endless and not this. The fix was the stash, not the signature -- the default is still
the right design.

THE ASK is a sweep, not a refactor. Any defaulted parameter whose default is a GLOBAL
READ has this property, and the tell is that the default is an expression rather than a
literal. For each one, two questions:

  1. does a test ever leave that global changed? if so, is it in the stash?
  2. would a reader of a CALL SITE know the behaviour depends on it?

STARTING DENOMINATOR, and do not trust it -- derive your own:

  grep -nE "func .*:= *[A-Z][A-Za-z]*\." game/*.gd

That pattern only catches `:= Global.something` in the signature. `best_for`'s own
default is `&""` with the global read in the BODY, which the grep misses entirely -- so
the real set is larger than any signature scan, and the honest first move is to say so.

IF THE COUNT IS SMALL, read them and fix the stash, and say so rather than building a
checker. .claude/skills/house-static-checker is explicit that a procedure ending in not
building one is a success.

ACCEPTANCE: the count recorded with the search that produced it AND a note on what that
search cannot see; every such parameter checked against the two questions above; and any
global a test can leave changed is in _stash_run_config or has a recorded reason it need
not be.

title: CLAUDE.md's 'headless gates are passive' is about the bus and reads as about disk
description:
SOURCE: cycle 172 step 4, from a sentence in CLAUDE.md that is true and reads as
saying more than it does.

The harness section says:

  "A headless gate never touches the bus. lint_project.gd / run_tests.gd bring the
  autoload up passive: safe to run while another session drives this game."

That is true OF THE BUS and it is what the paragraph is about. It reads as a general
claim about headless runs -- "passive", "safe to run" -- and cycle 172 is the
counter-example: a headless run brought RunConfig up, which loaded the player's real
save, migrated it and wrote it back. Passive on the bus, not passive on disk.

THE FIX IS ONE CLAUSE, not a rewrite: say the sentence is about the BUS, and that an
autoload's _ready() runs in a headless process exactly as it does in a real one, so
anything an autoload writes at process start is written by every gate.

WHY IT IS WORTH FILING RATHER THAN JUST EDITING: this text lives inside the harness's
own BEGIN/END markers in CLAUDE.md, which /scaffold-godot-harness rewrites. Editing it
locally is silently reverted on the next refresh -- the cycle skill says as much. So
this goes upstream via skill-feedback-issue against
SeveralHerr/godot-selftest-harness, or it does not stick.

CHECK 0.60.0 FIRST. This project runs 0.38.0 and the machine has 0.60.0
(plant-tower-defense-qcp1). The sentence may already have been reworded upstream, and
filing against a 22-releases-behind install is the failure mode that bead exists to
stop. Read the 0.60.0 template's copy before writing anything.

ACCEPTANCE: either an upstream issue with the proposed clause and the 0.60.0 text
quoted, or a recorded finding that 0.60.0 already says it -- both are a result, and
which one it is must be established by reading the newer template rather than the
installed one.

title: Decide whether run_tests.py should give each run its own save path
description:
SOURCE: cycle 172, kanban.md "New in cycle 172" bullet 3. OUTSIDE this cycle's
neighbourhood in the sense that matters: this is about the RUNNER, not about saving.

Cycle 172 pointed every headless process at RunConfig.HEADLESS_SAVE_PATH
(user://headless_scratch.save) instead of the player's real save. Two concurrent
headless runs therefore share one scratch file.

That is a large improvement on sharing the player's real save and it is not isolation.
user:// cannot be isolated at all -- Godot has no --user-data-dir flag and honours no
GODOT_USERDATA env var (harness gh#28, recorded in CLAUDE.md's bus section), which is
why `launch --isolated` isolates the BUS only.

THE SEAM ALREADY EXISTS and was built for this: PLANT_TD_SAVE_PATH beats the headless
default by design, so a runner that wants a private file sets one per process.

THE QUESTION IS WHETHER run_tests.py SHOULD SET IT AUTOMATICALLY, and it is a real
trade rather than an oversight:

  FOR   concurrent runs stop sharing state, which matters because the cycle skill's
        fan-out form runs several agents at once and name_check is currently the only
        gate documented as parallel-safe.
  AGAINST  a per-run temp path makes a failing run's save state harder to inspect
        afterwards -- right now it is one known file you can cat.

A middle answer exists and should be considered rather than skipped: a path derived
from the pid, kept rather than deleted, and named in the runner's output so a failing
run says where its state went.

DO NOT ALSO CHANGE THE DEFAULT. HEADLESS_SAVE_PATH staying a single known file is
what makes a bare `godot --headless --script res://tools/lint_project.gd` -- which no
wrapper touches -- still safe.

ACCEPTANCE: a recorded decision with its reasoning; if the answer is yes, two
concurrent run_tests.py invocations demonstrably do not share a save file, and the
runner prints where each one's state is.
close_reason: Decided yes: run_tests.py now sets PLANT_TD_SAVE_PATH to a per-pid path, kept and printed; default HEADLESS_SAVE_PATH untouched. Demonstrated with two real concurrent processes, no collision. Full suite 1112/1112 with the new code path live.

title: Decide whether 232px is the right budget for the selection panel's buttons
description:
SOURCE: cycle 171, kanban.md "New in cycle 171" bullet 2. OUTSIDE this cycle's
neighbourhood: the SelectionBox is a layout question, not an upgrade one.

The upgrade button is 232px -- SELECTION_BOX_WIDTH, which is PANEL_WIDTH - 24
(game/hud.gd:504). Cycle 171 put what an upgrade buys onto it and had to cut a verb
off two of the three gain phrases to make them fit:

  "Upgrade (30) · holds 11.4→15.9s"   252px of 232, refused
  "Upgrade (25) · eats 20% faster"    238px of 232, refused
  "Upgrade (20) · 1.0→3.6 dmg"        fits

Both survivors are as short as their unit allows. A fourth ladder plant gets roughly
fourteen characters after the price, and the next honest gain phrase that needs
fifteen has nowhere to go.

THE QUESTION, and it wants deciding once rather than re-litigating per phrase: is 232
the right width for this panel? The side panel is PANEL_WIDTH = 256 (game/hud.gd:31)
against a 1152-wide viewport, so the panel is 22% of the screen and the board has the
rest. Widening it moves the board, which is a real cost and is why this is a decision
rather than a tweak.

THE OTHER TWO ANSWERS, both legitimate: a second line under the button (the comment
above _refresh_selection says the VBox already runs to within 16px of the panel foot,
so this needs measuring, not assuming); or accept 232 and write the constraint into
Plant.upgrade_gain()'s header as a budget the next author has to respect, which is
the cheapest and may be the right one.

DO NOT START BY WIDENING ANYTHING. Measure first: how much slack does SelectionBox
actually have below the button, and what does the board lose per pixel the panel
gains. Both are answerable headlessly.

ACCEPTANCE: a recorded decision with the measurements behind it -- panel width stays
and the budget is documented where a gain phrase is written, OR the box changes and
test_every_upgrade_button_face_fits_the_panel plus the 8px SelectionBox clearance test
both still pass at every shipped viewport size.

title: Write down how to verify a road plant live, before a pest eats it mid-capture
description:
SOURCE: cycle 171 step 4, recorded there as a near-miss rather than a gap.

The Bramble is the only plant that stands ON the road (PlantCatalog.on_road,
game/plant_catalog.gd:454), which makes it the only plant whose live verification is
racing a wave. Cycle 171 placed one, read `upgrade_gain()` off it through
`find-nodes --class Bramble --call upgrade_gain`, took a `scene-tree` capture two
commands later, and the capture had no bramble.gd in it -- a pest had eaten the plant
in between. The ledger's reach line then said the file was not reached, which reads
exactly like the harness under-reporting a file that was executing.

IT WAS NOT A HARNESS BUG. Reach reported the tree as it was at capture time, correctly.
Two commands settled it (the node was absent from the capture; the Chomp's was present
with its script). The cost of NOT checking would have been a false report filed
upstream against a tool that was right.

THE ASK is a recipe, not code: write down how to verify a road plant live, in
.claude/skills/ beside read-a-moving-value, which owns the neighbouring question
("what was moving when I read it"). The candidate answers are `pause` before the
capture, placing during prep, or `set-game-speed` -- and which of those actually works
is the thing to establish by running it, not by reasoning. This is a small skill and
its whole value is that the next session does not re-derive it mid-verification.

CHECK FIRST WHETHER IT BELONGS IN AN EXISTING SKILL. read-a-moving-value may already
cover it, in which case the deliverable is a paragraph there and NOT a new skill --
cycle 168 logged a skill as missing that already existed under another name, and the
rule from that is that "absent" is matched on what a skill DOES, not on its title.

ACCEPTANCE: a written procedure that has been RUN once against a live Bramble and
records which of the candidate approaches actually held the plant still, in whichever
skill file is the right home for it.

title: Find the test helpers that swallow an unusable argument and return a plausible number
description:
SOURCE: cycle 170, from the design `_over_promise_run` needed. OUTSIDE the road
neighbourhood -- this is about the suite's helpers generally.

Cycle 170 gave `_over_promise_run` a road parameter and had to decide what a REFUSED
road does. Falling back to the default was the obvious thing and is the dangerous
one: a caller that passes a road it believes is legal and silently gets the shipped
snake would be measuring the default board and reporting it as the corpus. The
failure produces a PLAUSIBLE NUMBER, on the axis where plausible is
indistinguishable from right. So it returns `road_refusal` and no measurements at
all -- a caller cannot read a zero as a result -- and a test proves the parameter by
USE rather than by existence (same seed, same garden, different road-cell count).

THE ASK: find the other test helpers with the same shape. A helper that takes an
optional input, cannot use it, and carries on with a default is a test that passes
while measuring something other than what it says.

GET THE DENOMINATOR FIRST and do not trust this bead for it -- a first attempt at
the grep here returned 0 and was wrong, because a default argument is frequently on
the SECOND line of a wrapped signature and a single-line pattern misses it. Match
across the whole parameter list:
