  grep -rn -A2 "^func _" test/unit/*.gd | grep -E "= (\[\]|\"\"|0|null|\{\})\)"

For each hit, one question: if the caller passed something this helper cannot use,
would the test FAIL or would it quietly measure the default? Only the second kind is
a finding.

IF THE COUNT IS SMALL, fix them by hand and say so -- .claude/skills/house-static-checker
is explicit that a procedure ending in not building a checker is a success, and cycle
89 is the precedent. A checker here would also be hard to write well: distinguishing
a legitimate default from a swallowed one needs the caller's intent.

ACCEPTANCE: the count recorded with the grep that produced it; every helper that
swallows an unusable argument either refuses it or documents why the default is
right; and a recorded decision on whether a gate is warranted, with the count as its
evidence.

title: Collapse the nine hand-rolled source readers in test/unit onto one helper
description:
SOURCE: cycle 169 step 4, [G-145], filed upstream as
SeveralHerr/godot-selftest-harness#65.

The test helper `_T` ships no way to read a script's source. The checks that need
it are the ones whose seam is a GUARD rather than a value -- `if pest.is_winged:
continue` inside a private method has no predicate to call, and driving the
behaviour asserts the behaviour rather than the exemption.

So every test that has needed this opened a FileAccess by hand. Counted:

  test/unit/test_selftest.gd   5
  test/unit/test_placement.gd  2
  test/unit/test_economy.gd    1

Cycle 169 added a ninth as a file-local `_source_text` in test_selftest.gd, because
that was cheaper than the alternative -- which is exactly how the eighth got there.
Each of the nine re-decides what to do with a null handle, and an unreadable source
is precisely the case where a `contains()` check passes for the wrong reason.

BLOCKED, SOFTLY, ON TWO THINGS. gh#65 has to land, and this project has to be on a
harness that has it -- it currently runs 0.38.0 against 0.60.0 on the machine
(plant-tower-defense-qcp1). Neither is a hard blocker: the nine call sites can be
collapsed onto the local `_source_text` today and repointed at `_T.file_text` later,
and that is probably the right order since it is the same edit twice on a smaller
diff each time.

THE FIX IS NOT VERIFIED UPSTREAM AND THE OPEN QUESTION IS NAMED IN THE ISSUE:
whether `res://` resolves the same for a static on `_T` as for one on the test
script. Settle that before repointing anything.

ACCEPTANCE: the nine hand-rolled FileAccess readers in test/unit/ go through ONE
helper with one null policy; the count is stated in the closing commit; and if
gh#65 has landed and been installed by then, that helper is `_T.file_text` rather
than a project-local copy.

title: Nothing checks a comment that names a test, and this repo is full of them
description:
SOURCE: cycle 169, kanban.md "New in cycle 169" bullet 3. OUTSIDE the notebook
neighbourhood this cycle worked -- this is about GDScript comments repo-wide.

Cycle 169's card gate records, per claim, either an assertion or the NAME of a test
elsewhere that already covers it -- and then asserts that name still exists in the
suite source, so renaming the pointed-at test FAILS the gate rather than silently
orphaning the card. Verified by mutating one name and reading the failure.

THE UNCHECKED FORM IS EVERYWHERE ELSE. This repo's comments name tests and
file:line citations constantly, and nothing checks them. tools/citation_check.py
covers kanban.md and bd fields; its own NOT COVERED line is explicit that it reads
those sources and not GDScript comments.

GET THE DENOMINATOR FIRST, before deciding what to build:

  grep -rn "test_[a-z_]*" game/*.gd | wc -l        # comments naming a test
  grep -rnE "[a-z_]+\.gd:[0-9]+" game/*.gd | wc -l # comments citing a file:line

If either number is small, the right answer is to fix them by hand, say so, and
NOT build a checker -- .claude/skills/house-static-checker is explicit that a
procedure ending in not building one is a success, and cycle 89 is the precedent.
If they are large, the citation half is a mode on citation_check rather than a new
tool, since the resolver already exists and only the source list changes.

WATCH THE SCOPE TRAP: a comment naming a test and a comment citing a file:line are
two different checks with two different failure modes. A test name is verified by
existence; a citation is verified by existence AND by whether the line still
supports the sentence -- and citation_check says in its own output that it cannot
do the second. Do not let one number justify both.

ACCEPTANCE: both counts recorded; every dead test-name pointer in game/*.gd either
fixed or removed; and a decision recorded either way on whether a gate is warranted,
with the count as its evidence.

title: Sweep player-facing prose for qualifiers that are the only reason a sentence is true
description:
SOURCE: cycle 169, kanban.md "New in cycle 169" bullet 2.

Cycle 169 found TWO sentences in the seven-card notebook table whose truth rests
entirely on one qualifier that reads as ordinary prose:

  seen_road_tip       everything WALKING a Bramble stops to chew through it.
                      Bramble.stops() is `return not pest_is_winged`
                      (game/bramble.gd:167-168) -- a winged pest does not stop.
                      Drop the word for brevity and the card is false.

  seen_dead_ground_tip the bars are drawn SLANTED. DEAD_BAR_ANGLE is -PI * 0.25
                      (game/placement_preview.gd:161), and "slanted" is the
                      channel the card itself uses to tell these bars from the
                      bar square to the lane. Tidy toward "the bars" and the
                      distinction the sentence is drawing is gone.

Both are now asserted. Neither was found by READING the prose -- both surfaced
only when someone tried to write the assertion, which is the argument for
sweeping rather than proofreading.

THE ASK: read every player-facing sentence for a qualifier that is load-bearing.
Candidates: only, still, other, walking, slanted, on road, never, first. For each,
ask what would be true if the word were removed, and whether anything would fail.

DERIVE THE SET FROM THE CODE, not from this bead: Hud.message_corpus(),
Hud.HINT_CARDS, NotebookScreen's pages, and Game.refusal_corpus() are four
different tables and this bead names two. `grep -rn "\"note\"\|\"text\"" game/*.gd`
before starting.

FIRST SIGHTING OF THE SHAPE. A checker is NOT the deliverable here -- two
instances in one table is not a denominator, and .claude/skills/house-static-checker
says a procedure that ends in not building one is a success. The deliverable is
the sweep's result and a per-sentence verdict.

ACCEPTANCE: every player-facing sentence carrying a qualifier has a recorded
verdict -- load-bearing and asserted, load-bearing and unassertable with the reason,
or decorative -- and any newly-found load-bearing word has an assertion or a note
saying why it cannot have one.

title: A waiver names one tool; nothing asks what else the line was in scope for
description:
SOURCE: cycle 168, kanban.md "New in cycle 168" bullet 2.

A `# <tool>: ok - <reason>` waiver names ONE tool. Nothing asks what else the
waived line was in scope for.

The worked case: `game/game.gd:3018` carries
`# message-corpus-check: ok - placement refusals are assembled at runtime, not
written here`. That is correct and the reason is true. `message_corpus_check`'s own
NOT COVERED line even says it "does not know the row's WIDTH -- that is the
budget's job". But the budget --
`test_no_message_clips_for_any_plant_in_the_catalogue`
(test/unit/test_selftest.gd:11653) -- sweeps `Hud.message_corpus()`, and a waived
line is by definition not in the corpus. So the string was exempt from a gate that
never waived it, and refusals went unpriced for their whole life. Cycle 168 fixed
this instance via `Game.refusal_corpus()`; the SHAPE is unfixed.

READ THE DENOMINATOR BEFORE BUILDING ANYTHING. `message_corpus_check` reports 7
waived call sites. `python tools/check_all.py --quiet` lists 23 checkers, most of
which offer a waiver. Count the waivers across all of them first: if the total is
small, reading them by hand once is the deliverable and the honest close is "no
checker, here is the audit" -- the house-static-checker skill says a procedure that
ends in NOT building one is a success, and cycle 89 is the precedent.

ACCEPTANCE: a count of every `# <tool>: ok` waiver in the repo, grouped by tool,
with a per-waiver note saying which OTHER gates the waived expression is or is not
in scope for; and either a checker that enforces it or a recorded decision that the
denominator is too small to justify one.

title: The rules that keep being broken may want a checker, not another sentence
description: SOURCE: cycle 167's kanban entry, second bullet. THREE ESCAPING FAILURES IN ONE CYCLE, all of them rules this project has already written down: (1) a shell heredoc ate a backslash and put a LITERAL NEWLINE inside a GDScript string -- it compiled, the suite ran, and the helper silently returned empty; the loop's step 2 names this trap in as many words. (2) an equality test against a tab-indented return line never matched because these files are CRLF. (3) a backticked keyword passed to bd close as a shell argument was run as command substitution and left a HOLE in the field; the loop's step 6 names this trap too. THE UNCOMFORTABLE PART is that (1) and (3) are both documented, both were read recently, and both happened anyway. A rule that is broken by the session that just read it is not short of prose. WHAT A CHECKER WOULD LOOK LIKE, per failure: (1) is checkable statically -- a GDScript string literal containing a raw newline is findable by scanning source, and it is exactly the class house-static-checker exists for. (2) is a coding habit rather than a rule, and probably wants a note in the test helpers rather than a gate. (3) already HAS a checker -- bead_prose_check -- which caught nothing here, because it hunts MANGLED text (a space before a period) and this damage was a clean DELETION. Extending it to notice a suspiciously empty gap in a sentence is plausible but false-positive-prone; the cheaper fix may be a wrapper that refuses to pass prose to bd as an argument at all. ACCEPTANCE: a verdict per failure -- checker, habit note, or accept -- and at least the literal-newline one built, since it is the one that compiles clean and fails silently.

title: Walk gate_aim_check's other two lists: declared-but-undrawn, and getter-only colours
description: SOURCE: cycle 164's kanban entry, second bullet. Cycle 164 walked ONE of the three lists gate_aim_check prints -- the const colours declared in world-space scripts -- and it found a mark that clears neither ground (CornCobbler.SPREAD_ARC_COLOR, filed as plant-tower-defense-uwf8) with nothing having prompted the look. TWO LISTS REMAIN, both already derived and printed by the tool: (1) '11 of the 35 are not seen at a draw call in their own file -- handed to another node, or unused'. Those are the interesting ones, because a colour handed to another node is drawn somewhere the declaring file does not say, and a colour that is UNUSED is dead weight nobody has noticed. Sort them into those two piles; the second pile is deletable. (2) the GETTER colours -- board_dead_color, health_bar_color, hit_flash_color, reach_ring_color, ring_color, shell_flash_color and the rest -- which cycle 164's const scan could not price because they are static funcs rather than consts. Several are known quantities: board_dead_color is DEAD_COLOR at BOARD_DEAD_ALPHA and is already gated in substance; reach_ring_color is the plant reach ring and is adjacent to plant-tower-defense-qt79's open question about whether a ring owes a mark's floor at all. PRICE THEM THE SAME WAY: composited separation against every ground the ink can land on, at the alpha each ships with, using GardenTheme.reads_on_at. The scan cycle 164 used is ten lines and is in that cycle's commit if it helps. EXPECT MOST TO PASS and say so -- the deliverable is the verdict per colour and the two counts, not a bigger table. ACCEPTANCE: both lists walked, each colour given an in-table / out-of-scope / should-be-added verdict with its numbers, any unused colour deleted rather than documented, and gate_aim_check's ratio reported before and after.
close_reason: BOTH LISTS WALKED, and the headline is that nothing is broken -- but only after two computed failures turned out to be unreachable. THE DECLARED-BUT-UNDRAWN LIST (7): none is unused, so nothing is deletable. HEALTH_BAR_NOTCH_COLOR goes to a ColorRect on a plant's health bar (sprite scope). MARK_COLOR and RING_COLOR are returned by getters -- the sole-cover ring and the reach ring. board_dead_color is DEAD_COLOR at BOARD_DEAD_ALPHA and is gated in substance already. health_bar_color, hit_flash_color and shell_flash_color are pest and plant tints, all sprite scope. THE GETTER LIST: deferred_road_color gated; board_dead_color gated in substance; reach_ring_color / ring_color are the reach ring, which is plant-tower-defense-qt79's open question about whether a ring owes a mark's floor at all; the rest are sprite tints. THE REAL FIND IS THE DIMMED STATES. SelectionMarker.held_ink HALVES the alpha, and separation scales by exactly alpha, so every held-over mark loses half its contrast -- and nobody had priced that. Four reachable dimmed rows are now gating, and the tightest pair in the entire table is the held selection marker on grass at 0.124 against a floor of 0.12. TWO COMPUTED FAILURES WERE NOT FINDINGS, and catching that is most of what this cycle was worth: a dimmed WARNING colour fails dirt at 0.075 and CANNOT OCCUR, because both call sites refuse it in as many words ('ARMED OUTRANKS HELD', game/selection_marker.gd:309); and a dimmed sole-cover ring fails GRASS at 0.103 and cannot occur either, because those rings mark ROAD cells only (game/sole_cover_marks.gd:9). A computed failure is a claim and needs its reachability checked before it becomes a finding. gate_aim_check 8 of 35 to 9 of 35.

title: The corn spread arc clears neither ground, and its pips are in the same draw call
description:
SOURCE: cycle 164's triage of every colour declared in a world-space script. It is the ONE
mark on ground that clears neither, and it was found by walking the list rather than by
noticing it.

THE NUMBERS. CornCobbler.SPREAD_ARC_COLOR is luminance 0.785 at alpha 0.45. Composited
that is 0.064 against GROUND_GRASS and 0.113 against GROUND_DIRT, both under
GardenTheme.GROUND_SEPARATION_MIN of 0.12. The arc is drawn from muzzle_pivot(_aim_angle)
out to FAN_LENGTH (game/corn_cobbler.gd:367), so it lies across whatever ground the lane is
made of -- both, in practice, since a cob aims down a road from grass.

WHY CYCLE 164 DID NOT JUST FIX IT. The same draw call paints the muzzle pips in PIP_COLOR
two lines later, and the two read as ONE cue: an arc showing the spread and pips showing
where the kernels go. PIP_COLOR clears both grounds (0.135 / 0.238) because its alpha is
0.95. Moving the arc's colour without the pips splits a cue that is currently one thing,
and moving both is a visual change to the plant every player starts with. That is a
decision, not a repair.

THE ROUTES, and cycle 163 established the arithmetic for choosing between them:
  * RAISE THE ALPHA. At 0.70 the arc needs a base separation of 0.171, and its current
    0.142 from grass is close -- a slightly brighter yellow would clear. This keeps the arc
    and the pips the same hue family.
  * DARKEN IT, which is what BLOCKED_COLOR did. Both grounds sit in the middle of the
    luminance range, so a mark must leave the middle in one direction; from 0.785 the
    shorter trip is UP, not down, which makes this the less natural choice here.
  * DECIDE IT IS EXEMPT. The arc fades (SPREAD_ARC_COLOR.a * fade) and is only up while
    the cob is aiming, so it is arguably a motion cue rather than a mark. That reasoning
    has to be written down beside the constant if it is chosen -- and note it cuts the
    other way too: a cue you see only for a moment needs MORE contrast, not less.

DO NOT WIDEN THE FLOOR. GROUND_SEPARATION_MIN's own header records what it was calibrated
against and that DANGER on dirt already sits only a third clear of it.

ACCEPTANCE: a decision recorded beside SPREAD_ARC_COLOR with its numbers; the two ungated
rows in test_every_board_mark_clears_the_ground_floor_at_the_alpha_it_is_drawn_at either
promoted to gating or given a one-line reason naming this bead as closed; and if anything
moves, a live capture of a cob aiming across both grounds, since the arc and the pips have
to still read as one cue.
close_reason: FIXED WITH THE ANSWER ALREADY IN THE FILE. PIP_RIM_COLOR's own header says why a bare yellow dot needs a rim: 'a bare yellow dot this small dissolves into both a grass tile and the cob's own sprite, and the rim is what keeps it legible'. The spread arc is the SAME yellow as the pips -- literally the same RGB at 0.45 instead of 0.95 -- and had no rim, so it dissolved for exactly the stated reason: 0.064 separation on grass, 0.113 on dirt. The fan now draws the rim first at SPREAD_ARC_WIDTH + SPREAD_ARC_RIM_WIDTH * 2 and the fill on top, which is the pips' own two-pass pattern. THE RIM RATHER THAN A LOUDER ARC, and the arithmetic is why: clearing the floor with the fill alone needs alpha 0.85 -- twice what it is, on a 34 px arc that would then compete with the pips it exists to frame -- or a near-white yellow at luminance 0.91. The rim costs neither and clears both grounds at 0.427 and 0.329. A cue is legible by its darkest channel. THE FIRST MUTATION SURVIVED AND THAT IS THE OTHER HALF OF THIS BEAD. Deleting the rim pass entirely left all 1002 tests green, because the contrast table asserts PIP_RIM_COLOR clears the floor and says nothing about anything drawing with it -- a constant test and a call-site test are different claims, which this project has shipped the gap between before. test_the_spread_arc_is_actually_drawn_with_its_rim reads the source with comments blanked (the paragraph above the call names draw_arc while explaining why there are two) and asserts two arcs; the same mutation now fails naming 'found 1'. WHAT WAS NOT SETTLED: whether a dark outline makes a light arc heavy. At 34 px radius and a 1.2 px rim the captures did not resolve it, and sample-pixels cannot separate the arc's rim from the pips' identical ink at the same radius -- it confirms the ink is in the frame and no more. Resting on the file's own precedent for the identical problem one mark over, and recording that rather than claiming a look.

title: Which board cues are in the contrast table and which are merely correct today
description: SOURCE: cycle 163's kanban entry, second bullet. test_every_board_mark_clears_the_ground_floor_at_the_alpha_it_is_drawn_at (test/unit/test_placement.gd:7136) now carries TWELVE gating rows -- the dead-ground bar board-wide and hovered, the redundant-patch bars, the deferred-road bar, the risk ring on both grounds, and both placement brackets on both grounds -- plus two ungated reach-ring rows with their numbers printed. THE BOARD DRAWS MORE MARKS THAN TWELVE. So the answer to 'which cues are gated' is known to be 'not all of them', and the gap is enumerable: plant-tower-defense-w86n already asks for every drawn colour swept at its shipped alpha, and tools/gate_aim_check.py already derives the list of colours declared in world-space scripts -- 35 of them, 3 currently named in any gate assertion. THIS BEAD IS THE INTERSECTION: for each of those 35, is it in the contrast table, and if not, is that because it is out of scope (drawn on a sprite, carried by motion) or because nobody added it? THE DISTINCTION MATTERS because cycle 163's finding was not that a colour was wrong -- it was that OK_COLOR cleared both grounds and BLOCKED_COLOR cleared neither, and neither was in the table, so the asymmetry could exist for cycles. A cue that is correct today and ungated is one palette edit from being wrong silently. DO NOT ADD ALL 35. Several are on sprites and several are HUD colours that never touch ground. The deliverable is the verdict per colour and the count of each, not a bigger table. ACCEPTANCE: all 35 listed with an in-table / out-of-scope / should-be-added verdict, the should-be-added ones added, and the out-of-scope ones each carrying one sentence of reason.
close_reason: TRIAGED, and the triage is the deliverable. All 25 const colours declared in world-space scripts priced against BOTH grounds at the alpha each ships with, in one scan. THE VERDICTS: 4 already gated (DEAD, OK, BLOCKED, RISK) plus deferred_road_color. 4 ADDED as gating rows -- SelectionMarker.MARKER_COLOR and WARNING_COLOR, each on grass and dirt; both clear comfortably today, and the point of the rows is that BLOCKED_COLOR also looked fine right up until a palette convention pushed it to 0.004. 2 ADDED UNGATED with their numbers printed: CornCobbler.SPREAD_ARC_COLOR clears NEITHER ground at 0.064 grass and 0.113 dirt, and is drawn from muzzle_pivot out to FAN_LENGTH so it lies across the lane -- filed as plant-tower-defense-uwf8 rather than fixed, because the same draw call paints the muzzle pips in PIP_COLOR and moving one without the other splits a cue that reads as one thing. OUT OF SCOPE, with reasons: 14 are drawn on a SPRITE rather than on ground (the chomp's fangs and chew ring, the corn's pips, the sunflower's five gauge colours, the sundew's droplets, the plant health bars, the pest tints and fought ring) -- reads_on_ground's own header says it cannot see a sprite underneath. 4 are WASHES rather than marks (DROUGHT_TINT and RAIN_TINT at 0.20 and 0.18, PATCH_COLOR at 0.10, SHADOW_COLOR at 0.22): a wash is legible as a change to the whole field rather than as a shape against ground, and a mark's floor is the wrong question for it. THE SHARPEST FINDING IS AN ALPHA ONE: WARNING_COLOR is Color(GardenTheme.DANGER, 0.95), the SAME palette colour the blocked bracket failed with, and it clears dirt at 0.151 purely because its alpha is 0.95 rather than 0.75 -- at the bracket's alpha it would be 0.119, under the floor. One colour, two verdicts, decided by alpha alone. That is the whole argument for pricing marks AS DRAWN. gate_aim_check moved 3 of 35 to 8 of 35.

title: Keep the wrong drafts: which checkers still have their first-draft story
description: SOURCE: cycle 162's kanban entry, first bullet. THE OBSERVATION: tools/method_call_check.py went through three wrong states before it was worth committing, and every one produced a RULE rather than a tweak -- stopping at the project boundary resolved 0 of 2214; checking engine-typed receivers produced 29 findings that were all a Node-typed variable holding a scripted autoload; dropping the index-omissions list produced 4 that were all 'free', a real Object method the API index does not carry. All three are in its docstring, because the final logic alone does not explain why any of those guards exist and a future edit would remove them. WHICH CHECKERS HAVE THIS AND WHICH DO NOT: gate_aim_check (cycle 153) and teaching_ledger_check (cycle 154) both carry a first-draft story; method_call_check now does. The older ones -- group_leak_check, world_control_check, message_corpus_check, citation_check, suite_reach_check, mirror_check and the rest -- mostly carry a fixture-and-mutations block, which is the house convention, but not the DRAFTS. THE QUESTION IS NOT WHETHER THEY WERE BUILT RIGHT. It is whether the reasoning behind each guard survived. A mutations block says what to re-run; a draft story says why a guard is there, which is what stops it being deleted as dead weight. THE WORK: read each checker's guards and ask, per guard, whether the file says why it exists. Where it does not and the reason is recoverable from git history or a close reason, add a line. Where it is not recoverable, say so -- 'this guard predates the record' is worth knowing. ACCEPTANCE: a per-checker verdict, the recoverable reasons written into the files, and the unrecoverable ones named rather than invented.

title: Name the screens that speak in a register other than the player's
description: SOURCE: cycle 161's kanban entry, second bullet, after the label-reading sweep met its own limit. THE OBSERVATION: the Designer's Notebook legitimises developer vocabulary. Filenames (dandelion.png in the page footer), pixel counts ('Reaches 192 px, about 3.0 cells'), and 'never on paper' are all in-voice on a screen whose conceit is a designer's working notes -- and every one of them would be a finding on the pause card or the options rows. So plant-tower-defense-bo6h's method, reading each label as a player, is WEAKER on that screen than anywhere else, and the sweep cannot tell the difference from a screenshot. THE ASK IS SMALL AND IS MOSTLY WRITING IT DOWN: name the screens whose register differs from the player's, and say what that licenses. Today the answer is one screen and one licence -- the notebook may speak as a developer -- but the value is that the next person sweeping labels knows to stop rather than filing three findings that are the conceit working. WHERE IT GOES: notebook_screen.gd's own header is the obvious home, since it is the file a confused reader opens. A sentence in bo6h's method would rot; a sentence in the file will be found. CHECK THE OTHER DIRECTION TOO, which is the part that could produce real work: is there anywhere the notebook's register LEAKS into a screen that should be speaking to the player? The plant pages' 'Reaches 192 px' has a twin in the shop's own detail line, and if that one also says px it is a leak rather than a conceit. ACCEPTANCE: the register named in notebook_screen.gd's header with what it licenses; a check of whether any of the notebook's developer vocabulary appears on a player-facing surface outside it; and either a finding from that check or a sentence saying there was none.

title: Capture the analyzer's warnings in lint instead of inspecting the load result
description: SOURCE: cycle 160 closing plant-tower-defense-zlm2, which measured that the one-line fix does not work. THE STRUCTURAL PROBLEM: tools/lint_project.gd's _check_scripts_compile (line 693) calls load(p) and inspects res == null and can_instantiate(). A script carrying x.no_such_method() on a statically typed receiver does BOTH successfully, so Godot's unsafe_method_access warning -- which the analyzer does emit -- never reaches an exit code. Enabling it in project.godot was measured and changes nothing. WHAT WOULD WORK is capturing the analyzer's OUTPUT rather than the load RESULT: run the compile in a subprocess and scan stderr, the way tools/import_check.py already scans --import's output for SCRIPT ERROR. import_check is the working model in this very repo. WHY IT IS P3 RATHER THAN P1 despite the blind spot being real: lint_project.gd is HARNESS-OWNED, so a local patch is reverted by the next /scaffold-godot-harness. This wants filing upstream against godot-selftest-harness, and gh#64 already carries the documentation half with the load()-based cause recorded in it. Check whether that issue has been acted on before starting. EXPECT A LARGE FIRST COUNT and plan for it: this codebase calls methods on Variant-typed Dictionary values everywhere, which is the same warning class. The harness already has the pattern for that -- UI findings are split NEW vs PRE against a baseline -- so a baseline is the likely shape rather than a wall of findings on day one. ACCEPTANCE: the count printed before any gating decision, a working capture of at least the unsafe_method_access class, and either gating with a baseline or a recorded reason not to.
close_reason: PREMISE WRONG, AND THE MEASUREMENT IS BETTER THAN THE FIX WOULD HAVE BEEN. The bead asked lint to capture the analyzer's unsafe_method_access warning instead of inspecting the load result. There is no such warning to capture. Measured with three probes: (1) Godot DOES hard-error on an unknown method for a BUILTIN receiver -- var d: Dictionary then d.no_such() is 'Parse Error: Function not found in base Dictionary', exit 1, no settings needed; (2) it does NOT for an Object-derived one -- var n: Node2D then n.no_such_engine_method() is exit 0 and silent, because any Object may gain a method at runtime via a script or set_script, which is a language decision rather than a harness gap; (3) unsafe_method_access is the OPPOSITE case -- it fires on a VARIANT-typed receiver, warning when the type is unknown and saying nothing when the type is known and the method absent. That explains cycle 160's null result rather than leaving it filed. BUILT tools/method_call_check.py instead, project-owned so no scaffold reverts it; check_all 22 -> 23. It resolves a call where the receiver's declared type is one of THIS PROJECT's class_names, completing the member list through the engine API index name_check already maintains. 284 calls resolved, 0 findings today, and planting cycle 159's game.run_over() back produces exactly one finding naming the file, line, receiver and class. ITS OWN HISTORY IS THE FIXTURE and is in the docstring: stopping at the project boundary resolved 0 calls of 2214 (honest and worthless -- the denominator rule earning its place); checking engine-typed receivers gave 29 findings that were all 'var _dev: Node' holding the DevTools autoload, which is the language working; and dropping INDEX_OMITS gave 4 that were all 'free', a real Object method the 4.7.1 index does not list while queue_free is. Each was measured, not guessed. The 922 untyped and 842 engine-typed receivers it skips are counted and printed, because a checker resolving 284 of 2048 must say so.

title: Site every refusal's reasoning where the next person will be tempted
description:
SOURCE: cycle 160's kanban entry, second bullet, written after deciding where a negative
result should live.

THE OBSERVATION. Cycle 160 measured that a proposed fix does not work and put the finding
in tools/check_all.py's NOT COVERED -- the sentence a reader sees immediately after the
"22 of 22 clean" that invites the wrong conclusion. Not in the closed bead, because nobody
re-reads a closed bead before trying something; not only in log-devtools.md, because it is
chronological and nobody greps a log for "did we already try this".

THE SWEEP: every bead this project closed as REFUSED rather than as done, asking whether
its reasoning is readable from the CODE it is about or only from bd.

THE GOOD CASES ARE ALREADY HERE and are the model. plant-tower-defense-ix76 decided a
60-seed husk keeps the same rot floor, and the reasoning sits above MIN_HUSK_LIFETIME in
game/compost_meter.gd where anyone re-pricing that constant opens it. -7bhb decided the
husk rot clock gets no hold, and the reasoning sits above CompostMeter._process, which is
where a future reader would go to ADD one. Cycle 148's three-budget decision sits in
game/cue_legend.gd's audit block, which is the block anyone pricing a teaching surface
already reads.

THE CANDIDATES TO CHECK are the refusals whose subject is not a single constant, since
those are the ones with no obvious home: -xfbo (the second legend page), -i550 (a
duplicate), and any decision recorded only in a close reason. bd list --status=closed and
read the close reasons for the word DECIDED or NOT BUILDING.

THE TEST FOR EACH: if someone had the same idea tomorrow, what file would they open first?
If the reasoning is not in that file, it is not doing its job -- and the fix is a paragraph
where they will be standing, not a longer close reason.

DO NOT MOVE THE PROSE OUT OF bd. The close reason is the record of the decision and stays;
what is being added is a pointer at the place the temptation arrives. Duplication is the
right answer here and is why this is a sweep rather than a refactor.

ACCEPTANCE: every refused bead listed with the file a re-tempted reader would open, a
verdict on whether the reasoning is there, and a paragraph added for each one that is
missing. The count of each is the deliverable -- "eleven refusals, eight already sited,
three moved" says something a list of eleven does not.

title: Write down that the gates are strong on names and blind on calls
description: SOURCE: cycle 159's kanban entry, second bullet, written after finding that a call to a nonexistent method passes every gate (plant-tower-defense-zlm2 is the defect; this is the DOCUMENTATION half and is worth doing even if that one is refused). THE SPLIT: every static gate this project owns asks about NAMES. name_check resolves types, class_names, autoloads, preload paths and method names inside string literals. suite_reach_check counts whether a symbol is NAMED by a test. gate_aim_check counts whether a colour is NAMED in an assertion. bead_ref_check, citation_check, teaching_ledger_check -- all of them resolve identifiers or count mentions. NOT ONE asks whether a CALL is well-formed, and that is not an accident: a name is cheap to resolve from source and a call needs a type system. THE PROBLEM IS WHAT 'ALL GATES GREEN' READS AS. check_all prints '22 of 22 clean' and a reader takes more from that than it means. The one gate that could close the gap is lint_project.gd, which actually compiles -- and it is not asking Godot for the warnings that would. WHERE IT BELONGS: check_all.py's own NOT COVERED line is the right place, since it is the sentence a reader sees after the number that invites the wrong conclusion. It already says it inherits every blind spot below it and compiles nothing; what it does not say is that the blind spot has a SHAPE -- names yes, calls no. ACCEPTANCE: one paragraph in check_all.py's NOT COVERED naming the split, cross-referenced from name_check's, and a sentence in CLAUDE.md's harness section replacing 'engine classes and their members' which currently reads as covering call sites.

title: A verb label cannot be mistaken for a readout, and a noun label can
description: SOURCE: cycle 158's kanban entry, first bullet, written as a POSITIVE rule after a sweep in which two screens came back clean. THE OBSERVATION: the Keys screen is a model and nothing had said so. Every row is a verb phrase naming an action -- 'hold the garden still', 'run the garden faster, or slower', 'close what is open' -- so no noun/value confusion is available to it. The pause card's failure that same cycle was the opposite shape: two NOUN phrases ('Back to the garden', 'Back to the gate') three words apart doing opposite things. And cycle 157's difficulty button was the same class again -- a button reading 'Standard' is a value where the reader needs a verb or a noun for the setting. THREE INSTANCES, ONE RULE: a label naming a VERB cannot be read as a readout; a label naming a NOUN or a VALUE can. THE WORK is a positive sweep rather than a defect hunt: every Button text in game/, sorted into verb-labelled and noun-labelled, and for each noun-labelled one the question 'could a player read this as a readout rather than a control'. Most will be fine -- 'Options' and 'Keys' are doors and read as doors. The interesting ones are buttons whose text is a VALUE, since those are the ones that look like output. DERIVE THE SET rather than listing it: every string assigned to a Button's text or carried in a table that becomes one, which is Hud's packet rack, PauseScreen.BUTTONS, TitleScreen's menu, OptionsScreen's rows, KeyBindingScreen and RunSummary. ACCEPTANCE: the derived list with a verb/noun/value verdict each, the value-labelled ones examined specifically, and any change carrying the reason rather than a preference.

title: A blanked-string scan hides dictionary-key access, and nothing says so
description: SOURCE: cycle 156, caught mid-sweep. Every house checker in tools/ that scans GDScript uses gdsource.strip_comments with strings=BLANK, for a good reason stated everywhere: a rule satisfied by prose is not a rule. But this project passes run state between nodes as DICTIONARY KEYS -- Hud._refresh_prep_bar (game/hud.gd:1830) reads state.get('prep_total') -- and blanking hollows those out. A scan looking for readers of a value therefore misses every reader that goes through a Dictionary, which in this codebase is most of the ones that cross a node boundary. THE ASK IS NOT to stop blanking. It is a NOT COVERED sentence, in gdsource.py itself where every caller reads it, saying: BLANK hides Dictionary keys, and if what you are tracing crosses a node boundary in this project it probably travels as one. Then audit the existing checkers for which of them are answering a question that Dictionary keys are part of -- message_corpus_check and suite_reach_check are the first two to look at, since both trace values by name. ACCEPTANCE: the sentence in gdsource.py's docstring, and a verdict per existing checker on whether its question includes Dictionary-keyed access, with any that do either switched to KEEP with a reason or given their own NOT COVERED line.

title: A wave-strength multiplier, re-verified against the strictly-rising curve
description: SOURCE: cycle 155, deliberately cut from plant-tower-defense-s1o8.3's scope. Game.DIFFICULTIES (game/game.gd:54) now varies the three ROOM constants -- beds, prep seconds, opening seeds. It does not touch the wave curve, and that was a scope decision rather than an oversight. WHY IT IS NOT A ONE-LINE MULTIPLIER: WaveDirector._raw_threat's own block records that the threat curve is asserted to rise strictly wave over wave OUT TO 300, and that moving MUTATION_START_WAVE re-prices every wave from there to the end of the table. A strength scale is a change that has to be re-verified against that property, not added beside it. THE CANDIDATE HOOKS, read rather than guessed: WaveDirector.health_scale_for(wave) and speed_scale_for(wave) are static (game/wave_director.gd:1351 and :1362) so a per-run scale on them needs a different shape than a field; current_wave_pest_count() (game/wave_director.gd:969) is an instance method and is the clean single hook, at the cost of changing counts the threat table is asserted against. DECIDE WHICH AXIS FIRST -- count, health or speed -- because they are not interchangeable: more pests is more clicks, tougher pests is more damage per unit of the player's attention, and faster pests is less time to react. Only the last one interacts with prep_seconds, which the profiles already vary. ACCEPTANCE: one axis scaled per profile, the strictly-rising assertion re-run and still passing (or its threshold consciously moved with the reason recorded), and a live capture of the same wave on two profiles showing the difference.

title: Sort every hand-maintained table into missing-link and unformalisable
description:
SOURCE: cycle 154's kanban entry, second bullet, written after making one such table
checkable.

game/cue_legend.gd:80 carries a hand-maintained table, one line per grammar row, marking
each TAUGHT or untaught. It drifted twice in the same direction -- row 4, then row 6 --
each time claiming untaught for a cue that hints already taught. Correcting it a third
time would have bought exactly one cycle.

WHAT MADE IT CHECKABLE WAS A LINK THAT DID NOT EXIST. Hud.HINT_CARDS (game/hud.gd:3953)
gained a grammar_row key (game/hud.gd:3936) saying which numbered row each hint teaches,
0 for the four of seven that teach a RULE rather than a mark. Before that key, a tool
could confirm a row claiming TAUGHT named something real and could NOT confirm that a row
claiming untaught was unclaimed -- and only the second direction has ever gone wrong.

SO THE QUESTION FOR EVERY OTHER HAND-MAINTAINED TABLE HERE IS NOT "is it right" BUT "what
link is missing that would let something else say so". Enumerate them first; the ones
worth naming from this cycle's neighbourhood are the OVERLAY_GRAMMAR row table, the
notebook's PAGES kinds, RunConfig.HINTS against Hud.HINT_CARDS (already gated by
test_every_hint_has_a_notebook_card, so this one is DONE and is the model), and
Milestones.TABLE.

AND SORT THEM INTO TWO PILES, which is most of the value. plant-tower-defense-snhb is the
same class for notebook CARDS and is harder for a stated reason: a card's claim is prose
about a mechanic, and only a human can read whether it still describes the game. That is
not a missing link, it is an unformalisable claim, and a bead asking for a checker over it
would be asking for the wrong thing. Some of the tables in the sweep will land in that
pile and the deliverable for those is a sentence saying so.

ACCEPTANCE: every hand-maintained table in game/ enumerated with its two ends named; each
sorted into MISSING LINK (with the link named) or UNFORMALISABLE (with the reason); and at
least one from the first pile actually given its link and its checker, since a sweep that
produces only a list is the thing this project's own derive-the-list skill warns about.

title: Find a derivable denominator for the other two gate families
description:
SOURCE: cycle 153, building tools/gate_aim_check.py. It supports ONE gate family and says
so in its own NOT COVERED line; this is the item that would let it support the other two.

gate_aim_check answers "of the sites this gate could speak about, how many actually ask
it" and got 2 of 35 for the reads_on family. It works because that family's denominator IS
derivable: a colour declared in a world-space script is a colour drawn on the playfield.

THE OTHER TWO GATES HAVE NO SUCH DERIVATION, and that is the whole item:

  * `contained-in` asks whether a Control's box sits inside a panel's. The denominator is
    every (Control, panel) pair the game can put on screen -- and the containment
    relationships live in .tscn scenes and in runtime reparenting, neither of which a
    source scan can see. The live bridge CAN see them: `findings` already reports
    `ui_escapes_panel` for a sibling panel, so the denominator may be derivable from a
    scene-tree snapshot rather than from source. That is a different KIND of derivation
    than gate_aim_check currently does, and is the interesting part.
  * the budget helpers (rows_that_fit, the message-row width, panel_width) ask whether
    content fits a box. The denominator is every producer that can put text in that box --
    which plant-tower-defense-9ji4 is already about for the message row specifically, and
    which found the corpus and the width sweep covering different sets.

DO 9ji4 FIRST if only one gets done: it is the same question for one concrete box and its
answer will say whether the general version is worth building.

WHY NOT JUST HAND-MAINTAIN A LIST: because a hand-maintained list of what a gate should
cover is exactly the thing that let the dead-ground bar sit below the floor for many
cycles while every gate passed. .claude/skills/derive-the-list is the standing rule and it
applies to a checker's own denominator more sharply than to anything else.

ACCEPTANCE: at least one more gate family supported with a DERIVED denominator, its
derivation printed so a reader can see what it swept, and the NOT COVERED line updated to
name what is still absent. A reasoned "this one cannot be derived, here is why" for a
family is also an acceptable close -- it is the same deliverable as the tool, written down.

title: A cue's ground is where its ink lands, not where its cell sits
description:
SOURCE: cycle 153's kanban entry, first bullet, written after a screenshot refuted a
reasoned exclusion in a constant's own header. PLAYER-FACING in consequence.

THE RULE THE SWEEP WOULD ESTABLISH: a cue's ground is the set of grounds its INK can land
on, not the ground of the cell that owns it.

WHAT PROMPTED IT. Cycle 153 priced RISK_COLOR against grass alone because hovering only
reaches buildable ground. True of the CELL and false of the RING: RISK_RADIUS is 30
(game/placement_preview.gd:94) against Board.CELL's 64 (game/board.gd:14), so a ring
anchored one cell from the lane spills across it, and the capture taken to confirm the
colour showed the lower arc on dirt at 0.063 separation. Every number said grass-only.

HALF THE ENUMERATION IS ALREADY DONE and it is reassuring, which is why this is P3 rather
than P2: CHEW_RING_RADIUS 22 (game/chomp_flower.gd:96), FANG_RADIUS 28 (:158) and
HIT_RADIUS 18 (game/kernel.gd:8) all sit inside the 32 px half-cell and cannot spill. The
extreme case is the other direction entirely -- a reach ring runs to 176 px, crosses both
grounds and several cells, and is already known to fail the floor
(plant-tower-defense-qt79). So the interesting population is the middle: cues between 32
and 64 px.

THE WORK: enumerate every drawn cue's INK EXTENT against the 32 px half-cell, and for each
one that exceeds it, price its colour against every ground the ink can reach rather than
against the anchor cell's. Extent is not always a named RADIUS -- a bar is an arm vector,
a bracket is a box, a dashed arc is a radius plus a width -- so the derivation is the work,
per .claude/skills/derive-the-list.

AND SAY WHAT YOU FOUND EVEN IF IT IS NOTHING. A sweep that reports "three cues can spill
and all three already clear both grounds" is worth the same as one that finds a failure,
because the next person adding a cue gets a number instead of a habit.

ACCEPTANCE: a table of cue, ink extent, cells reachable and grounds reachable; every cue
that can spill either already gated against every ground it reaches in
test_every_board_mark_clears_the_ground_floor_at_the_alpha_it_is_drawn_at, or given a
written reason; and the 32 px half-cell derived from Board.CELL rather than typed.

title: Reconcile the remaining 63 open gaps against 0.60.0
description: SOURCE: cycle 152 closing plant-tower-defense-8wzs, which reconciled 12 of 75 and said the rest should follow. The 63 remaining are OLDER and were filed against versions further back (many at 0.18.0 to 0.19.0, against a harness now 40+ releases ahead), so the hit rate should be at least as high as this cycle's 10-of-12. Use the same one command: python <0.60.0 templates>/tools/devtools.py --project . harness-version --client, then VERIFY what it says -- its second number was wrong twelve times out of twelve this cycle (gh#63), so treat its credited-fixed list as a hypothesis and open the installed code for each. Append one new status line per id, never rewrite. ACCEPTANCE: a commit appending the lines and printing the four-way split, partial fine.

title: Two tools read log-devtools.md with different resolution rules, and only one says which
description:
SOURCE: cycle 152, reconciling the gap ledger. Out-of-neighbourhood: nothing to do with
cues, colour or the board.

tools/upstream_gaps.py:245 filters a gap by `gap["fields"].get("status", "open")` -- the
status on THAT BLOCK, not the status resolved for that id from its last mention.
log-devtools.md is append-only by design, so a gap's history is `open` then `open` then
`fixed` on separate lines in separate blocks. A per-block filter therefore selects a gap
from an earlier `open` block even after a later block closed it.

DO NOT ASSUME THIS IS A BUG. The comment directly above it (tools/upstream_gaps.py:238-241)
records exactly why it reads blocks: two sessions once minted the same id for different
gaps, and pooling them silently dropped one for a whole release. The suffixed-id machinery
below (`G-027b`) exists to keep both. So per-block is deliberate for IDENTITY, and the open
question is narrower: does the STATUS FILTER want the block's status or the id's? Those are
the same until an id is reused, and reuse is precisely the case that code was written for.

WHY IT IS WORTH ASKING NOW: cycle 152 watched the 0.60.0 harness make the per-line version
of this mistake and report eleven fixed gaps as open (filed upstream as gh#63). This
project's own gap_ledger.py:189 gets it right and says so in four words -- "last write
wins: entries are chronological". Two tools in this repo read the same file with different
resolution rules, and only one of them has written down which rule it uses and why.

MEASURE BEFORE DECIDING. Run upstream_gaps.py over the current log and count how many
selected gaps have a LATER block marking them fixed or wontfix. If the answer is zero the
question is theoretical and the right output is a comment recording that; if it is not
zero, those are gaps that would be re-filed upstream after being closed, which is the
concrete cost.

ACCEPTANCE: the count, printed; and either a fix that resolves status per id while keeping
the suffixed-id identity rule intact, or a comment beside :245 stating that per-block is
the intended reading and what it costs. A tool that reads an append-only log owes the
reader its resolution rule in writing, which is the whole lesson gap_ledger.py:189 already
demonstrates.
close_reason: Fixed tools/upstream_gaps.py: status filter now resolves each gap id's latest block instead of the block being iterated (5 real ids affected: G-024,G-030,G-033,G-077,G-078). New tools/upstream_gaps_status_check.py fixture-checker added, picked up by check_all.py. Same bug confirmed live in installed harness 0.66.0, filed as [G-157] for upstream skill-feedback-issue.

title: Decide whether a reach ring owes the same ground floor a mark does
description:
SOURCE: cycle 152, found by the alpha-aware gate built for plant-tower-defense-3h0s the
moment it was pointed at the board. The ring row was in the sweep for completeness and it
is the row that failed.

THE NUMBER. PlacementPreview draws the reach ring in DEAD_COLOR at RING_ALPHA (0.30) when
the hovered cell is dead or redundant -- game/placement_preview.gd:229-231. Composited on
GROUND_GRASS that is 0.112 separation against GardenTheme.GROUND_SEPARATION_MIN of 0.12,
and on GROUND_DIRT it is worse. To clear the floor at 0.30 alpha a mark needs a BASE
separation of 0.400 from each ground, and the two grounds sit at luminance 0.643 and 0.534,
so a single colour clearing both at that alpha has to be at or under 0.134 -- near black.

WHY IT IS NOT SIMPLY FIXED, and why cycle 152 left it ungated with its number printed in
test_every_board_mark_clears_the_ground_floor_at_the_alpha_it_is_drawn_at rather than
waiving it or turning the gate red:

  * A RING MAY NOT BE A MARK. GROUND_SEPARATION_MIN's own header
    (game/garden_theme.gd:163) records what it was calibrated against: the page frame's
    cream, its ink hairline, and the road hatch -- small strokes, all of them. A 176 px
    radius arc is a different object and a floor derived from hairlines may simply be the
    wrong floor for it. Deciding that is the first half of this item and it is a judgement,
    not a measurement.
  * RING_ALPHA IS SHARED. The same constant carries every NON-dead reach ring, which is
    the cue a player sees on every hover of every plant and which nothing has ever
    complained about. Raising it to clear this floor changes a cue that is not broken.
  * THE DEAD RING IS EVIDENCE, NOT A CLAIM. DEAD_COLOR's header says the ring is drawn
    dimmed precisely so the player can watch the circle fall short of the road rather than
    be told it does. Its job is to be quiet next to the bar. A ring as loud as the bar
    would invert the pair.

SO THE ROUTES, and the bead does not pick one: split RING_ALPHA so the dead ring has its
own; give the ring a floor of its own with the reasoning written where the constant is;
or decide the ring is exempt by KIND and say so in GROUND_SEPARATION_MIN's header, which
is the block anyone pricing a mark already opens.

ACCEPTANCE: a decision recorded beside whichever constant it is about, the ungated rows in
that test either promoted to gating or given a one-line reason naming this bead as closed,
and if anything moves, a screenshot of a dead hover on a real board showing the ring and
the bar still read as one statement rather than two.

title: Count the kanban backlog's stale rate instead of estimating it at half
description:
SOURCE: cycle 151, step 6 -- mining kanban.md's older sections for an item outside the
cycle's neighbourhood, per the loop's own rule.

TWO ENTRIES WERE OPENED AND BOTH WERE FULLY SHIPPED. The region is around kanban.md:4471.

  * "A Sticky Sundew catching a pest is a metadata write with no picture and no sound."
    Both halves false: _claim() opens with Sfx.play(Sfx.SUNDEW_CLAIM)
    (game/sticky_sundew.gd:278) and calls pest.flash_hit(true) (:287), cycle 149's glancing
    flinch. Corrected in place by cycle 151 rather than deleted.
  * "A field named for the fix already exists on Plant, and nothing ever writes to it"
    (_wobble_time). Plant._wobble has driven every plant's idle sway for many cycles --
    cycle 70 already recorded believing this cue unbuilt and being wrong about it, which
    makes this the SECOND time that particular absence claim has been believed.

Two for two on a sample of two is not a measurement, and that is the point: the pre-flight
step says "roughly half of the historical sections are stale" and nobody has ever counted.

THE WORK: run kanban-staleness-audit over the region and PRINT THE RATIO -- entries checked,
entries shipped, entries still true, entries no longer meaningful. The number is the
deliverable. A miner who knows the local hit rate is 40 percent reads differently from one
who assumes the backlog is a backlog.

DO NOT DELETE THE STALE ONES. Cycle 151's correction is the pattern: leave the entry, append
a dated note saying what shipped and where, so the record of what was true survives and the
next miner is stopped before opening the file. kanban-staleness-audit's own closing note
makes this split.

ACCEPTANCE: a counted ratio over a named line range, every entry found shipped carrying an
in-place correction with a file:line, and any entry found STILL TRUE and worth doing filed
as its own bead -- which is the half of this that produces new work rather than tidying.

title: Sort the seven hint gates into threshold-by-necessity and threshold-by-convenience
description:
SOURCE: cycle 151's kanban entry, second bullet, written after building the first hint in
this game whose gate is not a threshold.

Every one-shot before cycle 151 waited for the board to cross a line.
Game.DEFER_HINT_MIN_GUNS (game/game.gd:30) is a count; the upgrade tip waits on a bank
balance; the sole-cover tip waits on a first selection. _offer_dead_ground_hint
(game/game.gd:1427) has no threshold and cannot have one -- PlacementPreview.board_dead_cells
falls back to the garden's unlocks, so its marks are on the board from the opening frame --
so it fires on the frame the cue starts being ABOUT something the player is doing.

THE GENERAL FORM: when a cue is ambient, no amount of it is informative, and the gate has to
be the MOMENT it acquires a subject rather than a QUANTITY of it.

THE WORK: walk all seven ids in RunConfig.HINTS (game/run_config.gd:275) and sort each gate
into threshold-by-necessity or threshold-by-convenience. _offer_defer_hint
(game/game.gd:1511) is genuinely the first kind and argues it at length -- a lone gun defers
every cell it covers on any board, so the mark says nothing about THIS garden until there
are two. The upgrade tip is the one to look at hardest: "can they afford it yet" may be the
second kind wearing the first's clothes, because affording an upgrade and being ready to
hear about one are different events, and cycle 145 already found the hint budget's real
scarcity is DELIVERY rather than slots.

NOT A REFACTOR. The deliverable is a verdict per hint with its reason, and a change only
where a gate is convenience. A hint whose gate is right needs its reason written down, which
is most of the value: the next cue's author copies whichever gate they read first.

ACCEPTANCE: seven verdicts recorded where the gate lives, not in the bead; and for any gate
found to be convenience, either the moment-shaped replacement with a test that pins it, or a
sentence saying why the threshold is kept.

title: A one-shot mutation runner that refuses a dirty tree
description:
SOURCE: cycle 150, method note from plant-tower-defense-4uts. Tooling, small,
and it would have saved that cycle roughly half an hour.

WHAT HAPPENED. A six-mutation sweep was run as one background command and KILLED
mid-mutation, twice, at around five suite runs in. Each kill left a game file
modified with a `.bak` beside it -- and a mutated working tree reads exactly like
a finding, so any gate run against it reports a defect that does not exist. Both
times the recovery was: notice the kill, check `git status`, confirm the `.bak`
matched HEAD byte-for-byte, restore from git, re-verify the suite.

The recovery is mechanical and always the same, which is the argument for a tool
rather than a note.

THE ASK: a small runner under tools/ that performs ONE mutation safely.

    python tools/mutate_once.py --file game/pest.gd --needle <file> --repl <file>

  * asserts the needle matches EXACTLY ONCE before touching anything, and exits 3
    with NOT-APPLIED otherwise -- "did not apply" and "survived" are opposite
    results and .claude/skills/house-static-checker says so at length;
  * writes the mutation, runs `tools/run_tests.py`, and restores in a `finally`;
  * reports RED / SURVIVED / BROKEN-RUN, mapping exit 2 explicitly rather than by
    truthiness (a `2` proves nothing was verified);
  * on startup, REFUSES to run if `git status --porcelain` shows a modified game
    file or any `*.bak` -- which is the check that turns a previous kill from a
    silent poisoning into a loud stop.

Needles come from FILES rather than argv because they are multi-line GDScript
with tabs; passing them through a shell is the escaping trap this repo has paid
for repeatedly.

NOT A CHECKER: it belongs in tools/ but must NOT carry the `NOT COVERED:` marker,
or check_all will try to run it as a gate. Add it to that file's NOT_A_CHECKER
with a reason, the way repo_walk.py is handled.

WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS UNNECESSARY: nothing. Mutation is how this project has
learned that four of its tests were fragile (cycle 150), that a guard was dead
code (146), that a survivor can be a finding about the code (142), and that two
freshly-written tests asserted the wrong thing (149). It is a standing practice
and it currently has no tool.

ACCEPTANCE: one mutation runs end to end through the tool, a deliberately
mis-typed needle reports NOT-APPLIED rather than doing nothing quietly, and a
dirty tree is refused. Exercise all three before closing.

title: The legend's TAUGHT/untaught ledger drifted, and both ends of it are enumerable
description:
SOURCE: cycle 148's kanban entry, second bullet. Tooling, and it is the SECOND
hand-maintained teaching table to drift in four cycles.

WHAT DRIFTED. game/cue_legend.gd carries a ledger, one line per grammar row,
marking each TAUGHT or untaught with the instances that draw it. Row 4 (small
solid ring) read "untaught" for two cycles after cycle 145 taught it with
RunConfig.HINT_SOLE_COVER. Nothing checks that table against anything.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A COMMENT USUALLY DOES. That ledger is not decoration:
it is the input to the audit block beneath it, which is where every "should this
cue get a legend row" decision in this project has been made and re-read. Cycle
148 closed plant-tower-defense-4tt4 by reading it. A wrong TAUGHT hides a cue
nobody is teaching; a wrong untaught invites work that is already done -- which
is the direction it drifted, and cycle 148 nearly spent a cycle on it.

WHY THIS IS EASIER THAN plant-tower-defense-snhb, which is the same class for
notebook CARDS: both ends of this mapping are enumerable in code.
  * The grammar rows are numbered 1..11 in the ledger itself.
  * The teaching surfaces are RunConfig.HINTS (six ids), CueLegend.ROWS (six
    rows, each with a "shape" key), and Hud.HINT_CARDS.
  * So "row N is TAUGHT" is a claim that some named surface teaches it, and
    "untaught" is a claim that none does.

snhb's problem is that a card's claim is PROSE about a mechanic and only a human
can read it. This one is a mapping between two lists.

THE ASK: a stdlib-only checker under tools/, per
.claude/skills/house-static-checker/SKILL.md, that parses the ledger and asserts:
  * every row marked TAUGHT names a shape that CueLegend.ROWS actually carries,
    OR a hint id that RunConfig.HINTS actually holds;
  * every row marked untaught has a verdict beneath it in the audit block (the
    block is delimited and the verdicts are bulleted, so this is findable);
  * the ledger's row count matches the grammar's.

MEASURE BEFORE BUILDING, which is that skill's first rule and the reason cycle 89
correctly did NOT build one: count how many rows there are (eleven), how many the
parse actually recognises, and how many mismatches exist today. If the answer is
"one, the one cycle 148 just fixed", the honest deliverable may be a kanban entry
recording the second sighting rather than a tool -- and that is a success, not a
failure of this bead.

WATCH THE REGION TRAP the same skill names: the ledger is scoped by a BEGIN/END
comment pair. mirror_check.py measured a 21-character stub for exactly this
reason and reported clean. Assert the parsed row count, or a truncated ledger
reads as a clean one.

ACCEPTANCE: either a checker with the usual exit contract, a printed denominator
naming how many ledger rows it parsed of how many exist, a NOT COVERED line and a
fixture -- or a written measurement saying why the count does not justify one.
close_reason: Built tools/teaching_ledger_check.py; check_all 21 -> 22. THE LEDGER HAD DRIFTED AGAIN, on a different row and in the same direction: row 6 read 'untaught' while HINT_DEFERRED_ROAD (cycle 144) and HINT_DEAD_GROUND (cycle 151) both taught its two bars -- and cycle 151 read that very block while shipping the second of them. The bead's own example, row 4, had already been fixed by hand; the drift it predicted was live somewhere else. Corrected. THE CHECKABLE DIRECTION NEEDED A NEW KEY: nothing in the codebase recorded which grammar row a hint teaches, so Hud.HINT_CARDS entries now carry grammar_row (0 for the four hints that teach a RULE rather than a mark). Without it a tool can confirm a TAUGHT row names something real but cannot confirm an 'untaught' row is unclaimed -- which is the only direction that has ever actually drifted here. GATING rather than advisory, deliberately: every finding has one correct response, so a red run is always actionable and can never become permanent. Two mutations: reverting row 6 produced the finding naming both hints; disabling the grammar_row read made it vanish while the ledger was still wrong. NOT COVERED is explicit that the TAUGHT direction is counted rather than matched -- the ledger names rows in prose and CueLegend.ROWS names them by SHAPE const, and deciding those are the same row is judgement, not lookup.

title: Ask for the constant term before adding a third wave to a crowded property
description:
SOURCE: cycle 147's kanban entry, second bullet, generalised from the wilt.

THE PATTERN. `Plant._wobble`'s rotation carries two sinusoids on deliberately
separate clocks -- the sway and the flinch -- and its own comment records why:
a shared clock at a harmonic ratio reads as "sways more when bitten" rather than
as a flinch. Adding a THIRD oscillation there has the same problem against
whichever of the two it comes closest to.

Cycle 147's wilt sidestepped it entirely by being a HELD OFFSET rather than a
wave. A DC term has no frequency to phase-lock with, composes additively by
construction, and leaves both existing channels at full amplitude -- a wilting
plant still breathes and still flinches, from a leaning rest position. That is a
strictly better outcome than a third wave and it cost nothing.

SO: whenever a property already carries motion and a new state needs saying, ask
for the CONSTANT TERM before reaching for another wave.

TWO CANDIDATES IN THIS GAME THAT ARE CURRENTLY UNSAID, and both are "this plant
cannot do its job right now", which is exactly the kind of state a held offset
suits:

  * A PLANT WHOSE MINT BUFF LAPSED. Game._refresh recomputes
    neighbour_interval_scale from scratch every time, and a plant that HAD a
    neighbour buff and lost it (the Mint was uprooted, eaten, or moved) fires
    slower with nothing on screen saying so. Confirm before building: read
    Plant.composed_interval and whatever writes neighbour_interval_scale, and
    check whether the selection panel already says it -- if the panel names the
    buff, this may be a non-problem.
  * A CHOMP ON COOLDOWN. Read chomp_flower.gd for whether a post-meal cooldown
    exists at all before assuming it does; the bead that filed the champ
    (plant-tower-defense-ts34) enumerated the Chomp's overrides and a cooldown
    was not among the ones it named.

BOTH ARE UNCONFIRMED and the first job is confirming them, not building. This
bead is the PATTERN plus two leads, and closing it with "neither turned out to be
real, and here is what I read" is a perfectly good outcome.

WATCH THE BUDGET THE WILT NOW SPENDS: rotation carries sway + flinch + wilt. A
third held offset on the SAME property would add to the wilt, and two constant
terms are indistinguishable from one larger one -- so a second held state on
rotation needs the states to be mutually exclusive, or it needs a different
property. Scale has the breathe and idle_scale_multiplier already. This is why
the pattern is worth writing down rather than applied twice by reflex.

ACCEPTANCE: each candidate confirmed or refuted against the code, in writing; if
one is real, a held offset with a pure static seam and a headless test in the
shape of test_the_wilt_is_a_held_lean_that_neighbours_do_not_share.

title: A by-hand prose correction is only as complete as the count nobody printed
description:
SOURCE: cycle 146's kanban entry, first bullet, found because a correction that
had been MADE turned out not to have held. Tooling, and the class is broader than
the instance.

WHAT HAPPENED. An id invented in cycle 142 was corrected in cycle 142 -- and was
still live in cycle 146, because the correction replaced one occurrence of two
and nobody counted. tools/bead_ref_check.py found it. That is not "somebody made
a mistake": the mistake was noticed, acted on, and the action was silently
incomplete.

THE CLASS. This repo corrects prose by string replacement constantly:
  * citation relocation -- plant-tower-defense-5w4v is 116 citations across four
    cycles, every one a find-and-replace in kanban.md or a bead description.
  * bead prose fixes after the shell ate something (bead_prose_check's whole
    subject).
  * renamed producers, renamed constants, reworded tips -- cycle 145 replaced
    "Hover to compare" in five places across three test files and got the count
    from grep rather than from having counted first.

In every one of those, the correction is only as complete as a count nobody
printed. And the failure is invisible: a partially-applied fix looks exactly like
a fully-applied one from the commit that made it.

THE ASK, and it is deliberately small because the general problem is not
solvable: a helper that makes the COUNT the deliverable rather than the edit.
Something in the shape of

    python tools/prose_replace.py --in kanban.md --from OLD --to NEW [--expect N]

which prints "OLD appears N times in <file>; replaced N" and exits 1 when
--expect disagrees, or when N is 0. Two properties matter more than the
implementation: it reports the count BEFORE and AFTER, and a zero-match
replacement is a FINDING rather than a silent no-op -- that second one is the
exact shape of cycle 143's bug, where two string replacements silently matched
nothing and the run reported success.

DO NOT build it as a general refactoring tool. The value is the denominator, not
the editing; a one-line wrapper that counts and refuses is worth more than
anything clever, and this repo already has the habit of reaching for Python
inline for these edits.

WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS UNNECESSARY: if every by-hand prose correction went through
a checker that re-runs afterwards, the count would not matter. That is true for
bead ids now (bead_ref_check) and for citations (citation_check --against), and
NOT true for the general case -- a reworded tip, a renamed producer, a corrected
count in prose. Those are the ones this is for.

ACCEPTANCE: a stdlib-only tool under tools/ following
.claude/skills/house-static-checker/SKILL.md, with the usual exit contract, that
refuses a zero-match replacement and prints before/after counts. It is a
DEVELOPER tool rather than a gate, so it does not need to join check_all -- and
per the house skill, a tools/*.py without a NOT COVERED line does not, which is
the right outcome here.

title: Audit every tip for whether it names a verb the player can perform
description:
SOURCE: cycle 145's kanban entry, second bullet. PLAYER-FACING, cheap, and every
fix is a rewording inside a budget that already fits.

THE TEST, one sentence: does the tip name a VERB THE PLAYER CAN PERFORM?

Cycle 145 found one that did not. The move tip said "Hover to compare a new
spot" -- true, and it described what the GAME does rather than what the player
can do, so the single sentence a player ever received about moving a plant never
mentioned that moving was possible. The mechanic had shipped two cycles earlier
and was undiscoverable. Reworded to "Or click a spot to move it there.", which
cost nothing because it replaced a clause rather than adding one.

THE REST OF THE SET, read but not yet judged -- that is this bead:

  defer_tip        "Bars mark road your plants skip -- each is busy with the
                   pest ahead. Add depth there."
                   PASSES. "Add depth there" is an instruction.

  sole_cover_tip   "Ringed road cells are held by this plant alone -- lose it
                   and they go unwatched."
                   FAILS the test as written: it is a fact about the mark, with
                   no action. Whether it SHOULD have one is the real question --
                   the player's response is "defend this plant" or "add a second
                   gun", and neither is a click. It may be right as a fact.

  flight_tip       borderline; read it.

  upgrade_tip, road_plant_tip, and the rest: unread.

DO NOT MECHANICALLY REWRITE THEM ALL. The test is a prompt for judgement, not a
rule. A cue that teaches a FACT the player then acts on freely is legitimate, and
turning every tip into an imperative would make the row read like a tutorial. The
sole-cover case is the interesting one precisely because the honest answer might
be "leave it".

WHAT TO ACTUALLY DECIDE, per tip: (1) is there a verb the player can perform in
response, (2) does the sentence name it, (3) if not, is the omission a choice or
an oversight. Cycle 145's was an oversight -- the sentence predated the verb.

BUDGET NOTE: every one of these lives in Hud.message_corpus() and the row's width
is enforced by check_budgets, which has refused a build over this exact prompt
before (188px over). A rewording that grows a clause has to be re-measured. A
rewording that replaces one, as cycle 145's did, does not.

ACCEPTANCE: each tip in the corpus has a recorded verdict -- names a verb,
deliberately does not, or was reworded -- and any rewording keeps the row's
budget green. The closing commit produces all of it.
close_reason:
Every message audited against "does it name a verb the player can perform".

THE VERDICT TABLE, now in test_every_player_message_names_a_verb_or_says_why_not
so a reworded tip has to come back and change a row:

  upgrade_tip           names a verb
  defer_tip             names a verb
  dead_ground_tip       names a verb
  move_window_closed_tip  names a verb
  road_plant_tip        names a verb
  flight_tip            NO, deliberately - names the plant that works; the
                        action is unmistakable, and an imperative here would be
                        telling the player what they can already see
  sole_cover_tip        NO, deliberately - the response is a plan ("defend this
                        plant", "add a second gun over that stretch"), not a
                        click, and both candidate verbs belong to other cues

THE FINDING WAS NOT IN THE TIPS. It was in the placement and move REFUSALS,
which game.gd:2973 and :2944 render to the player verbatim and which no part of
this audit's brief mentioned. Two defects:

1. Both call sites used String.capitalize(), which title-cases every word in
   Godot. The player has been reading "Pests Walk There." and "Something Is
   Already Growing There." for as long as refusals have existed. Confirmed with
   a probe before changing anything. Hud.as_sentence() replaces it.

2. "pests walk there" and "no pests walk there" named no verb, and the second
   reads as GOOD news out of context. Reworded to "pests walk there - try the
   grass" and "this one goes ON the road".

Rewording the first one falsified a comment in commit_move claiming it held "the
same refusal text place_plant gives" - a second copy of the literal, in the same
edit that read the comment saying it matched. Both sites now share
REFUSAL_ON_GRASS.

BUDGET: green, and the gate that should have enforced it did not exist.
Refusals are not in Hud.message_corpus() and cannot be - message_corpus_check
waives the call site as runtime-assembled and says so in its own NOT COVERED
line. That waiver is correct about the source scan and was doing double duty as
an exemption from the WIDTH budget, a different gate, so refusals were the one
class of player-visible message never priced. Game.refusal_corpus() now feeds
test_no_message_clips; a refusal lengthened past the row fails it at 987px of
876, naming the string. All ten refusals are priced, including the two currently
unreachable ones ("off the garden" is guarded out by _click_at, "not paid for"
shakes the plant button), so one that becomes reachable later need not remember
to be measured.

Verified: 1006 tests / 19175 assertions, lint 0, check_all 23/23, name_check 0.
Live: as_sentence through the real show_message renders "Pests walk there - try
the grass." at visible_ratio 1.0 in the 876px row; place_plant on a road cell
returns the reworded string. Ledger reach 2/2 this session's files.

title: Let the over-promise simulator take a road, which unblocks the sibling that needs it
description:
SOURCE: plant-tower-defense-s1o8.1's own "what a fix breaks" section, left
undone by cycle 142 deliberately and recorded in that bead's notes. Small,
concrete, and it unblocks a sibling.

WHAT IT IS. test/unit/test_combat.gd's `_over_promise_run` -- the headless
driven-wave simulator every over-promise test runs on -- builds its board with a
bare `var board := Board.new()` and takes no road. Every wave-pressure number
those tests produce is therefore about one specific snake, and there is no way to
ask "what does this wave do on a different road".

WHY NOW: cycle 142 made the road settable. `Board.set_road(corners)` exists,
returns a refusal string, and must be called BEFORE the board enters the tree --
which is where `_over_promise_run` builds it anyway, so the change is an optional
parameter and one call.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING TIDINESS: s1o8.1's own text says child bead 5
"cannot be written at all" until this takes a board or a road. And the pest
ceiling now has a density test across a three-road corpus
(test_the_pest_ceiling_stays_a_playable_density_on_every_road_in_the_corpus in
test/unit/test_board.gd) which prices 40 pests per road STATICALLY. What it
cannot do is run a wave. The simulator can, and it is the only thing in the suite
that can, so it is the difference between "40 pests would be dense on that road"
and "this wave actually puts N on it".

SCOPE, kept deliberately small:
  * `_over_promise_run` gains an optional road parameter defaulting to the
    default board, so all existing callers are untouched and their numbers do
    not move.
  * ONE test that runs an existing over-promise scenario on a second road from
    the corpus and asserts something true of both -- the peak stays under
    SIMULTANEOUS_PEST_CEILING is the obvious candidate, since that is the bound
    the whole wave table is constructed to hold.

DO NOT, in this bead, convert the four remaining shape-dependent tests (dead
ground, the split cell, the recorded gardens, the Sundew coverage). Those are
s1o8.1's second half, they are geometry rather than pacing, and s1o8.1's notes
already record the hard part: reproducing the game's own search asserts nothing,
so each needs an independent derivation or a property a bad road violates.

ACCEPTANCE: `_over_promise_run` takes a road, every existing over-promise test
passes unchanged with numbers identical to today, and one new test runs a wave on
a non-default corpus road and asserts the ceiling holds. The closing commit
produces all of it -- no running game, no screenshot.

title: verify_ledger --about takes one file while /verify documents it plural, and the fan-out is what needs several
description:
SOURCE: cycle 141, log-devtools.md [G-140]. OUT OF NEIGHBOURHOOD: this is the
verify harness's own tooling, not the game and not the cue or animation work the
last three cycles have been in.

THE GAP. `verify_ledger.py record --about` accepts exactly ONE path and says so
only by failing:

    $ python tools/verify_ledger.py record ... --about game/chomp_flower.gd game/plant.gd
    usage: verify_ledger.py [-h] {record,reach,stats} ...
    verify_ledger.py: error: unrecognized arguments: game/plant.gd

/verify's Phase 5 text describes it plural and bracketed -- "--about <file>
[<file> ...] naming only the file(s) this run set out to verify" -- so the skill
this project runs and the tool this project installs disagree about the
signature. That is the same 0.38.0-vs-0.60.0 spread as G-130 (the ledger
silently dropping `tier`), arriving in a different place.

WHY IT IS WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN NOTING. Cycle 141's change genuinely spanned
two files -- the hook in game/plant.gd and the champ in game/chomp_flower.gd --
and `--about` is precisely the narrowing for that case. Nothing was lost this
time, because the run was not a fan-out and reach came out 1/2 (+1 by alias)
correctly. But `--about` exists FOR the fan-out, where reach's default
denominator is the whole dirty tree and a lane is otherwise graded on a
sibling's uncommitted file. A lane whose work spans two files is exactly the
case that needs it and is exactly the case that cannot use it.

FIRST STEP, and do not skip it: check whether 0.60.0 already takes several.
`python tools/devtools.py harness-version --client` reports this project on
0.38.0 with 0.60.0 on the machine, and .claude/skills/gap-reconcile/SKILL.md is
the procedure for asking that question against the INSTALLED version rather than
the pinned one. If 0.60.0 fixed it, this closes as fixed-in and the entry in
log-devtools.md gets a new status line appended -- never a rewrite of the
existing one.

IF IT IS STILL OPEN AT 0.60.0: it is `nargs="+"` on one argument, and it ships
from a repo I own, so it goes upstream via
.claude/skills/skill-feedback-issue/SKILL.md with the exact command and error
above in the body.

ACCEPTANCE: either a new status line on [G-140] in log-devtools.md recording
`fixed-in: <version>` with the evidence read out of the installed templates, or
an upstream issue filed with the reproduction. Both are things the closing
commit can produce. Do NOT fix it by editing tools/verify_ledger.py in this
