repo: it is harness-managed, .harness_manifest.json lists it, and a local patch
is silently reverted by the next /scaffold-godot-harness.
close_reason: Reconciled via gap-reconcile: fixed-in harness 0.66.0, [G-140] status line appended. No repo code change needed.

title: citation_check counts targets and says drifted, so the pass looks finished before it is
description:
SOURCE: cycle 141, found while relocating drifted citations for the third round
running. Tooling. Small, and it changes how a number in the loop is read.

THE FINDING. `citation_check --against` prints `N drifted` where N counts
distinct TARGETS, not citations. A target cited from three places is one line of
output, so fixing it and re-running surfaces the second citing location as if it
were new drift. Cycle 141 relocated ten, re-ran and got four more, fixed those,
re-ran and got one more -- three rounds, all of them the same targets cited from
somewhere else. `game/chomp_flower.gd:674` alone was cited from a kanban entry,
from a second kanban entry, and from a bead description.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING COSMETIC:
  * The pass looks finished twice before it is, which is how a cycle ends with
    drift it believes it cleared.
  * The loop's step 3 now has a THRESHOLD on this number -- "if --against reports
    more than ten drifted, the relocation is a work item" (added cycle 140). Ten
    targets can be thirty citations, so the threshold is measuring a unit that is
    not the work. That rule is one cycle old and this is the first thing found
    wrong with it.

The tool already knows the answer: it groups locations under each target to
print them. This is a second number from data it holds.

THE ASK: print both counts -- something in the shape of
`N target(s) drifted across M citation(s)` -- and use the citation count in the
loop's threshold. Add the distinction to the tool's own NOT COVERED line, since
"drifted" reading as "citations" is exactly the kind of denominator confusion
every other checker in this repo prints a line about.

GOES WITH plant-tower-defense-nalv rather than being independent: that bead adds
a --symbol mode to the same file and will be reading the same grouping structure.
Doing them together is one read of citation_check.py instead of two, and -nalv's
cross-note on -2174 already ties the three together.

ACCEPTANCE: `citation_check --beads --against <snapshot>` prints both a target
count and a citation count on its summary line, the NOT COVERED line says which
one "drifted" has historically meant, and the loop's step 3 threshold is updated
to name the citation count. The closing commit can produce all three.

title: Schedule the citation-relocation sweep instead of absorbing it into whatever cycle touches a busy file
description:
SOURCE: cycle 140's step-5 workflow change, and two cycles of paying for it.
OUT OF NEIGHBOURHOOD: this is about the loop's own bookkeeping, not the game and
not the cue system cycle 140 worked in.

THE NUMBER. Cycles 139 and 140 each spent something like a third of the cycle
relocating drifted citations, and neither planned to. 139 found ELEVEN dead
citations in game/pest.gd; 140 found NINE more across game/game.gd,
game/hud.gd and game/run_config.gd. Twenty in two cycles.

WHAT MAKES IT A SCHEDULING PROBLEM RATHER THAN A TOOLING ONE (the tooling half
is already plant-tower-defense-nalv and -2174): the size of the pass is set by
HOW MANY LINES THE CYCLE'S FEATURE HAPPENED TO INSERT into a heavily-cited file,
which has nothing to do with what the cycle is for. Cycle 140 added ~30 lines to
game.gd for a one-shot hint and inherited 47 drifted citations. A cycle that
added the same feature to a quiet file would have inherited none.

And every one of the twenty was ALREADY WRONG before the cycle that found it, so
this is not cleanup after one's own mess -- it is real, valuable, previously
invisible work arriving as a tax on whoever touches a busy file.

THE CHANGE IS ALREADY MADE, in .claude/skills/cycle/SKILL.md step 3: if
--against reports more than ten drifted, fix what your own entries cite, file
the rest, and say in the close how many were left. THIS BEAD IS THE OTHER HALF
-- somewhere for the rest to go, and a place to record whether the rule held.

THE WORK: sweep the remaining drifted citations in kanban.md and open bead
descriptions, in batches, reading each landing against the sentence that cites
it rather than restoring by offset. The loop's own step 3 says why offset
restoration is not enough and cycles 139 and 140 both demonstrated it: a
citation landing on a blank line, a bare `##` or a closing brace matches
anywhere, and two of cycle 139's eleven were blank-line landings that a uniform
offset would have carried forward looking perfect.

ACCEPTANCE: a commit that reports the before/after drifted count from
`python tools/citation_check.py --beads --against <snapshot>`, and names how
many of the relocations were pure offset versus how many were already wrong.
That split is the number worth having -- it is the evidence for -nalv, and
nothing else in the repo produces it. Partial is expected and fine; say what
was left.
notes: Cycle 155 measured 94 drifted targets, 79 of them in CLOSED beads -- by a wide margin the highest of the series (13, 21, 71, 11, 0, 14, 26, 13, 73, 14, 22, 94). Cause is the same thesis at its most extreme: ~90 lines inserted at line 51 of game.gd, the most-cited file in the repo, which shifts every citation below it. Drift tracks WHERE a cycle edits, not how much -- and 'near the top of game.gd' is the worst possible where.

title: Name all three teaching-surface budgets where people already read about the first
description:
SOURCE: cycle 140's kanban entry "New in cycle 140", first bullet -- found by a
test failure, not by reading. Tooling/docs, not player-facing.

THE FINDING. This project has THREE teaching-surface budgets and only one of
them is documented anywhere a reader will find it.

  1. The cue legend page. Famous. game/cue_legend.gd:102 prices it -- "row's
     text ends at 294 px inside a 300 px matte and a seventh lands at 340" --
     and at least three beads turn on that number.
  2. The notebook HINTS page. Same matte (NotebookScreen.DRAWING_BOX,
     game/notebook_screen.gd:59, 360x300), entirely separate capacity model:
     hints_capacity() at game/notebook_screen.gd:384 derives three rows from
     SHELF_ROW_TOP 3, HINT_ROW_PITCH 98 and a 94px row, and
     hint_pages_needed() at :402 pages past that. NOTHING outside
     notebook_screen.gd mentions it.
  3. The HUD message row's WIDTH, which is a different axis again and is priced
     by Hud.message_corpus() plus the budget tests.

Cycle 140 added a sixth one-shot hint and hit (2) and (3) in the same run, having
gone in aware only of (1). The card overflowed by 35px and
test_the_notebook_hints_page_gives_back_a_hint_that_was_never_shown caught it,
printing the two available fixes in its own failure message.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING A NEAR-MISS: the legend's audit block is where
anyone pricing a teaching surface will already be reading -- it is the block that
argues, cue by cue, which marks earn a row. Someone standing there learns that
the legend is full and learns nothing about the other two ceilings, so the
natural next thought ("put it in the notebook instead") walks into an
undocumented budget.

THE ASK, deliberately small: one sentence in game/cue_legend.gd's audit block
naming hints_capacity() and the message-row width budget as the other two
ceilings, so the three are legible from the one place people already read. Do
NOT unify them into a shared constant -- they are the same number for different
reasons (a matte height, a row pitch, a font width) and collapsing them would
create a false dependency between three surfaces that are free to change apart.

ACCEPTANCE: the audit block in game/cue_legend.gd names all three budgets with a
file:line for each, and the closing commit can produce that on its own -- no
running game, no screenshot.

title: The bead checkers read a passive export and cannot say it is stale, in either direction
description:
SOURCE: cycle 139's step-3 pass, second sighting of the same mechanism.
G-139 in log-devtools.md filed the first, from the opposite direction.

THE MECHANISM. .beads/issues.jsonl is a PASSIVE EXPORT, and both bead-reading
checkers in this repo read it rather than the Dolt DB:
tools/citation_check.py --beads and tools/bead_prose_check.py. Each says so in
its own NOT COVERED line. What neither says, and what costs time in both
directions:

  * G-139 (cycle 138): the export LAGS bd create, so running the checkers
    straight after filing checks almost nothing. Six beads were filed and
    grep -c s1o8 .beads/issues.jsonl returned 1.
  * THIS SIGHTING (cycle 139), the other direction and worse: after fixing
    four drifted citations inside bead descriptions with bd update
    --body-file, bd show confirmed the DB held the corrected text
    (kanban.md:2119-2127) while citation_check --beads kept reporting the OLD
    text as drifted, because the export still held it. Running `bd export -o
    .beads/issues.jsonl` by hand took the run from "4 drifted, exit 1" to
    "0 drifted, exit 0" with no other change.

A stale export therefore makes a checker report findings that are ALREADY
FIXED. That is strictly worse than missing new ones: a false finding gets
investigated, and the investigation ends at the tool rather than at the data,
which is the "audit the tool" reflex this repo has already filed once
(-efjq, "bisect your own change before auditing the tool").

THE ASK, smallest thing that closes it: have both bead-reading checkers print
a SECOND DENOMINATOR comparing the export against the tracker -- "N issue(s)
in the export; the tracker holds M" -- and say plainly that a mismatch means
the result describes the export rather than the tracker. bd stats gives M
without opening Dolt directly. This is the same shape as every other
denominator in this repo: the number that makes a clean run legible as stale.

Optionally, and cheaper still: have them exit 2 (could not run) rather than 0
when the counts disagree, since "the input is stale" is exactly the
could-not-run case the house contract reserves 2 for.

NOT THE ASK: making the checkers read Dolt. They are stdlib-only static
checkers by house convention (.claude/skills/house-static-checker) and
parallel-safe, and shelling out to bd would cost both properties.

ACCEPTANCE: citation_check.py --beads and bead_prose_check.py each print the
export-vs-tracker pair on every run, a fixture demonstrates the mismatch case,
and the NOT COVERED lines are updated to name it. G-139 gets a new status line
appended in log-devtools.md recording the second sighting and the fix -- never
a rewrite of the existing entry.

title: bead-from-report has no acceptance-file rule, and citation_check saw 1 of 40 draft citations
description:
Two defects found while using .claude/skills/bead-from-report/SKILL.md to file the
plant-tower-defense-s1o8 epic on 2026-08-19. Both are in this repo, so this is a bead
rather than an upstream issue.

## 1. The skill's anti-substitution rule has a hole it does not name

SKILL.md's "Writing it down" section says: "Never put prose in a `bd` field as a shell
argument... Write the description to a file with an editor tool and pass `--body-file`;
`--stdin` and `--design-file` are the same mechanism for the other fields."

`bd create --help` offers `--body-file`, `--design-file` and `--stdin`. It offers **no
acceptance equivalent** — `--acceptance` is a plain string flag. So the single field the
skill does not mention is the only one that MUST go through a shell argument, and it is
subject to exactly the substitution the paragraph exists to prevent.

Fix: add to that section — "Acceptance has no `--file` form. Put the criteria in the body
file as well, and keep the `--acceptance` string free of backticks, `$` and `!`."

## 2. citation_check.py over a draft bead body is near-vacuous

Ran `python tools/citation_check.py --quiet` over six draft bead bodies carrying roughly
forty `file:line` citations. Output:

    citation_check: 1 citation(s) across 6 file(s) [...], 1 resolved, 0 finding(s)

The parser recognised one. Citations written as `(game/board.gd:50-59)` — in parentheses,
without backticks — are invisible to it. Two of the forty were wrong:
`Board.GRASS_EDGE_TILE` cited at board.gd:76 is at :72, and the climb comment cited at
:33-45 is at :36-43. Both were caught by opening the file; the clean run said nothing
about either.

The tool's own NOT COVERED line is honest about what it cannot judge (whether a landed
line SUPPORTS a claim) but says nothing about how much prose its parser simply does not
see. The denominator it prints — "1 citation(s)" — is the signal, and it is easy to read
as "one citation, checked" rather than "thirty-nine invisible".

Fix, either or both:
- SKILL.md: verify citations by reading the landed lines; a clean citation_check on a
  draft is a statement about the handful it parsed.
- citation_check.py: widen the parser to bare parenthesised `path.ext:NN` / `:NN-MM`, or
  print a second denominator naming how many `path:line`-shaped strings it saw and
  declined to parse.

## ACCEPTANCE

- SKILL.md carries the acceptance-flag warning.
- Either citation_check.py parses parenthesised citations (proved by a fixture that
  currently reports 1 and then reports the real count), or SKILL.md states the limit.
- If the parser is widened, `python tools/citation_check.py --self-check` still passes and
  the existing baseline is re-taken deliberately rather than absorbed.
acceptance_criteria: SKILL.md carries the acceptance-flag warning; either citation_check.py parses parenthesised path:line citations, proved by a fixture that reports 1 today and the real count after, or SKILL.md states the limit explicitly.

title: Pick a board and a difficulty on the title screen, inside menu_capacity
description:
## THE ASK

Let the player pick a board and a difficulty before starting a run. Depends on beads
1 and 3.

## THE BUDGET THIS LANDS IN

The title menu is derived, not hand-placed, and it has a computed ceiling:

- `TitleScreen.MENU_BUTTON_NAMES` (game/title_screen.gd:96-98) holds five entries:
  Start, Endless, Notebook, Keys, Options. Its own comment states the contract —
  "the first PRIMARY_COUNT are the full-width rows, the rest fill the grid
  left-to-right then top-to-bottom, and both the focus ring and the entrance stagger
  read it".
- `TitleScreen.menu_capacity()` (game/title_screen.gd:169) **computes** the largest
  menu whose hint line still clears `TitleBackdrop.HORIZON`. It is computed
  precisely so a new destination is checked rather than assumed, and
  test/unit/test_selftest.gd:1181-1182 already compares
  `MENU_BUTTON_NAMES.size()` against it.
- title_screen.gd:41 anticipates this exact bead: "So a sixth destination — credits,
  a difficulty picker, the trophy shelf if it..."

So the design question is not "where does the button go", which is answered, but
whether board and difficulty are **two more destinations** (2 of the remaining
capacity) or **one setup screen** (1). Answer it in the bead's design field before
building, because bead 3 may also want a slot and the capacity is shared.

## WHAT A FIX BREAKS

- test/unit/test_selftest.gd:1155-1250 and test/unit/test_placement.gd:2544-2546
  both iterate `MENU_BUTTON_NAMES + ["HintLabel"]` rather than spelling the list
  out, so they follow a new button automatically — which is what makes them the
  gate rather than a chore.
- The focus ring (`_link_focus`, game/title_screen.gd:711) and the entrance stagger
  (`_play_entrance`, :856) both read the same order.
- `TitleScreen.high_score_text()` (game/title_screen.gd:550) renders
  "Campaign %d · Endless %d". If bead 3 splits scores by difficulty, this string
  and its width budget change with it.

## ACCEPTANCE

- The picked board and difficulty reach `Game` through `RunConfig` and are asserted
  to change the run headlessly.
- `MENU_BUTTON_NAMES.size() <= menu_capacity()` still holds at the shipped viewport
  sizes, by the existing test, with the new destinations in place.
- `python tools/devtools.py findings` reports no NEW UI findings over the title
  screen at the sizes already covered.
- A `/verify` Phase 4 bridge check drives the picker with `press` and confirms the
  run that starts is the one that was picked. This is the one part that genuinely
  needs a live game.
acceptance_criteria: The picked board and difficulty reach Game through RunConfig and change the run, asserted headlessly; MENU_BUTTON_NAMES.size() is still within menu_capacity() at the shipped viewport sizes by the existing test; devtools findings reports no NEW UI findings over the title screen; a /verify Phase 4 bridge check drives the picker with press and confirms the run that starts is the one picked.
notes:
SURFACED BY CYCLE 170's new pre-flight line (bd list --status=in_progress).

This bead is IN_PROGRESS and invisible to both `bd ready` (which excludes in-progress
items) and `bd blocked` (which prints a dependency, not its state). That is exactly
how plant-tower-defense-s1o8.1 sat half-finished for many cycles while blocking three
beads, and cycle 170 added the pre-flight line specifically so this stops happening.

NOT A JUDGEMENT ON THE WORK -- a note that it is claimed and unfinished. If its
expensive half is done, it is now among the cheapest items in the queue and should say
so in its own NOTES the way s1o8.1's did. If it was claimed and never started,
un-claim it so `bd ready` can offer it.

RELEVANT TO CYCLE 170 SPECIFICALLY: the live Sundew coverage test in test_combat.gd
still runs on a `Game`, which builds the default board and cannot be given a road.
Giving Game a road is this bead's plumbing, not s1o8.1's, and s1o8.1 closed saying so.

title: Ask a cell which cues claim it, instead of bisecting the board with screenshots
description:
SOURCE: log-devtools.md [G-138], filed this cycle. HARNESS GAP, and the item
here is the in-project half.

Identifying a 32x5 dark mark on the board took five `screenshot --hide NODE
--region ...` rounds plus a `scene-tree --depth 1` sweep of every child's
position, and the answer was a Line2D pool under a node the first sweep did not
descend into. Two wrong theories came first: `WeatherOverlay.DROUGHT_MARK` (a
horizontal line, but 7px and unaligned to the grid) and a pest health bar (a
32x5 ColorRect at (-16,-34), the right SHAPE, but no pest was within four cells).

`find-nodes --class` cannot answer this, because the question is not what the
node IS. `node-bounds` computes a screen rect for one node; what is wanted is
that inverted over the tree.

THE VERB: `what-drew --at X,Y` walking the CanvasItem tree back-to-front,
reporting every node whose screen bounds contain the point, with `script`,
`z_index`, and whether it paints via `_draw()`, a `Sprite2D`, or a `Line2D`
child. Filed upstream against godot-selftest-harness as [G-138]; this bead is
for the project-side follow-up, which is the part the harness cannot do.

THE PROJECT-SIDE HALF, and it is the more useful one: this board draws at least
four straight marks that a reader has to already know the rules to tell apart --
`placement_preview.gd`'s a6rf block enumerates them and the channels that
separate them (position, orientation, length, count). A `cmd` verb registered in
`devtools_ext/commands.gd` that takes a cell and reports EVERY cue currently
claiming it -- deferred, dead ground, sole cover, unaimed, lane pressure -- is
one call instead of five screenshots, and it is a question only this project can
answer because only this project knows the cue set.

ACCEPTANCE: `cmd cues_at --args '{"x":6,"y":1}'` returns the cues on that cell by
name, with the source each was pushed from. Driven once from a live board and
compared against a `--hide` bisect of the same cell, so the verb is checked
against the method it replaces rather than against itself.
notes: SECOND SIGHTING, cycle 166. Verifying that a Corn Cobbler's spread arc had gained a rim needed 'is this ink at THIS DRAW' and the only tool available answers 'is this ink in this RECT'. sample-pixels over the cob's 80x80 region reported darkest r=0.302 g=0.204 b=0.067 -- PIP_RIM_COLOR on grass, so the ink is in the frame -- but the muzzle PIPS carry the identical rim ink at the identical radius, so no narrowing of --rect can separate the arc's rim from theirs. The verb behaved exactly as documented; what is missing is the question this bead names. CONCRETE SHAPE THIS SIGHTING SUGGESTS: the useful answer would be per-DRAW rather than per-cell -- 'what painted the pixel at (x, y)', with the node and the draw call that owns it. A cell-level answer would not have helped here either, since both marks are in the same cell.

title: A skill for the record-it-or-derive-it fork in a catalogue
description:
SOURCE: lane -i8k9's own report, cycle 137. A skill gap identified by a lane while
doing the work the gap is about; this is the FIRST identification, filed rather than
built per the loop's two-identifications rule.

THE RECURRING DECISION. This repo's catalogues keep meeting the same fork: a fact about
a plant can be RECORDED as a key in PLANTS, or DERIVED by a static function reading
each plant's own constants. Cycle 137's -i8k9 chose derived for `damages` and had to
re-argue the whole trade-off from scratch. The arguments it assembled:

  * FOR RECORDING: the entry is a denominator. A new plant with no `damages` row fails
    loudly at the table, so the decision is forced on whoever adds the plant.
  * FOR DERIVING: there is no second value to leave un-set, so it cannot drift. The
    evidence in-repo is brutal -- plant_catalog.gd's CORN entry carried "the only plant
    in the game that does damage" while three other plants damaged, and
    RunSummary.par_reach_px built its entire benchmark on a citation to that comment.
  * THE CONSTRAINT THAT KILLS THE THIRD OPTION: a Plant virtual method (the shape
    bite_resistance() uses) is unavailable when there is no instance --
    Game.engagement_reach is a static func, and PlacementPreview.dead_ground_cells
    draws the hover cue before any plant of the hovered kind exists. That is the same
    constraint that made `engages` a catalogue key rather than a method, and it is
    checkable rather than a matter of taste.

WHY IT IS A SKILL AND NOT A NOTE. derive-the-list already covers "do not hand-type a
list of cases", and it is cited constantly here. What it does not cover is this fork,
where BOTH options are derived-ish and the question is where the source of truth should
live -- nor the static-context test, which is the thing that actually decides it and is
one grep.

RELATIONSHIP TO -vte, the other lane the same cycle: that one hit the ADJACENT gap, a
derivation whose predicate is a judgement ("the keys the engine names badly") and has
to be a proxy. Both lanes reported derive-the-list as insufficient in the same cycle,
for two different reasons. If a second identification arrives for either, that is the
threshold.

ACCEPTANCE: either the skill exists and has been applied to code it was not written
about, or this is closed recording that the second identification never came.

title: panel_width has no viewport guard, and cycle 137 made SHORT_NAMES able to spend it
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md "New in cycle 137", third entry. Reported by the key-column lane
(-22a) as a latent issue in a file it had just changed, and correctly not fixed there.

THE ASYMMETRY. KeyBindingScreen.panel_height() has a documented viewport ceiling and a
test guarding it, because nine binding rows can outgrow the screen. panel_width() has
NEITHER, and it has the same exposure.

WHY IT IS LIVE NOW RATHER THAN THEORETICAL. Before cycle 137, key_column_width() swept
OS.get_keycode_string(code); a wider SHORT_NAMES entry changed nothing about the panel.
Cycle 137's -vte lane changed the sweep to measure KeyBindings.key_label(code), which
is the correct derivation -- the column should size to what is DRAWN -- and the side
effect is that SHORT_NAMES now feeds panel width. A long enough entry widens the panel
and nothing says so.

THE NUMBERS, as they stand. The widest label label_for() can return is "On-screen
keyboard", 18 characters, measured at 157px at ROW_FONT_SIZE 16 -- the note recording
that measurement is at test/unit/test_selftest.gd:10668. panel_width() takes
KEY_MIN_WIDTH = 140 as a FLOOR, so the column currently sits above its floor at 157.
The viewport is 1152 wide (confirmed live in cycle 137: `findings` reports 1152x648).
So there is a lot of headroom today and no guard on spending it.

Note the widest label is NOT a SHORT_NAMES value -- "On-screen keyboard" has no short
name and no glyph, it is the engine's own. The widest SHORT_NAMES value is 5 characters
("Space", "Num 0", "Num *"). So the two ways to blow this budget are different and a
test should say which it is bounding.

ACCEPTANCE: panel_width() is bounded against the viewport the way panel_height() is,
with the mirror of the height test, and the bound names whether it is the engine's
widest name or the widest SHORT_NAMES row that is being constrained.

title: No bridge-reachable way to select a placed plant, so the uproot message producer cannot be measured
description:
FOUND IN CYCLE 128, and it blocked half of -gd27's acceptance.

-gd27 asked for a run containing "arm and cancel uproots repeatedly". arm_uproot (game/game.gd:1762) requires a PLACED plant to be selected, and there is no way to select one from the bridge:

  run-method /root/Game _select ["<node path>"]  -- _select takes a Plant NODE; the bridge
                                                    passes a String, so this cannot work
  cmd list has no select verb                    -- 69 registered commands, none of them select
  touch press/release at the plant's global_position (224,296, read off the node) --
      selected_placed stayed "" through four attempts, and `touch list` reported
      "No active touches" afterwards

So arm_uproot returned "nothing is selected" every time after the first accidental selection was consumed. The MESSAGE_DEADLINE producer -- one of the two the bead named as most likely to stack -- went unmeasured.

WHY THE WORKAROUND IS THE INTERESTING PART. cycle-log.md states as durable knowledge that "a plant is selected by a real click, which cmd touch_press/touch_release at its global_position will deliver". That did not deliver here. Either the note is stale, or it depends on something this run did not do (set-feature --touchscreen before the scene loads is the obvious candidate), or the emulated-mouse guard added to _unhandled_input in the touch-layer work changed which events reach the handler. All three are checkable and none was checked -- do not fix the note until you know which.

ACCEPTANCE: a bridge-reachable way to select a placed plant, plus a cancel path for the armed state, so the DEADLINE producer can be exercised. The obvious shape is a project verb in devtools_ext/commands.gd taking a cell -- select_plant x,y -- beside the existing place_plant/upgrade_plant/collect_husk, all of which already take x,y. Register a cancel too, or arming becomes a one-way trip that uproots the plant on the second call (which is what happened here: the second arm_uproot returned "" and the plant was gone).

AND FIRST, per the note above: determine whether touch press/release CAN select, because if it can then the gap is documentation and a verb is a convenience rather than a fix. That is a five-minute check and it changes the whole answer.

RELATED: -a9pi asks whether the message counters should get a devtools verb. Both are the same shape -- a measurement the bridge cannot currently reach -- and if a verb is being added for one, consider both.
close_reason: Two verbs, select_plant and deselect_plant, in devtools_ext/commands.gd. Verified OVER THE BUS, which is the only thing that could verify it: the tests call the handlers as pure functions against a hosted Game and never touch the bridge. Live, cycle-128's blocked scenario ran end to end -- select_plant put a plant in selected_placed, arm_uproot answered 'confirm needed' where it had answered 'nothing is selected' through four attempts, and deselect_plant reported was_armed true then uproot_armed false. Both call _select AND _refresh, which is what the real board click does at game.gd:2547; _select alone leaves the HUD showing the previous selection. Separate verbs rather than one with an optional cell, so a dropped x is refused instead of silently deselecting. Found on the way: the pre-existing test_every_positional_devtools_verb_refuses_a_call_with_no_position failed on the new verb before a test was written for it -- it derives the verb list out of commands.gd source and asserts both directions, and did exactly its job on code added a hundred cycles later.

title: The ledger's reach denominator is the whole unpushed branch, so reach decays toward zero
description:
SOURCE: log-devtools.md, gap G-131, cycle 127.

THE MEASUREMENT. A cycle-127 run recorded "reached 2/15 changed file(s)" while git status --porcelain showed FIVE modified files, two of them .gd. Both numbers are correct; they answer different questions.

tools/verify_ledger.py:297 derives the changed set as

    git diff --name-only <base> HEAD

where base is the first of origin/main, main, origin/master, master that resolves. Its docstring at :274 says so plainly: "Commits on this branch not on the base - the branch's accumulated diff." The implementation matches the documentation. The problem is the project it is running in.

WHY IT BITES HERE SPECIFICALLY. This checkout is 56 commits ahead of origin/main, and that is deliberate: a bd memory records that every push to origin/main auto-deploys to itch.io via .github/workflows/deploy-to-itchio.yml with no paths filter, so the standing policy is to commit once per bd item and BATCH the pushes. The denominator is therefore 56 cycles of accumulated work and it grows every cycle until somebody pushes.

THE CONSEQUENCE, and it is about the ledger's own purpose. reach exists so a run cannot grade itself -- it is the diff intersected against what the running game loaded. On a long-lived unpushed branch the ratio decays toward zero no matter how well-targeted any individual run is, and verify_ledger.py stats aggregates it across rows. A reader looking at the history cannot tell "this run touched little of a long branch" from "this run verified little of what it changed", which is precisely the distinction reach was built to make.

The NUMERATOR stays honest, which is worth saying: game/notebook_screen.gd was reached and is absent from the NOT-reached list. Only the ratio misleads.

ACCEPTANCE, and the first option is preferred: derive the denominator from the run's own working-tree diff plus the commits since the LAST LEDGER ROW -- the ledger is append-only and already knows its previous row's sha, so this needs no new state. Failing that, print BOTH denominators with labels, so the branch figure and the run figure are distinguishable at a glance.

CHECK BEFORE CHANGING ANYTHING: whether this is upstream harness behaviour or a local edit. tools/verify_ledger.py is a harness template file (it is in /verify's drift-check list), this project runs harness 0.38.0 while 0.60.0 is on the machine, and -ny3h tracks the refresh being blocked on upstream gh#43. Read the 0.60.0 template first -- if it already fixes this, the answer is the refresh, not a patch, and a local edit would be reverted by the next scaffold.

DO NOT rewrite existing rows. The historical ratios were computed against the branch base and are what they are; a new field or a note on new rows is the honest way to change the meaning.
close_reason:
SHIPPED in lane/6wfo, merged to main -- and the READ was worth more than the change.

"CHECK BEFORE CHANGING ANYTHING: whether this is upstream harness behaviour or a local edit. Read the 0.60.0 template first -- if it already fixes this, the answer is the refresh, not a patch."
    -- READ FIRST, and it does NOT fix it. Three quotes settle it: `changed_branch` at
    0.60.0:399-426 is byte-identical to the installed 0.38.0:273-300, same base walk and same
    `git diff --name-only base HEAD`; `cmd_record` at 0.60.0:1261 still prints
    `_reach_line(u)` alone; and grep for `last_row` / `previous row` / `last ledger` returns
    nothing in either template, so the bead's PREFERRED acceptance is unimplemented upstream.

"derive the denominator from the working-tree diff plus commits since the LAST LEDGER ROW"
    -- NOT DONE, and the read is why: it exists nowhere upstream, so building it locally
    means maintaining a divergence on a template file forever.

"Failing that, print BOTH denominators with labels"
    -- DONE, and smaller than the bead thought. `cmd_reach` has printed both, labelled, since
    0.8.0; this project's verify-bd-item skill already pipes it through `grep '^worktree'`. So
    the entire live gap was `record`'s one print. The union line is unchanged and first, so
    anything parsing `reached N/M changed file(s)` keeps working; the labelled worktree line
    follows. Proved on the very next row recorded after the merge:
        union    2/18 changed file(s)
        worktree 1/1
    Same run, opposite readings.

"DO NOT rewrite existing rows"
    -- untouched. Still 148 rows at merge time, and nothing stored changed: the row has
    carried reach.worktree / reach.branch since 0.8.0, so no new field was needed.

THE BEAD IS UNDERSTATED ONCE AND OVERSTATED ONCE.
  Understated: the union also feeds `_reconcile_value`, which downgrades warranted ->
  insufficient only when `reached` is EMPTY. With the union as denominator, an old committed
  file that happens to load every session supplies the credit and the guard silently cannot
  fire. Measured: 1 of 148 rows. Deliberately NOT changed -- it grades a self-reported field
  and switching its denominator would flip verdicts. That belongs upstream.
  Overstated: "it grows every cycle". It does not. The branch denominator SATURATES at 12-14
  and has been flat since the second row, because the same handful of game files get
  retouched. The dilution is real; the unbounded growth is not.

Measured over 148 rows: union 65% (508/777), worktree 80% (225/281).

AND THE FINDING THAT OUTLIVES THIS BEAD, which is why the lane was worth spending:
`tools/verify_ledger.py` IS ALREADY LOCALLY PATCHED with two commits absent from 0.60.0 --
3432654 (split unreachable-by-construction out of NOT reached) and 30d1268 (the
`.claude/worktrees` exclusion that stops a fan-out resolving `extends Foo` to a stale
sibling lane's copy). `grep -c unreachable_static` returns 0 in BOTH templates. So -ny3h's
refresh is not a clean overwrite: it must re-apply three commits or silently revert two
features nobody knew were local. -ny3h's scope needs that correction.

TEMPORARY BY CONSTRUCTION and said so in the commit: `/scaffold-godot-harness` reverts this.
Worth having because that refresh already owes a re-apply on this file, so this adds a third
line to a list that exists rather than creating one.

NOT DONE: the upstream issue. Five parallel lanes filing issues is the wrong shape and the
lane's gate allowlist does not cover it; the material is copy-pasteable from commit 5da7779.

title: The notebook calls a two-step drawing 'the whole upgrade path' beside a three-rung ladder
description:
MILD DRIFT, filed because the audit that found it was told to file rather than fix.

The notebook's third page (game/notebook_screen.gd:435) describes the original pencil drawing and ends: "That is the whole upgrade path -- one kernel becomes several at once -- and the D-shapes became the kernel sprite."

The corn ladder has THREE rungs, not two. game/corn_cobbler.gd:100-104: single (1 kernel), triple (3 kernels, 26 degrees spread), bunch (5 kernels, 52 degrees). The drawing showed one arrow from one cob to another and the top rung is named "bunch"; the middle rung, triple, is not in the drawing and is not in the sentence.

WHY THIS IS THE WEAKEST OF THE THREE FINDINGS, and worth saying so. The page's job is to describe a pencil drawing that really does show one arrow, and every other sentence on it is about the artefact ("An arrow from one cob to another", "a scatter of D-shapes flying off to the right"). Only the clause "That is the whole upgrade path" makes a claim about the GAME, and it is that clause that went stale. A reasonable answer is that the sentence is about the drawing and should be reworded to say so, not that the page should document the ladder.

VERIFY BEFORE FIXING: game/corn_cobbler.gd:106-112 says the ladder is now drawn on the board ("every cob now wears the shot it actually fires: one pip per kernel"), so a player CAN see the three rungs without the notebook. That weakens the case for documenting them here and strengthens the case for rewording.

ACCEPTANCE: either the clause is scoped to the drawing, or the page names the three rungs. Both are one sentence. What is not acceptable is leaving a sentence that says "the whole upgrade path" beside a three-rung ladder.
close_reason:
SHIPPED in lane/qewm-hvdj, merged to main. One sentence in game/notebook_screen.gd.

DECISION: REWORD, not document -- and it was decided on this bead's own counter-argument rather than against it.

Both claims re-confirmed on main. game/notebook_screen.gd:435 is exactly the "note" line ending "That is the whole upgrade path". game/corn_cobbler.gd:100-104 is the three-rung ladder: single / triple / bunch.

What settled it was the bead's own third paragraph, verified rather than taken on trust: game/corn_cobbler.gd:106-112 says "every cob now wears the shot it actually fires: one pip per kernel ... Drawing and firing read the same function, so the picture cannot drift away from the behaviour". So the three rungs are already legible ON THE BOARD. Documenting them in the notebook would add a second place to drift from, in order to tell the player something they can already count.

And every other clause on that page is about the pencil artefact -- "An arrow from one cob to another", "a scatter of D-shapes flying off to the right". Only "that is the whole upgrade path" made a claim about the GAME, which is exactly the clause that went stale.

New clause: "That is one rung of the three the upgrade path ended up with." Scoped to the drawing AND carrying the count, so a fourth rung would read wrong here too rather than silently.

263 characters against the 300-char budget enforced by test_notebook_every_page_carries_a_caption_and_a_note -- checked, not assumed.

title: Ask who writes a source before pointing a citation checker at it -- three conventions, three misses
description:
THREE SIGHTINGS OF ONE SHAPE, and citation_check.py's own comments predicted the third.

1. tools/citation_check.py:81-86 -- game/OVERLAY_GRAMMAR.md lives in game/ and cites its neighbours bare (chomp_flower.gd:164). The first version demanded a directory part and saw none of its twelve citations. That file is nothing BUT citations.
2. tools/citation_check.py:90-94 -- the continuation form ('game/sfx.gd:86', ':91', ':106'). 44 of these in kanban.md, invisible to the first version: a third again on top of the 130 it did see, in a convention this project invented for itself.
3. Cycle 126 -- bd stores description and close_reason as PLAIN TEXT. Nothing renders them, so nothing rewards backticks: 95 backticked against 495 unbackticked. The first working --beads printed '468 bead(s) ... 0 finding(s)' over an input set 84% invisible.

Each time the tool was written from outside the document and imported the convention of the document it was written for. Each time the failure was SILENT and clean-looking, and twice the miss was larger than the hit.

WHAT TO ACTUALLY DO, and it is small. Before a new source is added to citation_check.py -- or to any checker that reads human prose -- answer two questions in a comment beside the source:
  - who writes this file, and with what tool?
  - what does the RENDERING of it reward? (markdown rewards backticks; a bd description renders nowhere and rewards nothing; a GDScript comment rewards neither)
Then measure both forms over the real corpus and print the ratio, the way the 95/495 measurement is recorded at tools/citation_check.py:97-108.

ACCEPTANCE. A short section in .claude/skills/house-static-checker/SKILL.md -- the file that already holds this repo's checker contract -- saying that a checker reading human prose must state its extraction convention and the measurement that justified it, with these three sightings as the evidence. Confirm first that the skill does not already say it: the contract there is about exit codes and denominators, and this is a different failure (the denominator was printed correctly and was simply small).

CONSIDER AND REJECT IF WRONG: making PLAIN the default everywhere. Loosening the markdown path would start matching prose -- the backticks in kanban.md ARE the convention there, and the tool has a false-positive history (heredoc_survey's first version reported 554). Per-source, measured, is the answer this bead argues for.
close_reason:
SHIPPED as part of a 4-lane parallel fan-out. Merged to main in the lane/yla3-fwlg merge; the section is in .claude/skills/house-static-checker/SKILL.md.

ACCEPTANCE: "a short section in house-static-checker's SKILL.md saying that a checker reading human prose must state its extraction convention and the measurement that justified it, with these three sightings as the evidence" -- done, and the prior clause "confirm first that the skill does not already say it" was honoured rather than assumed. The lane grepped for prose|convention|corpus|backtick|render|who writes|author and got eleven hits, none about extraction from a hand-written source. The nearest relative is "The region you measure is itself a denominator", which is a different mechanism: the REGION shrinks, rather than the pattern missing the document's own convention.

ALL THREE CITATIONS RE-CONFIRMED against main, individually:
  tools/citation_check.py:81-86  the bare-filename comment, "twelve citations in the one
                                 file whose entire content is citations"
  tools/citation_check.py:90-94  the continuation-form comment, "44 of these ... a third
                                 again on top of the 130 it did see"
  tools/citation_check.py:97-108 BEAD PROSE IS NOT MARKDOWN, carrying "95 backticked
                                 against 495 unbackticked" and the "468 bead(s) ... 0
                                 finding(s)" line
Cross-checked against :307-308, which says "95 of 590"; 95 + 495 = 590, consistent.

THE PIVOT THE LANE CHOSE, and it is better than what the bead asked for. The bead framed this as an addition to the checker contract. The lane made the pivot the bead's own caveat instead: the denominator rule DID fire and printed a true "468 bead(s)". The number that was small was the EXTRACTION, and nobody printed that. So this is not a second denominator rule; it is the observation that a correct denominator over a wrongly-extracted corpus reads exactly like a clean run.

PLACEMENT, which the bead left open: under "## Writing the scan", as the last ### before the raw-docstring rule -- with the other rules about CHOOSING the pattern, not under "## Hard requirements", which the bead explicitly distinguished it from.

WORTH RECORDING FOR THE NEXT FAN-OUT: this lane's worktree was checked out 71 COMMITS BEHIND main. On that tree, citation_check.py was 339 lines with no --beads mode at all, so the third sighting did not exist and the honest report would have been "premise disconfirmed". The lane noticed, branched from main instead, and said so -- which is the only reason this bead was not closed as invalid. Lane 4 was stale the same way and was told to rebase. Lanes 2 and 3 were on main. A stale worktree turns every absence claim in a lane into a fact about the checkout.

NOT VERIFIED, and the lane said so plainly: nothing in this lane compiled anything. It changed one markdown file, so there is nothing a compiler could have an opinion about -- but "18 of 19 checkers clean" means the docs edit broke no checker, not that the repo compiles.

title: SIGNATURE B misses a broken comment containing parens, which is most of this codebase's comments
description:
SOURCE: cycle 125, where I introduced SIGNATURE B and the survey built one cycle earlier
specifically to detect it reported 0 hits.

WHAT HAPPENED. Editing test/unit/test_selftest.gd through a script dropped the leading '#'
from a comment line, leaving this at statement position:

    	reason Hud.selection_level_names() is -- upgrade_ladder() is an instance virtual and

`python .claude/surveys/heredoc_survey.py --worktree` reported "SIGNATURE B comment prose
with no leading #: 0 hit(s)". lint_project.gd caught it: "Parse Error: Expected end of
statement after expression" at the exact line.

WHY IT MISSED, read off the detector rather than guessed:

    PROSE = re.compile(r"^[ \t]*[A-Z][a-z]+(?: [A-Za-z,'-]+){2,}[.:,]?[ \t]*$")
    CODE_TOKEN = re.compile(r"[=(){}\[\]:;]|->|\bfunc\b|\bvar\b|\bconst\b|\breturn\b")

Two independent reasons, either alone sufficient:
  * PROSE requires the line to START with a Capitalised word. Mine started "reason".
  * CODE_TOKEN excludes any line containing parens. Mine contained
    "selection_level_names()".

THE SECOND IS THE STRUCTURAL ONE. This codebase's comments cite function names constantly
-- a quick sample of comment lines in game/ shows a large fraction contain parens, a colon,
or an arrow. So CODE_TOKEN excludes a big share of exactly the prose that could lose its
marker. SIGNATURE B's real coverage is much narrower than its name.

DO NOT JUST WIDEN THE REGEX. CODE_TOKEN is there for a reason and the file's own header
records what happens without care: the survey's FIRST version reported 554 hits, every one
false. Trading a false negative for hundreds of false positives makes it worse, and a
survey nobody believes is a survey nobody runs.

WHAT TO TRY, in order:
  1. BUILD THE FIXTURE FIRST. .claude/surveys/heredoc_survey_controls.py already exists and
     reports "0 of 5 control(s) failed" -- it is the file that proves the detectors can
     fire. Add the missed case to it BEFORE touching PROSE, so the change is measured
     against a control that currently fails.
  2. Then consider: dropping the leading-capital requirement (cheap, probably safe --
     a comment can start mid-sentence in a wrapped block, which is precisely this case), and
     narrowing CODE_TOKEN so that parens alone do not exclude a line when the rest of it
     parses as prose.
  3. Re-run the HISTORY sweep after any change and compare the hit count to today's 0. A
     jump to hundreds means the widening was wrong, and history is the corpus that tells
     you cheaply.

WORTH ASKING FIRST, and it may close this: is SIGNATURE B worth detecting at all now?
Every instance of it in this project's history has been a hard parse error caught the same
day by lint -- the survey's own header says "Almost all are hard parse errors, which is why
they were caught the same day -- so the question is whether any ever SURVIVED into a
commit." The history sweep answers that: 0 in 1028 file versions. If none has ever survived,
the value of SIGNATURE B is only for the parallel case, where lint cannot run -- which is
real but narrow, and worth saying out loud rather than assuming.

ACCEPTANCE: a decision recorded. If widening: the control case added first and failing,
PROSE changed, the control passing, and the history sweep's hit count reported before and
after. If not: the reason written into the survey's NOT COVERED line, which currently does
not mention this limitation at all.
close_reason:
SHIPPED in lane/n228, merged to main. Widened, and the decision is recorded as BOTH -- widen the rule AND narrow the claim.

ACCEPTANCE, clause by clause (seeded from the criterion, per verify-bd-item):

"a decision recorded"
    -- KEEP IT, NARROWLY SCOPED, and say so. The history sweep confirms 0 instances of
    SIGNATURE B ever survived into a commit across 1042 .gd versions, because lint catches
    them the same day. So its value is `--worktree` ONLY: the pre-commit window, and the
    parallel fan-out where lint cannot run at all. That is now written into the NOT COVERED
    line, which previously implied broader cover. At 6.3% recall it was not earning even
    that narrow keep; at 97.1% it is.

"If widening: the control case added first and failing"
    -- DONE, and it reproduced this project's own tracked-fixture trap exactly. With the
    damaged .gd UNTRACKED: `scanning 63 tracked .gd file(s)`, 0 hits, exit 0 -- over live
    damage sitting on disk. After `git add -N`: `scanning 64`, 1 hit naming the file and
    line, exit 1. And the PRE-CHANGE survey over that identical 64-file tree reported 0 hits
    / exit 0, so the control demonstrably failed before and passes after.

"PROSE changed, the control passing"
    -- DONE. The new rule is a fact about the GRAMMAR rather than a guess about English:
    GDScript has no production placing two bare identifiers side by side separated only by
    whitespace; every such construct spells one side as a keyword. That is why it survives
    parens, which the old CODE_TOKEN rule could not.

"and the history sweep's hit count reported before and after"
    -- 0 before, 0 after. That is the bead's own falsification test ("a jump to hundreds
    means the widening was wrong") and it passes.

"If not: the reason written into the survey's NOT COVERED line"
    -- both halves apply here, and the NOT COVERED line was rewritten regardless of the
    widening, because the old one overclaimed.

THE NUMBERS, which are the result and were not in the bead:

    corpus: every one of this repo's 27,755 prose-shaped comment lines with its '#'
            deleted -- derived, not hand-picked, and it IS the damage

    old rule   1,742 / 27,755 =  6.3% recall
    new rule  26,949 / 27,755 = 97.1% recall

    false positives: 0 of 47,143 working-tree statement lines, 0 of 2,074,810 historical
    statement lines across 1042 .gd versions, 0 of 22 hand-written awkward-but-valid lines
    including Godot 3 spellings. The old rule is a strict SUBSET -- none of its 1,742 hits
    are missed now.

ONE CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S TEXT: it calls CODE_TOKEN "THE STRUCTURAL ONE". Measured, the
leading-capital requirement discarded 70.4% and CODE_TOKEN 30.9%. The bead named the smaller
of the two as the structural problem.

ONE THING BEYOND THE ASK, and it is the same defect class the bead is about:
heredoc_survey_controls.py carried its own private COPY of PROSE and CODE_TOKEN. A control
testing a transcription passes green forever the moment the copy drifts. It imports the
survey's own now.

VERIFIED AFTER MERGE by the parent, on the real tree: `--worktree` reports `scanning 63
tracked .gd file(s)`, 0 hits both signatures, exit 0; check_all 19 of 19 clean.

title: Decide whether the catalogue wants damages beside engages, now three readouts have wanted it
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md "New in cycle 123", second entry. THIRD time this distinction has been
wanted, which is usually the number at which it is real.

PlantCatalog.engages(id) answers "can this touch a pest", and its own header defines that as
"true if it can damage OR HOLD a pest" -- the Chomp is in the list for holding rather than
hurting, and the Barrier Bramble is in it for the same reason while doing no damage at all.
That definition is correct and deliberate; the key was named and documented for the coverage
map, which asks "does this cell defend the lane".

THREE READOUTS HAVE SINCE WANTED "DAMAGES" SPECIFICALLY, and each worked around it:

1. THE COVERAGE NOTE. Game.engagement_reach returns PlantCatalog.reach(id) for an engaging
   plant and 0.0 otherwise -- so a Bramble contributes 0 coverage, correctly, but by the
   accident that its reach is 0 rather than because anything asked whether it damages. A
   future holding plant WITH a reach would be counted as covering road it cannot hurt
   anything on.
2. THE BRAMBLE'S BLURB, cycle 123. "Hurts nothing" is true, and is the one clause in nine
   blurbs that could not be asserted: `engages` is the obvious key and says the opposite,
   and there is no other.
3. THE POST-MORTEM'S "HELD" ROW, which is -fohy and still open. That row counts KILLS, and
   the whole of -fohy is that a plant can now hold without killing.

THE QUESTION: does PlantCatalog want a second key -- `damages` -- beside `engages`?

ARGUMENTS FOR: three consumers, each currently expressing "damage" by a proxy that works
today for reasons unrelated to the question. The Bramble is the first plant where engages
and damages differ, and a second such plant makes all three proxies wrong at once.

ARGUMENTS AGAINST, and they are not weak:
  * `engages`'s header is emphatic that the key lives beside the plant so the answer is
    written where the plant is, and that a missing key must FAIL rather than default
    (test_every_plant_declares_whether_it_engages). A second key doubles that ceremony for
    nine plants to serve three readouts.
  * Two boolean keys that are equal for eight of nine entries invite exactly the drift the
    single key was introduced to prevent -- somebody sets one and not the other.
  * It may be derivable instead: "damages" is arguably `engagement_reach(id) > 0.0 or the
    plant is a Chomp`, which is ugly, or a method on Plant that the base class answers false
    to -- the shape Plant.bite_resistance() already uses successfully for a different
    per-plant fact.

PREFER THE THIRD OPTION IF IT WORKS: a `Plant` virtual (`func damages() -> bool: return
false`) overridden by the four plants that do, in the same shape as bite_resistance().
That keeps the answer beside the plant, needs no catalogue ceremony, and cannot drift from a
second key -- but CHECK IT FIRST, because the coverage map is static and asks the catalogue
without a plant instance, which is exactly why `engages` is a catalogue key and not a
method. That constraint may kill the option outright.

ACCEPTANCE: a decision recorded with its reasoning. If YES: the key or method exists, all
three consumers read it instead of their proxy, and a test asserts engages and damages
DIFFER for at least one plant -- without which the two are indistinguishable and the whole
exercise is ceremony. If NO: the reason written beside `engages`, naming the three proxies
so the next reader does not re-open it.
close_reason: Lane 4. DECIDED YES to damages, NO to a second key: PlantCatalog.damages(id) ships as a DERIVED static function, not as a boolean beside engages in PLANTS. The bead argued both sides and its strongest objection -- two booleans equal for eight of nine entries invite the drift the single key was introduced to prevent -- is decisive against the second-key SHAPE only. A derived function has no second value to leave un-set; it reads each plant's own damage constant the way reach() already does. The bead's preferred option, a Plant virtual in the shape of bite_resistance(), is DEAD and this was checked rather than assumed: Game.engagement_reach is a static func and PlacementPreview.dead_ground_cells draws the hover cue before any plant of the hovered kind exists, so there is no instance to ask -- the same constraint that made engages a key rather than a method. The case is stronger than the bead's three-consumer count: enumerating every consumer rather than the three named, Game.engagement_reach is the ONLY production reader of engages there is, everything downstream of it is worded 'aimed at', and it returned 0.0 for a Bramble only because a Bramble's reach happens to be 0.0. engages stays, correct and unchanged, with its header naming the split. THE EVIDENCE FOR DERIVING WAS IN THE FILE: plant_catalog.gd's CORN entry said 'the only plant in the game that does damage' while Nettle stings, the Dandelion's seeds bomb and the Chomp kills outright, and RunSummary.par_reach_px built its whole benchmark on a citation to that comment. Both retired -- the benchmark now argues from free_starter, which is true on CORN and false on all eight others. Also found: Game.engaging_plants() has no production caller at all, only tests, and suite_reach_check cannot see that because tests do name it. Changes no number in today's catalogue, which is the point.

title: Decide whether the palette-vs-background audit becomes a checker, and derive the surface if so
description:
SOURCE: cycle 121, immediately after building .claude/skills/palette-against-the-background
and applying it to the sprite set.

WHAT THE SKILL ESTABLISHED, so this bead does not re-derive it:
  * the grass tile is a flat #2ECC71 (which is GardenTheme.LEAF exactly) and the road tile a
    flat #BB8044, both measured off the Kenney PNGs rather than assumed;
  * a sprite's separation from its ground lives in the RIM, not the fill, because
    art_src/STYLE.md mandates "outline = darker shade of the fill, 2px";
  * so the audit reads the BEST MAJOR colour's luminance gap with a 5% floor, not the
    dominant colour's -- the naive version flagged five sprites and all five were fine;
  * over 22 sprites checked against the surface each actually sits on: 0 findings.

THE QUESTION: should that audit become a checker under tools/, or stay a skill?

THE ARGUMENT FOR is the usual one -- a skill is read when somebody chooses to read it, and
the failure it catches is invisible in the asset and only appears composited. The next sprite
is the one at risk, and nobody will think to run a manual audit for it.

THE ARGUMENT AGAINST, and it needs answering rather than dismissing: a checker needs to know
WHICH SURFACE each sprite sits on, and a hand-list of sprite -> surface goes stale exactly
when the check matters -- the day a sprite moves. That is the skill's own named blind spot
("a plant sprite audited against grass is audited against the wrong surface the day it moves
to the road"), and it is not hypothetical: it is what happened here, one plant ago.

BUT THE MAPPING IS DERIVABLE, which is what makes this worth filing rather than dismissing:
  * plants -> PlantCatalog.on_road(id) picks road or grass. Already the source of truth for
    placement, so it cannot drift from where the plant actually stands.
  * pests -> always the road; Board.route() is the only thing they walk.
  * everything else (seed packet, kernel, seed glyph, UI) -> NO single surface. These must be
    SKIPPED WITH A REASON and counted, never silently dropped, per the house contract.
The awkward part: the mapping lives in GDScript and a tools/*.py checker cannot call it.
Either parse plant_catalog.gd for the on_road keys (fragile, and this repo has been bitten
by regex-parsing GDScript) or export it. Decide which before writing anything.

BEWARE A PERMANENTLY-GREEN GATE. It is 0 of 22 today. That is fine only if the check can
actually fail -- so it needs the house contract's synthetic fixture: a sprite recoloured to
sit on top of its background must make it exit 1, and the real set must keep it at 0. Both
directions, or it is decoration.

ACCEPTANCE: a decision recorded either way. If YES: a checker with a DERIVED surface mapping
(not a hand-list), a printed denominator naming what it skipped and why, a NOT COVERED line
(it says nothing about silhouette, overlays, or a health bar drawn on top), and a fixture
proving both directions. If NO: the reason written into the skill, so the next reader does
not re-open it.

title: Decide what a settings toggle does when its own write fails, now that it can know
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md "New in cycle 120", first entry, filed the moment the mechanism existed.

-bia gave RunConfig._save() a return value and threaded it through store_key_bindings to
KeyBindingScreen, which now says "NOT saved -- this key is set for now, but will be back to
normal next time you play." when a write does not land. That bead deliberately scoped itself
to the Keys screen and said why: "the write is synchronous with a button press, so there is
an unambiguous moment to report."

EVERYTHING ELSE THAT PERSISTS STILL CANNOT SAY. Confirm the list before acting -- these are
read off the setters in game/run_config.gd and may have moved:
  * the options toggles -- mute, sfx, music, garden speed, colourblind bars. Each writes on
    a click with the screen staying put.
  * the high-score write, which happens as a run ends while the player is reading the
    post-mortem card.
  * the milestone/hint writes (spend_hint), which happen mid-play with no screen involved.

THE QUESTION, and it is a design one rather than plumbing, because the plumbing is done:
WHAT DOES A SETTINGS TOGGLE DO WHEN ITS OWN WRITE FAILS? The toggle has already moved on
screen. Silence is a lie. Reverting it is worse -- the setting IS in force for this session,
which is exactly what -bia's wording had to get right for keys ("set for now, but back to
normal next time").

Three candidate answers, and the third may well be correct:
  (a) The same sentence the Keys screen uses, in whatever note line the options screen has.
      Consistent, and it is the shape already proven.
  (b) One shared line somewhere global, since a failing save fails for everything at once
      and five separate reports of one disk problem is noise.
  (c) NOTHING, with a recorded reason. A mis-set mute that reverts next launch costs the
      player one click; a mis-set KEY costs them a control they had to go and find. The
      asymmetry may be real enough that only keys deserve words.

THE HINT/MILESTONE WRITES ARE ALMOST CERTAINLY (c) AND SHOULD BE SAID SO EXPLICITLY: they
happen mid-play with no screen and no player attention available, and a hint that has to be
shown twice is not a defect worth a sentence.

WATCH FOR: a per-setter bool cascade. -bia added a return to exactly ONE setter on purpose,
with a comment saying why the others stayed void -- "giving them all a return value nobody
reads would be the dead code this repo has been bitten by before". Whatever this bead
decides, it should not end with five setters returning bools that four callers discard.

ACCEPTANCE: a decision recorded with its reasoning for each of the three groups above; if
the answer for any group is "report it", the implementation and a test in the shape -bia
used (a pure static building both sentences, asserted in both directions, since the failure
branch is unreachable in normal play); and if the answer is "say nothing", that reason
written where the setter is, not only in this bead.

title: A comment arguing why a constant has its value is not an argument the behaviour is right
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md "New in cycle 118", second entry, found while confirming -ix76's premise.

THE CONFUSION, concretely. CompostMeter.FULL_VALUE (game/compost_meter.gd:97) carries a long
and correct argument for why it is 9 and not 60: "It is the knob lifetime_for was tuned
against, so widening it to 60 would silently slow the rot of every husk in the game -- a
balance change wearing a legibility fix's clothes."

Reading that, it is easy to conclude the matter is settled. It is not. It settles the KNOB
and says nothing about whether the BEHAVIOUR the knob produces is wanted -- which is exactly
what -ix76 asked ("should a 60-seed husk rot faster than a 9-seed one?") and what cycle 118
had to decide separately, with different reasons.

THE CLASS: an argument for why a constant has its value is not an argument that the
resulting behaviour is right. The two read alike. This repo is dense with the first kind --
it is one of the best things about it -- and a reader looking for the second will accept the
first and move on.

THE WORK is a sweep, and it is deliberately NOT a checker for the same reason -u9zb settled
for prose: whether a comment argues the right thing is a read, not a predicate.

Population, derived rather than listed: the balance constants are the ones a player can feel
-- start there rather than at every `const` in the repo. A reasonable first cut is the
`const` declarations in game/compost_meter.gd, game/pest.gd, game/wave_director.gd,
game/plant.gd and each plant subclass that carry a doc comment of more than about three
lines. Count them first and put the number in the close, the way -u9zb put 33 in its.

For each, sort into:
  * ARGUES THE BEHAVIOUR -- "3.0 HP/s against a mouth taking a plant down in 2.86s, and that
    ceiling is the design" (Aloe.HEAL_PER_SECOND) is this kind. Nothing to do.
  * ARGUES THE VALUE ONLY -- "widening it would silently change X" is this kind. The
    behaviour may be right, wrong or never considered, and the comment cannot tell you.
    These are the finding.
  * NEITHER -- a bare constant. Also a finding, and a cheaper one.

WHAT TO DO WITH THE SECOND CATEGORY is the decision this bead wants, and it should be made
once rather than per constant: either every such comment gains a sentence saying the
behaviour was considered (cheap, and risks becoming a ritual), or the ones where nobody has
actually considered it become their own beads (honest, and the list may be long). Cycle
118's answer for -ix76 was the second, and it cost one cycle for one constant.

DO NOT let this become a rewrite of good comments. The FULL_VALUE comment is excellent and
should not change; what it needed was a SECOND paragraph, which -ix76 added above
MIN_HUSK_LIFETIME rather than by editing it.

ACCEPTANCE: the population counted and stated; each sorted into the three categories; a
stated decision about what happens to the second category; and any constant where the
behaviour turns out to be genuinely unconsidered filed as its own bead. "Most of them argue
the behaviour and here are the four that do not" is the likeliest outcome and a good one.
close_reason:
SHIPPED in lane/8v43, merged to main -- and the sweep turned up a live defect the bead had no category for.

THE POPULATION, COUNTED rather than sampled. Const declarations carrying a doc comment of more than ~3 lines: 47 in the four named files, 49 more across the nine "extends Plant" subclasses, 96 total.

THE THREE-WAY SORT, for the 47 in the owned files:

  ARGUES THE BEHAVIOUR -- 41. The bead's predicted outcome held and understated the quality:
    wave_director.gd 13/13, pest.gd 17/17, plant.gd 9/13, compost_meter.gd 1/3. Three are the
    repo's own model answer and SAY SO in the comment -- Pest.GAIT_REFERENCE_SPEED ("THIS WAS
    PICKED AS A MIDPOINT AND IS NO LONGER ONE ... Do not restore the midpoint claim without
    re-deriving it"), Plant.STEM_PIVOT_Y (a test re-measures the eight PNGs), and
    Plant.FLINCH_RADIANS (pinned as an absolute pixel floor "rather than as a multiple of the
    constant -- an assertion written in the units of the thing under test passes when that
    thing is zeroed").

  ARGUES THE VALUE ONLY -- 5, each listed with what asserts its behaviour today: the
    CompostMeter BASE_VALUE/FULL_VALUE saturation (the bead's own exhibit -- rot is asserted,
    saturation is argued nowhere and asserted nowhere), COLLECT_RADIUS (the clearance is
    asserted, the reachability of a 28px target is not), Plant.HEALTH_BAR_ORIGIN (the
    relationship is asserted against a hand-copied Rect2, the placement is not),
    REACH_RING_ALPHA, and EXIT_SHRINK_SECONDS (nothing at all).

  NEITHER -- 0 inside the >3-line cut, BY CONSTRUCTION, and that is a real limit of the
    bead's own population rule: the cut hides them. Bare or <=3-line and player-felt:
    Pest.EAT_DPS = 14.0 with NO doc at all -- and MAX_HEALTH / EAT_DPS = 2.86s is quoted as
    "the design" in four other comments -- plus MUTATION_CHANCE, MUTATION_CHANCE_MAX,
    THREAT_LEVEL_BASE, HUSK_LIFETIME and MAX_HEALTH.

THE FOURTH CATEGORY THE BEAD HAD NO SLOT FOR, and it is the finding.

WaveDirector.CAMPAIGN_HEALTH_STEP argues its behaviour thoroughly, in the player's own units,
FOR A VALUE THE CONSTANT HAS NOT HAD SINCE a067d5f. Shipped at 0.04, settled at 0.03, and
every figure in the "WHAT 0.04 BUYS" paragraph was priced at 0.04 with none re-derived:

    finale                x1.665   ->  x1.469
    steepest step         +18.2%   ->  +17.0%    (wave 12)
    back half average     +10.9%   ->   +9.9%
    smallest step          +6.2%   ->   +5.2%
    aphid's 5th kernel    wave 17  ->  wave 19
    endless health pins   wave 36  ->  wave 40

Re-derived against _raw_threat offline, and the model reproduces every 0.04 figure to the
decimal FIRST -- so the arithmetic is checked in both directions rather than merely asserted.
Its +5.2% for wave 20 matches the 0.052237 that test_combat.gd already recorded from a real
run.

WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT is the half worth keeping: both tests over this ramp derive their
expectation FROM the constant, so both pass identically at 0.03 and at 0.04. Correct about the
SHAPE, and every magnitude unchecked by construction. Derived-not-typed is house style here
and this is its cost -- A TEST THAT DERIVES ITS EXPECTATION FROM A CONSTANT CANNOT PROTECT
PROSE THAT QUOTES A NUMBER.

THE DECISION THE BEAD ASKED FOR: neither of its two options. Five beads for five secondary
constants spends five cycles on the least consequential members. The rule instead: A COMMENT
THAT QUANTIFIES A BEHAVIOUR MUST NAME THE TEST THAT PINS THE QUANTITY, IN UNITS THAT ARE NOT
THE CONSTANT. That is already what the three model answers do and say; it is simply not
applied uniformly.

Two new tests assert the magnitudes without restating the constant -- kernel boundaries
1/10/19, finale 1.468534, steepest 1.17045 at wave 12, caps 40/62 -- every expected value
verified numerically against the offline model before being written.

PARENT APPLIED the four stale 0.04 figures in test/unit/test_combat.gd (lines 7734, 7862,
7925, 7961), a file the lane did not own. Its ASSERTIONS were already correct; only the prose
was stale, which is the same defect one file over. Three remaining "0.04" mentions in that
file are legitimate -- two narrate the history deliberately, one is about audio volume.

VERIFIED BY THE PARENT: lint 0/0, import clean, suite 933/933 with 18125 assertions, 19 of 19
checkers clean, findings 0 across 4 of 5.

title: Write the safe-sentence shape where somebody adding a producer will read it
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md "New in cycle 115", first entry, and the residue of -u9zb's sweep.

Counted rather than estimated: of the 33 sentence-producers in game/hud.gd, 21 INTERPOLATE
the thing they describe -- corn_detail ("%.1f dmg / %.2fs, %d kernel(s)"), sundew_detail
("Slowing %d pest(s) to %d%% speed."), wave_cleared_note ("%d pests turned back."). A retune
moves the number and the sentence follows it. They cannot rot.

Every defect found in two cycles of looking has been in the handful that NAME A MECHANISM in
prose instead:
  * eaten_message, "A hungry pest ate your %s!" -- true of every plant death until a plant
    arrived that is chewed by every pest (fixed cycle 112).
  * idle_detail, "Idle -- waiting for a pest." -- shown by two plants that cannot touch one
    (fixed cycle 115).

-u9zb's close records the decision that this cannot be MECHANISED and why: accuracy is a
claim about the relationship between English and code, and there is no shared vocabulary to
check. That decision stands and this bead does not reopen it.

THE WORK IS ONE PARAGRAPH, and its whole value is being at the point of writing rather than
in a document: a note in Hud.message_corpus()'s header saying PREFER INTERPOLATING THE THING
YOU ARE DESCRIBING OVER NAMING IT, with the two defects above as evidence and the 21-of-33
count as the reason to believe it generalises.

Why there and not in a skill: message_corpus()'s header is what a person reads when adding a
producer, because adding one without a corpus entry fails message_corpus_check.py and sends
them straight to it. A skill file is read when somebody chooses to read it; this header is
read when somebody is about to make the mistake.

ACCEPTANCE: the paragraph exists in that header, names both defects with the cycle that
found each, and states the count. No code change and no test -- and say so in the close
rather than inventing one, since a test asserting a writing preference would be theatre.
close_reason:
SHIPPED in lane/3w66, merged to main. 27 comment lines into `message_corpus()`'s doc block -- which is where `message_corpus_check.py` sends an author who forgot a corpus entry, so it is the paragraph a new producer's writer actually meets. That placement was the bead's ask and it is the whole point: the rule lives where the mistake is made.

CONFIRMED. Both named defects are real and documented in-file: `eaten_message` with the story in `chewed_through_message`'s header (Barrier Bramble, cycle 112), and `idle_detail` with the story in the `mint_detail`/`aloe_detail` header (cycle 115). `cycle-log.md` records the cycle-115 lesson verbatim including the exact "33 producers / 21 interpolate" sentence the bead carries.

UNDERSTATED TWICE, both found by re-deriving rather than re-reading:

1. THE COUNT IS STALE BY 85 COMMITS. `grep -c '^static func .*-> String:'` answers 33 at origin/main -- exactly where the bead's number came from -- and 39 on main. The never-interpolating set grew 6 to 9. So the surface where this mistake can be made is ~24% larger than the bead says.

2. THE SWEPT POPULATION WAS A FLOOR, NOT A CENSUS. -u9zb's derivation regex admits two things that are not sentence producers at all (one returns Dictionary, one returns bool) and misses every `_tooltip`, `_label`, `_name` and `hint_title`. Its own "21 producers" list contains 22 names. **And there is a THIRD instance of the defect class sitting outside the swept set**: `packet_tooltip`'s header records that it used to read "the only reliable way to a Seed Sunflower" -- true when the Sunflower was the only tier-2 plant, false silently the moment a fourth plant shipped.

AND A NUANCE THAT REFUTES THE BEAD'S OWN HEURISTIC. `eaten_message` DOES interpolate -- "A hungry pest ate your %s!" -- and rotted anyway, because it claimed a KILLER and interpolated a VICTIM. So "prefer interpolating" as the bead states it is not sufficient; the rule has to be **interpolate the thing the sentence CLAIMS**. That is the case the paragraph holds on to, and it is the part I would not have got from the bead alone.

The count is stated AS OF CYCLE 115 rather than as a live claim, plus the note that it is a floor. A dated observation cannot rot, which is the lesson of the file it sits in -- and the alternative would have put a fourth stale number in a file whose subject is stale numbers.

NO TEST, deliberately, per the bead's own acceptance: "No code change and no test -- and say so in the close rather than inventing one, since a test asserting a writing preference would be theatre."

No width budget moved: the diff adds no player-visible string and touches no literal in message_corpus(), selection_corpus(), WORST_CASE_TEXT or stats_row_budget(). message_corpus_check, readout_shape_check and sfx_call_check all stayed clean.

VERIFIED BY THE PARENT: lint 0/0, suite 933/933, 19 of 19 checkers clean.

title: Decide whether a teaching tip names the cheapest answer or the complete one
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md "New in cycle 115", second entry, found while reading all 33 HUD producers
for -u9zb.

Hud.flight_tip (game/hud.gd:3695) reads "That pest flies over Chomp Flowers. Corn Cobblers
can still hit it." Both sentences are TRUE. It is NARROW: a winged pest is also reachable by
the Bomb Dandelion, whose blast hits whatever is standing there, and by the Prickly Nettle,
which exists specifically to sting the mutations -- armoured, winged, hungry -- and whose
notebook card says so.

This is NOT filed as a defect. It is filed because nobody has decided whether a teaching
line should name the CHEAPEST answer or the COMPLETE one, and there are three such lines
that will all face the question as the catalogue grows:
  * flight_tip -- names Corn, where three plants now answer.
  * upgrade_tip -- names the cheapest plant to upgrade, which is already the cheapest-answer
    policy applied without anyone writing it down as one.
  * the move tip inside uproot_armed_message.

Each has a paired notebook card in Hud.HINT_CARDS, and test_every_hint_has_a_notebook_card
keeps the two lists together -- so a natural split is already available: the ROW says the
cheapest thing to do next, the CARD carries the complete rule.

TASTE, argue with it: name the cheapest answer in the row, always, and let the notebook
carry the complete one. A once-per-save line shown to a player watching a specific bug walk
over a specific mouth should be memorable, not exhaustive, and "Corn Cobblers can still hit
it" is more actionable than a list of three. Under that policy flight_tip is CORRECT AS
WRITTEN and the work is to record the policy rather than to change the copy.

CHECK BEFORE CHANGING ANY COPY: all three are priced by Hud.message_corpus(), and the
message row clips silently rather than erroring -- hud.gd's header explains why. A longer
tip needs its corpus entry updated or the budget under-measures the row.

ACCEPTANCE: the policy is written down once, beside flight_tip and upgrade_tip rather than
in a doc nobody opens; each of the three lines is checked against it; any that violates it
is fixed. "All three already comply, and here is the policy" is the likeliest outcome and a
completely valid one.

title: house-static-checker says a no-op mutation is not a survivor, but not how to tell
description:
SOURCE: cycle 114. A gap in .claude/skills/house-static-checker/SKILL.md's guidance,
identified by hitting it.

That skill has a section headed "A mutation that changes nothing is not a survivor" and it
is correct. What it does not give is a way to TELL, and cycle 114 spent a real detour on
exactly that: mutating Bramble.DAMAGE_THRESHOLDS by swapping its two entries produced no
test failure. That reads, in the moment and in a log, exactly like a weak test.

It was an equivalent mutant. texture_for_health COUNTS how many thresholds the fraction is
below rather than walking them in order, so the array's order genuinely cannot matter. A
second mutation (setting both thresholds equal, making the ragged frame unreachable) was
caught immediately and named the frame that vanished.

THE THING WORTH WRITING DOWN is the disambiguation, because "the mutant survived" and "the
test is weak" are the same observation until you do it:

  * Before believing a survivor, ask whether the mutated expression is READ in a way that
    can distinguish the change. An order swap cannot be seen by a counter; a threshold
    nudged past a sampled point cannot be seen by a test that samples only midpoints; a
    constant scaled cannot be seen by an assertion written as a ratio of it.
  * If the mutation is equivalent, the finding is about the CODE and is usually a small
    virtue -- here, that the table cannot be mis-ordered. Record it as such.
  * Then mutate again, differently, until one is caught. A single surviving mutant proves
    nothing either way.

WHERE IT GOES: house-static-checker's existing section, as a short "how to tell" list under
the heading it already has. Not a new skill, and not confirm-the-premise's business.

ACCEPTANCE: the section names at least the three shapes above with the cycle that paid for
one of them, and says explicitly that a single surviving mutant is not evidence. Keep it
