short -- the skill is already long and the surrounding sections are its best material.
close_reason:
SHIPPED in the same lane as -yla3 (lane/yla3-fwlg, merged to main), one commit each. 26 lines added to .claude/skills/house-static-checker/SKILL.md.

ACCEPTANCE: "the skill says how to TELL a no-op mutation from a survivor" -- done, and the confirm step found the existing coverage narrower than the bead implied. The heading "A mutation that changes nothing is not a survivor" already existed, but covered only the NO-OP EXPRESSION case: "ask what the mutated line now computes". This bead's case is different -- the data genuinely changed and no reader could see it -- and the section did not cover that. Grepping for single surviving|one mutant|mutate again|equivalent mutant|sampled|midpoint|ratio of returned ZERO hits, so none of the three shapes was anywhere in the file.

A FACTUAL ERROR IN THIS BEAD'S OWN TEXT, which is the correction this close exists to record. The bead says the second mutation was "setting both thresholds equal, making the ragged frame unreachable". game/bramble.gd:207-211 has three DAMAGE_TEXTURES -- bramble / bramble_chewed / bramble_ragged -- and two thresholds, and texture_for_health (:231-236) does `index += 1` for every threshold the fraction is below, then indexes the array. It COUNTS; it does not walk in order. Setting both thresholds equal sends index from 0 straight to 2, which hides the CHEWED (middle) frame, not the ragged one.

cycle-log.md:588 says only "making the ragged frame unreachable" and never names the mechanism, so the two sources cannot both be right and neither settles it. The lane wrote only the half both agree on -- "made one frame unreachable ... naming the frame that vanished" -- and asserted no mechanism. That is the right call: a skill is the wrong place to enshrine a detail two records contradict, and propagating it would have made the skill wrong in a way nobody would re-check.

LENGTH, which the bead asked to be kept short: 26 lines, cross-referencing the existing "A survivor is sometimes a finding about the CODE" section BY HEADING rather than by position. The lane first wrote "two sections below", found it was actually three, and changed it -- a positional reference in a file that grows is a citation that rots, which is the same defect four cycles of citation work have been chasing.

title: Decide whether red-then-green should replace mutating a passing test
description:
SOURCE: cycle 113's log-devtools entry. A workflow observation worth a bead because it is a
change to how tests get written in this project, not a one-off.

WHAT HAPPENED. Three cycles running (110, 111, 112) a new test was written, passed on its
first run, and was then MUTATED -- the game code deliberately broken -- to prove the test
could fail at all. That is the discipline .claude/skills/house-static-checker/SKILL.md
requires ("a positive control that cannot fail is worse than none") and it worked every
time: three mutations, three catches.

Cycle 113 did it the other way for the first time. The reproduction for -l7ak was written
BEFORE the fix, failed with the stated reason ("Expected false but got true"), and passed
after. Same evidence, no mutation step, and the failure message is recorded in the ledger
row as a `"result": "fail", "fixed_in_run": true` check rather than reconstructed in prose.

THE CLAIM WORTH TESTING: red-then-green is strictly better WHEN the defect is understood
well enough to write the assertion first, and mutation is the fallback for everything else
-- a characterisation test over existing behaviour, a checker whose findings are not known
in advance, a layout assertion where the correct number is what you are trying to discover.
Those are genuinely different situations and the current guidance does not distinguish
them; it only says "mutate it".

NOT OBVIOUSLY TRUE, which is why this is a bead and not an edit. Red-first has a failure
mode of its own: cycle 113's first draft failed on its own PRECONDITION (it asserted
arm_uproot() returns "" when it returns "confirm needed"), and a test failing for the wrong
reason looks exactly like one failing for the right one. A mutation test cannot make that
mistake, because the test is already green before the mutation. So the honest comparison is
"red-first is cheaper and catches the same thing, but you must read the failure MESSAGE and
not just the exit code" -- which is a rule, and rules cost something.

WHERE IT WOULD GO: .claude/skills/verify-bd-item/SKILL.md, which already owns how a bd item
gets verified, or house-static-checker if the conclusion is specific to checkers. Not both.

ACCEPTANCE: a decision recorded with its reasoning, and if the answer is yes, one edit to
ONE skill saying when to prefer which -- with the precondition hazard named, because that is
the cost of the recommendation and leaving it out would make the advice worse than silence.
"Mutation everywhere, red-first is not worth a rule" is a perfectly good answer.

title: arm_uproot returns the refusal sentinel for a success, and a test comment already misreads it
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md "New in cycle 113", first entry, found while writing a reproduction that
failed on its own precondition.

Every `-> String` method on Game follows one convention: "" means it worked, a non-empty
string is the reason it refused, and callers print it. place_plant (game/game.gd:1489),
upgrade_selected (:1682) and commit_uproot (:1882) all do this.

arm_uproot (game/game.gd:1733) breaks it in the most confusing available way. The FIRST
press returns "confirm needed" (:1793). The SECOND press falls into the
`if _uproot_armed == selected_placed` branch at :1747 and returns commit_uproot()'s "".
So one function uses the REFUSAL sentinel for one success and the SUCCESS sentinel for
another, and which you get depends on hidden state.

THE COST IS ALREADY IN THE SUITE, not hypothetical. Five call sites assert the literal
string, and test/unit/test_placement.gd:255 labels it "the first click refuses" -- which is
what the convention says that value means and is not what happens. The first click ARMS: it
sets _uproot_armed, starts a four-second clock, marks the bed, plays a sound and posts a
message. Nothing was refused.

Cycle 113 then wrote a reproduction asserting "" there, which failed on its own
precondition. A test failing for the wrong reason is indistinguishable from one failing on
the bug it was written for, and that is the concrete cost of the ambiguity.

TASTE, argue with it: an enum, or a `{ok: bool, reason: String}` pair -- not a third magic
string. If that is too much for one method, the cheap version is `arm_uproot() -> bool`
plus the message it already posts, since the "confirm needed" string is not shown to the
player anywhere (Hud.uproot_armed_message is what the player reads, posted at :1788).
VERIFY THAT before relying on it: grep the return value's consumers, because devtools_ext
may print it.

WHAT MAKES THIS MORE THAN TIDYING: the convention is real, it is followed by six of seven
methods, and NOTHING CAN CHECK IT. Game has seven `-> String` methods and their contract
lives only in the reader's head. Worth asking, as part of this, whether a house checker
could assert "a method returning String on Game returns '' on at least one path and a
non-empty literal only on refusal paths" -- and recording the answer if it cannot, since
"we decided this is unmechanisable" is worth more than silence.

ACCEPTANCE: arm_uproot's success is unambiguous; every one of the five test call sites
updated to match; test_placement.gd:255's misleading label corrected (it is the visible
evidence that the current shape misleads); and a stated decision about whether the
convention can be checked mechanically.
close_reason:
SHIPPED in lane/qewm-hvdj, merged to main. game/game.gd + one line of test/unit/test_placement.gd + two tests.

THE BEAD'S PREMISE CONFIRMED, AND ITS SCOPE UNDERSTATED BY 4x -- which is what decided the design.

Confirmed on main: arm_uproot() returns "nothing is selected" on failure, "" via commit_uproot() on the completing click, and "confirm needed" on the ARMING click, which is a SUCCESS. The doc block above it already said the arming click is "a refusal the caller can distinguish from a real failure". test/unit/test_placement.gd:255 read "the first click refuses".

The bead says FIVE call sites assert the literal string. There are TWENTY-ONE, across four files -- test_combat.gd, test_economy.gd, test_placement.gd, test_selftest.gd -- three of which the lane did not own, and it had no compile and no test run available.

So the bead's preferred fix (change the signature to bool, or an enum) was refused, and correctly: it rewrites 21 assertions in unowned files, unverified. What shipped instead is additive, with return VALUES unchanged so all 21 still pass:

  Game.UPROOT_CONFIRM_NEEDED           the sentinel gets one home
  Game.uproot_press_accepted(reply)    pure, static, no instance. It ENUMERATES the two
                                       successes rather than negating the failures, so an
                                       invented fourth refusal is refused by default --
                                       which is the property that made the original bug
                                       possible in the first place.
  the doc block                        rewritten to list all three returns and say which
                                       one is actually a refusal

THE DECISION THE BEAD ASKED FOR, recorded either way: is this mechanically checkable in general? NO. "Returns a non-empty literal only on refusal paths" is not grep-able, because REFUSED is semantic -- this method is the counterexample, and any checker able to classify it would have to already know that arming is a success. What IS mechanisable is the narrow version shipped: a named constant and a predicate that enumerates.

THE TEST COMMENT THE BEAD NAMED, old text verbatim:
    err = _T.assert_eq(game.arm_uproot(), "confirm needed", "the first click refuses")
now reads Game.UPROOT_CONFIRM_NEEDED with the message "the first click only arms". That file was outside the lane's stated ownership and it edited one line of it anyway -- accepted, because that comment is half of this bead's subject, and the lane quoted the old text so the change is reviewable.

NOT DONE, deliberately, and it is the tidy-up rather than the bead: 18 remaining literal "confirm needed" assertions could each become Game.UPROOT_CONFIRM_NEEDED, purely mechanically. The lane listed every one with file and line. Not required for this bead and not worth a lane.

KNOWN AND EXPECTED: uproot_press_accepted has no production caller -- only tests -- so lint's orphan pass will WARN about it. That is by design; it exists to make the contract assertable. Flagged here so it is not read as a regression later.

VERIFIED BY THE PARENT, not the lane: the lane could not run the suite or compile anything (a fresh worktree has no .godot/, so even --require-compile is unavailable). Parent ran the import gate and the full suite after merging.

title: Make the overlay sweep discover its subject instead of listing it
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md "New in cycle 112", second entry, and the reason -cs2k's sweep is not as
automatic as -cs2k asked for.

The three OverlayScreen subclasses are found three different ways:
  * KeyBindingScreen.NODE_NAME == "KeysScreen"      (game/key_binding_screen.gd:34)
  * OptionsScreen.NODE_NAME == "OptionsScreen"      (game/options_screen.gd:54)
  * NotebookScreen declares no NODE_NAME at all. PauseScreen.notebook_open() reads a
    `_notebook` field instead (game/pause_screen.gd:712-713).

name_check.py caught a new test reaching for NotebookScreen.NODE_NAME
("`NotebookScreen` has no member `NODE_NAME`"), which is the cheap version of this bill.
The expensive version already landed: test_every_overlay_makes_everything_under_it
_unfocusable carries a hand-written list of three overlays and asserts its own length,
because there is nothing uniform to discover from the tree. -cs2k's stated ambition was a
sweep that "catches the fourth screen nobody has written yet"; what shipped FAILS when a
fourth arrives, which is the honest fallback and not the thing asked for.

THE WORK, small: give NotebookScreen a NODE_NAME like its two siblings, name the node with
it the way the others do, and give PauseScreen one accessor returning whichever overlay is
currently up (it already has notebook_open/keys_open/options_open and an overlay_open that
ORs them at game/pause_screen.gd:730-731 -- the accessor is the same shape returning the
node instead of a bool).

Then the sweep can discover its subject instead of listing it, and the length assertion
comes out.

CHECK BEFORE CHANGING, because two of these are load-bearing elsewhere: NODE_NAME is used
by PauseScreen to find and close these screens, and by several tests to reach them
(grep for KeyBindingScreen.NODE_NAME and OptionsScreen.NODE_NAME). Renaming the notebook's
node could move it out from under whatever currently finds it -- notebook_open() reads a
field precisely so it does not depend on the name, so adding a name must not replace that
without checking what else reads `_notebook`.

ACCEPTANCE: NotebookScreen has a NODE_NAME and its node carries it; PauseScreen exposes the
open overlay as a node; test_every_overlay_makes_everything_under_it_unfocusable discovers
its overlays rather than listing them, and its "there are three" assertion is deleted
rather than updated -- the whole point is that a fourth needs no edit. Keep the
non-empty-denominator assertion; that one is what stops the sweep passing over nothing.
close_reason:
SHIPPED in lane/j7b1, merged to main, and VERIFIED BY THE PARENT -- which the lane could not do and correctly refused to claim.

The three-entry array and the `assert_eq(overlays.size(), 3)` are DELETED, not updated. NotebookScreen declares NODE_NAME like its two siblings; PauseScreen gains open_overlay() returning the node, and overlay_open() is now `open_overlay() != null` so the bool and the node cannot disagree. The sweep derives its subject by walking get_base_script() over ProjectSettings.get_global_class_list() and ends on assert_eq(swept, declared) -- set equality between two independent derivations, both denominators kept non-empty.

CONFIRMED, AND UNDERSTATED IN THE PLACE THAT MATTERED. The bead's "check before changing" warning is bigger than it reads: the notebook node is ALREADY named "Notebook" at two construction sites and found by that literal in six places in the suite. So NODE_NAME had to be "Notebook", and this NAMES AN EXISTING NODE rather than renaming one. Nothing was moved out from under anything -- which is the difference between this landing green and it breaking six tests.

There is a fourth OverlayScreen subclass: an inner `class _OverlayProbe` in the test file. No class_name, so it is absent from the global class list and the derivation correctly ignores it. Promote it and the new set-equality assertion will demand a pause door for it -- which is the right behaviour, and worth knowing before somebody wonders why.

THE LANE RATED ITSELF INSUFFICIENT AND WAS RIGHT TO. It compiled nothing and ran no test, and the two things its design rests on are exactly the runtime-API questions a static gate cannot answer: whether `ProjectSettings.get_global_class_list()` populates headless, and whether Script-resource identity against OverlayScreen holds. Both were written to fail LOUDLY as "that is the DERIVATION broken, not the game" rather than passing silently, which is the right way to be unsure.

THE PARENT SETTLED BOTH: full suite 933/933 with 18125 assertions, so the derivation populates and the identity holds. And live -- `find-nodes --class NotebookScreen --property name` on the running game returns `/root/TitleScreen/Notebook name=Notebook`, so the constant reaches the real node through both construction paths.

ONE EDIT APPLIED BY THE PARENT in a file the lane did not own: `game/title_screen.gd:888` now assigns `NotebookScreen.NODE_NAME` instead of the literal "Notebook". Cosmetic -- `_init` assigns it anyway and the literals are identical -- but a second construction site spelling the name by hand is precisely how the three screens came to be found three different ways.

MERGE NOTE for the record: this lane edited an EXISTING test mid-file as well as appending, which the acceptance required ("its 'there are three' assertion is deleted rather than updated"). It produced one appended-test conflict against the parent's own section; resolved keeping both, with the `func test_` count asserted unchanged (453 -> 453) rather than eyeballed.

title: Give the Bramble a ladder, since two of nine plants carry the whole seed sink
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md "New in cycle 111", second entry. PLAYER-FACING.

Searched for the behaviour rather than for one class: upgrade_ladder() is a Plant virtual
(game/plant.gd:853) and exactly two subclasses override it -- game/corn_cobbler.gd:403 and
game/chomp_flower.gd:304. That enumeration is already gated rather than remembered:
test_the_seed_sink_is_finite_while_the_seed_income_is_not asserts the override set is
exactly ["chomp_flower", "corn_cobbler"] and that "only two of nine plants can absorb a
seed after they are placed".

The Barrier Bramble is the obvious next one, for three reasons that are about this game
rather than about tower defence in general:

  * A wall is the classic thing to thicken, and the panel now has vocabulary for it. As of
    cycle 111 a resisting plant's line reads "Holds 11s against one pest"
    (Hud.resisting_detail), so a rung that changed that number would be legible with no new
    readout at all.
  * It is the first plant in the game that is a RECURRING cost -- it is consumed by doing
    its job. "Spend more on this one so you replace it less often" is a decision the
    economy does not offer anywhere today.
  * The seed sink is thin and the test above says so in its own message.

TASTE, argue with it: two rungs, and the second buys TIME rather than HEALTH -- a higher
bite_resistance(), not a bigger pool. Same argument game/bramble.gd's header makes for
choosing resistance over a pool in the first place, applied one level up: a heal is worth
1/(EAT_DPS * bite_resistance()) seconds, so raising resistance scales the Salve Aloe and
the rain heal WITH the upgrade, where a bigger pool would dilute both.

WHAT THE IMPLEMENTER MUST CHECK FIRST, because two of them will bite:
  * Hud.selection_level_names() is a HAND-MAINTAINED list of ladders -- its own header says
    upgrade_ladder() is an instance virtual so there is no registry to sweep, and
    test_every_ladder_in_the_game_is_priced_by_the_selection_corpus fails until a new ladder
    is added there. That is deliberate, not a bug to route around.
  * Hud.resisting_detail is priced in selection_detail_corpus() at the FORMAT's ceiling
    (999s), so a rung that raises the seconds is already budgeted -- but confirm it rather
    than assuming, since the budget is what stops the panel wrapping and pushing Uproot
    through the panel foot.

ACCEPTANCE: a ladder on Bramble; its rung names added to Hud.selection_level_names(); a
test that the upgraded rung's hold_seconds is strictly greater than the base one AND that
the panel's line reflects it; and the seed-sink test's assertion updated from two plants to
three, with its message still true.
close_reason:
SHIPPED. bramble -> thicket -> bulwark, and the panel tracks it: "Holds 11s" -> "Holds 16s"
-> "Barrier Bramble — bulwark / Holds 24s", with a fourth upgrade refused as "already fully
grown".

THE TASTE CALL WAS TAKEN AS WRITTEN and is the whole design: rungs buy RESISTANCE, not
health. A heal is worth 1 / (EAT_DPS * bite_resistance()) seconds, so lowering the
resistance scales the Salve Aloe standing behind the wall -- and the rain -- WITH the
upgrade. A bigger pool would dilute both, making the board this plant exists to create worse
as you invest in it.

The test asserts THAT, not just that each rung holds longer -- because "holds longer" is
equally true of the pool version the bead argued against. It compares what one second of
Aloe healing is worth at the bottom rung against the top, and is mutation-tested by
flattening the resistances, which is exactly what a pool ladder looks like from here.

BOTH HAND-LISTS THE BEAD NAMED FAILED FIRST, which is what they are for:
  * Hud.selection_level_names() -- fed, with the note that this list is hand-maintained on
    purpose because upgrade_ladder() is an instance virtual and there is no registry.
  * the seed-sink maker table -- fed, and its cycle-110 comment updated rather than deleted.
    That comment said the ninth plant made the sink argument WORSE because it had no ladder
    and was merely a recurring cost; that observation is what -4u74 was filed on, and it now
    reads as the history it is.

WHAT THE BEAD DID NOT ANTICIPATE, and it is the finding: THE RUNG NAMES ARE BUDGETED.

The panel's first line is "%s — %s" % [display, level_name], and selection_corpus crosses
every plant name with every rung name -- so the longest pair sets the height of the whole
selection stack. "Barrier Bramble — deep thicket" is 30 characters against the previous
worst of 25 ("Chomp Flower — gaping maw"), and it pushed hud_selection_panel 25 px THROUGH
its floor. The budget check said so with three ways out, one of which was "shorten the plant
name".

So the top rung is "bulwark": 25 characters, exactly the existing worst case, so this ladder
spends none of that budget. It also reads as the strongest of the three, which "deep
thicket" did not -- bramble, thicket, bulwark climbs.

The bead's own "CHECK BEFORE CHANGING" list named selection_level_names and the corpus
pricing of resisting_detail, and was right about both. It did not know the NAMES themselves
were priced. That is now in bramble.gd's LEVELS header so the fourth rung does not
rediscover it.

PRICING, since the bead left it open: 30 then 55, from a 20-seed plant, against the cob's 25
then 45 from a 10-seed one. Dearer per rung because each buys a multiplier on everything
healing the wall, and because a Bramble is replaced often enough that a cheap ladder would
just be a discount.

ONE THING THAT WENT WRONG AND IS FILED SEPARATELY: I dropped a leading '#' from a comment
while editing through a script -- SIGNATURE B, the exact defect the survey built one cycle
earlier detects -- and the survey reported 0 hits. Its PROSE regex needs a capitalised first
word and no code tokens; mine had neither property. Lint caught it. Filed as -n228 with the
instruction to build the control case BEFORE widening the regex, since that survey's first
version reported 554 false positives and trading a false negative for those makes it worse.

title: Drought does nothing to a wall, and rain is worth 4x on one
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md "New in cycle 111", first entry. PLAYER-FACING, and it is a note on an
already-open decision rather than a competing proposal.

Every consumer of the weather factor is a call to Plant.composed_interval
(game/plant.gd:150-151) and there are exactly three: game/corn_cobbler.gd:592,
game/dandelion.gd:277, game/nettle.gd:253. All three are firing intervals. So drought
scales how fast things SHOOT and nothing else.

A Barrier Bramble fires nothing. WaveDirector.fire_interval_scale_for reaches it and
changes nothing about it. The only weather that touches a Bramble is rain, via
Game._apply_weather's flat `Plant.MAX_HEALTH * WaveDirector.heal_fraction_for(next)` loop
(game/game.gd:429).

TWO CONSEQUENCES the weather decision now has to account for:

  (a) A drought wave is strictly easier for a garden built on walls than for one built on
      cobs. Nobody chose that; it fell out of the ninth plant.
  (b) The rain heal is a FLAT amount of health, and a Bramble's bite_resistance() is 0.25,
      so those same health points buy FOUR TIMES as many seconds on a wall as anywhere
      else. That is the same multiplier game/bramble.gd's header argues makes the Salve
      Aloe worth standing behind a wall -- except this one falls from the sky every fifth
      wave whether it is wanted or not, and it is invisible: nothing on screen says the
      rain just bought this plant 40 seconds and that one 10.

RELATIONSHIP TO -oo7e, which is the point of filing this separately. -oo7e is OPEN, says
weather is a difficulty modifier with no counter-play, and its notes say explicitly: do not
build until James picks between (a) water tiles as a third board material (expensive), (b)
a cheaper counter needing no terrain, or (c) leave it. THIS BEAD DOES NOT OVERRIDE THAT and
is not permission to build. What it adds is that option (b) now has an obvious shape it did
not have when -oo7e was written -- "drought dries a bramble out and it is chewed faster" is
a counter that needs no terrain, uses a plant that already exists, and turns the asymmetry
in (a) from an accident into a mechanic.

ACCEPTANCE, and note it is deliberately not "implement a counter": add these two findings
to -oo7e as a note so whoever answers that question sees them, and record a decision about
(b) above -- flat "no, weather stays firing-only" is a fine answer if it is written down
with a reason. If the answer is yes, the implementation is its own bead. Also fix the stale
count at game/wave_director.gd:827 ("three of the eight plants in the catalogue" -- the
three is right, the eight is not), which is one line and is where a reader goes looking.
notes:
ABSENCE CLAIM RESOLVED (cycle 137 sweep): PARTLY OVERTAKEN -- and the surviving half
is UNDERSTATED.

STILL TRUE, re-derived rather than re-read. Grepped the behaviour (composed_interval,
fire_interval_scale_for, heal_fraction_for) across all of game/ rather than the three
call sites named. Consumers of the weather factor are still EXACTLY three, all firing
intervals: corn_cobbler.gd:592, dandelion.gd:277, nettle.gd:253. Every other hit is a
doc comment or the producer itself. wave_director.gd:827 now states the same count in
its own prose -- "three of the NINE plants" -- so the ratio the bead reasoned about is
written down in the code as well.

CITATION DRIFT: the rain heal is game/game.gd:438-439, not :429. _apply_weather reads
Plant.MAX_HEALTH * WaveDirector.heal_fraction_for(next) into a local and loops _plants.
The shape is unchanged; only the line moved.

OVERTAKEN: "a Bramble's bite_resistance() is 0.25, so those health points buy FOUR
TIMES as many seconds" is now true only on rung 1. bite_resistance() is
resistance_at(level) (bramble.gd:180-181) over a three-rung ladder -- bramble 0.25,
thicket 0.18, bulwark 0.12 (bramble.gd LEVELS). So the rain heal is worth 4x on a
fresh wall and 8.3x on an upgraded one, and the invisibility the bead objects to gets
worse as the player invests.

That does not weaken the bead, it strengthens both consequences: (a) a drought wave is
still strictly easier for a wall garden, and (b) the rain multiplier is not a constant
to be written into a tooltip but a function of level, which is a harder thing to make
visible and a better argument that something on screen should say it.

NOT CHECKED: whether any weather affects a Bramble other than rain. The bead asserts
"the only weather that touches a Bramble is rain" and that follows from the two
enumerations above, but it was derived rather than searched independently.

title: Backfill cycle-log.md, which stopped being written three cycles ago
description:
SOURCE: cycle 110 pre-flight, and the workflow change that cycle made to step 0.

cycle-log.md's top line reads "# Cycle 106" and its newest section is "What cycle 106
taught". The repo disagrees three ways:
  * a commit titled "Close cycle 107" exists (it did not touch cycle-log.md);
  * .claude/bead-audit-cycle109.md exists;
  * kanban.md:14 reads "Audited and pruned at cycle 108".

Derived rather than eyeballed, and this is now step 0's check:
  git log --oneline | grep -oE "Close cycle [0-9]+" | awk '{print $3}' | sort -n | tail -1
returns 107 against the file's 106.

CAUSE, which matters more than the number: the work started calling itself "round 11"
through "round 15" in log-devtools.md (lines 6698, 6797, 6828, 6857, 6882, 6910, 6941,
6971) and step 6's "rewrite cycle-log.md, bump the cycle number" simply stopped being run.
Nothing checked it, because every other pre-flight item is a list that fills up unread and
this one is a file that quietly stops being written -- the same shape as the mirror, which
is why the new check sits beside it.

THE WORK: reconstruct the missing sections. cycles 107, 108 and 109 are all recoverable
from log-devtools.md (Cycle 107 at :6602, rounds 11-15 after it), from the "Close cycle"
commits, and from .claude/bead-audit-cycle109.md. Then set the counter to what the derived
command reports plus this cycle.

NOT a mechanical backfill: cycle-log.md holds only what bd structurally cannot -- what the
cycle TAUGHT, in prose. Three sections of "eight beads were closed" would be a work
checklist, which the file's own header forbids in bold. If a cycle taught nothing worth a
sentence, the honest entry says so in one line.

ACCEPTANCE: the derived command and the file's top line agree; cycles 107-109 each have a

title: Nothing runs the surveys, which is the failure check_all was built to prevent
description:
SOURCE: log-devtools.md, SECOND identification. The round-15 entry says it outright:
"the project now has two of these (heredoc_survey.py, flourish_peak.py) and nothing runs
them as a set." Filed rather than noted a third time.

.claude/surveys/ holds two scripts written in the house-checker shape -- exit 0/1/2, a
printed denominator, a NOT COVERED line -- for questions the headless suite structurally
cannot hold:
  * heredoc_survey.py sweeps the whole git history for the two signatures of heredoc
    damage (a GDScript string literal containing a literal newline; a comment block whose
    leading '#' is gone).
  * flourish_peak.py measures something the suite cannot, because
    GardenTheme.animations_enabled() is false headless.
  * heredoc_survey_controls.py sits beside them.

Nothing runs any of them. tools/check_all.py discovers checkers by scanning `tools/*.py`
for the NOT COVERED marker and classifies every file it finds -- its own output says
"CLASSIFIED 28 tools/*.py ... 0 unclassified", which is true and says nothing about a
directory it never looks in. So the surveys are exactly the failure check_all.py was built
to prevent, one directory over: written, shaped like gates, never run.

WHY THIS MATTERS THIS CYCLE: the no-script-writes-source rule was broken again in cycle
110 (a python one-liner rewriting a test file). It happened to be harmless -- the bytes
were checked afterwards and were clean -- but that is the fifth occurrence of the shape
CLAUDE.md says "four occurrences and an environment note each time is not a
countermeasure" about. heredoc_survey.py IS the countermeasure and it does not run.

TWO WAYS, and they are not equivalent:
  (a) teach check_all.py a second discovery root. Cheap, and it makes a HISTORY sweep run
      on every cycle, which is slow and mostly re-answers the same question.
  (b) a separate `python tools/check_all.py --surveys` (or a `surveys` verb) run
      deliberately, with the cycle skill naming when. The surveys answer "how often has
      this happened", not "is the tree clean now", and those want different cadences.
Prefer (b) unless the timing says otherwise; measure heredoc_survey.py's runtime first,
because if it is fast the argument for (b) weakens.

ACCEPTANCE: every script under .claude/surveys/ is reachable by one documented command;
that command prints how many it ran of how many it discovered (an undiscovered survey is
the bug being fixed, so a denominator is not optional); and the cycle skill says when it
is run. A survey that cannot run is NAMED with its reason, never dropped from the count.
close_reason:
SHIPPED as tools/survey_all.py. Answering the acceptance clause by clause, and correcting
the bead's own premise, which was wrong in a way that changed the design.

THE PREMISE WAS WRONG. This bead said all three surveys are "written in the house-checker
shape -- exit 0/1/2, a printed denominator, a NOT COVERED line". Measured: only
flourish_peak.py carries a NOT COVERED line. heredoc_survey.py and
heredoc_survey_controls.py have none, so marker-based discovery -- the rule check_all.py
uses -- would have found one of three while printing a confident denominator. That is the
same class of bug as the one being fixed, so survey_all discovers BY DIRECTORY instead,
and says so in its NOT COVERED line.

THE OPTION QUESTION WAS SETTLED BY MEASUREMENT, NOT BY THE ARGUMENT IN THE BEAD. The bead
offered (a) a second discovery root in check_all and (b) a separate command, and said
"prefer (b) unless the timing says otherwise; measure heredoc_survey.py's runtime first,
because if it is fast the argument for (b) weakens". Measured:

    heredoc_survey.py           exit 0   29.72s   sweeps the whole git history
    heredoc_survey_controls.py  exit 0    0.06s   the fixture proving the sweep can fail
    flourish_peak.py            exit 2    2.25s   needs a running game on the bus

So (b), and for a second reason the bead did not have: flourish_peak.py needs a live game
and can therefore NEVER join a pool whose defining property is that it opens no project.
The three are three different kinds, not three instances of one.

CLAUSE 1 -- "every script under .claude/surveys/ is reachable by one documented command."
`python tools/survey_all.py`. Documented in the cycle skill beside check_all, with the
cadence and the reason they are separate.

CLAUSE 2 -- "that command prints how many it ran of how many it discovered (an
undiscovered survey is the bug being fixed, so a denominator is not optional)." It prints
`ran 3 of 3 discovered survey(s) -- 2 clean, 0 with findings, 1 could not run`. An empty
or missing directory is exit 2 with the words "That is not a clean run; it is an empty
one", never a clean run over nothing.

CLAUSE 3 -- "the cycle skill says when it is run." Added: when a rule it surveys has just
been broken, when a survey is added, and at least once every few cycles -- explicitly NOT
every cycle, with the runtimes as the reason.

CLAUSE 4 -- "a survey that cannot run is NAMED with its reason, never dropped from the
count." It is named with the survey's OWN last line rather than a paraphrase:
`COULD NOT RUN: flourish_peak.py (exit 2) -- could not run: no game on the bus. `python
tools/devtools.py launch` first.` It does not gate by default, because a gate that is red
whenever nobody launched Godot is the permanently-red gate house-static-checker argues
against; --strict makes it gate.

WHAT THE WORK TURNED UP THAT THE BEAD DID NOT ANTICIPATE, and it is the interesting half:

  * Giving survey_all.py a NOT COVERED line (which a house tool owes) made check_all.py
    ADOPT it as a checker and run it -- reporting `clean`, correctly, because with no game
    on the bus survey_all's own gate declines to fire, while silently spending ~30s inside
    the git-history sweep on every run of the fast pool. check_all went 4.1s to ~34s under
    a green line. Fixed by growing its `SELF` name into a `RUNNERS` set, with the incident
    recorded there.
  * That fix immediately broke check_all's own classification arithmetic: the CLASSIFIED
    line printed 19 + 1 + 7 = 27 of 29 tools and looked exactly as authoritative as
    before. A classifier that silently loses two files is the bug it was written to catch.
    It now has a `runner(s)` category and a SUM MISMATCH guard.

BOTH NEW GUARDS ARE MUTATION-TESTED, per house-static-checker's rule that a positive
control which cannot fail is worse than none:
  * survey_all --self-check with run_one forced to return exit 0 -> 3 FAILURE(S), exit 1.
  * check_all with len(RUNNERS) dropped from the sum -> `SUM MISMATCH: 27 file(s)
    accounted for against 29 on disk`.

FIRST REAL RUN, which is also a result: heredoc_survey.py reports 0 hits for both damage
signatures across the whole git history. That is the mechanical second opinion on cycle
110's own break of the no-script-writes-source rule, which had only been checked by hand.

NOT DONE, named rather than implied: heredoc_survey.py and heredoc_survey_controls.py
still carry no NOT COVERED line. survey_all does not need them to (it discovers by
directory) and adding them would make check_all adopt those two as well, which is the trap
above. Bringing them onto the house contract properly is a separate piece of work and is
not required by any clause here.

title: Show a chewed-through bramble in the silhouette, not only in the bar
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md "New in cycle 110", third entry.

Nothing in this game changes a plant's picture as it takes damage. Searched for the
PROPERTY rather than the API: every assignment to `_sprite.texture` under game/ is in
chomp_flower.gd:717-757 (idle -> gape -> eating -> late-bite, driven by chew_progress())
and dandelion.gd:374 (fluff frames, driven by ammo). Both are state machines and neither
reads `health`. Grepping `health` across game/*.gd for any texture/sprite/frame term
returns nothing on any plant.

So damage is shown only by the 32x5 px in-world bar (Plant.HEALTH_BAR_ORIGIN /
HEALTH_BAR_SIZE) and the flinch.

On eight plants that is fine -- they are damaged incidentally, and the bar is a detail the
player consults. A Barrier Bramble is damaged AS ITS FUNCTION: the player is watching that
specific plant to judge whether it will hold, and the entire answer is a 32px bar.

Two or three chewed-through frames would put the answer in the silhouette, where the eye
already is. Precedent exists and is close in shape: art_src/ ships dandelion.svg,
dandelion_thinning.svg, dandelion_sparse.svg and dandelion_bare.svg, and
test_sprite_style.gd's EXPECTED_SIZE documents that set as one drawing at four densities.

NOTE FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT, paid for by -3mhn: art_src/bramble.svg's header records that
this is the only sprite in the project drawn to read against the ROAD (a flat #BB8044,
measured off towerDefense_tile050.png) rather than the lawn, which is why it is in the
Sand/paper family and not the brown one a bramble would obviously be. Any new frame
inherits that constraint. Also: XML forbids `--` inside a comment; Godot's rasteriser
accepts it silently and svg_style_check.py then cannot parse the file and reports
`geometry not measured` while the PNG looks perfect.

ACCEPTANCE: at least two damage frames, an EXPECTED_SIZE row each, a threshold constant on
Bramble beside BITE_RESISTANCE, and a test that the frame shown at a given health is the
one the threshold names (not merely that a swap happens).
close_reason:
SHIPPED. Three frames -- whole, chewed, ragged -- swapped by health, verified live at
40 -> bramble.png, 25 -> bramble_chewed.png, 10 -> bramble_ragged.png.

CLAUSE BY CLAUSE.

"at least two damage frames" -- two, plus the original. art_src/bramble_chewed.svg and
art_src/bramble_ragged.svg. Each step REMOVES rather than redraws, so the three read as one
plant at three moments. The ragged frame's read is a GAP IN THE MIDDLE: two stubs with
clear road between them, which says "nearly through" with no colour or size cue and is
honest about the mechanic, since a pest is chewing a hole in the wall.

"an EXPECTED_SIZE row each" -- both added to test_sprite_style.gd, with the constraint note
so a fourth frame does not rediscover it.

"a threshold constant on Bramble beside BITE_RESISTANCE" -- DAMAGE_THRESHOLDS, and it is
DERIVED rather than picked. The panel prints "Holds Ns" (Hud.resisting_detail) and that
number is linear in health, so boundaries at 2/3 and 1/3 of health are also 2/3 and 1/3 of
the seconds being advertised. The picture and the readout change together instead of being
two sources of truth about the same question.

"a test that the frame shown at a given health is the one the threshold names (not merely
that a swap happens)" -- test_a_bramble_wears_a_worse_frame_the_further_it_is_chewed sweeps
health from 1.0 to 0 in 1% steps and asserts the sequence of DISTINCT frames equals
DAMAGE_TEXTURES exactly. Sampling one fraction per frame would pass on a table whose middle
entries were swapped; the sweep cannot.

THREE THINGS THE BEAD DID NOT ASK FOR AND SHOULD HAVE:

1. THE FRAMES MUST SHARE A PAINTED BASE. They first rendered at 53 and 52 against the whole
   frame's 56 -- a 3-4px JUMP the instant the plant is bitten. Invisible in any still,
   obvious in play, and it put two of three outside the family's stem-pivot spread. Caught
   by measuring the rendered PNGs, not by looking at them. Now pinned by
   test_every_bramble_frame_is_the_same_plant_standing_in_the_same_place, which holds the
   frames against EACH OTHER -- a tighter claim than the style suite's per-frame check
   against the family, and the one that matters for an animation.

2. DAMAGE MUST BE SYMMETRIC. test_content_is_bilaterally_centred measures the content box
   midpoint against x=32 within 1px, so breaking ONE cane -- which reads far better -- fails
   the gate, and the failure looks like a rendering fault rather than a drawing decision.
   Both new SVG headers state this, along with "chew from the top and middle, never the
   bottom" for the pivot.

3. THE SWAP BELONGS ON _refresh_health_bar, NOT take_damage. Health goes UP: Plant.heal (the
   Salve Aloe, the rain) and Plant._regrow both call it. A wall repaired but still showing a
   chewed picture would be exactly the misleading readout this plant was given a picture to
   avoid. test_the_wall_sprite_follows_the_damage_in_both_directions asserts the healing
   direction specifically, which a take_damage-only implementation would fail.

MUTATION-TESTED, and worth reading: the FIRST mutant SURVIVED and was right to. Swapping
DAMAGE_THRESHOLDS changes nothing, because texture_for_health COUNTS how many thresholds
the fraction is below rather than walking them in order -- an equivalent mutant, not an
untested path. The second (making the ragged frame unreachable) was caught and named the
frame that vanished. Recording both because "the mutant survived" and "the test is weak"
read identically in a log and only one is a finding.

VERIFIED LIVE beyond the property reads: under a real aphid the frame changed between health
32.53 (fraction 0.813) and 25.83 (0.646) -- the 2/3 boundary, crossed by damage rather than
by a setter. A test writing health proves the function; only the running game proves the
function is wired to the thing that damages plants.

NOT DONE: the frames are static. There is no transition, no flinch tied to the swap, and the
plant does not shed anything when it changes. That is deliberate -- Plant already flinches on
every bite and a second motion on the same event would fight it -- but if the swap ever reads
as a pop rather than a change, that is where to look.

title: The panel says Health 40/40 for a plant that lasts four times as long
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md "New in cycle 110", second entry. PLAYER-FACING readout gap, created by
-3mhn.

game/hud.gd:2365 computes `fraction = plant.health / Plant.MAX_HEALTH` and :2373 prints
"Health %d/%d" against the same constant. Both are CORRECT for all nine plants -- Bramble
does not change MAX_HEALTH. It scales the incoming bite instead, at game/bramble.gd:120
(`super.take_damage(amount * BITE_RESISTANCE)`, BITE_RESISTANCE 0.25).

So a Barrier Bramble reading "Health 40/40" survives four times longer under one mouth
than a Corn Cobbler reading the same 40/40, and nothing on screen distinguishes them.

The claim is NOT that the number is wrong. It is that the selection panel has no
vocabulary for TOUGHNESS as distinct from HEALTH, and this is the first plant that needs
one. It will not be the last: resistance is the obvious knob for any future defensive
plant, and Pest already has the mirror concept (the Shield Bug's plate, `shell_absorb`).

Bramble.hold_seconds(n) already computes the honest answer in seconds and is currently
dead outside tests -- lint reports `hold_seconds() is referenced only from tests`, which
is the orphan-scan warning working as intended.

TASTE (argue with it, no citation offered): one extra line on the panel, shown only on a
plant where the two numbers differ, reading in seconds rather than in a multiplier. A
second bar is more machinery than the distinction is worth.

ACCEPTANCE: the panel says something true about a Bramble's durability that it does not
say about a cob; a test pins that it appears for a resisting plant and does NOT appear for
a non-resisting one (the second half is what stops it becoming a line on every plant); the
panel's width budget is re-measured, since hud.gd gates its rows on one.
close_reason:
SHIPPED, commit 481df02. The panel now reads "Barrier Bramble / Holds 11s against one
pest." Answering the acceptance clause by clause.

CLAUSE 1 -- "the panel says something true about a Bramble's durability that it does not
say about a cob." Done. Plant.bite_resistance() returns 1.0 on the base class and Bramble
overrides it; Plant.seconds_of_chewing_left(dps) turns that plus current health into
seconds; Hud.resisting_detail() formats it into the existing `detail` slot.

Asked of the PLANT rather than of `plant as Bramble`, deliberately: the second tough plant
needs no branch in the HUD, which is the same move the ladder line already makes with
has_upgrades(). And Bramble.take_damage() now reads bite_resistance() rather than its own
BITE_RESISTANCE constant, so a readout saying "holds 11s" and the mouth actually eating it
cannot come apart.

CLAUSE 2 -- "a test pins that it appears for a resisting plant and does NOT appear for a
non-resisting one (the second half is what stops it becoming a line on every plant)."
Done: test_only_a_plant_that_resists_gets_the_holds_line places a Bramble and a Sunflower
in one run and asserts both directions on the real Label. Verified live as well: a Corn
Cobbler one cell over reads "Corn Cobbler -- single / 1.0 dmg / 0.80s, 1 kernel(s)".

CLAUSE 3 -- "the panel's width budget is re-measured, since hud.gd gates its rows on one."
Done, and the shape matters. The line does NOT add a row: hud.gd's own header records that
a detail line too wide for the 232px box does not clip, it WRAPS, the label grows a row,
and the VBox pushes Upgrade and Uproot past the panel's foot -- and _health_text's comment
records a third text row pushing SelectionBox's foot to exactly 648, flush with the panel
edge. So it rides in the `detail` slot seven plants already fill with idle_detail(), and
is registered in selection_detail_corpus() priced at the FORMAT's ceiling (999s) rather
than at today's 11s. test_the_holds_line_is_priced_by_the_selection_budget pins both
halves: that the widest line is in the corpus, and that the corpus is NOT tracking the
live number.

THE BEAD'S TASTE CALL WAS TAKEN AS WRITTEN -- "one extra line, shown only where the two
numbers differ, reading in seconds rather than in a multiplier" -- and runtime is what
justified the seconds half rather than my agreeing with it. The number tracks: health 40.0
-> "11s", 39.42 -> "11s", 21.86 -> "6s". A multiplier would have been static, and no
static test of the formatter could have told the difference.

WHAT THIS TURNED UP THAT THE BEAD DID NOT ANTICIPATE, and it is the more important half:

  test_the_selection_box_stays_inside_the_side_panel_when_damaged -- the test that should
  have gated this whole change -- had SILENTLY STOPPED COVERING THE PLANT THE CHANGE IS
  FOR. Its own comment says "Every plant kind". It asked _grass(game) for every id and
  `continue`d on a refusal, so the Barrier Bramble (refused on grass since cycle 110) was
  skipped and the test went on passing. Worse than the one plant: the same `continue`
  swallowed "not paid for" exactly as silently, so the loop was only ever measuring
  whatever the starting unlocks happened to cover.

  Fixed: the catalogue is unlocked, the cell is chosen per plant (road for an on_road
  plant, grass otherwise), a refusal is now a FAILURE rather than a skip, and
  `covered == PlantCatalog.ids().size()` is asserted at the end. That last line is the
  point -- without a denominator the test could cover eight of nine and report clean,
  which is exactly what it had been doing.

ALSO WORTH THE NEXT READER'S TIME: Plant.MAX_HEALTH is still a shared const and this bead
did not change that. The panel now has a vocabulary for toughness, and the HEALTH numbers
are still raw. That is deliberate -- bramble.gd's header argues resistance over a
per-plant pool because of what it does to the Aloe's heal -- but it means "Health 40/40"
is still literally what a Bramble shows, with the seconds line beside it doing the work.
If a future plant makes that pairing confusing, the fix is the health row's text, not this
line.

NOT DONE: the run-summary card and the in-world bar are untouched; only the selection
panel learned the word. -fohy is the related open question about the post-mortem.

title: Should the garden speed be remembered between runs?
description:
SOURCE: cycle 102's -03t6 runtime pass. Taste call, argued rather than measured.

WHAT THE GAME DOES NOW (verified 2026-08-17): `GameSpeed` cycles 1x -> 2x -> half
and parks at 1x while the pause card is up (`hold()`/`release()`). It resets on
`_end_run` and on `Game._exit_tree`, so the choice does NOT survive a run, a
restart, or a quit.

That reset is right for correctness -- `Engine.time_scale` is process-global and
outlives every node, so leaving it at 2x across a scene change would be a bug.
It is probably wrong for the player: someone who plays at 2x almost certainly
wants 2x next time, and re-pressing the button every run is the same friction the
"does not reset on wave end" decision already refused once.

THE MECHANISM EXISTS: `RunConfig` is an autoload that already persists audio
mutes and key bindings (`apply_audio_mutes`, `apply_key_bindings`), so this is a
preference joining a set that has a home, not a new save system.

CARE NEEDED, and this is the whole reason it is a bead rather than a one-liner:
- Restoring a speed at launch must not fight the pause parking, `_end_run`, or
  `_exit_tree` -- there are now four places that write `Engine.time_scale`.
- A saved half-speed makes a FIRST run slow for a player who has forgotten they
  set it. Decide whether the persisted value is clamped to {1x, 2x} or whether
  the slow mode is deliberately sticky too (kanban says the slow mode is for the
  person who drew the game, which argues sticky).
- The suite writes the developer's real `user://` unless redirected --
  `save_persist_check.py` exists for exactly this and will fire on any test that
  can reach `RunConfig._save()`.

ACCEPTANCE: a speed chosen in one run is the speed the next run starts at; a
headless test pins that resuming from pause is still 1x and that the persisted
value survives a RunConfig round-trip; `save_persist_check.py` stays clean.
close_reason:
DONE. The garden remembers the speed the player chose, across a run, a restart and
a quit. Save format v6 -> v7.

DECISION, STATED: STICKY, AND HALF SPEED IS STICKY TOO. The button prints its own
current step on the top bar of every frame with the next step in its tooltip, one
press from normal -- and that visibility is exactly what makes a sticky setting
safe, because a forgotten half speed is self-announcing. Clamping to {1x, 2x} buys
a defect with NO signal: two of three steps remembered and the third silently not.
kanban also has the slow mode down as being for the person who drew the game, a
deliberate audience who would otherwise re-choose it every launch.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE THAT: the speed readout leaving the top bar -- hidden behind a
menu, or a button that stops printing the current step -- which turns it into
invisible state and makes the clamp right. Or an actual playtest report of a slow
first run confusing someone. Pinned by a test, so a future clamp has to argue with
a failing assertion rather than with a comment.

THE FOUR Engine.time_scale PATHS were enumerated before designing, which is what
made the restore safe: _apply() via cycle()/set_step(), hold() from pause_run(),
release() from resume_run(), reset() from _exit_tree() and _end_run(). The restore
goes in through set_step(), so a hold is honoured (the parked choice moves, the
engine stays 1x), reset() keeps clearing the engine on every way out, and the
choice now lives on disk where reset() cannot see it.

OLD SAVES: v1/v2/v5/v6 all read game_speed_step = 0, which is the state of a player
who never had the control; load_status becomes "migrated" and the file is rewritten
once in the v7 shape with everything else intact. The fixture for that test
deliberately carries a milestone and a rebound key -- the fields a bump actually
loses. A step index from a FUTURE build is kept verbatim rather than condemning the
file (scores cannot be re-earned; a speed can) and falls back to 1x at the point of
use rather than being wrapped.

The line was widened rather than added, following v6's precedent literally, with a
VERSION_WITH_SPEED constant so the parser is told which shape it is looking at
instead of comparing against whatever SAVE_VERSION happens to be. Honest note left
in the file: the speed is NOT an Options-screen switch, and a fifth non-switch
preference should rename the line rather than grow it again.

PARENT WIRING, which the lane could not do and correctly handed back as exact
edits: Game._ready() calls apply_game_speed() -- in _ready and not in RunConfig's,
because a saved half speed applied at process start would slow the TITLE screen for
no reason a reader of that scene could find -- and cycle_speed() files the step. A
stale comment at _end_run claiming "a restart from this screen must start at 1x" is
corrected; it now comes back at the remembered speed.

TWO TESTS FAILED ON THE MERGE AND BOTH WERE RIGHT: the game had genuinely stopped
starting at 1x. GameSpeed._step is static and RunConfig.game_speed_step is autoload
state loaded from the real save before any setup() runs, so the chosen speed is
process-global twice over and a GameSpeed.reset() at the top of a test is no longer
enough. Pinned in the suite's setup()/teardown(), Engine.time_scale included -- a
suite left at 2x retimes every later script's tweens and awaits.

FILED, NOT HIDDEN: the first suite run after the bump migrated the developer's REAL
highscore.save to v7, before any redirect could apply, because RunConfig is an
autoload and _ready() beats setup(). Nothing was lost and the migration is what the

title: findings names the viewport when a panel is what overflowed
description:
SOURCE: log-devtools.md cycle 98, gap [G-072]. Two steps, in order.

findings reports a Control that overflows as "extends past viewport", naming the OUTERMOST
boundary rather than the nearest one:

  GridContainer 'PlantBar' extends past viewport (rect: 908,116 -> 1319,332, viewport: 1152x648)

True, and the least useful true thing available. PlantBar is a child of a 256px-wide SidePanel
and broke THAT first, by 167px; the viewport only afterwards. A reader chasing "past the
viewport" looks at screen size and anchors, and the fix was in a container three levels in.

The harness already has the idea: `contained-in --node PATH --within PATH` reports per-side
overhang, and findings surfaces `ui_escapes_panel` for a SIBLING panel. What it does not do is
check a Control against its own ANCESTOR, which is the containment a layout bug most often
breaks.

The work:
  (a) RECONCILE FIRST against the installed 0.54.0 per gap-reconcile. Three of the last six
      gaps filed from here were sharper after reading the current source, and two earlier ones
      turned out already fixed. Do not skip this.
  (b) If it survives, file upstream with the captured message above and the proposal: when a
      Control overflows the viewport, walk its ancestors and name the NEAREST Control it also
      escapes -- "extends past its parent 'SidePanel' by 167px (and the viewport)". The rects
      are already in hand at that point and the walk is a few lines.

Note what makes this worth filing rather than shrugging at: the finding was CORRECT and still
cost time, because it pointed at the screen when the problem was a panel. A finding that names
the wrong container is the same class as cycle 97's suite_reach finding that accused the test
suite when the cause was a string literal -- both were true, both sent the reader to the wrong
place, and both had the better answer in hand at the moment of reporting.

ACCEPTANCE: 0.54.0 is checked and the result recorded either way; if the gap survives, an
upstream issue exists quoting the real message, and the [G-072] entry gains a status line
naming the version checked and the issue number.
close_reason: Reconciled against 0.54.0 and filed. dev_tools.gd:3915 still formats the ui_overflow message with no ancestor walk, so the gap survives. Filed as gh#57 together with G-073 (screenshot --region takes output pixels while node-bounds reports viewport coordinates) because they share a shape: a reply that is true, is the most general true statement available, and sends the reader to the outermost cause when the specific one was already computed.

title: How often has a heredoc silently damaged a file here?
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md New this cycle (97), second entry, and the cycle-97 workflow change.
OUTSIDE this cycle's neighbourhood -- the work was a grammar document; this is about how
edits get made.

CLAUDE.md step 2 has forbidden writing code through a shell heredoc since cycle 54, in those
words, and names four occurrences where one stripped the leading `#` from GDScript comment
blocks. Cycle 97 broke it a fifth time in a NEW shape: a Python script inside a heredoc,
splicing a line range, which is the same shell plus a second escaping layer. The rule now
names that shape and names the sanctioned fallback (Read the exact bytes and Edit again, or
Write the whole file).

What is worth measuring, and cannot be measured by reading the rule: how often does this
project's own history contain the pattern? The log records four comment-stripping incidents
and now one escaping incident, but those are the ones that were NOTICED. A heredoc that ate a
backslash somewhere harmless would never have been written down.

The work: grep the git history for commits whose diff introduced a GDScript string literal
containing a literal newline, or a comment block whose leading `#` is missing. Both are
mechanically findable in a diff. Report the count and the cycles.

Expect this to find little. The four known incidents were all caught the same day by a
compile failure or a denominator, which is the point -- the dangerous version is the one that
compiles and behaves correctly, and cycle 97's did. A survey that finds zero silent instances
is a real answer and says the existing gates are catching this class.

Do NOT build a checker for it without that count. house-static-checker's denominator rule has
correctly refused three checkers in this project already, and a fifth-occurrence-of-a-known-
rule is exactly the kind of thing that feels like it deserves a tool.

ACCEPTANCE: the history is swept for both signatures with the command recorded so it can be
re-run; the count is reported per signature; and a decision on a checker is written with the
count as its justification either way.
close_reason:
Swept, and the answer is ZERO on both signatures.

THE COMMANDS, recorded so they can be re-run:
    python .claude/surveys/heredoc_survey.py            # the sweep
    python .claude/surveys/heredoc_survey_controls.py   # the positive control

RESULT: 933 (commit, .gd file) versions across 631 commits and all branches. Signature A (a string literal containing a literal newline) = 0. Signature B (comment prose with no leading #) = 0.

THE ZERO IS LOAD-BEARING, so it is controlled. A sweep that reports 0 and a sweep that is broken read identically, and this one was broken twice before it was right:
  - v1 scanned diff LINES and reported 554 hits, ALL FALSE -- every one a prose comment in which a quoted phrase wrapped across two # lines. Counting quotes per line cannot tell a broken string from a sentence.
  - v2 used a hand-rolled (?<!\)" regex and reported 144 hits, ALL FALSE -- every one an 'if c == "\\\\":' in the test suite, because that regex does not know an escaped backslash is not an escaped quote.
  - v3 asks tools/gdsource.py's literal_spans instead, which is the same scanner pass that does the blanking and therefore cannot disagree with it. 0.
The control file pins all four outcomes: it fires on real Signature A damage, fires on real Signature B damage, and stays silent on both false-positive classes above. 5 of 5 pass. So the zero is a measurement, not an absence of measurement.

DECISION: NO CHECKER, and the count is the justification. house-static-checker's denominator rule wants evidence the defect happens; the denominator is 0 in 933. More useful than the number is WHY it is zero -- there are two escape paths and both already terminate in a parser. Damage to GDScript is caught by lint/import/compile; damage to the scratch script doing the editing is caught by Python's own parser. Neither can be silent for long, which is exactly what the five known incidents show: all were caught the same day.

SIXTH OCCURRENCE, observed live, and it is the first one caught IN THE ACT rather than reconstructed: while writing this very survey I patched it through 'python - <<PY', the heredoc ate the backslash in every "\n", and the escape became a literal newline inside a string literal -- an unterminated string at the exact line the patch touched. That is precisely the cycle-97 shape (a Python script inside a heredoc, shell plus a second escaping layer), reproduced by the person surveying how often it happens, one hour after quoting the rule to two lanes. Python's SyntaxError caught it within one command.

So the rule in CLAUDE.md step 2 EARNS ITS KEEP -- it saves real time -- but it does not need a tool behind it. Its value is avoiding the loop, not preventing a silent defect, because a silent one has never been demonstrated here and the survey now says so with a denominator.

title: A blanked-region finding should say the token was there
description:
SOURCE: log-devtools.md cycle 97, gap [G-071]. In-project checker, not the harness -- the fix
is ours.

tools/suite_reach_check.py reported four symbols as "public and no test names it" while all
four were named in real code at lines I could point at (test/unit/test_placement.gd:3868,
:3973, :3985, and pane_label_for near the end). It cost several minutes of treating the
checker as broken -- probing strip_comments, checking line endings, reading STRING_RE --
before a `git stash push <one file>` bisect showed the cause was my own edit.

The checker was RIGHT. A heredoc had eaten a backslash and put a literal newline inside a
string literal, so blank_strings correctly treated the remaining 1018 characters of the file
as one string body and every symbol after that point was invisible to the scan.

The finding accused the test suite ("no test names it") when the cause was the file's syntax.
Both facts were in hand at the moment of reporting: the checker holds `raw` and the blanked
source at that point, and the token IS present in raw.

The improvement is one clause in the finding text: when a symbol is reported unreached AND
its token appears in the raw text of some test file, say so.

  FINDING: game/cue_legend.gd:89 func `row_count` is public and no test names it.
    note: the token DOES appear in test/unit/test_placement.gd but only inside a region this
          scan blanked -- check that file for an unterminated or multi-line string literal.

That converts a finding that sends you to write a test into one that sends you to the actual
defect. Note the house rule this serves: every finding carries the fix, and "write a test for
it" was the wrong fix here.

Check while in there whether the sibling checkers can mislead the same way -- group_leak,
settle_read, save_persist and message_corpus all blank strings over the same corpus, so a
runaway string literal would silence each of them differently. If they can, the clause is
worth sharing rather than copying (see -g1j9, which already proposes a shared source blanker
for tools/).

ACCEPTANCE: a symbol reported unreached whose token is present in a test file's raw text says
so in the finding, naming the file; the behaviour is demonstrated by reintroducing the
cycle-97 defect in a scratch copy and observing the improved message; and the other
string-blanking checkers are checked for the same blind spot with the result recorded either
way.
close_reason: Cycle 107 five-lane fan-out; merged to main, 744 tests green, findings 5/5 clean, reach 7/9 nothing unreached

title: Assert a live scenario's precondition where it is consumed
description:
SOURCE: cycle 96's live scenario failing twice in the same way. Not player-facing; the
sentence saying why is that it is the reason two runtime checks this cycle and last were
recorded blocked or wasted.

Twice now a live scenario has silently lost its precondition and the failure surfaced one verb
downstream as something else:

  * Cycle 94: killed the plant that was selected, then arm_uproot answered "nothing is
    selected" and read as a broken uproot.
  * Cycle 96: the unread-then-displaced case lost its selection between steps; arm_uproot
    answered "nothing is selected" again, nothing was driven, and the ledger row is `partial`
    with that check marked blocked (correctly -- the mechanism worked).

Both times the scenario was several commands long and the precondition was established near
the start. Nothing re-checks it, and the verbs that consume it answer with a refusal that
reads as a finding about the FEATURE rather than about the setup.

The cheap fix is a habit and it is worth writing down where scenarios are driven: assert the
precondition IMMEDIATELY BEFORE the step that consumes it, not once at the top. For selection
that is one call -- run-method state and grep selected_placed -- and it converts "nothing is
selected" from a mystery into a known setup failure.

Consider also whether devtools_ext should help. -nj7w already proposes that project verbs
refuse a call with a missing required argument; this is the same shape one level up, where the
argument is game STATE rather than a parameter. A `cmd require_selection` that fails loudly
would be one option, but note honestly that a verb which only asserts is a verb nobody
remembers to call -- the habit may be the better answer, and saying so is a legitimate
outcome.

ACCEPTANCE: the practice is written wherever runtime scenarios are described for this project
(a skill, not CLAUDE.md -- step 5 prefers deleting rules to adding them), with both failures
named; and a decision is recorded on whether any devtools_ext support is worth building, with
the reason if not.

title: Does any remaining untaught cue deserve the legend's layout cost?
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md New this cycle (95), second entry. PLAYER-FACING, and it is a question about
what NOT to build.

The cue legend teaches six of the grammar's ten shapes and a seventh row does not fit: six
rows end at 294 of the 300px matte, seven would end at 340 (derived from CueLegend's
constants, and test_the_legend_fits_the_page_it_is_drawn_on holds the bound). So the next cue
taught is a layout decision -- a shorter ROW_PITCH, a second legend page, or dropping one of
the six -- rather than an append.

Four cues remain untaught, and cycle 95 established that ONE OF THEM NEEDS NO ROW. The
weather's scattered marks are the obvious candidate, because a player sees the whole board
change texture. But the game already says it in words three times: Hud.show_weather
(game/hud.gd:1899) raises a banner naming it, Hud.weather_headline (:1907) writes that
sentence, and Hud.next_wave_note (:1582) names the coming weather in the prep note. The marks
are a second channel on a named state, which is the two-channel rule working -- the opposite
of the ARMED cue's situation, which had no words anywhere and is why it earned the row.

So the real question is whether either of the remaining three deserves the layout cost:
  * the straight-line state (placement_preview.gd:322, dead ground; :331-332, redundant patch)
  * the husk's pip count (husk_layer.gd:117-124)
  * the small-solid-ring marked cell (sole_cover_marks.gd:154)

Apply the same test to each before touching layout: DOES THE GAME SAY IT IN WORDS ANYWHERE?
That is the question that settled the weather in one grep and it is cheaper than any design
discussion. A cue with a banner does not need a legend row; a cue with nothing does.

If all three have words somewhere, this closes with "six is the right number" -- which is a
real and useful answer, and would mean the legend is finished rather than merely unfinished.

ACCEPTANCE: each of the three remaining untaught cues is checked for whether the game names
it in words anywhere the player sees, with the file:line either way; the ones that have words
are recorded as not needing a row; and if any lacks words, the layout cost of teaching it is
priced (pitch, second page, or a swap) before anything is drawn.
close_reason: Answered NO. Legend page is exactly full (294 of 300px; a 7th row lands at 340 and cannot be bought by tightening pitch). All six untaught cues argued individually. Two findings: the grammar's derivation grep is blind to Line2D marks, and the lane-pressure hatch has no row.

title: Two tests still hand-copy a list the game declares
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md New this cycle (95), first entry. Not player-facing; the sentence saying why
is that it is two tests that will break the next person who adds a sound or a mutation.

Three tests kept a hand-written copy of a list the game already declares. One fired this cycle
for exactly that reason -- adding a sixth legend row broke the test that the same edit was
supposed to satisfy -- and was fixed by deriving from the source. Two remain, and they are NOT
the same problem:

  (a) test/unit/test_combat.gd:5255 -- `var all: Array[StringName] = [Pest.MUTATION_ARMOURED,
      Pest.MUTATION_WINGED, Pest.MUTATION_HUNGRY]`. Trivially derivable:
      Pest.MUTATION_HUSK_MULTIPLIER is described elsewhere in this same suite as "the

  (b) test/unit/test_combat.gd:637 -- `var used: Array[StringName] = [Sfx.PLANT_PLACED, ...]`,
      the event ids the CALL SITES use. This one cannot come from Sfx.SOUNDS, because SOUNDS

(b) has a working precedent in this repo: tools/message_corpus_check.py does exactly that for
show_message call sites, and it exists BECAUSE the same list was being rebuilt by hand for
three cycles. So the shape is known and the checker conventions are written down in
.claude/skills/house-static-checker/SKILL.md.

Do (a) first -- it is one line and it removes a copy. Then decide (b) on the denominator:
cycle 87 had to hand-edit that list when adding PEST_KILLED_HARD, which is one known
occurrence. house-static-checker's own rule is that a checker never observed to fire is not a

occurrence plus a precedent may still not be two occurrences.

ACCEPTANCE: (a) is derived from Pest.MUTATION_HUSK_MULTIPLIER and the hand-list deleted; (b)
is either built as a checker following the house conventions, or refused in writing with the
occurrence count that justified the refusal, so nobody proposes it a third time.
