title: Assert the invariant, not the three instances
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (25 of 30)'. Three separate tests check three screens going inert, each written when that screen got caught. The invariant is one sentence -- nothing behind a full-screen backdrop is focusable -- and it is checkable in one sweep: with an overlay up, walk every Control under a lower CanvasLayer and assert focus_mode == FOCUS_NONE. That catches the fourth screen nobody has written yet, which is the whole point.
notes:
PREMISE CONFIRMED CYCLE 112, and two of its three claims are wrong. Checked with
.claude/skills/confirm-the-premise (built this cycle; this is its first application).

COUNT CLAIM -- "Three separate tests check three screens going inert." REFUTED. Re-derived
rather than read: seven test functions in test/unit/test_selftest.gd assert a focus_mode
transition, across five distinct screen pairings --
  test_opening_the_notebook_takes_focus_away_from_the_menu_behind_it        (:1341)
  test_the_keys_screen_is_reachable_from_the_title_and_does_not_stack       (:1369)
  test_the_options_screen_is_reachable_from_the_title_and_does_not_stack    (:1877)
  test_closing_the_notebook_gives_the_pause_card_back_still_paused          (:6137)
  test_escape_in_the_keys_screen_closes_it_without_unpausing_the_run        (:6424)
  test_escape_in_the_options_screen_closes_it_without_unpausing_the_run     (:6606)
  test_the_hud_is_inert_while_an_overlay_is_open                            (:11461)

THE ASK -- "replace them with one sweep" -- IS PARTLY SATISFIED, by the last of those.
test_the_hud_is_inert_while_an_overlay_is_open (plant-tower-defense-csrc) already does the
derived-set version of exactly this idea: it takes Hud.interactive_controls() rather than a
written list, so a plant added to PlantCatalog is covered without anyone remembering, and it
asserts FOCUS_ALL -> FOCUS_NONE -> FOCUS_ALL plus MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE. What it does NOT do
is generalise: it covers ONE overlay (the pause card) over ONE layer (the HUD).

So the remaining work is not "write the sweep". It is the CROSS-PRODUCT: three
OverlayScreen subclasses (game/key_binding_screen.gd, game/notebook_screen.gd,
game/options_screen.gd) against the layers beneath them (_summary_layer at 20 and
_pause_layer at 30 in game/game.gd:1073-1169, plus the HUD's own).

FEASIBILITY CLAIM -- "walk every Control under a lower CanvasLayer and assert focus_mode ==
FOCUS_NONE" -- IS NEARLY VACUOUS AS WORDED, and this is the part that would have wasted the
cycle. A Label, a ColorRect and a Panel are FOCUS_NONE at all times, so a sweep asserting
FOCUS_NONE over every Control passes over a screen that was never focusable in the first
place and over one that correctly went inert, identically. test_the_hud_is_inert... avoids
this by asserting FOCUS_ALL FIRST, so the set is proved non-empty and live before it is
proved dead -- and by asserting a non-empty denominator (`controls.size() > 4`) with the
message "an empty list here would pass this whole test without checking anything".

Any general sweep MUST keep both of those. The subject is "every Control that is focusable
DURING PLAY", which is a set that has to be collected while the overlay is closed, not a
predicate that can be evaluated while it is open.

NOT A BLOCKER, and Hud.interactive_controls() is the only accessor of its kind
(grep: it exists on Hud and nowhere else), so a generic walk needs a tree walk rather than
a per-screen method.
close_reason:
SHIPPED as test_every_overlay_makes_everything_under_it_unfocusable. The bead's premise was
confirmed first with the new .claude/skills/confirm-the-premise, and all three of its
factual claims moved -- the full confirmation is on this issue as a note and is worth
reading before the summary below.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY BUILT, which is not what the bead asked for:

The bead asked to replace three tests with one sweep. There were SEVEN tests, and one of
them (test_the_hud_is_inert_while_an_overlay_is_open, plant-tower-defense-csrc) was already
the derived-set version of this idea -- it takes Hud.interactive_controls() rather than a
written list, and asserts FOCUS_ALL -> FOCUS_NONE -> FOCUS_ALL plus MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE. It
covers ONE overlay (the pause card) over ONE layer (the HUD).

So the gap was the CROSS-PRODUCT, and that is what landed: all three OverlayScreen
subclasses (notebook, keys, options) over the pause card and the HUD beneath it, each
opened through PauseScreen's own button, each closed through its own Escape handling, with
the round trip asserted both ways.

THE ONE THING THAT WOULD HAVE MADE THIS USELESS, and it was in the bead's own proposed
implementation: "walk every Control under a lower CanvasLayer and assert focus_mode ==
FOCUS_NONE" is nearly vacuous. A Label, a ColorRect and a Panel are FOCUS_NONE at all
times, so that assertion passes identically over a screen that went inert and over one that
was never focusable. Written as specified this would have been a permanently-green test.

The fix came from the existing test's own defence against exactly that: the subject is
COLLECTED while nothing is open (every Control that is FOCUS_ALL during play), so a screen
contributing nothing to the set contributes nothing to the assertion -- and the denominator
is asserted (`live.size() > 2`) with a message saying why. Both borrowed deliberately
rather than reinvented.

MUTATION-TESTED, because it passed on its first run and a test that goes green immediately
has not yet told you it can fail. Forcing PauseScreen._set_card_active to always FOCUS_ALL:

  [FAIL] test_every_overlay_makes_everything_under_it_unfocusable
         GateButton is unfocusable behind the notebook screen -- Tab does not care what is
         drawn on top: Expected 0 but got 2

WHAT THE BEAD WANTED AND DID NOT GET, named rather than implied: it says the sweep should
"catch the fourth screen nobody has written yet". This catches a fourth screen only if
somebody adds a row to the `overlays` array -- and the test asserts that array is size 3
with a message saying a fourth OverlayScreen subclass needs a row. That is a deliberate
downgrade from the bead's ambition: a truly automatic sweep would have to discover overlays
from the tree, and PauseScreen opens each of the three by a different route (two by
NODE_NAME, the notebook by a `_notebook` field), so there is nothing uniform to discover.
The named list plus the count assertion is the honest version -- it FAILS when a fourth
arrives instead of silently not covering it, which is the property that actually mattered.

THE SEVEN EXISTING TESTS WERE NOT DELETED. The bead's title says "assert the invariant, not
the three instances", and deleting them was tempting. They are not instances of this
invariant: six of the seven assert things this sweep does not -- that Escape reaches the
right handler, that P does not unpause through an open overlay, that the card declines the
keystroke its child just answered. Those are input-routing claims that happen to check a
focus value on the way past. Removing them would have traded seven specific guarantees for
one general one.

title: Move set_active onto OverlayScreen and let the overlay call it
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (25 of 30)'. TitleScreen._set_menu_active, PauseScreen._set_card_active and Hud.set_active are the same eight lines under three names -- focus mode and mouse filter over a list of buttons -- each written when its own screen got caught. Three copies is where an idea becomes a helper, and OverlayScreen is what opens over all three. More importantly it should also be what CALLS them: an overlay knows when it opens and closes, and today each opener has to remember. The HUD's opener forgot for many cycles, which is plant-tower-defense-csrc.
close_reason:
SHIPPED in lane/9a2y, merged to main, and VERIFIED BY THE PARENT — the lane rated itself inconclusive because it could compile nothing and run nothing, which was the honest verdict for a lane.

Three byte-identical copies of the same eight FOCUS_NONE lines become one static on OverlayScreen. Hud.set_active delegates to it (applied by the parent, since hud.gd was another lane's file), PauseScreen._set_card_active is deleted outright, and TitleScreen._set_menu_active is left alone deliberately — see below.

UNDERSTATED THREE WAYS, all found by deriving rather than reading:

1. "each opener has to remember" is FIFTEEN call sites, not three: six in pause_screen, six in title_screen, three in game.gd. Every one is a line somebody has to not forget, in BOTH directions. Six of them are now zero.

2. ALL THREE COPIES RESTORED A DEFAULT, NOT WHAT THEY FOUND. They write FOCUS_ALL / MOUSE_FILTER_STOP unconditionally on release, so a control deliberately left unfocusable or click-through underneath comes back live and nothing says so. Invisible today only because every covered surface happens to be all-default buttons — which means it is a defect waiting for the first surface that is not. hold_inert() snapshots each control's prior state and release_inert() restores exactly that.

3. Two doc citations were ALREADY stale on main: hud.gd and test_selftest.gd both said "the same hazard OverlayScreen's class header documents", and that header said nothing about focus or inertness at all. The new header section makes the citation true rather than the citation being deleted.

THE DETAIL THAT MAKES IT WORK, and the lane found it rather than being told: close() NOT queue_free() at the close paths. queue_free defers to end of frame, so an _exit_tree restore lands AFTER the opener's grab_focus() — and grab_focus() on a FOCUS_NONE control is an error, not a focus. _exit_tree stays as a backstop for Game.resume_run() freeing the whole pause layer with an overlay still open.

The cover set is DERIVED from the tree rather than kept as a list, with the overlay's own subtree skipped so it can never kill its own Back button. And the hold is idempotent per control, which is exactly what lets TitleScreen._set_menu_active keep running alongside without its redundant calls turning the release into a no-op — that is why title_screen was left untouched rather than half-converted.

VERIFIED BY THE PARENT, which is the whole point of the lane's own verdict: 943/943 with 18284 assertions, so the three unexercised tests now pass along with every existing overlay test the lane flagged for watching. Plus lint 0/0, import clean, 19 of 19 checkers, and findings 0 across 4 of 5 on a live game.

STILL OPEN, and correctly not done at merge time: title_screen.gd could drop its six redundant _set_menu_active calls and swap three queue_free() for close(). Everything works untouched today because the hold is idempotent, so this is a dedup rather than a fix — and the close() swap is REQUIRED if the six calls go, or grab_focus() lands on a still-FOCUS_NONE button. Worth its own bead rather than a merge-time edit.

title: One table for every glyph the game draws, and what it means
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (24 of 30)'. Two vocabularies collide: KeyBindings.SHORT_NAMES owns the four arrows as KEY NAMES, and the UI owns the left arrow for Back, the middot as a separator, the em dash, the infinity sign for endless, and now a bullet for the revert mark. Choosing the left arrow as that mark collided with KEY_LEFT's own name and was caught only by looking at a screenshot. A single table naming each glyph and its meaning makes the collision checkable -- derive-the-list applies: the UI's marks must not intersect SHORT_NAMES.values().
close_reason:
Built: game/glyphs.gd, class_name Glyphs, 18 characters with a role each, gated nine ways.

THE BEAD'S OWN COLLISION IS ALREADY FIXED. KEY_REVERT_MARK is a bullet, and key_binding_screen.gd:159-168 carries a long comment explaining why it is not an arrow ('a moved one would read left-arrow left-arrow'). That reasoning lived in a comment and nothing gated it -- which is the actual defect, and is now gated.

A SECOND, LIVE INTERSECTION REMAINS, ON THE SAME SCREEN. OverlayScreen.BACK_TEXT is 'left-arrow Back' and KeyBindingScreen extends OverlayScreen, so the key screen draws the left arrow as its Back button AND as KEY_LEFT's printed name. Also title_screen.gd:539. NOT fixed, and the reason is the good part: the collision only bites a glyph that stands ALONE beside a value. 'left-arrow Back' carries a word. So the gate is narrower than the bead's literal wording -- 'no UI glyph may intersect SHORT_NAMES.values()' would have gone red on 'left-arrow Back' on day one and been waived, which is the hand-maintained list the table exists to remove. The exception is written INTO the assertion instead: the left arrow is recorded as carrying two roles, and a test asserts exactly one glyph does, that it is that one, and that it never becomes a MARK.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT MADE THE TABLE POSSIBLE: gdsource.strip_comments in KEEP mode (comments blanked, string bodies kept -- glyphs INSIDE literals, not glyphs in the comments explaining them). A raw scan of game/ finds the em dash 1858 times; through KEEP it is 78. The middot goes 17 to 9, and key_bindings.gd:60's middot correctly drops out as prose while :156's KEY_JOIN survives. That is the difference between a table of prose and a table of glyphs.

Also: zero non-ASCII in any .tscn or .tres -- every drawn glyph is built in code.

SIX PLANTED FAILURE STATES, each red for its own reason, including the historical bug replanted (mark set to the left arrow) and SHORT_NAMES gaining a key the table lacks. Every sweep carries a denominator assertion, and the witness and meaning tests each carry a CONTROL character the project has never used, asserted absent -- so 'contains' cannot be a sentence true of everything.

DELIBERATELY NOT WIRED, and I took a third option over the lane's recommendation. It offered one wiring edit (KEY_REVERT_MARK from Glyphs.BULLET) and noted honestly that wiring makes that glyph's anchor assertion compare Glyphs.BULLET to Glyphs.BULLET. The table earns its keep by being a CHECKED CACHE WITH TWO INDEPENDENT SIDES; wiring collapses it to one and the check stops being able to fail. So the constant keeps its literal and gains a prose pointer telling the next chooser to read Glyphs.ROLE_MARK first -- discoverability without spending an assertion.

The lane also declined to wire hud.gd, correctly: readout_shape_check.py reads worst_case and shapes out of Hud.STAT_READOUTS with a string-literal regex, so splitting 'Wave 9999 infinity threat 99' at Glyphs.INFINITY would leave it measuring a silently shorter declared worst case -- the exact defect that checker exists to catch.

THE MERGE COST ONE FAILURE, and it is the textbook one: eight 'var err := _T.assert_gt(...)' sites. name_check reports that clean; lint does not. 'Cannot infer the type of err variable because the value doesn't have a set type' is verbatim the class the not-a-compile caveat names, and it is the first time this project has hit it from a lane.

No player-visible change; nothing on screen moves.

VERIFIED: 880/880 tests, import OK (mandatory here -- new class_name), lint 0, check_all 19/19, suite_reach 0 NEW.

title: Mark the plant an armed uproot will remove
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (24 of 30)'. Uproot arms for UPROOT_CONFIRM_SECONDS and says so in a message; the plant it will remove is not marked on the board. The armed reset on the Keys screen just got the two-channel treatment (a bullet mark plus a DANGER tint) for exactly this reason -- a pending destructive change should be visible on the thing it will destroy, not only in a sentence. Game._uproot_left already carries the armed state and Plant already has a selection ring to build on. Second channel matters here too: a tint alone is what colorblind_safe exists to make unreliable.
close_reason: The armed bed's selection marker turns DANGER red and doubles its line width, restored in _disarm_uproot. Two channels because a hue alone is what colorblind_safe exists to make unreliable. Marker also gained a NODE_NAME -- it was auto-named and therefore unaddressable. Verified live including that the placement preview's own marker is untouched.

title: Assert GardenTheme.measure agrees with a real Label at every size it is used at
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (23 of 30)'. GardenTheme.measure() is a DETACHED Label resolving the default theme, and it is now load-bearing for three budgets and four tests. Its correctness rests on 'this project sets no custom theme', which is asserted in exactly one place -- test_the_cards_own_measurement_agrees_with_the_labels_it_builds -- and only for the pause card's font size. The message row measures at MESSAGE_FONT_SIZE and the stats row at STAT_FONT_SIZE, and neither path is compared against a real in-tree Label. Sweep the sizes actually used.
close_reason:
SHIPPED in lane/fo96, merged to main — and it found a real budget defect, which the parent then confirmed and fixed.

ACCEPTANCE, clause by clause (seeded from the criterion, per verify-bd-item):

"assert GardenTheme.measure agrees with a real Label at every size it is used at"
    -- DONE, and the set was DERIVED rather than taken from the bead: FIVE distinct sizes
    (13, 15, 16, 17, 18) across eight production calls in six files. The only pre-existing
    agreement assertion covered 13 alone, via PauseScreen._measure.

THE BEAD IS WRONG IN ONE DETAIL AND UNDERSTATED IN THREE.

WRONG: it says "the stats row at STAT_FONT_SIZE". Hud.STAT_FONT_SIZE (26) is NEVER passed to
measure -- the stats row is budgeted from WORST_CASE_TEXT slots. A sweep that trusted the
bead would have measured a size nothing is priced at, and passed.

UNDERSTATED: five unchecked sizes rather than two; the docstring the bead quotes ("three
screens ... four tests") was itself stale at six files and twelve test references; and --
the one the bead does not mention at all -- Hud.selection_panel_budget() INLINES A SECOND
COPY of measure, its own detached probe Label calling Font.get_string_size directly at a
sixth size. No sweep of measure's CALLERS can ever reach it, because it is not a caller.

THE DEFECT, and this is the result rather than the sweep. The lane could not execute, so it
handed over an instrument and predicted what it would say. It was right:

    Root/SidePanel/PacketButton renders at 16 but Hud.packet_rack_budget()
    via GardenTheme.BUTTON_FONT_SIZE prices it at 18

The comment beside that budget argued the reasoning correctly and concluded it wrongly:
"these buttons set no font override, so they render at the theme's Button size". Sound --
except the HUD deliberately refuses GardenTheme.build(), the one surface that does. So with
no override they resolved the DEFAULT theme's Button size, and the budget priced a rack two
points wider than the one on screen. Over-pricing, so nothing overflowed; it reported less
headroom than the rack has, for as long as the comment beside it argued it was right. That
comment's "149 px for something that draws 179" was the same mistake stated as a
measurement. Live, after the fix: 159 of 232 px.

FIXED SO THEY CANNOT DISAGREE BY COINCIDENCE: Hud.PACKET_BUTTON_FONT_SIZE = 16, worn by the
buttons as an explicit override and read by the budget AND by the budget's own observation
string, which was separately still saying 18. 16 is what they already rendered at, so
nothing on screen moved.

The test's row reads that constant too, so it asserts the two AGREE rather than asserting a
number -- the version hardcoding 18 would have gone green by being edited to match whatever
the budget said, which is the failure mode of every test written after the code.

ONE DEFECT FIXED IN THE OWNED FILE: measure now splits on newlines and takes the widest
line. Font.get_string_size measures its argument as one run, so a two-line string returned
roughly the SUM of its lines where a Label draws only the wider one. No shipped number moves
-- every caller today passes single-line text.

THE VACUITY GUARD is the load-bearing part of the new tests and the lane said so: measure
returns 0.0 when no font resolves, and _T.text_width returns 0.0 for the same reason, so the
obvious equality passes UNCONDITIONALLY on exactly the broken run. Every comparison asserts
drawn > 0.0 first, and get_minimum_size() is used nowhere (it reports the clip stub on any
Label with clip_text, which is the trap this project already documents).

STILL OPEN, and worth its own bead when somebody takes it: selection_panel_budget()'s inline
copy should call GardenTheme.measure so the sixth size joins the sweep. Not done here
because it is hud.gd surgery that the sweep does not need in order to be correct.

VERIFIED BY THE PARENT: the failing test reproduced, the fix applied, 943/943 with 18284
assertions, lint 0/0, import clean, 19 of 19 checkers, findings 0 across 4 of 5, and the
corrected size read back off the running game.

title: Price the side panel the way the message row is priced
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (23 of 30)'. Hud._build_side_panel carries the widest column of text in the game -- plant names, blurbs and prices, all content-driven, all growing when a plant is added, none measured. Same defect class as the message row, one panel over, and the fix is the same shape: sweep PlantCatalog.PLANTS through whatever renders each row, measure with GardenTheme.measure(), declare it in BUDGET_FLOOR. Note the panel has several distinct text roles (name, blurb, price) and they may want separate budgets rather than one worst-of.
close_reason:
Priced -- but the bead's premise was wrong, and correcting it is most of the answer.

THE PREMISE: 'Hud._build_side_panel carries the widest column of text in the game -- plant names, blurbs and prices, all content-driven'. It is none of those things, and mostly it is not text at all:
  * THE PLANT BUTTONS ARE ICON-ONLY. button.icon = load(texture_path(id)) with expand_icon = true, and the names and blurbs live in tooltip_text. A tooltip is a floating popup: no slot, nothing to clip against, nothing to push. The panel's own comment says the button 'no longer shows' the name.
  * The heading is the literal 'Garden'.
  * The SelectionBox is already priced by -r722 (hud_selection_panel).
  * And it is not the widest column in the game either -- that is the selection panel at 330 of 335 px and the run summary at 330 of 335.2 px, both measured and both budgeted this cycle.

WHAT IS REAL, and it is narrow: the packet rack. Tier names crossed with prices crossed with stock state, drawn into the FIXED 232 px rect packet_row_rect hands each button. Fixed is the operative word -- applying -yoc2's rule, a button that cannot grow cannot push, so an over-long label does not move any layout a gate is watching. Same silence as a clipping label, for the same reason.

MEASURED: widest label is 'Common Packet (20)' at 179 of 232 px -- 53 px spare, 77% used. Six labels (3 tiers x 2 stock states).

I measured it wrong once first, and the code now says so: I used font size 15 and got 149 px. These buttons set no font override, so they render at GardenTheme.BUTTON_FONT_SIZE = 18, which is 179. Measuring at a size the button does not use prices a rack that does not exist.

SHIPPED: Hud.packet_rack_corpus() sweeping SeedBank.PACKET_ORDER (not listing three strings), Hud.packet_rack_budget(), a packet_rack budget entry -- the tenth -- with a floor of 40, and two tests.

THE FLOOR IS 40, NOT 53, ON PURPOSE. This budget is not guarding today's margin: a price would have to gain four digits to close 53 px. It is guarding A FOURTH TIER WITH A LONGER NAME, which is the only realistic way the rack overflows -- which is also why the corpus sweeps PACKET_ORDER, so a new tier is priced the day it is added rather than the day it breaks. The failing test invents 'Heirloom Collector Packet (250)' at 287 px and watches the warning fire.

ONE THING THE TEST TAUGHT ME: my first version rebuilt the budget entry with an abbreviated consequence string and then asserted the warning contained wording only the PRODUCTION string has. It failed, correctly -- an assertion against a sentence the test itself typed proves nothing. The consequence is now Game.PACKET_RACK_WHEN_FULL, read by both sides, so the test checks that the production sentence reaches the warning.

VERIFIED: 870/870 tests, import OK, check_all 19/19, suite_reach 0 NEW.

title: Give the banner a painter before a standing claim arrives
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (22 of 30)'. Hud._show_banner is private with three public callers (announce_wave, announce_wave_cleared, show_weather) and _fade_banner runs on a timer -- exactly the arrangement that produced two defects on the message row this cycle and last: several writers, one Control, timing between them. The banner has no painter. It has not bitten yet only because every claim on it is transient; the first standing one will. The message row's fix is the worked example: one _paint function owning the assignment, each writer setting its own claim.
close_reason: Lane 3, and the premise was UNDERSTATED in the way that mattered. The bead said three writers; enumerating the BEHAVIOUR (anything writing the banner Labels or the fade clock) rather than the spelling of _show_banner found four public entry points plus two internal -- the fourth being refresh() calling hide_banner() on game_over/victory, a CLEARING writer, which is exactly the class an arbitration has to handle and the one a three-claimant design would have missed. Painter copied from the message row's shape, as the bead asked. Four claim names on two rungs: both wave beats above weather, unknown BELOW unclaimed so a typoed name loses the banner rather than taking it. Tie goes to the ARRIVING claim, deliberately the opposite of the message queue, because the only reachable tie is two consecutive wave beats and refusing it would leave 'Wave 7 cleared' over a wave 8 already spawning. All three public signatures byte-identical, so game.gd needed no edit. The painter is now provably the only writer of both Labels' text/visible/modulate. AND IT FOUND SOMETHING BIGGER, filed as -zhqf: Game._on_wave_started calls show_weather at game.gd:453 and announce_wave at :465, same call stack, zero frames apart, and show_weather is called from nowhere else -- so the weather banner has never once been visible to a player. The weather claim now loses BY RULE instead of being written and stomped: same pixels, honest mechanism, and the design question is open rather than hidden. Confirmed live: with a wave beat standing, show_weather is refused and banner_claim() still reads 'wave'.

title: Give the message row one owner instead of three writers
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (21 of 30)'. show_message (the priority queue), _advance_message_queue (expiry) and _refresh_prep_note (the standing note) all set .text on one Label in game/hud.gd, and BOTH defects found this cycle were seams between them -- the note not surviving expiry, and not coming down when the wave started. It works now because each writer checks _message_left and the current text by hand, which is three conventions that happen to agree. A row with one owner and a stack of claims (highest priority wins, the note is the floor) makes the arbitration a rule. Note that show_message already HAS priorities and the standing note sits outside them, which is right with one note and wrong with two.
close_reason: One painter, two claims: _paint_message_row is the only assignment to the Label. 547/547 unchanged across the refactor, plus a new test for the collision the old text comparison could not survive. The last-wave branch went in on top of the clean ownership.

'Wave 16 next -- the last one.' is a one-branch change in next_wave_note plus a 'last' flag in the state dict (WaveDirector.WAVES.size() is static, and director.endless already distinguishes the mode that has no last wave).
close_reason: One painter, two claims: _paint_message_row is the only assignment to the Label. 547/547 unchanged across the refactor, plus a new test for the collision the old text comparison could not survive. The last-wave branch went in on top of the clean ownership.

title: Write the animation-testing pattern into a local skill
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (20 of 30)'. The record roll is the only animation in this game with a test; eleven others (Plant._pop, PauseScreen._play_entrance, TitleScreen._play_entrance, Hud._punch_readout, the husk fade, the banner fade) are verified by nobody, and headless cannot see any of them because GardenTheme.animations_enabled() is false there by design. The pattern that made the roll testable generalises: a PURE renderer for the moving value, the final state set before the tween exists, and a callback restoring it if the tween is interrupted. Plus the runtime half nothing states: set_game_speed 0.05 is what makes a tween observable at all -- at 1.0 a 0.8s animation finishes inside one bridge round-trip, which cost four wasted attempts this cycle.
close_reason:
SHIPPED in lane/itbj, merged to main: .claude/skills/assert-an-animation/SKILL.md, 132 lines.

CONFIRMING THE PREMISE WAS MOST OF THE WORK AND IT CHANGED THE DELIVERABLE TWICE.

FIRST: the bead's central claim is STALE. It says "the record roll is the only animation in this game with a test; eleven others are verified by nobody." On main, FOUR of the six it names now have tests — RunSummary._play_entrance, _fade_banner, PLANTING_POP via the duration sweep, and an entire seeds roll that did not exist when the bead was filed. Still unverified: Hud._punch_readout, PauseScreen._play_entrance, TitleScreen._play_entrance.

The denominator is wrong in both directions too: THIRTY create_tween() sites across sixteen files, not eleven — and a create_tween census is the WRONG SET anyway. Plant._wobble and _gait are _process sinusoids with no Tween at all, which is precisely why cycle 70 closed a bead as "verified unbuilt" for something that had shipped in the first playable build.

The correction STRENGTHENS the bead rather than weakening it: the pattern has been reached independently at least FIVE times by different cycles and written down nowhere. Five independent rediscoveries is better evidence for a skill than one exemplar was.

SECOND: two thirds of the requested content already lives in two other skills. The pure-renderer-past-the-gate half is extract-a-testable-seam; the entire set_game_speed / pause + step-time runtime half is read-a-moving-value, which already carries the cycle-72 recipe verbatim. The lane cross-linked rather than restated — so what shipped is 132 lines covering only what was genuinely unwritten: the final-state-before-the-tween rule, the restoring callback, kill-before-rearm, the pre-tween displacement as the assertable number, and the no-Tween-at-all rung.

That is the difference between a skill and a duplicate, and it is only visible if you read the neighbours first.

EVIDENCE GATHERED RATHER THAN RECALLED. Twelve incidents, each cited — including two the bead does not mention that are the sharpest: TWO MUTATIONS SURVIVED a test that pumped _wobble (aiming the breathe at _sprite.scale, and BREATHE_AMOUNT = 0.0, because every assertion was written RELATIVE to it); and the seeds roll independently reached the same three-part pattern, including killing the live tween before the worth-showing test.

ONE THING DELIBERATELY LEFT OUT, and the reason is the point: the container-child data.transform rule appears in CLAUDE.md's Gotchas and as an illustrative TEMPLATE entry at the top of log-devtools.md, but not as something that happened in this repo. The lane refused to cite seeded example text as an incident. A skill whose rules each carry a real incident is the format; one rule with a fabricated provenance would poison that.

ALL 24 CITATIONS READ BACK individually through citation_check on the file itself: 24 of 24 resolved. Two land on doc-comment lines deliberately, because in both cases the COMMENT is the claim being cited — not the cycles-68/76 error the checker warns about.

A GATE GAP THE LANE FOUND, worth acting on: citation_check --beads reads kanban.md plus bead prose and does NOT walk .claude/skills/. Every skill in this repo carrying file:line claims is outside the citation gate's denominator; this one was only checked because the lane invoked the checker on the file by hand.

A LIVE DEFECT FOUND IN PASSING, unfiled per the no-new-beads instruction and recorded here so it is findable: TitleScreen.RATCHET_STEPS is declared and read NOWHERE, under a comment claiming it "is what the roll actually shows" — and hud.gd:914 and test_selftest.gd:15461 both already describe that gap from across the repo. Also game/plant.gd has two stacked doc comments where breathe_scale's header is attached to flinch_amount.

VERIFIED BY THE PARENT: citation_check on the file 24/24 resolved, check_all 19 of 19 clean, suite 943/943, lint 0/0.

title: Derive the seen: count instead of incrementing it by hand
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (19 of 30)'. G-044 reads 'seen: 7', the single strongest signal in log-devtools.md -- seven independent sightings of one defect. It is incremented by hand and this cycle's audit found ids where a later entry re-described the same gap without bumping it, so the field understates. tools/gap_ledger.py already parses every mention of every id: counting them IS the seen count. Report derived-vs-declared and flag the disagreements; do not rewrite the old lines (same rule as the status).
close_reason:
Done, but the bead's premise was WRONG and the fix is a different check.

The bead reasoned: gap_ledger already parses every mention of every id, so counting
them IS the seen count. It is not. G-009 is FILED at `seen: 4` on its own first line
(log-devtools.md:467) -- four sightings happened before anyone wrote the id down.
Deriving the field outright reports 32 disagreements, of which four (G-009, G-010,
G-028, G-076) are the format working exactly as intended.

Mentions are a FLOOR on seen:, never an equality. Shipped in e19558c as three
findings on the summary line plus a --seen listing:

  understated (15) -- current line declares fewer sightings than there are lines
  mentioning the id. THIS IS THE BEAD'S REAL FINDING and the count it wanted:
  G-024, G-050, G-051, G-059, G-060, G-063, G-065, G-066, G-067, G-070, G-072,
  G-073, G-077, G-078, G-123.

  decreasing (0) -- seen: going down between mentions. Zero today; included because
  it is the shape a bad bulk edit takes and nothing else in the toolchain sees it.

  absent (12) -- current line carries no seen: at all, all twelve from the single
  bulk reconciliation block at 3969-3979 that marked eleven gaps fixed against
  0.38.0. Reported separately and NOT as a defect: a status change is a legitimate
  mention that is not a sighting.

Old lines left in place, same rule as the status field.

Two things found on the way. G-000 is the "no gaps this turn" sentinel rather than a
gap, and the status regex's bare word-character class was matching `n` in "n/a" and
turning it into a status of its own -- so the open count was 69 and is now 68. And
the four mutations the docstring names were RUN, not asserted: 15 -> 19, 15 -> 16,
15 -> 0, and 0/0/0. Cycle 136 shipped a fixture that asserted only the exit code and
survived four mutations, so these assert the counts.

title: Say what the next wave is worth during the prep gap

WaveDirector.threat_for() and pests_in_wave() are both static and both exist. Costs no bar space -- the banner slot is free between waves, which is exactly the window this would fill. title: Weather needs counter-play, or it is a difficulty modifier
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (17 of 30)'. Rain and drought arrive and are simply true -- the player watches. The design brief's own version had a counter ('unless a plant sits next to water') and it was dropped because Board is grass and dirt road only (game/board.gd:56, GRASS_EDGE_TILE maps masks over exactly two materials). Options: water tiles as a third material (expensive -- Board.PATH_CORNERS' header warns three numbers in other files were measured against this route and nothing recomputes them), or a cheaper counter that needs no terrain, e.g. a plant or upgrade that ignores drought. Decide which before building either.
notes:
CYCLE 111 NOTE, not a proposal and not permission to build -- this bead's own instruction
to wait for James still stands.

The ninth plant (Barrier Bramble, -3mhn) changed the ground this question sits on, in two
ways worth knowing before the decision is made. Both are filed with citations as -j0x2.

  1. Drought's whole effect is firing intervals. Enumerated: every consumer of the weather
     factor is a call to Plant.composed_interval (game/plant.gd:150-151) and there are
     exactly three -- corn_cobbler.gd:592, dandelion.gd:277, nettle.gd:253. A Bramble fires
     nothing, so a drought wave is now strictly easier for a garden built on walls than for
     one built on cobs. Nobody chose that.

  2. Option (b) in this bead's notes -- "a cheaper counter that needs no terrain" -- now has
     a concrete shape it did not have when this was written: drought dries a bramble out and
     it is chewed faster. It needs no third board material, uses a plant that already
     exists, and turns finding 1 from an accident into a mechanic.

Also: the rain heal is a FLAT Plant.MAX_HEALTH * heal_fraction (game/game.gd:425), and a
Bramble's bite_resistance() is 0.25, so those health points buy four times as many seconds
on a wall as anywhere else -- silently, with nothing on screen saying so.

title: Give weather a standing readout on the top bar
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (17 of 30)'. Hud.show_weather fires a banner as the wave opens and the banner fades; there is no standing readout, so a player who looks away has no way to ask 'why is my corn slow'. The top bar already carries 'Wave 2 / 16' and 'threat 2' and has room beside them. Cheap, and it is what makes a drought legible as a rule rather than as the game feeling wrong.
notes: MEASURED AND REFUSED, not forgotten. The top bar cannot afford weather: the wave slot's base string 'Wave  9999 infinity   threat 99' measures 302px in a 312px slot, so every candidate tag overflows -- '  rain' 366, '  dry' 357, ' ~' 324, even a bare '*' 317. Widening the slot to 366 made the project's own budget check report hud_stats_row at -35px (contents 1147 of 1112 max), i.e. the row overflows and shoves the wave button off the bar. Reverted in the same cycle; the measurement is recorded in Hud.WORST_CASE_TEXT so the next attempt reads it first. What DID land is plant-tower-defense-cxru: the selection panel now quotes the drought-stretched interval, which is the surface a player actually consults when asking 'why is my corn slow'. Reopen only with a decision about WHERE -- a new bar row, the message line, or paying the stats-row budget by trimming another slot.
close_reason: Shipped as game/weather_overlay.gd: weather is drawn on the board rather than the top bar, which the bead's own measurement had already ruled out. Two channels -- hue plus mark shape, flat dashes for drought and slanted streaks for rain. 8e37b2f

title: The selection readout ignores the weather multiplier
description: Source: cycle 35's runtime check, seen in a screenshot rather than caught by an assertion. The side panel prints '1.0 dmg / 0.80s, 1 kernel(s)' from CornCobbler.LEVELS (game/corn_cobbler.gd:49) -- the level table's own interval. Under a drought wave the cob actually fires every 1.60s (Plant.fire_interval_scale = 2.0), so the readout tells the player a number the game is not using. Same class as the fire-rate half of the weather feature: the rule reached the plants and not the surface that describes the plants. Hud._refresh_selection is where it lands.
close_reason: fire_interval() now returns the effective interval (level table x Plant.fire_interval_scale) and both surfaces read it. Found a SECOND instance of the same bug while fixing the first: readiness() divided a cooldown armed at 1.60 by a base of 0.80, so the cob's arming glow sat empty for the whole first half of every reload under a drought. Planted and watched fail.

title: Drive a live rebinding in the suite, not just a rebuilt card
description: Source: cycle 33's step 5 reflection, generalising the defect runtime caught. title: Say when a binding is actually saved
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (14 of 30)'. KeyBindingScreen._persist() writes on every capture and the only feedback is the row's key text changing -- which would look identical if the write had failed. RunConfig._save() has three separate push_warning paths for a write that did not land (cannot open the temp file, a short write, a readback that does not parse) and none of them reaches a screen. Start here rather than with the general save-confirmation idea: the write is synchronous with a button press, so there is an unambiguous moment to report.
close_reason:
SHIPPED. A binding that did not reach disk now says so, on the screen, in words a player can
act on.

THE PREMISE HELD EXACTLY. RunConfig._save() was `-> void` with four failure paths --
FileAccess.open returning null, a short write, a readback that does not parse, and a failed
rename -- each reporting via push_warning and nothing else. push_warning reaches the editor
log, which a player does not have and a screen cannot read. So KeyBindingScreen._persist()
wrote on every capture and the only feedback was the row's key text changing, which is
identical whether or not the write landed.

THE CHANGE. _save() returns whether the record reached disk; store_key_bindings and
_persist() thread it to the two places that can say something (a capture and the reset). All
13 other _save() callers ignore it and are still correct -- they had no answer before and the
behaviour on failure is unchanged.

TWO JUDGEMENTS, and neither is obvious until you have to write the sentence:

1. THE RENAME FAILURE RETURNS TRUE. Its own warning reads "The finished save is at %s and
   _load will adopt it" -- the record is complete, validated, and on disk; the next launch
   picks it up. Three of the four paths lose the write and return false. This one does not.
   A save confirmation that claims work was lost when it was not is worse than no
   confirmation at all, and that failure direction is the one a player cannot recover from
   by ignoring it.

2. THE SUCCESS SENTENCE SAYS NOTHING. "Set: M sound effects on or off" is what a player
   wants to read. Appending "saved" to every capture would put a word about disks on a
   screen about keys, forever, to cover a case that essentially never happens. Silence is the
   confirmation; the failure is what needs words.

   That asymmetry is also what made this testable: persisted_note() returns its caller's own
   sentence UNCHANGED on success, so both branches are pure and assertable with no screen,
   no save file and no failing disk.

WHY THAT PURITY MATTERS MORE THAN USUAL HERE: the failure sentence is unreachable in normal
play. An unreachable sentence is exactly the kind that ships misspelled, and building it
inline at the two call sites would have put it somewhere no test could read it.

TESTED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, plus the wiring:
  * a landed save adds nothing to the note;
  * a failed one keeps what was set and adds "NOT saved -- this key is set for now, but will
    be back to normal next time you play.";
  * store_key_bindings into an unwritable path returns false;
  * and into a writable one returns true -- without which the first assertion would pass on
    an implementation that always reports failure.
Mutation-tested: _save returning true on the open-failure path fails the test by name.

THE LAUNCH WAS DECLINED FOR SAFETY, and this is worth recording because every other decline
this session was "the test already makes this claim". Reaching this branch on a live session
means making a save FAIL, which writes the developer's real user:// -- CLAUDE.md warns about
exactly this and --isolated does not isolate user://. The test redirects RunConfig.save_path
to an unwritable path and restores it, which is the only safe way in.

WHAT IS NOT DONE, and the bead names it: this is the Keys screen only. The bead said "Start
here rather than with the general save-confirmation idea: the write is synchronous with a
button press, so there is an unambiguous moment to report." That is still the right scope --
the options toggles and the high-score write have no such moment, and giving them one is a
different design question. _save() now returns the answer, so whoever takes that on has the
mechanism already.

The deliberate click that starts the countdown is the one press in the whole attack chain (plant sounds, kernel hit flash, wave-clear banner) with no feedback of its own. Add a distinct button-press cue to the Grow-the-next-wave button.
close_reason: Shipped in 5e6f766: new Sfx.BUTTON_PRESSED (minimize_006.ogg at -10 dB, the quietest row in the table) plays from Game._on_next_wave_requested, a handler now sitting between hud.next_wave_requested and start_next_wave so the prep-timer expiry and the devtools start_wave verb stay silent. Extended to the plant bar (_on_plant_chosen), the other press with no cue of its own; Upgrade, Uproot and the packets were deliberately left alone since each already rings its own outcome and PURCHASE_DENIED stays the only sound a refused press makes. Note the issue's premise about timing: WAVE_STARTED is NOT later - start_next_wave reaches wave_started synchronously, so the bell is in the press's own frame, which is why the press cue is trimmed to sit under it. Verified live: Voice0 minimize_006 at -10.0, Voice1 impactBell at 0.0, same press, wave 1 live.

title: A swept husk's seeds appear on the HUD with no visual connection to where it was collected

Only a queued caption connects the two events. A seed glyph that flies from the husk's own position to the Seeds label, sized off HuskLayer.radius_for(value), would carry the payout across the screen instead of asking the player to read the same number twice in two different places. (From the original kanban idea backlog, cycle 20.)

title: StickySundew's _wash_order counter never resets
description: StickySundew._next_wash_order (sticky_sundew.gd:112) is a class-level static that only ever goes up - not on reload_current_scene, not between runs. Nothing breaks at any plausible count, but it is a number that only increases for as long as the process lives, in a file that also keeps a static list of live patches (_live). Worth a deliberate decision: either document why it is safe to never reset (and add a test pinning that a very large value still orders correctly), or reset it at a defined point (e.g. when the last patch is freed, or on a fresh run start).
close_reason: Chose (a) reset: _exit_tree resets _next_wash_order to 0 the instant _live empties -- the one moment resetting costs nothing, since nothing alive could still be compared against the number being handed back. Pinned by a new test (constructs+frees a warmup patch to prove the counter was >0, then confirms it drops to exactly 0 once the only live patch is freed). Verified headless (name_check, lint, run_tests 421/421, meta_key/group_leak/suite_reach/settle_read checkers all clean of new findings) and live: placed a Sundew (wash_order=1), freed it through its own exit tween, placed a second at a fresh cell, and confirmed it also got wash_order=1 rather than 2.

The last second or two before a wave lands is exactly when a player most wants a nudge. Add a brief pulse on _prep_bar.modulate once prep_left drops under ~2 seconds, reusing the same _ease_threat_tint-style kill-and-restart Tween shape t5l already applied to the HUD readout punches.
close_reason: Prep bar pulses (modulate alpha, looping kill-and-restart tween) once prep_left crosses PREP_BAR_URGENT_SECONDS=2.0; edge-detected so refresh()'s per-frame calls don't restart it. Verified live via bridge with a slowed game-speed window. Commit 676c465.

title: A seed packet's gamble resolves in the same frame it is bought
description:
SeedBank's own header calls a packet purchase "a gamble rather than a menu" and "with
a short catalogue that reads as suspense" (seed_bank.gd:8-10), but buy_packet()
(seed_bank.gd:176-197) deducts the cost, rolls the pool and emits plant_unlocked in
one synchronous call, landing as a text banner the instant the button is released. No
beat between spending the seeds and knowing the result. Add a brief reveal -- even a
short flicker through the tier-eligible pool before landing on the roll -- so the
suspense the code's own comment promises actually shows up on screen.
close_reason: Added Game._open_packet(): a short 3-step, ~0.27s flourish flashing other tier-eligible candidates before Game._reveal_plant_unlock shows the real banner (now MESSAGE_IMPORTANT so it isn't queued behind an ambient hint). buy_packet() itself is untouched/synchronous. Gated behind GardenTheme.animations_enabled(); headless keeps the instant reveal. Commit cf352da.

title: Distinguish naming a symbol from checking it
description: suite_reach_check concedes 'naming is a floor, not exercise' - a test writing WaveDirector.reset() and asserting nothing counts as reach. The honest upgrade is not a stricter name match but a second signal: whether the named symbol appears inside an assert_* argument or only in a statement. That distinguishes 'called it' from 'checked it' without pretending to understand the test.
close_reason: Added assert-argument co-occurrence as a second, advisory-only signal in suite_reach_check.py (commit 489193e). Naming still gates exactly as before; the new NOTE reports how many reached gating symbols never sit inside a _T.assert_*(...) argument anywhere in the test tree. Docstring extended (new WHAT THE ASSERT SIGNAL section + NOT COVERED caveat). Checker sanity-run clean against the repo (283 reached, 85 assert-only-absent). Headless /verify gates (name_check, import_check, lint, run_tests) all clean; full runtime bridge skipped as this touches no .gd/.tscn.

title: Measure how far coverage over-promises
description: The derived coverage map is an upper bound: a Corn shoots only the furthest-along pest, a busy Chomp grabs nothing, a winged pest is unreachable by a Chomp. So 'covered' over-promises exactly when a player is losing. An observed map was rejected because _ever_engaged is monotone - but a per-cell record of 'something was in range and did not fire' is not monotone and would measure the over-promise directly.
close_reason: Closed

title: Let a plant declare whether it engages, instead of a list two files away
description: Game.ENGAGING_PLANTS is a positive list of CORN and CHOMP. A fifth plant fails a test, which is the right failure, but it fails AFTER someone has written the plant. A PlantCatalog entry could declare it, so the answer lives with the plant. Note PlantCatalog.reach() is NOT this - it returns SAP_RADIUS for the Sundew for the dead-ground cue, and a Sundew engages nothing.
close_reason: Closed

title: Map where the garden never reached, not just that it did not
description: was_engaged() answers one question at one instant, at the exit. The same flag sampled per road cell would say WHERE the garden stopped reaching - the coverage-hole map the post-mortem's 'walked in untouched' line currently only aggregates. Genuinely different from lane pressure: pressure says where they got to, this says where nothing could touch them.
close_reason: Closed

title: cmd budgets refuses to answer without a Game in the tree
description: The budgets verb returns 'no Game in the tree' on the title screen. Two of its six entries do not need a Game at all: notebook_subhead builds its own SubViewport, and road_shape reads Board statics. The notebook budget in particular is about a title-screen subscreen, so requiring a run to read it is backwards. Degrade per entry instead of refusing wholesale.
close_reason: Shipped: road_shape builds a throwaway Board, 4 remaining entries degrade to unmeasured per-entry, commit 96acf81

title: Nothing stops the sixth world-space Control forgetting the rule
description: Plant and Pest each grew a _make_world_controls_click_through(), deliberately duplicated rather than shared. Two copies of a rule with no third enforcement. The test enumerates the live tree so it would catch a new offender, but only one on screen during that test - a Control appearing only on a boss wave, or in a menu the test never opens, is invisible to it.
close_reason: Closed

title: An escape records nothing about how it happened
description: _on_pest_escaped files every escape against Board.exit_cell() because the pest's own position is off-board when the signal fires. Eight beetles through one gap and eight stragglers over forty waves produce byte-identical evidence. The pest knows where it entered the exit cell from, how long it survived, and what it walked past untouched.
close_reason: Closed

title: BLOCKED_COLOR is a hand-typed near-red the palette merge missed
description: PlacementPreview.BLOCKED_COLOR is Color(0.95, 0.42, 0.36, 0.75), a hand-typed near-red that the GardenTheme palette merge did not catch. It should probably alias GardenTheme.DANGER. Note it draws brackets (already a shape channel) rather than a surface, so it is a value change belonging to the merge, not a legibility fix.
close_reason: Closed

title: Separate what is true of a road from what is true of THIS road
description: PATH_CORNERS produces 32 road cells and 2112px of walking. At least four things are calibrated against that route: the endless road budget's pests-per-cell, the Sundew's coverage arithmetic, the dead-ground count of 15 of 94, and the husk clearance. Each is tested individually; a second route would move all four at once and nothing says which are properties of a road and which of this one.
close_reason: Closed

title: The title screen's lawn and the notebook both predate half the catalogue
description: TitleScreen.PLANTS is a literal list of a Sunflower, two Corn Cobblers and a Chomp, chosen when those were the whole catalogue -- the Sticky Sundew is absent, so the first thing a new player sees advertises three quarters of the game. Separately, the notebook's five pages cover the Corn, the packet, the kernel and the Chomp twice; a grep for sunflower or sundew across notebook_screen.gd returns zero, so both tier-2 plants -- the ones unlocked late and least understood -- appear nowhere in the only place the game explains anything.
acceptance_criteria: The lawn is derived from PlantCatalog rather than a literal list, so a new plant appears without anyone remembering, and every plant in the catalogue has a notebook page. A test asserts both against PlantCatalog.ids().
close_reason: Closed

title: Compost swept is a numerator with no denominator
description: CompostMeter gained a husk_rotted signal in the sound pass and Game._on_husk_rotted receives it, plays a sound and increments nothing. So the post-mortem reports 'Compost swept 12' with no way to know whether four rotted or forty did. Every other row on that card is a total or a bound; this is the one that is neither, and the missing half is the one that tells a player whether sweeping is a skill they have.
acceptance_criteria: The post-mortem reports husks missed alongside husks swept, and the counter survives to the end of the run. A unit test drives a husk to rot through the real timer and asserts the count.
close_reason: Closed

title: Two palettes, one game, and the HUD's private half is now the bigger one
description: garden_theme.gd states outright that it does not touch the in-game HUD, and hud.gd re-declares INK, PAPER, PAPER_DARK and LEAF with identical values. That was a fair split when the HUD had four colours. It has since grown UPROOT_ARMED, THREAT_WARM, THREAT_HOT, HEALTH_BACK, HEALTH_FULL and HEALTH_LOW -- six more the title screen, the notebook and the post-mortem cannot reach, even though the post-mortem is a paper card that would want the same red for 'this cost you something'. The HUD references GardenTheme only for animations_enabled().
acceptance_criteria: One palette, reachable from every screen, with the HUD's semantic colours named where the other screens can use them. No colour value is declared twice.
close_reason: Closed

title: Node metadata is a cross-script contract that no gate can see
description: A Sundew's entire slow correctness lives in set_meta on a Pest -- the base speed and the source count are stored under string keys read by another script. title_screen.gd does the same with bare 'speed' and 'offset' literals. Because the keys are strings, name_check.py cannot resolve them, lint and import_check only type-check declarations, and coverage_check.py's eight defect classes are all Controls, signals, orphans, input, scenes, shaders and names. A typo in a metadata key is silent everywhere and produces a plant that simply does nothing.
acceptance_criteria: Something fails when a set_meta key is written in one script and read with a different spelling in another. A parallel-safe checker in name_check.py's shape would fit the existing toolchain.
close_reason: tools/meta_key_check.py gates both ends of every metadata key; corrected the premise -- all five keys are single-file, not cross-script, and the checker labels the difference

title: Four keyboard verbs in a run and no screen names any of them
description: R restarts on game over, Escape and P pause, M mutes. The only mention anywhere is 'Press M to bring it back', printed after you have already found M. The title screen documents its own three keys in a HintLabel, so the convention exists; the run does not follow it. The pause card is the natural home -- it is already a full-screen surface with room, and it is where a player goes when they want to know what their options are.
acceptance_criteria: Every key binding available during a run is discoverable from within the run without pressing it first. A test asserts the listed keys match the ones _unhandled_input actually handles.
close_reason: Closed

title: Two sprite gates and neither can tell you the PNG came from the SVG
description: tools/svg_style_check.py never opens a raster; test/unit/test_sprite_style.gd reads PNGs against a hand-written 12-name EXPECTED_SIZE and never opens a source. So a stale render passes both -- edit an SVG, forget to run render_svg.gd, and every gate stays green over a PNG that no longer matches its source. A 13th SVG is also invisible to the raster gate until someone remembers to add its name.
acceptance_criteria: Something fails when a PNG is older than its SVG, or when an SVG has no corresponding rendered pair. Ideally EXPECTED_SIZE is derived from art_src/ rather than hand-maintained.
close_reason: Closed

title: The rare packet's tooltip names one plant and the packet now holds two
description: Hud.PACKET_TOOLTIP[rare] still reads 'the only reliable way to a Seed Sunflower'. The catalogue now has two tier-2 plants, so the rare packet rolls between the Sunflower and the Sticky Sundew and the sentence is false. SeedBank.packet_pool already computes the real pool and _refresh_packet_button already swaps the tooltip at runtime, so the surface to fix it exists.
acceptance_criteria: The rare packet's resting tooltip describes what the tier actually contains and stays true as the catalogue grows. A test asserts it does not name a specific plant.
close_reason: Closed

title: STYLE.md and the sprite gate's palette have drifted apart
description: The new tools/svg_style_check.py cross-checks the two places the palette is written down and reports: the gate's PALETTE in test/unit/test_sprite_style.gd carries #5E5E5E (beetle legs/rim) and #D7C9A8 (the seed packet's torn top) which art_src/STYLE.md documents nowhere. So a sprite author reading STYLE.md sees a 30-colour palette while the build enforces 32, and two legitimate colours look like violations until you read the test instead. STYLE.md is described as the measured contract, so it is the document that should be authoritative.
acceptance_criteria: STYLE.md and test_sprite_style.gd's PALETTE list the same colours, and svg_style_check.py's contract advisory is silent.
close_reason: Closed

title: An SVG style-contract linter that does not need the renderer
description: Authoring art_src/sticky_sundew.svg meant reasoning by hand about STYLE.md's palette and geometry rules -- canvas size, centred axis, edge margin, kit-palette-or-blend-of-two -- because the only way to find out whether a sprite drifts is to render it and run test_sprite_style.gd, which needs Godot. A pure-Python check of the SVG's own fills and strokes against STYLE.md would catch a wrong hue or an off-centre axis at authoring time, and would be parallel-safe, which matters because sprite authoring is exactly the kind of task that gets fanned out.
acceptance_criteria: A script reads art_src/*.svg and reports palette and geometry violations without launching Godot, and agrees with test_sprite_style.gd on every sprite currently in the repo.
close_reason: Closed

title: A fifth plant will not fit in the plant bar
description: Hud._plant_bar is a VBoxContainer at y=44 with 56px buttons and 8px separation. Four plants = 248px, ending at y=292, and _packet_button is hard-coded at y=300 -- so the fourth plant fits with exactly 8px to spare and a fifth overlaps the packet buttons. The side panel has no other slack; the selection box already runs to within 16px of the panel foot. The bar needs to scroll, shrink, or become a grid before the catalogue grows again.
acceptance_criteria: A fifth plant can be added without any side-panel control overlapping another. The existing sibling-occlusion test covers the plant bar at full catalogue size.
close_reason: Closed

title: The rare packet is a button that works once per run
description: PlantCatalog holds three plants, tiers 1/1/2, and the rare packet's max_tier is 99 over a single tier-2 plant. So the rare packet is meaningful exactly once per run and then is only a more expensive common packet. The catalogue is the constraint, not the packet system -- a fourth plant is what makes the tier ladder mean anything.
acceptance_criteria: A fourth plant exists with a mechanic none of the current three cover, and the rare packet remains meaningful after the Sunflower is unlocked.
close_reason: Closed

title: The post-mortem can only count what the run lost
description: RunSummary shows five rows and four of them are damage: waves survived, threat reached, beds lost, compost swept, weakest ground. Nothing counts what the player did well, because no counter exists -- Game._on_pest_died is the single kill funnel and increments nothing, no Time. call appears anywhere in game/, and _on_plant_destroyed frees the node without tallying. A post-mortem that can only report losses reads as a scolding rather than a record.
acceptance_criteria: The summary reports at least pests defeated and run duration alongside the losses, with the counters surviving to the end of the run. Unit tests cover each new counter through the real code path that increments it.
close_reason: Closed

title: The Seed Sunflower is the economy plant with nothing on the board to read
description: Sunflower pays YIELD seeds every INTERVAL seconds and calls _bloom() at the payout, but the only readout of when the next payout lands is the click-gated 'Next %d seeds in %.0fs' line in the selection panel. Corn Cobbler now shows its level as a muzzle fan and Chomp Flower shows chew progress as a shrinking ring; the plant whose entire purpose is a clock is the one plant with no clock on the board.
acceptance_criteria: A Sunflower's progress toward its next payout is visible on the board without selecting it, and the payout itself has a moment. Unit test asserts the drawn state tracks seconds_until_next_yield.
close_reason: Closed

title: The HUD still builds a Banner that nothing has called since the post-mortem shipped
description: hud.gd builds a full-width 48px Banner Label on every launch, and show_banner/hide_banner have zero callers anywhere in the repo now that RunSummary replaced the end-of-run banner. It is present in every scene-tree snapshot under .devtools/. The 0.23.0 orphan scan flags hide_banner independently. Either delete it, or give it the job it is obviously shaped for -- a wave-start announcement, which currently goes to the one-line message row and competes with everything else there.
acceptance_criteria: Either the Banner and its two methods are gone and no scene-tree snapshot contains it, or something calls show_banner and a test covers when it appears and when it clears.
close_reason: Closed

title: The HUD is the only part of the game that never moves
description: Zero create_tween calls in hud.gd, while plant.gd, corn_cobbler.gd, chomp_flower.gd, sunflower.gd, pest.gd, title_screen.gd and notebook_screen.gd all animate. The selection box appears instantly, the banner appears instantly, the uproot relabel snaps, and the threat tint jumps between colours rather than easing. GardenTheme.animations_enabled() already exists as the headless gate, so the pattern is established -- the HUD simply never adopted it.
acceptance_criteria: The selection panel, the message row and the threat tint all transition rather than snap, every animation is gated on GardenTheme.animations_enabled(), and the headless suite still passes because each animation layers on an already-correct final state.
close_reason: Closed

title: The common packet button stays lit once its tier is exhausted
description: Hud disables the common packet button only on locked_empty or seeds < cost. Now that a common packet correctly refuses once tier 1 is exhausted, the button stays lit and every click is a refusal message instead of a purchase. SeedBank.packet_pool(tier) already answers this exactly -- the button's disabled condition should include bank.packet_pool(&common).is_empty().
acceptance_criteria: A packet button is disabled when its tier has nothing left to give, and the tooltip says why. Unit test drains tier 1 and asserts the button is disabled.
close_reason: Closed

title: A Corn Cobbler at full bunch looks exactly like a fresh one
description: CornCobbler.LEVELS takes kernels 1 to 2 to 5 and spread_degrees 0 to 14 to 52, and upgrade() only bumps the level integer. Plant loads one texture once and never changes it, and RANGE is flat at every level. So the single most expensive decision in the game -- paying seeds to upgrade -- produces no visible change on the board at all. The only readout is a line in the selection panel, which requires clicking the plant to see.
acceptance_criteria: An upgraded Corn Cobbler is distinguishable from a level-1 one on the board without selecting it. Unit test asserts the visual differs per level.
close_reason: Closed

title: Project-identity devtools verb so a session can prove which build it is driving
description: A sibling git worktree of this project had its own Godot running and answered this session's devtools bus, because user:// is keyed on project name and shared across worktrees. It cost most of one runtime pass: symptoms were 'no Game in the tree' and node-not-found on paths that plainly existed, which reads as your own scene being broken. Register a project verb returning ProjectSettings.globalize_path('res://') plus the git branch, so any session can assert in one call that it is talking to its own build. Upstream fix filed as G-018; this is the local guard.
acceptance_criteria: cmd project_identity returns the absolute res:// path; a documented one-liner in CLAUDE.md compares it against the working directory before a runtime pass.
close_reason: project_identity verb reports project_root, user_dir, git branch/sha read from disk, worktree-aware; verified live against git rev-parse and offline discovery

title: Tint the threat level as it climbs
description: threat_level() renders as a small integer in the same cream as every other readout, so 'this wave is worse than the last' is something the player has to read and compare rather than see. Tint the threat portion of the wave label green -> amber -> red across the level range so the escalation is preattentive. The level is already a pure static function, so this is a colour lookup.
acceptance_criteria: A static Hud.threat_colour(level) with tests pinning the endpoints and monotonic movement between them; the label uses it.
close_reason: Wave readout tints cream->amber->red via static Hud.threat_color(), saturating at level 12; verified live at both ends

title: Placement preview should warn when a non-combat plant is road-adjacent
description: A hungry pest eats whatever plant is nearest and a Sunflower cannot fight back, but nothing on screen says 'this tile is one hungry mutation away from losing your economy plant'. PlacementPreview already computes reach and legality per cell, so this is nearly free now: road-adjacency is one is_path check on the four neighbours, and the preview is the node that would draw the warning. Only applies to plants with PlantCatalog.reach(id) == 0.0 -- a Corn Cobbler next to the road is fine, that is the point of it.
acceptance_criteria: Hovering a grass cell orthogonally adjacent to the road with the Sunflower selected draws a distinct warning cue; the same cell with a Corn Cobbler selected does not; both covered by unit tests.
close_reason: Closed

title: Per-run lane pressure for the end-of-run post-mortem
description: The lane pressure overlay now shows a whole wave's loss distribution, faded by one decay step per wave, which answers 'where did I lose this wave'. It cannot answer 'which cell has bled me all game'. Accumulate a second, never-faded tally alongside the per-wave one and show it on the end-of-run screen, so the post-mortem tells the player where their garden was actually weak.
acceptance_criteria: Board keeps a run-total pressure map separate from the decaying per-wave one; the end-of-run banner or screen renders it; a unit test shows the run map surviving fades that clear the wave map.
close_reason: Closed

title: Show a readable threat level for endless mode
description: Health, speed, count, gap and mutation chance now all climb independently past wave 8 and the player can see none of them -- the HUD just says 'Wave 39 / 8'. Derive one threat number (or a wave-start banner naming what went up this wave) from the five WaveDirector static functions, which are already pure and callable without a running wave. This is a readout, not a new system.
acceptance_criteria: A static WaveDirector.threat_for(wave) that is monotonic past the fixed table and constant inside it, shown on the HUD, with unit tests for both halves.
close_reason: Closed

title: A richer husk should rot faster, so sweep order becomes a decision
description: Husk size and glow now scale with value, but the timer does not: a 9-seed husk and a 2-seed one both rot in exactly CompostMeter.HUSK_LIFETIME (10s). Sweeping in any order is therefore optimal and the board asks nothing. Scale the lifetime inversely with value (a richer husk decays faster) so 'which one first?' is a real decision, and so the new size cue carries urgency as well as worth.
acceptance_criteria: drop_husk stores a per-husk lifetime derived from value; HuskLayer's rot ring reads that instead of the constant; a unit test shows a high-value husk expiring before a low-value one dropped at the same moment.
close_reason: Closed

title: Lane pressure should record every cell pests were lost at, not just the worst
description: Board.record_lane_pressure only ever receives the single furthest-reached cell for a wave (Game._wave_worst_cell), so a wave where pests died at scattered points along the lane only ever lights up the worst one. Recording every cell a pest died/escaped at (not just the max) would draw the whole 'where the damage happened' picture instead of one hot pixel.
close_reason: Closed

title: Endless mode should scale pest health/speed too
description: WaveDirector._endless_groups scales count/gap and mutation_chance_for scales mutation chance as endless mode runs longer, but Pest.SPECIES health/speed stay fixed forever -- a wave-60 pest is exactly as tough as a wave-9 one. Scale health and/or speed slightly past some endless threshold, mirroring the mutation-chance climb, so late-game pressure isn't pure quantity.
close_reason: Closed

title: Husk size/glow should scale with value
description: HuskLayer._draw() draws every husk at a fixed 9px radius regardless of CompostMeter's stored value, so a mutated pest's 1.5-2x husk_multiplier() payout is invisible until clicked. Scale the drawn radius (or ring brightness) by value so a bigger payout reads visually across the board, the way mutation tints already do for the pest itself.
close_reason: Closed

title: Second bite frame for a beetle's long chew
description: chomp_flower_eating.png is one fixed picture for the whole chew animation, aphid or beetle alike, even though a beetle's chew is 2.6s — long enough to read a second frame. Swap in an 'almost done' frame once chew_progress() > 0.6 (the same threshold the shrinking ring already reads) to sell 'big pests take a while' with just a second sprite and one if-check.

title: Endless mode should mutate faster over time
description: WaveDirector._endless_groups scales pest count and gap as endless mode continues, but MUTATION_CHANCE stays fixed at 40% forever, so wave 40 looks exactly as 'weird' as wave 8. Scale mutation chance upward (or widen MUTATIONS with a rarer fourth trait) past some endless-mode wave threshold so a long run keeps feeling different.

title: Pair the two claim rules where both are read
description: SOURCE: cycle 165's kanban entry, first bullet. TWO RULES NOW EXIST IN .claude/skills/cycle/references/why.md and they bracket one mistake: cycle 156's 'a REASONED EXCLUSION is a claim, and gets the same check as a citation' (written after a header confidently excluded a case a screenshot then refuted), and cycle 165's 'a COMPUTED FAILURE is a claim, and its reachability is part of it' (written after two correct numbers described states the code refuses at both call sites). THE MISTAKE THEY BRACKET is believing something about a case nobody looked at -- once by arguing it away, once by computing it. They are currently separated by several hundred lines of that file and neither points at the other. THE ASK IS SMALL: cross-reference them, and consider whether they want to be one rule with two faces rather than two rules. A reader who has just made one of these mistakes is not going to find the other by scrolling. WHY P4 AND NOT LOWER: because why.md is the file step 5 edits every cycle, and a file that grows two unconnected rules about the same thing is exactly what the 'simple is a constraint on the loop file itself' note at its top exists to prevent. This is small maintenance on the thing that keeps the loop readable. ACCEPTANCE: the two rules cross-referenced or merged, and a sentence saying which mistake they share -- since the shared shape is the transferable part and neither rule states it alone.

title: new-uid mints a .uid sidecar for any path, including a .py
description: SOURCE: cycle 153, log-devtools [G-143]. Ran 'python tools/devtools.py new-uid --write tools/gate_aim_check.py' out of habit after adding a tool file; it printed 'uid://bwfh52uu6dksi -> ...tools/gate_aim_check.py.uid' and wrote it. A UID is a Godot resource identity. A sidecar beside a Python file is meaningless, is invisible to lint's UID pass (which walks .gd), and sits in the tree unexplained -- deleted by hand this cycle. THE VERB HAS THE INFORMATION TO REFUSE: it knows the suffix. FIX: refuse a path whose suffix is not one Godot mints UIDs for (.gd, .tscn, .tres, .gdshader), naming the suffix it got. One if. This is harness code under tools/, so the fix belongs upstream in godot-selftest-harness rather than patched locally -- see the .harness_manifest.json rule. ACCEPTANCE: filed upstream with skill-feedback-issue, the issue number stamped on G-143's status line.

title: An armed move draws its ring over ground the plant could never occupy
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md "New in cycle 113", second entry, and named as NOT DONE in -l7ak's close.

BLOCKED ON -h5w6, deliberately, and this bead exists to record why rather than to be worked.

Cycle 113 stopped the move preview PROMISING cells the moved plant cannot occupy:
`_preview.placeable` now requires that the plant being described could stand there
(game/game.gd, the third term). But the ring, the reach and the coverage dots still paint
from those cells -- `_update_preview` sets `_preview.reach` and `_preview.plant_id` from
